## PR #5367 — pkg/snmp: canonical TimeTicks BER + RFC 3416 repetition-major GETBULK (#4924, #5065) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/4924-5065-snmp-ber-getbulk`

Bundles two SNMP wire-encoding-correctness fixes; both live in `pkg/snmp`
and are the same RFC-conformance class. Two logical commits, one per issue.

## FIXED — #4924: TimeTicks BER omits the leading zero for high-bit values
`berEncodeTimeTicks` (pkg/snmp/agent.go) stripped leading zero bytes but,
unlike its sibling unsigned encoders `berEncodeCounter32` /
`berEncodeGauge32` / `berEncodeCounter64`, never prepended a `0x00` when the
most-significant content octet has its high bit set. TimeTicks is an unsigned
APPLICATION integer, yet BER integer content is two's-complement, so at
`>= 0x80000000` hundredths (~248.5 days of uptime) `sysUpTime` and the v1/v2
link-trap timestamps encoded as negative / non-canonical signed BER — an
"invalid uptime" a strict manager rejects, surfacing only after months of
runtime.

**Fix:** after the leading-zero strip, prepend one `0x00` when
`buf[0]&0x80 != 0` — the exact pattern the Counter32/Counter64/Gauge32
encoders already use. Reproduced on current master before the change.

## FIXED — #5065: GETBULK encodes multiple repeaters column-major (RFC 3416 §4.2.3)
Both GETBULK handlers nested the per-repetition loop inside the
per-repeater-column loop — `handleGetBulk` (pkg/snmp/agent.go) and the v3
dispatcher (pkg/snmp/v3.go) — emitting column-major `A1,A2,B1,B2`. RFC 3416
§4.2.3 mandates repetition-major `A1,B1,A2,B2`; a table-oriented manager
reconstructs rows by the known repeater width R, so column-major
mis-associates columns whenever R >= 2. Two independent copies carried the
same bug.

**Fix:** extract one shared `(*Agent).buildBulkVarbinds` called by both the
v2c and v3 paths so they encode identical wire order. It keeps a persistent
GETNEXT cursor per repeater column, loops outermost over repetition and
innermost over column, and — when a column runs past the end of its MIB view
— emits `endOfMibView` (named with that column's terminal OID) in that
column's own grid cell for the exhausting repetition and every later one, so
the `row*R+col` index stays aligned. The old code broke out of the inner loop
on first exhaustion, collapsing the grid. Reproduced on current master before
the change.

## PR #5368 — pkg/config: fix LOW validation-residual cohort (#5194) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5194-config-validation-cohort`

Closes #5194

Fixes the 8-finding LOW-severity `pkg/config` validation-residual cohort from codex-review-177. Each sub-finding was independently re-verified as still reproducing on current `origin/master` (base `1ae3726cf`) before fixing. All 8 are genuine — none were skipped.

## Per-finding disposition

### FIXED — A3-b1-F2: bare destination/source-port `0`/`0-0` → (0,0) wildcard sentinel
`parsePortRange` returns `(0,0)` for a bare `0`/`0-0`, colliding with the Rust matcher's `(0,0)` "no constraint" sentinel, so a tolerantly-loaded `destination-port 0` app shipped a catalog row that over-matched every port. Added `appid.NormalizeExplicitPortRange` (empty = unconstrained; a bare `0`/`0-0` is unemittable; a `0-N` range narrows to `1-N`) and wired it into **both** `appid.BuildCatalog` and `pkg/dataplane.compileApplications` so the two AppNames maps stay byte-identical (`appid_catalog_parity_test.go`).

### FIXED — A3-b2-F1: apply-groups expansion had no depth/work budget
`expandGroupsRecursive` had only the `seen` cycle guard and the #4474 DAG memo — neither bounds a deep acyclic chain `g1->…->gN`, which recurses one frame per link toward stack exhaustion on commit/HA-sync. Threaded a `depth` counter (nested-group recursion only, **not** the config-tree descent — tree depth is already bounded by the #4148 brace-depth cap) capped at `maxGroupExpandDepth=64`, and a shared `groupExpandBudget.work` counter capped at `maxGroupExpandWork=100000`. Both fail cleanly; caps sit far above legitimate Junos nesting.

### FIXED — A3-b2-F9: full-domain IPv4 range count wraps to zero
`expandAddressRange` computed `highN-lowN+1` in `uint32`, so `0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255` wrapped `+1` to `0`, the `>256` gate passed, and the loop ran zero times — an empty pool with `nil` error instead of the size error. Now computed in `uint64`.

### FIXED — A3-b2-F11: display JSON overwrote repeated leaves
`nodesToJSON` projected each leaf into a single-value map, so repeated leaves (e.g. multiple `name-server`) overwrote last-wins and lost data. Repeats now promote to an ordered `[]interface{}` in document order (Junos `display json` semantics); a single occurrence stays scalar.

### FIXED — A3-b2-F12: unknown symbolic CoS code-point silently dropped
`expandCoSCodePointToken` returned `(nil,nil)` for an unknown symbolic DSCP token (a typo like `af99`) and the two 802.1p closures skipped any non-numeric token — silently dropped in strict **and** tolerant paths, unlike the numeric out-of-range path (#2447/#4953). Added `unknownCodePointTokenError` + `isDowngradableCoSCodePointError`; a typo now strict-rejects / lenient-warns uniformly across classifier+rewrite, DSCP+PCP. Blast radius is contained (each collector has one caller, all four carry the downgrade).

### FIXED — A3-b3-F5: uncapped quadratic VRF-overlap scan
`validateVRFOverlap` ran an uncapped `O(P²)` prefix-pair scan on every compile (incl. HA peer-sync) with no op budget or warning cap. Added a family-separated early-skip, a comparison budget (`1<<20`), and a warning cap (`64`) with a single truncation notice.

> Note: the finding also suggested a family-separated prefix trie/interval sweep. For a cold advisory-only path (a warning, never a reject) a full trie rewrite is disproportionate risk; the operation budget + warning cap eliminate the "genuinely unbounded" concern that made this a finding, and the family early-skip is retained. A trie is a perf optimization left for a future maintainer-gated follow-up.

### FIXED — A3-b3-F6: malformed WireGuard AllowedIPs commit then silently vanish
`canonicalAllowedIPPrefix` keyed an unparseable CIDR verbatim; the Rust hydrate (`forwarding_build/tunnels.rs`) then `Err(_) => continue` silently dropped it while keeping the peer. Added a strict `netip.ParsePrefix` gate in `validateOneWireguardTunnel` (reject on strict commit, warn on tolerant load via the existing `emit()`); also made the Rust drop **observable** (`eprintln` naming the dropped prefix) for the leniently-loaded case.

### FIXED — A3-b3-F7: flat-set parser silently discards tokens after `;`
`ParseSetVerb` broke on `TokenSemicolon` or `TokenEOF` without requiring EOF, so `set system host-name fw; delete security policies` applied only the hostname and dropped the rest while reporting success. Now permits at most one terminating `;` then requires EOF, rejecting any trailing token with line/column.

## RED-on-revert evidence (two most material)

- **Port-0 sentinel (F2):** neutered `NormalizeExplicitPortRange` to `return low, high, true`. `TestBuildCatalogPortZeroSentinel_5194` went RED — the `dstzero` app re-emitted a catalog entry `DstPortLow:0 DstPortHigh:0` (the over-match row); `TestAppCatalogParityOnPortZero_5194` also RED. Restored → green.
- **apply-groups depth (F1):** disabled the `depth > maxGroupExpandDepth` check (`if false && …`). `TestApplyGroupsDepthBudget_5194` went RED (a chain past the cap expanded with no error). Restored → green.

Every finding also carries its own fail-on-revert test.

- `go test ./pkg/config/... ./pkg/appid/... ./pkg/dataplane/... ./pkg/configstore/... ./pkg/eventengine/... ./pkg/cli/... ./pkg/grpcapi/...` → all `ok`

## PR #5369 — pkg/flowexport: clamp packet-count-fallback StartTime to EndTime (#4923) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/4923-flowexport-starttime-overflow`

## Summary

Fixes a `time.Duration` overflow in the flow-export packet-count fallback
that could place a flow's `StartTime` **after** its `EndTime`.

In `pkg/flowexport/manager.go`, the `Created==0` fallback in `flowStartTime`
computed:

```go
rec.Time.Add(-estimateSessionDuration(rec.SessionPkts, proto))
```

`estimateSessionDuration` multiplies the `uint64` packet count by a per-packet
time (100ms TCP / 50ms non-TCP). Above ~92.2 billion TCP packets (~184.5
billion non-TCP) the product overflows signed `time.Duration` to a **negative**
value; subtracting a negative duration from the record `EndTime` moves
`StartTime` after `EndTime`. NetFlow then emits first-switched after
last-switched and IPFIX emits contradictory absolute milliseconds that a
collector may reject — exactly on the legacy / HA-recovery fallback paths where
a synthesized close carries no creation instant.

The real-`created` branch already clamps a future stamp
(`if created.After(rec.Time) { return rec.Time, false }`); the packet-count
fallback had no such clamp.

## Fix

Minimal, two-layer, mirroring the existing skew clamp:

1. **Root cause** — `estimateSessionDuration` now **saturates** at a new
   `maxEstimatedSessionAge` constant (366 days — a defensible session ceiling
   ~9e12 ns below the int64 nanosecond limit) *before* the multiply can
   overflow, so the estimate is always bounded and non-negative. Packet counts
   below the cap threshold keep the **exact prior estimate**; only the
   pathological overflow regime changes.
2. **Invariant guard** — `flowStartTime` additionally clamps the fallback
   `StartTime` to `EndTime`, mirroring the `Created` skew clamp, so
   `StartTime <= EndTime` holds regardless of how the heuristic evolves.

## Validation

- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` — exit 0
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/...` — pass
- `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet ./pkg/flowexport/...` clean

### Fail-on-revert tests (`pkg/flowexport/flowstart_test.go`)

- `TestEstimateSessionDurationSaturates` — packet counts through
  `math.MaxUint64` for TCP and UDP assert `0 <= d <= maxEstimatedSessionAge`
  and exact-cap saturation.

## PR #5370 — cli/cmdtree/appid: fix nil-config completion, zone-prefix retention, custom-app status (#5196) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5196-cli-appid-ux`

Closes #5196

Low-severity CLI-completion and operator-facing status residuals from
codex-review-177 (A3-b1-F3/F4/F5). Each finding was re-verified against
current `origin/master` in a fresh worktree, fixed, and pinned with a
fail-on-revert test. All three findings reproduced on master.

Note on scope: the issue routes finding F4 to `pkg/cmdtree/tree.go`
(the operational-tree completion walker is the SSOT for tab completion
across the local CLI, remote CLI, and gRPC). The parent task labeled it
`pkg/cli`; the actual defect and fix live in `pkg/cmdtree`, which is what
`pkg/cli` calls.

## FIXED — A3-b1-F3: nil-config dynamic providers suppressed (pkg/cmdtree)

The completion walker gated **every** dynamic provider behind
`cfg != nil` at all four `DynamicValues` call sites (`CompleteFromTree`
leaf + end-of-loop, `CompleteFromTreeWithDesc` leaf + end-of-loop). That
caller gate suppressed config-independent providers that intentionally
supply defaults for a nil active config:

- `show route table` → `inet.0` / `inet6.0`
- `show route protocol` → the static protocol list

A nil active config is a real operator state (fresh boot before the
first commit, compile-failure recovery), so tab completion silently
offered nothing there.

I audited **all 40** `DynamicFn`/`ContextDynamicFn` providers in the
tree: every one is nil-safe — it guards `cfg == nil`, ignores `cfg`, or
delegates to a nil-safe helper (`routingInstanceTableNames`,
`cosClassifierNames`, `redundancyGroupIDs`, …). **Fix:** make nil-safety
the provider contract and drop the redundant `&& cfg != nil` caller gate
at all four sites.

**Test:** `pkg/cmdtree/completion_nil_provider_5196_test.go` drives the
real completers with a nil config (value + description walkers, plus a
partial-prefix case).

## FIXED — A3-b1-F4: context completion loses zone on prefixes (pkg/cmdtree)

`resolveTreeWord` accepts unique keyword prefixes for traversal but the
walker discarded the canonical name and passed the raw (abbreviated)
words to `ContextDynamicFn`. The policy-name provider under
`show security policies from-zone <z> to-zone <z> policy` recovers the
zone pair by scanning the consumed words for the **exact** keywords
`from-zone`/`to-zone`. With an accepted abbreviation (`from-z`/`to-z`)
the scan matched neither, both zones resolved to empty, and every
policy-name candidate was hidden.

## PR #5371 — pkg/config: collision-safe IPsec proposal names + redact VRRP track secret (#5195) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5195-config-secret-handling`

## Summary

Closes #5195. Drives the two codex-review-177 **pkg/config secret-handling** LOW-cohort findings to fixes, each re-verified present on current `origin/master` and each with a fail-on-revert test.

Control-plane config/validation only — no forwarding path, so no cluster smoke.

---

### A3-b2-F7 — synthetic proposal-set name collision → silent crypto downgrade — **FIXED**

**Reproduced on master:** `syntheticProposalSetName` (`compiler_ipsec_proposalset.go`) mints synthetic proposals under `__proposal-set/<policy>/<set>/<index>` names and `expandIKEProposalSets` / `expandIPsecProposalSets` write them into the **same** name-keyed `IKEProposals` / `Proposals` maps as operator-authored proposals, unconditionally, **after** those maps are built (lines 145 / 176 on master). The lexer permits `/ _ .` in bare identifiers, so an operator can author a proposal with that exact name — the map write then silently overwrites one with the other, installing a different (typically weaker) crypto proposal than configured. A silent crypto downgrade.

**Fix (fail-closed, #1960-correct):**
- New AST pre-walk gate `validateReservedIPsecProposalNamesAST` **reserves** the `__proposal-set/` prefix (`reservedProposalSetNamePrefix`, now the single source of truth shared with the name builder). A **strict** commit / commit-check **hard-rejects** any authored `security {ike|ipsec} proposal` using the prefix → the collision (and thus the downgrade) can never commit. The **tolerant** load / peer-sync path **warns** (`lenientReservedProposalSetNames`) so an already-persisted / peer-synced config an older binary accepted still boots. This lands on the correct side of the #1960 line: reject a genuine collision at strict commit; do not hard-fail a tolerant load.
- The gate enumerates names with the **same** `namedInstances` helper `compileIKE` / `compileIPsec` use to key the maps, so it checks exactly the names that could collide.
- Belt-and-suspenders: the two expand loops gain an **occupancy guard** — never overwrite a slot already taken — so a leniently-loaded squatter is preserved rather than clobbered (no downgrade even on the warn path).

**Tests** (`compiler_ipsec_reserved_proposal_name_5195_test.go`): strict reject of a reserved-prefix IKE **and** ESP proposal name; lenient path preserves the authored `aes-256-cbc` crypto instead of overwriting it with the `standard` set member `3des-cbc` (asserts **no downgrade** — the "distinct installed proposals" requirement); a no-false-positive clean-expansion case.

---

### A3-b2-F10 — VRRP track validator echoes the auth secret — **FIXED**

**Reproduced on master:** `validateVRRPTrackInterfaceAST` (`compiler_interfaces.go:934`) built the duplicate-`track-interface` diagnostic path from the **full** vrrp-group node `Keys` and passed it to `checkVRRPGroupTrackShape` (messages at :1064 / :1070). In the Keys-packed spelling `vrrp-group 1 authentication-key <secret> track-interface X track-interface Y`, the `authentication-key` VALUE rides on that Keys run, so the strict error / lenient warning **echoed the secret** into logs + CLI. The sibling #4288 auth validator already avoids this via `vrrpGroupIDKeys(n)`.

**Fix:** build the message path from `vrrpGroupIDKeys(n)` (the value-free `vrrp-group <id>` identity) **before** any message, mirroring `validateVRRPAuthenticationAST`. The recursion prefix keeps the full `nodePath` (children are separate nodes with no secret in their Keys), matching the auth validator's structure.

**Tests** (`vrrp_track_secret_5195_test.go`): a Keys-packed vrrp-group with a sentinel `authentication-key` + two `track-interface` statements rejects (strict) and warns (lenient) **without** the secret appearing, while still naming `vrrp-group 1` + the track-interface finding.

---

## PR #5372 — pkg/api: bound concurrent diagnostic ping/traceroute (#5057) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5057-api-diag-concurrency-limit`

Closes #5057

## Problem
The diagnostic REST/gRPC ping/traceroute endpoints (`pkg/api/system.go` `pingHandler`/`tracerouteHandler`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_ping.go` `Ping`/`Traceroute`) spawn one child process per request — plus pipes, buffered output, a handler goroutine and, on gRPC, a stream — with **only** a per-request deadline (`pingExecTimeout`/`diagTracerouteTimeout` + `WaitDelay`) and **no aggregate concurrency bound**. The only admission control in `pkg/api` is the Prometheus `MaxRequestsInFlight`, which does not cover these handlers.

A burst of concurrent diagnostic requests can therefore hold hundreds/thousands of PIDs/FDs/goroutines for up to the 150s `diagExecCeiling` — an authenticated management-plane DoS that starves the control plane driving the dataplane.

Gap confirmed on current `origin/master`: the handlers have a per-job deadline but no shared semaphore/queue/cap.

## Fix
Add a shared **fail-fast counting semaphore** `diagcmd.Limiter` + a process-wide `diagcmd.DefaultLimiter` (`MaxConcurrentDiagnostics = 4`) in a new `pkg/diagcmd/limiter.go`.

- **One cap covers both surfaces.** REST handlers and gRPC RPCs each acquire a slot before spawning any child, via a `diagLimiter` package var pointing at the **same** `DefaultLimiter`. `diagcmd` is the natural home — both API packages already import it for argv construction. A diagnostic admitted over REST and one over gRPC draw from the same budget.
- **Limit value: 4.** Small enough that a flood cannot exhaust host resources, large enough for a handful of legitimate concurrent operator/automation diagnostics. Named const.
- **Immediate rejection, no queue.** Acquire is non-blocking: when the cap is reached the request is rejected right away — REST `HTTP 429`, gRPC `codes.ResourceExhausted` — rather than piling up an unbounded backlog of waiters.
- **Release on all paths.** The slot is released via `defer` on success, exec error, ctx timeout/cancel, and panic. Release is idempotent (`sync.Once`) so an accidental double-defer cannot over-release and free another caller's slot (which would re-open the very DoS window this closes).
- **Test seams.** The child spawn routes through `diagRun` (REST) and `streamDiag` (gRPC) package vars so tests inject a fake slow diagnostic — no real ping/traceroute subprocesses.

## Tests
- `pkg/diagcmd/limiter_test.go` — cap-then-reject semantics, idempotent-release (double-release cannot leak a slot), and an N+K concurrent fake-diagnostic bound (all-attempted barrier → deterministic).
- `pkg/api/diag_concurrency_5057_test.go` / `pkg/grpcapi/diag_concurrency_5057_test.go` — fire `cap+excess` concurrent requests; assert ≤`cap` run concurrently, the excess get 429 / `ResourceExhausted` (not queued, not hung), and the limiter is fully released afterward (a subsequent request succeeds). Each package also asserts ping and traceroute share the single cap.

### RED-on-revert (proven)
Neutering the `diagLimiter.Acquire()` branch in both handler sides:
- REST: `429 count = 0, want 5 [200 200 200 200 200 200 200]` — all 7 admitted, **FAIL**
- gRPC: `ResourceExhausted count = 0, want 5 [<nil> <nil> <nil> <nil> <nil> <nil> <nil>]` — all 7 admitted, **FAIL**

Restored → green.

## Validation
- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0
- `go vet ./pkg/diagcmd/... ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/grpcapi/...` clean
- `go test ./pkg/diagcmd/... ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/grpcapi/...` pass; new tests green under `-race -count=5`
- `gofmt` clean
- Docs: `pkg/api/README.md` + `pkg/grpcapi/README.md` diagnostic-endpoint sections document the shared limiter, the 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED behavior, and release-on-all-paths.

No cluster smoke — control-plane API, no forwarding path.

## PR #5374 — pkg/grpcapi: reject duplicate ShowText test-routing selectors (#4921) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/4921-grpcapi-dup-selectors`

Closes #4921

## Problem
The gRPC `ShowText` `test-routing:` selector parser (`showTestRouting`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_routes_text.go`) rejects malformed grammar and unknown keys (#4589) but had **no `seen` map**, so a repeated *known* selector key silently **last-won** in the switch. A query like:

```
test-routing:dest=10.0.0.0/24,dest=192.0.2.1
test-routing:dest=192.0.2.1,instance=blue,instance=prod
```

ran the diagnostic route lookup against a **different destination/VRF than the operator typed**, with no warning — misleading during a routing investigation over REST or the remote CLI. This is the routing-simulator sibling of #3709, which fixed the analogous duplicate-selector gap for the `test-policy:` bridge.

## Fix
Add `seen := make(map[string]bool)` and, between the malformed-segment guard and the switch, reject a repeated key with the **same error shape** `showTestPolicy` uses — `selector %q specified more than once` — before the routing-manager / missing-dest fall-through. There is no correct silent pick for a duplicate, so a repeat is a hard client-input error. Because `parseErr` is set-once, a duplicate *unknown* key still surfaces its first-occurrence "unknown selector" error.

## Rationale
A diagnostic simulator must answer the exact query the operator typed. Silent last-wins made the route lookup answer for a packet the operator did not ask about, with no error. Matching #3709 keeps the two ShowText diagnostic bridges (`test-policy:` and `test-routing:`) consistent: both fail closed on an ambiguous duplicate rather than picking one value silently.

## RED-on-revert evidence
New test `server_show_test_routing_dupselector_4921_test.go` supplies a duplicate `dest` and a duplicate `instance`, asserting both the diagnostic string and that the query does **not** fall through to the lookup path; a distinct-key set is not flagged (no false-positive).

With `server_show_routes_text.go` reverted to `origin/master` (via `git stash`):

```

    ... = "Routing manager not available\n"; want it to contain
      "selector \"dest\" specified more than once"
--- FAIL: TestShowTestRoutingRejectsDuplicateSelector/duplicate_instance
    ... = "Routing manager not available\n"; want it to contain
      "selector \"instance\" specified more than once"
--- PASS: TestShowTestRoutingDistinctSelectorsNotFlagged
```

Restored to green: all `ShowTestRouting` tests PASS.

- `gofmt` clean

The in-code comment and tests are the contract for this topic, so no doc update.

## PR #5375 — pkg/api: close surviving listener on Run startup failure (#5058) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5058-api-listener-leak`

Closes #5058

## Problem
`pkg/api` `Server.Run` started the HTTP and (when configured) HTTPS
listeners in goroutines reporting to a shared `errCh`, and the `select`
returned on `case err := <-errCh` **before** the `Shutdown` block. When
one listener failed to bind/serve while the other was serving
successfully, `Run` returned the error immediately and never shut the
surviving listener down.

That leaves an **orphaned management socket**: the daemon wrapper
(`daemon_run.go`) logs the error, `wg.Done()`s, and marks its task done,
so later context cancellation can never reach the shutdown code. HTTPS is
a supported mode (self-signed cert generation), so both-listeners-active
is a real configuration.

## Fix
Treat the listeners as one lifecycle — startup all-or-nothing, any
terminal child error tears down every sibling:

- Bind both listeners synchronously up front via `net.Listen` (HTTP
  first). On HTTPS bind failure, close the already-bound HTTP listener
  and return **before** anything serves — a failed startup leaves no
  orphaned socket.
- Serve each bound listener via `Serve` / `ServeTLS(ln, "", "")` in a
  `WaitGroup`-tracked goroutine. `ServeTLS("", "")` uses the
  `TLSConfig.Certificates` already set in `NewServer`, identical to the
  prior `ListenAndServeTLS("", "")`.
- On any serve error **or** `ctx` cancellation, `Shutdown` **both**
  servers and `wg.Wait()` to join both goroutines before returning, so no
  listener, socket, or goroutine outlives `Run`. The serve error is
  returned ahead of any shutdown error.

Normal graceful-shutdown ordering (ctx cancel → Shutdown both → return
nil) is preserved.

## Tests — `pkg/api/server_run_leak_5058_test.go`
- **`TestRunClosesSurvivingListenerOnBindFailure`** pre-binds the HTTPS
  port to force its bind to fail, then asserts the sibling HTTP port is
  not still accepting connections (no leak) and is re-bindable.
- **`TestRunGracefulShutdownClosesBothListeners`** exercises the normal
  ctx-cancel path (both up → cancel → `Run` returns nil → both ports
  released), guarding the shutdown ordering.

Branch: `fix/5063-eventengine-armed-commit`

## Problem

The daemon's `CommitFn` (`commitAndApply` → `applyAndSyncCommitted`,
`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go`) is **tri-state**: on a NON-FATAL best-effort
subsystem apply error (networkd write / Kea restart / host-inbound nft, #4034)
it returns the just-committed `*config.Config` **alongside** the error — the
config is committed, active, and the dataplane is **armed**. The generation is
live.

But `applyOnce` (`pkg/eventengine/engine.go`) discarded that `compiled` config
and returned `errBatch` for **any** error, and `runAction` incremented
`committed` / armed the cooldown **only** on `err == nil`. Result: a live
autonomous change was miscounted **rejected**, no cooldown was armed, and the
same event could immediately re-commit — false telemetry plus control-plane
churn during an incident. #4034 documented the daemon-side non-fatal state but
never reconciled the engine accounting.

*Provenance: codex-review-177 [A9-b1-F4], Medium.*

## Fix

Read the returned `*config.Config`, **not the error**, as the authority on
whether the generation was promoted:

- `(compiled != nil, err)` → **committed-with-apply-debt**. `applyOnce` signals
  it as a new `commitDebtError` (wraps the subsystem error; `Unwrap` exposed).
  `runAction` detects it via `errors.As` **first**, counts `committed` + a new
  distinct `committedWithDebt` counter, arms the **same-generation** cooldown
  (the #5311 `authRev`), logs a WARN, and does **not** retry.
- `(nil, err)` → the only **genuine rejection** (commit never promoted /
  dataplane disarmed).

**Invariant:** once a generation is promoted and armed, the engine's commit
counters, cooldown, and audit record it as committed even if a best-effort
subsystem remains in debt.

Surfaced the debt subset as `xpf_event_actions_committed_with_debt_total`;
`xpf_event_actions_committed_total` now documents it INCLUDES the debt subset.

## Fail-on-revert tests (`engine_armed_debt_5063_test.go`)

Callback matrix — success, fatal, stale, active-with-nonfatal-error:

| case | commitFn returns | asserts |
|------|------------------|---------|
| active-with-nonfatal-error (**core**) | `(cfg, err)` | `Committed==1`, `CommittedWithDebt==1`, `Rejected==0`, cooldown armed, active config updated |
| genuine rejection | `(nil, err)` | `Rejected==1`, `Committed==0`, cooldown NOT armed, config unchanged |
| clean commit | `(cfg, nil)` | `Committed==1`, `CommittedWithDebt==0`, `Rejected==0` |

## PR #5377 — pkg/config: bound member-range expansion loop to prevent int64-overflow DoS (#5373) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5373-memberrange-overflow`

Closes #5373

## Problem
`expandMemberRange` (`pkg/config/compiler_interface_range.go`) expanded a
`member-range <start> to <end>` selector with a counting loop
`for i := sn; i <= en; i++`. `sn`/`en` come from `splitTrailingInt` →
`strconv.Atoi`, which accepts any decimal up to `math.MaxInt64`
(member-range tokens do NOT pass through typed-schema validation). The
`interfaceRangeMaxMembers = 4096` cap only bounds the **difference**
`en-sn`, not `en`'s absolute value, so a range whose endpoints sit just
below `MaxInt64` — e.g. `sn = MaxInt64-5, en = MaxInt64` (`en-sn = 5 < cap`)
— **passes** the guard yet overflows the loop: at `i == MaxInt64` the body
runs, then `i++` wraps to `MinInt64`, `MinInt64 <= MaxInt64` stays true, and
the loop appends member names forever → infinite loop + unbounded slice
growth → **OOM**.

`expandMemberRange` runs during config compilation, which executes at strict
commit **and** on the tolerant load / HA config-sync paths — so a persisted
or peer-synced config carrying this pattern hangs the daemon **on load** (a
fail-closed / HA-DoS violation), not only on an interactive commit.

This is a **distinct** overflow from #4807, which guarded the `en-sn+1`
capacity (negative-`make` panic) for ranges that *exceed* the cap. #5373
fires for ranges that *pass* the cap.

## Fix
Iterate on the bounded **count** instead of the raw endpoint. The existing
cap check already guarantees `n = en-sn` is in `[0, interfaceRangeMaxMembers)`,
so looping `k` over `0..n` keeps the loop variable small and independent of
`en`'s magnitude, while forming each name as `sn+k` still yields exactly
`sn..en` (`sn+n == en`, and every `sn+k <= en <= MaxInt64` is overflow-free):

```go
n := en - sn                 // < interfaceRangeMaxMembers, overflow-free
out := make([]string, 0, n+1)
for k := 0; k <= n; k++ {
    out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", sp, sn+k))
}
```

Cap semantics and the `sn>en` / prefix-mismatch rejections are unchanged.

## RED-on-revert evidence
New test `TestExpandMemberRangeNearMaxInt64Terminates` drives
`expandMemberRange(sn=MaxInt64-5, en=MaxInt64)` in a goroutine guarded by a
`select { case <-done: case <-time.After(2*time.Second): t.Fatal(...) }`
watchdog, and asserts the bounded 6-name `sn..en` list with no warning. With
the fix it returns instantly; without it the goroutine spins and the watchdog
fires — so the test goes RED on revert **without wedging** the rest of the
`go test` run.

## PR #5378 — pkg/api: honor page_size in cursor mode with include_peer (#4920) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/4920-api-cursor-pagesize`

## Summary
Closes #4920.

The REST session list's `include_peer=true` first-page peer fan-out dropped cursor-mode `page_size`. `peerSessionsRequest` (`pkg/api/sessions.go`) forwarded the offset-mode `limit` but never set `PageSize`, so a cursor-mode caller — `GET /api/v1/sessions?page_size=N&include_peer=true` with **no** `limit` — sent the peer gRPC request `Limit==0` **and** `PageSize==0`. The peer's `getSessionsLegacy` (`pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:588`) then defaults the peer list to 100 sessions, so the first REST page attached at most 100 peer sessions even though the local first page was sized for `page_size`. HA dashboards/automation using cursor pagination silently undercounted peer sessions whenever the peer held >100.

## Fix
In `peerSessionsRequest`, also forward a validated `page_size` as `PageSize`, so the peer fan-out honors the SAME page bound the local list did. The value is read leniently, mirroring the existing `limit` forward — the caller (`sessionsHandler`) already validated `page_size` via `queryIntStrict` before a peer fetch is attempted, and the peer's gRPC surface re-clamps it to the 10000 ceiling. `page_token` is intentionally **not** forwarded (tokens encode node-local map keys; the peer fetch only runs on the first page).

## Test — fail-on-revert
`TestRESTSessionListPeerHonorsPageSize` (in `sessions_ha_scope_3423_test.go`) drives the cursor-capable `multiSessionDP` with `page_size=1000&include_peer=true` (the real trigger: `page_size` set, no `limit`) and asserts, through the `fakeClusterSessionService` seam (no real peer), that the recorded peer request carries `PageSize==1000`, `Limit==0`, and `IncludePeer` set — plus that the peer leg still attaches to the REST response.

**RED-on-revert (verified):** removing the `page_size`→`PageSize` forward makes the recorded peer request carry `PageSize==0`:
```
sessions_ha_scope_3423_test.go:390: peer request PageSize = 0, want 1000
    (cursor-mode page_size not forwarded — peer undercounts to the 100 default)
--- FAIL: TestRESTSessionListPeerHonorsPageSize
```

## Validation
- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` — exit 0
- `go test ./pkg/api/...` — ok (3.4s)
- `gofmt -l` on touched files — clean
- Docs: `pkg/api/README.md` HA-scope bullet updated to state the peer fetch honors the same page bound (forwards `limit` AND `page_size`).

No cluster smoke — this is a REST↔gRPC schema-translation adapter with no forwarding effect.

## PR #5383 — pkg/config: nil-guard application-set value in show-configuration (#5221) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5221-nil-appset-showconfig`

Closes #5221

## Problem

#5179 (PR #5218, merged) fixed the nil application-set DoS at the resolution choke point (`lookupApplicationSet`), so `appid.CatalogNames` / config-compile no longer panic on a present-but-nil `ApplicationSets[name]` value. But three **display** paths still dereferenced that same tolerated null slot with no nil guard and panicked the read path:

- `pkg/api/show_text.go` — applications topic, `strings.Join(as.Applications, ...)`
- `pkg/cli/cli_show_security_objects.go` — `showApplications`, `as.Name` filter compare + `range as.Applications`
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_security_text.go` — `showApplications`, `strings.Join(as.Applications, ...)`

`ApplicationSets` is `map[string]*ApplicationSet`; a nil map value is admitted by the tolerant-load / peer-sync path (#1960) that the resolver already tolerates (#5179). Rendering `show configuration applications` / `show security` object dumps over a config carrying such a null slot ran the deref on a nil `*ApplicationSet` — a nil-deref that took down the REST/CLI/gRPC display handler. A DoS on the read path, distinct from the CatalogNames build path #5179 closed.

## Fix

Nil-guard each raw `ApplicationSets[name]` read on the three display surfaces:

```go
as := cfg.Applications.ApplicationSets[name]
if as == nil {
    // #5221: tolerated null slot (#1960/#5179) — skip, don't deref.
    continue
}
```

Matches the #4865 approach (guard each raw value read) and #5179's fail-closed philosophy. A strictly-compiled config never emits a nil slot, so a real application-set renders identically; only the tolerated null slot is skipped. The change is localized to the display path — it does **not** change how application-sets are compiled or stored.

## RED-on-revert evidence

A fail-on-revert test was added per surface — each injects a real + a nil application-set slot into the live `ActiveConfig` and drives the renderer, asserting no panic, the real set rendered, and the nil slot skipped:

- `pkg/api/show_appset_nil_5221_test.go`
- `pkg/cli/cli_show_appset_nil_5221_test.go`
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_appset_nil_5221_test.go`

## PR #5384 — pkg/configstore: enforce config-lock ownership in Store.Annotate (#5379) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5379-configstore-annotate-lock`

Closes #5379

## Problem
`Store.Annotate` (`pkg/configstore/store_command.go`) mutated the candidate
config (`ConfigTree.AnnotatePath`) and refreshed the config-lock idle lease
(`touchConfigLockLocked`) **with no config-lock ownership check**. It was the
one candidate mutator whose body never called `ensureHolderLocked`.

Every sibling candidate mutator (Set/Delete/Deactivate/Activate/Copy/Rename/
Insert/Load*/Rollback/ConfirmCommit) enforces ownership via a session-scoped
`*As` variant that calls `ensureHolderLocked(sessionID)` (#5059). `Annotate`
had **no `AnnotateAs` variant at all**, so a session-scoped caller could not
annotate under holder enforcement, and the structural bypass — annotate another
session's pending candidate and extend the true holder's idle lease with no
ownership check — had no guard.

Verified reproducing on current origin/master (`67598291c`): `Annotate` on
master contains no `ensureHolderLocked` call and no `AnnotateAs` variant exists.

## Fix
Minimal and mirroring the #5059 pattern exactly:

- Add `AnnotateAs(sessionID, path, comment)` that calls
  `ensureHolderLocked(sessionID)` in the same slot the siblings use (between
  `ensureWritableLocked` and the `candidate==nil` check).
- Make the plain `Annotate` delegate to `AnnotateAs("")` — the internal/system
  bypass.

A non-holder session id is now rejected with `ErrConfigLockedByOther`, the
identical sentinel every sibling returns.

The REST `configAnnotateHandler` and the in-process CLI `annotate` dispatch keep
calling the plain `Annotate` (`sessionID==""`), bit-identical to before and
consistent with how those same transports already call the plain
`SetFromInput`/`DeleteFromInput`. `Annotate` is not exposed over gRPC, so no
handler needed threading; the `AnnotateAs` variant exists so a future gRPC
annotate handler inherits enforcement for free like its siblings.

- Extended the canonical `TestStoreMutatorHolderEnforcement` enforcement table
  (`config_lock_holder_5059_test.go`) with an `AnnotateAs` non-holder row.
- New dedicated `TestAnnotateHolderEnforcement` (`annotate_lock_5379_test.go`):
  non-holder -> `ErrConfigLockedByOther` (and asserts the rejected annotation did
  NOT leak into the candidate), holder -> applied (`/* owned */` present), and
  both internal-bypass forms (plain `Annotate` + `AnnotateAs("")`).

`AnnotateAs`:

## PR #5385 — pkg/grpcapi: report PD-only delegated prefixes in GetDHCPLeases (#5382) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5382-grpcapi-dhcp-pd-only`

Closes #5382

## Problem
`GetDHCPLeases` (`pkg/grpcapi/server_dhcp.go`) dropped IPv6 delegated prefixes
(IA_PD) for a **prefix-delegation-only** interface. The standalone PD-only lease
entry was appended only when:

```go
if !attached && len(resp.Leases) > 0 {
```

When the interface has **no IA_NA (address) leases at all**, `resp.Leases` is
empty, so `len(resp.Leases) > 0` is false and every delegated prefix is silently
dropped. A PD-only DHCPv6 client therefore reported an empty lease table, hiding
the delegated prefix during troubleshooting even though vSRX/Junos shows it — a
display/observability parity gap (not a forwarding bug).

Verified against current `origin/master` (`67598291c`): the `len(resp.Leases) > 0`
guard is present and reproduces the drop.

## Fix
- Extract the aggregation into a pure helper
  `buildDHCPLeasesResponse([]*dhcp.Lease, []dhcp.DelegatedPrefix) *pb.GetDHCPLeasesResponse`.
  The RPC method is now a nil-check plus delegate.
- Drop the `&& len(resp.Leases) > 0` constraint so the standalone PD entry is
  appended whenever the prefix cannot attach to an existing inet6 lease —
  including the empty-lease case (`if !attached {`).
- A second delegated prefix on the same PD-only interface groups into the
  standalone entry created for the first (it now matches the attach loop),
  so a multi-PD interface yields one entry, not duplicates.
- Switch the family test from the literal `l.Family == 6` to `dhcp.AFInet6`.

The fix is minimal and consistent with how the pre-existing standalone-entry
path (already used when *other* interfaces had leases) emitted PD entries.

## Test — RED on revert

(no live `dhcp.Manager` / netlink needed):

- `TestBuildDHCPLeasesResponse_PDAttachesToInetLease` — matching inet6 IA_NA
  lease present → PD attaches to it (unchanged path; passes both pre/post fix).
- `TestBuildDHCPLeasesResponse_MultiPDOnlyGrouped` — two PDs on one PD-only
  interface group into a single entry.

## PR #5386 — pkg/cli: bound 'show log' line count to prevent unbounded buffering (#5069) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5069-show-log-unbounded`

Closes #5069

## Problem

`show log [<name>] N` (`showDaemonLog`, `pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go`) accepted
any positive `int` operand with **no upper cap** and fed it straight into
`tail -n N` (file path) / `journalctl -n N` (journald path), then buffered the
entire result via `CombinedOutput` before `fmt.Print`. A view-only (PermView)
account could run `show log 1000000000` and force an O(retained-log-size) heap
allocation plus a management stall — a resource-abuse / DoS vector.

## Fix

Extract a `parseShowLogCount(args, idx)` helper that:

- defaults to **50** when the operand is absent, non-positive, or unparseable
  (Junos-compatible leniency — unchanged behavior for those inputs), and
- clamps any `N` above **`maxTailLines` (100,000 lines)** to the cap.

Both show-log paths (file and journald) now route their count through the
helper, so the value handed to `tail`/`journalctl` is bounded regardless of the
operand.

**Cap value rationale:** reuse the existing `maxTailLines` const already defined
in this package (`cli_dispatch.go`) that bounds the `| last N` ring (#5037).
100,000 lines is far more log than any operator needs interactively, yet caps
the in-process buffer at a fixed size. Using the same const keeps **one**
operator line cap for both PermView log paths rather than introducing a second
magic number — minimal and consistent with the established clamp pattern.

## RED-on-revert evidence

Fail-on-revert test `TestParseShowLogCountCap`
(`pkg/cli/cli_show_log_cap_5069_test.go`) drives the pure helper across both arg
indices (journald `idx 0`, file `idx 1`), asserting the default/leniency
behavior **and** the over-cap clamp. Testing the parse seam needs no real large
log file.

Temporarily removing the `if n > maxTailLines` clamp:

```

```

## PR #5387 — pkg/api: bound BGP routes RIB materialization (#5056) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5056-api-bgp-rib-bound`

Closes #5056

## Problem
The REST BGP routes endpoint (`/api/routing/bgp?type=routes`, `bgpHandler` in `pkg/api/routing.go`) materialized the **entire upstream RIB** before responding. It called `frr.GetBGPRoutes`, which ran `vtysh "show bgp ipv4 unicast"` and buffered **all** of vtysh stdout into one growable string (`realExecutor.Vtysh`) plus a parsed `[]BGPRoute` — hundreds of MB for a full internet table (~1M routes) on a RAM-constrained firewall, **before the first byte went out**.

The prior #4708/#5232 work streamed only the *downstream* writer and added a per-1024-chunk client-cancel check, but:
- the already-completed vtysh work **upstream** was unbounded and uncancellable, and
- the `bw.Flush()` return was discarded, so a downstream **write failure** could not stop the dump.

## Fix — bound the materialization end-to-end
- **`frrExecutor.VtyshStream(ctx, command) (io.ReadCloser, func() error, error)`** — `realExecutor` runs `exec.CommandContext` with a `StdoutPipe`, so stdout is *streamed* rather than buffered, and cancelling `ctx` kills the vtysh process.
- **`Manager.StreamBGPRoutes(ctx, limit, fn)`** (`pkg/frr/status_parse.go`) — scans that pipe with a bounded `bufio.Scanner`, parses each line via the shared `parseBGPRouteLine` helper (extracted from `GetBGPRoutes` so both interpret the table identically), delivers each route to `fn`, stops after `limit` routes (reporting `truncated`), and cancels vtysh on ctx-cancellation or an `fn` error. `GetBGPRoutes` is unchanged — it still backs the CLI/gRPC show paths that render the whole result.
- **`bgpHandler`** now streams via `StreamBGPRoutes` with a `maxBGPRoutes` = **100000** cap:
  - Peak memory is **O(1)** in table size.
  - A client disconnect **or a downstream write failure** (the `bw.Flush()` return is now checked) aborts the scan **and** cancels vtysh.
  - When the cap trips, a trailing `... table truncated at N routes; use the CLI 'show route protocol bgp' for the full table` notice is appended **inside the JSON `output` string** — envelope shape unchanged, present only when truncated, so the non-truncated wire format stays **byte-identical** to #4708.
  - The `200` + envelope prefix is emitted **lazily** on the first route, so an upstream vtysh *start* failure still surfaces as a clean `500`.

The cap is consistent with the existing API bounding convention (e.g. #5069's 100k `show log` cap): a bounded response with a clear truncation indicator.

## RED-on-revert evidence
New fail-on-revert test `TestBGPRoutesEndpointCapTruncates` (`pkg/api/bgp_routes_cap_5056_test.go`) drives the endpoint through the fake-executor seam with a 50-route table and a lowered cap (10), asserting exactly 10 route lines, the truncation notice, the over-cap route absent, and a well-formed envelope.

Disabling the `count >= limit` cap in `StreamBGPRoutes` produced:
```
bgp_routes_cap_5056_test.go:77: rendered 50 route lines, want exactly the cap 10 (endpoint did not bound the table)
bgp_routes_cap_5056_test.go:81: truncation notice missing; a bounded/truncated response must tell the client
bgp_routes_cap_5056_test.go:87: over-cap route 10.0.49.0/24 present in output; table was not bounded
--- FAIL: TestBGPRoutesEndpointCapTruncates
```
Restored → PASS. The existing `bgp_routes_stream_4708_test.go` (wire-format + non-buffering) and `api_ctx_cancel_5232_5233_test.go` (client-cancel abort) now exercise the streaming path too (the api/frr/daemon test fakes gained a `VtyshStream` method) and stay green.

## Validation
- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` — exit 0
- `go test ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/frr/... ./pkg/daemon/... ./pkg/cli/... ./pkg/grpcapi/...` — all pass
- `go vet ./pkg/frr/... ./pkg/api/...` — clean
- `gofmt -l` — clean

## Docs
- `pkg/api/README.md` — `bgpHandler` bullet updated for upstream-streaming + cap/truncation.
- `pkg/frr/README.md` — `vtysh.go` / `status_parse.go` file-table entries and the "no streaming" note updated.

## PR #5388 — pkg/routing: handle per-family failure in route display backends (#5125) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5125-routing-display-perfamily`

Closes #5125

## Problem
The `show route` read backends dump IPv4 and IPv6 independently and
`continue`d on a per-family fetch/convert failure while returning a nil
error. A failed IPv6 netlink or FRR dump alongside a successful IPv4
dump therefore rendered as an authoritative partial/"no routes" result,
so a transient backend failure was indistinguishable from a genuinely
empty table — masking real routing state.

Verified GENUINE on current origin/master (`34dd996be`):
- `pkg/routing/routes.go` — `GetRoutes` / `GetRoutesForTable` per-family
  loops `continue` on error, `return entries, nil`.
- `pkg/frr/status_parse.go` — `GetRouteDetailJSON` `continue`s on both
  the vtysh error and the parse error, then `return all, nil`.

## Fix (minimal, localized to the display/backend read path)
Join per-family failures into the returned error instead of swallowing
them, while still returning whatever family succeeded:

- `routeReader.GetRoutes` / `GetRoutesForTable` `errors.Join` each
  per-family netlink failure with `inet`/`inet6` family context (new
  `familyName` helper) plus the table id, and still return the
  successful family's entries.
- `GetAllTableRoutes` joins the main-table error and each per-instance
  error (tagged with the routing-instance name) instead of silently
  dropping a VRF table on a transient failure.
- `frr.GetRouteDetailJSON` joins per-command vtysh + JSON-parse failures
  (tagged with the failing `show ip/ipv6 route json` command).

Every existing CLI/gRPC `show route` caller already returns on a non-nil
error, so a partial-dump failure now reaches the operator as a clear
diagnostic instead of empty output. The forwarding path is untouched.

seam and assert the error surfaces while the other family's entries are

## Problem
The local CLI `show interfaces` presenter family (terse / detail / extensive / `show vlans` / the summary walk) and the interface-name + unit-number value-hint completers dereferenced present-but-nil `InterfaceConfig` (`map[string]*InterfaceConfig`) and `InterfaceUnit` (`map[int]*InterfaceUnit`) map values with no nil guard.

Those nil slots are admitted on the tolerant / HA-sync config path that the compiler warn-pass already tolerates — `pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_nil_3494_test.go` codifies `"zz-nil-ifc": nil` (nil InterfaceConfig) and a nil `Units[N]` (nil InterfaceUnit) as map values the warn pass must not panic on — so such a persisted/HA-synced config can become the **active** config. Rendering `show interfaces terse` (or triggering interface-name value-hint completion) over it nil-dereferenced. `CLI.Run` has no panic recovery, so the in-process xpfd exits. Same class as the fixed #3476/#3493/#3494 but a distinct unguarded interface/unit map-value set.

## Fix
Mirrors the #5221/#3476 inline `if X == nil { continue }` pattern:

- **completion.go** — skip a nil interface value (`ValueHintInterfaceName`) and a nil unit value (`ValueHintUnitNumber`) before dereferencing `.Description`.
- **cli_show_interfaces_terse.go** — skip a nil interface value at the local and peer range-all loops, a nil unit in every unit loop, and a nil reth-parent lookup; harden the disable-flag and reth-address keyed lookups with `ifCfg != nil` / `unit != nil`.
- **cli_show_interfaces_detail.go / _extensive.go** — skip a nil interface value in the description/map-build loop.
- **cli_show_interfaces_stats.go (`showVlans`)** — skip a nil interface value and a nil unit value.
- **cli_show_interfaces.go** — harden the summary walk's vlan-id and DHCP keyed lookups with `ifCfg != nil`.

Scope is held to the `show interfaces` command family plus interface completion (the named panic surface). The sibling cluster/zones/session views that share the class are left for their own issue.

## RED-on-revert evidence
Fail-on-revert test `pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_nil_5068_test.go` injects a nil interface value, a zone-referenced nil interface, and a nil unit into the live `ActiveConfig`, then drives terse/detail/extensive/vlans/summary and both value-hint completers asserting no panic.

`git stash` of the six source guards (test retained) → the terse presenter panics:
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
  ...cli.(*CLI).showInterfacesTerse(...)
    pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_terse.go:43
--- FAIL: TestShowInterfacesNilMapValuesNoPanic5068
```
Restoring the guards → `ok github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/cli` (both subtests PASS).

Test note: detail/extensive use a no-match filter (the nil-deref map-build loop runs before the name filter) and each presenter runs in its own `captureStdout` call so the `os.Pipe` — drained only after the callback returns — cannot overrun on a many-netdev host.

## Docs
No operator-doc change: behavior for valid configs is unchanged; this is internal tolerant-config robustness, matching the #3476/#3494 precedent that added no doc.

## PR #5392 — pkg/cli: fix 'clear security flow session' argument parsing (#5066) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5066-cli-clear-flow-parse`

## Summary

`clear security flow session summary` (or `brief`, or `sort-by bytes`) parsed clean and **cleared every session on both HA nodes** — a fail-open destructive parse.

The shared show/clear filter parser (`parseSessionFilter`, `pkg/cli/session_filter.go`) recognized the presentation tokens `summary`/`brief`/`sort-by` and set their display flags **without** a parse error. But `hasFilter()` deliberately excludes those three (they are display modifiers, not selectors). On the clear path (`cli_clear.go` `handleClearSecurity` → flow/session) `hasFilter()` therefore returned `false`, and the command fell through to `ClearAllSessions()` **plus** an unfiltered `clearPeerSessions(nil)` — the most destructive path — for a pasted show-syntax token.

The remote `cli` clear parser (`cmd/cli/clear.go`) already rejected these via its `default` case; only the local interactive CLI was fail-open.

## Fix

Give clear a **selector-only** parser. `parseSessionFilter` is split into a shared `parseSessionFilterMode(args, clearMode)` with two entry points:

- `parseSessionFilter` (show, `clearMode=false`) — unchanged behavior, still accepts display modifiers.
- `parseClearSessionFilter` (clear, `clearMode=true`) — `summary`/`brief`/`sort-by` record a parse error instead of setting a display flag.

`hasFilter()` already reports `true` when `parseErr != nil`, so a rejected token routes into `clearFilteredSessions`, whose `validate()` returns the error **before** any iterate/delete/clear-all runs — **neither clear method is invoked**. An *exactly-empty* token list remains the only selector that means clear-all (fail-closed invariant).

Also hardens the **show** path: `sort-by` now validates its key is `bytes` or `packets`. An unknown value previously degraded silently to a plain per-session list instead of the requested top-talkers view; it now fails the command via the existing `showFlowSession` `validate()`.

## RED-on-revert evidence

Fail-on-revert test `pkg/cli/cli_clear_flow_display_reject_test.go` — a `clearCountDP` runtime counts `ClearAllSessions`/`IterateSessions` calls and asserts each display modifier is rejected with **both counters at zero**, that the no-arg clear still calls `ClearAllSessions` exactly once, and that the clear parser rejects the three tokens while the show parser still accepts them (and now rejects an invalid `sort-by`).

Reverting the clear call site to `parseSessionFilter` turns the reject subtests RED:

```
--- FAIL: TestClearFlowSessionRejectsDisplayModifiers/summary
    summary: expected an error rejecting the display modifier, got nil
    (output: "0 IPv4 and 0 IPv6 session entries cleared\n")
--- FAIL: .../brief          (output: "0 IPv4 and 0 IPv6 session entries cleared\n")
--- FAIL: .../sort-by_bytes  (output: "0 IPv4 and 0 IPv6 session entries cleared\n")
--- FAIL: .../filter_plus_summary (output: "0 IPv4 and 0 IPv6 matching sessions cleared\n")
```

i.e. the destructive clear-all fires on a display modifier. Restoring the fix → all PASS.

## Validation

- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` → exit 0
- `go test ./pkg/cli/... ./cmd/cli/...` → all pass
- `gofmt` clean

No cluster smoke: this is a control-plane CLI parse path, and the fix **prevents** a destructive dataplane action rather than changing forwarding.

## Docs

`docs/junos-cli-reference.md` "Security: Flow Sessions" gains a bullet documenting the clear-takes-selectors-only fail-closed invariant.

Closes #5066

## PR #5393 — pkg/routing+frr: surface per-family route-display failure without dropping the partial (#5125) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5125-routing-perfamily-v2`

Closes #5125

## Problem
The `show route` read backends dump IPv4 and IPv6 independently and
SILENTLY SWALLOW a per-family failure (`continue` on error, then
`return entries, nil`). A failed inet6 netlink/vtysh dump alongside a
successful inet4 dump therefore renders as an authoritative "no inet6
routes" — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty table during a
transient backend hiccup, masking real routing state.

Verified GENUINE on current origin/master (`61b216b49`, which already
contains #5387's `StreamBGPRoutes`/`parseBGPRouteLine`):
- `pkg/routing/routes.go` — `GetRoutes` / `GetRoutesForTable` per-family
  loops `continue` on error, `return entries, nil`; `GetAllTableRoutes`
  drops a whole VRF table on a per-instance error.
- `pkg/frr/status_parse.go` — `GetRouteDetailJSON` `continue`s on both
  the vtysh error and the parse error, then `return all, nil`.

## Fix — two layers
The prior attempt (#5388) did only layer 1 and REGRESSED the callers;
this is the redo.

### Layer 1 — backend: join, don't swallow
Join each per-family failure into the returned error (tagged with the
family / table / instance / failing command) while still returning the
family that succeeded:
- `routeReader.GetRoutes` / `GetRoutesForTable` `errors.Join` each
  per-family netlink failure with `inet`/`inet6` family context (new
  `familyName` helper) plus the table id, and still return the
  successful family's entries.
- `GetAllTableRoutes` joins the main-table error and each per-instance
  error (tagged with the routing-instance name) instead of dropping the
  whole VRF table, while still appending every table it could read.
- `frr.GetRouteDetailJSON` joins per-command vtysh + JSON-parse failures
  (tagged with the failing `show ip/ipv6 route json` command).

Contract: **a non-nil error alongside a non-empty result means
"partial"** — callers must render the partial and surface the error.

### Layer 2 — callers: render the partial, warn non-fatally (the part #5388 got wrong)
Once the backend returns a non-nil error on a partial, the existing
callers' `if err != nil { return err }` would break the ENTIRE `show
route` on a transient single-family hiccup — strictly worse than the old
swallow (which at least showed the inet4 partial). Every caller now
renders whatever was returned AND emits a non-fatal `warning: partial
route display (some address families unavailable): <err>` line:

- `pkg/cli/cli_show_routing.go` — `showRoutes`, `showRouteTerse`,
  `showRoutesForInstance`, `showRoutesForProtocol`, `showRoutesForPrefix`,
  `showRouteSummary`, `showRouteDetail`, and the instance-detail route

## PR #5394 — pkg/ddns: preserve foreign records in Route53 UpsertLease (#5389) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5389-route53-foreign-record`

Closes #5389

## Problem

`route53Backend.UpsertLease` issued a **bare full-RRset `UPSERT`** built from a single value. Route 53 `UPSERT` create-or-replaces the **entire** resource-record set at `name+type`, so any co-resident **foreign** member of that RRset — a manually-managed round-robin address, or another host's A/AAAA at the same FQDN — was silently deleted on the next publish/forced-refresh.

This is the Route 53 arm of #3739. The Cloudflare arm (list-then-PATCH the `PrevAddr` row) and the RFC 2136 arm (value-specific `prevSelfOwnedRR` delete) were fixed there; Route 53 was deferred (M07) and never implemented — `grep PrevAddr pkg/ddns/backend_route53.go` had 0 hits on master.

## Fix — ownership-scoped read-modify-write

Route 53 UPSERT/DELETE act on a whole RRset (no per-value add/remove, no compare-and-swap), so both publish and withdraw now first `ListResourceRecordSets`-read the live members and change **only xpf's own value**, mirroring the Cloudflare / RFC 2136 value-specific replace:

- **`listRRSet` (+ `listRRSetsXML`)** — a SigV4-signed GET filtered on an **exact** name+type match, so a Route 53 lexically-next neighbour set reads back as not-found rather than being adopted.
- **`UpsertLease`** — `mergeUpsertValues` keeps every current member **except** xpf's own prior value (`rec.PrevAddr`), adds `rec.Addr`, and UPSERTs the **merged** set. A live set already equal to the desired one (values + TTL) is a no-op; a first publish onto a foreign name is additive; a renumber with a lost prior value leaks a stale xpf row rather than clobbering a foreign one.
- **`DeleteLease`** — strip `rec.Addr` from the live set: absent set / xpf-value-absent ⇒ idempotent no-op (no change issued); foreign members remaining ⇒ UPSERT the reduced set (live TTL); xpf's value the sole member ⇒ DELETE the whole RRset (exact live-TTL match). The #2771 already-gone-DELETE idempotency (`r53DeleteAlreadyGone`) is preserved for the residual race where the record disappears between the List and the DELETE.

`buildChangeBatch` / `change` generalized to take an explicit value list + TTL.

### Concurrency caveat (documented in code + here)

Route 53 has **no compare-and-swap** for `ChangeResourceRecordSets`, so the read-modify-write is **not atomic** — a foreign member written by a human/automation between the List and the change is not observed and would be lost. The Surface A per-RG HA gate makes xpf itself a single writer for the name; the residual race is the same single-writer window the Cloudflare / RFC 2136 value-specific fixes already accept.

## Fail-on-revert tests

`backend_route53_test.go` is rewritten onto a stateful `r53FakeAPI` that models GET-list + POST-change RRset semantics (UPSERT create-or-replace, DELETE exact-match). Foreign-preservation fail-on-revert cases seed a co-resident foreign value and assert it **survives** while xpf's value is set/renumbered/removed:

- `TestRoute53UpsertPreservesForeignRecord`
- `TestRoute53RenumberPreservesForeign`
- `TestRoute53DeletePreservesForeign`

**RED-on-revert proven.** Reverting `UpsertLease` to the bare single-value UPSERT and `DeleteLease` to the bare single-value DELETE:

```
--- FAIL: TestRoute53UpsertPreservesForeignRecord
    UPSERT must carry the merged RRset (foreign + xpf), got 1 values: [{Value:203.0.113.5}]
--- FAIL: TestRoute53RenumberPreservesForeign
    FOREIGN A was clobbered on renumber: [203.0.113.9]
--- FAIL: TestRoute53DeletePreservesForeign
    must not DELETE a shared RRset, got deletes=1
```

Restored to green. Also added idempotent-no-op, ownership-conflict-no-op, absent-idempotent, raced-gone-idempotent, genuine-error-retry, and exact-match-list-filter coverage (14 Route53 tests total).

## Validation

- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` — exit 0
- `go test ./pkg/ddns/...` — ok
- `go vet ./pkg/ddns/...` — clean; `gofmt` clean
- Docs: `pkg/ddns/README.md` file-table entry, the Cloudflare cross-reference, the #3739 per-provider co-resident section (Route 53 moved deferred → implemented), and the #2771 already-gone note updated to describe the RMW + concurrency caveat.
- No cluster smoke — external DDNS control-plane path, no forwarding effect.

## PR #5395 — pkg/cli: fix rollback selector int32 truncation (#5052) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5052-cli-rollback-int32`

Closes #5052

## Problem
The read-only rollback **display** selectors truncated an out-of-range
index through `int32` and silently rendered the **wrong** rollback slot
with a success exit:

- `show system rollback [compare] N` — `cmd/cli/show_system.go`
- `show | compare rollback N` — `cmd/cli/show.go` (`handleConfigShow`)

All three parsed the selector with `strconv.Atoi` then cast `int32(n)`.
On a 64-bit target `strconv.Atoi("4294967297")` succeeds, passes the
`n >= 1` check, then `int32(4294967297) == 1` — so the
`ShowRollback`/`ShowCompare` RPC carried slot **1** while the operator
asked for a different (invalid) selector. The server
(`pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go`) validates only the already-truncated
positive value and cannot reconstruct the pre-truncation int, so it
returns slot 1 as if the request were legitimate.

The mutating `rollback N` path already had the `ParseInt(_,10,32)` guard
(#4868/#3447 in `shared.go`); these three display paths were missed.

## Fix
Per the issue's fix direction — **one shared parser**: add
`parseRollbackSelector(token, usage, min) (int32, error)` in
`cmd/cli/shared.go`, which parses with `strconv.ParseInt(token, 10, 32)`
so an out-of-range value returns `strconv.ErrRange` instead of wrapping.
`min` is `0` for the mutating `rollback` (0 = revert to active) and `1`
for the read-only display/compare selectors that require a positive
history slot. The mutating rollback case is refactored onto the shared
parser and all three display paths route through it; the `int32(n)`
casts on the RPC fields are dropped (the helper returns `int32`).

## Fail-on-revert test
`cmd/cli/show_rollback_int32_5052_test.go` — a recorder client records
`ShowRollback.N` / `ShowCompare.RollbackN`:

- `TestShowRollbackDisplaySelectorOverflowNoRPC_5052` drives all three
  display paths with `4294967297` / `4294967296` / `2147483648` / `foo`
  / `0` and asserts each returns an error with the display RPC issued
  **zero** times.
- `TestShowRollbackDisplaySelectorValidPassthrough_5052` proves valid
  slots (`2`, `3`, and the MaxInt32 boundary `2147483647`) pass through
  **unchanged**.

**RED-on-revert verified:** reverting `show.go`'s compare-rollback site
to `strconv.Atoi` + `int32()` makes the `show | compare rollback`
overflow subtests FAIL — a truncated `RollbackN=1` RPC is issued with a
nil error — while the other two (still fixed) paths and the
valid-passthrough tests keep passing. Restored → all PASS.

## PR #5396 — pkg/api+grpcapi: surface NAT stats read failure instead of healthy-zero (#5046) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5046-nat-stats-readfail`

Closes #5046

## Problem
The REST (`pkg/api/nat.go`) and gRPC (`pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go`) NAT-stats surfaces swallowed dataplane telemetry **read failures** and rendered them as a healthy zero-usage / zero-hit reading with a success status. An operator or monitoring system could not distinguish "NAT genuinely idle" from "NAT stats read failed" — a masked failure.

Four swallow sites defaulted a read error to a clean zero:
- `runtimeSourceNATPools` returned a bare `nil` on `provider.Status()` error (indistinguishable from provider-absent / empty).
- `natPoolStatsHandler`'s legacy `ReadNATPortCounter` fallback kept `used=0` on error (still HTTP 200).
- `natRuleStatsHandler` kept `hitPkts/hitBytes=0` on `ReadNATRuleCounter` error (still HTTP 200).
- gRPC `GetNATPoolStats` kept `used64=0` on `NATPortCounter` error; `GetNATRuleStats` returned `0,0` on `NATRuleCounter` error.

A missing apply-id / absent runtime entry legitimately means "no counter" and stays unflagged. The failure case is distinguishable: the id resolves **and** the telemetry call errors.

## Fix
Fail closed as *unavailable*, matching the #3345/#3408 counter-error contract already enforced on the zone/policy/filter surfaces:
- **REST**: `runtimeSourceNATPools` now returns `(map, error)` and propagates a `Status()` read failure; `natPoolStatsHandler` returns HTTP 500 on that error and on a fallback port-counter read failure; `natRuleStatsHandler` returns HTTP 500 on a rule-counter read failure.
- **gRPC**: `GetNATPoolStats` returns `codes.Internal` on a `NATPortCounter` failure; `GetNATRuleStats`'s `readCounter` helper now returns an error mapped to `codes.Internal` at both the source and destination call sites (matching `GetZones`/`GetPolicies`).
- **Prometheus**: `collectNATPoolMetrics` (`metrics_nat.go`) still OMITS the `xpf_nat_pool_used_ports` sample on a read failure (never a fake 0) but now also bumps the shared `xpf_counter_read_errors_total`; `metrics.go` moves the `collectNATPoolMetrics` call **before** `emitCounterReadErrors` so the bump lands in the same scrape (#3462 ordering).

## Tests (fail-on-revert)
- `pkg/api/nat_counter_error_test.go` — REST 500 on runtime-status / port-counter / rule-counter read failure, plus the Prometheus omit-sample-and-bump.
- `pkg/grpcapi/nat_counter_error_test.go` — gRPC `codes.Internal` on port/rule counter read failure. The gRPC mocks define their own `Telemetry()` routing through the mock, because the embedded `*dataplane.Manager` has a promoted `Telemetry()` that would otherwise wrap the raw Manager and bypass the injected read error.

### RED-on-revert evidence
Stashing the four source files (fixes reverted, tests kept) makes **all 6 tests FAIL**:
- REST `TestNATPoolStatsHandlerSurfacesRuntimeStatusReadError`: `status = 200, want 500` — body `{"success":true,...,"used_ports":0,...,"utilization":"0.0%"}`
- REST `TestNATPoolStatsHandlerSurfacesPortCounterReadError`: `status = 200, want 500` (healthy zero)
- REST `TestNATRuleStatsHandlerSurfacesRuleCounterReadError`: `status = 200, want 500` — `hit_packets:0`
- REST `TestCollectNATPoolMetricsSkipsSampleAndBumpsOnPortCounterError`: `counterReadErrors not bumped`
- gRPC `TestGetNATPoolStatsFailsOnPortCounterReadError`: `returned nil error ... want codes.Internal`
- gRPC `TestGetNATRuleStatsFailsOnRuleCounterReadError`: `returned nil error ... want codes.Internal`

Restoring the fixes → all green.

## PR #5397 — pkg/lldp: serialize Apply/Stop with a lifecycle mutex (#5121) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5121-lldp-lifecycle-mutex`

Closes #5121

## Problem
The LLDP `Manager`'s lifecycle transitions `Apply` (config commit) and `Stop` (daemon shutdown) shared no lifecycle lock. `Apply` writes `m.cancel` and calls `m.wg.Add(1)` per interface; `Stop` reads `m.cancel`, snapshots `m.sessions`, and calls `m.wg.Wait()`. Only `m.mu` guards the neighbor table / sessions — nothing serialized `cancel`, the `WaitGroup`, or the session publish-vs-snapshot across the two calls.

The race is reachable: the daemon shutdown path (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go` `runShutdownSequence`, ~L904) calls `lldpMgr.Stop()` **without** the `applySem` that `reconcileLLDP → Apply` (`daemon_apply.go` ~L2077) runs under. A `SIGTERM` arriving mid-commit races `Stop` against the in-flight `Apply`, producing:
- a **data race on `m.cancel`** (Apply write vs Stop read),
- a **`WaitGroup` misuse** — `Apply`'s `wg.Add(1)` racing `Stop`'s `wg.Wait()` (can panic or drop a goroutine from the join),
- a **session omitted from teardown** — a `Stop` that snapshots the session set before `Apply` publishes a later interface's session leaves that RX goroutine parked in `recv` forever; its fd is never closed, so shutdown hangs and the socket leaks.

Verified genuine on current `origin/master` (worktree base `8f92b07cb`).

## Fix
Add a dedicated `lifecycleMu sync.Mutex` (distinct from `m.mu`) held by `Apply` across the whole teardown-then-rebuild and by `Stop` across the teardown, so the `cancel` access, every `wg.Add` vs `wg.Wait`, and the session publish vs snapshot are atomic w.r.t. the other call. The old `Stop` body moves into an internal `stopLocked()` (caller holds `lifecycleMu`); `Apply` calls `stopLocked()` — not `Stop()` — to avoid re-acquiring the non-reentrant lock.

`lifecycleMu` is never taken by the TX/RX/expiry goroutines (they take only `m.mu`), so holding it across `wg.Wait()` cannot deadlock against the goroutines being joined. Minimal, mirroring how sibling lifecycle managers guard their transitions.

## RED-on-revert (under `-race`)
New `TestApplyStopLifecycleRace` drives two goroutines that hammer `Apply` and `Stop` 300× each concurrently, then asserts a coherent final teardown (`!Running()`, zero residual sessions).

Reverting the fix (unguarded `Apply` with internal `m.Stop()`, and `Stop` without the lock) and running `go test -race -run TestApplyStopLifecycleRace ./pkg/lldp/`:
```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Read at 0x... by goroutine 10:
  github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/lldp.(*Manager).Stop()
      .../pkg/lldp/lldp.go:352   <- reads m.cancel
Previous write at 0x... by goroutine 9:
  ...Manager.Apply -> m.cancel = cancel
... (further races on the WaitGroup / context internals)
--- FAIL: TestApplyStopLifecycleRace
FAIL   (exit 1)
```
With the mutex restored: `ok  github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/lldp`.

## Validation
- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` — exit 0
- `go test -race ./pkg/lldp/...` — pass
- `go test -race -run LLDP ./pkg/daemon/` — pass (day-2 reconcile diff-guard unaffected)
- `gofmt` clean; `go vet ./pkg/lldp/...` clean
- Docs: `pkg/lldp/README.md` gains an "Apply/Stop concurrency (#5121)" section + updated `Apply`/`Stop` entry-point lines.

No cluster smoke — control-plane lifecycle race, no forwarding effect.

## PR #5398 — pkg/snmp: populate IF-MIB ucast counters with unicast not total packets (#5050) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5050-snmp-ucast-counters`

Closes #5050

## Problem

`buildSNMPIfData` copied the Linux `rtnl_link_stats` **total** packet
counts straight into the IF-MIB high-capacity **unicast** counters:

- `ifHCInUcastPkts = stats.RxPackets`
- `ifHCOutUcastPkts = stats.TxPackets`

while separately publishing `ifInMulticastPkts = stats.Multicast`.
`RxPackets`/`TxPackets` include multicast and broadcast frames, so a
manager summing the unicast + non-unicast class columns double-counts
multicast/broadcast. Per RFC 2863 the unicast/multicast/broadcast class
columns must count exactly their named class and must not overlap.

## IF-MIB semantics vs. what Linux exposes

`ifInUcastPkts`/`ifHCInUcastPkts` and `ifOutUcastPkts`/`ifHCOutUcastPkts`
count only packets **not** addressed to a multicast or broadcast address.
Linux `rtnl_link_stats` (via netlink `LinkStatistics64`) reports total
`RxPackets`/`TxPackets` plus a single RX `Multicast` sub-count — it has
**no** RX broadcast count and **no** TX multicast/broadcast breakdown.

## Fix

Extract the stat→counter mapping into a pure `deriveIfCounters` seam and
correct the class semantics:

- **IN unicast = `RxPackets - Multicast`** (clamped at 0 for a racy,
  non-atomic stats read). Exact for the one non-unicast RX subset Linux
  exposes; IN unicast + `ifInMulticastPkts` now reconstructs `RxPackets`
  with no overlap.
- **OUT unicast = `TxPackets`** — a documented **upper-bound
  approximation**. `rtnl_link_stats` exposes no TX class breakdown to
  subtract; the TX non-unicast residual (negligible on a routed firewall)
  is not separable. This is a documented approximation, not a relabelled
  total for a counter we could otherwise split.
- **`ifInMulticastPkts = Multicast`** (unchanged). The broadcast columns
  and the TX class columns stay 0 — the kernel does not report them, and
  an honest zero beats folding those packets into unicast.

`ifTable` columns 11/17 (32-bit `ifInUcastPkts`/`ifOutUcastPkts`) are not
served by this agent (`ifTableColumns = {1,2,3,4,5,7,8,10,16}`), so only
the ifXTable HC unicast counters were affected.

Documented in `pkg/snmp/README.md` (new "IF-MIB class-counter semantics"
section).

## PR #5399 — pkg/cli: reject malformed 'monitor security packet-drop' args (#5051) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5051-cli-packetdrop-parse`

Closes #5051

## Problem

The remote CLI selector parser for `monitor security packet-drop`
(`handleMonitorSecurityPacketDrop`, `cmd/cli/monitor.go`) was **fail-open**:

- value-taking selectors used `if i+1 < len(args)` — a selector with **no value** was silently ignored;
- `source-port` / `destination-port` / `count` parsed with `if v, err := strconv.Atoi(...); err == nil` — a **non-numeric** value silently erased the field to `0` (the wildcard);
- there was **no `default` arm** for unknown tokens.

So `monitor security packet-drop source-port abc` left `SourcePort=0`, opened the stream, and displayed **ALL** drops with a **success exit**. The server's `>65535` range guard (`pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go`) never saw the erased-to-zero value. For an incident-response filter this is a fail-open telemetry-broadening bug (codex-review-177 [A10-b1-F4], cross-refs the #4883 cli fail-open cohort).

## Fix

Mirror the **strict local CLI parser** already present in `pkg/cli/monitor.go` (the same command, interactive surface — the remote CLI copy had drifted fail-open):

- a `needValue(i)` helper returns `"<sel> requires a value"` for a missing value;
- `source-port`/`destination-port` use `strconv.ParseUint(_,10,16)` → reject non-numeric / `>65535` (`invalid source-port %q: must be 0..65535`);
- `count` is range-checked to `1..8192` (`invalid count %q: must be 1..8192`);
- a `default` arm rejects unknown tokens (`unknown packet-drop option: %s`).

Every rejection **returns an error before** `c.client.MonitorPacketDrop` is dialed; the remote CLI dispatch (`cmd/cli/main.go` → `os.Exit(1)`) turns that into a **non-zero exit**. Pass-through string selectors (`source-prefix`, `destination-prefix`, `protocol`, `from-zone`, `interface`, `node`) still forward to the server, which already validates and rejects bad prefixes/protocol/zone/interface — those were never part of the erase-to-zero fail-open, so no redundant local re-validation was added.

## Fail-on-revert test — `cmd/cli/monitor_packetdrop_5051_test.go`

A `MonitorPacketDrop` stub + `fakePacketDropStream` (`Recv → io.EOF`) is added to the shared `fakeBpfrxClient`, so a request that reaches the RPC completes with a **nil** error. `TestRemotePacketDropStrictParse` drives 10 malformed inputs (non-numeric/out-of-range ports, missing values, non-numeric/zero/out-of-range count, unknown-selector typo, unknown trailing token) and asserts each **returns an error with the RPC issued 0 times**, plus a positive case proving a full valid selector set reaches the RPC **once** with the parsed request intact (`sport=1024 dport=443 tcp trust ge-0/0/0 count=10`).

**RED-on-revert VERIFIED:** `git stash` of `cmd/cli/monitor.go` (keeping the new test) makes all 10 reject subtests FAIL — each returns `err = <nil>` (the fail-open success path); restored → all PASS.

```
--- FAIL: TestRemotePacketDropStrictParse/non-numeric_source-port
    handleMonitorSecurityPacketDrop([source-port abc]) err = <nil>, want "invalid source-port"
--- FAIL: TestRemotePacketDropStrictParse/missing_value_trailing_selector
    handleMonitorSecurityPacketDrop([source-prefix]) err = <nil>, want "requires a value"
--- FAIL: TestRemotePacketDropStrictParse/unknown_selector_typo
    handleMonitorSecurityPacketDrop([protcol tcp]) err = <nil>, want "unknown packet-drop option"
  ... (10/10 reject subtests fail on revert)
```

## Validation

- `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` → exit 0
- `go test ./cmd/cli/...` → ok
- `gofmt` clean on touched files
- No cluster smoke: control-plane CLI parse path, no forwarding change.

## Docs

No doc change — the valid selector set is unchanged (`docs/monitor-interface-research.md` lists the same filter options). The fix only converts a silent unfiltered stream into a clean rejection of a malformed/unknown selector.

## PR #5400 — pkg/flowexport: make batch max-depth high-water update race-free (#5048) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-10)

Branch: `fix/5048-flowexport-hiwater-race`

## Summary
Closes #5048.

`flowBatch.add()` in `pkg/flowexport/transport.go` updated the batch
high-water mark (`maxDepth`) *after* `b.mu.Unlock()` with a plain
load-then-store:

```go
if depth > b.maxDepth.Load() { b.maxDepth.Store(depth) }
```

The append that computes `depth` is serialized by `b.mu`, but this
read-modify-write of `maxDepth` runs **outside** the lock. Two concurrent
adders race there: if A observes depth 1 and B observes depth 2, both can
`Load` the older value and pass the compare, then B stores 2 and A's later
store of 1 clobbers it — the published high-water mark **regresses** from 2
to 1 even though a depth of 2 was really reached. Both ops are atomic, so
`-race` reports nothing; the defect is a lost update that under-reports the
worst-case backlog surfaced by `MaxDepth()` on the live NetFlow/IPFIX export
status path.

## Fix
Replace the load-then-store with a lock-free **CAS-max loop** so every update
is an atomic `max(old, observed)`:

```go
for {
    cur := b.maxDepth.Load()
    if depth <= cur || b.maxDepth.CompareAndSwap(cur, depth) {
        break
    }
}
```

- Keeps the mark **monotonic** — a lower late store can never clobber a higher one.
- Stays **outside `b.mu`**, consistent with the sibling `dropped`/`handoffDropped`
  atomics that are also updated outside the lock; `add()`'s critical section is
  unchanged (no added lock contention on the hot flow-close path).

## Tests (RED-on-revert under `-race`)
Added `pkg/flowexport/maxdepth_race_5048_test.go`:

- **`TestFlowBatchMaxDepthMonotonicUnderConcurrentAdds`** — deterministic
  barrier test. A test-only `maxDepthHook` seam (mirroring the existing
  `inflightHook`) parks both adders at the load-then-store window after each
  has `Load`ed 0, releases the higher depth (2) first and the lower depth (1)
  second — forcing exactly the reverse-order store — and asserts the mark stays
  2.
- **`TestFlowBatchMaxDepthConcurrentStress`** — 256 concurrent adders, no
  drain; asserts `MaxDepth() == 256` under `-race`.
