## PR #5983 — cluster: probe IP monitors concurrently [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5301-ipmonitor-parallel-probe`

## Summary

The chassis-cluster monitor probed IP-monitor targets **serially**: `poll()` walked redundancy groups one at a time and `pollIPMonitors` called a synchronous ICMP probe bounded by an 800 ms per-socket read deadline. That deadline bounds one socket, not the aggregate sweep, so an **all-unreachable sweep blocked `len(targets) × 800 ms`** — 64 targets ≈ 51 s. During that single sweep later RGs are starved, the three-failure dampening debt is delayed ~153 s, and `Stop()` waits out the in-progress sweep → **HA failover delayed by minutes during the exact outage the monitor exists to detect** (distinct from #2527 services IP-monitoring and #5080 reconciliation).

## Fix

`poll()` → `pollCycle(ctx)` in three phases:

1. **Snapshot** every IP target across all RGs in stable RG/target order.
2. **Probe** the snapshot **concurrently** through a bounded worker pool (`ipProbeConcurrency = 16`) under an overall cycle deadline.
3. **Apply** the results **serially** in the identical interface-then-IP, RG-by-RG, target-by-target order the old serial code used.

Only the probe I/O moves off the owner goroutine. Phase 3 runs the exact per-target dampening/weight logic (extracted as `applyIPMonitorResult`) in the same order as before, so **the failover decision and weight accumulation are byte-identical → failover-neutral**. The interface link-state pass stays serial (fast local netlink, not the ~800 ms ICMP blocking).

- **`probeICMP` is now context-aware**: a watcher goroutine closes the socket on ctx cancellation so `Stop()` (and the cycle deadline) abort an in-flight probe promptly instead of waiting the 800 ms. It returns `(reachable, completed)`; a probe aborted by cancellation reports `completed=false` and is **skipped** for that cycle (no dampening advance) rather than miscounted as a failure. Per-socket matching + 800 ms deadline behavior otherwise unchanged.
- A cycle that exceeds its deadline records **`IPMonitorCycleOverruns`** and defers (never fails) its unfinished targets.
- A `probeFn` seam (defaulting to `probeICMP`) lets tests inject latency/cancellation without real sockets.

## Tests — fail-on-revert proven

`pkg/cluster/monitor_parallel_5301_test.go`:

- **`TestMonitor_IPProbesRunConcurrently_5301`** — 16 blocking targets complete in ~one probe deadline (0.3 s) via the pool. **RED on revert**: replacing the worker pool with a serial loop takes **4.81 s** (16 × 300 ms) and exceeds the 2.4 s limit → `FAIL`. Restored → `GREEN`.
- **`TestMonitor_IPProbeStableApplyOrder_5301`** — distinct per-address results across two RGs are each applied to their own target (guards result→target misindexing under parallel probing).
- **`TestMonitor_IPProbeCycleOverrun_5301`** — a tiny cycle deadline records exactly one overrun and leaves deferred targets' dampening state + RG weight untouched.
- **`TestMonitor_StopCancelsInflightProbe_5301`** — `Stop()` returns promptly with a probe hung on ctx, proving socket cancellation.

The three existing `probeICMP` callers are updated for the new signature.

## Validation

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/cluster`, and `go test -race ./pkg/cluster` all green. The failover **decision** is unchanged (only probe I/O is parallelized) → failover-neutral, so **no `test-failover` smoke is required** (and the shared loss cluster is shim-wall-blocked anyway).

Docs: updated `docs/feature-coverage.md` (Redundancy-group IP monitoring) with the parallel-sweep behavior.

Closes #5301

## PR #5984 — appid: assign stable name-derived app_id instead of positional [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5296-appid-stable-id`

## Problem (#5296)

The application catalog assigned `app_id` sequentially from 1 in sorted-name order on **every** build (`appid.BuildCatalog` + its `dataplane.compileApplications` twin). An ordinary catalog edit that inserts a name sorting before an existing application **renumbers every later app**: a retained session frozen at `app_id=k` then resolves to the newly-inserted app's name via `ResolveSessionName`'s early `AppNames` map hit, so application-scoped session `show`/filter/`clear` can target the **wrong flows**.

## Fix — Option B (deterministic stable-id), Go-only, no wire/ABI change

- New `config.StableAppID` folds the application **NAME** (FNV-1a → `[1,65535]`), mirroring `config.StableZoneID` which fixed the identical positional defect for zones (#3075).
- A shared `config.AssignStableAppIDs` SSOT is called by **both** producers, so their `AppNames` maps stay byte-identical (the `appid_catalog_parity_test.go` contract) and an id once given to a name is **stable across catalog edits**.
- **Collision policy** for the larger app namespace (~89 fixed predefined + arbitrary user names in the u16 space): predefined apps are a FIXED, mutually collision-free set (frozen by a test), placed first so they always own their slot and never renumber; a user app whose hash collides is displaced to a free slot deterministically, so only the colliding user apps can renumber — never the whole catalog.
- **No wire/ABI change**: `app_id` stays a u16 in the conntrack ABI + HA session-sync wire; the Rust dataplane stamps the Go-assigned id verbatim (**no Rust code change**). No new persisted/synced state — pure function of the name set → both HA nodes + a cold boot compute identical ids by construction.

## Behavior change (display/log-label only — NOT policy/forwarding)

The Rust classifier's same-tier overlap tiebreak (`AppCatalog::lookup_directional`, #3612) picks the lowest `app_id` — a documented proxy for "alphabetically-first name" that only held under positional ids. To keep the AppID-on/off label agreement:

- the AppID-**disabled** Go fallback `resolveTupleFallback` is **re-keyed** to break same-tier ties on the same `StableAppID` rather than alphabetically, and
- `BuildCatalog` now emits catalog entries in **ascending `app_id` order** so the Rust `exact_dst` first-writer-wins dedup also keeps the lowest id (under positional ids name-order == id-order gave this for free).

**Net observable change:** for a session matching multiple overlapping same-tier catalog apps, the displayed app-name label winner changes from "alphabetically-first" to "lowest `StableAppID`" — deterministic, reload-stable, and **identical on the enabled and disabled paths** (parity preserved). Policy matching (`CompiledApplications`) is unaffected.

**Zero-delta alternative for the maintainer (follow-up, not a blocker):** a classify-time `rank` field on the Go→Rust `AppCatalogEntry` snapshot (never stamped/persisted) that Rust ties on would decouple identity from precedence and preserve the exact alphabetical tiebreak — but that is a cross-language change beyond this bounded Go-only fix.

## Cross-language parity fixture (regenerated + binding)

`userspace-dp/tests/fixtures/appid_precedence_v1.json` is **regenerated programmatically** from `BuildCatalog` + `resolveTupleFallback` (`pkg/appid` `TestRegeneratePrecedenceFixture`, `BPFRX_REGEN_APPID_FIXTURE=1`) — no hand-tuned ids/names. A new **binding case** `exact_port_tie_breaks_by_stable_id_not_alphabetical` (two apps on exact tcp/8080 where `StableAppID(aaa-svc)=45553 > StableAppID(ccc-svc)=38751`) makes the fixture FAIL if on/off ever diverge on the label winner — the old fixture lacked such a case (its same-tier case coincided alphabetical==lowest-id).

**Binding proven on both sides:**
- Go: revert `resolveTupleFallback` to alphabetical → `TestAppIDPrecedenceParityFixture/exact_port_…` RED (`= "aaa-svc", want "ccc-svc"`).
- Rust: revert the ascending-id emit order (fixture catalog reordered) → `app_catalog_precedence_parity_fixture` RED (`app_id = 45553, want 38751`).

## Honest residual (documented in code + docs)

Stability is **not** absolute: a user app that hash-collides with an existing USER app can renumber that small colliding set — a **massive** reduction from the positional defect (renumber on ANY earlier-sorting insert), **not** zero. The zero-residual path (versioning application identity in session state) is a cross-language conntrack-ABI + HA-wire flag day = the issue's durable "Required design", deliberately out of scope for this bounded, Go-only fix.

## Fail-on-revert (proven)

- **Positional revert** of `AssignStableAppIDs` → `TestAssignStableAppIDsStableAcrossInsert` + `TestStableIDResolvesRetainedSessionAfterCatalogEdit` RED (existing ids shift; the frozen id resolves to the inserted app — the exact #5296 mis-label).
- **Alphabetical revert** of `resolveTupleFallback` → `TestResolveTupleFallbackTieBreakByStableID` + the fixture binding case RED.
- `TestPredefinedAppIDsCollisionFree` freezes the predefined set; `TestAssignStableAppIDsOrderIndependent` pins HA symmetry; `TestAssignStableAppIDsOverflow` pins the fail-closed u16 boundary.

## Validation

**Go:** `go build ./...` · `go vet ./pkg/appid ./pkg/config ./pkg/dataplane` · `go test -race ./pkg/appid ./pkg/config` — all green. `pkg/dataplane`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/api`, `pkg/cli`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace` pass **except** the pre-existing `TestUserspaceManagerDoesNotImportReflectOrUnsafe` canary, which fails identically on clean `origin/master` (`manager_overlay.go imports reflect`, untouched here — verified in a detached master worktree).

**Rust:** `cargo test --release --bin xpf-userspace-dp app_catalog` → **15 passed, 0 failed** (incl. `app_catalog_precedence_parity_fixture` + `app_catalog_overlap_lowest_id_wins`) against the **unchanged** Rust classifier with the new stable id values. (Ran with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` on disk rather than `/dev/shm` — the latter had only 2.7 G free.)

Closes #5296

## PR #5986 — host-inbound: clear enforced gate on successful teardown [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5790-hostinbound-enforced-teardown`

## Problem (#5790, bug + security — FAIL-OPEN)

The no-enforcement teardown branch of `applyHostInboundFilter`
(`pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go`) — the early path taken when no zone has an
enforceable host-inbound view, there are no addressed-but-unzoned
interfaces, and no junos-host DENY programs — deletes the
`inet xpf_hostinbound` table but **never cleared `d.hostInboundEnforced`**.

That flag means *"a successful real load or address-scoped fallback
established a protecting table."* Leaving it sticky-true after a teardown
that removed the table is a lie: no table is installed.

**Consequence — fail-open.** If a later generation becomes enforceable and
its **first** real nft load fails, the stale `true` takes the day-2
**retention** branch (`!hostInboundEnforced` is false, so the #5644
cold-boot fence is skipped) on the assumption that a retained prior table
still protects the addresses. But the table was torn down — there is no
retained generation — so host-bound services to newly reachable
firewall-local addresses become reachable with **no host-inbound
default-deny**.

## Fix (bounded)

After `nftDeleteTable` **succeeds** on the teardown path,
`d.hostInboundEnforced.Store(false)` before returning. With no table
installed the historical premise no longer holds, so a subsequent
first-install failure now routes through the `!hostInboundEnforced`
cold-boot fence path (fail closed).

- A teardown **failure** returns *before* the Store and **preserves** the
  flag — a table the delete could not remove may still be installed and
  protecting the addresses; clearing it there would be the opposite error.
- All three flag transitions are serialized under `applySem`, so the false
  publish cannot race a later apply's true publish.
- The two `Store(true)` sites (real-load success, address-scoped fallback
  success) and the zero-drop-fallback-leaves-false path are unchanged.

## Tests — fail-on-revert proven

`pkg/daemon/host_inbound_teardown_enforced_5790_test.go` drives the full
**install → teardown → failed-reinstall** ordering on the real
`applyHostInboundFilter` path through the existing `nftApplyPayload` /
`nftDeleteTable` package fakes:

- **Primary**: install (flag true) → non-enforceable config tears the
  table down (assert flag **FALSE**) → enforceable config whose real load
  **fails** must take the cold-boot fence path (a fence payload is emitted
  denying the enforced wan v4+v6 addresses; flag re-establishes true).
- **Contract guard**: a **FAILED** teardown must **NOT** clear the flag.

## PR #5987 — cluster: gate IP-monitor failover on global-threshold [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5271-ipmonitor-global-threshold`

## Summary

`pollIPMonitors` installed each failed IP-monitor target's `weight` as an **independent** RG election debt via `SetMonitorWeight`, and the configured ip-monitoring **`global-threshold` was parsed, typed, and tested but never read** in `pkg/cluster`. Cumulative-threshold failover suppression was unimplemented → **a single probe loss could move services**. On a group with `global-threshold 200`, `global-weight 100`, one weight-50 target failing dropped the RG weight 255→205 and could trigger failover even though the cumulative reachability-loss threshold (200) was never reached — a split-brain/availability risk and a vSRX-parity divergence.

## Fix (vSRX semantics)

Implement the Junos chassis-cluster ip-monitoring cumulative-threshold state machine:

- Per-target dampened failed/up state is still tracked **independently**.
- When an RG configures **`global-threshold > 0`**: a per-target transition no longer installs a per-target debt. `applyRGIPMonitorThreshold` sums the weights of the RG's currently-down targets and installs a **single** synthetic debt equal to `global-weight` **only while that sum ≥ `global-threshold`**, clearing it when the sum falls back below. Below the threshold **no** election debt is applied. The aggregate debt uses a distinct per-RG monitor name (`"ip-monitoring"`) that never collides with per-target `"ip:<addr>"` or interface-monitor names, and fires `SetMonitorWeight`/`RecordEvent` only on a real crossed↔cleared transition.
- When **`global-threshold` is unset (0)**: the historical **independent per-target** behavior is preserved **exactly** — each unreachable target subtracts its own weight (or `global-weight` fallback) immediately.

The #5301 concurrent-probe structure is unchanged (parallel probe, serial stable-order apply); the threshold gate lives entirely in the apply phase.

The existing `TestMonitor_IPMonitoring` **encoded the bug** (threshold 200 + one weight-50 target expecting 255→205); it's updated to drop the threshold so it exercises the independent (threshold-unset) path with its original assertions intact.

## Tests — fail-on-revert proven

`pkg/cluster/monitor_globalthreshold_5271_test.go`:

- **`TestMonitor_GlobalThresholdGatesFailover_5271`** — the issue's exact scenario: cumulative 50 < 200 → **stays 255**, 150 < 200 → stays 255, 200 ≥ 200 → **155** (255 − global-weight 100), recovery below threshold → **255**. **RED on revert**: removing the threshold-gate branch makes the first weight-50 failure deduct immediately (255→**205**), failing the sub-threshold assertion (confirmed in-run). Restored → GREEN.
- **`TestMonitor_GlobalThresholdUnsetIsIndependent_5271`** — byte-identical per-target debt (255 → 215 → 185) with no threshold.
- **`TestMonitor_GlobalThresholdPerRGIndependence_5271`** — one RG crossing its threshold does not leak into another sub-threshold RG.

## Validation

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/cluster`, and `go test -race ./pkg/cluster` all green.

**Failover-decision change:** this deterministically changes the failover decision and is fully unit-covered. The destructive cluster failover smoke (`test-failover`) is **shim-wall-blocked** on the shared loss cluster and is recorded as **no-regression** — the decision change is deterministic and exercised by the tables above.

Docs: `docs/feature-coverage.md` (Redundancy-group IP monitoring) updated with the global-threshold gate semantics.

Closes #5271

## PR #5989 — host-inbound: fence day-2 coverage gaps with an additive table [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

## Problem (#5789, security fail-open — deeper follow-up to #5790)

`hostInboundEnforced=true` proves only that SOME protecting host-inbound
table loaded at SOME earlier generation. It does **not** prove the
RETAINED (atomic-untouched) nftables generation covers the CURRENT
desired destination-address set. Two fail-open paths remain after

1. A previously-addressed zone gains another static/DHCP/SLAAC address.
   The next real render fails; atomic nft retention keeps the OLD

2. A successful addressless **program-only** install stores
   `enforced=true` with **zero covered addresses**. An address later
   appears and a failed rerender skips the cold-boot fence on the
   `enforced=true` premise, even though the retained table denies no
   address.

The sticky boolean cannot distinguish retained-generation **coverage**
from mere table **existence**.

## STEP-0 assessment: bounded

Judged **bounded** (not needs-decision) because multi-table input-hook
composition is an already-established, tested pattern here — `xpf_lo0`

(#3364). A third `xpf_hostinbound_gap` table at prio 11 is
architecturally consistent, not novel.

- **`Daemon.hostInboundCoveredAddrs`** — the set of firewall-local
  destination addresses (`"<fam>|<addr>"`) the retained enforcement (last
  successful real load OR address-scoped cold-boot fence) drops. Set on
  success, **unchanged on failure** (atomic retention keeps the old
  generation), **cleared on a successful teardown** (composes with
  #5790).
- On a failed rerender while `enforced=true`, diff desired-drop vs
  covered; for any UNCOVERED destination install an **additive gap
  fence**: a SEPARATE `inet xpf_hostinbound_gap` base chain at
  `nftHostInboundGapPriority` (11), strictly after `xpf_hostinbound` (10)
  — itself after `xpf_lo0` (0) — denying **only** the uncovered addresses
  (same mandatory L3 / return admits as the cold-boot fence via the
  shared `hostInboundFenceMandatoryAdmits`). Being a separate table it
  does **not** replace `xpf_hostinbound`, so the retained generation's

## PR #5991 — upgrade: reject '%' in the pinned-ExecStart version grammar [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5713-version-sink-aware`

## Problem (#5713, codex-review-182 M41, Medium/security)

The in-place upgrade pins the daemon's ExecStart to the concrete versioned binary via a systemd drop-in — `flip.go:writeUnitDropin` templates `ExecStart=/var/lib/xpf/versions/<ver>/xpfd` into `10-xpf-version.conf`. That `<ver>` is gated by `upgrade.ValidateVersionSegment` (`cutover.go` validates `TargetVersion`/`PreviousVersion`/`stagedVer` before the flip).

`ValidateVersionSegment` rejected path-escaping input (`/`, `..`, leading dot, whitespace, control, non-ASCII) but treated the version as a bare filesystem path segment and accepted every other printable ASCII — **including `%`**. `%` is a **systemd unit specifier** (`%i`, `%n`, `%h`, `%%`). A crafted/format-drifted version like `%i` or `1.0%n` therefore **passed validation, landed in the pinned ExecStart, and was expanded by systemd** — silently rewriting `argv[0]` to an unintended binary **after the upgrade STOP**. The shell parity twin (`debian/xpf.preinst:is_safe_segment`, `tr -d '[:graph:]'`) accepted `%` the same way.

## ⚠️ Scope correction — the M41 sink is Go + shell, NOT Python

The issue named the *direction* ("build/deploy tooling"), not the exact sink. The systemd-exec-path sink is the **upgrade version grammar (`pkg/upgrade`) + its shell parity twin (`debian/xpf.preinst`)** — not the Python `scripts/` tooling. `bake.py` / `xpf-deploy.py fetch` only substitute the version into **artifact file names** (`xpf-<ver>.qcow2`), never a systemd ExecStart. That Python artifact-path concern is a *separate* path-traversal gap, split out to **#5992** (see Related) to keep this PR focused on the M41 systemd sink.

## Fix — sink-aware strict allowlist, fail-closed (Go + shell parity)

- `ValidateVersionSegment` tightened from a permissive "reject the bad" filter to a strict **allowlist**: accept only `[A-Za-z0-9]` plus `. _ + ~ - :`, `default`-reject everything else. Debian/semver versions carry exactly those (`1:2.3.4-1` epoch, `1.0.0~beta1`, `1.0.0+build.7`, `v1.2.3`), so nothing legitimate is rejected; `%` and the other systemd argv metacharacters (`$`, `"`, `'`, `\`, backtick, glob `* ? [ ]`, `;`, `=`, `,`) are refused **before substitution**.
  - *Not* the issue's literal `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]$` regex — that rejects the repo's legitimate `:` (epoch) and `~` (pre-release) Debian versions in the valid-test set. (Endorsed by review.)
- `debian/xpf.preinst is_safe_segment` switched to the **char-for-char identical** allowlist (`tr -d 'A-Za-z0-9.:+~_-'`) to preserve the documented Go↔shell validator-parity contract.
- `ValidateKernelSegment` docstring corrected (it asserted `ValidateVersionSegment` permits `* ? [ ] " \`).
- `docs/in-place-upgrade.md` updated with the sink-aware version-grammar note.

## Caller safety (no legit version regresses)

All `ValidateVersionSegment` callers source `xpfd version` output / staged / journal versions (`cutover.go` ×3, `runtime/seed.go`, `system_linux.go`) — all git-describe or Debian-shaped (`1.2.3-5-gabcdef`, `1:2.3.4-1`). None legitimately contains a now-rejected char, so the tightening rejects nothing a real upgrade flow produces.

## Fail-on-revert (proven both sides)

- **Go** (`pkg/upgrade/version_test.go`): `%i`, `1.0%n`, `100%`, `%%`, `$`, `"`, `\`, backtick, `*`, `;`, space, `,`, `=` added to the rejected set; every existing valid version still asserted ACCEPT. Reverting the allowlist `default`→permissive makes all rejects accepted (`ValidateVersionSegment("%i") = nil, want error`) → RED; restored → GREEN.
- **Shell** (`test/debian/preinst-safe-segment-test.sh`, NEW): sources the real `is_safe_segment` out of `debian/xpf.preinst` (not a copy) and asserts accept(legit)/reject(`%`+metachars) under `sh` and `dash`. Reverting the shell `tr` set to `[:graph:]` → the `%`/`$`/`"`/backtick/`*`/`;` cases accepted → RED; restored → GREEN.

## Validation

`go build ./...` · `go vet ./pkg/upgrade` · `go test ./pkg/upgrade/...` — all green. `debian/xpf.preinst` maintainer-script tests (`preinst-migrate`, `preinst-besteffort`) pass with legit versions (`1.0.0` / `0.9.0+deb1`) still accepted. New shell parity test green (sh + dash). `make selftest`: **38 passed, 0 failed** (incl. `test_xpf_deploy_pathsafety.py`).

## Related

- **#5992** — separate Python artifact-path traversal (`xpf-deploy fetch` / `bake.py` substitute an unvalidated `--version` into `os.path.join` write paths). Split out to keep this PR focused on the M41 systemd sink.

Closes #5713

## PR #5993 — deploy: validate --version before it names artifact paths [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5992-deploy-version-pathsafe`

## Problem (#5992, security path-traversal — Python `scripts/`)

`xpf-deploy.py` `fetch` and `bake.py` substitute an operator-supplied `--version` straight into artifact **write** paths under the output dir — `os.path.join(out, f"xpf-{ver}.qcow2")` and its `.incus-metadata.tar.gz` / `.SHA256SUMS` / `.minisig` siblings — **with no validation**:

```
xpf-deploy.py fetch --version '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' --out /tmp/dl ...
# dst = os.path.join("/tmp/dl", "xpf-../../../../etc/cron.d/x.qcow2")  ->  escapes --out
```

`os.path.join` does not neutralize an embedded `..`, so the download is written outside `--out`. This is **inconsistent** with the same file's `--name` / `--image`, which already pass through `validate_identifier` / `_SAFE_IDENT` (the #4905-B path-escape hardening). Split out from #5713 (the systemd-ExecStart version sink, which was Go+shell).

## Fix — validator approach (and why)

Added a `validate_version(value, field)` (`_SAFE_VERSION`) to **both** tools, with the **same fail-closed discipline as `validate_identifier`** (reject absolute path / separator / leading dash, then an allowlist regex). I did **not** reuse `_SAFE_IDENT` — its `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` charset is too strict for a version (forbids `+`/`~`) and would reject legit `1.0.0+build.7` / `1.0.0~rc1`.

**Charset: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+~-]*`** — accepts git-describe (`1.2.3-5-gabcdef`) and semver (`1.0.0+build.7`, `1.0.0~rc1`); rejects `/`, `\`, `..`, absolute paths, leading `.`/`-`, whitespace, `%`, and shell metacharacters. It **mirrors `pkg/upgrade.ValidateVersionSegment`** (the #5713 systemd sink) with one deliberate difference: it **drops the Debian epoch `:`** — an epoch is never part of an artifact *filename* (dpkg encodes `:` as `%3a`), and `:` in `xpf-<ver>.qcow2` would confuse the incus image alias / tooling. The filename sink's needs differ from the systemd exec-path sink (as the task anticipated).

- `fetch` validates `args.version` up front **and** routes the download write through the existing `contained_join(out, name)` realpath-containment belt (defense-in-depth).
- `bake.py` validates `a.version` right after arg parse.
- The two tools are invoked independently from different dirs (each has its own `die()`), so rather than a fragile cross-dir import they each carry the small validator, **pinned in parity** by `test_bake_version_pathsafe.py::test_charset_parity_with_deploy` (both must accept/reject the same set).

## Fail-on-revert (proven)

`test_xpf_deploy_pathsafety.py` gains `ValidateVersionTests` (accept/reject lists) + `FetchVersionSinkTests`. Reverting **both** gates (the `validate_version(args.version)` call **and** the `contained_join` write) makes `cmd_fetch` accept a `../../…` version and, in dry-run, resolve the escaping `dst` without raising → `test_fetch_rejects_traversal_version` flips **RED**; restored → GREEN. `bake.py`'s validator is covered by `test_bake_version_pathsafe.py`.

## Validation

`test_xpf_deploy_pathsafety.py` (16 tests) + `test_bake_version_pathsafe.py` (3 tests) pass. `make selftest`: **39 passed, 0 failed** (both new tests auto-discovered). Python-only — no Go change.

## Related

- **#5713** — the systemd-ExecStart version sink (Go `pkg/upgrade` + shell `debian/xpf.preinst`), already merged. This PR is the Python artifact-path sibling.

Closes #5992

## PR #5994 — nat: represent SNAT tuple-unknown out-of-band for protocol 0 (#5687) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5687-nat-proto0-sentinel`

## Summary

Fixes #5687 (codex-review-182 finding M04). SNAT used the protocol value `0`
as an in-code "L4 tuple unknown" sentinel, colliding with the real IPv4
protocol number 0 (HOPOPT). A genuine protocol-0 packet reached
`match_source_nat_result_for_tuple` (via `match_source_nat_for_flow_result_at`,
`afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs`) with `forward_key.protocol == 0`, was misclassified
as tuple-unknown, and took the **synthetic round-robin path** (`try_next_port`,
`rewrite_src_port: Some(_)`) that mints **no reverse-identity occupancy token**
— instead of the real port-less address-only path (`reserve_address_only`) used
by GRE/ESP/OSPF. So a real HOPOPT flow's reverse tuple could not be
matched/disambiguated (the #5269 collision hole, but for protocol 0), breaking
reverse translation for protocol 0.

## Fix (bounded, out-of-band sentinel)

Represent the protocol **out-of-band** as `Option<u8>` at the
`match_source_nat_result_for_tuple` boundary:

- `None` = tuple unknown (the address-only `match_source_nat` wrapper)
- `Some(0)` = real HOPOPT
- `Some(n)` = any other real protocol (TCP=6, UDP=17, ICMP=1, …)

Decode once at the top (`tuple_unknown = protocol.is_none(); protocol =
protocol.unwrap_or(0)`), gate `port_less` on `!tuple_unknown` (was `protocol
!= 0`), and thread `tuple_unknown` into `SourceNatRule::matches` → `l4_matches`
(was keyed on `protocol == 0`). A real HOPOPT is now port-less like GRE/ESP: it
takes the real address-only path, mints the reverse token, and preserves the
wire source port (`rewrite_src_port: None`).

### Map-key layout: UNCHANGED

The `SourceNatFlowKey.protocol` reverse-index key stays `u8` (the real value, 0
for HOPOPT), so the in-map / HA-sync tuple **key layout is byte-identical for
ALL protocols** — only the in-code "is this unknown?" test moved out-of-band.
**No wire / HA ABI change.** Normal-protocol (TCP/UDP/ICMP) tuple
representation, hash, and equality are untouched.

## Tests (fail-on-revert, cargo)

- `pool_snat_protocol0_hopopt_is_real_address_only_not_unknown_5687` — a HOPOPT
  SNAT flow mints a reverse-identity token, preserves the wire port, and a
  colliding second HOPOPT flow to the same remote is DENIED as exhaustion while
  a different remote disambiguates (owner keyed on real protocol 0).
- `pool_snat_unknown_tuple_distinct_from_real_hopopt_5687` — the `None` unknown
  wrapper keeps its synthetic round-robin, no-token behavior; `Some(0)` HOPOPT
  mints a token; `Some(6)` TCP still PATs (no regression).

**Proven RED on revert:** reintroducing the `protocol == 0` classification
(`let tuple_unknown = protocol.map_or(true, |p| p == 0)`) sends a real HOPOPT

## PR #5995 — dist: validate apt base URL before signing install.sh (#5685) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5685-release-url-validate`

## Bug (#5685, M40 — supply-chain / signed root shell injection)

`scripts/dist/publish.py stamp_installer` took a lower-trust config input
(`--apt-base-url` / `XPF_APT_BASE_URL`) and substituted it **literally** into
`install.sh`, which is then **signed** with minisign and piped to `sudo sh` on a
fresh host (the Tier-A `curl … | sudo sh` one-liner):

```python
text = text.replace("%%XPF_APT_BASE_URL%%", apt_url)   # unvalidated
```

The marker lives inside a **single-quoted shell literal** in `install.sh`:

```sh
XPF_APT_BASE_URL_BAKED='%%XPF_APT_BASE_URL%%'
```

so a single quote in the URL breaks out of the literal and the tail becomes
signed, root-executed shell:

```
--apt-base-url "https://x.invalid/apt'; rm -rf / #"
  ->  XPF_APT_BASE_URL_BAKED=''; rm -rf / #'
```

The unvalidated value crossed the **signing trust boundary** — a
malformed/attacker-influenced apt URL became signed, root-run shell, and the
release signature attests to whatever was stamped in. Confirmed present on
`origin/master` (`e60e23cd5`); not stale-fixed.

## Fix — validate BEFORE the signing/stamping boundary, fail CLOSED

`validate_apt_url(value)` is called at the top of `stamp_installer` (before any
substitution / key read), so a bad value aborts the release with the installer
**never written or signed**. It requires a strict `https://` URL and rejects in
two layers:

1. **per-character denylist** — any shell metacharacter, quote, whitespace,
   control byte, `%`, or `=` (a `%%` pair would also defeat install.sh's
   unsubstituted-marker guard);
2. **structural allowlist** via `urllib.parse.urlsplit` — scheme must be
   `https`, netloc a bare `host[:port]` with **no** userinfo, and no query /
   fragment / non-allowlisted path character.

An apt base URL is a bare `dists/`+`pool/` directory host, so it never needs
userinfo, a query, a fragment, or a percent-escape; the narrow charset
(`[A-Za-z0-9._~-]` + `/` in path + `:` for port) cannot host a shell breakout.
Mirrors the `validate_identifier` / `validate_version` fail-closed idiom in
`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py`, widened to a URL-appropriate charset (a plain
identifier allowlist is too strict for a URL).

## PR #5996 — Use O(N) HashSet dedup for DemoteOwnerRGS cancelled keys [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5155-demote-dedup-hashset`

## Problem (#5155, perf — packet-worker failover stall)

`handle_demote_owner_rgs`
(`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/commands/demote_owner_rgs.rs`)
deduplicated every demoted session key against the accumulated
`cancelled_keys` with a **linear** scan before pushing:

```rust
if !cancelled_keys.iter().any(|key| key == &demoted_key) {
    cancelled_keys.push(demoted_key);
}
```

`SessionTable::demote_owner_rg` yields **unique** keys, so every `.any()`
scan walks to the tail of the growing `Vec` — the whole demote pass is
**O(N²)**. At `max_sessions` = 131072 that is **~8.6e9 `SessionKey`
comparisons on the packet worker**, run ahead of the `heartbeat.store()`
at the end of the command loop → a multi-second failover-time stall on
the very thread that must resume forwarding. (Not a dup of #4069.)

## Fix (O(N) — internal dedup structure only)

Keep a companion `rustc_hash::FxHashSet<SessionKey>`
(`cancelled_keys_seen`) for an O(1) membership test:
`set.insert(key.clone())` returns `true` only on first sight, so the
pass is **O(N)**.

- **Behavior identical.** `cancelled_keys` stays a `Vec`, so
  first-occurrence output order is preserved for the downstream
  `cancel_queued_flow_on_binding` / `delete_session_map_redirect_for_session`
  iteration (and the #1346 dispatch order-pin test). Same set of keys, no
  duplicate processing. **No session-map key, wire, or protocol change.**
- The set is threaded from the caller (`apply_worker_commands`) alongside
  the Vec so the dedup persists across the multiple `DemoteOwnerRGS` arms
  in one dispatch loop. The dedup is **load-bearing, not
  belt-and-braces**: `demote_owner_rg` only flips origin to `SyncImport`
  and does not clear the owner-RG bucket, so a repeated `Demote{[rg]}`
  re-discovers the same key.
- Not pre-sized — common no-demote ticks pay no allocation; demotions are
  a cold failover path. `FxHashSet` matches the crate's hasher convention
  (`rustc_hash` already used in `nat/`, `event_stream/`, …).

## Test — fail-on-revert (proven)

New `apply_worker_commands_demote_dedup_is_linear_not_quadratic` installs
**N=48000** unique sessions on one inactive owner RG, issues one
`DemoteOwnerRGS`, and asserts:
- exactly N unique keys cancelled (dedup drops/duplicates nothing), **and**
- the pass completes in **< 3s** (`session_map_fd = -1` makes the per-key
  publish early-return, so the O(N²) scan dominates the revert).

destination — into one slice, and only `BuildPBRRules` **then** truncated
it to `maxPBRRules` (`config.PBRRuleWindow = 1000`) via
`rules[:maxPBRRules]`.

So the 1,000-rule cap engaged **after** the whole product was already
built. A config whose dimensions multiply to millions of tuples
exhausted memory/CPU **during** expansion, before the cap protected
anything — the cap did not bound the blow-up it was meant to bound.
`BuildPBRRules` runs on the daemon **apply** path (`daemon_apply.go` step
3d) **and** on the `PBRBuildStats` **Prometheus scrape**
(`pkg/api/metrics_counters.go`), so a crafted or merely large PBR stanza
was a commit/apply/scrape exhaustion vector.

Confirmed live on `origin/master` e60e23cd5 before the fix.

## Fix — enforce the cap DURING expansion

`buildPBRFromFilter` now takes a remaining-window **budget** and, BEFORE
the nested loop, computes the term's product **size** from the resolved
dimension lengths (`pbrTermProduct` — O(dimensions), saturating multiply
capped at `maxPBRRules+1` so it cannot overflow `int`). A term whose
product would push the running total past the budget is **dropped whole**
— the same fail-safe under-steer to the main table as the #3730
unrepresentable / #4534 contradictory drops — with a degraded error
naming the offending filter/term and its product-vs-cap. An overflow flag
stops `BuildPBRRules` feeding further attachments once the window is full.
**The full product is never allocated.** The terminal
`rules[:maxPBRRules]` truncation is kept as a defense-in-depth no-op belt.

A **pkg/config commit-check gate was deliberately not added**: pkg/config
cannot import pkg/routing without a cycle, so a commit-side gate would
have to duplicate routing's drop semantics (DSCP-0 drop, unrepresentable
-term drop, prefix-list expansion, empty-set skip). An over-count there
would falsely reject a legitimate under-cap config; the in-emission guard
is exact by construction, drift-free, and protects **every**
`BuildPBRRules` caller (apply + scrape), not just commit.

A config **under** the cap expands **byte-identically** (the guard never
fires) — no regression for legit PBR.

## PR #5998 — routing: carry qualified-next-hop preference into the AF_XDP snapshot (#5678) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5678-qnh-snapshot-pref`

## Problem (#5678, routing-semantics M12, codex-review-182)

A static route's **qualified-next-hop preference** — the Junos floating-static idiom, a primary next-hop plus a less-preferred backup (`qualified-next-hop <gw> { preference N; }`, #3871) — was **lost when the route was lowered into the AF_XDP snapshot**.

`buildRouteSnapshots` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go`) collapsed **every** next-hop of a route onto **one** `RouteSnapshot` at the single route-level `Preference`, dropping the per-next-hop admin distance carried on the qualified backup (`NextHopEntry.HasPreference`/`Preference`). The backup was therefore installed at **equal cost** to the primary, and the Rust FIB **load-balanced (ECMP) across both** instead of using the backup only as a standby. Traffic that should egress only the primary was silently split to the backup — a silent routing-semantics change.

The FRR/kernel path already renders this correctly (#3871, `pkg/frr/config_render.go` emits one `ip route` line per next-hop at `dist = nh.Preference` when `HasPreference` else the route-level distance); only the AF_XDP snapshot boundary dropped it.

## Fix — bounded, no schema change

Group a route's next-hops by their **effective preference** (the qualified `nh.Preference` when `HasPreference`, else the route-level `Preference`) and emit **one `RouteSnapshot` per distinct preference**.

The backup then arrives as a **separate, higher-preference route** for the same prefix. The Rust FIB's existing same-prefix tie-break (#2390 `sort_routes`: descending prefix length, then ascending preference, with first-match `routes.iter().find(prefix.contains)`) **selects the primary and holds the backup as a standby entry** that is never reached while the primary route is present.

This reuses the **existing per-route `Preference` wire field** — the snapshot schema already supports same-prefix multi-preference routes and the Rust FIB already honors them, so **no snapshot-schema or Rust change is required**. (This is why it is a bounded patch, not the larger link-state design proposal in the issue thread — that proposal concerns automatically *activating* the backup on primary next-hop failure, a separate, larger question.)

- Next-hops that **share** a preference (a plain `next-hop [ a b ]` list, or qualified next-hops at the same distance) still collapse to **one equal-cost ECMP snapshot** — real ECMP is unaffected.
- Discard, reject, and next-table routes carry no forwarding next-hop and emit the base disposition unchanged.

## Test — fail-on-revert

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes_qnh_preference_5678_test.go`:

- **Floating static** (primary + qualified backup at preference 250) → lowers to **two distinct-preference snapshots**, each with a single next-hop; the backup is strictly less preferred. Reverting the preference-carry folds both into one ECMP snapshot (`NextHops:[10.0.0.1 10.0.0.2] Preference:5`) → **RED**.
- **Same-preference qualified next-hops** stay ECMP with each other, distinct-distance tier is a separate standby → **RED** on revert.
- **Plain `next-hop [ a b ]` list** → still one equal-cost ECMP snapshot → **GREEN** across the revert (no regression).

Validation: `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean; `go test -race` green for `pkg/dataplane/userspace`, `pkg/config`, `pkg/routing`, `pkg/frr`.

Closes #5678

## PR #5999 — daemon: run HA sync invalidators on best-effort tail error [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5564-syncapply-invalidators`

## Summary

On the HA receive side, `syncAndApply` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go`) promotes
the peer config to active (`configstore.SyncApply`) and arms the dataplane
snapshot (`applyConfigLocked`) **before** it runs the three session invalidators
(`clearSessionsForPolicyChanges`: the #4234 deletion-clear, the modified-policy
re-eval, and the #4342 default-policy change). It returned early on **any**
`applyConfigLocked` error, so a **non-fatal** best-effort tail failure
(host-inbound/lo0 nft, networkd, …) skipped the invalidators. Surviving
established sessions then kept forwarding under their **old** authorization on an
armed standby — a security **fail-open**: a session a peer-tightened/deleted
policy should now deny keeps flowing under the stale decision, eligible to
forward immediately at failover.

Because `SyncApply` already promoted the incoming text to active, the primary's
equal-active-text re-push hits `handleConfigSync`'s fast path
(`activeText == incomingText`) and returns success without re-entering
`syncAndApply`, making the omission **permanent**. The commit path
`applyAndSyncCommitted` already handled this correctly (classify via
`applyErrSkipsPeerSync`, still run the invalidators for a non-fatal tail error);
the receive path had diverged.

## Fix

Mirror the commit path:

- Capture the apply error instead of early-returning on any error.
- Return early **only** for the two fatal classes `applyErrSkipsPeerSync`
  matches — a required-protocol-gate error (dataplane **disarmed**, #2138) and a
  daemon-stop context abort (#2926) — where the config is not live-forwarding and
  there is no session state to invalidate. On those, discard the config (nil) and
  return the error with **no** spurious invalidation (preserves existing fatal
  behavior).
- For every other (non-fatal tail) error the config reached active + the snapshot
  is armed, so run the invalidators and **surface** the tail error joined with any
  #5578 partial-invalidation error rather than swallowing it.
- The invalidation runs from a **deferred, guarded** (`armedActive`) block on a
  named-return function so a future early-return added between the apply and the
  invalidators cannot re-introduce the skip. `deviceMapPassiveAdmissionAlarm`
  moves into the same block.

Control-flow fix only — no wire/protocol/failover-machinery change.

`p-first` id-0 + `p-web` id-1 committed active) and a fake dataplane holding v4+v6
established sessions under `p-web`; the peer text deletes `p-web`.

## Problem (#5151, perf — zero-allocation warmed-packet-path invariant)

`impl Default for FilterResult` set `forwarding_class: Arc::<str>::from("")`,
which allocates an Arc header/data block on **every** `FilterResult::default()`.
That default is the accumulator init for the full v4/v6/lo0 filter evaluators
(`evaluate_filter_ref_counted_v{4,6}`, etc.), so every full filter evaluation on
the packet path (session-miss / cache-sensitive) paid an empty-Arc allocation.

`TxSelectionFilterResult` and `CachedTxSelectionFilterResult` already meet the
zero-alloc invariant with `Option<Arc<str>> = None`. `FilterResult` was the
inconsistent hold-out.

- `FilterResult.forwarding_class`: `Arc<str>` → `Option<Arc<str>>`, default `None`
  (zero-alloc). `None` is semantically identical to the historical empty `""`
  ("no forwarding-class").
- The **only** write site — `merge_matched_modifiers` in `filter/engine/eval.rs`,
  where a matched term's forwarding-class is folded into a `FilterResult`
  accumulator — wraps the clone in `Some(...)`, so the Arc is cloned **only when
  a term actually sets a forwarding-class** (allocation on a match, never on the
  default).

No production code reads `FilterResult.forwarding_class`:
- The CoS forwarding-class classification path uses the dedicated TxSelection

- The only readers are **3 tests**, migrated from
  `result.forwarding_class.as_ref() == "x"` → `.as_deref() == Some("x")`.

`FilterResult` is a pure in-process eval result (`#[derive(Clone, Debug,
PartialEq, Eq)]`, **not** `#[repr(C)]`, not serialized, not HA-synced, not a map
struct) — **no wire/serialized/map struct touched.**

## PR #6001 — daemon: flush stale kernel host-inbound conntrack on tightening (#5566) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5566-hostinbound-conntrack-flush`

## Summary
Fixes #5566 — a host-inbound **security fail-open** on the direct-kernel delivery path.

The `inet xpf_hostinbound` chain leads with `ct state established,related accept`, which precedes every per-zone coarse host-inbound catch-all DROP, and replacing the `xpf_hostinbound` table does **not** flush Linux netfilter conntrack. So removing a host service (SSH/HTTPS/SNMP/…) left an **existing direct-kernel connection authorized under the OLD config**: the leading established-accept short-circuits the new drop, producing no host-inbound deny counter/log. The Rust userspace local-delivery path already re-checks the effective host-inbound set on every session hit and tears a now-denied session down (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs`); the kernel path had no equivalent teardown.

## STEP-0 (verified vs origin/master `d9cb7d1ff`)
- `buildHostInboundFilterPayload` emits `ct state established,related accept` before the per-zone coarse drops (both the no-program `else` branch and, as the residual established accept, the `to-zone junos-host` program branch).
- Table replacement (`add`/`delete`/redefine) does not flush conntrack → stale authorization survives a tightening. Bounded, not a design fork.

## Fix
A conntrack **reconcile** at the tail of `applyHostInboundFilter` (new `pkg/daemon/host_inbound_conntrack_flush.go`). After a successful real table load, delete every established/related kernel conntrack entry whose original-direction destination is a **covered** firewall-local host-inbound address (the #5789 `desiredDrop` set — lifelines `fxp0`/`em0`/`fab*` are excluded from the views, so never eligible) and whose `(proto, dport)` the **current** coarse rules no longer admit. The next original-direction packet is then re-evaluated and dropped by the per-zone catch-all instead of riding the established-accept — mirroring the Rust per-hit teardown.

Key properties:
- **Reconcile, not a delta.** Flush condition = "not admitted by the CURRENT config", derived from the SAME structured SSOT the nft chain renders from (`config.HostInboundServiceMatch` / `HostInboundProtocolMatch`), so the admit decision cannot drift. Still-permitted services are never flushed (no reset regression); no-op on loosening/unchanged commits; no prior-config snapshot persisted.
- **Lifeline-safe.** Only covered default-deny addresses are eligible; management/cluster-control lifelines are never flushed. Addressed-but-unzoned addresses (#4420) are covered with an empty admit set.
- **Global exemptions preserved** — ESP/AH (50/51), ICMP ND/PMTUD/echo, and the #5582 WireGuard listen port are never flushed.
- **Best effort.** NEW-connection enforcement is already applied, so a conntrack-subsystem flush failure is logged (WARN), not surfaced as a commit failure.
- **Seam.** `conntrackDeleteFilters` package var wraps `netlink.ConntrackDeleteFilters` (netlink is already a direct dep; no `conntrack-tools` binary dependency). Kernel netfilter conntrack here tracks only host-terminated/kernel-forwarded flows (transit runs through userspace-dp's own session table), so the swept table is small.

## Tests — fail-on-revert
`pkg/daemon/host_inbound_conntrack_flush_5566_test.go`:
- **Matcher** — now-denied ssh (tcp/22) flushed; still-permitted snmp (udp/161), an allows-all zone, a lifeline address, ESP/AH, ICMP, WireGuard, and transit destinations all preserved (v4 + v6).
- **End-to-end wiring** — a tightening apply (remove ssh, keep snmp) drives the reconcile with a filter that flushes the ssh flow and preserves the snmp flow.
- Verified RED on revert: neutering the matcher **and** removing the flush call each fail the suite. `go test -race ./pkg/daemon` green; `go build ./...` + `gofmt` clean.

## Docs
`docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md` (new "Stale kernel authorization on a tightening (#5566)" section + established/related row note) and `_Log.md`.

Closes #5566

## PR #6002 — nat: reach embedded-ICMP NAT reversal on the flowless poll path (#5690) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5690-embedded-icmp-reversal-reachable`

## Problem (#5690, codex-review-182 M07)

The generic embedded-ICMP NAT reversal (`try_embedded_icmp_nat_match` →
`build_nat_reversed_icmp_error_v4/v6`) reverse-translates the inner quoted
packet of an ICMP error so an error referencing a NAT'd flow reaches the real
internal host. It was wired **only** into the flow-backed session-miss arm of
`poll_binding_process_descriptor` (`if let Some(flow)` → `if is_embedded_icmp_error`).

But a non-query ICMP error is **flowless by construction**:
`parse_session_flow_from_bytes` (#3290) discards the metadata pseudo-port for
every non-query ICMP type, so `parse_session_flow` returns `None` and the packet
takes the flowless `else` arm — it never enters the flow-backed arm (query and
error types are disjoint via `icmp_identifier_bearing`, so a flow-backed ICMP
packet is always a query/echo). `is_embedded_icmp_error` was therefore
**structurally always false** where the reversal lived: the reversal was dead in
production. The helper unit tests call `try_embedded_icmp_nat_match_from_frame`
directly and bypass the dead poll control flow → **tested-but-not-live**. A real
ICMP error for a NAT'd flow was never reverse-translated on the production path.

## Why the suppression exists (preserved)

The XDP shim stamps `bytes[l4+4..l4+6]` as `flow_src_port` for *every* ICMP type
with no query gate; #3290 discards it for non-query ICMP so the ungated control
word can't seed a bogus identifier-keyed session (session-table pollution /
spurious collisions). That flowless routing is **correct** and this change does
not touch it.

## Fix (control-flow reachability; no tuple/map-key/wire change)

Extract the reversal into `poll_descriptor/embedded_icmp.rs`
(`try_reverse_embedded_icmp_error`, flow-independent) and call it **first** in
the flowless arm — the path these errors actually take. A match
reverse-translates and queues the error as a `Prebuilt` forward toward the
client and consumes the descriptor; a miss / no-source-rewrite / unbuildable
frame / CoS-drop falls through (or fail-closed recycles) to normal flowless
enforcement. The pending forward carries `flow_key: None`, so the non-query
error never becomes a session/flow-cache authority — the #3290 no-fake-session
invariant is **preserved, not bypassed**. CoS classifies with `flow_key = None`
too (a synthesized L3 reply has no trustworthy 5-tuple → port-bearing terms fail
closed). The now-dead flow-backed reversal block, its `is_embedded_icmp_error`
compute, and the always-false `!is_embedded_icmp_error` caching guard are removed
(behavior-preserving; logic de-duplicated into the one helper).

an inbound NAT44 SNAT ICMP Time-Exceeded (addressed to the firewall SNAT

and asserts **exactly one** queued `Prebuilt` reversed forward with the outer
destination, inner source, and inner source port restored to the pre-NAT

## PR #6003 — cluster: order IPsec/DHCP full-set sync by (incarnation, seq) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5706-ha-fullset-sequence`

## Problem (#5706, HA correctness M32)

IPsec SA sync (`syncMsgIPsecSA`) and DHCP-server lease sync
(`syncMsgDHCPLeaseV4/V6`) are **full-set pushes** — each message REPLACES the
peer's held set wholesale. Both fabric connections (`conn0`/`conn1`) run their
own `receiveLoop` goroutine, so a peer's frames are processed by two concurrent
**redundant streams**. A full-set delivered OUT OF ORDER across those streams
(or a reordered/duplicated stream) could overwrite a newer set with an older one
— a state **regression**: a torn-down tunnel resurrected on the standby, a
released lease revived. Unlike sessions (#2170) and config (#3931), these
full-sets carried no sequence, so nothing rejected the reorder.

Confirmed live on origin/master `f15869f89`: the IPsec/DHCP receive handlers
applied the incoming set unconditionally (`peerIPsecSAs = names` /
`storePeerDHCPLeases`).

## Fix (peer-incarnation + per-type monotonic sequence; reject regressions)

Each full-set now carries a trailing `(incarnation, seq)` framing, mirroring the
#3931 config-generation trailer:

```
[ base payload ][ fullSetSeqMagic (8B) ][ incarnation (8B LE) ][ seq (8B LE) ]
```

- **incarnation** = the sender's process epoch (`syncEpoch`, the
  CLOCK_MONOTONIC construction seed — constant per boot; a process restart draws
  a strictly-greater epoch and supersedes).
- **seq** = a **per-type strictly-monotonic** counter. IPsec, DHCP-v4 and
  DHCP-v6 draw from INDEPENDENT counters, so a v4 push never gates a v6 one and
  an IPsec seq never gates a DHCP one. Per-peer is implicit (2-node cluster, one
  peer; the two fabric conns are two paths to the same peer).

The receiver keeps a `fullSetSeqGuard` high-water per stream
(`ipsecRecvSeq`/`dhcpV4RecvSeq`/`dhcpV6RecvSeq`, guarded by `recvSeqMu` because
both receiveLoops touch them) and admits only a strictly-newer `(incarnation,
seq)` — lexicographic, a higher incarnation always supersedes. A stale reorder
is DROPPED and counted (`IPsecSAStaleIgnored` / `DHCPLeasesStaleIgnored`) with
the held set untouched.

**Both sides** (wire-protocol-both-sides): the SENDER stamps
(`QueueIPsecSA`/`QueueDHCPLeases` → `appendFullSetSeq`), the RECEIVER compares
(`handleMessage` → `stripFullSetSeq` → `fullSetSeqGuard.admit`).

**Cross-boot / rebooted peer**: an OS reboot restarts the monotonic epoch lower,
so the per-stream guards are `reset()` on a peer bulk re-prime (`resetRecvGen`,
fired on the reconnect `BulkStart`) — the rebooted peer's fresh re-advertised set
is then admitted (the #2198 F2 stale-RETAIN inverse, applied to full-set sync).

## PR #6004 — nat: fail closed when interface SNAT has no egress address [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5688-interface-snat-no-egress-drop`

## Problem (#5688, Rust NAT security/correctness M05)

Interface-mode source NAT translates the source to the **egress interface's own address of the packet's family**. In `match_source_nat_result_for_tuple` (`userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs`) the `interface_mode` branch resolved `rewrite_src` from `egress_v4`/`egress_v6` and returned `SourceNatLookup::Matched` **unconditionally** — including when that address was `None`:

```rust
let rewrite_src = match src_ip {
    IpAddr::V4(_) => egress_v4.map(IpAddr::V4),
    IpAddr::V6(_) => egress_v6.map(IpAddr::V6),
};
return SourceNatLookup::Matched(NatDecision { rewrite_src, .. }); // rewrite_src may be None!
```

A `Matched` decision carrying a `None` source rewrite forwards the packet **UNTRANSLATED**. So a v4 packet whose egress interface has no v4 address (or a v6 packet with no v6 egress address) leaked its **private/internal source onto the egress** — the exact leak interface SNAT exists to prevent. Confirmed live on origin/master `04e1527ab` (provenance M05, `fc479ca65`).

## Fix (fail closed)

When the same-family egress address is absent, return `SourceNatLookup::Unavailable(SourceNatFailureReason::InterfaceNoEgressAddress)` (new runtime-only reason, exception string `source_nat_interface_no_egress_address`) instead of `Matched`-with-`None`. That funnels through the **same drop / `nat_alloc_fail` disposition** (`record_source_nat_failure` in `poll_descriptor/nat_exception.rs`) a pool-mode allocation failure takes — so the flow is dropped **and counted**, with consistent telemetry.

- **Disposition-only** change (`Matched` → `Unavailable` on the no-same-family-egress-address branch). **No NAT tuple / map-key / wire layout change.**
- Families resolved **independently**: a v4 packet checks the v4 egress address, a v6 packet the v6 one.
- **Working case preserved**: egress HAS a same-family address → still translates (no regression).

## Validation

- `cargo test --release` **full suite: 3945 passed / 0 failed**.
- **Fail-on-revert proven**: reverting to `Matched`-with-`None`-rewrite turns `interface_source_nat_no_v4_egress_addr_fails_closed` and `interface_source_nat_no_v6_egress_addr_fails_closed` **RED**, while the no-regression / dual-stack test `interface_source_nat_translates_when_same_family_egress_addr_present` stays **GREEN**.
- Smoke deferred (loss-cluster shim-wall) — unit-covered fail-closed.

Docs: `userspace-dp/README.md` source-NAT semantics bullet + `_Log.md`.

Closes #5688

## PR #6005 — routing: reject per-instance next-table, drop userspace-only leak [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5830-per-instance-nexttable`

## Problem (#5830)

A static `next-table` route authored **inside a routing-instance** was accepted at commit, but the three forwarding surfaces diverged:

- **Validator** — `validateNextTableTargetReferencesStrict` (the #5693 definedness gate) inspected only the **global** `inet.0`/`inet6.0` routes, so an undefined per-instance target bypassed the commit-time protection.
- **Kernel/FRR** — `daemon_apply` feeds only `cfg.RoutingOptions.Static/Inet6StaticRoutes` to `ApplyNextTableRules`, and `pkg/frr/config_render.go` renders nothing for a `NextTable` route → the per-instance route was **omitted entirely**.
- **Userspace FIB** — `buildRouteSnapshots` **published** it as a live `NextTable` route in the instance's `<inst>.inet[6].0` table.

Net effect: the same committed config **leaked traffic in the userspace dataplane** while the kernel/FRR view had no equivalent route (a control-plane/data-plane split-brain), and undefined per-instance targets sidestepped #5693.

## Direction chosen: (A) reject-consistently

Per-instance next-table is **not a supported/programmed feature**. The kernel `ip rule` the applier installs is a global destination-only `to <dst> lookup <table>` with **no source-table scoping**; honoring a per-instance leak would need source-table-scoped (`iif`/fwmark) rules — the same substrate the rib-group VRF→VRF import target is deferred to **Phase 2** for. Appending per-instance routes to the global `ApplyNextTableRules` call would lose source-table identity and could steer traffic from unrelated VRFs (the issue warns against exactly this). Full parity (B) is therefore a **feature-add, out of scope**; the userspace publish is the bug.

The fix makes all three surfaces agree that per-instance next-table is **not a live forwarding route**:

1. `validateNextTableTargetReferencesStrict` now **hard-rejects at commit** ANY next-table under a routing-instance (defined or undefined target; an undefined target is additionally named). Strict on commit / commit-check; downgraded to a warning on tolerant load / peer-sync via the existing `lenientNextTableRefs` flag (#1960 no-brick) so an already-persisted or peer-synced legacy config still boots.
2. `buildRouteSnapshots` no longer publishes a per-instance next-table (a `perInstance` guard in `addRoutes`). **Global** next-table IS programmed via `ip rule` and stays published so the Rust FIB can cross-reference the target table. A leniently-loaded legacy per-instance next-table is thus inert on **both** planes.

## PR #6006 — daemon: join RG reconcile loop before HA ownership cleanup (#5681/M23) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5681-ha-reconcile-shutdown-join`

## Summary

Fixes codex-review-182 finding **M23** (High, HA correctness): the redundancy-group (RG) reconcile safety-net goroutine was not joined before shutdown ownership cleanup, so a late reconcile pass could re-assert mastership after the node had begun relinquishing ownership → transient dual-master / blackhole window on planned shutdown or failover.

## Root cause

`Run()` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go`) spawned the reconcile loop as a **bare goroutine**:

```go
if d.cluster != nil {
    go d.reconcileRGStateLoop(ctx)   // NOT registered on the run WaitGroup
}
```

Unlike the sibling DDNS / proxy-ARP / Surface-A reconcile loops immediately above it, this loop used no `wg.Add(1)` / `defer wg.Done()`, so `runShutdownSequence`'s `wg.Wait()` did **not** join it. `stop()` cancels the loop's `ctx`, but with no join a tick already past the `case <-ctx.Done(): return` select — or blocked mid-pass in `reconcileRGState` on a control-socket `SetRGActive` — can complete **after** `wg.Wait()` returns, during the later HA ownership-relinquish phase (`rg_active` clear → RA withdraw → direct-mode VIP removal → VRRP `Stop`), and re-enable forwarding / re-add VIPs.

## Fix

Extract the spawn into a `startReconcileRGStateLoop(ctx, *wg)` helper (matching the codebase's `startHTTPServer` / `startGRPCServer` / `stopPinRetryLoop` lifecycle-helper convention) that does the `wg.Add(1)` / `defer wg.Done()` wrap exactly like the sibling loops. `Run()` calls it under the existing `if d.cluster != nil` guard.

**Ordering verified:** every ownership-relinquish step in `runShutdownSequence` runs strictly **after** `wg.Wait()` (line 990), so registering the loop on the run WaitGroup is sufficient — no explicit cancel+join-before-teardown seam (the #5308 `stopPolicySchedulerLoop`/`stopPinRetryLoop` pattern) is needed, because the reconcile loop binds the run/signal `ctx` (cancelled by `stop()`), not the never-cancelled `d.daemonCtx`.

**No shutdown behavior removed:** quiescing the safety-net loop early is correct — the VRRP BACKUP transition during shutdown is driven by `watchVRRPEvents` (deliberately on `context.Background()` so it outlives ctx cancel), **not** the reconcile loop.

## Ordering caveat

A reconcile pass's `SetRGActive` uses `context.Background()` (deliberate — the BPF map update must complete), so an in-flight pass at cancel time delays the join by that pass's duration. This is bounded in the normal case (local BPF map update + unix-socket control send under `m.mu` — the same primitive the already-wg-registered sibling loops use) and backstopped by the systemd unit `TimeoutStopSec=20`. Registering on `wg` is strictly safer than the prior bare-`go`, which let the pass run *concurrently with* cleanup.

## Fail-on-revert test (merge gate)

New `pkg/daemon/ha_shutdown_reconcile_join_5681_test.go` binds the ordering invariant: it holds one reconcile pass in-flight (injectable `reconcileTickHook`, routed through the new `reconcileRGStatePass` wrapper), spawns through the production `startReconcileRGStateLoop` seam, cancels ctx, then asserts `wg.Wait()` does **not** return while the pass is in flight and **does** return once it completes.

Reverting `startReconcileRGStateLoop` to a bare `go` (dropping `wg.Add`/`wg.Done`) turns it **RED**:

```

--- FAIL: TestReconcileRGStateLoopJoinedBeforeOwnershipCleanup_5681 (0.00s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/daemon	0.029s
```

Restored → GREEN.

- Full `pkg/daemon` suite GREEN under `-race` (23.9s).

## PR #6007 — HA config-sync: reconcile the config-push invariant to desired state (#5863) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5863-ha-configsync-reconcile`

## Root cause

Config replication to a reconnecting cluster peer was **edge-triggered only** by the `OnPeerConnected` callback (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go`). That callback skipped the push when the node was **not RG0 primary** at connect time OR had been up **<30s**, and *nothing re-evaluated the skipped work*:

1. Session-sync connects while this node is secondary (or at uptime 10s) → the callback skips the push.
2. The node later becomes RG0 primary (or uptime reaches 30s) while the connection stays up.
3. No new connect edge and no commit occurs → the peer retains stale active config **indefinitely**.

The RG0 promotion handler (`applyRG0OwnershipTransition`) re-initiated IPsec SAs and nudged DHCP lease-sync but did **not** push/reconcile config, and the 30s threshold had **no** timer callback.

## Fix — reconcile to desired, not a second edge

The bug is an edge-triggered gate over **persistent state** (config authority + peer connectivity + post-boot stability). Rather than bolt on a second edge (a push on promotion) with its own ordering gaps, the push is modeled as **reconciliation to a desired state**.

`reconcileConfigSyncToPeer` re-evaluates the invariant on every input change:

> *this node is the RG0 config authority (`rg0ConfigSyncAuthority`) AND stable (uptime ≥ 30s) AND a peer is connected AND config sync is enabled AND the current config generation has not already been pushed on this peer's current connection*

…and pushes **only when desired-vs-actual diverges**. It is invoked on:
- **(c) peer (re)connect** — `OnPeerConnected` (the existing callback, rewired).
- **(a) RG0 promotion** — hooked into the existing `applyRG0OwnershipTransition` StatePrimary path.
- **(b) crossing the 30s stability threshold** + safety net — a low-frequency `configSyncReconcileLoop` that wakes exactly at the stability threshold and thereafter on a coarse 30s tick to recover any dropped promotion/connect edge.

This mirrors the discipline of the sibling nudges (`nudgeDHCPLeaseSync` / `nudgeIPsecSASync` / `advertiseIPsecSAOnce`): RG-master-gated and idempotent.

## Control-socket safety (CLAUDE.md rule)

The config push is heavy and the userspace control socket is shared (status poll, HA sync, session installs, snapshot sync). The reconcile is **deduped by a `(peer-connection-epoch × config-generation)` marker** so it pushes **at most once per connection per generation**:
- `syncPeerConnEpoch` is bumped on each (re)connect, so a fresh connection re-receives the config even if the generation is unchanged; a stale connection's marker never matches the new epoch.
- The commit-path push (`pushConfigToPeer`) records the same marker, so a subsequent reconcile is a no-op (no duplicate push after a commit).
- Every already-satisfied evaluation is a cheap no-op (state gates + one FNV hash of the config text, **no `QueueConfig`**), so a safety-net tick or a burst of triggers cannot storm the socket or starve session installs during bulk sync.
- Per-tick reconcile traces use `slog.Debug`; only an actual push logs `slog.Info`.

## No regression of the #2239/#4385 no-overwrite guard

The reconcile stays **RG0-primary-gated** exactly like the old connect edge (`rg0ConfigSyncAuthority`), so a reconnecting **SECONDARY** still never overwrites the authoritative primary's config. The receiver-side rejection (`handleConfigSync` → `errConfigSyncRejectedPrimary`) is untouched.

## Fail-on-revert tests (merge gate)

New `pkg/daemon/configsync_reconcile_5863_test.go` reproduces the ordering bug and guards the regressions, driving promotion + uptime transitions against a real store (config-sync enabled) and counting pushes via a seam:

- `PushesAfterPromotion` — connect while **secondary** → 0 pushes; **promote** with connection up → exactly 1 push; further ticks → still 1.
- `PushesAfterStabilityCrossing` — connect while primary but **uptime 0** → 0 pushes; **cross 30s** → exactly 1 push.
- `HappyPathPushesOnce` — primary + stable + connected → exactly 1 push across 10 ticks (no storm).
- `SecondaryNeverPushes` — reconnecting secondary → 0 pushes across 10 ticks (no authoritative-overwrite).
- `DisconnectedSkips`, `ReconnectRepushes` (new epoch → re-push), `ConfigChangeRepushes` (new generation → re-push), and `ReconcileLoop_FiresOnStabilityCrossing` (loop end-to-end).

**Fail-on-revert proven firsthand.** Neutralizing the reconciler (early `return` at the top of `reconcileConfigSyncToPeer`) → RED:

## PR #6008 — vrrp: clamp gratuitous-arp-count burst budget (#5695 M16) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5695-garp-count-cap`

Closes #5695

## Root cause (codex-182 M16, Medium/security)
The chassis-cluster / RETH `gratuitous-arp-count` leaf carried
`ValidateIntegerMin(1)` — a **minimum only, no maximum** — and had **no
runtime upper bound**. A large configured count scheduled an effectively
**unbounded per-VIP raw-socket send budget on failover**: each VIP fans out
the full count, and the burst helper fans `(count-1)` follow-up frames over
`(count-1)*50ms`. A pathological count (e.g. `100000`) is ~83 minutes of raw
GARP/NA sends **per VIP across every VIP** — a self-inflicted CPU/socket
exhaustion vector.

Grepped all consumers (`GARPCount` / `GratuitousARPCount`): the two **live**
send sites are `pkg/vrrp/instance.go` `sendGARP` (RETH/standalone VRRP) and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go` `directSendGARPs` (direct-mode cluster). The
`pkg/cluster` `m.garpCounts` map is **written but never read** (dead), so it
needs no clamp.

## Fix — doctrine-aligned
Respects the **no-schema-only-caps doctrine** (`schema_chassis.go`, PR #1845:
*"Junos caps at 16, but enforcing that here would reject configs the runtime
executes fine; a sanity cap belongs in the runtime first"*).

**1. PRIMARY runtime clamp (closes M16).** New `config.GratuitousARPBurstClamp
= 32` + `config.ClampGratuitousARPCount`. Both send sites clamp the effective
burst count and `slog.Warn` **once** when they clamp (per-instance
`atomic.Bool` in vrrp; per-RG mutex-guarded map `warnGARPClampOnce` in
daemon — **never per-send**, per the logging rules for the per-failover path).

**Clamp value = 32, rationale:** `2×` the Junos `1..16` documented maximum.
Every legitimate config (the deployed `8`, the Junos max `16`, plus generous
over-provisioning to `32`) passes through **unchanged** — the clamp never
alters a count an operator could plausibly intend. It hard-bounds the per-VIP
budget to 32 raw-socket sends and a `~(32-1)*50ms ≈ 1.55s` burst tail. Beyond
~16 frames a GARP/NA burst adds no neighbor-cache benefit, so the headroom is
pure safety.

**2. Commit-side signal (defense-in-depth — option a).** New AST pre-walk gate
`validateGratuitousARPCountAST` in `runPreWalkGates` emits a **WARNING, never a
hard reject**, when a configured count exceeds the clamp — the operator learns
the value will be clamped at runtime. This keeps the doctrine (a runtime-valid
count is never rejected at commit; mirrors the #1960 lenient/warn posture). A
count in `1..32` is silent. **I chose option (a) over the absurd-bound
hard-reject (b)** because the runtime already clamps a too-large count *fine*,
so a warning gives the operator the signal without ever rejecting a config the
runtime executes — the cleaner operator experience and the stricter reading of
the no-schema-only-caps doctrine.

the existing `arpProbeFn` seam) so tests capture the effective burst count with

## PR #6009 — frame: saturate 16-bit length casts in the AF_XDP dataplane (#5765) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5765-u16-lencast-hardening`

## Summary

Four `... as u16` casts on packet/segment/frame lengths in the Rust
`userspace-dp` would silently **wrap** for a length > 65535 (65536 → 0),
forging a plausible-but-wrong pseudo-header / total-length / payload-length
field. Per the `claude-spark-review-002` cohort (#5765), all four are
**unreachable-for-wrap on current master** — an AF_XDP frame is bounded by the
UMEM frame size, and an IPv4 `total_length` is itself a 16-bit field — so this
is pre-emptive **defense-in-depth**, not a live bug fix.

The fix adds one shared saturating-narrowing helper, `saturate_len16(usize) ->
u16` (`u16::try_from(len).unwrap_or(u16::MAX)`), mirroring the
validated-narrowing newtype idiom already used at the forwarding-build trust
boundary (`VlanId`/`TunnelTtl`/`QueueId` in
`afxdp/forwarding_build/validated.rs`). The valid (<64K) path is
**byte-identical** to the old cast — a legitimate packet checksums and injects
unchanged. Only the (unreachable) >64K case changes, from a silent wrap to a
deterministic saturate that can never masquerade as a small valid length.

## Per-site disposition

| # | Site | Disposition |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | `frame/checksum.rs` `checksum16_ipv4` (IPv4 pseudo-header length) | **HARDENED** — reachable-in-principle (returns plain `u16`); fail-on-revert tested directly at the function boundary with a synthetic 65540-byte payload. |
| 2 | `frame/mod.rs` ×3 TCP/UDP checksum-verify pseudo-headers (incl. `CSUM_BAD` debug block) | **HARDENED** via the shared helper. Structurally capped by the u16 `ip_total_len` wire field → unreachable at the `verify_checksums` boundary; coverage rides on the shared-helper test. |
| 3 | `coordinator/inject.rs` (`frame_len.min(u16::MAX)`) | **LEFT AS-IS** — already saturating + gated upstream by `check_inject_packet_length` (#2443, rejects oversize). Touching it would be churn and risk regressing a correct fail-closed path. |
| 4 | `frame/tcp.rs` SYN-cookie reply builders (IPv4 total_length / IPv6 payload_length) | **HARDENED for idiom-consistency, but truly unreachable-for-wrap even at the boundary**: `write_syn_cookie_tcp_header` hard-rejects any `tcp_len ∉ {20,24}` (returns `None`) *before* a reply is emitted, so `total_len ≤ 44`. Guarded that structural gate with tests (oversized `tcp_len` → `None`) rather than a vacuous saturate test. |

## Fail-on-revert (the merge gate)

Neutralizing `saturate_len16` to the bare `len as u16` and re-running the new
tests:

```
running 6 tests

test ...::syn_cookie_reply_v4_in_range_length_is_exact ... ok
test ...::syn_cookie_reply_v4_rejects_oversized_tcp_len ... ok
test ...::syn_cookie_reply_v6_rejects_oversized_tcp_len ... ok
test ...::saturate_len16_passes_through_in_range_and_saturates_above ... FAILED
test ...::checksum16_ipv4_saturates_length_above_u16 ... FAILED

## PR #6010 — daemon: fail closed on unreadable kernel-upgrade journal [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5682-upgrade-journal-failclosed`

Closes #5682 (codex-review-182 M24, High, security)

## Root cause
On a kernel-candidate boot, `holdSecondaryIfKernelCandidateArmed`
(`pkg/daemon/kernel_selfrecover.go`) reads the kernel-upgrade journal via
`KernelRunner.IsArmed()`. The old guard was:

```go
armed, j, err := r.IsArmed()
if err != nil || !armed {
    return   // <- no hold set; node runs a NORMAL election
}
d.cluster.SetKernelUpgradeHold()
```

`IsArmed` → `loadKernelJournal` already folds a clean **ENOENT** to
`KernelStateInit` + nil error, so `err != nil` is reached **only** on a
genuine read/parse failure of an existing-but-unreadable journal (I/O
error, corruption, malformed content). Collapsing that into the same
`return` as `!armed` meant an **unreadable** journal was treated as "not
armed" and the node proceeded to a normal candidate election — it could
elect/promote as if no upgrade were pending. Because an unreadable journal
is a failure mode that itself **correlates** with a bad upgrade (a
candidate kernel that corrupted `/var/lib/xpf`, a half-written journal
from a crash mid-roll), this failed **OPEN** and defeated the
promote/rollback safety of the #1930 A/B kernel channel.

## Fix
Split the branch in `holdSecondaryIfKernelCandidateArmed`:

- **`err != nil` (UNREADABLE / ambiguous)** → `SetKernelUpgradeHold()`
  **fail-CLOSED** + `slog.Warn` once, and record the fail-closed reason.
- **`!armed` (clean read, no upgrade)** → proceed normally (no hold).
- **armed** → hold as before (`slog.Info`).

### ENOENT vs. unreadable
The distinction is made precisely, one layer down, in `loadKernelJournal`:
`os.IsNotExist(err)` returns a zero `KernelStateInit` journal with a **nil**
error (so a missing file is a legitimate "not armed" and still proceeds —
a node that simply never armed an upgrade is **never** bricked into a
spurious hold), while every other read error and every `json.Unmarshal`
failure propagates as a non-nil error. So reaching the new fail-closed
branch means the journal **exists but cannot be read/parsed** — exactly
the case that must fail closed.

### Not stranded (bounded recovery)
A fail-closed hold set on a **transient** I/O blip (no upgrade actually in
progress) has no promotion marker to wait on, so the existing
marker-only release in `reconcileKernelUpgradeHold` would never fire and
the node would sit SECONDARY forever. To prevent that, the fail-closed

## PR #6011 — dataplane: scope ifindex preflight to XPF-referenced links [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-16)

Branch: `fix/5836-ifindex-preflight-scope`

## Summary

`Manager.preflightCheckIfindexCaps` (`pkg/dataplane/loader.go`) enumerated
the **entire host network namespace** via `netlink.LinkList` and rejected the
compile if **any** link had an ifindex outside `[0, MaxInterfaces)` (65536).
The check was not scoped to the interfaces XPF actually references, so a
completely unrelated bridge, veth, management link, container link, or an
abandoned operator netdev with ifindex ≥ 65536 made **every** subsequent
`CompileUserspaceShim` fail. Long-lived namespaces reach that value through
interface churn even when XPF's managed ports stay low — the firewall could
wedge with no bad config of its own. The function's own comment already noted
that the real call-site checks (`AddTxPort`, `userspace/maps_sync.go`) are what
actually matter.

Closes #5836

## Root cause

`preflightCheckIfindexCaps` ran `for _, l := range linkLister()` and rejected on
`uint32(attrs.Index) >= MaxInterfaces` for **any** link — never filtered to the
links XPF attaches AF_XDP to or inserts into a dense per-interface dataplane map.

Which links actually need `ifindex < MaxInterfaces`?
- **`userspace_bindings`** is an `ebpf.Array` indexed by
  `idx = ifindex*BindingQueuesPerIface + queue`, so a bound interface's ifindex
  must stay under the cap or the flat index overflows. This is the real
  truncation surface.
- **`userspace_ingress_ifaces`** is a `HASH` keyed by ifindex — a high ifindex
  is a valid key, no cap needed.
- **`tx_ports`** (DEVMAP, `AddTxPort`) is **not populated** on the userspace
  path — `userspaceShimCompileDataplane.AddTxPort` is a no-op — it only applies
  to the retired-eBPF `Manager.Compile` path.

So only the interfaces in the compiled port set can overflow a map; unrelated
host links cannot.

## Fix — Option A (SCOPE), not Option B (remove)

`preflightCheckIfindexCaps(referenced map[int]bool)` now rejects **only** links
whose ifindex is in `referenced`. Callers pass `result.pendingXDP` — the
compiler's resolved port set (physical zone interfaces, RETH members, VLAN
parents, tunnels, and fabric parents, all resolved to `physIface.Index` in
`compiler_iface.go`). An unrelated high-ifindex host link is skipped.

Both call sites now run the check **after** `CompileConfig` (so `pendingXDP` is
populated):
- `CompileUserspaceShim` (loader.go) — the live path.
- `Manager.Compile` (compiler.go) — the retired-eBPF path, fixed for
  consistency (same false-rejection existed there).
