## PR #6452 — config: reject duplicate NAT rule names at commit [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/5649-dup-nat-rule-names`

## Summary

Advances #5649 by fixing the **C181-M18** survivor from the
codex-review-181 audit cohort. This is one finding of the 19-item
cohort; the issue stays open for the remaining survivors.

A NAT rule-set is an ordered, first-match table and each rule's
operational / counter identity is `natType/ruleset/rule`
(`pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go`). Two rules authored with the **same
name** in one rule-set are NOT reduced to last-writer-wins like a #5180
hierarchical block — they **both survive**: `namedInstances` (the rule
loop in `compiler_nat_source.go` / `_destination.go` / `_static.go`)
appends each as a separate row. The first shadows the second
(first-match), the second is unreachable, and both map to the one
name-derived counter identity, so `show` / counter surfaces cannot tell
the rows apart and reordering equivalent text can silently change
enforcement.

## Change

- **`validateDuplicateNATRuleNamesAST`** (`pkg/config/dup_nat_rule_names.go`),
  wired beside the #5180 duplicate-named-block gate in both
  `compileConfigWithOpts` and `compileConfigForNodeWithOpts`.
- Runs **pre-expansion** on top-level `security` stanzas only —
  apply-groups deep-merges a same-named rule rather than duplicating it,
  and the flat `set` form reuses the rule node, so only a
  directly-authored hierarchical duplicate reaches the gate (mirrors the
  #5180 rationale). Seen-set keyed by `(natType, rule-set, rule)`,
  unioned across repeated `security` / `nat` /
  `source|destination|static` blocks (compileNAT merges those, #3915).
- The same rule name in two **different** rule-sets (a distinct
  identity) is accepted.
- **Strict** (commit / commit-check) hard-rejects; **lenient** (load /
  peer-sync) warns via `opts.lenientDuplicateNATRuleName` so an
  already-persisted / peer-synced config still boots through (#1960
  no-brick, matching every sibling gate).
- Docs: sibling gate subsection in `docs/config-schema.md`; regenerated
  `docs/refactoring-audit-current.txt` (`compiler_opts.go` +15 lines).

## Fail-on-revert test

`TestDuplicateNATRuleNameRejected` drives source / destination / static
duplicates through `CompileConfig` (the stable public entrypoint).
**Neutralization recipe:** add `return nil, nil` at the top of
`validateDuplicateNATRuleNamesAST` → all three sub-tests go
clean-assertion RED (`CompileConfig must reject ...`), no build break.
`TestDuplicateNATRuleNameLenientWarns` proves the lenient downgrade;
`TestDuplicateNATRuleNameNoFalsePositive` guards distinct-name /
different-rule-set / flat-set-merge acceptance.

## PR #6453 — configstore: fix -race data race on test warn-log buffer [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6446-configstore-race`

## Summary

Fixes a `-race`-detected data race in `pkg/configstore` between the
`#4579` downgrade-warn tests and a leaked `persistRetryLoop` goroutine,
firsthand-confirmed at current master.

## Root cause

`captureWarnLogs` installs a `bytes.Buffer` as the **process-global**
`slog.Default()` so the `#4579` tests can assert on logged output. A
`persistRetryLoop` goroutine leaked from an earlier test in the package
(store_persist.go documents that the retry loop has no close signal and
is abandoned at process exit) keeps calling `slog.Warn()` and writes
through the newly-installed handler while the 4579 test reads the raw
buffer via `String()`. slog's handler mutex only serializes writers
among themselves; a caller reading the underlying `bytes.Buffer`
directly bypasses it, so the read races the write.

This is a **test-only** artifact — production never swaps
`slog.Default()` under a running loop and then reads its sink — so
there are no production code changes.

## Fix

Wrap the capture buffer in a `syncBuffer` whose `Write` and `String`
share one mutex, so the test's read is synchronized against any leaked
goroutine's slog write.

## Validation

- **Before (master, raw `bytes.Buffer`):** `go test ./pkg/configstore/
  -race -count=5` → 10 `DATA RACE` stacks + `FAIL
  TestEncryptedRoundTripNoWarn_4579` (bytes.Buffer.grow write in
  persistRetryLoop vs. bytes.Buffer.String read in the test).
- **After (fix, syncBuffer):** `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -race
  -count=10` → clean, 0 races, package PASS.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/configstore/`, and full `go test
  ./...` all pass.

Closes #6446

## PR #6456 — Advance #5557: case-fold host-inbound service tokens in junos-host shield [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/5557-hostinbound-service-token-case`

Advances #5557. Fixes one claude-review-003 A3 survivor (host-inbound
service-token case-sensitivity in `junos_host_deny.go`), distinct from
the seven Go control-plane items already merged in #6393.

## The bug

The junos-host coarse `application any` shield decides which ingress
netdevs are exempt from its DROP for IKE/NAT-T (udp 500/4500) and ident
(tcp 113 RST) by reading each interface's effective host-inbound
`system-services` set and comparing tokens **case-sensitively**:
`s == "ike"`, `s == "ipsec"`, `s == "ident-reset"`, and
`HostInboundFullAdmitService`'s `== "all"`.

Enforcement lower-cases every host-inbound token before admitting — the
dataplane snapshot (`unionHostInboundTokens`/`lowerTokens` in
`pkg/dataplane/userspace`) and the Rust classifier
(`classify_system_service`, `host_inbound.rs:78`). Wrong-case tokens are
rejected at commit but only **warned** on the lenient / HA-sync load
path (#1960 no-brick), so a persisted or peer-synced config can carry an
upper-case `IKE`/`IPSEC`/`ALL`/`IDENT-RESET` to runtime.

For such a config enforcement full-admits IKE, but the shield's
case-sensitive comparison leaves `CoarseAdmitsIKE`/`CoarseIdentResets`
false → no exemption is emitted ahead of the drop → the coarse
`application any` DROP shadows and drops the very IKE/NAT-T (VPN control
plane) and ident traffic the host-inbound gate admitted. A fail-closed
drift between the shield and the enforcement path it mirrors. The
sibling **protocol** path in the same file (`junosHostAppL4`) already
lower-cases, so the service path was the one un-normalized match.

## The fix

- `junosHostSvcAdmitsIKE` + the `junosHostZoneExemptNetdevs` `note()`
  loop: lower-case (and trim) each service token before comparison.
- `HostInboundFullAdmitService` (documented SSOT for full-admit tokens):
  case/space-insensitive. Enforcement callers already feed it
  lower-cased tokens (idempotent); this additionally fixes the #3226
  commit-time full-admit breadth advisory silently skipping upper-case
  `ALL`.

Commit-time strict validation is unchanged — wrong-case is still
rejected at commit / warned on lenient load. Only the runtime coarse
verdict now conforms to the module's documented "both layers normalize
case, no runtime split-brain" invariant.

## PR #6479 — config: reject non-numeric static-NAT mapped-port at strict commit (C179-038) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/5523-nat-static-mapped-port-malformed`

Advances #5523 (codex-179 cohort — one item, **C179-038**). The cohort
issue stays OPEN.

## Problem (C179-038)
A `then static-nat prefix <ip> mapped-port <token>` value rides inside
the children:nil `static-nat` schema leaf, so the schema value validator
never sees the token. `staticNATMappedPortFromKeys` folded BOTH an
absent `mapped-port` and a present-but-non-numeric one to a bare `0`, so:

```
set security nat static rule-set rs1 rule r1 \
    then static-nat prefix 10.0.0.5/32 mapped-port notaport
```

compiled clean to `MappedPort==0` ("no port translation") with **no
diagnostic** — even though a WELL-FORMED value in that same position
without a `match destination-port` IS rejected at strict commit-check
(the #2769 gate). Garbage was treated more leniently than a valid value.

## Fix
- `staticNATMappedPortFromKeys` now returns `(port int, malformedRaw
  string)`: a present-but-non-numeric value yields `(0, "<raw token>")`,
  distinguishing it from an absent keyword.
- **Both** parse sites record it: the collapsed-keys flat-set path
  (`staticNATMappedPortFromKeys(t.Keys)` / `(pn.Keys)`) and the
  hierarchical sibling-node path (`static-nat { prefix X; mapped-port P;
  }`), which now records a non-numeric sibling value as malformed
  instead of letting it collapse to `0`.
- New `StaticNATRule.MappedPortRaw` field carries the bad token; it is
  reset per then-block alongside the other then-set fields so a prior
  block's token cannot leak.
- `validateNATHostMaskStrict` rejects a non-empty `MappedPortRaw`.

## Strict-vs-lenient split (#1960 no-brick)
- **Strict** (commit / commit-check): hard error — `... then static-nat
  mapped-port "notaport" is not a valid port number (1-65535)`.
- **Lenient** (load / peer-sync): downgraded to a warning; the compiled
  rule keeps `MappedPort==0` so the dataplane installs a plain 1:1 (no
  bogus port), matching the pre-fix fail-closed behaviour. An
  already-persisted or peer-synced config still boots.

## Validation
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/config/`, `gofmt -l` — all clean.
- New `TestStaticNATMappedPortMalformedRejected` (strict rejects, error
  names `mapped-port` + `notaport`) and
  `TestStaticNATMappedPortMalformedLenientWarns` (lenient warns, keeps
  `MappedPort==0`) pass; full `pkg/config` suite green.
- **Parent-RED self-check**: neutralizing the strict gate turns both
  tests RED on clean assertions (not a build break):
  - `expected CompileConfig to reject a non-numeric mapped-port`

## PR #6480 — fix(userspace): rebuild policy scheduler bits in route-overlay publish (#5328 A6-b2-F4) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/5328-overlay-scheduler-policy`

## Summary

Advances #5328 — cohort item **A6-b2-F4** (codex-178 survivors). One
focused control-plane fix in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go`.
The `[cohort]` tracking issue stays **open**; this PR does not close it.

`PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot(cfg, overlay, schedulerState)` documented that
a non-nil `schedulerState` refreshes the policy snapshots **in the same
publish**, but the code only cached `m.policySchedulerActive` while
`next := *m.lastSnapshot` inherited the PRIOR compiled `Policies` /
`AddressBooks` verbatim. The helper therefore enforced **stale schedule
bits** until a later `UpdatePolicyScheduleState` callback fired (plus a
redundant full reconcile).

The ip-monitoring actuator (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go`) calls this helper
with a live `scheduler.ActiveState()`, so a probe-driven route flap could
ship a snapshot that **reports success while the dataplane enforces a
scheduled permit against the wrong window** — a fail-open gap: a permit
whose schedule window just closed stays live until the next scheduler tick.

## Fix

When `schedulerState != nil`, rebuild the published snapshot's policy
sections in THIS publish, exactly as the dedicated scheduler-only republish
(`UpdatePolicyScheduleState`) does:

- `next.Policies` via `buildPolicySnapshotsWithSchedulerStateAndFeeds`
- `next.Capabilities.PolicyContentRejected` via
  `collectPolicyContentRejections` (#3261)
- `next.AddressBooks` via `buildAddressBookTableWithFeeds` (#1606)

reusing the cached feed overlay so a concurrent CoS scheduler flip is not
dropped. Key invariants (verified firsthand):

- `m.policySchedulerActive` is updated from `schedulerState` **earlier** in
  the function, so the rebuild consumes the NEW state.
- The rebuild is placed **BEFORE** the duplicate-publish content-hash skip,
  so a scheduler-only inactive-bit flip on unchanged routes is not falsely
  deduped away.
- A `nil` `schedulerState` leaves the inherited policy sections untouched
  (the route-apply caller path that never carries scheduler state).

`docs/userspace-dataplane-architecture.md` records the route-overlay
republish co-honoring the policy-scheduler contract.

## PR #6481 — fix(cli): escape terminal control bytes in device-supplied lease fields (#6468) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6468-cli-lease-hostname-escape`

## Summary

`show dhcp server leases` printed a DHCP lease **hostname** — a
client-controlled value (DHCP option 12, stored opaque by Kea) — verbatim to
the operator's terminal. A device on a served segment could embed terminal
escape sequences in its hostname (OSC 52 clipboard write, OSC 8 hyperlink, CSI
cursor/erase controls) that the operator's terminal would **act on** when the
lease table is displayed, yielding **clipboard hijack** and **output spoofing**
(a forged `commit complete` line, or a rogue lease row erased from view). The
client hardware address and the DHCP-DDNS forward record name (built from the
same client hostname) carry the same exposure.

`show dhcp server` runs on **both** the local interactive CLI and the **remote
`cli`** (over gRPC). Both are guarded here.

## Injection vector

- `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go` reads `Hostname` verbatim from the Kea lease
  CSV (opaque, no charset enforcement).
- `pkg/cli/show_services_dhcp.go` printed `l.Hostname` / `l.HWAddress` raw.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_dhcp_lldp_snmp.go` formats the **same** raw fields
  into text, and `cmd/cli` prints that text verbatim (`fmt.Print(resp.Output)`)
  — the identical vector on the remote surface.

## Fix (display boundary, both surfaces, shared leaf)

Add `pkg/termsafe` — a **stdlib-only leaf package** so both `pkg/cli` and
`pkg/grpcapi` can share one implementation (`pkg/cli` imports `pkg/grpcapi`, so
the helper cannot live in `pkg/cli`). `termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay`
backslash-hex escapes every C0 control byte (`0x00-0x1F`), DEL (`0x7F`), C1
control byte (`0x80-0x9F`), and invalid UTF-8 byte — an ESC renders as the four
printable characters `\x1b` — while passing every printable rune, **including
legitimate multibyte UTF-8**, through unchanged. A `DisplaySafe` fast path
keeps the common clean case allocation-free.

Applied at the terminal render sites for **device-originated** fields on **both**
surfaces:

| Field | `pkg/cli` | `pkg/grpcapi` (remote cli) |
|---|---|---|
| DHCPv4/v6 lease `Hostname` + `HWAddress` (brief + detail) | ✅ `show_services_dhcp.go` | ✅ `server_show_dhcp_lldp_snmp.go` |
| DHCP-DDNS owned-record `FQDN` | ✅ `show_services_ddns.go` | ✅ `server_show_dhcp_lldp_snmp.go` |

`cmd/cli` needs no change (it already prints the server's text verbatim; the
server now sends sanitized text). Stored lease data and the gRPC/JSON structs
are **unchanged** — machine consumers keep the raw value.

## PR #6484 — config: reject multi-target static-NAT rule at commit-check [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6483-multitarget-static-nat`

## Summary

A Junos static-NAT rule maps to **exactly one** translation target — one of `prefix <ip>` | `prefix-name <name>` | `nptv6-prefix <p6>` | `inet`. Authoring two or more (both a `prefix` and a `prefix-name`, an `inet` sibling alongside a `prefix` sibling, or two prefixes) is invalid Junos, but the compiler silently **accepted** it: `compileNATStatic`'s child loop honors the FIRST target by a fixed priority (`nptv6-prefix > prefix-name > prefix > inet`) and drops the rest, and since `prefix`/`inet`/`nptv6-prefix` all land in the shared `Then` field a later target overwrites an earlier one. The rule compiled to one arbitrary target with no operator feedback — `inet` + `prefix` even installed as a plain prefix rule, **evading the #5859 inet reject**.

Dropping a target this way also dropped any `mapped-port` that rode **only** on the discarded target (the #6479/C179-038 residual): that target's node was never the one whose modifier the mapped-port fold read, so `then { static-nat { inet mapped-port <bad>; } static-nat { prefix <ip>; } }` silently lost the malformed port and compiled clean. Rejecting the multi-target rule outright is the Junos-faithful closure and forecloses that residual as a side effect.

## Implementation

- **`staticNATThenTargetCount`** (`compiler_nat_static.go`) counts the **distinct `(keyword, value)` target identities** a `then` block declares, from the AST, across every authoring shape (flat-set targets collapse onto one `static-nat` node's children; the hierarchical `then { static-nat {…} static-nat {…} }` shape spreads them across siblings). Counting *distinct identities* (not occurrences) keeps the canonical "restate the target to attach a mapped-port" form — `prefix-name N` + `prefix-name N mapped-port P` — a single target, and skips a modifier carrier (`prefix mapped-port <port>`) the same way the mapped-port fold does.
- Recorded as **`StaticNATRule.ThenTargetCount`** (`json:"-"`, compile-only, last `then` block wins per #3850) — the collapsed field state cannot reveal a multi-target rule.
- **`validateStaticNATSingleTargetStrict`** rejects a rule whose winning block declares >1 target. It runs in `runTailGates` **after** the host-mask (#2173) and NPTv6 (#2240/#5818) gates, so a rule that *also* carries a malformed `mapped-port` / bad nptv6 prefix reports that concrete token first (the multi-target defect is caught on the next compile once fixed — never masked; existing #6479 multi-block tests keep their diagnostics). Zero-target rules stay the empty-target gate's domain (#4290).
- Strict on commit / commit-check (hard reject); tolerant load / peer-sync downgrades to a warning (`opts.lenientFirewallRefs`, #1960 no-brick).

## Was the multi-target rule reachable? How represented?

Yes. Investigated empirically: the flat-set lines `then static-nat prefix <ip>` + `then static-nat prefix-name <name>` **collapse onto one `static-nat` node with two target children**; the hierarchical form spreads targets across sibling `static-nat` nodes. Both silently accepted on `origin/master` (`inet`+`prefix`, `prefix`+`prefix-name`, two-`prefix`, hier two-block all compiled with `err == nil`).

## Validation

- New `static_nat_multitarget_6483_test.go`: strict REJECT / lenient WARN for prefix+prefix-name, inet+prefix, two-prefix, hierarchical two-block; the **#6479 dropped-target mapped-port residual** (silent-accept on master) now rejects; single-target ACCEPT for each of the four targets in collapsed + hierarchical shapes, plus the mapped-port / routing-instance modifier and the restated-name form; a lone `inet` is not falsely flagged multi.
- **PARENT-RED**: neutralizing the `> 1` guard turns the five reject cases clean-assertion RED (`strict CompileConfig must reject a multi-target static-nat rule`), `go vet` still clean; restore → GREEN.
- `gofmt` / `go vet` / `go build ./...` and the full `pkg/config` suite pass; `docs/refactoring-audit-current.txt` regenerated (`compiler_validate_strict_nat.go` 2865→2928). `docs/config-schema.md` documents the one-target invariant and the residual closure.

Closes #6483

Also closes the #6479 static-NAT multi-target dropped mapped-port residual.

## PR #6485 — nat: DNAT bare destination-port matches tcp AND udp (#6462) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6462-dnat-bare-destport-dualproto`

## Summary

- A destination-NAT rule with `match destination-port` but **no** `match protocol` installed a **TCP-only** table entry, so **UDP to the VIP:port was silently not translated** (local-delivered, then dropped by host-inbound). Junos matches a bare destination-port across **both** TCP and UDP.
- Blast radius: UDP services behind a port-based DNAT (DNS, SIP, VPN) silently dead on a common protocol-less config, while `show security nat destination` still lists the rule installed — a silent outage plus an observability lie. Fail direction is fail-closed (no security bypass).
- Fix: `buildDestinationNATSnapshots` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_destination.go`) replaces the scalar `proto = "tcp"` default with a `protos` slice — a protocol-less port-based rule now emits one snapshot per protocol under **`tcp` AND `udp`**. Explicit `match protocol` is honored verbatim; a protocol-less rule with **no** port stays a single match-any (empty-protocol) entry, unchanged.

## Why two explicit rows, not PROTO_ANY

- `PROTO_ANY` would wrongly translate ICMP/other (ports are meaningless there).
- The Rust `DnatTable` lookup probes `(proto,dst_ip,dst_port) -> (proto,dst_ip,0) -> (PROTO_ANY,dst_ip,0)` and **never** `(PROTO_ANY,dst_ip,dst_port)`, so a single PROTO_ANY+port entry would be unreachable for a UDP packet anyway. Two keyed rows are the only fix a UDP proto-17 packet can hit via the first probe.
- Both rows share the rule's single `CounterID` (mirrors an explicit `match protocol [ tcp udp ]`, #3431): a packet is TCP or UDP, hits exactly one row, counter increments once — no double-count.

## Scope

Go control-plane only. No Rust (`userspace-dp/`) touched.

## Test plan

- [x] New `nat_destination_6462_test.go`: exact-port and range paths each emit a **tcp AND a udp** entry sharing one `CounterID`; explicit protocol is **not** dual-emitted; a no-port rule stays match-any.
- [x] **RED-on-revert**: neutralizing the dual-emit hunk to `protos = []string{"tcp"}` makes `TestBuildDNATBareDestPortEmitsTCPAndUDP_6462` fail with `no udp-keyed entry for 198.51.100.10:53 (the #6462 bug)` — verified, then restored.
- [x] `#3449` range-expansion and `#3446` port-validity tests pinned to `match protocol tcp` to isolate their single concern from the new dual-emit.
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/`, `gofmt -l` (clean), `go test ./pkg/dataplane/...`, `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -run TestHeatmapNotStale` — all green.

- `docs/config-schema.md` — DNAT per-protocol expansion note.
- `docs/feature-coverage.md` — Destination NAT row.

- Closes #6462

  every config-static next-table leak into the userspace FIB **uncapped**,
  so leak #101+ existed in the userspace FIB but not the kernel ip-rule
  table. A slow-path packet (XDP_PASS / IPsec-reinjected / non-native-XDP
  fabric) matching leak #101+ then resolved into the target VRF on the
  AF_XDP fast path but the **main table** in the kernel — two engines, two
  verdicts for the same flow, and the commit reported success.

## Fix (Go control-plane only)

- **Aggregated apply error.** `Apply` now appends a degraded error naming
  how many next-table routes past the cap are not leaked (mirroring the
  rib-group/PBR cap idiom precisely — same `errs` slice, `errors.Join`).
  The loop is index-based to count the dropped tail. The strict commit
  gate (`validateRoutingRuleWindowsStrict`, #5854) already rejects an
  over-subscribed config up front; this belt catches the tolerant-load /
  peer-sync path where that gate is downgraded to a warning.
- **FIB cap reconcile.** `buildRouteSnapshots` caps GLOBAL config-static
  next-table leaks at the same window via a shared v4-then-v6 counter,
  matching the applier's single shared priority counter, so both planes
  truncate the identical tail and the FIB never carries a leak the kernel
  dropped.
- **SSOT.** Promoted the window to an exported
  `config.NextTableRuleWindow` (+ `config.NextTableRulePriorityBase`),
  mirroring the #4479 PBR band constants. The commit gate
  (`pkg/config` `maxNextTableRules`, #5854), the applier
  (`pkg/routing.maxNextTableRules`), and the userspace FIB mirror all
  derive from that one value — replacing the prior keep-in-sync
  duplication comment, so drift is impossible.

Behavior below the cap is unchanged: a config with ≤ 100 next-table
routes installs and publishes every leak exactly as before.

## PR #6487 — ipsec: sanitize swanctl local_addrs/remote_addrs at render [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6469-swanctl-addr-sanitize`

## Summary

Closes the last raw-`%s` swanctl-injection surface. The connection
`local_addrs`/`remote_addrs` render lines in `pkg/ipsec/policy.go`
interpolated the resolved endpoint verbatim, while the render belt that
already guards the connection name, IKE `id`/`certs`, PSK `secret`, and
the `local_ts`/`remote_ts` child-SA selectors did not cover the endpoint
address fields.

## The gap

On a path that reaches `renderConfig` without the strict commit-time
endpoint validator (`validateIPsecEndpointsStrict`) — HA peer-sync of a
config persisted before the fix, or a directly-constructed `IPsecConfig`
— a gateway whose `address`/`dynamic hostname`/`local-address` carries an
embedded newline lands verbatim in `/etc/swanctl/conf.d/xpf.conf`,
injecting strongSwan connection keys (downgrade `version`, flip
`aggressive`, add `also`/`children`). `resolveRemoteAddr` takes
`gw.Address`/`gw.DynamicHostname` verbatim for the Gateways-map shape;
only the legacy inline `vpn.Gateway` shape was independently filtered by
`config.IsUsableIPsecEndpoint`.

## Fix

Wrap both `policy.go` Fprintf sites in `sanitizeSwanctlValue`. These are
UNQUOTED comma-list slots, so — exactly like the `local_ts`/`remote_ts`
belt — sanitize alone is the correct form. `escapeSwanctlQuoted` is for
the quoted `id`/`cert`/`secret` slots only and would mis-escape an
unquoted value. `sanitizeSwanctlValue` collapses the newline to a space,
keeping a tampered endpoint inert on one line instead of a live
directive, and touches nothing in a legitimate endpoint (`.`, `,`, `:`,
`%` preserved), so a single address, a comma-separated multi-address
list, an IPv6 literal, and the responder-only `%any` sentinel render
byte-identical. This is the by-construction backstop mirroring the
#1798/#2126/#4098 belt doctrine; the commit-time gate remains the hard
diagnostic on operator commit.

## Test (fail-on-revert)

`swanctl_addr_sanitize_6469_test.go` renders an endpoint carrying
`203.0.113.1\n    reauth_time = 0` via each of the four
validation-bypassed shapes (`gw.Address`, `gw.DynamicHostname`,
`gw.LocalAddress`, `vpn.LocalAddr`) and asserts the injected directive
never appears as a live line; an over-escape guard asserts a legit
single / comma-list / IPv6 / `%any` endpoint still renders. Reverting the
sanitize wrap to raw `%s` fails with a clean assertion (`swanctl
injection NOT neutralized: reauth_time = 0 rendered as a live directive
line`), confirmed firsthand.

## PR #6488 — config: reject duplicate NAT rule-SET names within one nat type (#6454) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6454-dup-nat-ruleset-names`

## Summary

- PR #6452 (#5649, C181-M18) rejects duplicate NAT rule-**names** within one
  rule-set. This closes the sibling fail-open one level up: duplicate NAT
  rule-**SET** names.
- Two rule-sets authored with the same name **within one nat type**
  (`source`/`destination`/`static`/`nat64`) both SURVIVE — `compileNATSource` /
  `compileNATDestination` / `compileNATStatic` / `compileNAT64` each **append**
  the rule-set (`sec.NAT.Source` / `Destination.RuleSets` / `Static` / `NAT64`),
  never merging by name. Both compile as separate first-match tables sharing one
  operational identity (the rule-set name), so for the counted natTypes their
  rules map onto the shared `natType/ruleSet/rule` counter namespace
  (`NATCounterKey`) — per-rule telemetry merges and `show`/counter surfaces
  cannot disambiguate. A `nat64` rule-set is counter-less (prefix/source-pool, no
  `rule` nodes — correctly excluded from the #5649 rule-name gate) but still
  shares its show-surface name identity, so it is deduped here too.
- New gate `validateDuplicateNATRuleSetNamesAST` (`pkg/config/dup_nat_ruleset_names.go`),
  wired beside the #5649 gate in both `compileConfigWithOpts` and
  `compileConfigForNodeWithOpts`. Mirrors the #5649 idiom: pre-expansion,
  top-level `security` stanzas only, keyed by `(natType, rule-set)`, unioned
  across repeated sub-blocks (a rule-set name split across two `source {}` blocks,
  #3915, is caught). Strict rejects; lenient warns via
  `opts.lenientDuplicateNATRuleSetName` (#1960 no-brick).

## Scope decision — per-natType namespace

Reject only **within** one nat type, never **across**. `NATCounterKey` is
prefixed by natType (`snat`/`dnat`/`static`), so Junos' independent per-type name
spaces are genuinely distinct identities — a `source` rule-set and a `static`
rule-set may legitimately share a name. Only same-natType duplicates collide, so
the seen-set key includes the natType.

## AST-instance-level dedup (not compiled)

The dedup is at the AST rule-set-**instance** level, NOT the compiled level: a
single authored rule-set carrying a bracket list of from/to scopes
Cartesian-expands into MULTIPLE same-named `NATRuleSet` objects downstream
(#3096). That is one AST instance and is NOT flagged — a compiled-level dedup
would false-positive on legitimate scope expansion.

## Test plan

- [x] `dup_nat_ruleset_names_6454_test.go`: strict reject for source / destination
      / static / nat64 (disjoint rule names inside each, so the #5649 rule-name
      gate does not pre-empt this one).
- [x] nat64 counter-less-diagnostic guard: the type-agnostic message must not
      claim a per-rule counter.
- [x] Lenient path warns exactly once (#1960).
- [x] No-false-positive accepts: distinct names; same name across different nat
      types; #3096 bracket-list scope expansion; flat-set merge.

## PR #6489 — daemon(nft): fail closed on a cold-boot lo0 filter install failure (#6476) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6476-lo0-cold-boot-fence`

## Summary

- The operator's lo0 RE-protection filter (`interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet filter input <name>`, the Junos protect-RE pattern) lowers to the `inet xpf_lo0` input chain at hook-input priority 0 — strictly before the `xpf_hostinbound` backstop (10). Unlike host-inbound it had **no cold-boot fence**.
- On a **COLD BOOT** no prior `xpf_lo0` table exists to retain, and the boot apply reaches `applyLo0Filter` through `applyConfig`, which only **logs and discards** the error (a boot apply must not brick startup). So a failed `InstallLo0` left the RE input path with no lo0 filter and only a WARN, while the daemon published host service / VIP / HA-ready — the exact fail-open #5644 closed for host-inbound. Any service protected ONLY via the lo0 filter is unenforced until the next clean commit.
- **Fix (mirrors #5644):** add a `d.lo0Enforced` gate; on a failed `InstallLo0` while false, install a fail-closed fence into the `xpf_lo0` table (priority 0) that denies host-bound traffic to the **same lifeline-excluded firewall-local address sets** and the **same fence body** as the host-inbound cold-boot fence. Because the fence occupies the real filter's table/slot, a later successful `InstallLo0` **atomically replaces** it. Install goes through a new `Installer.InstallLo0ColdBootFence` seam.
- **No day-2 gap fence** (deliberate #5789 divergence): the `xpf_hostinbound` table is auto-generated and per-destination-address scoped, so a newly-appeared address needs an additive gap fence. The operator's lo0 filter is hand-authored and NOT per-destination scoped — its terms (typically ending in a catch-all `discard`) govern every local address, including one that appears later — so a day-2 failure retains the prior real filter and that generation still covers new addresses.
- **One source of truth:** extracted `buildFenceTablePayload(tableName, priority, ...)` so the host-inbound and lo0 fence oracles share one body and cannot drift; the netlink `InstallLo0ColdBootFence` reuses `buildHostInboundFenceNetlink`, so only the table wrapper differs.

## Fence rule shape

Identical to the #5644 host-inbound cold-boot fence — mandatory L3 / return admits (`ct established,related`, raw ESP/AH `l4proto {50,51}`, IPv6 ND, v4/v6 PMTUD+error, the configured WireGuard listen port) followed by a catch-all `<fam> daddr <addrs> drop` — with **no per-service accept and no named counters**. The address sets are lifeline-excluded (`fxp0`/`em0`/`fab*`), so the fence can never strand management or break HA.

## Test plan

- [x] `pkg/daemon/lo0_coldboot_fence_6476_test.go` — fail-on-revert proof:
  - cold-boot `InstallLo0` failure installs exactly one **lo0-table** fence (routing it to the host-inbound seam leaves the count at 0)
  - lifeline safety (em0 `10.99.0.1` never fenced; wan address is) via `buildLo0FencePayload`, asserting the `xpf_lo0` table at priority 0
  - mandatory-L3 + WG admits present
  - **day-2** retention installs **no** fence
  - catastrophic double-failure joins both errors and leaves `lo0Enforced` false
  - zero-drop fence leaves `lo0Enforced` false (retry semantics)
  - successful teardown clears `lo0Enforced`
- [x] **Parent-RED confirmed firsthand:** neutralizing the fence install turns the primary test RED with `cold-boot lo0 install failure must install exactly one fail-closed lo0 fence, got 0` (clean assertion failure, not a build break), then restored.
- [x] `lo0_cold_boot_fence` case added to the T1 netlink parity gate (`daemon_nft_netlink_parity_test.go`).
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/daemon/ ./pkg/nftables/`, `gofmt -l` (touched files clean), full `pkg/daemon` + `pkg/nftables` suites, and the `refactoraudit` heatmap gate (regenerated `docs/refactoring-audit-current.txt`) all pass.
- Not run: live cluster smoke — control-plane-only nft fence path, no dataplane/forwarding change; exercised by unit tests + the parity gate.

## Docs

`docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md` gains a "lo0 RE-protection cold-boot fence (#6476)" subsection documenting the mechanism and the #5789 (no gap fence) divergence.

## Refs

- Mirrors #5644 (host-inbound cold-boot fence), #5790 (teardown clears the gate), and diverges from #5789 (no lo0 gap fence, with rationale).

Closes #6476

## PR #6491 — config: quoted-empty dup-name reject; defer group-authored (#6455) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6455-dupname-group-quotedempty`

## Summary (SPLIT after a Codex MAJOR)

The first commit added a pre-expansion per-group-body duplicate scan. A Codex
hostile review flagged it as a false-reject, and firsthand verification
confirmed it: the per-group-body scan **false-rejects a legitimate apply-groups
FRAGMENT config**. This PR keeps the correct quoted-empty half and withdraws the
flawed group-authored scan.

## Firsthand verification (why the per-body scan is wrong)

Fragments of ONE named object authored across repeated group roots COALESCE into
a single object under `mergeNodes` during `ExpandGroups`. Observed by
neutralizing the group scan and compiling:

| case | authored | compiles to |
|------|----------|-------------|
| interface fragments across two `interfaces` roots | `ge-0/0/0 {unit 0}` + `ge-0/0/0 {unit 1}` | ONE `ge-0/0/0` (units=2) |
| screen profile ICMP + TCP fragments | `ids-option P {icmp}` + `ids-option P {tcp}` | ONE `P` (icmp+tcp) |
| NAT rule match/then fragments | `rule R {match}` + `rule R {then}` | ONE rule `R` |

The per-body scan REJECTED all three. A pre-expansion sibling-scan cannot model
that same-pass coalescing — unacceptable for a commit gate.

## Kept (correct) — quoted-empty names

All three gates used to `continue` on an empty name, so `rule ""` / `rule-set ""`
/ `group ""` / `interface ""` / `ids-option ""` was neither dup-rejected nor
empty-rejected. An empty name is not a valid operational identity (the object
cannot be referenced or shown by name), so each gate now rejects it (strict) /
warns (lenient), mirroring the #5636 empty-credential rejection. The empty
**rule-set** name is owned solely by the #6454 gate (the #5649 rule-name gate
skips an empty rule-set), so the lenient warning fires exactly once — the Codex
double-report MINOR.

## Withdrawn (flawed) — group-authored per-body scan

`scanNamespaces` + the group-context machinery are removed. The three gates
return to their top-level-only pre-expansion scan, so the duplicate diagnostics
are byte-identical to before. `compiler.go` call-site comments on both compile
paths note the quoted-empty reject.

## Deferred — group-authored duplicate detection

The correct fix runs AFTER `ExpandGroups` (the coalesced tree) but before the
#3096 Cartesian bracket-list expansion in `compileExpanded`
(`compiler_nat_source.go:766`), and must union the node0 and node1 expansions to
stay HA-symmetric like the sibling tunnel / zone / unit-alias gates. That is a
design pass, tracked as the group-authored half of #6455.

## Summary

An empty element now rejects the snapshot the same way; the `== "any"` token stays the genuine wildcard. The check is explicit rather than relying on `zone_name_to_id_from_snapshot` never holding an empty name.

A host-bound non-first fragment overlapping a port-bearing junos-host DENY fell through to a later junos-host PERMIT — or to the deliver-on-no-match lifeline — and reached the host stack even though the first fragment (with the real port) is denied. The gate now runs the same `note_skipped_frag_deny` / `apply_frag_deny_override` machinery across all three tiers (exact pair, from-any wildcard, host-scoped global), and converts the no-match fall-through into `Some(frag_associated_deny_result)` when a deny was skipped (the lifeline is a permit-like posture, so it takes the same override a transit default-PERMIT takes).

Both sites are cold paths (snapshot decode; host-bound flowless/session-miss evaluation), not the established-session fast path. #6465 adds one 8-byte `Option<SkippedFragDeny>` stack slot plus, per non-matching rule, one early-out branch (`l4_present || skipped.is_some()`) — the same shape the transit #4569 guard already pays. ## PR #6506 — userspace-dp: invalidate flow cache on control-plane session delete (#6457) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6457-flowcache-delete-invalidate`

## Summary

- The per-worker flow cache was never invalidated on a control-plane
  session delete, so a revoked but continuously-active 5-tuple kept
  forwarding on the owning worker via a stage-12 flow-cache HIT — no
  session row, no policy re-evaluation, no `show security flow session`
  visibility, no HA sync. Three delete flows funnel through
  `WorkerCommand::DeleteSynced` and none bumps config/fib generation, RG
  epoch, or RG lease (the only stamps the hit path validates): the
  operator `clear security flow session [all]` (Go `ClearAllSessions` /
  singular `DeleteSession`), the cluster-stale sweep
  (`BatchDeleteSessions`), and HA DeleteSynced propagation
  (`delete_synced_session_gen` fan-out + cross-worker
  `replicate_session_delete`). The operator's explicit revocation
  primitive was silently defeated on the fast path (fail-open).
- Fix extends the #3776 GC-reap invalidation pattern to the delete path:
  `handle_delete_synced` records every deleted key —
  **unconditionally**, even when the worker's session table has no entry
  (a stale cached descriptor outlives its table entry; that survival is
  the bug) — into the new `WorkerCommandResults.deleted_synced_keys`.
  `apply_worker_commands` has no `BindingWorker` access (the same
  constraint that put the #941 vacate dispatch in the worker loop), so
  the worker loop drains the list through the new
  `invalidate_flow_cache_slots_for_deleted_sessions`, calling
  `flow_cache.invalidate_slot(&key, binding.ifindex)` on every binding.
  The next packet on the revoked tuple MISSES the cache and re-runs full
  session lookup/creation + policy — fail-closed.
- The eviction is same-thread (per-binding caches are worker-owned),
  key+ifindex precise (the every-binding walk can never evict another
  live flow's entry), and covers both directions (the fan-out pushes
  forward AND reverse keys).
- Out of scope, verified non-issues: `delete_terminal_half`'s local half
  (LocalDelivery dispositions are never cached — `is_cacheable()` admits
  only ForwardCandidate/FabricRedirect; its peer broadcast already flows
  through DeleteSynced) and the DSCP-filter purge (covered by the
  commit's config-generation bump, as the issue's verifier noted).

## Hot-path shape

Zero per-packet cost. One `Vec::push` per processed `DeleteSynced`
command plus one `invalidate_slot` set-walk per binding per deleted key —
bounded by the control-plane delete rate, all on the cold command
dispatch path. The per-packet hit path (`flow_cache_hit.rs`) is
untouched (no new generation check); ticks with no deletes skip the walk
via an `is_empty()` guard; `Vec::new()` on empty ticks allocates nothing.

      `delete_synced_records_key_even_when_session_already_absent`

## PR #6507 — userspace-dp: reject non-global embedded IPv4 in NAT64 destinations (#6475) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-25)

Branch: `fix/6475-nat64-dst-nonglobal-gate`

## Summary

- NAT64 destination extraction is now screened: `classify_ipv6_dest`
  rejects an extracted embedded IPv4 that is non-global per RFC 6052
  §2.2 — 0.0.0.0/8 (includes the `<prefix>::` lower boundary),
  127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, 224.0.0.0/4, and 240.0.0.0/4 (subsumes
  255.255.255.255/32 and the `<prefix>::ffff:ffff` upper boundary) —
  returning a new fail-closed `Nat64Match::IneligibleDestination`. The
  pre-routing classify drops the packet before route lookup, policy,
  `allocate_source`, or the `local_v4` LocalDelivery resolution, so no
  session/BIB/allocation state is minted.
- Closes the control-plane exposure from the issue: pre-gate,
  `64:ff9b::127.0.0.1` classified `MatchReady(127.0.0.1)` and, with lo0
  configured (its addresses land in `state.local_v4`), LocalDelivered
  NAT64-client traffic to sockets bound to 127.0.0.1 on the firewall
  itself (the localhost-only admin plane: gRPC 50051, REST 8080) through
  a minted bidirectional session.
- New distinct per-binding `nat64_ineligible_dest` counter plumbed

## Summary

  class). The MissingNeighbor arm carried five such pairs deep in nested

  consumer at the arm tail performs the one push + continue (the same
  consumer shape `stage_link_layer_classify` already uses at the stage-5

branch: **14653 vs 14641 instructions, 482 vs 478 direct calls, 112 vs 112
locked instructions**; after address normalization the 146-line residual is

## PR #6516 — userspace-dp: evaluate static NAT before the DNAT pool inbound (#6473) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-24)

Branch: `fix/6473-static-nat-precedence`

## Summary

- **BEHAVIOR CHANGE (vsrx-parity).** The inbound pre-routing NAT evaluation
  consulted the DNAT pool table FIRST and only fell back to static-DNAT on
  a pool miss — inverted vs Junos (first-packet order: static NAT →
  destination NAT → route → policy → reverse static → source NAT; "static
  NAT rules take precedence over destination NAT rules", verifier-confirmed
  externally in the issue).
- The codebase was also internally inconsistent: the OUTBOUND direction
  already evaluates static SNAT first (`source_nat_decision_for_flow` in
  `nat_exception.rs`), so the two directions disagreed on which backend
  owns an overlapping address.
- Flip the pre-routing arm to static-first: `match_dnat_with_counter_scoped`
  runs first, the pool lookup only on a static miss; the winner's per-rule
  hit counter flows into `pre_routing_dnat_counter` exactly as before.
  Where the static rule does NOT match (port-specific static, packet to
  another port) the pool still applies.
- **Stacked on #6514 (#6433), which is stacked on #6508 (#6432)** — merge
  those first; only commit 2fded8ff is this PR's.

## Migration note (operator-visible)

A deployment that RELIED on the DNAT-first shadowing — a pool rule
intentionally overriding a co-covering static rule — changes behavior: the
static mapping now wins for every packet the static rule matches, and the
static rule's hit counter advances instead of the pool rule's. Make the
override explicit by narrowing the static rule's scope (`from` zone /
interface / routing-instance, or `match source-address` / `match
destination-port`) or by removing the overlap. Documented in
`docs/feature-coverage.md` (Destination NAT row + Static NAT row cross-ref).

## Hot-path shape

Cold-path only: the pre-routing NAT evaluation runs once per new flow
(session install), never per established-flow packet (flow-cache hits never
reach it). Cost delta per new flow: a pure-DNAT deployment pays one extra
static-table prefix probe (static miss → pool hit, 2 lookups vs 1); a
static-matching flow saves the pool lookup. No new allocations, no atomics,
no signature changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Fail-on-revert `static_nat_precedes_overlapping_dnat_pool_6473` —
      external address covered by BOTH a static 1:1 (→ 10.0.61.50) and a
      DNAT pool rule (:443 → 10.0.61.102:8443): asserts the installed
      session carries the STATIC translation and no pool port rewrite.
      **RED on the pre-flip code** ("the static 1:1 mapping must win the
      overlap" — pool shadowed it), GREEN after.
- [x] Full `cargo test --release -- --test-threads=1`: 4252 passed, 0
      failed — no existing test had baked the DNAT-first order.

## PR #6518 — userspace-dp: gate Responder-SPI IKE on a live-exchange seed at Stage 11 (#6471) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-25)

Branch: `fix/6471-ike-responder-spi-gate`

## Summary

- On the AF_XDP secondary path (DNAT/static-NAT-to-self, native-GRE-inner), Stage 11 classified **any** IKE packet with a non-zero Responder SPI as `Exempt` and reinjected it to the local XFRM stack unconditionally. The SPI bytes are attacker-controlled, so a forged Responder-SPI IKE packet bypassed the per-zone host-inbound `ike` gate and reached strongSwan on a zone the operator closed to IKE.
- The primary path (direct IKE to an interface IP) cannot be fooled this way — the kernel nftables chain admits return IKE via `ct state established,related`, and conntrack NEW/ESTABLISHED cannot be faked by a first packet. Stage 11 now applies the equivalent discriminator via a new node-shared live-exchange table (`IkeExchangeTable`) playing the conntrack role the secondary path lacks.
- The table is **seeded** (a) at Stage 11 when a NEW IKE initiation (all-zero Responder SPI) *passes* the host-inbound gate — a denied initiation never seeds, or a forged follow-up would mint its own entry — and (b) in the native-GRE local-origin path when the firewall initiates IKE through a tunnel, so firewall-initiated tunnels on `ike`-omitting zones keep working (the ratified #4323 "return IKE never drops" semantic).
- A Responder-SPI-nonzero IKE packet matching **no** seed now faces the SAME host-inbound gate a NEW initiation faces: denied on a zone omitting `ike` (forgery closed), admitted on a zone listing `ike` (config-sanctioned openness — primary-path parity, the kernel chain admits NEW IKE there too).
- Classification is refactored onto a single `isakmp_demux` helper (SSOT) shared by `classify_ipsec_admission` (behavior-identical, pinned by a demux-parity test) and the two SPI extractors. `forwarding/README.md` host-inbound ordering docs updated (the documented forged-SPI residual is now closed).

## Design notes

- Match key is `(Initiator SPI, peer IP, local IP)`: no ports (an RFC 5996 NAT-T float must not strand the seed) and no Responder SPI (the reply is never observed on the inbound-only dataplane). Bounded: 4096-entry cap (oldest evicted on full), 24h sliding idle reap, poison-tolerant lock.
- Runtime state on the Coordinator — NOT config: a snapshot apply does not wipe seeds. Shared with workers via `WorkerSharedDataplane` (new field, `Arc::ptr_eq` wiring assertion added) and with the GRE local-origin threads at the tunnel-spawn site.
- Not HA-synced: the primary path's kernel conntrack for host-terminated IKE is not synced either — identical failover posture. An xpfd restart drops seeds; they self-heal on the next admitted initiation or firewall-outbound IKE packet, with the ESP data plane exempt throughout.

## Hot-path shape

Zero new work for non-IKE traffic. ESP/AH and ESP-in-UDP pay one extra protocol compare in the shared demux (they bail before any table access). IKE-to-self (control-plane pps, flood-bounded upstream by the stage-10 udp-flood screen) pays one 16-byte SPI parse + one short mutex + one FxHashMap lookup per packet; seed inserts are per-exchange and never on the data plane. No allocations on lookup; no atomics changed.

## Test plan

- [x] `stage_ipsec_passthrough_gates_forged_responder_spi_6471` (new, fail-on-revert): forged Responder-SPI IKE (UDP 500 and NAT-T 4500) on an `ike`-omitting zone → `Denied`; same packet on an `ike`-permitting zone → admitted; seeded-exchange follow-up → admitted; wrong Initiator SPI / wrong peer address → `Denied`; ESP-in-UDP untouched.
- [x] RED/GREEN proof: gate neutralized → the forged-deny assertions flip to `Passthrough` (FAILED as expected); restored → GREEN. Run twice (pre- and post-final tree).
- [x] `stage_ipsec_passthrough_gates_new_ike_4323` updated: established-on-deny-zone now passes via the seed planted by the admitted NEW initiation (seed existence asserted).
- [x] ipsec.rs unit tests: SPI extractors (NAT-T marker, truncation fail-safe), demux parity vs the pre-refactor open-coded match, seed/match/refresh, 24h idle reap, full-table oldest-eviction, local-origin seed only for genuine initiations.
- [x] Full Rust suite `cargo test --release -- --test-threads=1` (the `make test-rust` legs): EXIT=0 on the final tree.
- [x] clippy clean on the new code (a `too_many_arguments` on the seed helper was fixed by keying on `&SessionFlow`).
- [ ] Cluster smoke / deploy: not run (campaign engineer scope — unit and suite level only; no dataplane-behavior lane for IKE-to-self exists in the smoke env). No Go files touched: the kernel nft primary path already enforces conntrack NEW and is unchanged.

## PR #6571 — userspace-dp: validate fabric zone-encoded src-MAC against link identity and RG ownership (#6458) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-26)

Branch: `fix/6458-fabric-zone-stamp-validation`

## Summary

- A zone-encoded synthetic source MAC (`02:bf:72:fe:<hi>:<lo>`) on a
  fabric-ingress frame picked the ingress ZONE for new-flow policy,
  screens, SYN-cookie, IKE admission, and host-inbound evaluation on the
  receiving node. The decode checked only fabric-ingress + magic +
  zone-existence, and `StableZoneID` is a public name hash — an
  L2-adjacent host on the fabric segment could compute any zone's stamp
  offline and fail OPEN the zone-policy / screen / host-inbound
  boundaries (the `mgmt`-stamp variant needs no transit policy at all).
- The stamp is load-bearing for legitimate new flows punted to the
  egress-RG owner in split-RG active/active or asymmetric failover
  windows (`docs/active-active-new-connections.md`), so it is VALIDATED,
  not removed: **V1a** unicast dst == our fabric link `local_mac`;
  **V1b** claimed zone has RG-bound members (new
  `ForwardingState.zone_to_rgs`) and none is forwarding-active locally
  (stage 9); **V2** at every session-miss zone-pair site the override
  holds only when the resolution's owner RG is forwarding-active locally
  (`gate_fabric_zone_override_on_owner_rg`).
- Resulting posture: single-primary clusters reject every forged stamp on
  BOTH nodes (V1b on the primary; V2 + HAInactive on the backup);
  split-RG honors exactly the stamp shapes matching the live RG split —
  the legitimate punt keeps working. A rejected stamp degrades to today's
  unstamped fabric-frame posture, never below it.
- Residual (documented in `docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md`): on a
  SHARED fabric segment with a live RG split, a cloned
  currently-legitimate stamp shape is indistinguishable at L2 — full
  closure needs direct-attached or MACsec fabric (same trust-domain
  boundary as #4107's control-plane auth).

## Hot-path shape

Non-fabric packets: zero added cost (all checks sit behind the existing
`ingress_is_fabric` early-return). A stamped fabric-ingress frame: one
6-byte compare + one `zone_to_rgs` hash lookup + one `ha_state` BTreeMap
lookup per bound RG (typically 1) ≈ 15 ns. V2 runs on the session-miss
path only (one `owner_rg_for_resolution` — already computed nearby — and
one BTreeMap lookup). No allocations, no atomics, no new locks, no
wire-format change (rolling-upgrade safe: new receiver + old sender
validates the same wire stamp; old receiver + new sender keeps the old
receiver's pre-existing behavior).

## PR #6572 — userspace-dp: wire NAT64 ICMP error translation into the flowless arm (#6472) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-26)

Branch: `fix/6472-nat64-icmp-error-translation`

## Summary

- The RFC 7915 §4.2/§5.2 ICMP error translators in `nat64.rs` were unreachable in production: callable only via `build_nat64_forwarded_frame` on the flow-backed path, and a non-query ICMP error never has a flow (#3290 routes it flowless). The #5690 same-family reversal matched the NAT64 session but its single-family builders declined the cross-family `original_src`, and flowless L3 enforcement then dropped the error — MissingNeighbor on the pool address (v4→v6), NoRoute on the synthetic Pref64 destination (v6→v4). PMTUD and traceroute were dead across the boundary despite the #2219 doc claim.
- The flowless arm now tries a dedicated NAT64 arm BEFORE the #5690 reversal, NOT gated on `allow_embedded_icmp` (translating errors for the translator's OWN admitted sessions is core RFC 7915 behavior, not the optional passthrough that flag controls). `icmp_embed::nat64_match` classifies direction behind an RFC 792 fail-closed gate: the error's outer destination must equal the quote's source.
- v4→v6: an ICMPv4 error quoting the forward wire packet matches the v4 reverse companion via the quote's reply key → translated ICMPv6 toward the client (outer src = Pref64 ∷ error-sender per §6, outer dst = `orig_src_v6`). v6→v4: an ICMPv6 error about the translated reply, addressed to the synthetic Pref64 dst, matches the forward session's primary key → translated ICMPv4 toward the server (outer src = pool address — the RFC 6791 §6 case for an untranslatable v6 sender — outer dst = extracted server v4).
- The embedded quote's L4 port/echo id is restored to the value the error RECEIVER carries (client's original port v4→v6 via the reverse decision's `rewrite_dst_port`; translated pool port v6→v4 via the forward decision's `rewrite_src_port`) — without it the error is delivered but unassociable and PMTUD is dead on arrival. The restore rides two new `Option<u16>` fields on the embedded-mapping structs, applied inside the translators BEFORE the outer ICMP checksum; every data-packet caller passes `None` (byte-identical to pre-#6472).
- Shared mechanics: the #5690 queue tail is extracted as `queue_prebuilt_embedded_icmp_error` (HA/fabric finalizer, CoS with `flow_key = None`, prebuilt forward — never a session/flow-cache authority); `finalize_embedded_icmp_resolution_parts` factors the (resolution, ingress-zone) finalizer core. Both keep the #5690 path byte-identical.

## Hot-path shape

One `Vec::is_empty()` branch per flowless packet for non-NAT64 deployments (the NAT64 arm exits before any parse); the ICMP-error classification and quote parse run only when a NAT64 prefix is configured AND the packet is a non-query ICMP error. No new per-packet allocations on the data path (the translated frame's single `Vec` mirrors the #5690 reversed-frame allocation on this cold, per-error path). No atomic-ordering changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `poll_descriptor_nat64_icmp_error_v4_to_v6_translated_on_flowless_path_6472` — PTB toward a NAT64 session → exactly one prebuilt forward: ICMPv6 PTB type 2, MTU 1420 (=1400+20), outer src `64:ff9b::ac10:5001`, outer dst client, quote `(client:12345 → 64:ff9b::808:808:443)`, ICMPv6 checksum oracle — **RED with the call site disabled** (nothing queued)
- [x] `poll_descriptor_nat64_icmp_error_v6_to_v4_translated_on_flowless_path_6472` — Time-Exceeded toward the synthetic dst → ICMPv4 TE to the server, outer src pool, quote `(8.8.8.8:443 → pool:40000)` with the **destination port restored to the translated value**, checksum oracles — **RED with the call site disabled** (error forwarded UNTRANSLATED)
- [x] `poll_descriptor_nat64_icmp_error_outer_dst_mismatch_declined_6472` — RFC 792 anti-spoof gate (outer dst ≠ quote source → declined)
- [x] `poll_descriptor_same_family_reversal_not_stolen_by_nat64_arm_6472` — #5690 NAT44 reversal unchanged with a NAT64 prefix configured
- [x] `nat64_{v4_to_v6,v6_to_v4}_icmp_error_restores_embedded_{src,dst}_port_6472` / `_echo_id_6472` — translator-level quote port/id fidelity, each **RED with the restore stubbed out**; `None` byte-identity with the data-packet entry pinned
- [x] Full cargo suite GREEN: 4207 bin + 60 + 8 + 22 + 1 tests, `--test-threads=1`
- [x] Warning parity 161/161 (`cargo check`) vs pristine base; `--features debug-log` build clean
- [ ] Cluster smoke: not run (campaign engineer — parent reviews/merges; NAT64 is not configured in the loss-cluster smoke config)

## Deferred

- A dedicated operator counter for NAT64 error translations (the arm sets `counters.touched` like the #5690 path; no new `BatchCounters` field in this PR).

  owner-sync hop is refuted — reverse + fabric_ingress seeds are excluded
  from every export path — so the exposure is confined to the receiving
  node.)

  from unauthenticated frames. This REMOVES the fast path and its call
  site: session-less fabric-ingress packets take the normal miss path —
  policy under the #6458-validated zone, source-NAT applied, FORWARD

  function.

sync-race sub-window the fast path covered (peer-punted return packet
ahead of its synced session) reverts to a bounded drop: return-direction
resolutions are HAInactive until the RG converges and the sync lands
inside the 1 s incremental sweep — the trade the #6478 verifier
explicitly prefers over unauthenticated seeding.

## PR #6574 — userspace-dp: re-NAT outbound ICMP errors through source NAT (#6474) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-26)

Branch: `fix/6474-snat-outbound-icmp-error`

## Summary

- An internal host behind SNAT that emits an ICMP error about the session's REPLY (e.g. a port-unreachable for a closed socket) quotes the PRE-NAT tuple, so the quote's reply key EQUALS the forward session's primary key and the #5690 flowless session-fallback matched with `is_reverse == false`. The #5690 builders rewrite the outer source only under `had_dst_nat`, so the error went onto the wire with the INTERNAL (pre-NAT) source and a quote the remote cannot associate — RFC 5508 §4 violation, a silent internal-address leak on every outbound ICMP error through SNAT, and dead return-path PMTUD. The reversal also consumed the descriptor, so the error could not even fall through to clean untranslated forwarding.
- The session-fallback arms (`icmp_embed/nat_match_{v4,v6}`) now map the as-is and reply-key lookups separately and discriminate direction (an ICMP error is always addressed to the source of the offending packet, RFC 792): a reply-key hit with `is_reverse == false` on a pure source-NAT flow (`rewrite_src` set, no dst NAT) is OUTBOUND and is marked `EmbeddedIcmpMatch.outbound_snat`.
- `try_reverse_embedded_icmp_error` routes marked matches to the new `build_snat_outbound_icmp_error_{v4,v6}` builders: outer source → the SNAT address, embedded quote destination address → the SNAT address, embedded L4 destination port / echo identifier → the translated value (`rewrite_src_port`), with the outer IP + ICMP(v6) checksums and the embedded IP checksum recomputed (quoted L4 checksum stays informational, mirroring the #5690 policy). The outer destination and the quote's source are untouched — the error is addressed to the remote, exactly who must associate it.
- Scoping (bit-for-bit preserved): a DNAT-carrying or no-NAT flow keeps the pre-#6474 behavior (marker gated on `rewrite_dst.is_none()`); an error quoting the REPLY wire tuple (as-is hit, `is_reverse == true`) was already declined by the historical `rewrite_src.is_none()` gate into clean untranslated flowless forwarding — no new code needed there. The outbound re-NAT rides the admitted session and the #5690 queue tail (prebuilt forward, `flow_key = None`, gated on `allow_embedded_icmp`) — never a session/flow-cache authority.
- Originally stacked on PR #6572 (#6472); that PR has merged and this branch is rebased onto current master, so the diff here is exactly the #6474 change.

## Hot-path shape

No change to the flow-backed hot path. The flowless embedded-ICMP arm does one extra boolean disjunction per matched error (the two lookups were already performed; they are now mapped separately). The outbound builders mirror the #5690 builders' single output `Vec` on this cold per-error path. No new atomics, no ordering changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `poll_descriptor_snat_outbound_icmp_error_renat_v4_6474` — outbound dest-unreach via SNAT → exactly one prebuilt forward: outer src = the SNAT (external) address, outer dst = the remote, embedded quote dst addr + port translated to the external identity the server associates, outer IP / ICMP / embedded IP checksum oracles — **RED with the marker forced off** (pre-#6474 identity consume recreated)
- [x] `poll_descriptor_snat_outbound_icmp_error_renat_v6_6474` — the SNAT66 twin, with the ICMPv6 pseudo-header checksum oracle
- [x] `embedded_icmp_outbound_snat_marker_scoping_6474` — marker scoping: pure-SNAT outbound marks, DNAT-only does NOT, the #5690 inbound match never does
- [x] Regression: existing #5690 inbound tests (`poll_descriptor_embedded_icmp_reversal_reachable_on_flowless_path_5690`, `embedded_icmp_nat_match_*`, `tests_icmp_reject_reversal`) and the #6472 NAT64 tests stay GREEN
- [x] Full cargo suite GREEN: 4210 bin + 60 + 8 + 22 + 1 tests, `--test-threads=1`
- [x] Warning parity 161/161 vs base; `--features debug-log` build clean
- [ ] Cluster smoke: not run (campaign engineer — parent reviews/merges)

## Docs

`afxdp/README.md` flowless-arm bullets updated. `docs/feature-coverage.md` carries no embedded-ICMP behavioral claim beyond listing `allow-embedded-icmp` as a flow option, so no downgrade/correction is needed there.

## PR #6578 — policymatch: close two simulator-vs-dataplane divergences (#6576, #6577) [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-31)

Branch: `fix/6576-6577-policymatch-parity`

Two defects where `pkg/policymatch` — the package whose entire contract is
dataplane parity — reported **PERMIT for traffic the box DROPS**. Both were
found by the `claude-opus-review-001` campaign and both were missed by that
campaign's own triage, which filed from the report's suggested issue split
rather than walking every sub-report finding.

Both fail in the permissive direction, which is why they are worth fixing even
though neither changes enforcement: an operator using the simulator to certify
posture was told traffic was allowed that the dataplane drops.

## Commit 1 — #6577: v6 containment folded a mapped address

`net.IPNet.Contains` opens with `if x := ip.To4(); x != nil { ip = x }`, so an
IPv4-mapped IPv6 address folds to 4 bytes and then fails Contains' own
`len(ip) != len(nn)` guard against **every** 16-byte v6 prefix — `::/0`
included. The dataplane compares unfolded 128-bit values
(`userspace-dp/src/prefix.rs`), so a mapped destination matched a v6 DENY there
while the simulator fell through to a later PERMIT.

This is the untested half of #6377: that issue fixed *which family's rules* a
mapped address is tested against; this is *how containment is performed* once it
lands in the v6 branch.

The v4 branch deliberately keeps `Contains` — `net.ParseIP` returns a 16-byte
4-in-6 slice for a dotted quad while v4 prefixes are stored 4-byte, so the fold
is what makes those widths meet. Only the v6 branch moves to an explicit
16-byte masked compare, which is safe because a net reaches a v6 set only when
`ipnet.IP.To4() == nil`.

## Commit 2 — #6576: the junos-host walk had no fragment override

PR #6505 taught the dataplane's junos-host gate the #4569 fragment-associated
deny (#6465). It touched five files, none in `pkg/policymatch`, so
`show security match-policies ... to-zone junos-host ... non-first-fragment`
kept reporting PERMIT / "local delivery" for a fragment the box drops.

The structural cause explains the fix shape: the transit walk owned the
machinery as local closures declared at `Match:1133`, and `matchJunosHost`
returns at `Match:1107` — before they exist. The two walks *could not* share
code, so the host gate silently lacked an override rather than visibly
diverging. Both now drive one `fragDenyTracker`, so a future host-gate change
cannot drift again. Moving `Match` onto the tracker is behavior-preserving and
the existing #5572 suite covers it.

`overridePermissiveTerminal` is the half a naive port of the transit override
would miss: the host walk has no default-policy arm — its fall-through *is* the
permit — so the skipped deny must win there too. That mirrors the #6465
post-walk arm verbatim.

## PR #6579 — termsafe: close the two residual device-text terminal surfaces from #6468 [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-31)

Branch: `fix/6468-termsafe-residual-surfaces`

#6468 escaped the DHCP lease fields it named — hostname, HWAddress, DDNS FQDN —
on both terminal surfaces, and that part is correct and well tested. A hostile
post-merge review of that closure found **two other device/remote-supplied
strings still reaching an operator terminal raw**. Both Low; neither is the
LAN-adjacent DHCP vector the issue was filed for.

## D1 — DDNS `LastError`

It can carry a **provider response body**. Cloudflare
(`backend_cloudflare.go:166`) and Route 53 (`backend_route53.go:195,277`) embed
the provider's own message with `%s`. So a hostile or compromised provider — or
an operator pointed at an attacker-run endpoint — can land an OSC/CSI sequence
on the terminal via `show services dynamic-dns`. The other backends do not
reach the terminal with raw bytes: dyndns2 and duckdns wrap the response token
in `%q`, **generic omits the body entirely** (`backend_generic.go:242` formats
only the configured success tokens with `%v`), and rfc2136 reports a fixed
rcode string from `dns.RcodeToString`.

Path: `err.Error()` → `surface_a.go` `rt.lastErr` → `v.LastError` → the two
print sites.

Fixed at the **display** sites rather than per-backend: it covers the class
regardless of which backend produced the string, and is smaller than auditing
every backend's format verb.

> Worth noting this corrects an earlier review of mine, which cleared DDNS
> `LastError` as safe on the grounds that the embedding sites use `%q`.
>
> **Correction (Codex round, folded in `83aba402d`):** an earlier revision of
> this PR body and of the code comments said dyndns2/duckdns/**generic** all
> wrap the body in `%q`. Generic does not — it omits the body entirely. The
> correct tally is: **two** embed it unquoted (Cloudflare, Route 53), two quote
> it (dyndns2, duckdns), generic omits it, rfc2136 uses fixed rcode strings.
> The fix is unaffected — the two unsafe backends are the two identified — and
> sanitizing at the display site is precisely what makes this tally a
> documentation detail rather than a security dependency.

## D2 — raw `vtysh` stdout

Every `fmt.Print(output)` in `cli_show_routing.go` printed unmodified `vtysh`
output, and several of those commands render remote-advertised text: the BGP
peer's **hostname capability**, IS-IS **dynamic hostname TLVs**, OSPF router
IDs. All 12 sites are `c.frr.Get*` calls, so they are sanitized uniformly
rather than only the three BGP ones the review named — the same text class
reaches the terminal through each.

## PR #6580 — test(routes): bind the #6467 next-table cap as SHARED across families [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-31)

Branch: `test/6467-crossfamily-cap-binding`

Test-only. `pkg/dataplane/userspace` production code is untouched.

A hostile post-merge review of the #6467 closure found its code correct on both
sides but one invariant **unbound by any test**.

## The invariant

The kernel programs global next-table leaks from a **single shared priority
counter** — `pkg/routing` `nextTableManager.Apply` iterates v4 then v6 advancing
one `prio` — so the 100-entry window is shared, not per-family.
`buildRouteSnapshots` mirrors that by declaring `nextTableLeakCount` **outside**
the `addRoutes` closure, so the two global calls draw down one budget.

## Why it was never bound

Every #6467 fixture is v4-only. With one family in play a per-call counter still
caps at 100, so every existing assertion holds either way.

## Proven by mutation, not inspection

Moving `nextTableLeakCount := 0` into the `addRoutes` closure (making the window
per-call):

- all four shipped #6467 tests stay **GREEN** —
  `go test -run 'TestBuildRouteSnapshotsCapsConfigStaticNextTableLeaks|…'` → `ok`
- the new cross-family test goes **RED**

Under that mutation a 60 v4 + 60 v6 config publishes **120** FIB leaks against
the kernel's 100 — the #6467 kernel/dataplane verdict split restored in its
cross-family form, where leak #101+ resolves into the target VRF on the AF_XDP
fast path but the main table for a slow-path (XDP_PASS / IPsec-reinjected /
non-native-XDP fabric) packet on the same flow.

## What the test asserts

The per-family **split** — 60 inet + 40 inet6 — not merely a total of 100. A
total-only assertion is also satisfied by a 50/50 split, which the kernel would
never produce because it fills v4 first.

A second test covers the mirror gap the v4-only fixtures also left open: a
**v6-only** over-window config must cap too. A regression that capped only the
*first* `addRoutes` call would otherwise pass the cross-family test, since v4
fills the window there.

Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` package green.

## PR #6581 — dhcp: refuse a DHCPv6 IA_PD prefix-length of 0 or > 128 [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-31)

Branch: `fix/6531-iapd-prefixlen-guard`

Closes #6531

## Problem

A DHCPv6 IA_PD option whose IAPREFIX carries a wire prefix-length **> 128** decoded to a `<ip>/0` delegated prefix that was stored and then **advertised to the downstream LAN** in a Router Advertisement as on-link + autonomous.

`insomniacslk/dhcp` builds the prefix as `net.CIDRMask(int(length), 128)`. `net.CIDRMask` returns a **nil** mask when `ones > bits`, and `net.IPMask(nil).Size()` is `(0, 0)` — so `extractDelegatedPrefixes` reading only `ones` and discarding `bits` turned a crafted length of 129..255 into a `/0`. It survived `IsValid()` and `DeriveSubPrefix` and reached `pkg/ra`, which applies no sanity floor of its own.

Trust boundary: the upstream WAN DHCPv6 server, hostile or merely buggy. It also fed the RENEW echo path (`renew.go:155`), which re-offers held prefixes back to the server.

## Firsthand verification (not taken on faith)

Driving real wire bytes through the pinned library:

| wire length | library `Prefix` | `Mask.Size()` | old xpf result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **nil** | — | skipped by the pre-existing nil check |
| 1 / 48 / 56 / 64 / 128 | valid mask | `(n, 128)` | correct `/n` |
| 129 / 130 / 255 | non-nil, **nil Mask** | `(0, 0)` | **`2001:db8:1000::/0`** |

This **narrows the issue**: a wire length of 0 maps to a nil `Prefix` and was already skipped, so the issue's `ones == 0` reasoning is not reachable from the wire today. The load-bearing arm is `bits != 128` (a nil mask and a non-contiguous mask both report `bits` 0). `ones == 0` is retained as belt-and-braces for a genuine all-zero 128-bit mask, which only an in-process constructor can build.

## Skip the entry, not the whole reply — deliberate

The v4 twin `leaseFromACKv4` refuses the whole message, but that precedent does not transfer: a v4 ACK carries **exactly one** address+mask, so "skip the bad element" and "refuse the message" are the same action. The matching-shape precedent is the **multi-element** container in the same package — the RFC 3442 classless-route loop (`dhcpv4.go:428`) skips an entry whose mask reports `bits != 32` and keeps its siblings. This change follows that.

**Can a hostile server smuggle a bad prefix past the guard by pairing it with a good one?** No. A skipped entry never becomes a `DelegatedPrefix`, so it reaches neither the live set, the withdrawn set, nor the RA sender. Accepting the well-formed sibling grants the attacker nothing they could not get by sending that prefix alone. The alternative — refusing the whole reply — would additionally discard the IA_NA address and DNS servers in the same message, which only hands a *buggy* server the power to knock IPv6 WAN out entirely over one cosmetic malformation. If the skip empties both sets, the existing caller already treats the reply as unusable and retries rather than settling into an empty lease. Both orderings (bad-first, good-first) are pinned so the guard cannot be order-sensitive.

The guard also covers the **withdrawal** path. `reconcileDelegatedPDs` keys its withdrawal set by exact `netip.Prefix` equality, so a `/0` withdrawal cannot mass-revoke held prefixes today — but letting it through would log a phantom withdrawal and leave a containment-based matcher one refactor away from a wipe.

## Boundary table

| length | disposition | why |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | refused | no zero-length delegation; already skipped via nil `Prefix` (green before and after) |
| 1 | **accepted** | legal contiguous mask; RFC 8415 sets no floor. A minimum-size policy would be a new behavior change, not a decode fix — out of scope |
| 48 / 56 / 64 | **accepted** | over-reach guard: the common delegations still decode |
| 128 | **accepted** | legal single-address delegation — the bound is **inclusive**; a `>= 128` guard would reject a conforming server |
| 129 / 130 / 255 | refused | nil-mask decode |

## Tests drive the WIRE DECODER

This is the whole reason the bug survived. The pre-existing IA_PD tests build `OptIAPrefix` structs directly, which can only hold a mask `net.CIDRMask` already accepted. The option bytes here are **hand-rolled**: `OptIAPrefix.ToBytes` derives the wire length from `Mask.Size()`, so the library's own marshaller is structurally incapable of emitting a length > 128 — a round-trip can never produce the hostile input.

`decodeReplyWire` asserts the IAPREFIX sub-options **survived the parse**, so the tests cannot pass for the wrong reason if a future library version starts rejecting the option before xpf's guard runs.

**RED-on-revert** (restore `ones, _ :=`): the 129/130/255 rows, both orderings of the good+bad sibling test, and the malformed-withdrawal test fail with a live `/0` — real assertion failures, not a build break. The 0/1/48/56/64/128 over-reach rows and both `pkg/ra` tests stay **green**.

`pkg/ra/sender_prefixlen_6531_test.go` pins the blast radius from the consumer side: a `/64` still marshals as `PrefixLength 64`, and a `/0` that reaches that far **is** advertised on-link + autonomous — which is why the refusal must live at the DHCPv6 decoder, where the prefix is still distinguishable from an operator-authored one.

## PR #6582 — config: quote keys that would re-parse as a comment or marker [MERGED] (merged 2026-07-31)

Branch: `fix/6523-quotekey-relex`

Closes #6523

## Problem

`quoteKey` emitted a configuration key **bare** whenever every byte satisfied `isIdentChar`. That is the *lexer's* ident set — it admits `/`, `*` and `:` — and it is **not** the set of texts that survive a serialize/re-parse cycle. Four ident-char-only texts are re-interpreted **structurally** when the emitted config is read back, with zero parse errors and zero warnings:

| Value | What the re-read does |
|---|---|
| `//x` | `skipWhitespaceAndComments` consumes to end-of-line — the key **and every key after it on that line** silently vanish |
| `/*x*/` | Terminated block comment — swallowed silently |
| `/*x` | Unterminated block comment — swallows the rest of the config; `Parse` errors |
| `inactive:` | The parser's deactivation marker: **leading**, sets `Node.Inactive` on an unrelated statement; **inline**, TRUNCATES the key list |

Every serialize-then-reparse path is affected — HA config sync, rollback, archive, rescue — the paths an operator leans on when something has already gone wrong. Demonstrated end states: a `security-zone` compiled with **zero interfaces**, `permit junos-http` widened to **`permit any any any`**, and an IKE pre-shared-key becoming the literal string `ascii-text`.

Reachable from the plain `set` CLI (`set ... description inactive:`), not only hierarchical ingest. **Both** serializers are affected: hierarchical `Format` (`QuotedKeyPath`) and `| display set` (`joinQuotedKeys`), the latter replayed through `ParseSetVerb`, which drives the same lexer.

## Fix

The predicate is replaced, not denylisted — a hardcoded three-value list re-breaks the day someone adds a comment syntax. `bareKeySafe` asks the code that will actually read the config back:

1. **every byte is an `isIdentChar`** — retained as a NECESSARY pre-condition so the change is *monotone*: output only ever gains quotes, never loses them. Without it a bracketed endpoint `[2001:db8::1]:51820` would newly go bare, since `tryBracketedEndpointLiteral` (#5182) hands it back as one identifier equal to itself.
2. **the bare text re-lexes as exactly one `TokenIdentifier` whose value is the text itself, then `TokenEOF`.**
3. **it is not a parser-level marker** (`inactiveMarker`) — the one thing the lexer cannot see.

Quoting also re-arms the parser's existing defence: a quoted `"inactive:"` arrives as a `TokenString`, which `parseStatement` already refuses to treat as a marker (#4348).

## Premise verified firsthand

Confirmed on current master: `isIdentChar` admits `/`, `*`, `:`; the `//` arm consumes to EOL with **no error at all**; `inactiveMarker` detection runs post-tokenize (leading *and* inline).

## Hazard set independently re-derived — not taken from the issue

Rather than trust the issue's "exactly three", the set was re-derived by brute force through the real `Format`→`Parse`:

- **exhaustive** every 1-, 2- and 3-byte text over the lexer's full 74-byte ident alphabet (438,976 candidates),
- **exhaustive** every 1- to 5-byte text over the punctuation subset (5,908 hazards found),
- every 2-byte prefix with assorted tails, plus 2-byte pairs embedded mid-value and at the tail,
- each in three key positions (leading / inline / trailing).

**Result: zero hazards beyond leading `//`, leading `/*`, and exactly `inactive:`.** The issue's claim holds.

Two things worth flagging beyond the issue text:

- **`/*` has two distinct end states**, not one. A *terminated* `/*x*/` is swallowed silently (fail-open); an *unterminated* `/*x` eats the rest of the config and fails the load — the lexer returns `TokenError`, so `/*x` is the one hazard that is **not** silent. The other three (`//x`, `/*x*/`, `inactive:`) produce zero parse errors, which is what makes them dangerous. Both `/*` forms are fixed; both are pinned separately.
- **`#` was checked and ruled out.** It is a comment introducer but is *not* an `isIdentChar`, so it was already being quoted. Same for `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `;`, `|`, `"`.

## Not over-quoting

`TestQuoteKeyNoOverReach6523` asserts ordinary values still emit **unquoted**: `10.0.0.0/24`, `2001:db8::/32`, `ge-0/0/0`, `xe-1/0/0:3`, `reth0.50`, `<*>`, `<ge-*>`, `ascii-text`, `00:00:00`, `1024-65535`, `50%`, MAC addresses (`00:11:22:33:44:55` — `:` is the same byte that makes `inactive:` a marker) and application names (`junos-ssh`, `junos-http` — the operand of the policy widening this issue demonstrated), plus the near-misses `a//b`, `a/*b`, `a*/b`, `*/`, `/x`, `/`, `inactive`, `inactive::`, `inactive:x`. `/` is legitimate and common, so a naive "reject any value containing `/`" would be wrong — this guard is what catches it. Over-quoting would churn every archived config and every HA config-sync diff.
