## PR #13035 — config: normalize interface-valued qualified-next-hops and union shared-bind selectors (#12909) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/12909-campaign-pub`

Closes #12909

## Why

`qualified-next-hop <ifname>` (e.g. a floating backup over `st0.0`) stored the tunnel name in `NextHopEntry.Address`:

- **FRR** dropped it as a non-IP operand (`validFRRNextHopAddress`) instead of rendering an interface route — the backup silently never installed.
- **Userspace FIB** got the bare non-IP token, which the Rust FIB cannot parse (and a route whose only gateway looked bare-unresolvable was dropped by the #11317 row gate).
- The **#11422** route-vs-rendered-selector gate only inspects next-hops with an interface set, so the backup bypassed the XFRM blackhole check entirely.

A plain `next-hop st0.0` was already promoted to `{Interface: "st0.0"}` (#12036) — the qualified clause was the unnormalized twin. Separately, #11422 demanded that ONE VPN cover the whole routed destination, falsely rejecting aggregates split across complementary VPNs sharing a bind-interface — a topology #11380 explicitly supports.

## What

1. **`pkg/config/compiler_routing.go`** — the #12036 interface-only predicate is extracted to `interfaceOnlyNextHopValue` so both clause families share the exact definition.

## PR #13040 — config: merge sibling security-flow stanzas in compileFlow (#13009) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/13009-campaign-pub`

config: merge sibling security-flow stanzas in compileFlow (#13009)

## Why
The hierarchical parser keeps repeated blocks as separate siblings (same root cause as #4818/#4820/#4821) and `compileSecurity` calls `compileFlow` once per `security flow` stanza, but `compileFlow` read `tcp-session`/`aging`/`traceoptions`/`tcp-mss` with a **first-only** `FindChild` and **recreated** `TCPSession`/`Traceoptions` per stanza. So:

- a later sibling stanza's block was silently dropped (`flow { tcp-session { no-syn-check; } }` after `flow { tcp-session { initial-timeout 30; } }` compiled with `initial-timeout` wiped), and
- a later stanza's `traceoptions` wholesale-replaced the earlier stanza's, discarding its flags and packet filters

while the #3566 strict gates validate **every** sibling stanza — the compiler and the gates read different configs. Second half of #12888 (the validator half landed in #12888; this is the compiler half).

## What
- Every stanza-sensitive read in `compileFlow` now iterates `FindChildren` and merges into `sec.Flow`: `tcp-session`, `aging`, `udp-session`, `icmp-session`, `tcp-mss`, `traceoptions` (plus `traceoptions > file` and the value leaves `route-change-timeout`, `multicast-session-lifetime`, `syn-flood-protection-mode`).
- `TCPSession`/`Traceoptions` are find-or-create (#4821 doctrine) instead of recreated per stanza.
- Merge semantics: each block contributes the fields it sets; a scalar set by two blocks keeps the **last** occurrence (exactly what the last stanza already produced pre-fix); lists (trace flags, packet filters, unknown aging leaves) accumulate.
- Set-path configs are unaffected (SetPath merges same-key nodes) — pinned by a single-stanza `DeepEqual` control.

## Validation
- Regression RED on pristine master at `fefd415a5` (recreation wipe, first-only FindChild drop, traceoptions wholesale replace), GREEN post-fix.
- Single-stanza control compiles to the exact same merged picture (`reflect.DeepEqual`); conflicting-scalar last-wins control green on both sides.
- `go test ./pkg/config/` green (full package, 405s); downstream consumers (`pkg/cli`, `pkg/daemon`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/logging`) green.

## Risk
Fail-closed only: the strict gates already walked every sibling, so the compiler now stores exactly what they check. A leniently-loaded duplicate stanza now keeps earlier stanzas' values instead of discarding them; nothing that previously compiled changes meaning on the set path.

Closes #13009

## PR #13041 — userspace: release stale syn-cookie state on profile edits (#12876) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/12876-campaign-pub`

Closes #12876.

Why
----
`ZoneScreenState::reconcile_substate` carried the per-zone `syn_cookie_active_until_secs` latch across commits that changed the terms the latch was measured under: a `syn-cookie` disable/re-enable cycle or an attack-threshold (`syn_flood_threshold`) increase. The latch is derived state ("the aggregate crossed the attack threshold while cookies were on"), so after those edits a zone kept skipping its configured per-source SYN sketch and kept hard-dropping unrelated session-miss ACKs as `Invalid` for up to the remaining 64 s cookie epoch — on terms the latch was never measured under. Separately, `syn_cookie_profile_signature` omitted `syn_flood_src_threshold`, so tightening the per-source cap left already-validated sources certified to keep their #9945 bypass of that cap for up to the validated-cache TTL; the operator's commit silently did not apply to exactly the sources most likely to be flooding.

What
----
- `update_profiles` computes an activation-slice change (`(`syn_cookie`, `syn_flood_threshold`)` — exactly the fields that gate whether `syn_flood_gate` may set the latch) and passes it to `reconcile_substate`, which clears the latch when it changed, alongside the existing #9425 audit clear. Fail-closed in the only direction that matters: a still-real flood re-latches on its next over-attack SYN because the count-all aggregate counter is carried over untouched.
- `syn_cookie_profile_signature` widens to `(syn_cookie, syn_flood_threshold, syn_flood_src_threshold)`, so a per-source-cap edit bumps the zone's generation and decertifies validated clients (recertification = one fresh challenge). The latch is NOT cleared on a src-threshold-only edit: the source cap never gates the latch, and cookie-active deliberately skips it (D3/#9945).

Validation
----
- **RED** on pristine `origin/master` (`fefd415a5`, wt-12876red) with only the three new tests copied in: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 12876` — 0 passed / 3 failed with the defect's exact outcomes (stale-latch `Invalid` on both the threshold-raise and disable/re-enable ACK paths; stale `SynCookieBypass` after src-threshold tightening).
- **GREEN** post-fix: same filter — 3 passed / 0 failed.
- Full screen module suite post-fix: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- screen::` — 321 passed / 0 failed.

Risk
----
Clearing the latch costs at most one packet of cookie-active enforcement when the activation slice changes under a still-real flood (the next over-attack SYN re-latches). A src-threshold edit now re-challenges validated clients (one extra challenge per cached client, the fail-closed direction); the symmetric generation churn on a loosening edit is accepted because the signature is not directional. No wire-format, epoch, or key-ring change.

## PR #13042 — userspace-dp: gate the session-miss SYN alarm drain on the ingress zone (#13000) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/13000-campaign-pub`

## Why

`syn_alarm_pending` is a **worker-global** flag on `ScreenState`. #12875 gated the screen stages' drains on the ingress zone's own screen state, but the session-miss drain in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (the #12872 SYN-ACK miss-hook drain) still called `take_syn_alarm_event()` for **every** zone's session-miss packet. That arm runs for unscreened zones too, so an ingress zone with no screen configuration of its own could consume a screened zone's pending alarm and emit it as a log-only `syn-flood-alarm` against the **unscreened** packet's tuple and `from_zone_id` — the same mis-attribution class #12875 removed from the stages, surviving at the one drain site it did not touch.

## What

- The session-miss drain now runs only when `screen.zone_has_screen_state(from_zone)` — the #12875 helper over the same three sets (resolved profile, unresolved reference, inert reference).
- The gate short-circuits **before** the take: a zone with no screen state leaves the flag pending for the next screened-zone packet instead of clearing it unserved.
- Zones with screen state (the raising zone included) are unchanged — the drain still fires while the raising packet's tuple/zone are in scope, exactly as #12872 wired. No verdict, drop, counter, or cadence behavior changes; the alarm stays log-only (PERMIT).
- `ScreenState` doc comments and the afxdp README document the doctrine; the #12872 wiring guard's matcher follows the take call into the gated condition (its tuple/zone/reason assertions unchanged).

## Validation

- **RED** on pristine origin/master `fefd415a5` (test change only): `miss_syn_alarm_drain_is_gated_on_ingress_zone_13000` failed at the gate expectation; the three #12872 guards still passed.
- **GREEN** on the fix: the new guard passes; all four #12872 tests pass, including the real-descriptor-path `syn_ack_miss_alarm_emits_on_originating_packet_12872` (the raising screened packet still drains and emits its own alarm through the gated call); `screen::tests` 261/261; the #12875 stage regressions pass; the full `--bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite passes (7872 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored); `git diff --check` and `cargo fmt --check` clean for every touched line.

## Risk

Zero for packets whose ingress zone has screen state — the gate is true and the drain is byte-for-byte the #12872 behavior. For a session-miss packet on a zone with no screen state the drain is skipped and a pending flag is left for the next screened-zone packet; on current master both setters of the flag drain it same-packet, so no observable sequence changes today — this removes the latent ungated drain the #12875 doctrine left behind. Residual (out of scope, noted in `docs/log/13000.md`): the adjacent `take_scan_table_pressure_event` drain has the same latent shape but its only setter is the same-block scan/sweep hook, so it is same-packet balanced today.

Closes #13000

## Why
The `zoneByIface[unit0Name]` zone-ownership clause of the unit-0 collapse gate in `junosHostZoneExemptNetdevs` (`pkg/config/junos_host_deny.go`) is load-bearing: when unit 0 is **quarantined** (its key claimed by two zones, so `junosHostZoneByInterface` carries no row for it for any zone), a zone holding the bare physical ref keeps its ike / ident-reset exemptions **only** through that arm's bare-row retention. No committed test discriminated it — every #12838 fixture keeps unit 0 owned by the exercising zone, and that zone's unit row inherits the physical override via the #3720 base-union, so deleting the arm left the suite green while silently withdrawing the bare-ref zone's exemptions (fail-closed). Found as GLM review F1 of PR #12943; follow-up to #12838.

- `TestJunosHostZoneOwner12951QuarantinedCollapseKeepsBareRow` — same-netdev collapse (#12838's shape): bare row survives only via the arm; IKE/ident lists exactly `[ge-0-0-2]`.
- `TestJunosHostZoneOwner12951QuarantinedDistinctUnit0KeepsBareRowOnly` — distinct VLAN unit-0 netdev: physical row kept via the arm; quarantined VLAN device `ge-0-0-2.100` excluded from exemptions and ingress scope.
- `TestJunosHostZoneOwner12951QuarantinedClaimantFailsClosed` — quarantined claimant (zone-level ike/ident-reset) resolves no ingress netdevs and no exemptions; guards against quarantine erosion (sorted-name winner).
- `require12951Quarantine` asserts the conflicted-key exclusion as a precondition so the cell cannot silently degrade into a naive fixture that passes with the arm deleted.

## Validation

- Mutation probe (arm deleted: `} else if unit0 == nil || zoneByIface[unit0Name] != zoneName {` → `} else if unit0 == nil {`): both keep-bare-row cells FAIL with `IKE exempt = []` / `ident reset = []` — the exact silent fail-closed withdrawal the issue describes. Mutation reverted; targeted run PASS again.
- `go test ./pkg/config -count=1`: ok (433s). `go vet ./pkg/config/`: clean.

None beyond test maintenance; no runtime path touched.

The in-process simulator (`policymatch expandBookNameWithMemo`) skipped the empty overlay row and appended the static value, so `show security match-policies` and gRPC MatchPolicies reported static matching where the dataplane now enforces match-none. - `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go` — `expandBookNameWithMemo` returns the present-empty overlay row without descending into same-named static addresses/sets when the declared binding has `FailMode == "drop"`, directly and for members nested in address-sets (mirrors `addressBookExpansionResolver.expand`).

- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go` — doc now states the drop exception to the book-row parity claim.
- Regressions in both packages: simulator direct/nested/destination match-none with later-permit fall-through; NAT direct/nested resolution and fallback tokens; controls for the ready-feed union, the declared-but-absent fail-closed quarantine, pure-static aliases, and retain+empty keeping static.

## Scope: PARTIAL — the ruling-independent populated-RI leg only

**Refs #11416 (not closing):** the issue's maintainer ruling on the HA-safe config-write environment (design-v4 review options **A** cluster reservation / **B** HA-policy change / **C** isolated target — reviewer recommended C) is **not recorded** as of 2026-10-14 (last issue comment, 2026-10-10, defers exactly that decision). Per the assignment, this PR implements only what needs no ruling — the **populated-RI positive leg for the EXISTING IPv4/UDP probe shape** — using the gate's existing per-statement config-write pattern. The **IPv6 twin, TCP, and return-path legs (dual-stack echo sender, managed-peer responder) remain blocked on the ruling** and must stay open on the issue.

## Why

The gate proved only an empty-RI miss (`probe_leaked=0` vs a main-route control). That verdict is satisfied even if every legitimate VRF-routed packet also drops (over-deny): nothing proved a populated RI forwards the steered tuple, nor that removing the route stops it.

## What

- **Populated phase** — the gate commits a test-owned GRE member into the RI (`gr-0/0/1`: device-level `tunnel source <WAN_SRC> / destination <DEST_IP>` + unit-0 address from the reserved 198.18.0.0/15 family, RI list membership, wan-zone placement so the existing lan→wan permit policy and interface SNAT apply) and an exact `/32` static route for the probe destination. It re-offers the steered tuple with a **fresh source port** interleaved with a fresh near-miss control (tags R/B). The window's capture filter admits the steered probe **only in proto-47 form**, so a main-table fallback cannot score as the positive pass.
- **Route-removed discrimination** — deleting only the `/32` and re-offering another fresh tuple (tags D/E) must stop delivery **in any form** (GRE or plain); continued delivery is a FAIL ("populated leg FAILs when RI route removed").
- **Verdict contract** — `wire_routing_separation_window_verdict` takes 8 new required metrics. Precedence: miss-phase FAIL sticky; populated/removed violations are FAILs even over a miss-phase VOID or a weak sibling leg; thin/blind positive legs demote a would-be PASS to VOID; a miss-phase VOID keeps its slug. An authenticated FAIL now survives a failed restore (`restore_failed=1`) instead of being demoted to RESTORE_VOID — scoped to this gate only.
- **Ownership** — GRE member/address absence preflighted on both node baselines; cleanup deletes only owned leaves; destination/port session clears folded into one shared per-phase helper.
- Adapter required-metric set, temporal selftest, probe tags, harness-design row, and `docs/log/11416.md` updated.

## Validation

- `test/incus/harness-result-selftest.sh`: **246 passed, 0 failed**.

## PR #13060 — nfqueue,userspace-dp: enforce decrypted-ingress permits through the capture adjudication (#9506) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/9506-p2f-campaign`

Closes #9506

## Why

At master (`ba3ba7dd9`) route-based IPsec decrypted ingress is deny-only end to end: the enforcing capture pipeline counts a zone-PASS frame as `V1PermitSuppressed` (`pkg/nfqueue/pipeline.go` `submitEligible`), the Rust worker maps a successful D13/D14 adjudication to `ReinjectOutcome::WouldPermit` (`slowpath_reinject_9506.rs` `resolve_ipsec_inner_verdict`), and D14 explicitly deferred destination containment ("acceptable only while the terminal below remains deny-only"). The a6b4fe465 merge message says it outright: "Nothing forwards: every decrypted packet still DROP." The issue's acceptance cell — denied AND permitted flows with policy/counter evidence — was therefore unmet: this is the remaining unimplemented slice (P2 S9.5 FORWARD permit join).

## What

- **D14 destination containment (the landed prerequisite)**: a frame's destination must be inside the tunnel's selector projection (`PMechTunnelRow::allows_destination` over the construction-frozen ingress prefixes, which `from_snapshot` proves equal to the effective projection and the route-derived recomputation). Outside → `d22_destination_outside_selector` / DOMAIN_OVERLAP. The deny-only-phase cell that let a 0/0-routed outside destination Would-Permit ("source proof replaces destination prefix gate") is re-grounded to the new denial; an inside-selector Would-Permit cell is retained.
- **Rust permit join**: new `SUBMIT_FLAG_FORWARD` (0x04) submit-wire bit. At a Would-Permit verdict for a flagged frame the worker (still owning the slab) copies the frame and calls `SlowPathReinjector::forward_ipsec_inner_permit`, which arms the completion-table entry (`ReinjectCore::arm_write`) and enqueues a **leased** `PacketRequest{queue: Adjudicated}` on the delegated outlet. The existing writer thread's `pre_write_check` remains the authorization linearization point and `resolve_write` emits the terminal (Written/Refused/Fenced). An armed entry is NOT terminalized by its Would-Permit verdict; an enqueue refusal rolls back to a definitive Refused; unflagged frames (the D11 witness) keep the deny-only Would-Permit terminal.
- **Go permit arm**: `submitEligible`'s zone-PASS FORWARD arm mints a lease, tracks the pending reinject, and submits through a shared `submitAdmitted` tail extracted from `attestSubmit` (D11 now calls the same helper). A `Written` completion accounts `Written`/`Reinjected` and terminally DROPs the held original — the Rust re-entry carries the traffic; an NF_ACCEPT here could only create a duplicate. INPUT-hook frames and pipelines without a submitter/lease minter keep the fail-closed `V1PermitSuppressed` drop (D12a input permits remain a separate slice). A Would-Permit completion stays a suppressed DROP (defensive fallback, e.g. a Rust build that did not arm the write).
- **Counter/witness**: new Rust counter `ipsec_inner_permit_forward_armed_total` projected through `protocol/status.rs`, `server/helpers/status.rs`, `server/lifecycle.rs`, the Go decode (`IpsecInnerPermitForwardArmedTotal`), and Prometheus (`xpf_userspace_ipsec_inner_permit_forward_armed_total`).
- **Advisory/docs re-grounded**: the #5619 IPsec plaintext advisory and `docs/userspace-dataplane-gaps.md` now state the true residual (stateless FORWARD adjudication — no session/NAT/screen — and dropped INPUT) instead of "the zone does not govern decrypted traffic". `docs/log/9506.md` records the slice.

## Validation

- `go build ./pkg/...` PASS.
- `go test ./pkg/nfqueue` PASS except the pre-existing netns `TestMeasureMemory9506` (fails identically on pristine master — verified by stash).
- New Go cells: `TestEnforcingZonePassSubmitsForwardPermit9506` (submit with forward flag → Written completion → Reinjected++ + original DROP), `...AdmissionRefusedDrops`, `...TransportErrorIsUncertainDrop`, `...InputHookZonePassStaysSuppressed`, `...CompletionWouldPermitStaysFailClosed` — all PASS (RED against the deny-only master: Adjudicated stays 0).
- `go test ./pkg/config -run Plaintext`, `./pkg/api`, `./pkg/daemon -run 'IpsecCapture|9506'`, `./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run 'ProtocolStatus|PMech'` PASS; `go vet` + `gofmt` clean on touched files.
- Rust: `cargo check` PASS; `cargo test afxdp::ipsec_inner` 14 passed (2 new destination-containment cells, 1 re-grounded); `slowpath_reinject_9506::tests` 84 passed (2 new armed/unarmed join cells); `afxdp::coordinator` 322 passed.

## Risk

The permit is stateless: no session install, NAT, screen, or HA publication runs on the permitted path. INPUT permits (D12a Option A) remain denied; fragments are denied. The live SA-level denied+permitted witness, HA behaviour, and the per-packet pricing gate (V2) still require a live two-node run — disclosed residuals, not silently narrowed. Wire: one flag bit inside the existing submit flags byte; unset frames encode byte-identical.

## PR #13184 — test: enforce three-snapshot queue monotonicity in the CoS BE contention validator (#13067) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/13067-campaign-pub`

## Why

`analyze_phase` in `test/incus/cos_be_contention_validate.py` compared queue DrainShape telemetry only across the before→after endpoints (`deltas`) and before→during (`during_deltas`) — it never computed `queue_deltas(during_shapes, after_shapes)`. The harness therefore certified `PASS` when:

- the dataplane restarted between the during and after snapshots (counters reset to near zero from a cold `before`: before=0, during=500,000,000, after=1 → PASS, demonstrated in deep-review D10-07),
- a queue wedged right after t=2s (`after == during` for the remaining ~6s of the phase), or
- a non-expected queue's counters dipped and recovered to a net-zero before→after delta (invisible to every existing gate).

Closes #13067 (research-validated defect D10-07 from the deep-review source report).

## What

- `test/incus/cos_be_contention_validate.py`: `analyze_phase` now also computes `post_during_deltas = queue_deltas(during_shapes, after_shapes)` and enforces `before <= during < after` across **every** queue's `sent_bytes`/`park_root`/`park_queue` counters in **all three** windows via a shared `_negative_drain_delta_failure` helper (the existing before→after message text is unchanged). Each expected queue's during→after `sent_bytes` delta must also clear `min_expected_sent_bytes`, so traffic must flow in both halves of the phase under the same tolerant/strict operator knob (`MIN_EXPECTED_SENT_BYTES`, CLI `--min-expected-sent-bytes`). All new failures are per-cell `failure_reasons`; verdicts stay fail-closed, including the missing-snapshot fallbacks.
- `test/incus/cos_be_contention_validate_test.py`: four regressions, each green on every other gate so only the blind window distinguishes — mid-phase counter reset (the finding's decisive scenario), complete post-during stall, park-token regression invisible to the net before→after delta, and a net-zero dip on a non-expected queue.
- `docs/cos-best-effort-contention-harness.md`: the gates section and `MIN_EXPECTED_SENT_BYTES` semantics now state both-window enforcement.

## Validation

- **RED** on pristine `origin/master` (`ac4dcdfc1`) with only the regression cells added: `python3 test/incus/cos_be_contention_validate_test.py` → `Ran 19 tests ... FAILED (failures=4)`, each `AssertionError: 'PASS' != 'FAIL'`; the 15 pre-existing cells passed.
- **GREEN** post-fix: the same command → `Ran 19 tests ... OK`.
- `sh scripts/harness-census.sh` and `bash test/incus/harness-census-selftest.sh` reproduce the identical pre-existing `#12495` undeclared-harness problem on pristine master and on this branch (this change adds/removes no harness). Python-only change; the Go/Rust CI jobs are unreachable from it.

## Risk

Low. The gates only add FAIL directions on non-monotone artifacts; healthy monotone snapshots — including every pre-existing test fixture — are unaffected. Live-run operators who see genuine counter resets between snapshots now get an explicit FAIL naming the window, which is the intended fail-closed behavior.

## PR #13185 — harness: reject mixed target pairs in the mouse-latency reducer (#13066) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/13066-campaign-pub`

Closes #13066

## Why

Finding `D10-02` (deep-review source report `review-work.2e4cldwkh1`, research-validated): `shared_target_pair` returned `None` both when no valid rep declared a `(mouse_target, elephant_target)` pair and when the valid reps split across pairs, and `summarize_cell` only acted on the not-`None` case. A partially re-run cell summarised as a clean `OK` carrying no targets; `decide()` read `(None, None)`, skipped the #8259 `VOID-NOT-ATTRIBUTABLE` guard, and emitted a citable `PASS` even when 9 of 10 reps — including the median rep — terminated on a shared host. The docstring promised caller-side rejection of mixed pairs; it was never implemented.

## What

- `test/incus/mouse_latency_aggregate.py`
  - `_unique_target_pairs(valid)` mirrors `_unique_probe_configs`: more than one distinct declared pair records `summary["target_pairs"]` and `status = "INCONSISTENT-TARGETS"` with an early return, placed ahead of both the probe-config and valid-rep-count checks (attribution is the prior question — same ordering philosophy as the void check in `decide()`). `decide()` refuses the verdict through the existing status gate: `INSUFFICIENT-DATA`, exit 2. Legacy artifacts declaring no pair remain summarisable and are not voided on a guess.
  - Fix-direction tail: the across-rep spread follows the representative percentile (`iqr_p999_across_reps` for p999 gates; legacy `iqr_p99_across_reps` key retained) using interpolated inclusive quartiles (`statistics.quantiles(..., n=4, method="inclusive")`) instead of biased order-index slicing.
  - `shared_target_pair` removed (sole caller migrated); module docstring updated.
- `test/incus/mouse_latency_aggregate_test.py` — new `MixedTargetPairTests`: end-to-end positive control (consistent shared pair → `VOID-NOT-ATTRIBUTABLE`), mixed-pair cell rejection, the exact false-PASS shape from the finding (9/10 shared-target loaded reps, ratio 1.5 ≤ 2.0), `INCONSISTENT-TARGETS` precedence over `INSUFFICIENT-VALID-REPS`, representative-percentile IQR.
- `docs/per-5-tuple/state.md` — #1321 reducer contract records the target-pair agreement requirement; `docs/log/13066.md` action log added.

## Validation

- **RED on pristine master** (`ac4dcdfc1`): 4 of 5 new tests fail with the finding's signature — `'PASS' == 'PASS'` on the mixed-pair gate, status `'OK'` vs `INCONSISTENT-TARGETS`, `INSUFFICIENT-VALID-REPS` vs `INCONSISTENT-TARGETS`, missing `iqr_p999_across_reps`; the positive control passes pre-fix.
- **GREEN post-fix**: `mouse_latency_aggregate_test` 45/45; `make test-incus-lib` 551/551 OK; `make test-mouse-elephant-lib` OK (selftest + 24 shell tests).
- **End-to-end CLI** on synthetic on-disk cells: mixed-pair loaded cell → `INCONSISTENT-TARGETS` / `INSUFFICIENT-DATA` / exit 2; clean split-target 100E100M p999 run → `PASS` / exit 0 with interpolated `iqr_p999_across_reps` (4.5, not index-snapped).
- `test/incus/harness-result-selftest.sh` 252/253 — the single failure (#12140 census count 25 ≠ 24) reproduces identically on pristine origin/master; pre-existing, unrelated (no Makefile gate lines touched).

## Risk

Fail-closed by design: cells whose valid reps straddle two termination topologies now report `INCONSISTENT-TARGETS` instead of a verdict built on silently dropped targets; such a cell must be re-run against one target set — more reps cannot fix it. Default-path `iqr_p99_across_reps` values shift from index-snapped to interpolated quartiles (diagnostic field; no gate consumes it). Residual: a cell mixing legacy no-pair reps with new declaring reps still summarises under the declared pair (pre-existing, conservative — it can only void, never falsely pass, when that pair is shared).

## PR #13186 — test/incus: gate mixed-CoS precheck on MIXED_PORT and reap the harness group on wrapper abort (#13068) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/13068-campaign-pub`

Research-validated fix for D10-13: the mixed-CoS fairness gate burned a full run window (plus deploy and the exclusive harness lock) before discovering a dead `MIXED_PORT` listener, and any Ctrl-C / outer `timeout` orphaned the whole `start_new_session=True` harness process group — `fairness-harness.sh`, its `iperf3` elephants, and the `/metrics` scraper loop — contaminating subsequent benchmark runs.

## Why
- `fairness-harness.sh` ran the #8040 `target-services.sh check` gate before `MIXED_PORT` was even initialized, probing only `"$PORT"` — never `"$MIXED_PORT"` under `--mixed-cos` / `--mixed-cos-isolated`.
- `fairness_multi_sample.py` cleaned up its child group only inside `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. `SIGINT` (`KeyboardInterrupt`) and `SIGTERM` killed the wrapper mid-`communicate()` with no unwinding (SIGTERM's default disposition never runs `finally`), leaking the group and `/tmp/xpf-fairness-harness.lock`.

## What
- `fairness-harness.sh`: precheck moved after the defaults/deprecation checks (still before work dir, lock, and any traffic); predicate is now exactly the ports this run sends to — `("$PORT")` plus `"$MIXED_PORT"` when `MIXED_COS=1`, so an overridden `MIXED_PORT` is what gets gated. `SKIP_TARGET_PRECHECK=1` hermetic runs and the single-class single-port predicate are unchanged (no over-rejection).
- `fairness_multi_sample.py`: any abort unwinds through `_kill_process_group(pgid)` (`except BaseException: … raise`) plus a bounded leader reap in `finally`; `main()` converts SIGTERM to `SystemExit(128+signum)` so cleanup fires while the shell-visible status keeps the 143 death-by-signal convention. The abort kill is unconditional (not `poll()`-guarded) because the group can hold live descendants even after the shell leader exited. Normal, timeout, and error paths are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `docs/log/13068.md` records cause, coverage, RED/GREEN evidence, and residuals.

## Validation
- **RED on pristine origin/master (`ac4dcdfc1`), test-file only**: both mixed-precheck tests fail `['check','5202'] != ['check','5202','5205']` (and the `6205` override variant); SIGINT fails `harness process group NNN survived the wrapper abort`; SIGTERM fails `-15 != 143`; the two guard tests pass on master.
- **GREEN post-fix**: all six new tests pass; full `fairness_multi_sample_test.py` **49/49 OK**; `cos_port_grid_test.py` **8/8 OK**; `target-services-selftest.sh` passes; `bash -n`, `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, `shellcheck` clean (remaining shellcheck warnings and the harness-census positive-control failure are byte-identical on pristine master — pre-existing, unrelated).

## Risk
TEST-ONLY reachability. Operators gain an immediate exit-1 abort when the mixed listener is down — the intended gate; hermetic callers already bypass via `SKIP_TARGET_PRECHECK=1`. Wrapper exit codes for normal/timeout/error paths are unchanged; only signal aborts now clean up, and a SIGTERM'd wrapper still reports 143. Residual (separate finding, out of scope): the sweep/headroom wrappers' own trap coverage for their background captures (D10-14).

Closes #13068

## PR #13188 — userspace-dp: size the v8 equal-flow cap from the epoch-sticky flow count (#13071) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-14)

Branch: `fix/13071-campaign-pub`

userspace-dp: size the v8 equal-flow cap from the epoch-sticky flow count (#13071)

## Why

`SharedCoSQueueLease::equal_flow_cap_v8` multiplied the published
`current_target_per_flow` by the live instantaneous
`worker_active_flow_buckets[worker_id]` count (deep-review finding `D2-06`,
filed as #13071). Under `V8RateMode::EqualFlowSuppress`:

- A peer flow that drained mid-epoch — after consuming its per-flow target —
  decremented the live count while the epoch's fair budget had been computed
  for, and partially consumed by, the original count. The worker cap collapsed
  retroactively below bytes already spent, starving the remaining flows for the
  rest of the 200 µs epoch (up to `1/K` throughput loss per draining flow) and
  feeding artificially low grants into the next epoch's `Slowest`/`Mean`
  target calculation (progressive downward ratchet of `current_target_per_flow`).
- A live count that reached 0 at cap-evaluation produced a synthetic
  `Some(0)` cap: every remaining byte of the epoch was denied and
  `cap_hit_events` / `suppressed_grant_bytes` recorded suppression telemetry
  for a cap that was zero only because the flow count was.

## What

- `equal_flow_cap_v8` now derives the cap denominator from the
  epoch-consistent flow count:
  `max(live worker_active_flow_buckets, worker_equal_flow_active_samples for
  the acquirer's epoch tag)` — the same #1745 sticky-max acquire-time sample
  the rotation publisher uses as the epoch denominator — so the cap can only
  stay at or above the count the epoch's budget was sized for.
- The sample slot is read with tag equality against the acquirer's epoch tag
  (wrap-safe discipline of `record_equal_flow_active_sample`); a mismatched
  slot reads as 0 and falls back to the live count.
- A worker with no live flows and no epoch sample returns `None` instead of
  `Some(0)`, matching the existing read-only `target == 0` / stale-tag
  doctrine where rotation owns fail-open publication.
- Scope: `V8RateMode::EqualFlowSuppress` only; `CstructDefault` behavior is
  unchanged. Class-level bounds (epoch cap, outstanding-leased cap,
  per-worker fair share) are unchanged.
- Regression tests (both from the finding) and `docs/log/13071.md` added.

## Regression proof (RED → GREEN)

- `v8_equal_flow_cap_preserves_remaining_flow_share_when_sibling_flow_drains_mid_epoch`
- `v8_equal_flow_cap_is_none_for_worker_with_no_flows_and_no_epoch_sample`

Both **failed on pristine `origin/master`** with the exact defect values
(`Some(5_400)` collapsed cap; `Some(0)` synthetic zero — see the logs below)
and **pass with the fix**.

## PR #13253 — xdp: gate IPv6 WireGuard claims on declared payload (#13084) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

## Why

`parse_ipv6` reads UDP against the capture bound for its verifier-compatible 9-byte WireGuard classifier. If IPv6 `payload_len` is exactly the 8-byte UDP header, the payload offset equals `declared_end` and the truncation check accepts it, while Ethernet padding can supply a false type-4 byte.

Gate only IPv6 WireGuard transport-data classification on whether the declared datagram contains its first UDP payload byte. Keep capture-bound parsing and port extraction intact. ## PR #13256 — userspace-dp: report BA-reclassified queue in active-flow telemetry (#13077) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13077-campaign-pub`

Why: `FlowCache::active_flow_debug_entries` attributed every active flow to `descriptor.tx_selection.queue_id` frozen at seed time. A `ba_reclassify` flow deliberately serves successive packets on different CoS queues (per-packet DSCP/PCP), so per-queue `cos_counts` and the per-flow debug rows permanently credited the seed queue (e.g. a SYN seeded on queue 0 while all payload served on queue 3), corrupting `xpf_userspace_cos_active_flow_count` and the v8 equal-flow estimator (finding D5-01).

What: add `RewriteDescriptor::last_queue_id` (the one deliberately non-constant descriptor field, read only by the debug scan). `insert` seeds it from `tx_selection.queue_id`; `stage_flow_cache_hit` stamps the effective (BA-reclassified or pinned) queue through the entry borrow it already holds after the drop/policer gates. The scan reports `last_queue_id` with the seed as fallback only when never stamped, so queue-less entries stay unattributed. NOT changed: `tx_selection.queue_id` stays the frozen seed selection every other consumer reads correctly.

RED with the scan reverted to the seed queue (queue 0 instead of 3); GREEN post-fix (`flow_cache::` 121 passed). Full `--bins` suite 7887 passed, 1 failed (`wire_invariant_default_specimens`, also failing on pristine master 8e26b24d8).

Risk: single `Option<u8>` store on the forwarded cache-hit path; no extra cache scan, allocation, or atomic. Dropped/TTL-expired/rejected hits never reach the stamp; flows serving on multiple queues within one window report their most recent queue.

Closes #13077

## PR #13310 — config: warn on inert snmp/system knobs in every AST spelling (#13089) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13089-campaign-pub`

Closes #13089 (research D7-13, deep-review finding: `snmpInertKnobWarnings` / `systemInertKnobWarnings` inspect only `node.Children` / `FindChild`, missing packed bodies, flat-set chains, and subsequent sibling blocks).

## Why

`snmpInertKnobWarnings` walked raw `node.Children` through a one-level `nodeHasSub`, and `systemInertKnobWarnings` read one `FindChild` block per group, so security-relevant accept-but-inert advisories — `snmp community view` (the community answers the full ifTable), `snmp community logical-system` (nested source restriction NOT applied), `system ntp authentication-key` (NTP auth NOT enforced), `system login retry-options` (login lockout NOT enforced) — were silently suppressed on AST shapes the compilers accept and compile:

- flat-set chains (`set snmp community <c> authorization ro view v` nests `view` under `authorization`, #8778; `set system services ssh root-login deny rate-limit 5` nests `rate-limit` under `root-login`),
- two-level community containers (`snmp { community { <name> { view v; } } }`),
- second sibling blocks (`system { login {...} login {...} }` — `FindChild` saw only the first),
- brace-elided bodies packed on the block's or the whole `system` line's own Keys (#2419).

The advisory is the only defense for these knobs (they commit clean and compile to nothing); a line break decided whether it fired.

## What

`pkg/config/compiler_system.go`:

- `snmpInertKnobWarnings` now takes the `snmpChildren` list `compileSNMP` already built with `packedBodyChildren`, and the community search (`communityHasInertStatement13089`) spans the community's Keys tail, every name block of a two-level container, and the whole statement subtree (`subtreeHasStatement13089`).
- `systemInertKnobWarnings` walks every sibling `login`/`ntp`/`internet-options`/`services` block, hoists flat-set chains with `expandRun9235` (`systemServicesSSHSchema13089`), reads one-liner bodies packed on a block's own Keys via `blockHas`, and synthesizes the braced shape for a fully packed `system` line via `packedBodyChildren` guarded on empty `Children` (a node can carry both a packed tail and a braced body — `system host-name fw1 { ... }` — and the synthesis must not drop the body).
- `internet-options` extras are collected recursively (`collectInternetOptionsExtras13089`) so an extra chained under the modelled leaf is still named.
- Advisory wording, dedup, and the never-echo-secrets rule (community name, NTP key value) are unchanged.
- NOT changed: snmp tail keywords `schemaSNMP` does not declare (`snmp view v ...;`, `snmp health-monitor;` brace-elided on one line) stay advisory-silent — `packedBodyChildren` refuses to synthesize undeclared tails and no compiler reader sees them either; declaring them is separate schema work.

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/compiler_inert_knobs_13089_test.go`: 13 shape cells (snmp chain ×3, two-level container ×2; system sibling blocks ×3, chained ssh, packed ssh/ntp one-liners, packed `system` line, internet-options chain) verified **RED on pristine origin/master `18c285c29`** and green on this head; regression guards for the already-warning spellings plus negative controls (no new advisories on modelled-only configs; secrets never echoed) green on both.
- `go test ./pkg/config/` full suite: **ok, 6144 top-level test results**, 0 failures (~400 s).
- Rebased onto current master (`2ced657ce`, #13090 sibling-chassis fold landed mid-flight — no overlap) and re-gated green.

## Risk

Low. Advisory-only: no compile output, gate, or dataplane behavior changes; warnings appear on configs that previously committed silently, which is the point. Tolerant loads (`Store.Load`, `SyncApply`) of configs using these spellings now surface the advisories too. Residual: brace-elided one-line snmp knobs whose keywords are not declared in `schemaSNMP` (view/trap-options/health-monitor/rmon) remain advisory-silent in that one spelling — the compiler is blind to them as well; worth a follow-up schema-declaration change.

## Why

`buildOneRuleSnapshot` only poisoned undefined-scheduler DENY/REJECT rules when `LenientContentDropped` was set. Programmatic or partial configs could therefore publish an inactive deny and let traffic fall through. Rejection diagnostics also misattributed generic application carriers and dropped co-occurring malformed-shape / unknown-child causes.

## What

Always poison undefined-scheduler DENY/REJECT rules; attribute the rejection to the scheduler. Report malformed-zone and unknown-child metadata independently and suppress generic-only carrier attribution when metadata identifies the cause. Add focused D4-13 regressions and `docs/log/13169.md`. PERMIT scheduler behavior and wire fields remain unchanged.

- Full `go test -count=1 ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/...` has unrelated pre-existing failures: pristine master reproduces the package failures; the `format` subpackage passed.

## Risk

Partial/programmatic configs with an undefined scheduler on deny/reject now refuse the whole snapshot instead of publishing an inactive rule, matching the fail-closed contract. Existing unrelated full-suite failures are documented in `docs/log/13169.md`.

Closes #13169

## PR #13420 — userspace-dp: keep GRE forwards endpoint-pinned (#13419) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13182-correction-campaign-pub`

Why: #13410 stamped a GRE TUN-origin forward decision with the inner tunnel VRF's install-table identity. Stamped sessions validate that registry before the tunnel-endpoint resolver; if the inner `cust` row disappears while the endpoint and underlay remain live, re-resolution returns `TableUnavailable` instead of resolving the configured endpoint. Tunnel outcomes are explicitly endpoint-pinned and table-free by `install_table_stamp_for_miss`.

What: Restore `(0,0)` for the GRE forward decision and compute the tunnel table identity only at its existing uses for local-source admission and table-scoped reverse synthesis. Extend the existing real GRE VRF test: assert the cust row exists, remove only that row, then require the forward session to re-resolve to `ForwardCandidate` on the expected GRE endpoint. This supersedes the stamp-equality test from #13410 and refutes the D6-08 default-table-leak premise.

Validation: The real endpoint-resolution assertion failed against a temporary #13410-stamp mutant with `TableUnavailable` (expected `ForwardCandidate`). `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bins afxdp::wg::decap_tests -- --nocapture`: 41 passed. `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bins`: passed with existing warnings.

Risk: This removes only the unintended install-table gate from endpoint-pinned GRE forwards; reverse VRF stamping and the forward flow key's routing domain remain unchanged.

Closes #13419

## PR #13473 — userspace-dp: detect session gaps on trusted headers (#13238) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13238-campaign-pub`

Why: readLoop previously handled oversized and undecodable session frames before detecting gaps. During the decode-resync cooldown, refusal could acknowledge past missing events; treating an over-ceiling garbage header as a real gap would also bypass the oversized-frame resync limiter.

What: detect gaps on ordinary session frames before decode; for oversized frames, detect a gap only after a within-ceiling drain succeeds. Keep over-ceiling and failed-drain headers untrusted and rate-limited. Add regressions for undecodable frames, trusted oversized gaps, and forged over-ceiling headers. Record the remediation in docs/log/13238.md.

- `go build ./...` passed.

## PR #13586 — userspace-dp: distrust stale IPv6 session offsets (#13529) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13529-campaign-pub`

## Why
The IPv6 session parser trusted a relative L4 offset even when the #9900
L3 stamp check had rejected the L3 offset. Pairing the corrected L3 with
the stale relative offset could read payload bytes as ports and fabricate
a session tuple.

## What
Use `nibble_checked_l3` for the IPv6 frame parser and apply the metadata
relative L4 displacement only when `stamp_trusted` is true. Otherwise,
derive L4 from the packet's IPv6 extension-header chain. Add a fail-on-revert
stale-offset test plus a trusted-stamp control and document the producer
trace in `docs/log/13529.md`.

## Validation
- Pristine master regression: RED (expected source port 0x1234; got stale
  payload port 0xabcd).
- Fixed worktree regression: 1 passed.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp inspect_iplen_tests`: 55 passed.
- Full `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp`: blocked by the unrelated
  `runtime_view_publish_and_read_sites_are_pinned` source-canary test (six
  violations in untouched runtime-view files).
- `cargo clippy -p xpf-userspace-dp --tests -- -D warnings`: blocked by
  existing lints in untouched `build.rs`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `rustfmt --check` on touched files find
  existing formatting drift outside this change; no broad formatting churn
  was applied.

## Risk
The IPv6 frame parser's untrusted-stamp path now uses the wire extension
header walk; the existing declared-end and non-first-fragment checks are
unchanged. Full-crate runtime-view canary, strict-clippy and format failures
remain unrelated to this patch.

Closes #13529

## PR #13587 — userspace-dp: fence deferred flowless NAT and segment TCP (#13527) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13527-campaign-pub`

Why: Neighbor-retry evaluated the IPsec selector fence before
retry_flowless_fragment_nat populated decision.nat. A selector covering only
the translated tuple therefore did not fence the deferred fragment, allowing
cleartext TX. The retry path also skipped TCP segmentation and could queue an
oversized datagram whole.

What: Move the #10683 selector fence after retry-time flowless NAT and reuse
the forwarded TCP segmentation builder before PMTU/PTB handling. Add retry
regressions for post-NAT selector coverage and oversized TCP segmentation.
Record the change in docs/log/13527.md; NAT64 behavior remains unchanged.

Validation:
- Regression RED before the fix: 0 passed, 2 failed (post-NAT selector escape
  and whole oversized TCP replay); GREEN after: 2 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml afxdp::neighbor_dispatch::`:
  47 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp`:
  passed.
- Full `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml`: failed in the
  unrelated `runtime_view_publish_and_read_sites_are_pinned` canary (30 passed,
  1 failed in that target, reporting runtime-view violations in untouched files).

Risk: Segmented retry frames use the existing copy-TX segmentation builder,
limited to oversized TCP frames. The full-suite runtime-view canary failure
remains.

Closes #13527

## PR #13594 — forwarding: admit missing-neighbor seeds (#13526) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13526-campaign-pub`

Closes #13526

## Why
Missing-neighbor seeds committed sessions without publishing first-fragment associations and refused pressure-eligible TCP openings at capacity. A published first-fragment association also needs to carry its authenticated translation decision through the missing-neighbor safety fence for a following fragment.

## What
Install eligible same-family fragment associations after seed session commit using the raw ingress authority. Apply the existing TCP opening pressure-shed policy before refusing a missing-neighbor seed, including session/BPF/NAT cleanup and replication. On a live association hit, preserve its committed translation through the missing-neighbor NAT-miss fence so the tail can be parked for retry. NAT64 fail-closed handling remains unchanged.

## Validation
- Pristine-master runs: the association and pressure-shed regressions failed at their expected acceptance assertions.
- Rebased branch: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp missing_neighbor_first_fragment_installs_frag_assoc_13526 -- --nocapture` — passed; the following SNAT fragment is parked with its rewrite and no untranslated-fragment drop.
- Full `afxdp::tests_fragment::` module: 36 passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml -- --check` — not clean; it reports extensive formatting diffs across existing workspace files.

## Risk
Only live, authority-scoped association hits bypass the NAT-miss fence. Pressure shedding follows the existing incomplete-TCP-opening policy; no new idle-session expiry policy or NAT64 admission behavior is introduced.

## PR #13597 — forwarding: preserve missing-neighbor fragment hits (#13526) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13526-frag-assoc-followup`

Closes #13526

This follow-up completes the fragment-association path merged in #13594. Review found that an association hit uses raw ingress authority, while MissingNeighbor seed publication must capture that authority before owner-RG gating; the generic NAT-miss fence also needs authenticated association-hit provenance for port-dependent translations.

## What
- Publish the seed association with the same raw ingress fragment authority used by normal session installs.
- Carry authenticated, session-live fragment-association-hit provenance through the MissingNeighbor NAT-miss fence, allowing its committed app-scoped SNAT rewrite to accompany a tail parked for neighbor retry.
- Keep established sessions out of pressure shedding and refuse a new seed when no pressure-safe victim exists.

Only live, authority-scoped association hits bypass the NAT-miss fence. Existing worker housekeeping remains responsible for expiry; this does not add an extra packet-path sweep. NAT64 missing-neighbor fail-closed behavior is unchanged.

## PR #13605 — nat: preserve NAT off exemption for empty app sets (#13547) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13547-campaign-pub`

## Why

Tolerant application-set expansion can return no members or an error for an authored set. In a mixed valid/empty list, DNAT/SNAT emitted only valid member terms, narrowing `then ... off` and letting other traffic fall through to later NAT rules.

## What

Treat empty and failed application-set expansions as broken match axes in DNAT and SNAT off rules, matching the existing #12631 match-all over-exemption behavior. Translation rules remain fail-closed. Add DNAT/SNAT mixed, empty-only, broken-set-only, and translation controls.

- Full `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=1` ran but failed on unattributed package assertions, snapshot goldens, and Unix socket path errors; see `docs/log/13547.md`.

## Risk

Tolerant `off` rules with malformed or empty sets now exempt all traffic on the application axis, intentionally bounded by their other match fields. No change to translation-rule behavior.

## PR #13606 — nat: allow DNAT prefixes and count exemptions (#13548) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13548-campaign-pub`

## Why

`CompileUserspaceShim` reaches `compileNAT` before snapshot creation. The shim rejected non-host DNAT match CIDRs even though the snapshot carries them as `destination_prefix` and Rust installs them through longest-prefix matching. It also skipped DNAT `off` rules before allocating counter IDs, so the exemption snapshot could not carry its per-rule ID.

## What

Accept non-host CIDRs in the DNAT match destination validation while keeping pool addresses host-only (Rust parses pool addresses as a single `IpAddr`). Allocate the DNAT counter ID before continuing over `off` exemptions. Add IPv4/IPv6 prefix and DNAT-off counter regressions plus a pool-prefix rejection control. Record the change in `docs/log/13548.md`. No Rust or snapshot-builder changes; those paths already support the accepted match-prefix shape.

## Validation

- RED on pristine `origin/master` (`d7fe769aa`): the focused regression rejected IPv4 `/24` and IPv6 `/64`, and reported no `dnat/rs-dnat/r-off` counter key.
- GREEN: `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/dataplane -run 'TestCompileNATDNAT(PrefixMatchCompiles|PrefixPoolStillRejected|OffGetsCounterID)13548' -count=1`.
- `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/t go vet ./pkg/dataplane/...` passed.
- Full `go test ./pkg/dataplane/... -count=1` and `go test ./pkg/dataplane -count=1` fail on unrelated current-tree checks (stale XDP manifest/object, method/import canaries, snapshot/protocol goldens, Junos scope/parity, and Unix-socket path errors); see `docs/log/13548.md`.

## PR #13631 — grpcapi: align annotate authorization with handler parsing (#13628) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13628-authz-followup`

## PR #13732 — userspace-dp: gate quoted ICMP identifier rewrite on bearing types (#13650) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13650-campaign`

Why:
The four embedded-ICMP NAT builders rewrote quoted ICMP/ICMPv6 bytes 4..6 as an echo Identifier for every quoted message type. For Destination-Unreachable, Time-Exceeded, Packet-Too-Big, Parameter-Problem and Redirect quotes those bytes are the unused/MTU/gateway word; overwriting them with a NAT port/identifier corrupts the quoted error. The v6 reversed builder also repaired the quoted checksum with an incremental identifier-only adjust ignoring the embedded source-address rewrite, leaving it invalid over the egress pseudo-header.

What:
Gate every quoted-ICMP identifier write in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/builders.rs` on the shared `icmp_identifier_bearing` predicate; on both v6 builders recompute the quoted ICMPv6 checksum in full over the egress embedded pseudo-header when identifier-bearing.

Validation:

Full `--bins`: 7959 passed, 1 failed (`f035_parked_fragment_overlap_10659`, also failing on clean master in the same revert run), 8 ignored.

Risk:
Quoted non-identifier messages keep their semantic word; quoted echo identifiers still restored and now verify over the egress v6 pseudo-header.

Closes #13650

## PR #13733 — userspace-dp: enforce PBR deny terms on packet-varying hits (#13648) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13648-campaign`

Why:
Established-session PBR revalidation delegates discard/reject semantics to the input-filter evaluator. When a filter has a per-packet condition, the session-hit path instead runs only the non-routing walk, which defers a matching routing-instance term as Accept. Packets on established sessions consequently bypass PBR deny terms.

What:
Preserve the ordinary per-packet evaluation, then evaluate the routing-instance walk against the same packet predicates when the ordinary verdict permits and the filter affects route lookup. PBR denies use the counted evaluator and PBR log source. Added IPv4/IPv6 discard and reject regression coverage. No other path changed.

Risk:
The operator-configured PBR discard/reject terms now apply to established session hits when packet-varying filter terms are present; no other behavior is intentionally changed.

## PR #13737 — policy: evict stale denies on scheduler recovery (#13639) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13639-campaign-zero`

## Why
A scheduled PERMIT is fail-closed while its scheduler lease is expired. Traffic may then fall through to an unscheduled DENY and cache a PolicyDenied result. When the lease recovers, that stale deny previously remained live and blackholed traffic. Scheduled DENY/REJECT entries were also seeded during expiry only to be evicted on the next lookup.

## What
- Invalidate cached PolicyDenied entries on scheduler recovery when scheduled policy eligibility can change, without flushing unrelated forwarding entries.
- Keep existing expiry invalidation for scheduled DENY/REJECT rules.
- Skip cache seeding for scheduled DENY/REJECT verdicts while the lease is expired to prevent seed-then-evict churn.
- Add a recovery regression and docs/log/13639.md.

## Validation
- RED on pristine master 761931ff: the new regression fails at the recovery cache-miss assertion.
- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp afxdp::flow_cache::tests:: -- --nocapture`: 70 passed.
- Full bin suite: 7959 passed, 1 failed, 8 ignored. The #10659 failure reproduces on pristine master with the same assertion.

## Risk
Recovery evicts cached PolicyDenied entries when scheduler eligibility can change; unrelated forward cache entries remain available. No wire or control-plane behavior changes.

Closes #13639

When ctrl is disabled, the degraded shim could parse frames from attached interfaces absent from the adjudicated ingress set. Raw-L3 source octets can then affect parse and local/control decisions. Passing such unadjudicated traffic to the kernel would violate the disabled-path fail-closed policy, so the fix drops it before parsing.

## What
- Gate `degraded_ctrl_disabled_action` on the ADJUDICATED ingress flag before parsing any bytes; preserve disabled-control DROP accounting.
- Add Rust source-order regression and privileged raw-L3 BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN regression; seed adjudicated rows in existing fixtures and clarify the distinct enabled #8279 pass behavior.
- Rebuild and include the verifier-approved BPF object and generated verdict/manifest.

## Validation
- Focused Rust regression: RED on pristine master and guard-reverted, GREEN after fix and after rebase.
- BPF verifier PASS: 767,365 processed instructions, 23.26% headroom.
- Full Rust suite: 7,959 passed, 1 failure, 8 ignored; the failing case also fails alone on pristine master.
- Full Go package: 8 unrelated failures reproduced on pristine master. Focused raw-L3 privileged test skipped because `RemoveMemlock` is denied.

See `docs/log/13632.md` for exact commands and evidence.

## PR #13775 — userspace-dp: adjust zero quoted ICMPv6 checksums (#13773) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13773-campaign-pub`

Why:
The quoted ICMPv6 checksum repair in both reverse and outbound NAT
builders skipped incremental adjustment when the original checksum
field was zero. ICMPv6 does not use zero to mean checksum omitted, so
rewritten quoted addresses or identifiers left a stale checksum for
the receiver.

What:
Apply RFC 1624 checksum deltas regardless of the current quoted
ICMPv6 checksum in both builders, preserving zero-result
canonicalization. Add a regression using a valid, genuinely-zero
quoted ICMPv6 checksum that exercises both builder paths. NOT changed:
ICMPv4 and UDP checksum omission semantics.

Validation:
New regression RED before fix (stored 0 vs expected 40126), GREEN after
fix; `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml icmp_embed_`
passed (5 tests). Full `--bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite had one known
unrelated failure: f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659.
`cargo fmt -- --check` reports existing formatting differences across
numerous unrelated files.

Risk:
Quoted ICMPv6 packets with a zero checksum now receive the required
delta after NAT rewrites. No ICMPv4/UDP zero-checksum behavior changes.

Closes #13773

## PR #13778 — fairness-eval: align Cstruct RSS gate (#13658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13658-observed-contract`

## Why

`fairness-eval` reports the selected fail-closed Gate-2 `cstruct`, but passed the raw observed-distribution Cstruct into the `cstruct-max` RSS expectation. An accepted stale-count overcount could therefore fail a ceiling against a value different from the one reported and used by Gate 2.

## What

Pass the selected Cstruct to RSS expectation evaluation, without normalizing its distribution input. Thus `cstruct-max` checks the same chosen Cstruct shown in the report, while distribution-based expectations (`max-worker-flow-share`, `balanced`, active-worker count) and report fields such as `max_worker_flow_share` continue to describe observed RSS placement. The black-box tests now pin both sides: the `[4,4,4,3,0,0]` observed max share is exactly `4/15`, while its selected normalized Cstruct is 0 and passes `cstruct-max:1%`.

## Adjudication

This is a narrow production fix, not a re-pin to make all consumers use trimmed data. Commit `66bd82e28` (“Preserve observed RSS expectation input”) deliberately preserves the observed distribution for RSS-placement expectations: trimming `[4,4,4,3,0,0]` to `[3,3,3,3,0,0]` for those expectations would hide a worker's actual 4/15 share and falsely pass a 25% cap. That contract and its existing black-box test are retained. `cstruct-max` is different: it constrains the Cstruct used by Gate 2, so it must compare against the selected, report-visible Cstruct rather than `cstruct_raw`. The new regression failed on pristine master before the fix and passes afterward.

## Validation

- RED on pristine `origin/master` (`5e8c92302`): `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --test fairness_eval_blackbox cstruct_max_expectation_uses_selected_gate2_cstruct -- --nocapture` failed with subprocess status 1 instead of expected 0 (raw Cstruct ~0.125 vs selected Cstruct 0).
- GREEN: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --test fairness_eval_blackbox -- --nocapture` — 23 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin fairness-eval` — 63 passed.
- The new regression passed five consecutive runs.

## Risk

Only `cstruct-max` changes behavior, now aligned with Gate 2 and the reported Cstruct. Other observed-distribution RSS expectations, report schema, and packet path are unchanged.

Closes #13658

## PR #13794 — userspace-dp: gate companion retention on established state (#13679) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13679-campaign`

## Why

`SessionTable::companion_keeps_alive` rejected a TCP companion only when `handshake_pending` was true. A bare-SYN install leaves both halves `established=false, handshake_pending=false`, so a fresh but un-replied companion could repeatedly re-stamp its paired entry and keep it alive beyond the paired entry's shorter opening timeout (including a per-zone SYN-flood override).

## What

Require the companion to be established as well as non-pending before it can retain its peer. Add regression coverage for asymmetric opening-window TCP expiry in both directions, SYN retransmit-only activity, continued retention by an established companion, and un-replied app-gated UDP parity. Record the change in `docs/log/13679.md`.

## Validation

- RED on the pre-guard predicate: 3 un-replied TCP/UDP regressions failed; the established-companion control passed.
- GREEN before rebase: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml companion_established_13679 -- --nocapture` — 4 passed.
- `cargo build --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml` passed before rebase.
- Full crate test run before rebase: 8001 passed, 2 failed, 8 ignored. Failures were `f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659` and `c3_forward_control_survives_full_window_per_permit_shape_10591`; baseline attribution was not established.
- After rebasing on newer master, focused tests could not compile because master has `error[E0432]: unresolved import promote::purge_translated_synced_hit` at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/mod.rs:59`; this issue does not touch that code.

## Risk

Only an un-established or handshake-pending companion is newly ineligible to refresh its peer. Established, non-pending session retention remains unchanged.

Closes #13679

## PR #13797 — userspace-dp: reject unsupported GRE flags on decap (#13662) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13662-gre-reserved0-v2`

## Why

The native GRE decapsulator checked the version and Routing bits, but accepted legacy Strict Source Route (`0x0800`) and Recursion Control bit 0 (`0x0400`). A matching GRE peer could therefore have an unsupported header promoted as tunnel traffic.

## What

Reject only flags masked by `0x0c00` before reading optional fields. The regression distinguishes these unsupported bits from RFC 2784 §2.3 bits `0x03f8`, which receivers must ignore, and confirms valid Key/Sequence behavior remains unchanged. Transit classification is not changed; the finding is scoped to native decapsulation.

## Validation

- Regression failed on pristine `origin/master`: `unsupported_legacy_gre_bits_are_refused_13662` decapsulated `0x0800`.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp gre_reserved0_13662`: 2 passed.
- `cargo build -p xpf-userspace-dp`: passed.
- Full crate test run: exit 101 with three failures in unrelated tests; the parked-fragment retry test also fails on pristine master, and both GRE host-inbound tests pass individually on pristine master.
- `rustfmt --check` on the regression file passed. Workspace formatting check reports existing drift in untouched files.

## Risk

Frames carrying either unsupported legacy bit are no longer native-decapsulated. RFC-mandated must-ignore flags and RFC 2890 optional fields remain accepted.

Closes #13662

## PR #13803 — userspace-dp: gate conntrack RMW operations (#13668) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13668-campaign-pub`

# #13668 — gate conntrack RMW operations through TupleGate

- **Base**: fc806aa (origin/master at implementation)
- **Branch**: fix/13668-campaign-pub

## Why
`restamp_bpf_conntrack_policy`, `restamp_bpf_conntrack_app_id`,
`refresh_bpf_conntrack_last_seen`, and `update_session_cluster_synced_origin`
did lookup→modify→`BPF_EXIST` writes without TupleGate admission. They could
clobber a live row held under a gate lease or write during a map-wide
ClearFence, unlike the gated publish/delete twins.

## What
- Added `with_conntrack_rmw` in `bpf_map/mod.rs` mirroring `with_publish`:
  decline on gate-busy/clear-fenced, holding admission across the synchronous
  RMW.
- Wrapped all four functions (refresh gated per walked tuple); `fd < 0`
  no-map early-true stays inside raw bodies so declines never fake success.
- Test seams model origin writes and count refresh writes.
- Added six regressions for lease/clear-fence declines and an unleased positive
  control in `bpf_map_tests.rs`.

## Validation
- RED on pre-fix code: two app-id regressions failed on the named lease and
  clear-fence assertions.
- GREEN focused: `cargo test --bins conntrack_rmw_` → 6 passed on current master.
- Full `cargo test --bins`: 8022 passed, 2 failed, 8 ignored. The failures were
  `afxdp::cos::queue_service::tests::sojourn::submit_local_publishes_committed_vtime_on_settle`
  and `afxdp::tests_9950::f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659`;
  neither exercises conntrack RMW.
- RED-on-revert: bypassing gate admission made four decline tests fail; restored
  the gate implementation.

## Risk
Refresh skips a declined tuple for this slice; subsequent budgeted walks retry.
App-id and policy restamps return false so their existing retry/fail-closed
behavior remains intact. Origin transition updates silently skip; a later
transition/refresh can restamp the bit.

## PR #13809 — afxdp: parallelize WireGuard endpoint lookups (#13666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13666-campaign-v2`

Why: Blocking `to_socket_addrs` calls delayed every following WireGuard peer refresh; additionally, a slow lookup delayed adoption of already completed peer results, and Drop waited for uncancellable DNS work.

What: Resolve names through at most eight scoped workers that claim new peers as they finish. Apply each answer immediately on the resolver thread. On Drop, set the stop flag and detach the resolver thread; workers no longer claim peers and outstanding results are discarded after shutdown begins. Regression tests cover bounded concurrency, early result application while a prior lookup remains blocked, panic isolation, and nonblocking Drop with unscheduled peers. See `docs/log/13666.md`.

Validation: `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp endpoint_resolver` — 10 passed; `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both edited Rust files passed. RED proof on pristine master: setting the worker limit to one failed because peer lookups were serialized. Earlier full bin suite: 8019 tests ran with one unrelated failure at `afxdp::tests_9950::f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659`; clippy stopped at the existing mutable-borrow error in `src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241`.

Risk: Operating-system DNS resolution cannot be interrupted; the detached resolver thread retains its shared state until in-flight lookups return.

Closes #13666

## PR #13826 — afxdp: apply endpoint answers before slow lookups finish (#13666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13666-completion-shutdown`

Why: Blocking `to_socket_addrs` calls delayed every following WireGuard peer refresh; additionally, a slow lookup delayed adoption of already completed peer results, and Drop waited for uncancellable DNS work.

What: Resolve names through at most eight scoped workers that claim new peers as they finish. Apply each answer immediately on the resolver thread. On Drop, set the stop flag and detach the resolver thread; workers no longer claim peers and outstanding results are discarded after shutdown begins. Regression tests cover bounded concurrency, early result application while a prior lookup remains blocked, panic isolation, and nonblocking Drop with unscheduled peers. See `docs/log/13666.md`.

Validation: `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp endpoint_resolver` — 10 passed; `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both edited Rust files passed. RED proof on pristine master: setting the worker limit to one failed because peer lookups were serialized. Earlier full bin suite: 8019 tests ran with one unrelated failure at `afxdp::tests_9950::f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659`; clippy stopped at the existing mutable-borrow error in `src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241`.

Risk: Operating-system DNS resolution cannot be interrupted; the detached resolver thread retains its shared state until in-flight lookups return.

Closes #13666

## PR #13831 — userspace-dp: align transit GRE legacy flag checks (#13662) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13662-gre-transit-flags-buildable`

## Follow-up to #13662 / PR #13797

The first fix added the RFC 2784 legacy-bit refusal to native GRE decapsulation. The production transit `gre_discriminator` is the guarded sibling: its module documentation says version/routing refusal discipline is shared with decapsulation, but it still extracted an RFC 2890 Key from `0x0800` and `0x0400`. That could create keyed transit session identity for headers the decapsulator refuses.

This change shares the mask and returns `Unparseable` before keyed/unkeyed classification. It preserves RFC 2784 §2.3 must-ignore bits through `0x03f8` and the RFC 2890 optional fields.

## Validation

- New transit regression failed on the merged decapsulation-only baseline: `0x0800` produced `Keyed(85)` instead of `Unparseable`.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp unsupported_legacy_bits_are_unparseable_13662`: passed on the merged baseline after the change.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp gre_discriminator::tests`: passed on the merged baseline after the change.
- `cargo build -p xpf-userspace-dp`: passed on the merged baseline after the change.

The current `origin/master` test build also has an unrelated compile failure in `session_glue::mod.rs` (`purge_translated_synced_hit` imported while gated with `#[cfg(test)]`); this PR was rebased to current master after validation on the buildable merged baseline.

## Risk

Transit GRE carrying these unsupported bits no longer receives keyed session identity and stays on the flowless path. Packet forwarding behavior is unchanged.

transit could spend all tokens and starve trusted control-plane punts;

What: Keep independent RateLimiter instances for Trusted, Adjudicated, and
Delegated PacketQueue classes. Refund tokens when bounded enqueue fails in
both legacy and leased adjudicated paths. Add per-class starvation and
queue-full regressions, and document the per-outlet contract.

Validation: RED on origin/master 02ba5b2: the delegated-flood regression
failed because the trusted control punt was rate-limited. GREEN: focused
regression 1 passed; the full slowpath::tests:: module passed 50 tests
(8,039 filtered out) on the latest base.

Risk: The independent buckets each receive the configured per-outlet limit,
so aggregate slow-path admission can exceed the previous shared limit.

Closes #13707

## PR #13850 — afxdp: recover bindings after ifindex resolution (#13714) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13714-campaign-zero`

Why: An unresolved initial ifindex leaves a candidate unregistered and unarmed, but the planner stamps last_change. On a later replan after ifindex resolution, the timestamp makes the row look previously registered, so it skips registration/arm initialization. With unchanged global forwarding state, no arm RPC repairs it and the whole dataplane remains disabled.

What: Treat prior binding state as existing only if the prior ifindex was positive. Newly resolvable rows re-register and inherit the global arm state; still-unresolved rows remain fail-closed. Added regressions for armed/disarmed recovery, repeated-replan stability, and an unresolved sibling. Added docs/log/13714.md.

The full unfiltered binary run reported four failures and stalled before a final summary. All four failures were independently reproduced on pristine origin/master fd94c3a7d: fragment-overlap sibling outcome (0 vs 1), both GRE inner ICMP LocalDelivery outcomes (0 vs 1), and session-hit window expiry at tick 21. Details are in the issue log.

Risk: Only a prior non-positive ifindex changes recovery behavior. Existing positive-ifindex registrations retain manual registration and arm state; unresolved bindings remain unarmed.

Closes #13714

## PR #13869 — userspace-dp: isolate per-session counter query replies (#13711) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13711-campaign`

Why: A full worker-command queue refuses the counter-query command, but the
kick path discarded that result and still waited for its acknowledgement. The
query then spent the full three-second deadline waiting for work that could not
have been queued. Separately, workers share one reply slot and the reader
accepted any sequence at least as new as its own, allowing a later session's
counters to answer an earlier request.

What: Track refused worker IDs separately and report them unanswered without
adding them to the wait set. Require exact sequence equality; if a newer
sequence has overwritten the single reply slot, report unanswered instead of
borrowing another session's counters. Add full-queue and cross-session
regressions in coordinator/tests.rs. No queue policy or wire shape changed.

wait exceeded 1 s; B's 999 packets were returned for A). Focused after fix:

additional screen-cookie failure passed isolated on both trees. Clippy
all-targets is blocked by pre-existing clippy::mut_from_ref in
src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241 on both trees; strict -D warnings also flags four
pre-existing build.rs lints.

Risk: An earlier query whose reply slot is overwritten by a later query is
now explicitly reported unanswered rather than cross-attributed. It retains
the existing three-second bound for queued workers that do not answer.

## PR #13875 — userspace-dp: isolate concurrent counter replies (#13711) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13711-reply-race`

Why: A post-merge review of #13869 identified a remaining race in its shared response slot. A waiter could match sequence A, then a worker could publish B's six payload fields before A read them. A could therefore return B's counters as an answered A response.

What: Give every queued counter query an independent reply slot. The worker publishes the complete `SessionCounterAnswer` under that slot's mutex, and the waiter reads the same snapshot under the mutex. Remove the shared diagnostic atomics. Add a deterministic overlap regression that holds A's slot while B publishes, then verifies both queries retain their own counters. Queue-refusal handling and the off-lock bounded wait remain intact.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp counter_query_ -- --nocapture`: 2 passed, including the concurrent per-request snapshot regression.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp failover_before_rename_joint_purges_10589 -- --nocapture`: 1 passed, exercising the real worker command path.
- The full crate suite and clippy were not repeated for this follow-up. Results and base comparison from #13869 are recorded in `docs/log/13711.md`.

Risk: This diagnostic now allocates one reply slot per queued worker and takes a short mutex to publish or copy its snapshot. The worker-command queue remains bounded, and the off-lock wait retains its three-second deadline.

Closes #13711

## PR #13877 — userspace-dp: gate FullResync ACKs on fresh exports (#13725) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13725-campaign-zero`

Closes #13725

## Why

`ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` scans shards incrementally. A FullResync arriving
during a scan can represent drops in shards the scan already visited, so
coalescing the barrier into that worker can retire and cumulatively ACK it
without exporting the missing sessions.

## What

Each FullResync barrier now runs its own worker export and remains queued until
that export succeeds. Removed coalesced-marker retirement and failure-reset
logic. Added #13725 in-flight and failure-retry regressions, updated #9630
tests, and recorded the behavior in `docs/log/13725.md`.

## Validation

- RED: the in-flight barrier regression failed on pristine `origin/master`
  `2cae7b02a`; source files involved are unchanged through current base
  `07eeae9ed`.
- GREEN after rebase:
  `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp
  go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run
  'TestEventStreamFullResync(ArrivingDuringInFlightWorkerRunsPostBarrierExport13725|FailureRetriesEveryBarrier13725|DuringInFlightExportRunsAnotherExport9630|BarriersQueuedBeforeCallbackEachExport9630)$' -count=1`
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite was attempted twice. AF_UNIX socket
  fixtures fail to bind with `invalid argument` because their generated temp
  paths exceed the socket path limit. Eight unrelated non-socket test failures
  were reproduced on pristine `origin/master` `07eeae9ed`; see `docs/log/13725.md`.

## Risk

Repeated barriers each perform an export, increasing export work during bursts.
This avoids ACKing state not covered by a post-drop scan; queue overflow still
forces helper reconnect/replay.
