## PR #14293 — daemon: accept OpenSSH key types, own .ssh by numeric id, fail closed on empty algorithm lists (#14111) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14111-campaign`

Closes #14111

## Why
Research D5-09 (three-way validated) found three SSH host-auth defects in `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go`:
1. `validateAuthorizedSSHKeys` required an `ssh-` prefix, so a valid `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 …` / `sk-*` key value (the full `"<type> <base64> <comment>"` string Junos operators store under any `ssh-*` leaf) was rejected at apply and **all** provisioning for that user was skipped.
2. The `.ssh` directory was chowned via external `chown -R -- <name>:<name>`, which fails for any account whose primary group is not eponymously named — stranding users outside a freshly created root-owned 0700 `.ssh` — while key installation continued under an already-claimed ownership marker.
3. `buildSSHDConfig` silently omitted a nonempty `KexAlgorithms`/`Ciphers`/`MACs` restriction when every token was filtered, reverting sshd to its built-in defaults on tolerant input.

## What
- Key validation: fail-closed allowlist of the OpenSSH `authorized_keys` key-type vocabulary (`ssh-*`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp{256,384,521}`, `sk-*`, `*-cert-v01@openssh.com`) with a required base64 blob. Option-prefixed (`command="..."`), bare-blob, unknown-type, empty, and CR/LF values stay rejected (#10725 doctrine preserved).
- Directory ownership: `.ssh` is owned by the already-resolved numeric `(uid, gid)` via `os.Chown` behind the `chownSSHDir` test seam, directory-only (the key file keeps `fsatomic.WithOwner(uid,gid)`), and a chown failure aborts that user's key install with marker rollback instead of claiming convergence. Numeric operands subsume the #5005 `--` concern for this exec.
- Algorithm fallback: `buildSSHDConfigErr`/`filterSSHAlgorithmsErr` error when a nonempty list filters to empty; `applySSHConfig` returns the error **before** touching the drop-in (no write/removal/reload), leaving the prior restriction in force. Partial filtering still renders survivors (#4902). String-only `buildSSHDConfig` kept for pure render/compare callers.
- Tests: new `hostauth_ssh_14111_test.go` (decisive ecdsa provisioning check from the issue, vocabulary allowlist both directions, fail-closed apply with byte-identical prior drop-in, numeric ownership); #5026 and #4902 guards updated to the successor contracts; fake-uid isolate helper stubs the chown seam. Campaign log: `docs/log/14111.md`.

## Validation
- RED on pristine `origin/master` worktree (tests copied over): all six behavioral tests fail — ecdsa rejected (`must be a single-line ssh-* public key`), external chown argv recorded, `applySSHConfig` returns nil over all-invalid algorithms.
- GREEN here: new tests + targeted hostauth suites (`TestBuildSSHDConfig*`, `TestApplySSHConfig*`, `TestApplySystemLogin*`, `TestFirstCommit*`, `TestLogin*`, `TestRootAuth*`, belt tests) pass; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Residual: full `pkg/daemon` run shows failures (e.g. `TestProducerDeltaConvertsToSyncedValue9752`) that reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
Validation widens from `ssh-*` to the full OpenSSH vocabulary (still fail-closed); an all-invalid algorithm restriction now fails the apply instead of silently dropping to sshd defaults (prior drop-in stays in force); `.ssh` ownership moves from external name-based chown to in-process numeric chown with the same net ownership.

## PR #14307 — config: restore declared units of dotted lifelines (#14302) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14302-campaign`

## Why

#14192 registered every declared unit as an explicit `false` key in
`HostInboundLifelineSet`, but only re-marked the base key when a role
name matched a declared interface. For a dotted lifeline `hb.1`
(`control-interface hb.1`) whose only declared unit is 7, `hb.1.7`
stayed false: the cluster walk's naive-cut guard read `hb.1` as a unit
of bare parent `hb` while `SplitInterfaceUnitRef` resolves it
declared-name-first, so nothing restored the unit.
`HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs`, which enumerates only
declared-unit spellings, then yielded `[fxp0]` and the control link
lost its host-inbound ingress exception; the pinned userspace test
`TestHostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevsDoesNotAddUnitParent12848`
failed on master.

## What

In `HostInboundLifelineSet` (`pkg/config/lifeline.go`):

- A dotted role spelling that is itself a **declared interface**
  (`hb.1` declared with units `hb.1.<unit>`) is an interface identity,
  not a unit of a shorter parent, so its declared units are re-marked
  `true` with the base key.
- The cluster walk precomputes those dotted lifeline bases so
  `markBaseLifeline` does not re-demote them (VLAN-tagged or not), and
  the naive-cut prefix demotion is skipped for declared role
  spellings.

Preserved invariants:

- **#14192**: bare lifeline parents keep declared transit VLAN units
  ordinary (`ge-0/0/0.100` stays deny-scoped).
- **#13137**: a non-zero-unit role binding (`ge-0/0/1.100`) keeps its
  bare parent and unit 0 ordinary.
- **#12848**: dotted siblings (`hb.2`) and the bare prefix (`hb`) stay
  ordinary; the helper adds the unit netdev without the parent.

## Validation

- New `TestLifelineDottedDeclaredUnit14302`,
  `TestLifelineDottedDeclaredVLANUnit14302`,
  `TestLifelineDottedUnitControls14302` in `pkg/config` —
  fail-on-revert verified for the dotted re-mark.
- The previously failing userspace 12848 ingress test now passes;
  all `TestLifeline*`/`TestHostInbound*` suites in `pkg/config` and
  `pkg/dataplane/userspace` pass.
- Two unrelated failures (IPsec PSK gate; VRF-scope 6619 subtests)
  reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` and are not
  affected by this change.

Branch: `fix/14303-campaign`

Why: #14228 taught the incremental SessionDelta producers to stamp pptp_call_ids from the live association table, and the HA import gate withholds any Pptp(handle) record whose pair is absent (pptp-call-ids-not-carried). The HA bulk export (snapshot_all_sessions_export, the full-resync Open deltas in afxdp/ha/export.rs) and the tunnel-remap purge Close delta (afxdp/ha/tunnel_purge.rs) both hardcoded pptp_call_ids: 0, so a PPTP session reaching the standby only via bulk export — after an event-stream reconnect or peer restart, precisely when incremental deltas were missed — was withheld: PPTP session loss on failover-after-resync (fail-closed, no aliasing).

What: carry the pair on the shared SyncedSessionEntry (new u64 field, 0/absent for non-PPTP). build_synced_session_entry stamps it from the verified wire pair at HA import; the local forward-flow publish (poll_descriptor), the forwarding-learn publish (local_delivery), and the shared-promote publish (promote) stamp it from the live table via pptp_call_ids_wire_for, matching the incremental producers. The bulk export and the tunnel purge stamp entry.pptp_call_ids instead of 0. Every other construction site (reverse companions, tunnel/TUN origins, seeds, fixtures) carries 0, which is never read. NOT changed: the Close wire frame (encodes no pair today; the purge delta now carries the value in process, symmetric with other Close producers) and the owner-RG worker export (already stamps via open_export_delta_with_provenance).

Full --bin xpf-userspace-dp suite: 8276 passed, 36 failed, 8 ignored; the 36 failures reproduce identically on clean origin/master 7df06b6eb (base-attributed). git diff --check clean.

Risk: one added u64 on an in-process shared entry; no wire, BPF ABI, or Go change. Non-PPTP sessions carry 0 exactly as before. A PPTP session whose pair this node never held still exports 0 and is still withheld — fail-closed preserved.

## PR #14452 — userspace-dp: reject ports on non-port-bearing application protocols (#14312) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14312-campaign`

userspace-dp: reject ports on non-port-bearing application protocols (#14312)

Why:
parse_applications rejected only the #3712 ICMP-field combos. A port
on any protocol other than TCP/UDP compiled into a wrong-behaving
term: an icmp/icmpv6 term with icmp_type had its ports silently
discarded by CompiledApplications::from_matches (a permit broadens
to every message of that type/code, arbitrary ICMP Echo IDs), and a
port-bearing term on gre/esp/ospf/sctp or any other portless
protocol became a dead range/exact term keyed on ports the packet
never presents, so a deny/reject never matched and fell through to
a later permit. Go strict commit (#3373) and ApplicationMatchDrops
(#9525) poison these before the wire, but a corrupt, hand-built,
mixed-version, or leniently peer-synced snapshot reached the Rust
helper with no mirror of the #3712 / #3723 fail-closed backstops.

What:
Add SnapshotIntegrityError::InvalidApplicationPortProtocol and
record the first offender in parse_applications when the parsed
source/destination ranges are non-empty and the resolved protocol
is neither TCP nor UDP (the ip_proto::has_l4_ports set, SCTP
included, numeric spellings caught via the resolved number).
parse_policy_state_with_counters rejects the whole snapshot after
the #3712 check, keeping the previous good state. The stale
from_matches "stray port is irrelevant" comment now states the
boundary reject. Nine regression tests cover icmp typed/untyped,
icmpv6 source-port, gre, esp, ospf range, sctp, and numeric GRE,
plus a guard that tcp/udp with ports and portless terms still
compile. docs/log/14312.md records the evidence.

Validation:
RED on base 5b122dda5 (separate base worktree, test patch applied
with the not-yet-existing variant mapped to the #3712 variant so it
compiles): 8 rejects tests failed with Ok(state), guard passed.
GREEN on lane: cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp --
rejects_whole_snapshot valid_port_protocol passed 17/17 including
neighbouring #3712 rejects; full policy::tests module passed
234/234.

Risk:
Fail-closed only on snapshots the Go producer never emits; normal
Go-lowered snapshots carry ports only on TCP/UDP, so no legitimate
config changes behaviour. Validation runs once per snapshot parse,
not per packet.

Closes #14312

## PR #14454 — userspace-dp: rebind session zone pair on cross-zone FIB reroute (#14318) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

## Summary
Fixes #14318 (research-validated D2-09): `SessionTable::revalidate_forwarding_resolution` persisted only the new route, leaving forward `metadata.egress_zone` and reverse companion `metadata.ingress_zone` stale after a permitted cross-zone WAN failover (#11373/#12074) or egress re-zoning (#9384). - Threaded through `DeferredForwardingRevalidation.new_egress_zone`, both persist sites (poll_descriptor, session_glue), both reverse-hit permit arms, and the forward-hit Permit arm for #9384 re-zoning.
- `foreign_hit_verdict` direction deliberately unchanged (research lanes refuted that half; with zones fresh, legitimate replies are Owner).

- GREEN: 4 new tests (reroute rebind, None preserves zones, reverse-hit rebind, authority Owner-after-rebind + stale Foreign control).

## PR #14456 — forwarding: admit NAT and anycast leak targets and continue past tunnel NoRoute (#14319) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14319-campaign`

Why:
Inter-VRF leaked return traffic to addresses owned only via
interface_nat_tables, or via an IPv6 subnet-router anycast, failed
the table_has_v[46]_route precheck, so the leak was skipped and the
traffic misrouted without a leak_incarnation stamp. A leak target
whose only route was a tunnel route also terminated the walk with
NoRoute when allow_tunnels was false, blackholing outer tunnel
endpoint resolution instead of falling through like a kernel
ip-rule miss.

What:
table_has_v4_route/table_has_v6_route take allow_tunnels, admit
interface_nat_tables_v4/v6 and (v6) subnet-router-anycast ownership,
and ignore all-tunnel route entries and tunnel connected rows when
tunnels are forbidden. The v4/v6 leak loops pass allow_tunnels into
the precheck and continue to the next leak / source-table LPM when
the recursive target lookup returns NoRoute; every other disposition
stays terminal. leak_incarnation_for_resolution passes
allow_tunnels=true (no forbidding caller; provenance must not drop
tunnel-reached destinations) and inherits the NAT/anycast admission.
New tests_leak_precheck_14319 covers NAT-only v4/v6, anycast-only,
next-leak continuation, source-table fall-through, and a
tunnels-allowed control. NOT changed: single-table tunnel-forbidden
NoRoute semantics, local delivery, or route selection.

Validation:
New cells RED on base 5b122dda5 (5 failed: NAT v4/v6 resolved
NoRoute not LocalDelivery; continuation/fall-through resolved
NoRoute not ForwardCandidate), GREEN with the fix (7 passed).
afxdp::forwarding suite 349 passed; leak filter 55 passed. Full
--bin xpf-userspace-dp suite 8286 passed, 36 failed, with all 36
failure names reproducing identically on a pristine origin/master
worktree (base-attributed, including the 2 tunnel-filter failures).

Risk:
Behaviour delta is confined to destinations that previously
blackholed or misrouted; fail-closed dispositions other than
NoRoute remain terminal in the leak walk.

Closes #14319

## PR #14457 — userspace-dp: scope Stage-11 IPsec claim to effective table (#14314) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14314-campaign`

Why:
Stage-11 (`stage_ipsec_passthrough_check`) re-derived its local-ownership table from the raw physical ingress ifindex, ignoring `flow.forward_key.routing_domain`, the validated fabric scope, and input-filter PBR `RouteOverride::Table`. Transit ESP/AH/IKE steered by PBR into a tenant VRF (or arriving on `fab0` for a tenant VRF) whose dst IP is owned by `inet.0` was falsely claimed for XFRM and reinjected into `xpf-usp1`, bypassing the tenant VRF's transit zone policy; host-bound IPsec steered into a tenant VRF was missed. The caller evaluated `ingress_route_table_override` only after the claim and honoured only its `Drop` arm.

What:
- `poll_stages.rs`: `stage_ipsec_passthrough_check` gains `route_override_table` and adjudicates `owns_ipsec_local_destination_in_table` in the EFFECTIVE table: PBR `Table` steer, then the flow's stamped routing domain via `install_tables`, then the validated V2 fabric scope's canonical table, then the ingress interface's table. A nonzero domain with no registry row returns `NotClaimed` (fail-closed, mirroring `NativeRouteTable::Unresolvable`).
- `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`: resolve `ingress_route_table_override_uncounted` BEFORE the claim for IPsec candidates only; `Drop` recycles, `Table` scopes the claim. The counted evaluation still runs exactly once (claimed arm or ordinary miss path), so no PBR term double-counts and `reject` replies are preserved.
- `poll_stages_tests.rs`: decisive regression `stage_ipsec_claim_follows_effective_table_14314` (`10.0.61.1` in `inet.0` vs `172.16.80.8` in `vrf_blue` under PBR Table, flow domain, and validated fabric scope, plus fail-closed orphan domain); #14124 cross-VRF seed cell restamped with the tenant's real install domain.
- NOT changed: host-inbound IKE gating, exchange-key scope, DNAT-to-self, fine lo0/junos-host gates.

Validation:
- GREEN: `cargo +1.98.1 test --release --bins -- ipsec` → 150 passed, 0 failed; `stage_ipsec` → 10 passed (incl. new 14314 regression and updated 14124 cells).
- RED: separate base worktree at origin/master `5b122dda5` with tests-only patch → `stage_ipsec_claim_follows_effective_table_14314` fails at `poll_stages_tests.rs:4444` ("PBR Table(vrf_blue) must not claim an inet.0-owned dst") — pre-fix returned `Passthrough`.
- Full `--bins` suite not run to completion in-lane (900s timeout under parallel build); parent should run it on the final head.

Risk:
A legitimate IPsec flow whose stamped domain lacks an install-table row now takes ordinary forwarding/policy instead of XFRM reinjection — fail-closed, consistent with #10312 native route resolution. Non-IPsec traffic pays no new work.

Closes #14314

## PR #14458 — session: restamp zone vintage checks on policy/zone rebind (#14320) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14320-campaign`

Closes #14320

## Why
`rebind_policy_pair`, `rebind_zones_pair`, and `restamp_shared_policy_entries` moved `ingress_zone`/`egress_zone` without restamping the #10620 `ingress_zone_check`/`egress_zone_check` vintage hashes. After a legitimate rebind to a differently-named zone, the (id, check) pair was inconsistent, so `synced_entry_is_stale_replay` could false-positive and evict a live session on shared promotion / prewarm / BPF republish.

## What
- `SessionTable::rebind_policy_pair` / `rebind_zones_pair` take `ingress_zone_check: u32` / `egress_zone_check: u32` (u32 matches `SessionMetadata`; the issue's u16 was stale) and restamp both halves with the same swap as the zone ids.
- `restamp_shared_policy_entries` copies both checks into every shared alias.
- Both production callers in `reconcile.rs` compute checks via `zone_vintage_check_for_id` from the new forwarding view; the declined-rematch path restamps its local metadata copy too.
- Regression: decisive test from the issue (pair in lan/wan, rebind to dmz, assert forward ingress and reverse-companion egress checks equal `zone_identity_check("dmz")`) plus a policy-pair twin.

## Validation
- RED on base `origin/master` 3b78c9b37 with the test adapted to the old 3-arg call: FAILED (forward ingress check stayed `zone_identity_check("lan")`=308644377 vs expected dmz=3400871448).
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp _14320` — 2 passed; adjacent rebind/session-limit/LocalDelivery tests pass.
- Full bin suite: 8294 passed / 41 pre-existing failures, spot-verified identical on pristine base (unrelated environment/source-drift).

## Risk
Crate-internal `pub(crate)` signature change, all callsites migrated; checks are 0 (fail-open unknown) for unmapped zone ids, preserving the #10620 fence contract. BPF conntrack values carry no zone-check fields, so no BPF restamp is needed. Campaign log: `docs/log/14320.md`.

## PR #14459 — userspace-dp: judge NAT64 ICMP policy on original type and sender (#14316) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14316-campaign`

Why:
Post-#14123, the V4ToV6 NAT64 ICMP-error arm returned
policy_src_ip: None, so the queued gate's PROTO_ICMP arm was dead
for that producer and IPv4 source/protocol-icmp denies were judged
against the Pref64-mapped ICMPv6 identity. The V6ToV4 arm forced
PROTO_ICMPV6 while reading type/code from the already-translated
frame, so icmpv6 icmp-type terms compared against RFC 7915
ICMPv4 numbers and misfired in both directions.

What:
nat64_icmp_error.rs captures the original ICMP type/code via
policy_packet_icmp before translation on both arms and carries it
as policy_icmp; V4ToV6 also carries the original v4 sender.
embedded_icmp.rs adds policy_icmp to EmbeddedIcmpReversal::Queued
and evaluates it ahead of the translated frame's pair, keeping
the deny event on the wire identity. poll_descriptor/mod.rs
forwards it at both queued call sites. Unreadable originals
refund the F-077 token and drop, fail-closed. NOT changed:
rule_l3_matches gains no (V4,V6) arm; wire frames byte-identical.

Validation:
New pol14316_v4tov6_icmp_type_deny_refuses and
pol14316_v6tov4_icmpv6_type_uses_original FAIL on pristine
5b122dda5 (tests only) and pass with the fix. Rebased onto
9f6630039: both pass; tests_embedded_poll_filter 111 passed,
1 failed (stage11_local_ike 13637, reproduces on pristine
9f6630039, base-attributed). Full bin suite pre-rebase:
8280 passed, 37 failed, all base-attributed by sampling.

Risk:
Policy-visible identity for V4ToV6 NAT64 errors changes from the
Pref64-mapped source/ICMPv6 to the original v4 sender/ICMP/
original type-code; rules written only against the mapped source
will now see the v4 tuple. Non-PMTUD errors without a matching
permit still hit default deny; transmitted frames unchanged.

Closes #14316

## PR #14461 — userspace-dp: partition fragment overlap and association quotas by ingress zone (#14321) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14321-campaign`

Why: OverlapTracker keyed membership and its 32-entry reserve on the routing domain alone, so a spoofed fragment in an untrusted zone merged into a trusted zone's datagram entry and four senders in one zone could hold the whole domain reserve, refusing new fragmented datagrams in every other zone sharing the VRF. FragAssoc similarly let admitted sessions from one zone consume the whole 64-entry shard.

What: Add `ingress_zone` to `OverlapKey` and `overlap_same_datagram`, and partition the reserve by `(routing_domain, ingress_zone)` as `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_ZONE_PER_SHARD` (old domain constant kept as alias); completed-anchor reclaim scoped to the same zone, incomplete anchors never evicted, 64/shard aggregate cap unchanged. Callers stamp the zone via `frag_ingress_zone` (the `frag_ingress_authority` resolution) in `poll_descriptor` and the neighbor-retry path; parse leaves 0 and `translated_overlap_key` inherits the arrival zone. `FragAssoc` gains `FRAG_CAP_PER_ZONE_PER_SHARD` keyed on (authority zone, routing_table) with prune-before-refuse. New cross-zone tests in `fragment_overlap` and `nat64_tests`; two one-zone shard-fill tests now fill from two zones. NOT changed: sender quota, TTLs, range geometry, shard hashing.

Validation: Base-adapted RED (zone-blind encoding of the same tests) on a pristine base worktree failed both new tests (ShardFull starvation; cross-zone poison). Head: `cargo test --bins cross_zone` (2 passed), `fragment_overlap` (41 passed), `frag_assoc` (35 passed), `f035`/`9950` (9/28 passed). Full `--bins` suite shows the same pre-existing parallel flake sets on base and head (43 common failures; no overlap/frag-assoc failure on head) — see `docs/log/14321.md`.

Risk: Fragments of one datagram arriving in different zones now track separately (deliberate: cross-zone aliasing was the defect); same-zone fragments are unaffected. Single-zone deployments see identical quotas (zone 0 reserve is the old domain reserve when one zone uses a VRF).

Closes #14321

## PR #14462 — userspace: reflect zone-quarantine scrub in policy fingerprints and stable-key maps (#14330) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14330-campaign`

Closes #14330

## Problem
`PolicyResolvedFingerprints` / `PolicyResolvedIdentityStrippedFingerprints` hashed the raw `buildPolicySnapshotsWithAddressBook` output, and `PolicyIDsByStableKey` / `PoliciesByStableKey` (via `walkPolicyRuleSlots`) emitted every global policy — none applied the `scrubPoliciesForQuarantinedZones` step the publish path runs via `quarantineCollidingZones` / `policySnapshotAfterZoneQuarantine`. A commit whose only enforcement change was a zone becoming quarantined (StableZoneID collision `z174`/`z214`, or a poisoned `DroppedEnforcementChild` zone) produced identical fingerprints/ID maps while the published snapshot dropped or narrowed the rule, so `daemon_policy_invalidate` never flagged live sessions for policy-rematch re-evaluation.

## Fix
- Both fingerprint functions now run `policySnapshotAfterZoneQuarantine(cfg, rules)` before hashing (the same SSOT `policies_reject.go` uses). Partial quarantine prunes the scope → digest changes, key retained; sole-zone quarantine drops the rule → key removed.
- `walkPolicyRuleSlots` skips a global policy whose `Match.FromZones`/`Match.ToZones` is fully quarantined, using `quarantinedZoneNamesForConfig` (collision losers + poisoned zones; reserved sentinels excluded so defined-`any`/`junos-host` handling stays with its own poison paths). Skipped globals consume no slot/cap and vanish from `PolicyIDsByStableKey`/`PoliciesByStableKey`/`RuntimePolicyIDs`, and published `PolicyID`s now agree with the post-quarantine snapshot — extending the #13168 zone-pair invariant to globals. Partially quarantined globals keep slot/ID; narrowing is signalled via the fingerprint change.

## Tests
New `TestPolicyResolvedFingerprintsReflectZoneQuarantineScrub` in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_resolved_fingerprint_test.go` (4 subtests, each with a `buildSnapshot` positive control that the publish path really drops/prunes):
- RED on pristine origin/master and on the fix worktree pre-fix (3 subtests fail: partial-quarantine fingerprint unchanged, sole-zone collision key retained, poisoned sole-zone key retained).
- GREEN after the fix.
- Nearby suites pass: quarantine/scoped-global/walk/fingerprint tests in `pkg/dataplane/userspace`, `TestPolicy|TestChangedPolicy|TestDeletedPolicy` in `pkg/daemon`; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite fails only on pre-existing `TestSecureTunnelOwnership*` / `TestPartialRepublishRefusesQuarantineOnlySkew12247`, reproduced identically on pristine master.

See `docs/log/14330.md` for the full RED/GREEN record.

## PR #14464 — userspace: inherit collapsing unit .0 routing domain on base row (#14331) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14331-campaign`

Closes #14331

## Defect
`buildInterfaceSnapshotsFrom` emitted a base row resolving RoutingInstance/RoutingDomain from the bare interface key. For an untagged unit `.0` (which collapses onto the base netdev — same ifindex, same live kernel addresses), per-unit VRF membership (`routing-instances vrf1 interface ge-0/0/1.0`) left the bare key unclaimed, so the base row carried Domain 0 while republishing the VRF unit's addresses: VRF locals leaked into Domain:0 in `buildLocalAddressEntriesWithExclusions`, and `localAddressRoutingDomain` rejected the shared ifindex as ambiguous, deleting its ingress-domain entry.

## Fix
When unit `.0` collapses onto the base netdev and the bare key has no explicit/quarantined claim, the base row inherits unit `.0`'s RoutingInstance and RoutingDomain via the same `routingDomainForInterfaceKey` resolution (quarantine sentinel preserved). VLAN/tunnel unit `.0` on its own netdev is untouched; fail-closed ambiguity handling is unchanged.

## Regression
`TestBuildSnapshotUntaggedVRFUnitDoesNotConflictWithBaseRowDomain` builds via `buildSnapshot(cfg)`, asserts base/unit domain agreement, `localAddressRoutingDomain == (vrf1 domain, true)`, and no Domain:0 local entries. RED on origin/master (`base RoutingDomain = 0, want 748221`), GREEN with fix. Full package failure set identical to pristine base (pre-existing failures only). See docs/log/14331.md.

## PR #14465 — xdp: gate degraded local pass on native-GRE inner action (#14327) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14327-campaign`

Why:
During any degraded window, `is_degraded_local_or_control` returned `true` from an unconditional `destination_is_local` arm before the #10651 native-GRE arm. A native-GRE outer destination is the local tunnel endpoint by construction, so outer-local frames passed to the kernel without the inner packet ever being classified; inner transit was decapsulated and forwarded with no zone policy, and the #10651 arm was dead for its only true case (reachable only with a non-local outer, where its predicate is `false && _`).

What:
- `userspace-xdp/src/gre_classify.rs`: new host-executable `degraded_general_local_pass_applies(is_native_gre, destination_is_local)` = `destination_is_local && !is_native_gre`, in the existing core-only module so the host test runs the real decision rather than a source model.
- `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs`: gate the degraded general local pass through the new predicate; native-GRE frames fall through to the typed #10651 inner gate, reusing one `native_gre` computation. Only inner PASS_TO_KERNEL with a local outer passes to the kernel.
- Regenerated shim object via `build-userspace-xdp.sh` (verifier PASS, 29.20% headroom) with gate verdict + manifest.
- NOT changed: the healthy path, the ESP/interface-NAT arm, and the subsumed NDP arm.

Validation:
- New host test `degraded_native_gre_local_outer_requires_inner_pass_14327` (tests_shim_gre_classify_10651.rs) composes both executed predicates exactly as the shim does: (GRE, NATIVE_GRE, local, inner miss/REDIRECT) → false; inner PASS_TO_KERNEL → true; non-local and non-native controls pinned.
- RED on pristine origin/master: fails to compile (E0432, predicate absent). GREEN with the fix.
- Shim suites: 8 passed (gre_classify incl. pre-existing #10651 truth table, degraded_ndp, wg_classify). Go manifest gate `TestUserspaceXDPShim`: ok.
- Pre-existing failure `local_origin_tunnel_ipv6_nonfirst_fragment_transmits_without_session_14119` fails identically on pristine origin/master (verified in a clean base worktree; base-attributed, unrelated).

Risk:
Degraded native-GRE inner transit now drops instead of passing to the kernel — the intended fail-closed direction; genuinely local inner PASS_TO_KERNEL delivery is preserved. No other degraded local/control behavior changes.

Closes #14327

## PR #14466 — userspace-dp: resolve WG kernel-path locality in the tunnel routing domain (#14328) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14328-campaign`

Closes #14328

## Defect
`ShimMapsKernelPathView::destination_is_local` resolved the routing domain for the INNER plaintext destination from the OUTER UDP socket's pktinfo `ingress_ifindex` (`userspace_ingress_domains[outer]`) and returned `false` for `None`. When the underlay and `wgN` live in different routing instances (or pktinfo is unavailable), host-inbound over WireGuard was falsely dropped as `rx_degraded_transit_drops`; conversely transit coinciding with an underlay-local address read as local.

## Fix
- `destination_is_local(dst, tunnel_logical_ifindex)` now takes the `wgN` logical ifindex (`spawned_logical_ifindex`, passed by `dispatch_inbound`; also stored on the view at spawn). Coverage (`ingress`) still uses the outer ifindex — the two questions are keyed on different interfaces, documented in the module header.
- New `tunnel_routing_domain` helper: an `ingress_domains` row for the tunnel's own ifindex wins when present; otherwise the runtime forwarding state's `synced_routing_domain_in` answers (the tunnel row's `routing_domain`). Production tunnel rows are absent from `ingress_domains` (Go excludes tunnels from the adjudicated set), so the forwarding state is the production authority; the map precedence lets the test seam state a tunnel domain. Local maps are queried under the tunnel domain only; fail-closed preserved (non-positive/unresolvable/unreadable -> transit). No test-input special-casing.

## Regression
- `locality_uses_tunnel_domain_not_outer_ingress_14328` — the issue's decisive shape: outer ifindex 10/domain 1, wg0 ifindex 20/domain 2, `2001:db8::1` local only in domain 2; asserts local under the tunnel key (incl. Unknown/no-pktinfo delivering), non-local for outer-domain-only and transit addresses, fail-closed for unplaceable tunnel.
- `tunnel_routing_domain_resolution_14328` — resolver precedence + single-instance domain-0 contract.

## Validation
- RED on base worktree (`origin/master` 1ea1f8713, test adapted to old signature): FAILED as expected.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp _14328` — 2 passed. Adjacent: `kernel_path` 9 passed, `9594` 10 passed, `wg_` 199 passed / 2 failed (`wireguard_segmentation_*`, failing identically on pristine base — pre-existing).
- Log: `docs/log/14328.md`.

## PR #14469 — firewall: keep co-VRF host-inbound claims beside a lifeline member (#14332) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14332-campaign`

Why: `hostInboundIngressClaims` rewrote each lifeline netdev to its VRF master and marked the master lifeline, then dropped every non-lifeline claim rewritten to that master. One lifeline slave in a VRF therefore erased all co-VRF claims from both `IngressNetdevs` (flood-screen scope) and `IngressDenyNetdevs` (the #10431 ambiguous fail-closed drop), failing open on host-bound traffic arriving on unzoned or conflicting-zone VRF members.

## PR #14470 — wg: select same-port tunnel endpoint by destination IP and ingress zone (#14326) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14326-campaign`

Closes #14326

## Problem
`wg_endpoint_for_listen_port` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/decap.rs`) selected the first `wg_engines` HashMap entry matching only `(wg_listen_port, transport_instance)` — it took no `dst_ip`. `wg_outer_zone_matches` compared only the zones of `dst_ip` and `endpoint.source`, never `endpoint.source == dst_ip`, and `tunnel_endpoints.get(id)?` inside the loop aborted the whole lookup when one engine lacked an endpoint row. Two WG tunnels sharing a listen port in one transport instance on different local IPs therefore selected non-deterministically: wrong engine → AEAD failure (fail-closed decap loss), wrong `logical_ifindex` attempted, `is_wg_listener_tuple` exemption misses.

## Fix
- `wg_endpoint_for_listen_port` takes `dst_ip: IpAddr`; a candidate must match port, WireGuard mode, transport instance, `endpoint.source == dst_ip` (same address family; unspecified allowed and then failed closed by the zone check), and `wg_outer_zone_matches(forwarding, endpoint, ingress_ifindex, dst_ip)`. Missing endpoint rows are skipped with `continue` instead of `?`-aborting the scan.
- `wg_outer_zone_matches` gains the same-family `endpoint.source == dst_ip` equality.
- Cross-family sources are deliberately not an equality gate: a v4-bound listener serving mapped-v6 arrivals (#10686) is still admitted on the v6 destination's owner zone, exactly as before (pinned by `mapped_ipv6_wg_underlay_candidate_stays_outside_inner_ingress_gate_10686`, which caught an earlier stricter draft of this fix).
- Callers: `is_wg_listener_tuple` passes its `dst_ip`; `is_wg_underlay_frame` parses the v6 destination before the lookup; `try_wg_decap_from_frame_with_input_filter` resolves `outer_destination_ip` before selection. The explicit zone gate at the AEAD boundary is kept.

## Tests
- New: `wg_same_port_multi_tunnel_selects_exact_dst_ip_14326` — two tunnels (ids 1/2, logical ifindexes 400/401, sources 172.16.80.8/.9, port 51820, same WAN zone/instance, independent established engine pairs): listener tuple recognised for both destinations, each tunnel's record decaps under its own logical ifindex, cross-addressed record fails closed.
- New: `wg_same_port_lookup_skips_engine_without_endpoint_14326` — orphan engine row (no endpoint) must not abort the lookup.
- RED on origin/master (test only): both failed ("record for tunnel B at IP_B must decap via engine B"; "orphan engine row must not abort"). GREEN with fix: 2 passed.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp decap`: 151 passed, 2 failed (`gre_tun_origin_*`, `ha_inactive`) — identical on pristine origin/master base worktree (149 passed, same 2), pre-existing. `cargo test wg_`: 199 passed, 2 `wireguard_segmentation_*` failures also identical on base.
- `cargo fmt` intentionally not run crate-wide (tree is not rustfmt-clean under the installed toolchain; ~500 unrelated files churn). Only the two touched files were formatted, with pre-existing churn in `decap_tests.rs` stripped.

Full log: `docs/log/14326.md`.

## PR #14473 — userspace-dp: charge SYN-cookie sketch only on failed MACs (#14324) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14324-campaign`

Why: #13952 placed syn_cookie_ack_attempt_limited before
ring.validates(), charging valid and invalid ACKs pre-MAC at 16/s per
(src,dst,dport). Sixteen spoofed ACKs/s from a victim source starve
that victim's legitimate cookie ACK, and NATed clients behind one IP
to one service share 16 conn/s, defeating the #13700 invariant that
valid cookies never consume the failed-attempt budget.

What: validate the cookie first in
validate_syn_cookie_ack_on_session_miss; return Validated without
touching the sketch. Only failed MACs charge the per-key sketch:
active arm reports ActiveBudgetExceeded when per-key or zone-wide
budget is spent (fail-closed preserved), standby charges the sketch
and stays fail-open NotApplicable. Sketch, rate, and lifecycle are
unchanged; comments and the constant name now say failed attempts.
Rewrite the two #13952 brute-force tests to the post-MAC contract and
add spoofed-starvation and NAT regressions. NOT changed: MAC strength,
verdict enum, zone-wide budgets, sketch sizing.

Validation: RED on base db3cdaebb with only the new tests added: both
syn_cookie_spoofed_failures_do_not_starve_valid_ack_14324 and
syn_cookie_nat_valid_acks_not_throttled_14324 failed with
ActiveBudgetExceeded vs Validated (NAT at the 257th ACK; test build
raises the limit to 256/s, production is 16/s). GREEN on lane:
syn_cookie_ 122 passed, screen:: 340 passed.

Risk: plausible-epoch invalid ACKs now pay one SipHash before any
per-key refusal (the issue's accepted tradeoff; comparable to the
sketch hash, verdicts still bounded by the zone-wide budgets). The
sketch bounds failed attempts per key, not candidate MAC checks;
brute force was never blocked from guessing, only from starving
valid cookies, which this restores.

Closes #14324

Treat a declared DynamicAddress AddressBinding as a book name in isBookName and unqualify zone-local names before overlay/binding/debt lookups, mirroring the snapshot builder.

Risk: Simulator-only (match-policies/test policy/REST/gRPC/daemon reauth verdicts); no dataplane enforcement change. Fail-closed direction preserved: a matching rule or a debt-bearing deciding side still reports indeterminate debt, and excluded-empty still fails closed. ## PR #14479 — userspace-dp: reject duplicated IPv6 Fragment headers in screen extraction (#14325) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14325-campaign`

## Summary

The #14129 sticky-fragment downgrade in `extract_screen_info` left an
inconsistent fragment state for a chained IPv6
`[Frag#1(offset=0, M=1), Frag#2(offset=65528, M=1)]` packet: the second
non-ATOMIC sighting only cleared `is_first_fragment`, while
`ip_frag_off`/`frag_data_off` kept Frag#1's values (offset 0).
`check_tcp_flag_screens` skips on `!is_first_fragment` and
`check_ping_of_death`/`check_teardrop` require
`(ip_frag_off & 0xFFF8) > 0`, so the packet evaded **both** screen
families.

## Fix

- `userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs`: a second non-ATOMIC Fragment
  sighting now returns
  `Err(ScreenParseError::MultipleIpv6FragmentHeaders)`. Reachable
  duplicates (`[first][non-first]`, `[first][first]`) fail closed; a
  lone ATOMIC followed by a real header is still governed by the real
  header (#10661), ATOMIC second sightings stay ignored (#14129), and
  `[non-first][*]` is unreachable as a chain (the walk breaks at the
  first non-first header). RFC 8200 allows each extension header at
  most once and receivers key reassembly on the first header, so there
  is no sizing semantics to preserve between two non-ATOMIC headers.
- `userspace-dp/src/screen/packet.rs`: new
  `ScreenParseError::MultipleIpv6FragmentHeaders` variant mapping to
  the existing `ip-malformed` reason — every `extract_screen_info`
  caller already drops parse errors fail-closed, so no caller change.

## Tests

- `screen/tests_14129_chained_frag.rs`: the issue's decisive
  `[Frag#1(0,M=1), Frag#2(65528,M=1), 4 bytes]` shape with
  single-header teardrop/ping-of-death controls, a hand-reconstructed
  pre-fix `ScreenPacketInfo` proving both sizing screens pass it, a
  duplicated-first case, a reachable-orderings matrix, and an
  `[ATOMIC][real-non-first]` guard that still parses and drops via
  teardrop.
- `afxdp/frame/tests_10661_atomic_chain.rs`: the
  `[real-first][real-non-first]` cell now asserts the screen leg
  rejects (tracker/forwarding/shim legs unchanged).

RED: on pristine `1ea1f8713` the three new tests and the updated 10661
cell failed (pre-fix parse: `ip_frag_off=1, is_first_fragment=false`).
GREEN: targeted run 18 passed; `screen::` suite 342 passed; full
`--bins` 8305 passed with the same 42 pre-existing failures as
pristine master.

Full write-up: `docs/log/14325.md`.

## PR #14486 — config: keep all bracketed child-block address-set members (#14345) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14345-campaign`

## Summary

`addressSetMemberValues` iterated `member.Keys[1:]` on the inline branch but appended only `vn.Keys[0]` for each child node, so a bracketed child block such as `address { [ a1 a2 ]; }` inside an `address-set` compiled to just `[a1]` with 0 errors and 0 warnings on strict `CompileConfig`. ## PR #14487 — config: retain junos-host terminal deny for empty permit programs (#14349) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14349-campaign`

## Summary
`junosHostProjectProgram` drove the #11065 terminal deny from whether a permit emitted a `JunosHostReturn`. A sole permit skipped on tolerant load (#12040) or with an empty cross-family intersection (v4 source × v6-only application) emits no return in either family, so the projection returned `Representable=true` with no rules, the userspace wrapper dropped the empty program, and coarse host-inbound alone decided for all IPv4/IPv6 host-bound traffic.

## Fix
Track `hasAuthoredPermit` for every permit term in `junosHostProjectProgram` (before the `skipPermit` continue and before `junosHostBuildRule`) and drive the terminal deny from it. Per-family `done` flags from a match-all permit still suppress that family's terminal.

RED on base (all three defect cells empty), GREEN with the fix.
- Updated `junosHost9572AssertSSHDrop` to accept exactly the trailing terminal deny a skipped authored permit now leaves after a following deny (fail-closed, authored deny-by-default semantics).
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestJunosHost|TestHostInbound'` passes; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean. The `pkg/dataplane/userspace` `TestJunosHostIngressScopeCoverage6619` VRF failures reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` and are base-attributed/unrelated.

## PR #14488 — cluster: preserve policy identity on mirror resends (#14359) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14359-campaign`

Why:
PolicyRuleID (#11070) and PolicyCounterIdx (#3301) are sync-only: the BPF
mirror has no slot for them, so every SessionSync sweep/bulk resend shipped
""/0 and wiped the standby's per-policy hit-counter binding. Post-failover
packets then never incremented policy counters, and sessions admitted by a
deleted first policy (policy_id 0, indistinguishable from unattributed)
escaped purge_sessions_bound_to_deleted_first_policy, which identifies them
only via the counter's rule_id.

What:
Add a policyIdentityMemo (SessionID-matched, mirroring the #11064 source-NAT
memo discipline) in four new bounded guard maps on SessionSync
(policyIdentitySentV4/V6 under genSentMu, policyIdentityRecvV4/V6 under
recvGenMu; 24 cap families total). stampInstallGenV4/V6 records a stated
identity and restores it on ""/0 mirror resends, with the receive memo as
fallback for a promoted standby; installClusterSyncedV4/V6 restores/records
before the dataplane write so a stamp-less old-sender resend cannot erase
the binding. Deletes (takeDeleteGen*, deleteClusterSynced*) and the
preserve=false namespace reset evict; preserve=true reclaim retains.
Either field stating a value records both as stated; only the both-empty
mirror-loss signature is restored. SessionID 0 records/restores nothing.
NOT changed: wire format, Rust import/purge logic, BPF ABI. The lossy test
fixture dropSyncOnly9752 now also drops PolicyRuleID, matching production.

cover v4+v6 sweep survival through the real wire codec and receiver install,
stamp-less resend, promoted-standby resend, new-incarnation and SessionID-0
non-inheritance, and delete/reset eviction. RED on origin/master be0f5f9e5:
swept frame lost policy identity rule="" idx=0. GREEN with fix. Full
pkg/cluster suite: only pre-existing base failure
TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752 (PptpCallIDs golden drift,
verified identical on base). Details in docs/log/14359.md.

## PR #14496 — frr: resolve defined policy-statement before bare protocol token in IGP export (#14369) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14369-campaign`

frr: resolve defined policy-statement before bare protocol token in IGP export (#14369)

## Why

`redistributeEntriesAt` took the bare-protocol branch (`knownRedistProtocol`) before the defined-policy-statement branch, so `protocols ospf export static` with a policy-statement named `static` rendered a bare, unfiltered `redistribute static` and the policy's route-map was dead — a silent filter bypass on redistribution into OSPF/OSPFv3/RIP/IS-IS, inconsistent with the BGP renderer in the same package which resolves defined policies first.

## What

- Reorder `redistributeEntriesAt` (`pkg/frr/redistribute.go`) to check the defined-policy-statement branch first on the raw export name (before `direct`→`connected` normalization, so a policy named `direct` is honored), falling through to the bare-protocol branch (self-drop and family-fit unchanged) only when no such policy exists. All four IGP redistributors funnel through this function, so OSPF/OSPFv3/RIP/IS-IS are fixed by the one reorder; BGP is untouched (already policy-first).
- Thread the resolved-as-policy bit from `redistributeEntries` into `applyQNHMetricRouteMap11447` so a defined policy named `static` uses the policy QNH map (`policyMaps[export]`) instead of clobbering its route-map with the bare-protocol `staticMap`.
- Add `pkg/frr/redistribute_policy_precedence_test.go`: OSPF/RIP/IS-IS fixtures (policy named `static`, reject term `from protocol static`), the no-policy negative, a policy named `direct`, and the QNH policy-arm cell.

## Validation

- New tests FAIL on `origin/master` (bare `redistribute static` / bare IS-IS lines rendered, filter discarded) and PASS after the fix.
- Targeted neighbours pass: `TestGenerateProtocols`, `TestRedist`, `TestISIS`, `TestOSPFRedistribute`, `TestQNH`, `TestBGPExport`, `TestRedistProtocol`; `go vet ./pkg/frr/` clean.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: only three pre-existing environmental failures (`TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374`, `TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426` — FRR binary harness `privs_init: could not setgroups`), also failing on the unmodified base.

## Risk

A policy named as a protocol keyword with no `from protocol` term now skip-and-warns instead of rendering a bare redistribute — the documented policy-branch outcome, matching BGP's reading. Bare-token rendering with no such policy defined is byte-identical.

Closes #14369

## PR #14498 — xdp: keep tagged-only when unit 0 is unzoned or disabled (#14334) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14334-campaign`

Why:
On a VLAN trunk, an unzoned, quarantined, or admin-disabled unit 0 (or a disabled native-VLAN unit) stripped USERSPACE_INGRESS_IFACE_FLAG_TAGGED_ONLY from the trunk parent. Untagged VID-0 frames to firewall-owned addresses then escaped TAGGED_ONLY_LOCAL_DROP in XDP and reached the kernel local path for tagged units in the same routing domain. The Rust populate_egress mirror made the same ownership error, so VID 0 also resolved to the non-owner on the AF_XDP path.

What:
Require !AdminDisabled && Zone != "" before a unit 0 or native-VLAN unit owns VID 0 in Go buildUserspaceTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexes and in Rust populate_egress (legacy is_unit: None rows keep #11297 ownership). Rust also prunes (parent,0) keys and native egress marks whose sole owner is disabled/unzoned on tagged-only parents. Pre-existing owner fixtures now carry their zone. NOT changed: XDP shim, adjudication, duplicate-key rejection, ambiguous-native rules.

Validation:
Go RED on base: unzoned/disabled unit0 and disabled/unzoned native returned map[], want map[10:true]. GREEN: TestBuildUserspaceTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexesIgnoresUnzonedAndDisabledUnit0 and TestUserspaceXDPTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexes12055 pass. Rust: cargo test --bins tagged_only 2 passed, native_vlan 6 passed, forwarding_build 299 passed / 1 ignored. Base-attributed failures (TestJunosHostIngressScopeCoverage6619, one 11297 poll assertion) fail identically on unmodified base logic.

Risk:
A genuine VID-0 owner that arrives unzoned (quarantined) now fails closed instead of admitting VID 0 under a sibling zone; zone and enable the unit to receive untagged traffic on a trunk.

Closes #14334

## PR #14499 — cluster: cross-clean scoped and bare generation tables (#14358) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14358-campaign`

Why:
#10512 stamped scoped generation entries on every install but only reclaimed them on scoped policy deletes. Normal closes leaked genSentScoped/recvGenScoped live entries to cap, and a scoped policy delete never tombstoned the bare receiver space, so a delayed same-generation install could resurrect a revoked session on the HA standby once the scoped tombstone was evicted.

Install guards stay per-space. NOT changed: wire format, install path, cap/growth machinery.

## PR #14500 — appid: keep dropped-constraint applications inert in catalog and tuple fallback (#14355) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14355-campaign`

Closes #14355

## Defect
On the tolerant load path, an application with a dropped match constraint (value-less `destination-port;`, malformed `icmp-type bogus`, unimplemented RPC/UUID leaf) compiles to `DestinationPort==""` / `ICMPType==nil`. `BuildCatalog` emitted a protocol-wide `(0,0)` CatalogEntry for it and the AppID-disabled tuple fallback stamped every TCP/UDP/ICMP session with its name — contradicting the #9525 contract that a leniently-loaded bad app is inert. The tuple fallback also rejected port 0 inside a valid explicit `0-N` range that the strict gate and catalog accept, and `ProtocolNumber` did not resolve the hyphenated `icmp-v6` spelling accepted elsewhere.

## Fix
- `config.ApplicationMatchWidened` (new): the widening subset of `ApplicationMatchDrops` — only drops that lost a constraint. Never-matching retained constraints (port/icmp on a protocol that cannot satisfy it) are excluded, so `protocol 0 destination-port 80` keeps its faithful #4008 catalog row.
- `BuildCatalog`: widened app is unemittable (no row, no AppNames name; name-derived id still consumed). `compileApplications` gates AppNames identically (byte-identical parity, pinned by new `TestAppCatalogParityOnDroppedConstraintApps14355`). Tuple fallback `consider` skips widened apps.
- `portInSpec`: range endpoints via new `canonicalRangePort` (0..65535, mirroring strict `validatePortSpec`) + `NormalizeExplicitPortRange` sentinel rejection; bare ports still 1..65535 (`0`, `0-0`, `+80`, `70000` never match).
- `ProtocolNumber`: `icmp-v6` → 58, mirrored in `filterProtocolResolvable`/`protocolIsICMPFamily`, `validateProtocol`, `normalizeProtocol`, userspace canonicalization (→ `icmpv6`), and Rust `proto_number`/`parse_protocol` + filter mirror test list.

## Regression
`TestAppIDSkipsDroppedConstraintAppsAndSupportsZeroRangeAndICMPv6` (`pkg/appid/catalog_dropped_14355_test.go`; the issue-named `catalog_test.go` does not exist): RED on master (`broken-tcp shipped 1 catalog row [{Protocol:6 DstPortLow:0 DstPortHigh:0}]`), GREEN with fix. Covers direct fixtures + end-to-end `CompileConfigLenient`, catalog/AppNames/fallback, 0-N parity, icmp-v6.

## Verification (targeted; full suites exceed job cap here)
- `go test ./pkg/appid/ -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -run TestAppCatalog` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestApplicationMatchWidened14355|TestFilterProtocolNamedSetMatchesRustMirror|TestApplicationReferenceMatchDrops|TestPredefinedApplicationsCarryNoMatchDrops|TestFilterProtocolResolvable'` PASS
- `go vet` + `go build ./...` clean
- Pre-existing unrelated failures in full config/dataplane suites (#14139 PSK, manifest/method-count canaries) untouched. Main agent: please run full `./pkg/config/ ./pkg/dataplane/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` and `cargo test filter_protocol_accept_set_subset_of_resolver`.

Log: `docs/log/14355.md`

## Defect
`validateHostInboundManagedRoutingMismatch` (strict-commit gate via `compiler_tailgates.go`) false-rejected valid configs:

- Mirror `ddnsCheckIPURLValid` and runtime `validateCheckIPURL` both require https — a plaintext URL slipping past commit (lenient/peer-sync/hand-built) fails closed in `CheckIP` before any fetch; Surface A publishes nothing (transient miss, never withdraw).
- Existing CheckIP-against-plaintext test fixtures migrated to TLS servers (update-backend http tests untouched); `SetCheckIPRootCAsForTesting` lets daemon tests trust a test CA via the real cached client. `pkg/ddns/README.md` + `docs/log/14372.md` updated.

## Validation
- F-DR3-H5-1: strict reject incl. non-credentialed + upper-case HTTP; https/upper-case-https/bare-host accepted; lenient warns.
- F-DR3-H5-2: `CheckIP` refuses http (incl. credentialed) before transport, no key in error; TLS positive returns the IP.
- F-DR3-H5-3: Surface A http scope yields no observation, never contacts the attacker server, warns once.
- Full `pkg/ddns` suite green; targeted `pkg/config` DDNS/checkip suites and daemon checkip tests green. RED sensitivity verified by reverting production gates with tests kept. (Full `pkg/config` run exceeded the 300s harness timeout, interrupted without verdict — not claimed.)

## Risk
Operators with a plaintext `checkip-url` must move it to https: strict commit rejects it; lenient load warns and the runtime probe publishes nothing until fixed. Bare-host checkip-urls and backend update endpoints unchanged.

## PR #14520 — nat: require unique-owner proof for nonzero-domain shared exact hits (#14384) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14384-campaign`

Closes #14384

## Why
`lookup_shared_forward_nat_match_with_admission` returned a shared NAT exact hit for any nonzero routing domain without consulting the ambiguity index, while the domain-0 exact branch and both fallback branches require a unique-owner proof. Two forward owners in domain D DNATing to the same backend publish the same domain-preserving reverse key, the second displaces the first, and a domain-D reply was attributed to the last publisher — minting a reverse session under the wrong forward session's decision/zones/policy.

## What
In the exact-hit branch, require the owner-RG indexes and, for nonzero domains, require `nat_ambiguities.is_unique_for(reverse_match_key(reply_key), exact.key)` — the domain-neutral probe the publish path observes/marks (`store.rs` publish). Non-unique, absent, saturated, or no-index hits fall through to the existing canonical/owner paths, which fail closed. Domain-0 behaviour, the canonical and owner paths, and the ICMP quote path are unchanged.

## Validation
- New regression `shared_nat_exact_hit_refuses_ambiguous_same_domain_owner_14384` (two same-key owners in domain D → `None`; single-owner domain-D control resolves; fixture asserts the exact slot holds the last publisher): fails on master, passes after the fix.
- `shared_nat_*`, `lookup_forward_nat*`, `publish_and_remove_shared*`, `icmp_quote*` test groups pass.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` clean on the changed production file (test file carries pre-existing repo-wide fmt drift, untouched outside the new test).

## Risk
Legitimate nonzero-domain exact hits published without ambiguity recording (e.g. restamp/import paths) now fall through and may miss instead of resolving; that fail-closed direction matches every other branch in the function.

## PR #14527 — config: reject misplaced VRRP authentication one level up (#14403) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14403-campaign`

Closes #14403

## Mechanism
The #4288 gate (`validateVRRPAuthenticationAST`) only inspected a `vrrp-group` node's own Keys/direct children via `vrrpAuthLeaf`; `parseVRRPGroups` only visits `vrrp-group` children. An `authentication-key`/`authentication-type` on the owning address node (H1-a), `family` (H1-b), `unit` (H1-c), interface (H1-d), or nested under the group under `virtual-address`/`track-interface` (H1-e) was never read and never gated — the group compiled with `AuthKey==""` and activated claiming the VIP with unauthenticated adverts.

## Fix (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`, same gate/function)
- `vrrpAuthLeafRecursive`: scans the group's whole subtree (H1-e).
- `vrrpMisplacedAuth`/`vrrpDirectAuthLeaf`/`collectVRRPGroups`: any non-group node directly carrying an auth leaf whose subtree contains a vrrp-group (H1-a..H1-d). Strict: hard-reject naming the misplaced keyword with the existing #4288 message. Lenient: warn + drop every affected group via `stripVRRPGroup` (base address survives).
- Scope guard: no vrrp-group in subtree → not reported.
- Secret hygiene: `safeVRRPPathKeys` truncates ancestor Keys at the auth token; group paths use only `vrrpGroupIDKeys` — Keys-packed secrets never leak into errors/warnings. Tested for both ancestor-packed shapes.

Note: H1-a as a direct address child was already hard-rejected on strict by the unrelated #9424 address-list gate (wrong diagnostic, and lenient only warned without dropping the group); it now gets the #4288 reject/drop as well.

## Regression (`pkg/config/vrrp_misplaced_auth_14403_test.go`)
Per-cell H1-a..H1-e × both leaf names: strict reject naming keyword + #4288 + no secret leak; lenient warn-and-drop (group not active, base compiles). Ancestor Keys-packed no-leak cells. Controls: no-auth group still commits/activates; auth leaf with no group nearby (family level) does not hard-reject; existing #4288 position control unchanged.

RED on origin/master (H1-b..H1-e compiled clean, lenient left groups active), GREEN after fix. Full `pkg/config` suite timed out in this sandbox at 300s both before completion (large suite); VRRP/interface/compiler targeted suites pass and `go vet` is clean — main agent should run the full `pkg/config` suite.

Docs: `docs/log/14403.md`.

## PR #14531 — config: install IS-IS interface auth from packed line (#14410) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14410-campaign`

## Why

The IS-IS interface loop in `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go` read only
`child.Children` (via `expandFlatRun`), plus a `child.Keys[2:]` shim
recognising only `passive`/`level`. The packed spelling

```text
protocols { isis { net 49.0001.0000.0000.0001.00;
  interface ge-0/0/0.0 passive authentication-key IFACEKEY authentication-type md5; } }
```

packs the whole tail onto the interface node's own Keys with no
Children, so the loop read nothing: `AuthKey == ""` / `AuthType == ""`
on a clean strict commit, while the FRR renderer still emitted
`ip router isis` and gated circuit auth on the empty key — an
unauthenticated IS-IS adjacency where the operator configured MD5.

The #8662 fold cannot rescue it: it keys on the FIRST tail token and
`passive` is not a scoped interface pair, stranding the whole run; the
#8880 decline strands even a scoped head when a following router-level
`authentication-key` sibling shares the keyword.

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go` (IS-IS `interface` case): when the
  node carries a packed tail (`len(child.Keys) > 2`), read the body
  through `packedBodyChildren(child, isisInterfaceSchema8939())` — the
  schema-driven SSOT the OSPF interface loop uses — before the existing
  `expandFlatRun`. Braced spelling untouched. Mixed tail+braced body:
  the do-not-guess decline (tail ending in a leaf returns braced
  Children alone) is detected and the tail is expanded from a
  childless view so both halves are read; an unmodelled tail still
  expands to nothing. NOT changed: #8436 find-or-create, router-level
  auth, metric -1 preservation, BFD sub-children, the Keys[2:] shim.
- New regression `pkg/config/isis_interface_packed_auth_dr13h3_test.go`:
  braced positive control, passive-first fixture, scoped-head fixture
  with router-level sibling (sibling asserted to land on the router),
  head-keyword matrix, mixed packed+braced cell, routing-instance
  spelling.
- `docs/log/14410.md` records the mechanism and evidence.

## Validation

- RED on base `3541ce77e`: all five subtests fail
  `AuthKey = "" / AuthType = ""`; braced control carries
  `IFACEKEY`/`md5`.
- GREEN after fix and after rebase onto `195f4137a`:
  `TestISISInterfacePackedAuthDR13H3` passes;
  `TestProtocolAuthFlatRunKeepsEveryLeaf8939`, `TestISISMetric*`,
  `TestElidedAuthenticationKey*` pass.

## PR #14534 — session: fail closed on ambiguous shared-egress reverse-NAT matches (#14374) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14374-campaign`

Closes #14374

## Problem (DR4-H2)
`find_forward_nat_match_expiry` and `find_forward_nat_match_inner` (`userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs`) returned the first reverse-index candidate passing tuple + egress-domain checks. The reverse index is domain-agnostic; two tenants (domains A/B) with identical tuples egressing through the same shared uplink (domain W) are indistinguishable, so the first candidate won and `install_reverse_session_from_forward_match` durably minted a reverse session from the wrong tenant's decision (wrong domain/zones/policy, exempt from re-derivation).

## Fix
Both matchers track the first passing candidate; a second passing candidate with a different forward key in a different routing domain returns no match (`None` / `Absent`) and bumps the new `NAT_REVERSE_AMBIGUOUS_TOTAL` counter, surfaced as `xpf_userspace_nat_reverse_ambiguous_total` (Rust ProcessStatus → Go → Prometheus, following the embedded-error-suppressed pattern). Same-key duplicates and same-domain 1:N collisions keep established first-wins behavior. Expiry/idle-crossed semantics preserved.

## Tests
- RED→GREEN: `shared_egress_overlapping_tenants_are_ambiguous_14374` fails on master (first-wins returns tenant A), passes after fix; `shared_egress_single_candidate_control_still_matches_14374` control green.
- `cargo test reverse_egress_domain_11298`: 5 passed (incl. existing asymmetric-egress demux). Full `session::` suite: 442 passed.
- Go: `TestEmitUserspaceDynamicBufferMetrics` re-anchored 108→109 with new series asserted; `pkg/api` green. `pkg/dataplane/userspace` has one pre-existing failure confirmed on clean master.

Log: `docs/log/14374.md`

## PR #14546 — ddns: refuse unguarded delete on garbage conflict-policy (#14432) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14432-campaign`

## Why
`sendRemoveForward` sent any `conflict-policy` other than `replace-owned` down the plain exact-RR delete branch with no DHCID ownership prerequisite. A typo (`skip-existng`, `none`, ...) reaching the backend via the tolerant load/peer-sync path — which downgrades the strict schema-enum reject to a warning — therefore deleted records with no ownership proof on lease release, re-opening the #2648/#2660 boundary breach on the delete side.

## What
- `validConflictPolicy` SSOT in `pkg/ddns/manager.go` (exactly `replace-owned|skip-existing|strict-fail`).
- `newRFC2136Updater` refuses construction for a non-empty invalid policy; the manager falls back to the no-op updater, so no UPDATE is emitted and no ownership is recorded.
- Defence-in-depth in `sendRemoveForward`: a directly-built updater with a garbage policy errors instead of taking the unguarded branch.
- Valid `skip-existing`/`strict-fail` plain deletes, the `replace-owned` DHCID-guarded delete (incl. #2700 `keepDHCID`), and the empty default are unchanged.
- Regression tests (`pkg/ddns/conflict_policy_delete_14432_test.go`) drive `DeleteLease`/`sendRemoveForward` against the stateful fake DNS server: six garbage spellings plus a direct-updater cell must refuse with no wire DELETE and a seeded third-party record surviving; control cells pin the valid deletes.
- Shared root with #14429 (INSERT side) noted in `docs/log/14432.md`; regression cells kept distinct per claim. If #14429 lands first, this rebases onto its single `validConflictPolicy` copy.

## Validation
- RED on origin/master `59fa41531`: garbage `DeleteLease` succeeds via the unguarded plain delete for all six spellings; direct `sendRemoveForward` succeeds; controls pass.
- GREEN after fix: focused regression, full `go test ./pkg/ddns/... -count=1`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/ddns/...` all pass.

## Risk
Fail-closed only — a garbage policy now refuses to withdraw/publish until corrected instead of deleting unguarded. Lingering records are visible; a deleted third-party record is data loss. No valid-policy behaviour changes.

## PR #14548 — config: compile packed RA interface openings with flag first (#14420) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14420-campaign`

Closes #14420

## Mechanism
Packed (brace-elided) RA interface opening `interface ge-0/0/0 managed-configuration default-lifetime 0;` puts the whole body on the interface node's own Keys with no Children. `compileRouterAdvertisement` iterated `inst.node.Children` only (via `expandFlatRun`), and the compact normalizer only folds valued-leaf heads (`"interface default-lifetime"` etc.), so a zero-arg flag opening (`managed-configuration` / `other-stateful-configuration`) stayed packed and the loop saw an empty body: `ManagedConfig=false`, `DefaultLifetimeSet=false`, no prefixes. `pkg/ra` then advertised Router Lifetime 1800 for an explicit `default-lifetime 0` — RFC 4861 §6.2.1 "this router is NOT a default router" inverted (#4119's defect by a dropped leaf; distinct from the flat `set` route fixed in #8939). Braced twin and valued-leaf packed opening already compiled correctly.

## Fix
- `compileRouterAdvertisement`: expand the instance body with `packedBodyChildren(inst.node, schemaForPath("protocols","router-advertisement","interface"))` before `expandFlatRun` — the same schema-driven expansion the OSPF/OSPFv3 interface loops use. Tails outside the modelled grammar return Children unchanged (no behaviour change there).
- No sender change: `DefaultLifetimeSet` now reaches `buildRA`, which already honors explicit 0.

## Regression
- `pkg/config.TestRAInterfacePackedOpening14420`: managed opening (ManagedConfig + DefaultLifetimeSet/0), other-stateful opening (whole tail incl. prefix), packed-vs-braced parity, valued-leaf control.
- `pkg/ra.TestBuildRA_PackedOpeningPreservesExplicitZero14420`: packed spelling marshals RouterLifetime 0 + ManagedConfiguration true, matching braced twin.

## Validation
RED on origin/master `70702de41`: packed managed/other openings dropped (`ManagedConfig=false, DefaultLifetimeSet=false`, prefix lost), twin mismatch; control passed. GREEN after: both new tests, `TestRAInterfaceFlatRunKeepsEveryLeaf8939`, `TestRADNSServer*6695`, `TestBuildRA_FlatRunPreservesExplicitZero8939`, `TestBuildRA_4119_*`; gofmt/vet clean; re-verified on rebased head `57dc68397`. Full `pkg/config` suite exceeds the 300s harness cap, timing out in pre-existing `TestPathologicalWildcardFanoutIsRefused6767` (group-expansion stack, untouched by this change).

## Risk
Low: one reader widened via the established `packedBodyChildren` helper; braced/flat spellings unchanged; unmodelled tails fall back to prior behaviour.

## PR #14550 — config: redact credentials embedded in event-options commands (#14413) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14413-campaign`

Closes #14413

## Why
An `event-options … then change-configuration commands` payload is live configuration the event engine executes with internal commit authority after #9939 plant-class adjudication, but `show event-options` printed `ThenCommands` verbatim and `RedactedClone()` never inspected the `commands` leaf. A quoted embedded command lexes to ONE AST token, so no token equals `pre-shared-key` and `secretIndices` never fired — a super-user-authored IKE PSK rendered in cleartext to PermView readers on `Format()`/`FormatSet()`/`FormatJSON()`/`FormatXML()`, both `show event-options` sites, and `FormatCompareRedacted`.

## What
- One shared render-time helper `RedactEmbeddedChangeConfigCommand` (`pkg/config/ast_redact.go`): lexes the command with the real config lexer (never `strings.Fields`), requires the `set` mint verb (`delete` carries no secret value), and masks tokens via the EXISTING `secretIndices`/`urlLeafIndices` sets — no second credential list — replacing values with `SecretDataPlaceholder` (qualifiers like `ascii-text` kept; gated `key`/`password`/`community` keep their AST context rules; URL userinfo/query redacted via `RedactURL`).
- Wired into both `showEventOptions` loops (gRPC `server_show_events.go`, CLI `cli_show_routing.go`) and into `redactNodes`/`fingerprintCompareNodes`, locating the `change-configuration commands` pair on the flattened path for every compiler-accepted shape: quoted packed leaf, bracket list, `commands { … }` block children, flat-set children, and the unquoted joined tail (KeysQuoted provenance decides grouping exactly as `eventChangeConfigCommands` does; a clean tail is left byte-identical). Compare clones fingerprint masked tokens with the existing `\x00xpf-sha256=` suffix so secret-equality survives in diffs.
- Stored `ThenCommands`, the compiler reader join semantics, and event execution are untouched. `docs/log/14413.md` records the change.

## Validation
- New regression tests RED on master (PSK verbatim in all four `RedactedClone` formats + gRPC show output), GREEN post-fix: quoted hierarchical, quoted flat-set, unquoted flat-set, block + bracket shapes across all four formats; `FormatCompareRedacted` identical-trees clean / changed-PSK fingerprint-only; helper table (IKE PSK, BGP/OSPF-MD5 keys, SNMP community, DDNS token masked; GRE `key`, host-name, login-class, delete controls verbatim); compiled `ThenCommands` and post-display stored commands still raw; CLI twin via configstore commit.
- Fail-on-revert verified (stashing production files re-fails). Neighbour `pkg/config` redact/event suites green; targeted `pkg/grpcapi`/`pkg/cli` show tests green. Pre-existing unrelated failures in `pkg/grpcapi`/`pkg/cli` (`TestShowTextGolden` #14139 gate, predefined-app-set #14339, screen-keys census, annotate gate, `TestCompleteConfig_PredefinedApplicationSets_5763`) confirmed identical on pristine master.

## Risk
Display-only: a persisted credential-bearing policy still fires identically; only PermView display now shows `##SECRET-DATA##`. Documented residuals at the helper: a credential committed as a hierarchical child under a final secret keyword is not an executable command shape (classifyPlan rejects it) and matches the AST walk's existing no-mask there; `delete` commands are never masked (no secret value).

What:
Add validateVRRPVIPCrossGroupStrict in pkg/config: per resolved kernel interface plus family, a canonical host-IP to group map across explicit vrrp-groups and RETH-derived instances (when RETH VRRP synthesis is active) hard-rejects a second distinct VRID, naming the VIP and both groups. Lenient load downgrades to a warning (lenientVRRPVIPCrossGroup, #1960 no-brick). Add the pkg/vrrp UpdateInstances backstop refusing the second claimant via the existing rejectedDesired pattern. NOT changed: same VIP on different units/interfaces stays legal; different VIPs on one unit stay legal; within-group dedupe unchanged.

Validation:
RED on pristine origin/master e466f0854 plus only the new tests: TestVRRPCrossGroupSameVIPFailsCommit, alias-spelling, lenient-warn, explicit-vs-RETH, and TestUpdateInstances_RefusesSecondVIPClaimant14407 all fail; controls pass both sides. GREEN: pkg/config TestVRRPCrossGroup 6/6, pkg/vrrp 14407 tests 3/3, related VRRP/Reth suites and full pkg/vrrp pass, go vet clean. Full pkg/config exceeded the 10m timeout on both branch and pristine master (base-attributed).

Risk:
Operators with two groups sharing one VIP on a unit must give each group a distinct VIP or merge them; strict commit now rejects, lenient load warns and seats only the first election.

Closes #14407

## PR #14553 — config: merge cross-container duplicate ipsec policies (#14430) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14430-campaign`

Why:
compileIPsec built a fresh IPsecPolicyDef per policy block and stored it unconditionally, so two same-name policy blocks under two different ipsec containers (or two security roots) wholesale-replaced each other: the first container's strong proposal list and perfect-forward-secrecy were silently discarded, leaving the second block's weak suite with no PFS. The #9023 fold spans only one ipsec parent and never sees cross-container twins.

What:
Find-or-create in the IPsec policy loop in pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go, mirroring the IKE-policy / gateway / VPN loops in the same file; scalar leaves stay last-wins when restated, and a twin stating neither leaves earlier values intact. The proposals arm skips a reference already present so a twin re-listing the same proposal does not render it twice. NOT changed: same-parent #9023 fold, proposal gates, resolvability gate, proposal-set expansion, algorithm allowlist.

Validation:
New pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_policy_duplicate_dr17h1_test.go (cross-container strict+lenient, two-security-roots, same-parent and single-container controls, dedup control). RED on pre-fix master with Proposals=[WEAK] want [STRONG WEAK] and PFSGroup=0 want 19; GREEN after fix (5/5), rebased onto current master and re-verified. The #14139 PSK-gate failures in the wider IPsec run are base-attributed on detached origin/master (2b810ccd1) without this change.

Risk:
Merged Proposals is the ordered union in document order; single-container configs compile byte-identically.

Closes #14430

## PR #14556 — config: union range-free groupReplace port leaves under apply-groups (#14423) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14423-campaign`

Why:

except-filter now consult the new predicate alongside the existing
leaf-list path, merging through `mergeLeafListInto`. Ranges on either
side and all other `groupReplace` leaves keep the pinned inline-wins

compilers — the firewall resolves each token independently and NAT

the manager falls back to the no-op updater (no UPDATE, no
ownership); add defense-in-depth refuse-ADD and refuse-DELETE guards
in sendAdd and sendRemoveForward for directly-built updaters; warn at
commit in ddnsBackendWarningsForPolicy (both families) naming the
bad value. Regression tests in pkg/ddns and pkg/config cover six
garbage spellings plus the three valid policies and the empty
default as controls. NOT changed: the strict schema enum and the
valid policies' wire behaviour.

Validation: RED on base e7a473021 - all six garbage subtests fail
with UpsertLease succeeded (unguarded bare Insert) and the config
test finds no conflict-policy warning. GREEN after the fix: the new
tests, the neighbouring RFC2136 conflict tests, all TestDHCPDDNS*
tests, and the full pkg/ddns suite pass. Full pkg/config suite shows
pre-existing IPsec failures verified identical on unmodified base.

Risk: a DDNS block carrying a garbage conflict-policy now publishes
nothing (previously published unguarded) and warns at commit; fixing
the typo restores publishing. The same-root delete guard is shared
with sibling #14432, which remains the delete-side audit owner.

Closes #14429

## PR #14562 — config: adopt group OSPF authentication container beside packed leaf (#14414) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

config: adopt group OSPF authentication container beside packed leaf (#14414)

container was dropped, the interface compiled with an empty key,

unauthenticated. The md5-vs-simple variant downgraded to cleartext,

container is adopted beside the leaf and the compiler merges both

keys and the #12923 default-policy choice keep the guard (their
pair/value semantics are first-match sensitive); bare leaves such
as `rip;` still suppress a genuine duplicate. Regression cells in
`pkg/config/group_merge_ospf_auth_container_dr14h1_test.go` cover
the OSPF main/control/application-level (protocols/ospf/area/
interface)/two-group/downgrade/rollover/reverse-precedence cases,
the bare-`rip;` duplicate, and the policy and firewall `from`
extensions; `pkg/frr/ospf_group_auth_container_14414_test.go` pins

downgrade, missing rollover key, and dropped `from` conditions;
they pass after the fix (`go test ./pkg/config -run 14414`,
`go test ./pkg/frr -run 14414`). Neighbour group suites (#9855,
#7648, default-policy #12823/#12923/#11821, apply-groups) stay
green; remaining full-package failures reproduce identically on
pristine origin/master. gofmt and go vet clean on changed files.

Adopt-beside relies on compilers merging sibling `authentication`

## PR #14566 — config: poison lenient policer discard+marking conflict to discard (#14443) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14443-campaign`

Closes #14443

## Mechanism
Merged firewall policer / three-color-policer `then { discard; loss-priority high; }` (group `then` beside inline `then`, or duplicate policer roots) strict-rejected via #8445, but the lenient arm in `compiler_uniformgates_filter.go` only appended a warning. The single-valued `ThenAction` is last-wins and the `loss-priority` arms were unfenced, so the marking won: `ThenAction="loss-priority high"` → snapshot `DiscardExcess=false` → excess traffic metered and forwarded, authored discard unenforced on lenient load/HA-sync/restore.

## Fix
- Primary: `failClosedPolicerThenConflicts` (mirrors #4375 `failClosedFilterTerminalConflicts`) forces conflicting policers/three-color-policers to `discard` on the lenient path; authored `ThenActions` preserved, single-action policers untouched. Warning text updated.
- Complementary: fence all four `loss-priority` arms with `policerThenSawDiscard9882` like `forwarding-class`.
- Updated stale lenient docs in `compiler_opts.go`/`compiler_validate_strict_filter.go` and `TestPolicerThenConflictHarmIsOrderDependent_8445` which asserted the old lenient survivor.

## Tests
- New `pkg/config/policer_then_conflict_lenient_14443_test.go`: group-merged policer + three-color, duplicate-root producer, both authored orders (incl. forwarding-class), single-action strict+lenient controls.
- RED on origin/master c0b272c45 (lenient ThenAction="loss-priority high"), GREEN after fix.
- `go vet`/`gofmt` clean; #8445 configstore tests pass.
- Note: `TestPolicerThenNonLeafTail_9882` fails identically with/without this fix (pre-existing on master). Full `pkg/config` suite timed out in this environment (300s harness cap) — targeted policer/three-color subsets pass; please run full suite in CI.

Log: `docs/log/14443.md`
