## PR #14571 — config: capture packed NAT rule-set header scopes (#14421) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14421-campaign`

Closes #14421

## Why
A NAT rule-set with its `from`/`to` clause packed onto the header line (`rule-set RS from zone trust { rule ... }`) compiled match-any in strict (no error) and lenient (no warning) modes: `collectNATScopes` and all three NAT scope gates read only `node.Children`, so the packed tail was invisible and the rule-set installed with an empty (match-any) scope for source (`from`+`to`), destination (`from`), and static (`from`) NAT across zone/interface/routing-instance.

## What
- New shared helper `natRuleSetChildren` (`compiler_nat_helpers.go`) expands the packed header tail with the grammar's own arity — `from`/`to`, then a scope kind, then one synthesised clause child per scope value (empty bracket `from zone [ ]` synthesised present-but-empty via bracket provenance) — returning real children unchanged for braced/unmodelled tails. `packedBodyChildren` cannot serve here: the tail runs through the multi-valued `zone` leaf whose terminal declares no body (#6818 guard).
- `collectNATScopes`, the mixed-kind gate (#4881), the empty-scope gate (#7525), and DNAT-`to` detection (#3444, shared with the lenient-omit builder) all read through this SSOT; the three compiler call sites pass their NAT kind.
- Regression: `compiler_nat_packed_header_14421_test.go` — packed-vs-braced typed equality for every clause/kind cell, packed `from`+`to` pair, lenient capture, and gate cells (mixed packed+child, empty-bracket packed, DNAT-`to` packed) in strict-reject and lenient-warn modes.
- `docs/log/14421.md`.

## Validation
- RED on origin/master `70702de41`: all 14 packed cells compiled match-any, gate cells silently accepted.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestPackedNATRuleSetHeader|TestDNATRuleSet|TestValidateNATRuleSetMixedScope|TestNATRuleSet|TestCompilerStamps'` PASS; NAT neighbour suites green; `go vet` clean.
- Full `pkg/config` suite exceeds the 300s tool window in this worktree; `TestPackedOptInHoldsForEveryLeafPair8768` fails identically with the fix stashed (pre-existing on this base, unrelated).

## Risk
Braced and flat-set spellings return `node.Children` unchanged (bit-identical); unmodelled packed tails likewise. The only change is previously-invisible packed scopes/gate violations now behaving exactly as their braced twins.

## PR #14702 — config: compile NAT rules with a packed match (#14415) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14415-campaign`

Closes #14415

## Mechanism
`rule r1 match source-address 10.0.0.0/24 { then { ... } }` parses with the match packed into the rule node's Keys and only `then` in Children. The NAT compilers read match only via `FindChildren("match")` (Children-only), so the packed match was never seen: `matchAuthored` stayed false (disarming #8430/#9874), SNAT compiled unconstrained, and DNAT published no entry — silently deleting a `destination-nat off` exemption.

## Fix
- `compileNATSource`/`compileNATDestination`/`compileNATStatic` expand each rule node via `packedBody` with its rule schema and read match/then from the expanded node.
- `packedBodyChildren` leaf-body guard: when the deepest packed node is a leaf, return synthesized roots + real children as siblings if every real child is a declared sibling statement repeating no root head (preserves #6818 leaf decline, pinned by existing test).
- The primary normalize admission ("rule match") was measured and rejected: without `packedStatements` on NAT rule, the fold attached the braced `then` under the synthesized `match` and #9877 recorded `then` as unknown leaf. Documented in docs/log/14415.md.

## Regression
`pkg/config/compiler_nat_packed_match_dr14h2_test.go`: SNAT packed (SourceAddresses + matchAuthored), DNAT off packed+braced (destination, Off, installed via DestinationNATRuleExcludedReason), DNAT pool packed, scope-only control, fully-packed control. RED on origin/master, GREEN after. Sharded NAT/compact suite: only pre-existing failures also present on base (TestElidedDepthCoverage8850, TestPackedOptInHoldsForEveryLeafPair8768, TestZoneInterfacePackedApplyMacroOwnKeysCompiles12835). Full pkg/config suite exceeds local timeout; main agent should run it.

PERMIT via LenientContentDropped so the snapshot is refused;
deny/reject keep last-wins since refusing a deny would fail open.
Identical repeats stay legal. Scheduler definition merging (#5825),
the reference-existence gate, and description duplicates unchanged.

## PR #14743 — config: reject routing policy-term conflicting then actions (#14425) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

## Why
A merged routing policy-statement term carrying both `then accept` and `then reject` resolved silently: the compiler assigned the single `PolicyTerm.Action` field last-write-wins, and group expansion dropped the group terminal via the inline-wins override, so the conflict never reached any gate. An inline reject meant to block a BGP import could be silently overridden/dropped with a clean commit. Sibling gates existed for firewall (#4375) and security policy (#3043) but not routing terms.

Single-action controls (same-reject both sides, accept+local-preference, reject-only, modifier-only) unchanged.
- Full `pkg/config` suite minus `TestSlotEscapeSweep` (times out on pristine base too under host load): head failure set identical to base — 51 pre-existing IPsec/plaintext failures, no new failures.
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; gofmt clean on touched files.

## PR #14753 — config: require family segment before filter in packed unit gate (#14629) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14629-campaign`

## Summary

Follow-up to #14435/#14565 (merged `fda4502d5`). The #14435 gate exemption `unitPackedTailHasFamilyFilter14435` (`compiler_interfaces_unsupported.go`) returned true if `family inet|inet6` appeared **anywhere** in a packed unit's Keys tail, without requiring the filter to sit inside/after that family segment. `unit 0 filter input DISCARD-BAD family inet { address ...; }` (filter FIRST, family later) therefore exempted the unit-level filter from the #12090 gate while `packedBody` expanded only the trailing family segment — the filter, the addresses and the family were all dropped and the unit strict-committed as an empty `Unit{Number:0}` (no addresses, no filter, no family), lenient also silent: accepted-but-dropped, fail-open. Found by campaign hostile review (Fix14435b).

**Fix:** rename the helper to `unitPackedTailHasFamilyBeforeFilter14435` and make it schema-arity-aware. It walks the unit tail with the same open-levels stack `packedBodyChildren` keeps, consumes each statement by the unit schema's own arity (a value spelling `family`/`filter`/`inet`, e.g. `description family`, is never a keyword), honours quoted-token provenance, and returns true only when an unquoted `family inet|inet6` segment is reached **before** any unit-level `filter`/`simple-filter` hit. A filter hit first, an apply statement, a quoted keyword-position token, or a token outside the modelled grammar returns false (do-not-guess, fail-closed for the exemption). Both call sites updated (braced-filter-child exemption in `isInterfaceDirectFilterConsumerPath12090`, packed-tail exemption in `isInterfacePackedFilterConsumer12090`); old helper name removed, no shim. No compiler reader change: genuinely consumed spellings (family-first, point-to-point-first, tunnel-first, `family inet filter input …`) compile identically; only the previously mis-exempted filter-first spelling now strict-rejects (#12090, naming `filter input`) and lenient-warns (#1960 posture preserved).

Closes #14629

## Test report

- **New regression** `TestPackedUnitFilterFirstFamilyRejects14629` in `compiler_interfaces_packed_unit_dr17h6_test.go`: reject cells (inet/inet6 braced bodies, output direction, packed family body, `simple-filter` first, filter-first-then-braced-family-filter) each asserting strict #12090 rejection **and** a lenient #12090 warning; accept controls (family-first, point-to-point-first, family-packed filter, `description family`/`description filter` values consumed by arity, tunnel-first) asserting no #12090 diagnostic and populated `FamilyInet`/filter/address/tunnel hooks.
- **RED/GREEN verified:** restoring the HEAD (pre-fix) gate makes the five filter-first reject cells strict-compile clean (the bug); with the fix all cells pass. Pre-fix behaviour also measured directly: strict compiled the filter-first spelling to an empty `Unit{Number:0}` with no warning.
- **Focused suites pass:** `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestPackedUnit|TestFilterKeyword|TestPackedCompoundFamilyFilter|TestInterfaceMplsAny|PackedUnitFamily|TestCompactFilterHeads|TestInterfaceFilterPackedRun|TestMemberlessRange|12090'` — PASS (includes the unchanged #14435 p2p/tunnel, #9620 packed-family and #12090 population tests).

### Full-suite note (pre-existing upstream failures)

`go test ./pkg/config/` on this base additionally hits failures that reproduce **identically on a clean `origin/master` worktree** (48b24754c, newer than this branch's base) — a nil-pointer panic in `validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST`/`nodeVal` under the `TestCompactBlock*` census tests and `TestAuthKeyWithoutTypeInRoutingInstanceIsRefused14400` (#14400/#2419 area). They are unrelated to this change (different subsystem, present without it) and are not addressed here.

## PR #14754 — grpcapi: bind persistent-NAT clear generation in signed request (#14580) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14580-pnat-generation`

grpcapi: bind persistent-NAT clear generation in signed request (#14580)

Closes #14580

## Why
The forwarded `clear-persistent-nat` origin/generation rode unsigned gRPC metadata (`x-peer-persistent-nat-*`). The #4107 fabric token binds only method + protobuf request digest + window — no metadata — so a captured token replayed inside its window with `generation=MaxUint64` durably poisoned `RemoteGenerations[origin]=MaxUint64` on the receiver: every genuine peer lease batch was then silently dropped (`batch.Generation < generation → return nil`, no log) forever, surviving restart with no expiry or self-heal (Y06-02).

## What
- **Signed body (root fix):** origin/generation now travel inside `SystemActionRequest` (`persistent_nat_origin=9`, `persistent_nat_generation=10`; protobuf regenerated), so the existing #10709 request-digest MAC binds them. A replay whose origin/generation differs from the minted call is rejected `Unauthenticated` by the fabric interceptor before the handler/watermark runs.
- Deleted the unsigned-metadata extractor; both proxies (grpcapi `SystemAction` fan-out, CLI peer dial) forward via the signed body (`persistentNatClearRequestWithGeneration`, proto.Clone — caller's request never mutated).
- Legacy `x-peer-persistent-nat-{origin,generation}` keys added to `reservedPeerMetadataKeys`: stripped on both listeners, never honored. A legacy forwarded clear (empty body) clears locally with no fence (pre-#11486 semantics); non-forwarded calls smuggling the fields are rejected `InvalidArgument`.
- **Manager defense-in-depth** (`pkg/dataplane/userspace`): a forwarded clear jumping a *known* peer's watermark by >1024 generations is refused (error, `PersistentNatGenerationJumpsRejected` counter, Warn log, nothing persisted, helper never invoked); first contact with an unseen origin remains unbounded. ## Risk
Mixed-version cluster degrades safely: new→old peer clear = local clear with no fence on the old peer; old→new likewise (metadata ignored). No wire change for other `SystemAction` verbs (new fields default empty/zero). The 1024 jump bound only applies when a watermark already exists.

## PR #14755 — firewall: reject no-protocol disjoint L4 filter terms (#14445) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14445-campaign`

Why:
A firewall-filter term with no protocol that combines a port or tcp-flags predicate with an icmp-type/icmp-code predicate ANDs matcher arms no single packet can satisfy: ports require TCP/UDP, tcp-flags requires TCP, and icmp-type/code require ICMP/ICMPv6. The term could never match, so a then discard/reject term silently fell through to the implicit accept (fail-open), while each predicate alone with no protocol remains legitimate and enforceable.

What:
Extend validateFilterCrossFieldStrict in the Go compiler to strict-reject no-protocol port+icmp and tcp-flags+icmp pairs (all port polarities including *-except; lenient path keeps the existing cross-field warning) and extend the Rust check_cross_field_satisfiability backstop to fail the whole snapshot closed with the combined predicates port+icmp-type/code and tcp-flags+icmp-type/code. Ports plus tcp-flags together stay accepted because one TCP packet satisfies both. NOT changed: the matcher, single-predicate no-protocol terms, and the explicit-protocol #3723 arms.

Validation:
New Go TestFilterNoProtoDisjointRejected_14445 (9 cells) and TestFilterNoProtoSinglePredicateAccepted_14445 and Rust filter_disjoint_noproto_14445 tests fail on pristine 809a538ce and pass on this head; targeted Go cross-field suites and 12 Rust filter/crossfield tests pass. Full pkg/config suite shows only two failures reproduced identically on pristine base. go vet is clean.

Risk:
Leniently loaded legacy configs carrying this shape now warn in Go and have their userspace snapshot refused in favour of prior-good state; no committed valid config changes behaviour.

Closes #14445

## PR #14757 — dhcprelay: bind IA-less Confirm/Release/Decline replies (#14599) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14599-campaign`

Why: the DHCPv6 relay's pending key (xid + Client ID DUID + lowest IA type/IAID) could never match a server Reply carrying no IA, yet RFC 8415 makes the IA-less Reply the conformant shape for Confirm (§18.3.3 NotOnLink), Release (§18.3.7 Success), and Decline (§18.3.8). Those replies were dropped as `RepliesDroppedNoRequest`: a roaming client never learned NotOnLink and kept a stale address, and the drop counter misdirected operators.

What: `insertPending6` (`pkg/dhcprelay/pending6.go`) records the primary IA-bound binding plus, for exactly Confirm/Release/Decline, an IA-less alias key carrying the same recorded client address and request type. The production client loop and the test arming helper insert through it; `pending6KeyFor` is unchanged, so IA-echo (NoBinding) replies match as before, and every #10699/#14181 check (configured server source, outer peer-address equality, legitimate answer type, Interface-ID routing) applies on the alias path unchanged. Regression tests in `relay6_noia_14599_test.go` cover the probe rows, the drop boundary, the IA-echo control, and forged cells on the alias path. README and `docs/log/14599.md` document the alias.

Validation: RED on origin/master 8f89c2d89 — Confirm NotOnLink, Release Success, and Decline Success rows failed with client writes=0 (dropped as unmatched); GREEN after the fix — `go test ./pkg/dhcprelay/ -run 14599 -count=1` passes all 7 new tests, full `go test ./pkg/dhcprelay/ -count=1` passes (including #10699/#14181 suites), `go vet` and `gofmt` clean. An IA-less Reply to a recorded Solicit/Request/Renew/Rebind is still dropped, pinned by tests.

Risk: forged IA-less replies gain no new acceptance surface (same xid + exact DUID guess, configured server source, recorded peer). Confirm/Release/Decline transactions occupy two pending ring slots for their TTL; eviction remains availability-direction only. No live-cluster smoke (fake-conn scope per the issue's decisive check).

Closes #14599

## PR #14760 — dhcp: accept any server reply in REBINDING (#14600) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14600-campaign`

Why:
REBINDING required the granting server in both v4 and v6 matchers
(the rebind parameter was discarded), defeating T2 in failover-pair
deployments: RFC 2131 4.3.2 and RFC 8415 18.2.5 define REBINDING/
Rebind as any-server, so a partner ACK was rejected and the client
fell through to full re-acquisition with address/PD churn.

What:
Name the rebind parameter in v4RenewMatcher/v6RenewMatcher: in
rebind mode require only a present valid server identity while
keeping xid/chaddr/DUID/interface/type checks; renew mode keeps
the granting-server check. Accepted replies already store the
answering server (leaseFromACKv4 serverID, parseV6ReplyChecked
v6ServerDUID), so the partner becomes the next RENEW binding.
Update NAK/RenewalBindingStats docs, rewrite README 182-188, add
TestRebindAcceptsAnyServer14600 and update 9944 rebind cells.

Validation:
RED on master: partner ACK/NAK/Reply rejected. RED-on-revert
(stash renew.go only): new + updated 9944 tests fail. GREEN:
targeted matcher tests pass; go test ./pkg/dhcp/... -count=1,
go vet, git diff --check pass.

Risk:
Any server passing xid/chaddr/DUID on the interface socket can
now answer at T2 (RFC semantics, including NAK revocation);
bounded by those checks plus required server identity. No lab
failover capture; predicate and storage are unit-covered.

Closes #14600

## PR #14761 — daemon: re-resolve web-management bind after address convergence (#14582) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14582-webmgmt-rebind`

Closes #14582

## Defect (Y07-01)
`reconcileWebManagement` runs early in `applyConfigLocked` (deliberately, for credential revocation) before `applyDataplaneAndHACore`/networkd applies interface addresses. `resolveInterfaceAddr` read the live kernel, found no address yet, fell back to loopback, and the fingerprint recorded that as converged — `show system services` reported Listening, the `StateFailed`-only re-assert gate never re-drove it, and the DHCP lifeline fast path skipped web-management entirely. Off-box REST/J-Web stayed silently down until a later commit (fails closed to loopback; no exposure). Verified RED by executing the real reconcile + re-assert path against the kernel seam: address appearing afterwards changed nothing.

## Fix
- **Degraded is recorded, not converged**: `resolveInterfaceAddrDegraded` → per-leg `api.Config.HTTPBindDegraded/HTTPSBindDegraded` → `mgmtEndpoint.{http,https}Degraded`; `reconcileTo` treats a degraded-change as a leg change and advances the flag only on a successful rebind.
- **Honest state**: new `sysservices.StateStale` — a degraded (loopback-fallback) or address-replaced leg reports `addr (stale bind)`, never Listening, reflecting the address actually bound. `Daemon.effectiveListeners` folds in a per-leg re-resolution (`mgmtBindStaleLegs`) so the vanished-address case (fingerprint still matches an old resolution) is also Stale. `mgmtListenerDown` keys on `Failed || Stale` on that same snapshot, preserving the #6803 invariant that operator view and retry trigger are one question. The `xpf_management_listener_state` metric now also emits the https surface and the stale series (its test updated: 12 series).
- **Same-commit convergence**: second `reconcileWebManagement` in `applyConfigLocked` after `applyDataplaneAndHACore`, warn-only (retry debt, not a commit failure).
- **DHCP sibling**: `rebindWebMgmtForLeaseChange` on the management-only fast path — gated by `webMgmtBindsToDHCPInterface` (bound interface has a DHCP/DHCPv6 unit), serialized under `applySem`, re-reads the active config under the semaphore, non-fatal (the #2884 shape).

Auth safety unchanged: the fallback stays loopback, the nil-auth publish still gates on live addresses, and degraded→real rebinds flow through the existing sanctioned/intersection logic.

## Regression (`pkg/daemon/webmgmt_rebind_14582_test.go`)
- `TestWebMgmtRebindsWhenInterfaceAddressAppears14582` — decisive z4 cell: no-address-yet → Stale + owner-down; address appears; one tick → Listening at `10.0.0.1:443`; healthy leg not bounced.
- `TestWebMgmtRebindsOnAddressReplacement14582` — vanished/replaced address reports Stale, rebinds to the new address, stale socket closed.
- `TestWebMgmtDHCPLeaseChangeRebindsBoundInterface14582` — gate controls (DHCP vs static) + lease rebind counted via the seam.
- `TestWebMgmtPostNetworkdReconcileResolvesInSameApply14582` — source wiring (post-networkd reconcile + DHCP fast-path call).

Sensitivity: reverting the gate to Failed-only reds the decisive cell at the owner-down assertion (verified). Bounded daemon suite (`14582|6803|8597|5714|5715|6401|Management|Mgmt|WebMgmt`), `pkg/sysservices`, and the #8195 metric tests pass; `go vet` clean on touched packages.

## PR #14762 — config: stop empty redundant-ether-options panicking the RETH gate (#14729) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14729-campaign`

## Why

#14441 (86f517f8c) deleted the `rg == nil` guard in `validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST` when it added the elided-spelling expansion, so an interface with an **empty** `redundant-ether-options` stanza — `redundant-ether-options { }`, or the bare leaf `redundant-ether-options;` — reaches `nodeVal(nil)` and panics the pre-walk on commit, commit-check and the tolerant load / HA-sync path alike:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
  nodeVal(...)                               compiler_applications.go:1340
  validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST       compiler_reth_rg_token.go:113
  runPreWalkGates                            compiler_prewalk.go:778
```

`TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` (found by the #14442 lane, reproduced on clean `origin/master`) hit it deterministically via the census's empty-stanza skeleton fixture, so the test could not run at all. Any operator config carrying an empty reo stanza crashes the same way, bricking the boot the #1960 no-brick rule protects.

An empty stanza carries **no** `redundancy-group` token — the absent-token case #6782 deliberately scopes out (like no reo stanza at all). A present `redundancy-group;` leaf with no value still produces a node and must still be gated.

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_reth_rg_token.go`: restore the `rg == nil` guard after the #14441 expansions, with the absent-vs-present distinction recorded at the site. `nodeVal` deliberately unchanged (its callers nil-check explicitly; nil-tolerance would reclassify present-but-empty tokens as absent and mask the next dropped guard). The #6782 classifier, suppression and compiler reader are untouched.
- `pkg/config/compiler_reth_rg_token_6782_test.go`: new `TestEmptyRedundantEtherOptionsDoesNotPanic14729` — both empty spellings commit clean on strict + lenient, keep the address, no #6782 warning, `RedundancyGroup=0`; plus the boundary cell proving a present-but-valueless token still rejects naming `reth0` / warns+suppresses lenient.
- Census fallout the panic had masked (census now runs: 1202 checked, 72 divergent):
  - Removed the 13 `interfaces xpfname` lines fixed by #14442 and the 2 RA M/O lines fixed by #14420 from `compact_block_divergences_2419.txt` (regenerated via `XPF_GEN_2419=1`, drift classified in `inventoryNotes`).
  - `interfaces xpfname mtu`: `filedStillOpen` → `filedFixed` (`#14442`); RA M/O pair anchored in `filedFixed` (`#14420`). Known-true control re-anchored on the hand-verified `interfaces xpfname aggregated-ether-options lacp active` so it keeps two anchors from two compiler files.
  - Deleted the 15 stale rows from `compact_block_permanent_exclusions_8690.txt`; the two `family inet6` unit rows reclassed `open` → `partial` to match their new drop shape.
- `docs/log/14729.md`: defect, fix, census fallout, RED/GREEN.

## Validation

- **RED** on `origin/master` (9307e0940): `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` panics in `nodeVal(nil)`; minimal probes (`interfaces { xpfname { redundant-ether-options { } } }`, `interfaces { reth0 { redundant-ether-options; } }`) panic in `CompileConfigLenient`. New test panics identically with only the production fix reverted.
- **GREEN** with fix: `TestEmptyRedundantEtherOptionsDoesNotPanic14729`, `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419`, `TestCompactBlockCensusReport2419`, all #6782/#14441 reth tests, `TestFlatRunResidueSchemasResolve9792`, and the #8690 register gates pass; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean; `go build ./pkg/config` ok.
- **Base-attributed, not touched**: `TestPermanentExclusionsMatchTheInventory8690` (16 stale `open` rows from #14409/#14426/#14428-era fixes) and `TestCompactNormalizeScopePreservesCompiledResult8690` (4 unexaminable `policy-options … from` sites) fail identically with this change stashed — other lanes' inventory obligations, unblocked (not caused) by this fix.

## Risk

One nil guard restored to its pre-#14441 form in a single AST pre-walk gate; the present-but-empty token keeps its strict-reject / lenient warn+suppress behaviour (pinned by the boundary cell). Census artifacts only record measurements the panic had hidden. No compiler, wire or schema change beyond the panic itself.

sources drop per node; no-`from protocol` terms expand over the
node-fitting domain (#14380). The per-peer `route-map out` remains
the per-peer gate; bare protocol tokens keep the existing unfiltered
global path. This is not the #2473 leak (that was an *unfiltered*
`redistribute ospf`). `redistReferencedNodes14380` records both BGP
nodes so the maps are defined and join the ApplyFull collision belt.

encoded the bug are narrowed/updated, and the #9667 caller census

## Summary
The skip-existing/strict-fail RFC 2136 conflict guard used per-type `RRsetNotUsed`, so a LAN client could plant an A/AAAA at a foreign name holding only another type (AAAA/MX/TXT). Now uses name-level `NameNotUsed` (ANY/NONE); skip-existing keeps `errDDNSConflictRefused`, strict-fail keeps its hard error. The manager threads `SiblingFamilyOwned` (from its durable ownership scan, `crossTypeSiblingOwned`) so a legitimate dual-stack client's sibling-family publish keeps the per-type guard and A+AAAA both publish. Documented residual: a name already xpf-owned for one family plus a foreign RR of another type cannot be classified backend-side.

## Testing
- RED on origin/master: cross-type foreign (AAAA/MX/TXT) plants under skip-existing/strict-fail — all FAIL with err=nil/planted.
- GREEN: all #14604 regression tests pass; fresh name still publishes; same-type controls (`TestRFC2136SkipExistingConflictSkips`, `TestManagerSkipExistingConflictRecordsNoOwnership`) still pass; strengthened assert the prereq is NameNotUsed.
- `go test ./pkg/ddns -count=1` — PASS (17.5s)
- `go test ./pkg/dhcpserver -count=1` — PASS (2.5s)

Log: docs/log/14604.md

## PR #14769 — flowexport: resolve IPv4 route masks via OIF output lookup (#14610) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14610-campaign`

Why:
fibMatchMask set RTA_IIF with no RTA_SRC whenever the flow's ingress
ifindex was positive, which is always in production. The kernel IPv4
input path rejects a zero source as martian (EINVAL), so every IPv4
srcMask/dstMask lookup failed, was cached as (0,false), and exported
as an unresolved 0 indistinguishable from a real /0. The #2866
feature was dead for every IPv4 record; the unit tests faked the
lookup so nothing exercised the real netlink call.

What:
- pkg/flowexport/routemask.go: fibMatchMask now performs an output
  route lookup — vrfOifForIfindex maps the ingress ifindex to its
  l3mdev master (MasterIndex via LinkByIndex) and sets
  RouteGetOptions.OifIndex, which needs no source address and
  selects the enslaved interface's VRF table. A non-enslaved or
  unresolvable ifindex omits RTA_OIF and keeps the main-table
  lookup, bit-identical for default deployments. Seams
  routeMasterLinkByIndex/routeLookupWithOptions allow unit
  assertion of the query shape. False "bit-identical" comment fixed.
- pkg/flowexport/README.md: #3744 section documents the OIF output
  lookup and the #14610 EINVAL mechanism.
- pkg/flowexport/routemask_netns_14610_test.go: netns-gated
  real-netlink regression (IPv4 /24 both halves with positive
  ifindex, IPv6 /48 unchanged, VRF-enslaved member resolves to the
  VRF table's /16) plus a no-netns OIF query-shape pin.
- docs/log/14610.md: issue log.

NOT changed: MaskResolver signature, (ifindex,IP) cache key, async
background populate, miss counting, wire format.

Validation:
- Probe (private netns): the old IifIndex query returns invalid
  argument with no routes while production fibMatchMask(192.0.2.5,
  iif) returns (24,true).
- RED: new test cannot build on current master (seams absent); the
  old query shape is EINVAL for IPv4 in the same harness.
- GREEN: unshare -rn go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -run TestFibMatchMask
  -count=1 -v passes; go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -count=1 passes;
  go vet ./pkg/flowexport/, gofmt, git diff --check clean.

Risk:
One extra LinkByIndex call per background cache populate (bounded
by the 32-inflight cap and TTL cache); session-close hot path
unchanged. Torn-down interfaces fall back to the main table
instead of failing the lookup. No lab deployment run; kernel
behavior covered in-netns.

Closes #14610

## PR #14771 — ipsec: render dynamic hostname as responder IKE identity (#14590) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14590-campaign`

Closes #14590

## Problem
Junos `dynamic hostname <fqdn>` identifies a dynamic-IP peer by the IKE identity it presents (hub `dynamic hostname X` ↔ spoke `local-identity hostname X`). xpf rendered it as `remote_addrs = <fqdn>` — a DNS-resolved dial address — with no remote `id`, so migrated hub/spoke tunnels never came up when the peer name was not in DNS (the normal dynamic-peer case).

## Fix
- **Compiler** (`pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go`, both gateway paths): every `dynamic` block is responder-only; the FQDN is kept in `DynamicHostname` as the expected identity. Schema/struct docs updated (identity, not DNS-resolved). A DNS-dialed peer remains expressible via gateway `address <fqdn>`, unchanged.
- **Render** (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go`): `remote_addrs = %any`, `remote { id = "@<fqdn>" }` (explicit `remote-identity` still wins), PSK scoped by `id-1 = "@<fqdn>"`, no `start_action`; shared `responderOnlyGateway` helper also drives responder DPD (`ike.go`) and no eager re-initiation (`manager.go`), including directly-constructed configs where the compiled flag was not carried.
- **PrepareConfig** (`policy_addr.go`): family hint is pure — literal addresses classify directly, a dynamic identity is family-agnostic (IP literal still classifies) — so the bounded DNS resolver + worker pool are deleted; no DNS on the commit/apply path.

## Tests
- RED on master: config `ResponderOnly = false, want true` (flat/block/nested/set forms); ipsec `remote_addrs = "branch.example.net", want "%any"`, no remote id.
- New: `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_dynamic_identity_14590_test.go`, `pkg/ipsec/dynamic_hostname_identity_14590_test.go` (render, explicit-remote-id precedence, address-gateway control).
- Updated tests pinning the old DNS reading (DynamicHostname render, PrepareConfig family, #9641, #14140, #6469, #13540, parser test) and `pkg/ipsec/README.md` / `docs/config-schema.md`.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/ipsec -count=1`; focused `pkg/config` ipsec tests; `go vet` clean.
- Pre-existing: `TestValidateIPsecEndpoints_Accept` fails identically on pristine `origin/master` (#14139 PSK rejection) — verified in a base worktree, untouched here.

Live charon proof (`swanctl --list-conns` `id: @X`) is lab-bound; render/compile tests are the gate. Log: `docs/log/14590.md`.

Branch: `fix/14595-campaign`

Why:
ExtractPCIAddr/extractPCIAddr returned the last DDDD:BB:DD.F sysfs component with no bus check, so an x86 USB NIC behind an xHCI controller (`.../0000:00:14.0/usb2/2-1/2-1:1.0`) inherited the controller BDF `0000:00:14.0`. Only a sysfs device path whose last component is the BDF itself (or `virtioN` directly below its PCI function, a 1:1 channel linksetup already enumerates under that BDF) names a PCI device; any other tail yields `""`. Full pkg/daemon has one unrelated failure TestHostInboundTeardownClearsEnforcedThenFailedReinstallFences_5790 (host-inbound teardown, untouched by this change).

## PR #14774 — ddns: require TSIG-signed responses to signed UPDATEs (#14603) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14603-campaign`

Why:
A TSIG-signed RFC 2136 UPDATE accepted an unsigned response:
miekg/dns only verifies a reply MAC when the reply carries a TSIG
RR, so a forged unsigned NOERROR recorded phantom publishes and
deletes as settled, and a forged YX/NOTAUTH suppressed or
mis-skipped legitimate publishes — exactly in the deployments
that configured TSIG per the documented #4483 mitigation.

What:
`exchange()` now runs `validateTSIGResponse` on both the UDP leg
and the TCP truncation retry whenever a TSIG key is configured:
the reply must carry a TSIG RR matching the configured key name
and algorithm (canonical, case-insensitive), else it is a
transport error that never reaches the rcode verdict, records or
drops no ownership, and counts no conflict/PTR-skip. A truncated
TSIG exchange via a non-`*dns.Client` exchanger fails closed.
The fake DNS server in tests gains unsigned / wrong-key /
wrong-algorithm / wrong-secret / TCP-only forgery controls;
README, config-schema, and the commit-time warning comments
state the real mechanism. NOT changed: the no-TSIG warned
posture, DHCID guards, and the other DDNS backends.

Validation:
RED on base (production reverted, one unit test excluded to
compile): all 14 unsigned upsert/delete wire subtests and the
unsigned-TCP test failed with forged rcodes accepted as
verdicts; signed controls passed. GREEN: full
`go test ./pkg/ddns/ -count=1` passes, the TSIG selector passes,
pkg/config DDNS warning tests pass, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean.

Risk:
A TSIG-configured server that strips TSIG from responses now
fails closed with retries instead of accepting verdicts — the
intended posture; properly signing servers are unaffected.

Closes #14603

## PR #14775 — ddns: publish both families for dual-stack clients under replace-owned (#14602) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14602-campaign`

Why: under the default replace-owned policy a dual-stack DHCP client
never got both its A and AAAA. identity4 yields cid:/mac: identities
while identity6 yields duid:<duid>/<iaid>, and dhcidRR digests the raw
prefixed string, so the two families of one host always produce
different RFC 4701 DHCIDs. Whichever family published first owned the
name; the sibling's Attempt B (DHCID-matches-ours) could never match
and was refused every cycle (owned=1, err=nil), silently losing half
of each host's forward DNS. The #2700 fixture used one identical
identity for both families, a shape identity6 cannot produce.

What: sendAddOwned takes a sibling branch when the manager threads
SiblingFamilyOwned (upsertLocked's crossTypeSiblingOwned store scan,
merged for #14604): it adds this family's forward RR plus its own
per-family DHCID under a per-type RRsetNotUsed prerequisite, leaving
the sibling untouched. The store, not the wire digest, is the
cross-family ownership proof. Each family's delete already replays
its own identity, so teardown removes only its own A/AAAA+DHCID;
the identical-identity shared-DHCID keep-alive is unchanged. A name
with no owned sibling keeps every guard; a foreign same-type RRset
still fails the branch's RRsetNotUsed. Rewrites the #2700 fixture
with production-shaped identities (per-family DHCIDs) and updates
the README DHCID contract. NOT changed: skip-existing/strict-fail
(their sibling bypass already landed with #14604).

Validation: new TestDualStackProductionIdentitiesBothPublishReplaceOwned
fails pre-fix with "AAAA missing — v6 family lost the DHCID race"
(winner varies with map order) and passes after: A+AAAA present,
owned=2, SkippedConflict=0 across 2 cycles, concurrent foreign claim
refused with no ownership, full teardown orphan-free. Rewritten
TestPartialDualStackTeardownKeepsSharedDHCID passes. go test
./pkg/ddns -count=1 PASS, ./pkg/dhcpserver PASS, go vet clean;
#14604 cells still pass.

Risk: a name co-resident with a foreign RR of the sibling's type is
accepted once the manager owns the sibling (the store cannot
classify the foreign RR) — the same residual #14604 documented for
skip-existing. Per-family DHCIDs mean a name can carry two DHCID
RRs; RFC 4701 readers see both as ownership markers, and each is
removed by its own family's guarded delete.

Closes #14602

union), so stateless and PD-only DHCPv6 do not widen the keep.

CLAUDE.md, pkg/networkd/README.md and docs/log/14594.md record the

## PR #14777 — config: gate RA default-lifetime against max interval (#14605) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14605-campaign`

Why:
RFC 4861 §6.2.1 requires AdvDefaultLifetime to be 0 or within
[MaxRtrAdvInterval, 9000], defaulting to 3*MaxRtrAdvInterval.
`crossCheckRAIntervals` checked only `min <= 0.75*max` (#4525), so
`default-lifetime 10` with `max-advertisement-interval 600` committed
and hosts lost their default route (and inherited RDNSS/PREF64)
seconds after each RA. An unset lifetime stayed a fixed 1800s even at
max 1800 — one interval, no loss tolerance.

What:
- `crossCheckRAIntervals` (strict commit / commit-check / CheckText /
  #9619 peer pipeline) rejects an explicit positive `default-lifetime`
  below the effective max (configured max, or 600s when unset) or above
  9000, naming RFC 4861 §6.2.1; tolerant Load/SyncApply warns as before.
- New `RAInterfaceConfig` helpers (`EffectiveMaxAdvInterval`,
  `DefaultRouterLifetime` = min(3*max, 9000), `EffectiveRouterLifetime`)
  are the single derivation used by `buildRA`, Manager `Status()`, and
  `show`; inherited RDNSS/PREF64 floor at the derived default
  (RFC 8106 §5.1), so explicit-0 keeps DNS/NAT64 while declining
  default-router duty.
- NOT changed: the 0..65535 per-leaf wire bound, send-sink clamps, and
  explicit PREF64 RFC 8781 handling.

Validation:
- RED (sender.go + store.go swapped to HEAD, tests kept): new CheckText
  cells get nil for dl=10/max=600 and dl=9001; wire cells decode 1800s
  at max 1800 instead of 5400s.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/ra -count=1` ok; targeted configstore cells
  (#14605, #4525, #9619 peer pipeline, shipped HA configs) ok;
  `go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestSchema4119|TestSchema3895|TestCompile4119'`
  ok; `go vet` (ra/configstore/config/cli), gofmt, `git diff --check`
  clean. The full `./pkg/configstore` suite exceeded the 280s lane
  timeout under concurrent sibling lanes (unrelated contention);
  targeted RA/shipped-config cells pass — main agent should rerun the
  full configstore suite unloaded.

Risk:
Previously committable lifetimes in (0, max) or (9000, 65535] now fail
strict commit but still load tolerantly with a warning; their
RDNSS/PREF64 are floored at 3*max while the short Router Lifetime is
honored verbatim. Unset lifetimes with max > 600 now advertise 3*max
(the RFC default); `show`/Status report the derived value.

Closes #14605

## PR #14779 — dhcp: expire delegated prefixes on their own valid lifetime (#14598) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14598-campaign`

Why:
A DHCPv6 delegated prefix was retained and re-advertised on the IA_NA lease clock, not its own: DelegatedPrefixesForRA applied no per-prefix expiry, buildRAConfigs copied lifetimes verbatim, and a non-Success IA_PD on renew was treated as silence retaining the prior PD. LAN hosts kept SLAAC addresses from a prefix the ISP had reclaimed (RFC 8415 §6.3/§18.2.10.1, RFC 9096 L-15).

What:
- `pkg/dhcp`: `DelegatedPrefix.ExpiresAt/Expired/RemainingLifetimes`; prune expired PDs in `DelegatedPrefixes`/`DelegatedPrefixesForRA` (scheduling a recompile) and return decayed remaining lifetimes. T1/T2 waits wake at the earliest PD expiry, prune, and loop without abandoning a live IA_NA lease; PD-only lease deadline is the shortest delegated valid lifetime.
- A non-Success IA_PD (e.g. NoPrefixAvail) withdraws held PDs instead of being treated as silence; retained-but-expired prefixes are dropped in reconcile.
- `pkg/daemon`: `buildRAConfigs` advertises decayed remaining lifetimes.
- NOT changed: `pkg/ra` sender sentinel (owned by #14606); IA_NA LeaseTime is not shortened when IA_NA is present.

Validation:

## PR #14780 — telemetry: emit Junos sd-syslog RT_FLOW envelope (#14611) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14611-campaign`

Why:
sd-syslog wrapped the flat RT_FLOW body in a NILVALUE RFC 5424 header
(`xpf - - - RT_FLOW SESSION_OPEN src=...`), so SIEM parsers keyed on
`RT_FLOW_SESSION_*` MSGID and the `junos@2636` SD lost policy, zone
and NAT attribution. `structured` carried the SD only as RFC 3164 MSG
with a doubled `RT_FLOW -` lead-in.

What:
- `formatSDSyslogLine` (pkg/logging/format_rtflow.go): single RFC 5424
  builder shared by `SyslogClient.Send` and `LocalLogWriter.Send`.
  Session events: `<PRI>1 TS HOST RT_FLOW - RT_FLOW_SESSION_CREATE|CLOSE|DENY [junos@2636.1.1.1.2.129 source-address="..." ...]`
  (HOSTNAME present, no MSG after SD). Non-SD RT_FLOW bodies keep
  `RT_FLOW - - <flat>`; generic/non-RT_FLOW text keeps `xpf - - -`.
- Ringbuf fanout supplies the structured body to sd-syslog clients and
  local writers (previously the flat body).
- `structured` documented decision (docs/config-schema.md matrix):
  same Junos RT_FLOW body as MSG — RFC 3164 stream envelope / local
  timestamp+tag event prefix — with the redundant `RT_FLOW -` lead-in
  stripped.
- NOT changed: binary format, `formatStructuredMsg` output (pinned by
  #9321 goldens), generic system-syslog records.

Validation:
- New `pkg/logging/sd_syslog_14611_test.go`: RED on master
  (APP-NAME=`xpf`, doubled `RT_FLOW - RT_FLOW`) and RED on partial
  revert of the `SyslogClient.Send` line; GREEN after the fix.
  RFC 5424 parser asserts APP-NAME=RT_FLOW,
  MSGID=RT_FLOW_SESSION_CREATE, SD-ID `junos@2636.1.1.1.2.*`,
  `source-address` param, no MSG tail — for both the stream writer
  (raw frame → EventReader → UDP wire) and event-mode writer (file).
- `go test ./pkg/logging/ -count=1` passed; `go test ./pkg/config/
  -run 'TestLog|3349'` passed; gofmt/go vet clean.
- docs/log/14611.md records RED/GREEN.

Risk:
Intentional wire change for session events on sd-syslog/structured;
parsers pinned to the old NILVALUE envelope or doubled lead-in must
update. Generic sd-syslog text is byte-unchanged.

Closes #14611

## PR #14784 — cluster: chunk persistent-NAT lease batches below sync cap (#14607) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14607-campaign`

Why:
QueuePersistentNatLeaseBatch wrote the whole idle persistent-NAT lease
snapshot as one session-sync frame with no byte budget. Past roughly
215k-250k idle leases the frame exceeds the receiver's 16 MiB cap,
receiveLoop returns, and its deferred handleDisconnect tears down HA
session sync on every 30 s push, so the #8121 idle-lease rebuild never
converges. An export failure in the same daemon loop was logged only
at Debug, hiding the no-snapshot regime.

What:
- pkg/cluster: shared named maxSyncPayload constant used by the
  receive loop, the handshake reader (oversize now also counted), and
  the lease sender.
- encodePersistentNatLeaseBatchFrames splits one origin/generation
  batch into complete sub-cap batch payloads; records stay whole,
  oversize/unencodable records drop and count via
  MalformedRecordsDropped, and QueuePersistentNatLeaseBatch refuses
  any frame over the cap. Chunks are additive at the same generation:
  chunk one carries the clear barrier, the rest rebuild the set, and
  empty batches still emit exactly one barrier frame.
- pkg/daemon: export failures are counted
  (PersistentNatLeaseExportFailures) and logged at Warn rate-limited
  to once per minute, replacing the Debug-only log.
- NOT changed: Rust helper export, receiver import semantics, wire
  version, or message type 41.

Validation:
- New cluster cells pass for 262,144 remote-less leases, 1300x1024
  IPv6-remotes leases, and 300,000 leases: >1 frame each, every frame
  <= maxSyncPayload, and a receiver fed all frames in order delivers
  every lease under the same origin/generation. Encoder-bound and
  oversize-record cells pass; empty batch yields one barrier frame.
- Existing TestPersistentNatLease* and TestQueueStampsFullSetSeq pass.
- New daemon cell passes: first export failure Warns and counts, a
  second inside a minute counts without re-warning, a third after the
  interval Warns again.
- go vet ./pkg/cluster ./pkg/daemon clean. Full pkg/cluster suite has
  only TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752 failing, identical
  on the base commit (pre-existing, base-attributed).

Risk:
Mixed-version peers see ordinary type-41 additive chunks at one
generation and import the union; pre-#11486 peers ignore type 41 as
before. A single record over the frame budget drops counted instead
of disconnecting sync (unreachable for legal <=1024-remote leases).
The Rust helper export response is not paged; the capped transport
was the HA sync frame, now chunked.

Closes #14607

## PR #14785 — grpcapi/authz: non-root management-port holder no longer kills xpfd or impersonates it [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14581-management-port-holder`

Closes #14581

## Problem
#8233 made a persistent `EADDRINUSE` on `127.0.0.1:50051` fatal keyed only on the error, with no holder-UID check. Any non-root local process — an SSH remote forward (`ssh -R 127.0.0.1:50051:...`), a compromised service UID — holds the port as well as a second xpfd, so xpfd exited into a `Restart=on-failure` loop while the squatter impersonated the management server (including harvesting secrets in `set`/`load` RPCs).

## Fix (acceptance criteria from the issue)
1. **xpfd does not exit for a uid≠0 holder** — at the #8233 grace expiry the supervisor now attributes the LISTEN socket from `/proc/net/tcp{,6}` (`pkg/authz.LookupListenerOwner`: exact row wins, wildcard fallback, neighbour/ESTABLISHED rows are not the holder). Fatal (`ErrManagementPortHeld`) requires a **privileged** holder (uid 0 or xpfd's own uid — the duplicate-xpfd case, preserved). Non-root or unattributed holders stay supervised, alarm at ERROR on the grace cadence, and the daemon binds when the squatter leaves.
2. **cli/pkg/upgrade refuse a non-root server** — `pkg/authz.DialContext` (wired via `grpc.WithContextDialer` into `cmd/cli` dialOpts and `pkg/upgrade` grpcCluster) verifies at dial time, before any RPC byte is written, that a loopback server is privileged-owned, using the mirrored ESTABLISHED-row lookup. Non-loopback fabric targets are untouched (their #4107/#4122 chain owns them).
3. **sshd drop-in denies forwarding** — `DisableForwarding yes` in both the image factory drop-in (`scripts/image/bake.py`) and every daemon-managed drop-in (`buildSSHDConfig`).

## Tests
- New: injected-holder supervisor cells (non-root/root/own-uid/unattributed/lookup-failure), a **real-socket** non-root holder cell (uid-aware, skips where a root runner makes holder≡daemon indistinguishable) plus recovery-after-squatter-leaves, /proc fixture attribution matrix, client foreign-uid refusal, bake `sshd -T` forwarding assertion. Existing #8233 fatal test now injects a uid-0 holder (its premise is the duplicate-xpfd case).
- Mutations verified: always-fatal, Privileged=any-found, and client-accepts-foreign each fail the new cells.
- Suites: `pkg/authz`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/upgrade` pass; `cmd/cli` and `pkg/daemon` full runs hit pre-existing base failures (9-file gofmt backlog incl. `pkg/config`/`pkg/dataplane`, and a load-flaky credential test passing in isolation on both trees) — daemon SSH shards pass on head. `go vet` clean on all touched packages.
- Remaining validation per the issue: the VM check (`ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:50051:127.0.0.1:9` as a read-only login across `systemctl restart xpfd`) needs a live appliance; the forwarding denial now removes that actor on baked images.

test to first-occurrence semantics. NOT changed: the Rust dataplane

## PR #14789 — postrm: restore transit sysctls only on xpf-owned hosts (#14620) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14620-campaign`

Closes #14620

## Defect
`debian/xpf.postrm` `cleanup_transit_state` unconditionally wrote `1` to `ip_forward` and `ipv6/conf/all/forwarding` on `remove|purge` whenever `xpfd transit-barrier remove` exited 0 — which it does vacuously when no barrier ever existed (`RemoveTransitBarrier`: absent → nil). A foreign host that merely installed the package and never committed a config (xpf never wrote the sysctls there, per the #10733 contract) had forwarding silently flipped 0→1 on uninstall: an unfiltered IPv4/IPv6 router, plus loss of v6 RA acceptance.

## Fix
- **Daemon** (`pkg/daemon/daemon_transit_gate.go`): `recordTransitGateOwnership()` runs from every latch arm of `shouldManageTransitGate()`, before any gate sysctl write. It durably writes `/var/lib/xpf/transit-gate-owned` (`fsatomic.WriteFileDurable`) with the host's pre-xpf values (`ipv4=`/`ipv6=`), never overwriting an existing record so priors survive restarts/reinstalls. Best-effort: failure logs Warn, gate still actuates fail-closed.
- **postrm**: restores ONLY when the ownership record exists, restoring each recorded prior (new `restore_transit_sysctl` helper; values normalised 0|1, missing/corrupt → 1 so an owned host is never stranded transit-closed). No record → log + leave both sysctls untouched. `remove` leaves the record; `purge` consumes it after the restore (package-derived runtime state under `/var/lib/xpf`, not `/etc/xpf`).

## Regression
- `test/debian/postrm-test.sh`: decisive z6 cell `remove_never_owned_keeps_sysctls_closed` (no record, 0/0, stub barrier-remove succeeds → both stay 0) — **RED on the pre-fix postrm** (`FAIL: IPv4 forwarding opened on never-owned host (#14620)`), GREEN after; purge twin, owned/mixed/corrupt-record controls, purge-consumes-record; pre-existing owned cells seeded via `mark_transit_owned`. Barrier-failure cell still stays 0. Full suite passes under `sh` and `dash`.
- `pkg/daemon/transit_ownership_record_14620_test.go`: record-on-latch (priors captured, never overwritten) and no-record-on-never-owned.
- Note: the container test run wrote `/var/lib/xpf/transit-gate-owned` during the suite (same host-writing class as the pre-existing sysctl test seams; system file removed, follow-up cleanup harmless).

## Checks for main agent
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestTransitOwnership|TestForeignNeverCommitted|TestCommittedForeignHost|TestApplianceMarkerOwns|TestFirstCommitRollbackRetains' -count=1` (could not complete in this sandbox: host lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN, netlink socket fails; unrelated churn in transit test files also in flight)
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` (earlier run killed by sandbox, rerun)
- Full `./pkg/daemon/` and `./pkg/fsatomic/` suites on a privileged host.
- Residual: hosts owned by a pre-#14620 daemon have no record, so the new postrm leaves their sysctls at the shutdown-closed 0 (fail-closed) rather than restoring 1 — stated in `docs/log/14620.md`.

## PR #14790 — ipsec: require remote identity on responder-only PSK gateways (#14591) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14591-campaign`

## Summary

A responder-only (`dynamic`, `remote_addrs = %any`) PSK VPN whose gateway has no `remote-identity` rendered a `secrets{}` entry with **no `id` selector**. That secret matches any peer, and strongSwan selects keys by the claimed IDi — so a holder of *another* site's PSK could authenticate into this VPN by claiming that site's identity, landing on this VPN's st0/zone (Y09-04, residual of #3952).

## What changed

- **Render belt** (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go`): a responder-only PSK VPN whose gateway has no remote-identity is now **skipped by name** — the same fail-closed class as #14139's missing-secret skip. No connection, no orphan secret, and the rendered-set exclusion makes Apply unload it and tear down any stale SA. Pubkey (certificate) VPNs are unaffected.
- **Commit gate** (`pkg/config`): new `validateIPsecResponderIdentityStrict`, wired into `runUniformGatesIPsecEvent` with `lenientIPsecResponderIdentity`. Strict commit hard-rejects with a message naming the fix; tolerant load / HA peer-sync downgrades to a warning while the render belt keeps the unscoped connection from loading. The auth determination mirrors #14139's `ipsecVPNAuthNeedsPSK`, so cert VPNs are never rejected.
- With a remote-identity configured, the existing render already emits `remote { id = ... }` and scopes the secret to it (#3952); the new tests pin **both directions** of credential isolation (rw secret never claims the site identity, site secret never claims the rw identity).
- Migrated the pre-existing responder-only fixtures that encoded the vulnerable shape to carry a remote-identity; updated `pkg/ipsec/README.md` and `docs/config-schema.md`.

**NOT changed:** `dynamic hostname <fqdn>` rendering (#14590's separate mechanism) and no-ID secrets for non-responder shapes (fixed peers are scoped by gateway address).

## Validation

- **RED on base** (`c4848b1ae`): `TestResponderOnlyPSKScoping14591` rendered the unscoped rw connection + secret (`secret = "rw-secret"` with no `id-` selector); the config gate did not exist.
- **GREEN:** new `pkg/ipsec` + `pkg/config` tests pass; full `pkg/ipsec` suite passes; `go vet` clean.
- Full `pkg/config` suite shows only the pre-existing census-family failures (`TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` panic, ISIS #14400 cell) — outside this change's scope; Main should confirm base attribution on current master.

## Risk

A persisted responder-only PSK VPN without a remote-identity now loses that tunnel at render (warning names the fix) and is rejected at strict commit. Operators must configure `remote-identity` on the gateway — deliberate, fail-closed. See `docs/log/14591.md`.

Four duplicate unstaged #14588 files remain in `/var/worktrees/wt-14591` — discard them with the worktree; do not commit them here. The branch was **not** rebased (dirty worktree); HEAD is an ancestor of master, so the diff is clean — rebase at merge time as usual.

## PR #14791 — ra: advertise deprecated PD prefix with preferred lifetime 0 (#14606) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14606-campaign`

Why:
A DHCPv6-PD IAPREFIX with preferred lifetime 0 (deprecated, RFC 8415 §21.22) lost that value at two sentinel collisions: `buildRAConfigs` left it unset, and `pkg/ra` substituted the 7-day default for every `PreferredLife <= 0` then clamped to valid. LAN hosts therefore preferred the ISP's dying prefix for its whole valid life, inverting graceful renumbering (RFC 9096 L-15).

What:
Add `config.RAPrefix.PreferredLifeSet`, mirroring `DefaultLifetimeSet` (#4119). The compiler sets it when the `preferred-lifetime` leaf is present; `buildRAConfigs` stamps it on the PD path after the #14598 remaining-lifetime decay (inside the `ValidLifetime > 0` branch, preserving the no-clock sender-default sentinel), so a preferred lifetime decayed to 0 mid-life also advertises deprecated. `buildRA` honors an explicit preferred life including 0, while unset keeps the 7-day default. `configEqual` and `sortRAPrefixes` include the wire-affecting flag; the golden fixture gains `PreferredLifeSet: false` throughout. Helper wire bumped to protocol **v50** on both sides with manager gates rejecting old/missing scopes. Cluster binary encoding appends `EgressScope` after `RoutingScope`; wire fixture regenerated.

**Validation:**

## PR #14797 — config: model endpoint literal in load classifier and parse adjudicated text in store (#14572) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14572-campaign`

## Summary

#14572 (Y01-01, residual of #14145): a token-initial bracketed endpoint
literal hid denied config from the restricted-class `load` gate while
the store applied it. `ClassifyLoadContent` treated a token-initial
`[` as list sugar and left the scanner at a token boundary, so a
following block/line comment opener blanked every later statement in
the gate's view. The real lexer instead lexes
`[`+identrun+`]:`+identrun as ONE identifier (#5182), so no comment
opens, and the store's hierarchical branches re-parsed the raw body
and applied the hidden `root-authentication` / security-policy
subtrees. A regex-restricted operator (with one allowed free-text
leaf) could write any config path over CLI, REST and gRPC.

## Fix (both halves of "parse once")

- `pkg/config/authz_config_load_9892.go`: the classifier now models
  `tryBracketedEndpointLiteral` via the new
  `bracketedEndpointLiteralEnd` (same shape, reusing the lexer's own
  `isIdentChar`), also immediately after a boundary `]` where the
  real lexer's gap loop retries the literal. A matched literal is
  token text; non-literal brackets keep the #14145 list-sugar
  behaviour, so genuine comments after `[ /* ... */` still hide prose.
- `pkg/configstore/store_command.go`: `LoadMergeAsPlantClass` and
  `parseOverrideContent` now parse the classifier's uncommented text
  instead of the raw body, so the store applies exactly the
  representation the gate adjudicated, by construction.

Not changed: `SyncApply`/on-disk parsers (not gate-adjudicated), the
real lexer, flat routing.

## Tests

- `pkg/config/authz_config_load_14572_test.go`: the issue's decisive
  probe plus the line-comment spelling, both carried on an allowed
  `description` leaf, with bare-denied/allowed premise controls; a
  renderer test proving the denied leaves reach adjudication (no
  refuse-everything pass); narrowness controls (genuine endpoint
  literal loads, genuine comments still hide prose).
- `pkg/configstore/loadmerge_endpoint_literal_14572_test.go`: the
  acceptance property `set(store-applied) ⊆ set(LoadMutationLines(body))`
  over bracket/comment placements (token-initial, mid-token,
  stray-`]`, quoted, genuine comment/list controls) against the
  hierarchical merge branch, plus the same property for override.
- `docs/log/14572.md` records defect, fix and RED/GREEN.

RED on `a615690ed` (tests only): all four bypass bodies ALLOWED for
class `limited`; store applied the denied leaf unadjudicated.
GREEN with fix: focused `14572|14145|9892|10305|10734` runs pass in
both packages; `go vet` clean; full `pkg/configstore` suite passes

*(truncated — 57 lines total)*

## PR #14798 — config: require dh-group on referenced IKE proposals (#14588) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14588-campaign`

## Summary

An IKE proposal with **no `dh-group`** passed strict commit but rendered `proposals = aes256-sha256` — a proposal with no key-exchange method — which strongSwan 6.1.0 refuses (`invalid value for: proposals, config discarded, loaded 0 of 1`), discarding every connection in the file. Finding **Y09-01**, the #7165 commit⇒loadable breach. The DH value gate only sees present-but-bad values; an absent `dh-group` (`DHGroup 0`, no `InvalidSpec`) was invisible to it.

## Fix

- **`pkg/config`** — new `validateIPsecIkeDHGroupsPresentStrict` walks VPN → gateway → ike-policy → ike-proposal (plus the legacy direct-proposal fallback where the ike-policy value names an IPsec proposal) and rejects a DH-less IKE proposal referenced by a rendered VPN at strict commit, naming `dh-group`. It is placed **below** the IKE chain gate so dangling-chain diagnostics still win, and wired through new `lenientIKEProposalMissingDH` so tolerant load / peer-sync warn instead of bricking (#1960).
- **`pkg/ipsec`** — `ikeDHGroupMissing` filters DH-less proposals in `resolveIKESettings` (chain and legacy forms) through the existing `errDHGroupUnresolved` skip sentinel: a lenient-loaded copy skips only the affected VPN and other VPNs load.
- **Out of scope by design**: ESP proposals with no `dh-group` remain valid no-PFS suites (Junos `basic` ESP set); orphan IKE proposals no VPN renders still commit; no default DH group is invented.

## Validation

RED/GREEN (decisive cells from the issue):

- **RED on pristine `d08fbcf95`** (prod reverted, tests kept): `TestStrictRejectsIKEProposalNoDHGroup14588` fails (strict commit accepted the DH-less fixture), `TestTolerantWarnsIKEProposalNoDHGroup14588` fails (no dh-group warning), `TestRenderSkipsIKEProposalNoDHGroup14588` / `TestResolveIKESettingsNoDHGroupSentinel14588` / `TestResolveIKESettingsLegacyNoDHGroup14588` fail (DH-less VPN renders). The issue's controls (`group14` loads, `group99` rejected) pass on base.
- **GREEN after fix**: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 14588 -count=1` PASS; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 14588 -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/ipsec/` clean.
- **Controls preserved**: `dh-group group14` / `14` / `group19` / `2` / `group32` compile clean on strict and lenient paths with no dh-group warning; `dh-group group99` still rejected naming `99`; orphan DH-less proposal, no-PFS ESP proposal, and `proposal-set standard` fixtures still commit; `TestIKEPolicyProposalsDanglingSecondRejected` still names the dangling reference (gate ordering preserved).
- **Full suites**: `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1` PASS. `go test ./pkg/config/ -count=1` panics in the `TestCompactBlock*`/`TestCompactDepth1*` census (`validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST` → `nodeVal` at `compiler_applications.go:1340`) **identically on pristine HEAD** (verified in a throwaway base worktree at `d08fbcf95`); excluding the panic family, the HEAD-vs-base failure sets are **identical (28 pre-existing failures, all `#14139` PSK-presence or older gates hitting pre-existing fixtures)** — no new failures.
- `gofmt` clean on touched files (`pkg/config/compiler_opts.go`'s struct literal is not gofmt-clean on base; added lines match surrounding style).

## Risk

Strict commit now refuses a previously-accepted shape (an IKE proposal used by a VPN without `dh-group`); the operator fix is one line (`dh-group group<N>`). Already-persisted or peer-synced copies still boot with a warning, and the affected VPN is skipped rather than taking every tunnel down with charon's whole-file refusal. Orphan proposals and no-PFS ESP proposals are untouched.

Closes #14588

## PR #14799 — userspace-dp: never complete a TCP handshake on a closing entry (#14630) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14630-campaign`

Closes #14630

## Defect (Y25-01)
SYN → SYN-ACK → RST → bare ACK: `stamp_tcp_close` left `handshake_pending` set and `handshake_completed` consulted only packet flags, so the bare ACK completed the handshake and `propagate_tcp_state_to_companion` re-armed the reverse companion onto the 300 s established window. Forward reaped at RST+2 s; reverse survived as an uncounted orphan row admitting server→client hits for up to 5 min.

## Fix
Gate `promote_from_reverse` / `promote_from_asymmetric_ack` / `handshake_completed` on `!entry.closing` in `lookup.rs`, mirror in the `update_session` HA twin (+ its #1752 reference parity mirror), and refuse to promote/complete a closing companion in `propagate_tcp_state_to_companion`.

## Tests
New `rst_ack_handshake_14630_tests.rs`: decisive RST+ACK sequence (both halves stay on `TCP_RST_TIMEOUT_NS`, `expired==2` at RST+3 s, no orphan, count back to 0), SYN-ACK-first reverse-ACK variant, `update_session` twin, FIN variant, and a no-close control.
- RED on base: 4 failed, control passed.
- GREEN: 5 passed; full `session::` suite 450 passed (incl. #10885/#7342/#13676-78).

See `docs/log/14630.md`.

excluded traffic reached collectors.

  on the unit (clean cutover, no aliases); inet compiler arm writes V4,

## PR #14809 — userspace-dp: recycle deterministic ports on release (#14625) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14625-campaign`

Why:
Removing `port deterministic` reuses the same PortAllocator for round-robin PAT because `SourceNatPoolAllocatorKey` excludes mode. Deterministic frees used `free_no_recycle`, clearing the bit with no recycle token; PAT `claim()` reaches free ports only via its fresh cursor or the recycle FIFO, so once the cursor passed a freed deterministic offset the port was stranded — clear bit, reported free, yet `AllocatorExhausted` — until the pool key changed. The HA-synced release path had the identical hole.

What:
- `free_translated_port` loses its `recycle: bool` and always calls `free_recycle`; all callers (live unlink, lease teardowns, deterministic v4/v6 give-backs, GC reclaim, idle-import rollback) and the `freed` vectors updated. `claim_in_block` ignores the ring and the ring holds at most one token per offset (#7174), so recycling is harmless while deterministic and required after a flip.
- The `deterministic` flag stays for BIB/lease identity; stale no-recycle comments updated across `allocator.rs`, `source/{nat64_ports,synced,overlap}.rs`, `nat64.rs`.
- New `tests_det_flip_14625` decisive cell + PAT control; #9130/#14091/#5178 cells that asserted the defective no-recycle contract updated and renamed.
- NOT changed: allocator key (mode-in-key rejected — a fresh allocator would strand live deterministic releases), claim paths, cursor, Go owner-key contract. Full record: `docs/log/14625.md`.

Validation:
- RED on base `d19cc0368` (test + registration only): flip cell failed `Err(AllocatorExhausted)` vs `Ok(20000)`; PAT control passed.
- GREEN targeted (`14625 9130 5178 14091`): all pass.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp nat::`: 654 passed, 3 failed — `tests_idle_lease_sync_8121` (`..._11496`, `..._11475`, `..._13692`), reproduced identically on unmodified base, pre-existing and unrelated.

Risk:
A still-deterministic pool now accumulates at most `range` recycle tokens per address (bounded by the #7174 dedup bitset); PAT pops go through the normal claim CAS, so no duplicate identity is possible.

Closes #14625

## PR #14811 — config: reject packed tcp-mss tails at commit (#14576) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14576-campaign`

Why:
  `security flow tcp-mss <kind>` read only the selected MSS token;
  a second kind or trailing tokens packed into the same kind node
  (`gre-out mss 1300 all-tcp mss 1350`, `all-tcp mss 1350 bogus 7`,
  `all-tcp 1350 9999`) committed clean and were silently dropped —
  the configured clamp (notably `all-tcp`, the PMTU safeguard) never
  applied while `show configuration` still displayed it. Junos
  rejects these spellings; #8939 requires every leaf to compile or
  the command to fail. (Y03-01)

What:
  - `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`: `selectMSSValueEnd` mirrors
    `selectMSSToken` branch-for-branch (including the #1979
    mixed-shape precedence and #8824/#8838 branches);
    `mssLeftoverTokens` accounts for every token past the consumed
    value grammar across packed hierarchical nodes, braced `mss`
    children, flat-set value-carrier children, unparseable-child
    fallbacks, and never-read sibling children. Deliberately
    discarded #1979 tokens are not leftover, so mixed shapes keep
    compiling to the flat value.
  - `pkg/config/compiler_security_flow.go`: `checkTCPMSSKindTail`
    rejects leftovers on the strict path and warns on the lenient
    (boot/peer-sync) path, wired into `checkTCPMSSKind` before the
    range gate and into the `ipsec-vpn` branch before its rejection
    so a tail cannot hide behind it.
  - NOT changed: selection semantics, `compileFlow`, schema
    opacity, dataplane/wire/show behavior. No synthetic multi-kind
    splitting — Junos has no such statement.

Validation:
  - New `TestTCPMSSPackedTail{Rejected,Controls,Lenient}14576`
    (pkg/config, 14 defect rows + controls incl. two-set-line,
    braced, #1979 mixed, empty-body, prior typo/range refusals) and
    `TestCheckTextTCPMSSPackedTail14576` (pkg/configstore, the
    issue's decisive strict-CheckText instrument).
  - RED on pristine master `a615690ed`: every defect row accepted,
    lenient rows warn-free. GREEN after fix; all existing
    `TestTCPMSS*`/`TestCompactLeafTCPMSS*` and the full
    `TestCheckText*` set pass; `go vet` + `gofmt` clean.
  - Full `go test ./pkg/config/` panics in the compact-census
    family and times out in the spelling differential on pristine
    master too (verified in a detached base worktree), and
    `TestGroupRouteFilterORBesideInline14416` fails identically

    `docs/log/14576.md`.

  A legacy persisted/peer config carrying a packed tail now

## PR #14814 — userspace-dp: dedupe NAT64 pool members on first occurrence (#14624) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14624-campaign`

Why: On a tolerated load (legacy, mixed-version, or leniently loaded
config) the same NAT64 pool address can arrive twice, once bare and
once with the /32 host mask Go range-expansion stamps. Both NAT64
pool loops pushed every `parse_pool_v4` result with no seen-set, so
each duplicate got an independent occupancy bitmap and round-robin
placement minted the same (address, port) BIB for two IPv6
subscribers — reply traffic crosses subscribers (RFC 6146 §3.5).
The Go strict message and the overlap.rs #10700 note both claim
first-occurrence dedupe on tolerated loads; #10700 fixed only the
SNAT parser, so both claims were false for NAT64.

What: Add a first-occurrence `FxHashSet` seen-set to both NAT64 pool
loops in `nat64.rs` — the `from_snapshots_with_previous` build loop
and `nat64_rule_identity` — preserving first-seen order so the reuse
key, the #6982 aggregate charge, `PortAllocator` sizing, and
`build_deterministic_v6` host_count all see the identical deduped
pool. Add `nat64_14624` regression tests (unique tuples across 16
subscribers, identity == built pool, deterministic arm over a
duplicated list) and make the #6227 host-count-overflow fixture use
distinct addresses, since repeated copies now correctly dedupe.
NOT changed: `overlap.rs` or the Go strict message — the fix makes
both claims true rather than editing them.

Validation: `cargo test --bins nat64_14624` RED on base (pool_v4
`[203.0.113.1, 203.0.113.1]`, both tests failed) and GREEN after
the fix (2 passed). `cargo test --bins nat64::`: 218 passed.
`cargo test --bins nat::`: 652 passed, 3 failed in
`tests_idle_lease_sync_8121`, base-attributed at origin/master
8316f83a7 (identical failures on pristine base). Full crate suite
not run in-lane.

Risk: A pool now has fewer allocator slots when it carried true
duplicates; tuples stay unique so capacity accounting is more
honest, not smaller for any valid config. Deterministic pools
sized from duplicated lists report the deduped host_count;
subscribers only addressable via the phantom duplicate position
now fail closed, which is the intended BIB-uniqueness behavior.

Closes #14624

## PR #14815 — userspace-dp: make synthetic best-effort residual beside real queues (#14637) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14637-campaign`

Why: The #11428 synthetic best-effort queue was created with
guarantee_enabled=true at the full shaping rate even beside real
scheduler-map queues. The guarantee selector runs before strict-priority
surplus, so backlogged unclassified traffic could starve rate-less
priority classes, and the synthetic queue displaced an operator's
renamed queue-0 class (e.g. exact-capped be) as the default queue,
bypassing its cap for unclassified traffic.

(guarantee_enabled: false, shaping rate kept for burst/surplus) when
real queues exist; the no-real-queue case keeps the documented sole
root-shaped guarantee. Default selection among equally-low queues now
prefers queue 0, then literal best-effort, then lowest queue id.

best-effort queues, exact queues, or the priority-first ordering.

10000000), W2 default was synthetic id 1 not queue 0, queue-0 tiebreak
failed (1 != 0). GREEN: 4/4 14637 tests pass including the drain cell

Any one-peer WireGuard edit rebuilt the whole tunnel engine

surviving peer's adopted `live_endpoint` (#13664), reverting
roamed/NATed peers to their stale configured endpoint — or `None`

  identity-change rebuild only when that peer's configured endpoint
  is unchanged; an edited configured endpoint wins over the stale
  live value.

  high-water seeds. `peer_for_dest` and the control-thread
  `peer_endpoints()` re-seed both follow the roam with no
  `wg_control` change. `Peer::live_endpoint` doc corrected.
- NOT changed: session migration (documented drop, S5), the
  identity-unchanged Arc-reuse path, removed/re-keyed peers

A subnet without /len, a range outside the subnet or inverted, or a wrong-family router/dns-server committed clean, then Kea refused the whole rendered file and every pool of that family stopped, healthy pools included — the #9785 outage reached through four more leaves.

What: validateDHCPPoolValuesStrict (pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_dhcp_pool_14601.go) checks each pool, naming server/group/pool/leaf: subnet parses as a prefix of the server family (a bare address is Kea's no-/len refusal); each address-range bound parses, matches the family, lies inside the masked subnet, and low <= high; a v4 router is a valid IPv4 address (the v6 renderer emits no router option, so that leaf stays ungated); every dns-server element parses and matches the family. Wired in runUniformGatesDHCPApp after the #9785 duplicate-subnet gate, with lenientDHCPPoolValues downgrading to a warning on tolerant load/peer-sync so persisted configs still boot (#1960). The #6696 cells that encoded the old mixed-family contract are aligned (test-only, no assertion dropped). NOT changed: the Kea renderer — a mistyped value has no safe kept-pool arbitration, so commit is the gate.

Validation: regression cells fail on origin/master with only the test files present (every refusal case compiles clean; the four controls pass) and pass with the fix — pkg/config TestDHCPPoolValuesRefusedAtCommit14601 (23 cases) + TestDHCPPoolValuesLenientGate14601, pkg/configstore TestCheckTextRefusesBadDHCPPoolValues14601 through CheckText (the Store.Commit composition). Focused config/configstore/dhcpserver runs green; go vet clean. Full pkg/config carries 72 base-attributed failures at this master (sibling gates merged in parallel; verified identical on a clean master worktree); pkg/configstore full suite exceeds the 600s timeout on base and fix alike. No Kea binary in the test environment, so the optional kea-dhcp4 -t render check was not exercised — noted in docs/log/14601.md.

Risk: a persisted or peer-synced config carrying a bad pool value still boots on the tolerant path and reaches Kea exactly as before this gate; only new commits are refused. Residual: domain-name remains ungated (issue dropped its Kea-refusal claim as unverified).

Closes #14601

## PR #14820 — cluster: carry deterministic identity on idle-lease sync (#14638) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14638-campaign`

Why:
The cluster idle-lease codec wrote only the 14 non-deterministic
IdleLeaseWire fields, so every idle deterministic NAPT64 BIB exported
with deterministic=true and a V6 identity was stripped in transit and
refused by the peer import gate as identity-busy. The HA guarantee of
the #14242 deterministic BIB feature was silently void on failover,
and the counter pointed operators at identity contention instead.

What:
Add syncMsgPersistentNatLeaseDeterministic (43), whose record layout
appends the seven Deterministic* fields after TimeoutNs; the legacy
type 41 layout is byte-identical. Layout-aware encode/decode helpers
select the deterministic layout iff a batch contains a deterministic
lease, QueuePersistentNatLeaseBatch stamps the matching type on every
chunk frame, and types 41/43 share the generation/sequence handler.
The legacy encoder refuses a deterministic lease instead of stripping
it; the deterministic decoder validates the identity (mode/family,
non-zero parameters) and still demands exact consumption. The Rust
generic source-NAT import now refuses a deterministic-shaped lease as
identity-busy rather than installing it as dynamic. NOT changed:
SessionSyncWireVersion/CurrentHAProtocolVersion (additive type; an old
peer ignores it), the control-socket JSON wire, chunking, or replay
semantics.

Validation:
RED on base: the new reflection round-trip test failed with all seven
fields zeroed (Deterministic=false want true, Mode 0 want 2, HostBase
"" want 2001:db8::). GREEN: go test ./pkg/cluster -run
TestPersistentNatLease|TestLiveSyncMessageCensus|TestPeerCapabilities|TestLeaseCount
-count=1 passes at the final head; go vet clean. Full pkg/cluster
shows only TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752 failing,
identical on unmodified base (base-attributed). Rust: the new
generic-refusal cell and the #14091 BIB cell passed (2/2) and
idle_lease ran 74 passed with the same 3 failures as base; at the
final rebased head the Rust test binary does not compile due to two
stale call sites current master itself carries
(policy_revalidation.rs:461, tests_det_flip_14625.rs:44, E0061) in
files this branch does not touch.

Risk:
Mixed-version pairs lose only deterministic idle leases (type 43 is
ignored by old peers) until both sides upgrade; dynamic leases keep
type 41 in both directions and are never mis-installed. A mixed batch
rides type 43 whole, with dynamic records carrying a validated
all-zero deterministic tail.

Closes #14638

## PR #14821 — userspace-dp: suppress TE and PTB for tunnel-decapped inners (#14642) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14642-campaign`

## Summary
GRE/WireGuard decap fabricates a zero-MAC Ethernet header for the inner
packet (`TUNNEL_DECAP_INGRESS_FLAG`). #12864 gated only `reject`
against reflecting that fake L2; the Time Exceeded and Packet-Too-Big
builders reflected it anyway, queueing an unencapsulated ICMP error on
the underlay with destination MAC `00:00:00:00:00:00` — flooded as
unknown unicast, leaking cleartext inner header bytes, breaking
traceroute/PMTUD across the tunnel.

## Fix (#12864 parity — suppress)
- `icmp.rs`: `can_generate_icmp_error_reply` refuses tunnel-decapped
  inners; `build_local_icmp_error_v4/v6` return `None` on the flag as
  defense in depth (covers TE wrappers and reject builders).
- `icmp_ptb.rs`: `ptb_reply_suppressed` returns true on the flag (the
  dispatch caller still drops the oversize original via
  `mtu_signalled`); `build_frag_needed_v4` / `build_packet_too_big_v6`
  return `None` on the flag.
- Both GRE (`gre.rs`) and WG (`wg/decap.rs`, uncovered-forward
  injector) set the same flag, so both legs in the issue are covered.

NOT changed: session-miss install handling for suppressed TE
(Y32-02, owned by #14643 in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` — companion PR).

## Validation
- RED on `origin/master` ee661259a (tests only): all three new tests
  fail on the gate assertions.
- GREEN after fix: `time_exceeded_suppressed_for_tunnel_decap_inner_14642`,
  `time_exceeded_v6_suppressed_for_tunnel_decap_inner_14642`,
  `ptb_suppressed_for_tunnel_decap_inner_14642` pass, each with native
  positive controls.
- Adjacent icmp/ptb/reject filter run: 907 passed, 2 failed
  (`tests_policy_revocation_8356` #10507 pair, reproduced identically
  on unmodified base — base-attributed).
- Landing note: current `origin/master` (ffcb0bd38) does not compile
  even without this change (`policy_revalidation.rs:461`
  `persistent_inbound_lookup` arity, from #14793); branch is kept on
  the last verified base. Diff touches only `icmp.rs`/`icmp_ptb.rs`
  + tests, no overlap with the broken call site — rebase at landing
  once master compiles.

Docs: `docs/log/14642.md`.

Closes #14642
