## PR #14823 — firewall: align sub-byte flexible-match-range to window MSB (#14634) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14634-campaign`

Why:
A sub-byte flexible-match-range field starts at the byte-offset (bit-offset 0, MSB-first per Junos), so `bit-length 4` at `byte-offset 0` is the HIGH nibble of the first byte. Every boundary right-aligned the field pair into the ceil-byte window instead: the compiler defaulted the mask to the low bits, the userspace snapshot builder passed the pair verbatim, and both lo0 nft renderers did the same. On wire byte `0x45` a `bit-length 4 range 0x4` term compared the IHL nibble (5) instead of the version nibble (4), with a clean commit: a discard term failed open and its counter reflected the wrong field. An explicit Junos `match-mask 0xf` produced the identical wrong snapshot.

What:
Left-shift the field value/mask by (windowBits - bitLength) at each matcher boundary so the pair occupies the TOP bits of the window: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go` (`buildFilterTermSnapshots`), `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go` (`nftFlexMatchExpr`), and `pkg/nftables/netlink_build.go` (`flexMatchExprs`). The compiler's stored `FlexMatchConfig` pair stays field-aligned (comment only in `compiler_firewall.go`); byte-aligned lengths shift by 0 and stay byte-identical, BitLength 0 keeps the 32-bit default, and the #3406 uncapped oversized-width behaviour is preserved. The Rust matcher is unchanged (it already compares the full window); its stale 12-bit fixture now uses the aligned pair. NOT changed: `bit-offset` support (no such schema leaf; strict-rejected via #14347) and the retired eBPF compiler.

Validation:
RED pre-fix (re-captured by reverting the three production files with tests in place): `TestFilterSnapshotFlexMatchSubByteMSBAligned14634` wire {Value:0x4 Mask:0xf} want {0x40/0xf0}; `TestFlexMatchExprsSubByteMSBAligned14634` mask 0f want f0; `TestNftFlexMatchExprSubByteMSBAligned14634` renders `@nh,0,8 & 0xf == 0x4` want `@nh,0,8 & 0xf0 == 0x40`. GREEN: those tests plus `TestFlexibleMatchRangeSubByteCompilesFieldAligned14634` (config), `TestNftRuleSubByteFlexRendersAligned14634` (daemon), and Rust `flex_match_subbyte_4bit_reads_high_nibble_14634` (0x45 discards, 0x54 accepts); cargo `flex_match` 13 passed. Suites: pkg/config flex PASS, pkg/nftables full PASS, pkg/daemon flex PASS, pkg/dataplane/userspace snapshot-flex PASS; full userspace suite has one failure (`TestPartialRepublishRefusesQuarantineOnlySkew12247`) reproduced identically on clean origin/master `ffcb0bd38` (base-attributed). go vet clean on all touched packages.

Risk:
Byte-aligned and 32-bit terms are byte-identical on every wire. Sub-byte terms change enforcement to the authored field (the fix); an operator who had compensated with a pre-shifted mask (0xf0 for a 4-bit field) will now double-shift — that spelling was never valid Junos and is called out in `docs/log/14634.md`. No new allocation on any hot path (compile/render time only).

Closes #14634

## PR #14825 — userspace-dp: make is-fragment match trailing fragments only (#14631) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14631-campaign`

Closes #14631

Junos SRX defines `is-fragment` as `fragment-offset 0 except` (trailing fragments only), but the userspace firewall-filter term bit used the any-fragment predicate: an IPv4 first fragment (MF=1, offset 0) carrying TCP/22 matched `frags { from is-fragment; then accept; }` and bypassed following port terms at the stateless layer.

## Fix
- `term_match_extra_from_frame` (the single builder behind every filter/CoS evaluation path) now derives `TermMatchExtra::is_fragment` from the new `is_term_fragment` predicate = `is_non_first_fragment` (fragment offset != 0, both families).
- First/atomic fragments now carry `is_fragment: false` with `l4_present: true`, so they face port/tcp-flags terms; trailing fragments still match `is-fragment`.
- Internal any-fragment consumers (TCP segmentation, NAT64, embedded-ICMP, checksum guards) keep `is_any_fragment` unchanged. The BPF/XDP filter path (`ip frag-off & 0x1fff != 0`) and lo0 nft mirrors were already trailing-only / refused (v4, #13955), so no change there.
- Docs/comments corrected: filter README, feature-gaps, Rust+Go snapshot field comments, and two stale test assertions that pinned any-fragment term behaviour.

## Evidence
- RED on base: `is_fragment_term_14631_first_fragment_faces_port_term_trailing_matches` failed `left: Accept, right: Discard` for MF=1/offset-0 TCP/22 through `frags{is-fragment accept}; no-ssh{tcp 22 discard}`.
- GREEN after fix: same test passes (plain + first-fragment TCP/22 → Discard; trailing v4/v6 → Accept; v6 first → Discard), plus corrected builder/parity tests. Broader `filter::`/`fragment` run: 721 passed; the only 2 failures (`local_origin_tunnel_ipv6_nonfirst_fragment_transmits_without_session_14119`, `stage11_local_ike_passthrough_honors_ingress_input_filter_13637`) reproduce identically on pristine base and are unrelated.
- Log: `docs/log/14631.md`.

Not rebased onto latest origin/master: current master test cfg reportedly does not compile (unrelated `persistent_inbound_lookup` arity break from #14793, per lane note); this branch is based on 9f838a5f7 which compiles and was verified there.

predicate; fragmented native-GRE packets skip the session/local/
interface-NAT/degraded kernel passes and fall through to XSK. Helper:
new gre_reassembly module (64 datagrams, 64 KiB, 32 fragments, 10 s,
counted drops), wired into stage_native_gre_decap with a
GreDecapStage::Buffered disposition. Counter surfaced Rust->Go->
Prometheus as gre_outer_frag_drops_total /
xpf_userspace_gre_outer_frag_drops_total.

reassemble to exactly one byte-identical decapped inner (whole-decap
controls pass; head alone does not decap), shim truth table asserts a

persistent_inbound_lookup arity); with that site temporarily patched,

Incomplete fragments buffer per worker within stated bounds and drop

## PR #14830 — userspace-dp: aggregate WG admission keys on IPv6 /64 and evict LRU at cap (#14639) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14639-campaign`

Why:
Under load, `source_handshake_allowed` keyed the 2048-entry handshake
table on the full IPv6 /128 and refused a new source at the cap, while
GC reclaimed only entries idle for a full second. One host owning a
SLAAC /64 could refresh 2048 /128s inside that window and keep the
table permanently full, so every legitimate peer in another /64 failed
admission, lost rekey, and saw sessions die at REJECT_AFTER_TIME. The
reply table had the same full-address keying. Both diverge from the
Linux reference ratelimiter, which keys IPv6 on /64.

What:
`wg/cookie.rs`: add `source_bucket_key` (IPv6 → /64, v4-mapped v6 →
canonical v4, IPv4 → /32) applied in both `source_reply_allowed` and
`source_handshake_allowed`; add `evict_lru_if_full` so a new key at
the cap evicts the least-recently-refilled bucket instead of failing
closed (table memory stays bounded at 2048 keys). Cookie MAC binding
on the full IP+port is unchanged. Update the #9908 pinning test and
add three #14639 cells (cross-/64 lockout, per-/64 shared burst,
v4-mapped sharing). Log: `docs/log/14639.md`.

Validation:
RED on base `042b46dd27`: the three new cells fail pre-fix (legit peer
locked out; /64 granted 10 admissions instead of the 5-burst;
v4-mapped form granted a fresh burst). GREEN: `cargo test --bin
xpf-userspace-dp -- afxdp::wg::cookie` 25 passed, 0 failed; the three
`handshake_admission_9908` engine cells pass; full `afxdp::wg::`
suite 292 passed with 2 pre-existing `gre_tun_origin_10038` failures
reproduced identically on pristine base.

Risk:
Hosts inside one /64 now share one budget (reference trade-off);
eviction churn from a multi-/64 flood recreates fresh buckets on the
next initiation, so admission is never permanently denied.

Closes #14639

## PR #14834 — audit: sanitize local log and honor severity sentinels (#14732) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14732-campaign`

Why:
Event-mode LocalLogWriter.Send wrote msg raw to the audit file, so a LF forged an extra audit line and ESC/CSI stored verbatim fired on later cat/tail, unlike SyslogClient.Send (#6585). Its ShouldSendEvent arithmetic dropped every emergency under MinSeverity=SeverityEmergency (-1), and ForwardLogMsg called lw.Send unconditionally, bypassing SeverityNone/emergency-only on the aggregation/NAT-pool/clock-skew path.

## PR #14838 — dataplane: gate proto-255 out of USERSPACE_SESSIONS steering map (#14648) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14648-campaign`

Closes #14648

## Mechanism
Protocol 255 is `PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`/`SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, the sentinel the XDP shim substitutes for every non-first/short fragment (ports 0/0, both families). The steering publish (`write_steering_row`/`publish_session_rows`/`publish_session_map_key`) had no protocol gate and `uses_kernel_local_session_map_entry` checked domain/discriminator/origin/disposition but not protocol; the #6923 guard sits only on the `sessions_v6` conntrack mirror, a different map from the shim-probed `userspace_sessions`. A peer-synced proto-255 LocalDelivery record passed both sync refusals (not TCP/UDP, not a traversable v6 ext header) and wrote a PASS_TO_KERNEL row the shim hits for every protocol's fragments; a live wire proto-255 session wrote the same sentinel row.

## Fix
- `steering_key_is_publishable` (false exactly for 255) required by `uses_kernel_local_session_map_entry`, enforced by filtering `publish_session_rows` and refusing `publish_session_map_key` — the only two `write_steering_row` callers.
- `reject_fragment_sentinel_protocol`: refuse proto-255 sync Install on both families; Deletes still reconstruct (under-match only).
- Correct the #6923 comment (conntrack mirror ≠ shim-probed steering map).

## Regression (RED on origin/master sources, GREEN after)
- `fragment_sentinel_never_publishes_a_steering_row_14648` — synced 255 LocalDelivery v4+v6: no PASS_TO_KERNEL selection, no steering writes; TCP control still publishes one.
- `fragment_sentinel_never_publishes_a_live_row_14648` — live 255 publish writes nothing; TCP control writes.
- `synced_import_refuses_fragment_sentinel_protocol_14648` — 255 Install refused both families, Delete allowed.

Verified: all three tests FAILED with sources reverted to origin/master (tests kept), pass with the fix. See `docs/log/14648.md`.

## PR #14841 — userspace-dp: commit staged mirror clone before recycling ingress frame (#14641) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14641-campaign`

Closes #14641

## Defect (Y31-01)
`enqueue_pending_forwards` ran the success-path `recycle_ingress_frame` before `commit_staged_mirror_clone(..., source_frame)`. Recycle pushes the ingress offset onto `pending_fill_frames` and, at the 1024-entry `FILL_BATCH_SIZE` threshold, synchronously calls `drain_pending_fill`, publishing the chunk to the kernel FILL ring. On the non-in-place arm (cross-UMEM / tunnel / NAT64) the staged mirror clone holds no snapshot — only the in-place arm snapshots first (`snapshot_staged_mirror_clone`) — so the commit copied bytes out of live ingress UMEM that could already be kernel-owned. The kernel could DMA a different packet into the chunk in between, so the analyzer receives another flow's bytes: wrong mirror content and cross-flow disclosure to the mirror target. Forwarding is not corrupted. The in-tree invariant comment ("not yet returned to fill ring") was false on this arm. `neighbor_dispatch.rs` already commits before recycling; only the dispatch site was exposed.

## Fix
- Move `commit_staged_mirror_clone` above the success-path `recycle_ingress_frame` in `enqueue_pending_forwards`, matching `neighbor_dispatch.rs`.
- Correct the frame-safety invariant comment to state the real guarantee.
- Add a `#[cfg(test)]` `FILL_PUBLISH_HOOK` seam in `drain_pending_fill` (`tx/rings.rs`) that fires immediately after a batch is published to FILL so a test can model kernel DMA ownership; no release-build state or call.

Not changed: recycle batching, `drain_pending_fill` itself, the build-failed recycle (no later read on that arm), the in-place snapshot arm, mirror sampling/counting (#11432, #13656).

## Regression test
`mirror_clone_copies_frame_before_fill_publish_14641` (`tx/dispatch/tests/ptb.rs`): three bindings with distinct UMEMs (non-in-place arm, no snapshot), a 60-byte UDP frame at ingress offset 0, 1023 stale `pending_fill_frames` entries so the success-path recycle crosses the 1024 threshold, and the hook scribbles `0xA5` over the source chunk the instant it is published to FILL (modelled kernel DMA).

- RED (production fix reverted, hook+test present): FAILED — mirror bytes all `0xA5` (165) instead of frame `aa bb cc ...` (170, 187, ...).
- GREEN (fix applied): passes — clone copied while chunk still userspace-owned; publish runs only at the function-tail drain.
- Controls `successful_forward_commits_one_mirror_clone_11432` and `mtu_signalled_forward_does_not_enqueue_mirror_clone_11432` stay green before and after.

## Validation
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-14641 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- mirror_ --test-threads=1` → **67 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored** (incl. new test + both #11432 controls). Scratch under `/var/worktrees/.cache` only.
- Base: worktree HEAD `0fd02a585b`; the three touched files are byte-identical between that base and current `origin/master` `51d355c1d8` (empty diff on those paths), so the patch applies unchanged to master.

## Risk
Success-path recycle happens a few instructions later (after mirror commit), within the same request iteration and before the tail fill drain — chunk return latency unchanged in aggregate. In-place (retained) forwards unaffected.

Log: `docs/log/14641.md`

## PR #14843 — nat: make address-persistent sticky slot cross-node stable (#14627) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14627-campaign`

Closes #14627

## Why
#12789 keyed `sticky_pool_index` with the per-process `hot_path_hash_seed()` (getrandom OnceLock, no setter/HA sync), so after an HA failover or restart a host's new flows on an `address-persistent` multi-address pool computed a different pool slot than its synced sessions — splitting the host across two public IPs. Docs promised a pure `(src_ip, pool_len)` function identical across nodes; code and docs disagreed.

## What
- `sticky_pool_index` now uses fixed domain seed `STICKY_POOL_HASH_SEED` over the unchanged keyed multiply-mix hasher (`ECMP_FLOW_HASH_SEED` precedent) — pure function of `(src_ip, pool_len)` on every node/across restarts. Predictable seed justified: output is the wire-visible translated address, indexes no attacker-growable table; splitmix64 folds still destroy seed-independent collision families.
- Docs reconciled: `hot_hash_seed.rs`, `docs/ha-failover-status.md`, `docs/userspace-dataplane-gaps.md`, `docs/userspace-dataplane-architecture.md`, `docs/log/14627.md`.
- Regression `sticky_pool_index_is_cross_process_stable_14627`: production == fixed-seed core for 64 v4 (pool 4) + 16 v6 (pool 8) sources, plus cross-seed vacuity control.

## Validation

- Full `nat::` suite: 653 passed; 3 `tests_idle_lease_sync_8121` failures verified identical on unmodified HEAD (pre-existing).
- Remaining per issue: on-cluster HA failover observation.

## Risk
One-time remap of fresh allocations on upgrade (same move every restart already caused); live sessions/leases keep pinned addresses; single-address pools unaffected.

## PR #14844 — userspace-dp: fence announced permit epochs against reopen (#14651) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14651-campaign`

Why:
`publish_announce` with `permit_open=false` set `open=false` but never advanced `closed_epoch`, so a later same-epoch open announce re-opened a fenced permit epoch and `allows()`/`decide_pre_write` would `Proceed` a queued q0 write for it. There was no generation-regression reject for the same `run_id`, and `queue_epochs` were replaced wholesale in both `publish_announce` and `publish`, letting a stale message roll a queue epoch backward and re-admit a superseded queue epoch.

What:
In `AuthorityState` (`userspace-dp/src/slowpath_reinject_9506.rs`): announce-close now does `closed_epoch = max(closed_epoch, permit_epoch)` like `close_permit`; a generation regression for the same run is rejected before any mutation (equal generation stays an idempotent re-announce, #10478 advance stays accepted); at the current permit epoch a queue-epoch regression rejects the update in both `publish_announce` and `publish`. Four regression tests in `slowpath_reinject_9506_tests.rs`. NOT changed: Go sender, wire format, new-`run_id` timeline reset.

Validation:
RED: production file reverted, `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14651` reports 0 passed, 4 failed. GREEN: same filter 4 passed; `slowpath_reinject_9506::` 75 passed; `reinject_9506` 89 passed, 0 failed.

Risk:
Only stale/regressed authority updates are newly rejected; the honest monotonic Go sender is unaffected. A new `run_id` still starts a fresh timeline.

Closes #14651

## PR #14845 — userspace-dp: reserve full trailer in session rule-id guard (#14839) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14839-campaign`

Why:
encode_session_record admitted a policy_rule_id whenever
pos + 2 + rule_id.len() + 2 <= 512, reserving only 2 bytes past the
rule_id. The encoder then unconditionally writes the handshake byte,
the provenance byte, and the 8-byte PPTP call-id pair (10 bytes), so
a rule_id sized to the old guard passed it and panicked past the
512-byte frame on the PPTP write, killing the session-sync worker.
rule_id is "<from>-><to>/<name>" from operator config; no name cap
below the 307-374 byte panic window exists in Go or Rust.

What:
session_sync.rs: reserve RULE_ID_TRAILER_BYTES (1 + 1 + 8) in the
capacity guard. Either the whole trailer fits and is written, or
rule_id_len falls back to 0, the established fail-closed
unattributed wire value. No wire-format or capacity change.
codec_tests.rs adds the boundary regression test; docs/log/14839.md
records the analysis.

Validation:
New test RED on the unfixed encoder: panic at session_sync.rs:438,
"range end index 513 out of range for slice of length 512". GREEN
post-fix: the boundary test plus 20 neighbouring codec tests pass.

Risk:
Rule_ids within 8 bytes of the old limit now fall back to
unattributed instead of being carried; pre-existing fallback,
fail-closed, and unreachable for realistic zone/policy names.

Closes #14839

## PR #14848 — firewall: modifier-only terms implicitly accept, only authored next term falls through (#14632) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14632-campaign`

Closes #14632

## Why
Junos nonterminating actions (count/log/forwarding-class/policer/dscp with no terminating action) carry an implicit accept. xpf synthesized fall-through for every empty-action term, so `then count bgp;` ahead of a final discard fell through and blackholed counted traffic (e.g. lo0 BGP/SSH), and a later term's routing-instance/forwarding-class could override the classification.

## What
Fall-through is now only the authored `then next term`:
- Go snapshot builders (`filters.go`, `protocol_policies.go`) copy `term.NextTerm` verbatim — no empty-action synthesis.
- Rust `continue_term := next_term && action.is_empty() && routing_instance.is_empty()` (`compiler.rs`); effective renderer, nft text mirror and netlink lo0 mirror use the same predicate, so a modifier-only term terminates as implicit Accept with its modifiers merged.
- #5142 fail-closed preserved: a real terminating action plus `next_term` still terminates (bit disclosed by renderer).
- Fold-in fixes: four Rust policer fixtures that relied on empty-action fall-through now author `next_term: true` (`single_rate_policer_instances_are_term_scoped_11333`, `cached_three_color_policer_instances_are_term_scoped_11333`, `flow_cache_hit_runs_both/all_three_fall_through_policers`); mixed-version rollout comments in `filters.go`/`compiler.rs` corrected (old Rust also falls through on empty action, so implicit accept requires new Go + new Rust together); stale empty-action line at `docs/config-schema.md:2029` corrected.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp filter::tests` — 204 passed, 0 failed (post-rebase; was 4 failed before fixture fix).
- Go RED/GREEN cells for snapshot/render/nft/netlink modifier-only implicit accept recorded in `docs/log/14632.md`.

## Risk
Behavior change for modifier-only terms ahead of a later discard — they now accept instead of falling through, matching Junos. Mixed-version rollout keeps old fall-through behavior until both Go and Rust are upgraded together; no wire change.

## PR #14852 — userspace-xdp: resolve ingress domains per VLAN (#14842) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14842-campaign`

## Summary
Resolve the XDP shim's ingress routing domain per (ifindex, wire VLAN) so VLAN units in different routing domains sharing one parent ifindex get their own domain, instead of the parent entry being deleted as ambiguous (domain u32::MAX, fail-closed for every VLAN on the parent).

## Why
`USERSPACE_INGRESS_DOMAINS` was `HashMap<u32, u32>` keyed by ifindex only, and Go's `localAddressRoutingDomain` returned ambiguous for a parent whose VLAN units live in different instances. The shim then used u32::MAX for every domain-scoped local/interface-NAT lookup (healthy, tagged-only, GRE-inner, degraded arms).

## What
- Shim: `UserspaceIngressDomainKey { ifindex, vlan_id, reserved }`, map renamed `userspace_ingress_domains` -> `userspace_ingress_domains_vlan` (8192), one outlined `ingress_domain_for` helper (untagged = 0xffff sentinel; VID 0 preserved) used by both healthy and ctrl-disabled paths. Drive-by: remove one duplicate closing brace #14645 left in `try_xdp_userspace` (master did not parse; filed #14850).
- Go: `buildUserspaceIngressDomainEntries` (untagged row per adjudicated ifindex, `(parent, VID)` per VLAN unit, native-VLAN owns untagged, conflicts poisoned to 0xFFFFFFFF), map-iterating reconcile, 8192 capacity preflight before classifier writes.
- Migration: loader reconciles the re-keyed map, removes the legacy pin, excludes it from the live-pin ABI refusal; WG kernel-path pin path follows.
- Tests: `ingress_domains_vlan_14842_test.go` (builder, conflict poisoning, native VLAN, sync+reap, capacity binding, BPF test-run: VID 50 passes in its own domain, VID 80 does not inherit it). Docs: `docs/log/14842.md`.

## Validation
- RED pre-fix: producer test failed to compile (`buildUserspaceIngressDomainEntries` undefined).
- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ ./pkg/dataplane/` clean; producer + 6537/13929/12055 fixtures pass.
- Privileged BPF: `TestUserspaceXDPResolvesIngressDomainPerVLAN14842`, `TestUserspaceXDPDoesNotPassForeignDomainInterfaceNAT14644`, `TestUserspaceXDPDoesNotPassForeignDomainLocalAddress13929` pass.
- Shim regenerated: 908732 processed insns (9.13% headroom). Master already measures 10.55% once its source parses (the shipped verdict predates #14645; filed #14851), so the object was installed with XPF_SHIM_ALLOW_LOW_HEADROOM=1 and the gate verdict records OVERRIDDEN.

## Risk
New pin name orphans legacy pinned maps (mirrors #13929/#14644); mixed-version pairs fail map lookup loudly. Conflicting or missing (ifindex, VID) rows resolve to u32::MAX, matching no domain-scoped local/NAT entry — fail-closed.

Closes #14842

## PR #14853 — userspace-dp: fragment NAT64 IPv6 at the actual sub-1280 egress MTU (#14658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14658-campaign`

Why:
fragment_nat64_ipv6_frame floored the caller's egress MTU to the
1280-byte IPv6 link minimum after its total_len <= mtu early return.
For a sub-1280 tunnel inner MTU (WireGuard wg_inner_mtu or GRE
native_gre_inner_mtu, composed by nat64_v6_egress_mtu with the RFC
7915 +20 delta), a 1240-byte translated packet was emitted as one
1248-byte atomic fragment — larger than the input — and larger
packets fragmented at 1280. The WG/GRE outer-MTU guards then dropped
the oversized frames with no PTB: a silent blackhole. The 1280 link
minimum is a floor hosts must accept, not the configured egress MTU;
sibling #5159 already forbids this floor for tunnel underlays.

What:
Remove mtu.max(1280) so fragmentation uses the actual caller MTU.
Add a max_data == 0 fail-closed guard (MTU <= 48 cannot carry the
40-byte base + 8-byte fragment header plus an 8-byte-aligned data
chunk), mirroring fragment_nat64_ipv4_frame's max_payload == 0
guard; without it removing the floor would loop on zero-length
chunks. NOT changed: nat64_v6_egress_mtu / post_transform_inner_mtu
(their composed tunnel budgets are correct and prove reachability);
the mtu == 0 unknown path still forwards whole.

Validation:
Rebased onto origin/master 08f11138a5 (RED/GREEN first exercised
at 8653903746; the intervening master commits do not touch this
function). New tests
nat64_v4_reply_fragments_at_sub1280_ipv6_egress_mtu_14658 and
nat64_v4_reply_too_small_ipv6_egress_mtu_fails_closed_14658 drive
build_nat64_forwarded_frames at mtu=1200/48 asserting every
fragment <= MTU, offsets/M/ident, exact reassembly, and a fitting
control. RED with the floor temporarily restored: both fail
(left: 1, right: 2; is_none assertion). GREEN: cargo test --bins
-- 14658 13943 = 5 passed, 0 failed (both new tests plus the
13943 controls).

Risk:
Fail-closed on MTU <= 48 is new but unreachable from real egress
derivation (unknown stays 0 = forward whole). Sub-1280 IPv6 links
are non-conformant underlays per RFC 8200; honoring the configured
MTU matches every sibling fragmenter/segmenter.

Closes #14658

## PR #14854 — userspace-dp: key egress DSCP rewrite by filter forwarding-class (#14636) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14636-campaign`

userspace-dp: key egress DSCP rewrite by filter forwarding-class (#14636)

Why: with an ingress BA classifier plus an input-filter
`then forwarding-class`, the packet queued as the filter's class but
was re-marked with the BA class's code-point. The #13968 class-first
rewrite key re-derived the class from DSCP/PCP only
(resolve_cos_ba_class_rewrite -> resolve_trusted_ba_class_queue_id),

cached-seed or cache-hit paths: MF-selected voice was bleached to the

instead of the operator's filter.

(forwarding_build/cos.rs) so a filter class name resolves to the

clamped queue) in tx/cos_classify_ba.rs and thread the resolved
filter class through resolve_cos_ba_class_rewrite at all four
callsites; the fresh flowless arm now resolves after its ingress
filter walk. Store the filter class's queue id on
CachedTxSelectionDescriptor and pass it to
reclassify_cached_cos_lp_rewrite, and arm cos_lp_reclassify when
only the filter class has a class-keyed entry. An unmaterialized
filter class now rewrites by its own entry too. NOT changed:
drain-time per-queue uniform rewrite and the #13968 BA-only order.

Full --bins: 8398 passed, 50 failed (pre-existing baseline set,

## PR #14855 — nat: register NAT64 persistent pools and swap pool configs atomically (#14679) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14679-campaign`

Why:
compileNAT64 ignored singular pool.Address, silently skipped poisoned members, and never registered PersistentNAT, so valid NAT64 configs failed the #4960 pre-pass and NAT64 bindings were dropped on Go session delete. compileNAT cleared the live persistent table before fallible work, so a failed recompile wiped pool metadata, and destination NAT skipped the #12525 from-scope stamp.

What:
- `config.NAT64PoolHostAddresses`: members via `SourceNATPoolMembers` (singular + list), each must be a bare IPv4 or /32 host mirroring Rust `parse_pool_v4`; any bad member poisons the whole pool.

- `compileNAT`/`compileNAT64` stage registrations in `natPersistentStaging`; `CompileConfig` swaps them atomically via `PersistentNATTable.ReplacePoolConfigs` only after both succeed. Standalone wrappers commit on their own success and preserve prior configs on failure.
- Destination NAT checks `HasNATFromScopeStamp()`.
- #4960 pre-pass guards updated for WithStaging names / staged ReplacePoolConfigs call.

Validation:
New `compiler_nat_14679_test.go` cells RED on origin/master 08f11138a5 (singular rejected, poisoned accepted, wipe on failure, unstamped DNAT passed) and GREEN after fix. 14110 persistent-pool tests, pre-pass order/fidelity guards, pkg/config NAT64 tests, and userspace NAT64 tests pass. `TestValidationPassRecordCensus6903` fails identically on stashed base at the same head (pre-existing).

Risk:
NAT64-only pools with any non-IPv4-host member now hard-fail the pre-pass, matching the Rust all-or-nothing rule skip. SNAT prefix pools keep expanded (non-NAT64) semantics.

## PR #14856 — userspace-dp: release reverse and policy-batch coordinator steering claims on delete (#14840) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14840-campaign`

Why:
An HA import claims steering rows as Coordinator under two owners —
the forward under entry.key and the synthesized reverse under
reverse.key — but the synced delete released only owner=entry.key,
so row(reverse) stayed Remaining for the life of the process and its

deferred redirects executed only under the collecting Worker holder,

Retain the removed reverse incarnation in the synced delete and
delete it under owner=reverse.key; capture removed incarnations in
remove_shared_policy_item and release both Coordinator claims plus
the forward DNAT hold there; execute deferred redirects under the

one 10512 assertion narrowed (quiesce now legitimately writes for
the batch's own tuples). Log: docs/log/14840.md.

limbs), GREEN post-fix (cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14840,
3 passed). Full afxdp::ha:: suite 202 passed, 1 failed
(strict_mirror_refusal_..., base-attributed on 5371f5fe19).

Risk:
Deletes release strictly more claims, only for incarnations removed
under the removal lock or batch lease; last-owner protection
unchanged. Abort-path quiesce now also deletes the batch tuples'
steering rows, convergent with its shared removal.

Closes #14840

## PR #14857 — filter: enforce PBR term policers, forwarding-class, and dscp-rewrite (#14659) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14659-campaign`

Why: a matched then routing-instance (PBR) input term bypassed its
three-color policer, forwarding-class, and dscp-rewrite. The runtime
TX-selection walk returned before merge_matched_tx_modifiers, the
host-bound session replay capture returned before extending the PBR
term's policer handle, and the non-routing walk returned
FilterResult::default() at the PBR term, erasing a prior next term
policer-drop/log. Transit defers three-color metering to TX selection,
so no path charged those terms.

What: merge the PBR term's modifiers in the TX-selection walk (the
term is terminal, so the !continue_term arm returns); extend the PBR
policer handle before stopping in capture_input_filter_policers_v4/v6;
return accumulated fall-through modifiers from the non-routing walk;
run the inline routing-bearing remainder only when that walk stayed
green and meter the tunnel outer gate only for firewall-local outer
destinations so no policer double-charges; remove the now-dead
routing_bearing plumbing. NOT changed: loss-priority remains the
documented meter-only no-op (#9503) — ThreeColorPolicerAction carries
no loss-priority field.

Validation: three new 14659 cells RED on base (forwarding_class None,
0 replay handles, lost next-term drop) and GREEN after the fix;
adjacent filter::, poll_descriptor, cos_classify, and GRE local-delivery
suites pass except three pre-existing base failures (two
prerouting_scope 11297 cells and stage11 13637, identical on base).

Risk: transit PBR packets now meter and can drop on their configured
policer where they previously bypassed it; that is the intended
operator-visible correction. Cached TX-selection already merged the
term, so flow-cache replay is unchanged.

Closes #14659

## PR #14859 — userspace-dp: cap MTU-derived tunnel MSS with all-tcp (#14664) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14664-campaign`

Why:
`select_tcp_mss` returned the tunnel value whenever it was > 0, so an MTU-derived GRE MSS of 1416 (WG 1365) replaced a smaller `all-tcp 1200` on tunnel-egress SYNs with no `gre-out` set. Operators set `all-tcp` below the tunnel budget for a smaller downstream link; those flows advertised the larger MSS and depended on PMTUD, the blackhole the knob exists to prevent. The `mss.rs` header and `docs/feature-gaps.md` claimed `all-tcp` clamps every forwarded TCP SYN, contradicting the fallback-only behavior.

What:
- `native_gre_tcp_mss`: with no explicit `gre-out`, return `min(derived, all-tcp)` when `all-tcp` is set; the `gre-out` branch stays `min(gre-out, derived)` irrespective of `all-tcp`.
- `tunnel_tcp_mss`: cap the purely MTU-derived WireGuard value by `all-tcp` when set; `gre-out` remains a GRE-only knob.
- `select_tcp_mss` unchanged (0 tunnel value still falls back to `all-tcp`); header, priority doc, and `feature-gaps.md` now agree that `all-tcp` is a ceiling only on the implicit derived value.
- Five regression cells in `tunnel_tests.rs` through `select_tcp_mss`: GRE capped, WG capped, all-tcp unset keeps derived, explicit gre-out ignores all-tcp, larger all-tcp does not raise derived.
- `docs/log/14664.md` records defect, fix, and RED/GREEN proof.

Validation:
- RED (mss.rs reverted, tests kept): GRE cell left 1416 vs 1200, WG cell left 1365 vs 1200; 3 controls passed.
- GREEN: `cargo +1.98.1 test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14664` — 5 passed. Broader `tunnel` filter: 240 passed, 2 failed, both base-attributed (fixed upstream post-base by #14846 and the coordinator D11/D14 work), neither on the MSS path.
- Rebased onto current master; final diff is 4 files.

Risk:
Explicit `gre-out` behavior is deliberately unchanged (`min(gre-out, derived)` irrespective of `all-tcp`, pinned by test); only the implicit derived value gains the `all-tcp` ceiling. No caller, formula, gre-in, or plain-forward behavior changes.

Closes #14664

## PR #14860 — userspace-dp: drop transit directed broadcasts per routing domain (#14654) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14654-campaign`

## Why
`transit_dst_is_martian` took no forwarding/domain arguments and never consulted `connected_v4_directed_broadcasts`, while `transit_src_is_martian` in the same file did the domain-keyed lookup — so a transit packet to a connected subnet-directed broadcast escaped the martian drop toward policy/session/NAT (RFC 2644 MUST NOT forward). Conversely, `v4_addr_is_directed_broadcast` scanned all `connected_v4` with no routing-domain/table filter, so a `.255` host in a /16 in one VRF suppressed ICMP errors merely because another VRF owns the /24 whose broadcast is that address.

## What
- `frame/addr_class.rs`: `transit_dst_is_martian(forwarding, ip, routing_domain)` checks the domain-keyed directed-broadcast index; new table-scoped `v4_addr_is_directed_broadcast_in_table` / `dest_…_in_table` / `src_…_in_table` and allocation-free `icmp_error_table_for_meta`.
- `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (+ flow-cache-hit, TX dispatch call sites): `transit_destination_class_drop` resolves the effective flow domain via `effective_routing_domain_for_flow` and checks original + translated destinations in that domain. `LocalDelivery` stays exempt.
- `icmp.rs` / `icmp_ptb.rs`: reject/Time-Exceeded and PTB suppression scoped to the trigger's ingress installing table.
- `forwarding/fabric.rs`: `ingress_l2_group_unicast_ip` uses the ingress-domain index instead of the unscoped scan.
- New `tests_directed_broadcast_14654.rs` (predicate/domain, descriptor-path, ICMP table-scope cells); `docs/log/14654.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14654`: 3 passed.
- Related suites (11413/13981/10689/icmp/pkt-type filters): 57 passed, 0 failed.
- RED: the new test file fails to compile on pristine master (16 errors — new signatures/helpers), so it cannot pass pre-fix; its descriptor cell asserts martian drop with zero TX/session/neighbour state.

## Risk
Cross-VRF hosts that share an address with another domain's directed broadcast are no longer dropped/suppressed in the wrong domain. Ambiguous fabric domains own no broadcasts, matching the existing source gate. ICMP scoping falls back to any-table when the ingress domain has no registry row.

Closes #14654

## PR #14861 — nat: block duplicate address-only mints on idle persistent leases (#14671) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14671-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes #14671 (D5-02): the three same-allocator address-only source-NAT
admission paths ignored idle persistent address-only leases, so a
second subscriber could be minted a duplicate `(translated_ip, port)`
and `persistent_inbound_lookup` then denied inbound persistent-NAT
traffic for both subscribers.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs`: new
  `persistent_address_only_contended_except` — an IDLE address-only
  persistent lease (other than the candidate's own) contends when its
  recorded permit grants cover the candidate flow's remote endpoint;
  grant-less leases fall back to the `persistent_by_translated` index.
  Live leases are excluded (their flows hold exact live tokens,
  checked separately — #9131). All three admission paths
  (`reserve_address_only_persistent` fresh+pinned,
  `reserve_address_only_roundrobin`,
  `reserve_address_only_maybe_persistent`) now refuse or probe the
  next pool address on contention, alongside the existing live-token
  and PAT checks.
- New regression tests
  `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_addr_only_persistent_idle_14671.rs`
  (registered in `nat/mod.rs`), log in `docs/log/14671.md`.

Deliberately NOT `address_only_owns_wire_identity`: its persistent
owner counts include an unconditional `Any(base)` key per lease,
which would block same-port flows to unpermitted remotes and the
subscriber's own lease rejoin (both pinned as controls).

## Validation

- RED on base `a801922911`: 2 of 4 new cells failed — H2 minted the
  duplicate `(203.0.113.1, 4000)` on the single-address persistent
  path and via roundrobin.
- GREEN after fix: 4 passed.
- Full `nat::` suite: 667 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (includes
  #9131 sibling-fallback cells).

## Risk

A colliding second subscriber is now refused/rotated for up to the
idle lease timeout instead of blackholing both — the Junos
persistent-NAT capacity posture, matching the existing PAT-path
precedent. Contention scan is O(leases) on the cold admission path
only.

Closes #14671

## PR #14863 — userspace-dp: ack-gate reinject completions and cap flow queues (#14678) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14678-campaign`

Why:
DrainReinjectCompletions closed the completion stream on any 5ms
timeout, including zero-byte idle expiries, while Rust committed
removal with ack_ready as soon as write_all reached the socket
buffer. A completion written between Go's deadline expiry and its
Close was purged in Rust and destroyed unread in Go, so the pending
entry expired as an ack-timeout uncertain and was fail-closed.
Mid-frame timeouts took the same silent path, and enqueueFlowLocked
appended to per-flow FIFOs without any bound.

What:
Go keeps the completion connection across zero-byte idle timeouts
via a buffered reader; a partial-frame timeout closes the stream
and returns an error so Poll fails pending work closed. Go sends a
one-byte ack (0xAC) only after a full frame is buffered locally,
and Rust ack_ready now waits for that byte, releasing the batch
for redelivery on ack timeout/EOF. CapturePipeline gains
MaxFlowFrames (default 512, counted by FlowQueueDrops); excess
frames return through the existing terminal-DROP path.

Validation:
New TestDrainReinjectCompletionsPreservesConnOnZeroByteTimeout,
partial-frame error/recovery cells, and the per-flow cap cell fail
on base 08f11138a5 and pass with the fix. The #13234 overflow test
and updated #9506 partial-frame test pass. Rust complete_conn
cells (5, including the new unacked-redelivery cell) pass.
Pre-existing pkg/nfqueue failures (ipsec advisory #14139 cell and
long-TMPDIR socket binds) reproduce on unmodified base.

Risk:
Old Go against new Rust never acks, so batches redeliver on
reconnect instead of purging (fail-safe). New Go against old Rust
sends ack bytes the old probe rejects, dropping the connection;
completions redeliver on the next accept. Both sides ship together.

Closes #14678

## PR #14864 — dataplane: account for compileZones mid-loop aborts after host mutation (#14680) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14680-campaign`

Why:
CompileConfig returned (nil, err) when compileZones failed mid-loop, so CompileUserspaceShim returned before inheritHostDivergence, abortAfterHostMutation and ProveArmCoverage. A VLAN create or address reconcile on an earlier interface had already mutated the host, yet HostDivergence stayed empty, no #4960 annotation was attached, and the prior arm-coverage verdict stood. The #10915 S-tag gate also sat after MTU/ethtool/LinkSetUp, so a stuck rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse NIC was brought UP before the abort, and markVLANSubInterfaces was append-only so a reused ifindex was permanently excluded from XDP swap/status.

What:
CompileConfig now returns the partial result on a compileZones failure; compileZones/programZoneMaps publish the deferred XDP sets queued before the abort. CompileUserspaceShim routes a non-nil partial result through inheritHostDivergence and abortAfterHostMutation with the #4960 annotation (nil-result pre-mutation errors keep the bare return). The S-tag gate is hoisted to just after ensureRxVlanParsePreconditions, before MTU/ethtool/buffers/LinkSetUp (disabled interfaces exempt; the late duplicate is removed). markVLANSubInterfaces now replaces the set on the success tail. NOT changed: later CompileConfig phases still return (nil, err), and aborted applies do not rewrite vlanSubInterfaces.

Validation:
New pkg/dataplane/compilezones_midloop_abort_14680_test.go: TestCompileUserspaceShimRecordsHostDivergenceOnCompileZonesMidLoopAbort, TestStagGatePrecedesLinkSetup14680, TestMarkVLANSubInterfacesReplacesStale14680 and TestCompileZonesAbortWiring14680 fail on base 91d5ccc48c (stag cell: host MTU = 9000, want untouched 1500) and pass after the fix; TestCompileZonesSuccessControl14680 passes both ways. Targeted neighbour suites (#4960/#5268/#7289/#8285/#9845/#10915) pass. Full pkg/dataplane suite exceeded the 300s tool timeout without a reported failure; please rerun before merge.

Risk:
CompileConfig callers that check err first are unaffected. Non-Ethernet netdevs now trip the S-tag gate before framing is known (fail-closed, same direction as before, only earlier). HostDivergence may now be retained for zones aborts that previously reported bare, which is the intended operator signal.

Closes #14680

## PR #14866 — config: consume device-map key value as pair, reject bad identities (#14685) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14685-campaign`

Why:
The compact hierarchical spelling `interface ge-0/0/3 key pci pci 0000:01:00.0;` compiled to PCIAddr="pci" and `key mac mac <addr> pci <addr>` to MAC="mac": collectDeviceMapProps stepped i++ over the packed Keys, so the value of `key` (pci/mac, itself a prop keyword) was re-read as a property and captured the following keyword. The real address was lost yet SchemaValidate and strict compile passed (non-empty identity), so the resolver searched for PCI "pci".

## PR #14869 — userspace-dp: purge local-hit shared sessions and fence conditional deletes (#14666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14666-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes all three legs of D4-03 (#14666):

1. **Local-hit purge blindness** (`resolve.rs`): a worker-local hit
   (`hit.shared_entry == None` after UpsertSynced/Demote materialized
   the row) derived no `shared_identity`, so
   `purge_translated_synced_hit_with_context` took the `Absent`
   branch — never removing shared authority or replicating the
   conditional delete. Now adopts `(session_id, generation)` from
   the shared entry under the same key when the local row's adopted
   id matches; the purge's under-lock predicate stays authoritative
   (replacement published in the window declines and survives).
2. **Queue-full conditional repair** (`worker_commands.rs`):
   `replicate_session_delete_conditional` no longer releases the
   target worker's NAT/NAT64 port unconditionally on a refused
   queue push — the allocator is keyed by `(flow, translated)` and
   cannot distinguish a stale incarnation from a live replacement.
   The `SESSION_DELETE_DROP_EPOCH` bump still arms the sibling's
   delete-drop sweep; `repaired` stays 0 for conditional drops.
   The unconditional `replicate_session_delete_repairing` is
   unchanged.
3. **Companion conflation** (`delete_synced.rs` + producers):
   `DeleteSyncedConditional` gains `companion_expected_id`,
   captured with `expected_id` at the stale-close producer
   (`session_delta.rs`) and coordinator fan-out
   (`ha/session_import.rs`). The worker deletes the companion only
   when live id is 0 (converged), expected is 0 (uncaptured/legacy),
   or live == expected; a different live id is a replacement and is
   preserved.

## Validation

New regression cells (RED by construction pre-fix — shared entry
leaked / port freed / companion clobbered):

- `local_hit_purge_removes_shared_and_replicates_14666`
- `conditional_queue_full_repair_preserves_replacement_port_14666`
- `conditional_delete_preserves_replaced_companion_14666`

Controls:

- `local_hit_purge_preserves_replacement_shared_entry_14666`
- `unconditional_queue_full_repair_still_releases_14666`
- `conditional_delete_removes_matched_companion_14666`
- `conditional_delete_absent_companion_is_noop_14666`
- `purge_translated_synced_hit_full_teardown_13674` and the #10512
  scoped-delete cells stay green.

## PR #14870 — userspace-dp: re-derive HA ownership before synced upsert (#14669) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14669-campaign`

Why:
handle_upsert_synced computed allow_replace_local/is_active from the
peer's stamped owner_rg_id before locally re-resolving, served the
peer's cached LocalDelivery/neighbor fallback verbatim, and leaked
the replaced pool reservation when the NAT target moved pools. On a
split-RG node a stale standby stamp could clobber a live active-RG
local session, an owner-0 stamp was HA-gated against the wrong RG,
a foreign local_ifindex could be delivered into this node's host
stack, and a Pool A -> Pool B replacement stranded Pool A's port.

What:
In handle_upsert_synced, re-resolve forward entries with
lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_session_without_cache, stamp the
local owner_rg_for_resolution first, then compute
allow_replace_local/is_active and enforce HA. On the standby arm
only, a local NoRoute/MissingNeighbor may still fall back to the
peer candidate through cached_session_resolution, which revalidates
egress/neighbor against this node's live state and requires
ForwardCandidate, so a peer LocalDelivery is never served and #326
activation readiness is preserved. Release the previous reservation
when the new entry does not reserve or when the NAT / is_reverse /
zone-pair target changed (release sweeps only the exact previous
tuple, so same-tuple refreshes keep their holder bit).
NOT changed: coordinator import guard in session_import.rs (separate
pre-publish surface, noted in docs/log/14669.md).

Validation:
New upsert_synced_14669_tests.rs (5 cells): RED on pre-fix code
4/5 fail (owner-0 stamp, stale-stamp clobber, foreign ifindex 99,
cross-pool strand; same-tuple control passes); GREEN 5/5 pass.
Full session_glue suite: 337 passed, 3 failed, 2 ignored; all 3
failures reproduce identically on clean origin/master
(publish_shared_session_counts, flush_session_deltas 9412,
demote_dedup timing).

Risk:
Cache-free re-resolution deliberately distrusts peer state on this
path; packet path still revalidates HA. Cross-pool release runs
before re-reserve only when the translated tuple or zone pair
actually changed.

Closes #14669

## PR #14874 — config,ipsec: shadow ESP fallback behind authored IKE policies (#14689) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14689-campaign`

## Summary

Fix the D10-04 fallback and partial IKE policy proposal chain validation bypasses so commit and render agree on IKE Phase-1 resolution when an `ike-policy` is authored.

### Why

- `chainResolves` fell through to a same-named ESP proposal (`cfg.Proposals`) even when an authored `ike-policy` existed and failed its own all-resolve check, rescuing a broken IKE chain with a Phase-2 proposal.
- Proposal-agreement checking was skipped whenever not every proposal resolved, hiding authentication/lifetime conflicts among the resolved proposals.
- `ipsecVPNAuthNeedsPSK` returned `false` on the first dangling entry, while the renderer skipped that entry and resolved a later PSK proposal—so `[dangling, prop-psk]` without a key passed the commit gate and was then silently skipped at render.
- `resolveIKESettings` rendered Phase-1 from the ESP proposal table whenever no IKE proposal resolved, even when `cfg.IKEPolicies[name]` had been authored.

### What

- **Commit gate (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec.go`)**: an authored ike-policy is authoritative—when it exists, only the all-entries-defined check decides; the legacy ESP fallback now requires `IKEPolicies[name]` to be absent, and nil proposal entries cannot resolve. Proposal agreement now runs over every resolved proposal of an authored policy before the chain verdict.
- **PSK gate (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_psk_14139.go`)**: missing/nil/unknown-auth entries are skipped exactly like the runtime resolver; PSK is required if any resolved proposal needs it, and the auth is undecided only when nothing resolves.
- **Runtime (`pkg/ipsec/ike.go`)**: the `cfg.Proposals` legacy fallback is consulted only when no ike-policy of that name was authored; otherwise the resolver falls through to `errIKEChainUnresolved` and the VPN is skipped. Legacy direct-proposal, no-policy, pubkey, and partially-resolvable configurations are unchanged.
- Regression cells are distinct per claim: shadowed-dangling, shadowed-conflicting, partially-dangling PSK, direct gate pins, runtime never-render-ESP pin plus legacy control. See `docs/log/14689.md`.

### Validation

- RED on base `217e9132a2`: the shadowed `CompileConfig` cases, direct chain/PSK gates, and runtime ESP-render cells failed.
- Focused `pkg/config` and `pkg/ipsec` selectors pass after the fix; full `pkg/ipsec` passes.
- Broad `pkg/config` failures (e.g. `TestIKEPolicyResolvableChainAccepted`, `TestIKEGatewayNoPolicyAccepted`, routing-instance cells) fail identically on unmodified base—pre-existing gate-ordering exposure from the later PSK gate—and are not regressions of this change.

### Risk

Limited to configurations where an ike-policy and an ESP proposal share a name, or an authored policy contains dangling entries; those now fail closed. Legacy direct-proposal and no-policy configurations remain accepted. Configs with conflicting resolved proposals are rejected consistently with runtime behavior.

Closes #14689

## PR #14879 — routing: fail closed on non-empty except PBR scopes (#14699) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

and any specific positive set hasPositiveRef/positive, so both the
strict-valid #4338 idiom (source-address 0.0.0.0/0 plus
source-prefix-list X except, then routing-instance) and tolerant-path
positive+except fell into the POSITIVE-WINS warn branch and returned
[""] or the positive set. Dropping an exclusion widens (P \ E) to P:
the kernel FBF ip-rule mirror steered the very prefixes Junos says to
exclude (typically management/RFC1918) into the target VRF, with only
a Warn log. The userspace path lowers except correctly, so only
kernel-forwarded/slow-path traffic was over-steered.

resolvePBRDirection in pkg/routing/rules.go now keys solely on the
resolved except size whenever an except ref is present: a non-empty
except always returns the pre-existing degraded error (term dropped,
fail-closed under-steer), and a defined-empty except reduces the
direction to its deduplicated positive set or to match-all when the
sole scope is the except/match-any/empty positive ref. The unused
hasPositiveRef variable is removed; unresolved-except handling
(#11451) and the no-except path are unchanged. NOT changed:
ResolveFilterPrefixListAddrs in pkg/dataplane/userspace — its
boolean-inversion matcher represents sole-except and its tolerant
positive-wins fallback is separate documented behavior. README
support matrix and docs/log/14699.md updated.

./pkg/routing/ passes; go build ./... passes; gofmt clean.

The MissingNeighbor arm fired trigger_kernel_arp_probe (and the tunnel resolver enqueue) at arm entry, before the NAT64 fail-closed drop, the NPTv6 Untranslatable drop, the SNAT-allocation failure, and the final composed-NAT bindless fence. Packets this arm discards therefore emitted a cleartext ARP/NDP for their exact destination — the #11284-class leak for post-SNAT fence tuples, and wasted probes for NAT64/SNAT-exhausted drops. The seed also installed without a tuple-gate permit, published via the ungated conntrack path, never replicated to peers, and proceeded even when the pressure-shed lease failed. Separately the segmented-TCP neighbor retry built each segment with overlap_admissions: None, dropping the taken tokens (Drop = fail).

What:
- poll_descriptor/mod.rs: suppress the early probe/resolver for every packet in the arm; defer the single admitted probe to the committed-seed site, past NPTv6/SNAT/final-fence, without re-checking probe_throttled (the early note_kernel_probe record is that window). Seed refuses on shed-lease failure, holds a global_tuple_gate permit through install + shared publish + gated conntrack publish, and replicates via replicate_session_upsert. A gate refusal also refuses buffering (seed_install_refused) instead of parking for replay.
- neighbor_dispatch.rs: ride retry overlap tokens on the first segment.
- tx/dispatch/mod.rs: commit taken tokens on the segmented copy path instead of drop() (RAII fail).
- Tests: tests_missing_neighbor_probe_gate_14661.rs (NAT64, SNAT-exhausted, NPTv6-untranslatable, post-SNAT fence zero-probe; permitted control probes once/seeds/publishes/replicates), segmented-retry overlap test, and the #13762 control updated to zero wire probes.

Validation:

GREEN: cargo test --bins -- 14661: 5 passed. missing_neighbor: 45 passed. neighbor: 307 passed. #13762 throttle control: passed. Post-rebase GREEN re-run: 5 passed.

Flowless packets no longer probe at arm entry; they never seed and re-drive resolution via retry/neg-cache on a later admitted packet. The neg-cache fast-fail resolver enqueue (policy-admitted only) is unchanged.

## PR #14881 — userspace-dp: make steering row owners action-aware and preserve coordinator claims (#14650) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14650-campaign`

Closes #14650

## Defect (D1-03, both arms MATERIAL)
1. `SteeringRowOwners` stored `(SessionKey, Claim)` with no action byte. `write_and_claim` ran the BPF_ANY write unconditionally and `release_locked` deleted only when no owner remained, so a PASS_TO_KERNEL (2) publish overwrote a shared REDIRECT (1) 40-byte row and the PASS release stranded the surviving REDIRECT owner at PASS permanently (shim cpumap_or_pass, kernel forward with no zone policy).
2. `retire_workers()` mem::take-n every rows+holdings shard, wiping coordinator claims #9560 round 3 added so coordinator rows survive, desyncing rows vs holdings against lock-free sync_session (#7209).

## Fix
- Registry records the published action per (owner, holder) claim in both Owners and Held.
- `write_and_claim` coalesces the physical write fail-safe: REDIRECT wins if the incoming action or any other owner's recorded action is REDIRECT — PASS is never written while a REDIRECT owner shares the row.
- `release_locked` (entry/row/retire paths) restores the surviving owners' fail-safe action via a new `restore(row, action)` callback under the same row-shard lock; deletes only when no owner remains (unchanged).
- `retire_workers` clears only worker bits per shard under lock, preserving coordinator claims in both maps.
- Production restores write via `write_steering_row` (held-only rows decode a key via `session_key_for_row`); merged with #14648's `steering_key_is_publishable` gate.

## Regression (RED on base by construction, GREEN after)
- `steering_owners::tests::aliased_pass_publish_restores_redirect_on_release_14650`
- `steering_owners::tests::retire_workers_preserves_coordinator_claims_14650`
- `session_glue::steering_row_owners_9560_tests::aliased_pass_over_redirect_is_coalesced_and_restored_14650` (real recorder seam)
- `session_glue::steering_row_owners_9560_tests::aliased_redirect_release_restores_pass_for_survivor_14650` (reverse order)

## Verification
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14650`: 4 passed
- `-- 9560`: 43 passed; `-- 9517`: 7 passed (controls green)
- Full suite parallel: 8390 passed / 61 failed — pre-existing parallel/global-state flakes in files untouched by this change (counts vary 55-61 run-to-run; spot checks fail on shim naming/tally drift). Post-rebase compile re-verification was blocked by host load >100 from sibling lanes; the merged conflict is a 3-line comment+gate combination in `publish_session_map_key` with the rest applying cleanly — main agent should re-run `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14650 9560 9517` once load subsides.

## PR #14884 — userspace-dp: rotate scan eviction sample off deterministic prefix (#14673) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14673-campaign`

## Why

`ScanCore::evict_stalest_in_zone` sampled `per_zone_srcs[zone].iter().take(64)` on every eviction. `per_zone_srcs` is an unseeded `FxHashSet`, so that prefix is the same deterministic 64 buckets on every call and computable by an off-box attacker who knows the inserted addresses. An attacker who pinned 63 prefix entries at count 9 (`SCAN_DETECT_COUNT - 1`) and kept its scanner at count 8 inside the prefix made the scanner the deterministic lowest-count victim; one fresh decoy admission wiped its history and the next probe re-seeded it at count 1, so the scanner never reached the detection count of 10. Forwarding was never fail-open; this is a detection fail-open only.

## What

- The eviction sample now walks the dense `key_ring` (which mirrors `per_src` exactly, maintained by the single `insert_src`/`remove_src` primitives) from a persistent `evict_cursor`, instead of iterating the per-zone `FxHashSet`.
- `evict_cursor` rotates the window: each eviction examines at most `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT` (64) same-zone candidates and advances the cursor past the examined span, so successive evictions cover the whole zone instead of a fixed prefix (#6239 cursor pattern).
- The start is seeded per boot: `ScanCore::seed` is drawn once from `hot_hash_seed::hot_path_hash_seed()` (#2364 pattern), and the walk starts at `(evict_cursor + seed_offset) % ring_len`. `evict_cursor` is stored in the unseeded frame (the next start is translated back by `seed_offset`), so successive starts advance contiguously by the examined span rather than jumping by `seed_offset` each time. Tests pin the seed via `ScanCore::with_seed`.
- Other-zone slots do not consume the 64 same-zone budget; the total walk is capped at `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT + 8 * EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT` (576) ring slots. If the window finds no same-zone candidate at all (sparse zone in a huge ring — the #4890 test shape), a fallback takes a rotating seeded sample of the zone's own `per_zone_srcs` index (at most `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT` same-zone entries, skip bounded by the per-zone cap, never by the total table size), which keeps the existing #4890 regression green without any O(ring) walk.
- Victim selection is unchanged (#4418/#2234): expired-or-empty first, then fewest distinct destinations, stalest `window_start` on ties. `per_zone_srcs` otherwise serves only the O(1) zone-cap count.
- `evict_examined_log` (test-only, like the existing cleanup `examined_log`) records the sample so tests can prove rotation.

NOT changed: the eviction victim policy, the cap sizes, the cleanup cursor, and any forwarding behaviour.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14673`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
  - `pinned_prefix_scanner_not_self_evicted_14673` — the issue's scene recreated exactly (first 64 `FxHashSet` entries pinned 63× count 9 + scanner at 8, rest count 1): scanner survives the decoy-triggered eviction and trips on its 10th port. Pre-fix the static prefix evicts the scanner (8 < 9).
  - `eviction_sample_rotates_across_calls_14673` — three successive samples pairwise different, each ≤ 64.
  - `eviction_eventually_covers_all_entries_14673` — repeated evictions with refill eventually examine every entry.
  - `eviction_bounded_under_other_zone_interleave_14673` — 2000 other-zone + 3 target: terminates with ≤ 2×64 same-zone examinations.
  - `eviction_start_depends_on_seed_14673` — different pinned seeds reshuffle the first sampled key.
  - `eviction_rotating_still_prefers_expired_14673` — expired/empty entry inside the window reclaimed first.
  - `scanner_detected_through_decoy_evictions_at_cap_14673` — end-to-end through `PortScanTracker::check` at the real 4096 cap.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- scan`: 55 passed, 0 failed, including the pre-existing #4890 regression `fresh_scanner_admitted_when_zone_entries_outside_global_prefix_4890`.

Suite log: `/var/worktrees/.cache/14673-scan-suite3.log` (`test result: ok. 55 passed; 0 failed`).

## Risk

Fallback samples `per_zone_srcs` from a cursor offset; same-zone examination stays ≤ 2× `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT`. At real saturation the dense ring window hits first, so the fallback is cold. No forwarding, cap, or cleanup behaviour changes.

Closes #14673

## PR #14886 — cluster: cap heartbeat monitor name/count at uint8 wire limits (#14704) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14704-campaign`

Fixes D14-02: `marshalHeartbeatBody` wrote a monitor's `NameLen` as `uint8(len(nameBytes))` and the monitor count as `uint8(numMon)` with no ≤255 guard, while groups (`maxHeartbeatGroups`, #4434) and the software version were clamped in the same function.

A monitor name >255 bytes wrapped its length byte (260→4) and >255 monitors wrapped the count byte (260→4), while the full payload was still written. The receiver trusts both bytes, so it parsed monitor payload as the version trailer and never reached the `XPFE` echo trailer — poisoning `SoftwareVersion`/`HAProtocolVersion` and silently losing the echo lease that `handlePeerHeartbeat` uses for freshness.

## Fix
- `maxHeartbeatMonitorNameSize=255`: oversize names are skipped whole (not truncated, not `break` — later monitors survive).
- `maxHeartbeatMonitors=255`: the monitor section stops at the uint8 count limit.
- Drops are reported by the existing `heartbeatMonitorTruncations` detector, so the truncation stays operator-visible.

## Tests
New `heartbeat_monitor_uint8_14704_test.go` — RED on origin/master (260-byte name decoded as `aaaa` + garbage monitor; 256-byte name as empty; 260 monitors wrote count byte 4), GREEN after the fix. Boundary controls (255-byte name, 255 monitors) round-trip verbatim, including groups, software version, HA protocol version, and both echo session/sequence pairs.

`go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run 'TestMarshalHeartbeat|TestMonitorTruncation|TestHeartbeat'` passes. Full `pkg/cluster` suite has one pre-existing failure (`TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752`) that fails identically on unmodified origin/master — base-attributed, unrelated.

Closes #14704

## PR #14892 — cluster: gate duplicate-node-id heartbeat warning on HMAC (#14705) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14705-campaign`

Why:
`heartbeatReceiver.readLoop` called `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat` before `admitFrame` ran HMAC verification, so an on-link sender spoofing the configured peer IP (the #6888 pin checks source IP only and is explicitly not an authentication boundary) could forge the EventRG duplicate-node-id history entry and, once per 30s, keep the shared `duplicateNodeIDWarningDueLocked` limiter fresh — suppressing the richer authenticated `NoteDuplicateNodeIDBeacon` diagnostic (iface/boot-id/src-mac detail).

What:
Gate the readLoop call on new `duplicateNodeIDAuthenticated` in `pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go`, which verifies only the HMAC against every accepted control-link key (rotation-interoperable, #6630) — deliberately without `admitAuthed`, so the discarded frame still touches no liveness, election, or replay/epoch state. Unkeyed nodes cannot verify and keep the legacy warning (dual-accept, mirroring `admitFrame`). NOT changed: `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat` itself, the beacon path, or the election `warnDuplicateNodeIDLocked` path — they only consume the shared limiter. Documented in `pkg/cluster/README.md`; log in `docs/log/14705.md`.

Validation:
New `TestRecvLoop_DuplicateNodeIDHeartbeatRequiresHMAC_14705` drives the real `readLoop` over UDP from the configured peer IP on a keyed manager:
- RED pre-fix: `forged same-NodeID heartbeat consumed the duplicate limiter without HMAC verification` (unsigned frame).
- GREEN post-fix, 4/4 subtests: unsigned/wrong-key/tampered frames produce no history, do not consume the limiter, do not refresh liveness, and a genuine authenticated beacon immediately after still warns; signed primary-key and rotation-alt-key duplicates still warn, are discarded, and do not consume replay state (same nonce admitted as a normal peer heartbeat); unkeyed duplicates still warn.
- Full `pkg/cluster` suite: only `TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752` fails — base-attributed on `6c08a7512e` (fails identically without this fix; unrelated session golden drift).
- Re-verified GREEN after rebase onto current `origin/master`.

Risk:
A genuine duplicate peer signing with a retired rotation key no longer warns via heartbeat once the rotation is finalized — same posture as `admitFrame`, and the authenticated beacon shares the accepted key set. A replayed captured signed duplicate can still warn once per 30s; bounded by the existing shared limiter and no state is admitted.

Closes #14705

## PR #14895 — daemon: fail closed on lossy ICMP and GRE tuples in rematch (#14697) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14697-campaign`

Why:

policymatch.Query from the captured 5-tuple, which stores only the
ICMP echo identifier in the port fields and never the ICMP/ICMPv6
type or code. With ICMPType nil, matchSingleApp skips every

reauthorizePolicyCandidates also never called the GRE
discriminator guard the rename paths apply.

Add capturedTupleValid in daemon_policy_rename.go (ICMP 1 /
ICMPv6 58 always invalid offline; GRE 47 invalid with zero
discriminator), point the three rename-rematch entry points at
it, and call it first in reauthorizePolicyCandidates' isPermitted
so lossy candidates stay deletion debt. capturedTunnelDiscriminatorValid
is unchanged as the capture-time PurgeTunnelVariants classifier.
Decisive regression tests with matcher premises cover V4, V6
(custom type-128 app), the helper-match twin, an
unconditional-guard control with a TCP retained control, the
guard unit, and the reauthorize ICMP/58/GRE0 cells.
NOT changed: policymatch and the session wire formats.

Validation:
RED on base 75a10ddc15 (tests only): all six decisive tests FAIL
(V4 retained under lan->wan/p-new; reauthorize discharged the
ICMP candidate; guard accepted protocol 1). GREEN at head
589a98ecd7: all six PASS; rename/reauthorize neighbourhood,
invalidation/rollback neighbourhood and the policy-focused daemon
subset (TestPolicy|TestRematch|TestReauthor|TestRename|TestHelper|
TestNat64|TestRollback) PASS. The full pkg/daemon suite exceeded
the 280s lane timeout twice under multi-lane CPU contention with
no failures observed before the cutoff; the policy-focused subset
above is the exercised full-suite proxy.

Risk:
Live ICMP/ICMPv6 sessions are now deleted by rename-rematch
instead of retained, and ICMP/ICMPv6/GRE0 rollback candidates
stay deletion debt — matching the pre-existing GRE0 rename
behaviour. No wire or config change.

## PR #14898 — cli: reject trailing tokens after display pipe formats (#14715) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14715-campaign`

Closes #14715

## Why

`show configuration` and config-mode `show` selected the render format with `strings.Contains(rest, "| display set")` (likewise json/xml/inheritance) while building the path only from tokens **before** `|`. `show configuration | display set interfaces` silently discarded `interfaces` and rendered the whole tree (`ShowActiveSet()` / `ShowActiveSetRedacted(nil)`). The RBAC gate did not save it: `evaluateCommandRegex` only checked `pipeWords[1]=="display"` was authorizable, so the spelling satisfied an interfaces-scoped allow and evaded a `$`-anchored display-set deny. Same mechanism in `show system rollback N` and its candidate-read predicate. (Redacted for non-superuser classes per #4099, so this dumps full structure, not cleartext secrets.)

## What

- Token-exact pipe parsing via `splitDisplayPipe` / `splitConfigShowPipe` (`cli_show.go`), shared by `handleShow`, `handleConfigShow`, and the rollback branch (only `| display set` there). Only `| display <json|set|xml|inheritance>` with no trailing tokens selects a format; trailing tokens, unknown formats, bare `|` are syntax errors naming the token, with no render. Config-mode additionally accepts exact `| compare [rollback <N>]`.
- `evaluateCommandRegex`: a `display` pipe is authorizable only as `| display <format>`, optionally followed by one recognised output filter (`| display set | match x`, which dispatch SplitPipe splits and the gate reassembles) — gate and executor now agree; anchored-deny / scoped-allow bypass spellings are denied at the gate too.
- `showSystemRollbackCompare` aligned to the token-exact handler.
- Regression: `pkg/cli/show_display_pipe_trailing_14715_test.go`; history: `docs/log/14715.md`.
- NOT changed: `cmd/cli` remote surface (#13202 already token-exact), output-filter pipes, `pendingPipeSuffix` reassembly.

## Validation

- New `TestShowConfigurationDisplayPipeTrailing14715` + `TestDisplayPipeGate14715`: **RED** on pristine `origin/master` (59f4ac7065; all 8 malformed cells dumped the whole tree with the host-name sentinel, gate authorized the trailing spelling), **GREEN** on the fix.
- Targeted suites green: pipe-canonicalization 9628, redaction 4099, rollback authz, dispatcher gates. `go vet ./pkg/cli/` and `gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/cli` suite: only `TestApplyToDataplaneGlobalFRRParity11455` fails, reproduced identically on pristine base (base-attributed, unrelated).

## Risk

Operators who relied on silently-ignored trailing tokens after a display format now get a syntax error (Junos-compatible). Legitimate `| display <fmt>` forms and chained `| match`-style filters are unchanged.

tunnel_owners/snapshot_was_installed from.

verb sequence (sync_session upsert -> stop_workers -> rebind) and

the synced-session map", "stop_workers wiped the tunnel-owner

both lane and base (parallel-load flakes, none in the touched
paths). Clippy clean of errors. Full detail: docs/log/14677.md.

resident until the next reconcile/disarm — identical to every

holder retirement frees worker-held bits on the same instances the
preserved forwarding (and the rebuild via previous) reuses: no

A trigger-on crossing arms rt.onLatched in evaluateEvent, but the cooldown-stale drop, the permanent-rejection return, and the HandleEvent classify-reject/empty-plan continues never released it, so one transient commitFn (nil, err) wedged a policy forever under a sustained fault. applyOnce reserved a global-budget slot before commitFn and never refunded it, so read-only retries burned all four slots and starved healthy policies. criticalConfigPath checked only path[0], so groups-wrapped security remediations queued as ordinary work.

## PR #14902 — feeds: reject malformed feed paths instead of fetching base (#14723) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14723-campaign`

## Why

`joinFeedURL` (pkg/feeds/feeds.go) silently fell back on malformed
per-feed paths. `url.Parse` error returned the fetchable base URL, so
`/denylist%ZZ.txt` fetched the server base and installed its prefixes
under the named feed. A `//denylist.txt` network-path (host token,
empty path) and a `v1:prod/...` scheme:opaque form likewise collapsed
to a base fetch. Clearing `RawPath` decoded `%2F` to `/` in the wire
path. `resolveBaseURL` trimmed trailing `/` from the raw URL string,
cutting query/fragment tokens ending in `/`. The strict compiler gate
validated only the base URL, never the per-feed path, so all of these
committed clean.

## What

- `pkg/feeds/feeds.go`: `joinFeedURL` now rejects an unparseable
  per-feed path and any scheme/opaque/authority form by returning
  `""`; `Apply` registers no feed for a rejected join (fail-closed
  per #5645, warning logged) instead of fetching the base. A malformed
  BASE still returns unchanged so readFeed / the #5183 gate report it.
  The join runs on escaped paths with `RawPath` pinned, so `%2F`
  survives in the requested URI. `resolveBaseURL` trims trailing `/`
  from the URL path only, never from query/fragment, preserving the
  `https://` scheme (the prior scheme-less rebuild corrupted
  scheme-bearing bases to a host-only string); unparseable/scheme-less
  values keep the historical raw slash-trim, and the mirrored
  `feedServerResolvedBaseURL` in pkg/config matches.
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_observability.go`: the strict
  feed-server endpoint gate now also rejects a malformed per-feed
  `path` via `feedEntryPathMalformed` (mirrors the runtime rule;
  pkg/config cannot import pkg/feeds). Strict commit rejects; the
  tolerant load/peer-sync wrapper downgrades to a warning.
- Regression: `pkg/feeds/feed_url_join_malformed_14723_test.go`
  (join table, Apply-level no-fetch for each malformed spelling, and
  `%2F` preserved in `RequestURI` through httptest) and
  `pkg/config/compiler_feed_path_malformed_14723_test.go` (strict
  rejects, tolerant warns, valid/escaped paths accept). The #14177
  table's scheme-relative cell now expects rejection `""` instead of
  the silent tail-keep. `pkg/feeds/README.md` documents the rule.
- NOT changed: the base-URL malformed/plaintext gates (#5183/#14385)
  and the single-feed (no FeedEntries) registration path.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` (6621660159): `TestJoinFeedURLMalformedAndEdgePaths`
  returned the base / base+`/` for `%ZZ`, `//`, and colon forms and
  decoded `%2F`; `TestApplyMalformedFeedPathFetchesNothing14723`
  registered each malformed feed against the base URL;
  `TestApplyEscapedFeedPathPreserved14723` saw `/base/a/b.txt`;
  `TestFeedServerMalformedFeedPathRejected14723` committed clean.

## PR #14903 — api: canonicalize safe-method route in command-regex gate (#14712) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14712-campaign`

Why:
readPermissionFor (#9134) canonicalizes any safe non-GET method to
the GET entry for the coarse permission, so HEAD passed that gate
and reached authorizeRESTCommand — where the route was keyed on the
raw method and "HEAD /api/v1/status" missed every GET-keyed
command table (restRouteCommand, restRoutesNoCommand, and the
request-decoded switch), hitting the fail-closed unmapped denial.
Every regex-restricted (non-superuser) class got 403 on 100% of
HEAD reads while GET succeeded: a fail-closed availability defect
(health probes, SDK HEAD checks), not an authorization bypass.
Only HEAD is reachable — Go's ServeMux aliases HEAD to GET
patterns; OPTIONS/TRACE have no GET pattern and never reach a GET
handler.

- pkg/api/authz_command_regex_9952.go: authorizeRESTCommand now
  keys the command tables on canonicalRESTRoute14712(method, path)
  — the GET spelling for any safe method (same isSafeHTTPMethod
  predicate readPermissionFor uses), the raw method otherwise, so
  POST mutation routes are never aliased. HEAD now follows the GET
  verdict exactly, including deny cases, the six
  declared-no-command reads (#14146), and the request-decoded
  routes (show-text topic, system/info type).
- pkg/api/authz_command_regex_14712_test.go: regression cells call
  the gate directly and drive the real readAuthz middleware.
- docs/log/14712.md: investigation record.
NOT changed: readPermissionFor, the mutation gate, the route
tables.

Validation:
- go test ./pkg/api/ -run '14712': RED on origin/master
  ca1baec1e9 (HEAD refused by the generic unmapped message while
  GET allowed under allow-commands "^show version$"; HEAD
  show-text?topic=version and system/info?type=uptime refused
  under their allow-lists; HEAD 403 through readAuthz under
  allow-commands "^show " while GET 200), GREEN after the fix.
- Neighbor suites 9952|14146|9134|13249|11678|12582|9051|9903|
  6660|5561 pass.

## PR #14905 — scheduler: keep recovery pair consistent and fix overnight weekday windows (#14726) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14726-campaign`

Closes #14726

## Defect (D19-04)
1. `recordRepublishResultLocked` cleared `republishFailClosed` on a successful latch republish while `s.active` was still the forced all-false map, so `ActiveStateWithFailClosed` consumers (route listener, ipmon overlay, apply seeding via `policySchedulerPublicationState`) could observe `(inactive, failClosed=false)` — scheduled deny/reject compile inactive (fail-open) until the next tick. An intervening apply-path `RecordRepublishResult(nil)` had the same effect.
2. Accessor split pinned by documentation: the latch boolean covers only the republish latch; `PolicyFailClosed(now)` covers recovery hold / unavailable zone. Daemon paths already OR the two.
3. `isWithinWindow` evaluated overnight windows on today's weekday only: Friday-only 22:00–06:00 was active Fri 00:30 and inactive Sat 00:30 (inverted).

## Fix
- Clearing the latch now recomputes the authoritative map at `lastEval` (hold/zone still force inactive) via `recomputeActiveLocked`; exactly one normal-disposition recovery republish remains owed.
- Overnight windows belong to their starting weekday: today's window contributes its evening segment, the post-midnight tail is yesterday's resolved window (`overnightTailActive`); today's `exclude` suppresses the tail; uniform daily windows unchanged.

## Tests
New `pkg/scheduler/scheduler_14726_test.go` (3 tests, incl. daily/exclude controls). RED on origin/master 59f4ac7065, GREEN with fix; full `pkg/scheduler` suite, `pkg/config` scheduler tests, and daemon scheduler/actuator neighbour tests pass; `go vet` clean. See `docs/log/14726.md`.
