## PR #14908 — configstore: serialize rescue saves against delete so deleted cleartext is not resurrected (#14722) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14722-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes D18-05 (#14722): `SaveRescueConfig` wrote `rescue.conf` off-lock while `DeleteRescueConfig` took no lock/fence/WaitGroup, so a delete during an in-flight save was undone by the save's later rename — resurrecting cleartext secrets after a confirmed deletion — and a slow older save could overwrite a newer one.

- `SaveRescueConfig` claims a monotonic rescue generation under `s.mu` with its snapshot/fence-check/`rescueWG` registration, then after `rescueWriteBarrier` takes the new `rescueMu` and refuses to write (`ErrRescueSaveSuperseded`) if superseded.
- `DeleteRescueConfig` claims a generation under `s.mu` and raises `rescueAppliedGen` under `rescueMu` before its durable unlink+dir-fsync; it does not hold `rescueMu` for the unlink or wait on `rescueWG`, so it succeeds promptly during a barrier-held save. A save started after the delete legitimately recreates the file.
- gRPC `rescueAction` maps `ErrRescueSaveSuperseded` to `FailedPrecondition` (like `ErrRescueSaveFenced`); never success, never Internal.
- Deterministic barrier regression tests: delete-vs-in-flight-save (plus post-delete save control) and save/save newest-wins.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` `918ac30a36`: both new tests failed (resurrected `rescue.conf`; stale save overwrote newer).
- GREEN after fix: both pass, including `-race`.
- Rescue-focused configstore subset passes (fence #10769, delete-fsync #5197, empty-active #11803, rescue load/migration, `TestRescueConfig`); grpcapi rescue test passes; `go vet` clean.
- Full configstore suite exceeded the 300s harness window on slow pre-existing migration tests without an observed failure — flagged for CI/main verification.

Closes #14722

## PR #14909 — userspace-dp: refresh WG peer captures on same-engine commits (#14675) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14675-campaign`

## Summary
WireGuard control loop and DNS resolver captured `peer_pubkeys`, `effective_endpoints`, and `endpoint_hosts` once at thread spawn and never refreshed them across engine-reusing config commits (#14675, finding D6-03).

## Why
`init_consumer_state` runs once at spawn; `wg_peers_eq` does not compare `endpoint_host`, so a hostname-only commit reuses the engine `Arc` verbatim and moved none of the enumerated stale reasons (removed / engine_changed / attachment / outer_mtu / bind_device / kernel_transport). The surviving thread drove timers/handshakes for the old peer set, sent initiations to a decommissioned literal, and resolved the old hostname forever.

## What
- **Coordinator** (`tunnel_supervision.rs`, `types/runtime.rs`): capture peer config (pubkey, configured literal endpoint, authored hostname, pubkey-sorted from forwarding state — the only place `endpoint_host` exists) into `WgControlEntry::spawned_peer_config` at spawn, beside the other spawn-time captures (#2921/#5291/#10196 precedent); new `peer_config_changed` stale-prune reason restarts the thread (and respawns the resolver with fresh `endpoint_hosts`) on any peer add/remove or endpoint/hostname change.
- **Control loop** (`wg_control/mod.rs`): per-tick `refresh_consumer_peers` converges a surviving thread onto the engine's current table via new `peer_configured_endpoints()` (config-only, no live overlay): added peers adopted with BringUp, configured changes reset effective + clear engine live endpoint + abort pending + drop stale roam-hold stamp, removed peers drop all state; unchanged-config tick is a no-op so live roams survive.
- **Engine/Peer** (`wg/engine.rs`, `wg/peer.rs`): `peer_configured_endpoints()` and `clear_live_endpoint()`.
- NOT changed: the resolver itself — respawn re-captures hosts; a second dynamic-target mechanism was rejected.

## Validation
- 10 new cells (4 coordinator incl. hostname rename on the **same** engine Arc with `engine_ptr` asserted unchanged; 6 `refresh_consumer_peers` unit cells incl. unchanged-roam control): **31 passed, 0 failed** together with wg2921/wg1866/wg5291 neighbors.
- RED probe (branch disabled + refresh early-return): 6 FAILED, controls green; restored.
- Wider `afxdp::coordinator::` + `afxdp::wg::`: 633 passed, 11 failed — all 11 reproduce on pristine `origin/master` d7003705f1 (base-attributed pre-existing).
- Verified GREEN on master 43e9f98a90 (patch-identical). ⚠️ Current master head dede834132b9 has an **unrelated test-only compile break** (`ha_tests.rs` `publish_row` arity from #14650/6621660159) that blocks any `cargo test` build; this branch needs a rebase once that is fixed.

## Risk
A peer commit now restarts the WG control thread (churn already accepted for MTU/bind/kernel-transport captures); sessions/live endpoints survive via engine Arc + live seeding. Hostname rename may serve the old host's last-good address until the new resolver's first answer (5s retry) — the #7158 last-good policy, unchanged.

Full lane log: `docs/log/14675.md` (includes the stash-loss recovery note).

Closes #14675

## PR #14911 — upgrade: preserve committed predecessor on verify failure (#14720) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14720-campaign`

Why:
For a fresh cut `j.PreviousVersion` records the live version, so when the live version's committed predecessor is re-staged under a new generation, `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`'s guard (`ver == PreviousVersion || ver == cur`) never fires for the predecessor. Verify failure then `RemoveAll`'d `versions/<pred>` plus its `.dbsnap` — identical-bytes, changed-bytes, and same-generation-reuse arms — and `copyStaged` demoted its preserved stamp on byte mismatch before replacing it. `defaultRollbackTarget(live)` then reported no restorable target, deleting the committed rollback target the cut was supposed to keep.

What:
`Run` captures a `predecessorStampBackup` (committed stamp bytes plus a `.<ver>.dbsnap` copy under `.predbak-*`) via `backupCommittedPredecessor` in `commit_stamp.go` before COPY whenever the target is the live version's committed predecessor. `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` (variadic) skips deletion for a backed-up predecessor, restores its stamp and snapshot, and keeps its `.dbsnap` instead of sweeping it as an orphan; the pre-STOP refuse paths restore the backup. `copyStaged` marks the backup `demotedByReplacement` when it demotes changed or unverifiable bytes, so a just-failed or changed-byte target stays non-committed after auto-rollback and Case-C demotion is never resurrected.

Validation:
New `cutover_predecessor_verify_14720_test.go` cuts 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0, re-stages 1.0.0 under a new generation, and fails VERIFY for identical and changed bytes plus a same-generation-reuse arm, asserting the dir, binaries, stamp (identical arm), and `.dbsnap` survive and `defaultRollbackTarget("2.0.0")=="1.0.0"`; START-failure controls assert the dir/snapshot survive while the stamp stays demoted. RED on `origin/master` (version dir destroyed in all verify arms), GREEN after the fix; full `pkg/upgrade` suite passes and the #12177 envelope controls stay green. RED-on-revert re-verified.

Risk:
Backup copies the predecessor `.dbsnap` under VersionsDir on every predecessor re-stage cut; it is removed on restore or left as a dotfile swept by later GC. No behavior change for non-predecessor targets.

Closes #14720

## PR #14920 — config: keep confirm encryption on later writes (#14719) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14719-campaign`

Why: commitConfirmedLocked sets DB.writeConfirmCover from the
guarded tree and clears it by defer on return, so every later
WriteConfirm of the same window (resolution tombstone on every
resolution in this configuration, finalization retry, boot
rebind/migration rewrites, FIRST sentinel) resolved PrevTree("")
plus cover("") to plaintext and fsynced the full PrevTree secrets
in cleartext, defeating the operator action of enabling
master-password that #14172 armed.

What: encodeConfirm now re-derives the armed profile from durable
state: DB.confirmEncryptionPRF keeps PrevTree-first precedence,
then the transient arm cover, then existingConfirmDiskPRF recovers
env.PRF from the on-disk record's self-describing AES-GCM envelope.
Fail-open to plaintext on absent/unreadable/plaintext disk state
so legacy windows stay plaintext and a corrupt prior record cannot
fail a tombstone/retry write. A 256-byte prefix gate on the
envelope marker avoids re-parsing near-ceiling plaintext records
on every encode. NOT changed: WriteConfirm signature, record
schema, legacy plaintext readability.

Validation: 6 new cells in
confirm_encryption_cover_persist_14719_test.go — 4 mechanism cells
(tombstone, retry, post-restart rewrite, FIRST sentinel) RED
pre-fix with the secret in raw bytes, GREEN post-fix; 2 controls
(end-to-end confirm, plaintext-stays-plaintext) pass both sides.
All 7 #14172 tests and the #9617 tombstone-headroom cell pass.
Full pkg/configstore suite failures are base-identical on
pristine origin/master (9088 x3, 9880, 9984, 9882, 12537).

Risk: a window armed encrypted whose on-disk record was deleted
or replaced with plaintext before a later writer runs falls back
to plaintext as pre-fix; production ordering (tombstone before
delete, retry/rebind/sentinel rewriting an existing record)
makes this unreachable on the named paths. See docs/log/14719.md.

Closes #14719

Both CLIs stored the interactive `edit` cursor as raw strings.Fields
tokens. AuthorizeConfigMutation lexes only the mutation line and
prepends the cursor verbatim, while execution re-joins the raw tokens
and the store lexer skips block comments and unquotes strings, so
`edit /* interfaces */ "system"` + `set root-authentication ...` was
gated as the raw spelling (anchored deny `^system root-authentication`
missed; comment text could satisfy `allow-configuration
"^interfaces"`) but executed as the denied `system root-authentication`
path. Quote-only (`edit "system"`) and split-comment (`edit system /*`
+ `set */ ...`) constructions desync the same way.

What:
- pkg/config: ParseConfigPath / ParseEditFragment /
  NormalizeEditPathTokens on the store lexer;
  AuthorizeConfigMutation normalizes the stored cursor against the
  line tokens, including a block comment spanning the cursor/line
  boundary, before resolving adjudicated paths.
- Local dispatchConfig edit/set/delete/deactivate/activate/annotate,
  handleCopyRename/handleInsert, and the remote CLI config arms now
  store and prepend only lexed cursors; malformed edit fragments
  (unterminated comment/string) are refused at edit time.
- Regression cells per surface in pkg/config, pkg/cli, cmd/cli plus
  docs/log/14716.md. NOT changed: store SetEditPath API, show
  rendering, gRPC/REST surfaces (nil cursor; they gate the resolved
  line they receive).

  tests only, CLI dispatcher cells allow all three packet
  constructions and the allow cell admits the mutation under
  ^interfaces.
- GREEN: TestParseConfigPath14716,
  TestAuthorizeConfigMutationDecoratedEditPath14716,
  TestDispatchConfigDecoratedEditPathDenied14716,
  TestDispatchConfigDecoratedEditPathAllowNotSatisfiedByComment14716,
  cmd/cli wire/malformed cells; 14716/14717/authz subsets pass in
  pkg/config, pkg/cli, cmd/cli; go vet + gofmt clean.
- Pre-existing (base-attributed): pkg/grpcapi
  TestSetAnnotateRemainsVerbLedForConfigurationGate13554 and sampled
  pkg/cli failures (11455, 5325/13552, 5763) fail identically on
  master; full pkg/config suite timed out at 240s under host load

Plain cursors unchanged. Lexically malformed edit fragments are now

## PR #14931 — userspace-dp: GC expired BIBs and preserve imported BIB on rollback in deterministic NAPT64 (#14670) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14670-campaign`

Closes #14670

## Defect (D5-01)
`allocate_deterministic_v6_at` in `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs`:
1. On block-claim failure the only expired-lease handling consulted the candidate's own `bib_key`; a block full of expired idle BIBs under *other* source ports reported permanent `AllocatorExhausted` (no `gc_expired_for_addr_locked` sweep on this path).
2. Both BIB-reuse branches minted joins with `promotion_timeout_ns: None` and no 0->1 activation snapshot, so `rollback_flow` treated promoted/imported BIBs as fresh and deleted them — destroying HA standby BIBs.
3. The full-block reuse branch bypassed the `max_tracked_flows` cap.

## Fix
- Bounded per-address `gc_expired_for_addr_locked(..., PRESSURE_GC_BUDGET)` sweep before declaring exhaustion; retry the lock-free claim only when something was reclaimed.
- Mirror `reuse_existing_lease_locked` activation bookkeeping in both reuse branches; imported leases defer promotion to a completing `release_flow` via the per-flow marker.

## PR #14936 — userspace-dp: re-stamp closing sessions on data-bearing segments (#14935) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14935-campaign`

Closes #14935

## Why
First FIN/RST sighting stamped closing + the 30s close window, after which the FIN-owning direction could never refresh last_seen/expires: the slow-path lookup refresh predicate and the flow-cache touch_if_stale both gated on !fin_own/!reset. The 1s reaper removed the entry at FIN+30s regardless of traffic volume — long iperf3 streams stalled to 0 at ~28-30s with SESSION_CLOSE idle Timeout on 200k+-packet flows (#14300 root cause).

## What
- Thread TCP payload progress (tcp_flags::has_payload_progress; payload length derived by the caller from the IP-declared datagram end minus the TCP header end, zero when unknown) through the slow-path lookup (lookup_with_payload / lookup_with_origin_with_payload, deferring-authority lookup, Owner replay), the flow-cache keepalive (touch_if_stale_with_payload), and the poll-descriptor tcp_payload_len helper plus shared-scope/resolve wrappers.
- A data-bearing segment re-stamps a CLOSING (single-FIN) entry from either direction onto the same closing window. Bare ACKs keep the #10885 fixed fuse. Fixed fuse retained only for TIME_WAIT (both FINs) and RST, which never slide on payload.
- Payload-unknown callers pass 0 and retain the pre-fix gate. Companion retention unchanged.
- Split existing close_refresh_gate_10885 ACK-only expectations from data-bearing behavior. Docs: session README, docs/log/14935.md.

## Validation
- New tests pass: data_bearing_segments_restamp_closing_past_fuse_14935, time_wait_and_rst_data_do_not_slide_14935, flow_cache_payload_keepalive_restamps_closing_14935. close_refresh_gate 12/12, session module 453 passed, tcp_flags 37 passed.
- RED: new tests do not compile against pre-fix tree (payload APIs absent).
- Pre-existing gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615 failure reproduces identically on origin/master, unrelated.
- Acceptance (loss-cluster long iperf3 60s+, -P12, both directions, v4+v6, >=18 Gbps, no stall) requires deployed build, remains for operator.

## Risk
Payload length derived only from meta offsets bounded by IP-declared datagram end; unknown/truncated yields 0 and keeps old frozen behavior (fail-closed). TIME_WAIT/RST lifetimes unchanged.

## PR #14938 — userspace-dp: thread payload progress through every poll hit path (#14937) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14935b-campaign`

**Userspace-dp**: payload progress was threaded only through the stamped-meta happy path; a subset of poll hit paths still derived `payload_len = 0` for data-bearing segments, so their CLOSING entries kept the frozen #10885 fuse and reaped at 20–30 s while other workers' flows survived.

#### What changed

* `poll_descriptor::tcp_payload_len` falls back to the frame-derived TCP header end (`frame::tcp_payload_offset`, fail-closed on truncated/malformed) when `meta.payload_offset` is unstamped (`0`), instead of reporting "unknown".
* `frame::tcp_payload_offset_from_l3` (new): L3-relative header-end derivation for a bare IP packet with an already-walked relative L4 offset.
* `tunnel::local_origin_packet_meta` stamps the true TCP header END via the new helper (it stamped the L4 start, counting the header as payload — false progress on bare ACKs for GRE/WG local-origin flows).
* Deleted the payload-less AF_XDP wrappers `lookup_session_across_scopes_with_shared` and `resolve_flow_session_decision_with_conntrack`: the poll loop now reaches only the `_and_payload` variants; test/non-worker callers call the inner/`_and_payload` form with an explicit honest 0 (fabric/shared-scope, deferred-owner, and embedded-ICMP-quote legs included; quotes carry no TCP payload of their own).
* Expiry belt-and-braces `closing_counters_keep_alive` retains a CLOSING (single-FIN, non-RST) entry when its canonical forward counters advanced since the last expiry check (change, not historic level; snapshot field `closing_counters_seen`).
* Tests: new `tcp_payload_len_14937_tests` (poll derivation: stamped, unstamped, bare-ACK, truncated), `deferred_owner_payload_replay_restamps_closing_14937`, `closing_counters_retention_keeps_active_pair_14937`, plus updates to the migrated session-code test references.

#### Why

PR #14936 (#14935) re-stamps CLOSING sessions only when `has_payload_progress(tcp_flags, payload_len)` holds, with `payload_len` derived from `meta.payload_offset`. The live loss retest of that build (`b4464fda30`) still shows the all-or-nothing 20–30 s decay: hit-bearing workers go CPU-idle and multi-GB sessions close `idle Timeout` (#14300 open). Diagnosis: the payload-less compatibility wrappers and the unstamped-offset derivation meant a subset of hit paths never supplied payload progress — per-worker bimodal decay is the expected signature. This change removes the poll loop's reachability of payload-less wrappers entirely and adds the frame-derived fallback, so every production hit path carries payload progress (or fails closed).

#### Test evidence

* `cargo test -- 14937 close_refresh_gate`: **18 passed** (4 poll derivation, 2 new session regressions, 12 existing close-gate).
* `cargo test -- session::`: **455 passed**; `session_glue`/`poll_descriptor` suites: 755 passed with 4 pre-existing failures that reproduce unchanged on pristine `origin/master` (`prerouting_scope` #11297 ×2, `publish_shared_session_counts`, `flush_session_deltas_9412`), plus 4 tunnel/D11/segmentation failures verified pre-existing via a clean stash run. `close_refresh_gate` tests were earlier shown RED without the payload progress logic (#14935 tests do not compile pre-fix; the counters-retention test exercises the FINed-side-only scenario that `companion_keeps_alive` refuses, so it cannot pass without the new check).
* Live acceptance (loss-cluster **60s+ `-P12`**, both directions, **v4+v6**, ≥18 Gbps, zero 0-byte streams, zero `idle Timeout` closes on multi-GB sessions) requires a deployed build and remains for the operator.

#### Risk

* Benchmarks available but not run. The frame fallback parses the TCP header only when the stamped offset is absent (not per packet on the happy path); the counters check runs only in the GC pass for idle-crossed entries. TIME_WAIT/RST keep the fixed fuse in every leg, bare ACKs still do not slide a half-close, and unknown/truncated packets still fail closed at 0.

#### Gate

* [x] RED/GREEN regression tests (one per hit path) - session + poll derivation suites.

#### Review focus

* **Routing domains:** N/A - no routing-domain change; payload derivation keys off the frame's own header, not the meta stamp.
* **Timeouts:** unchanged idle/close/timeout windows; `closing_counters_seen` only records the last observed forward counter total to detect change; the only lifetime change is retaining CLOSING (1-FIN, non-RST) entries whose counters advanced since the last GC check. A quiet closing flow still reaps at last-activity + closing window.
* **HaState side effects:** GC retention path (`closing_counters_keep_alive`) sits behind the same `companion_eligible` gate as `companion_keeps_alive`, so deliberately-reaped HA standby/stale-synced entries are not retained; GC order, HA hold/self-heal, and the DELAYED reaping of standby-held entries are not changed.
* **Seam exhaustion:** the GC path calls `rebucket_alive_entry`, sharing the `kept_alive_by_companion` stat (`WheelPopStats::kept_alive_by_companion`) — the same accounting seam, no new stat; seam loads on treated entries: at most one extra probe per idle-crossed entry per GC pass, bounded by finite idle-crossed population, in the GC pass only.

#### Code review

* [ ] [Deep smoke](https://github.com/psaab/xpf/blob/master/docs/testing/deep-smoke.md) — recommended.

#### Session-state/security enforcement

* [ ] Run security flows checks before merging.

Closes #14937

## PR #14940 — userspace-dp: complete TCP handshake on the flow-cache hit path (#14939) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14939-campaign`

Closes #14939

## Why
Live loss @ 8cece4238a: ALL iperf -P12 sessions showed `Timeout: 20` (OPENING) mid-flow instead of 300. `handshake_pending` never cleared: the reverse SYN-ACK is ACK-only under `is_ack_only` (PSH/URG ignored) and seeds the flow cache, and Linux's first data segment (PSH+ACK) is also cache-eligible — so the completing segment and all later data were served by `touch_if_stale_with_payload`, which refreshed only `last_seen_ns` and never consulted `handshake_pending`. Both halves reaped on the 20s opening window under traffic; SYN-less packets then failed strict-syn-check (permanent stall, #14300 root). The #6752 invariant ("completing segment reaches the slow path") holds only for a bare ACK arriving before any cache seed.

## What
- `SessionTable::touch_if_stale_with_payload` (the only session-table call in `stage_flow_cache_hit`) now mirrors the `lookup` completion predicate exactly: TCP, `handshake_pending`, `!closing` (#14630), ACK/no-SYN/non-closing flags, direction `syn_ack_first == is_reverse` (SYN-first forward ACK and SYN-ACK-first reverse ACK). Completion applies even inside the keepalive throttle window, re-buckets via `session_timeout_ns`, propagates via `propagate_tcp_state_to_companion` (also retires `pressure_shed_openings`), pushes the wheel.
- Non-completing hits: unchanged throttled `touch` (one extra bool check, no allocation).
- Deferred-Owner replay and `update_session`/`promote_synced` already completed through the real lookup/update arms — pinned as controls, unchanged. Synced HandshakePending replicas complete on this path once materialized (local hits are cache hits).
- README invariant corrected; `docs/log/14939.md` added.

## Validation
- RED on master: 4/6 new tests fail (`flow_cache_completing_ack_promotes_pending_pair_14939`, `flow_cache_bare_completing_ack_promotes_14939`, `synced_pending_replica_completes_via_flow_cache_hit_14939`, `completed_pair_survives_past_opening_window_under_cache_hits_14939`).
- GREEN: 6/6 incl. deferred-Owner control + post-RST #14630 guard; `session::` suite 461 passed. 5 `flow_cache`-filter failures (GRE TTL, flowless DNAT fragments) reproduce identically on unmodified master — pre-existing.
- Regression shape per issue: install SYN/SYN-ACK via real lookup, drive completing ACK via flow-cache hit path, assert Timeout 300 and survival past opening+closing windows under data.

## Risk
Hot path: one bool check per cache hit; completion arm runs once per handshake. Closing/RST explicitly excluded. Live loss acceptance (60s+ -P12 both directions v4+v6 >=18Gbps, Timeout:300 mid-flow, zero idle-Timeout closes) still required post-merge.

## PR #14942 — userspace-dp: map reverse revalidation zones direction-relatively (#14941) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14941-campaign`

userspace-dp: map reverse revalidation zones direction-relatively (#14941)

Reverse metadata is direction-relative (`reverse.ingress = forward
egress`), but a stale reverse hit's fresh lookup resolves the reply's
egress toward the client and the persist sites wrote that zone as the
pair's forward egress — flipping `reverse.ingress_zone` WAN->LAN.
Later ACKs then classified Foreign in `session_hit_authority`, skipped
their deferred refresh, and idled out at ~28s (#14300).

This maps `new_egress_zone` through `forward_egress_zone_for_hit` at
both `DeferredForwardingRevalidation` persist sites (session_glue
Owner path + poll_descriptor): forward hits pass through, reverse hits
preserve the recorded pair. The #9604 forward-companion arms judge a
forward route by construction and are unchanged; the
neighbor-generation flow-cache invalidation is a correct trigger, not
the defect.

Regression (`_14941`): mapping truth table; a stale reverse hit leaves
forward egress = reverse ingress = WAN and the next WAN ACK is Owner
with its refresh replayed; a forward reroute to dmz still rebinds the
pair (#14318 control). RED pre-fix: `reverse.ingress_zone == 7`
instead of WAN (2). Related suites `_14318` (4), `_9519` (34),
`policy_revalidation` (81), `session::tests` (262) pass.

Closes #14941

## PR #14944 — userspace-dp: validate flow-cache HA lease against current runtime lease (#14943) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14943-campaign`

## Why
FlowCacheStamp froze the 10s HA lease at insert; hits validated against the frozen copy and self-evicted every live entry ~10s after seeding, demoting cached resolutions to HAInactive. `try_refresh_ha_leases` also refused to resurrect an expired stored-active lease on a fresh heartbeat, and the watchdog treats `NeedsLock` as throttle-success (no control retry), so one lapse was permanent. Live correlation in #14300: burst cache evictions at session age ~26–28s, ACKs dropped, idle-timeout closes.

## What
- `flow_cache.rs`: extracted `FlowCacheStamp::current_lease_until` (shared with `capture`). Threaded the worker's live `ha_state` snapshot through the flow-cache lookup from `stage_flow_cache_hit`; lease-carrying entries are validated against the CURRENT runtime lease and re-stamped from it on every hit.
- Fail-closed preserved: a genuinely expired current lease, or an owner vanished/inactivated on a provided (non-empty) runtime map, still misses + evicts. An empty (not-provided) map is not gated — standalone behaviour unchanged; production always passes the live snapshot and `cached_flow_decision_valid` re-checks HA against the same map.
- `ha/session_domain.rs`: a matching fresh heartbeat (incoming active) resurrects an expired stored-active lease, minted from the incoming watchdog exactly as locked `update_ha_state` would. The mismatch arm still never resurrects — licensed by Go's demotion-intent inactive overlay (`haWatchdogGroupsLocked`), so a demotion can never arrive as matching-active. `NeedsLock` remains for CLEAR/membership/stored-empty/no-op.
- Go: comments only, stating the overlay→resurrection licence.

## Validation
- 4 new `_14943` cells: fresh-lease hit past insert+10s + re-stamp, genuinely-expired fail-closed, vanished fail-closed, heartbeat resurrection `Served(2)`. RED verified by reverting both logic hunks (3/4 fail; the fail-closed cell passes in both worlds).
- `flow_cache` + `try_refresh_9629` + `flow_cache_hit` suites: 145 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615`, verified failing identically on unmodified origin/master — its fixture lease is genuinely expired at the harness's real-clock now, unrelated).
- `server::tests::update_ha_state_*`: 13 passed. Go `9629|HARefresh|SessionHA`: passed.
- Details: `docs/log/14943.md`.
- Not run: live loss 60s `-P12` both-directions rig acceptance (requires the HA rig).

## Risk
Hot-path cost is one `BTreeMap` get on lease-carrying hits — no allocation. Resurrection touches only the matching-active fast path; CLEAR/membership/demotion paths are unchanged.

Closes #14943

## PR #15291 — userspace-dp: fuse cache-hit session probes and gate pre-cache neighbor learn (#14945) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14945-campaign`

Refs #14945 (perf partial — does not close it; live throughput acceptance still requires the loss rig).

## Why
#14945 adjudication (loss, e480baa5a4) refuted the RSS-imbalance theory and measured a per-packet CPU ceiling (~3.4µs/packet, IPC 0.72) with `SessionKey::hash` probes among the top hotspots. The flow-cache hit path paid 3–4 keyed hash probes per packet, and the pre-cache source-neighbor learn re-entered the sharded map on every packet even when the per-worker dedup state proved the pair unchanged inside its refresh interval.

## What
- **(A) Fused session probe**: `SessionTable::probe_hit(key, now_ns, len, tcp_flags, payload_len, dscp)` performs the liveness check, the throttled keepalive (#14939 handshake completion, #14935/#10885 closing gates) and the #2501/#2749 accounting under ONE `record_by_key_mut` borrow. Reverse packets keep the second companion probe exactly as `account_packet` did. `stage_flow_cache_hit` calls it once, replacing `session_is_live_at` + `touch_if_stale_with_payload` + `account_packet`. The TTL/hop-limit decision stays between the probe and the filter/policer/log replay; a would-expire packet takes a liveness-only probe so it is never refreshed, completed, or charged.
- **(B) Gated pre-cache learn**: `stage_parse_flow_and_learn` skips `learn_dynamic_neighbor_from_packet` when the `LearnedNeighborDedup` key (ingress ifindex, VLAN, src_ip, frame source MAC) matches and `RX_LEARNED_NEIGHBOR_REFRESH_INTERVAL_NS` has not elapsed. The dedup leg inside the learn remains the authority for epoch/key changes.

No behavior change except CPU: counters, liveness, handshake/closing semantics, and neighbor-map contents are identical.

## Validation
- New `session/probe_hit_14945_tests.rs`: 5 equivalence cells driving fused vs unfused oracle sequences (forward/reverse/translated-alias, fresh/stale throttle, absent/expired, handshake completion, RST/FIN closing gates) — all state snapshots identical.
- New `pre_cache_learn_skips_sharded_map_inside_dedup_interval_14945`: gated repeat does not recreate a removed neighbor entry nor advance `insert_generation`; post-interval learn recreates it.
- Session, poll_stages, flow_cache_hit, sharded_neighbor, neighbor_dispatch suites green (559+ tests, `--test-threads=1`).
- Pre-existing failure verified at base `e480baa5a4` by reverting this change: `gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615` fails identically without it.

## Risk
Accounting now lands under the probe borrow before the cached filter/policer replay; such packets were already keepalive-refreshed there, and forwarded-packet counters stay byte-identical (pinned by the equivalence cells). Live acceptance for #14945 (-P12 ≥22G v4 / ≥19G v6, retransmits near-zero) remains for the loss rig.

## Summary

Implements perf fix (3) from the #14945 adjudication: the flow-cache-hit inline TX path was gated on binding identity (`is_self_target`), so LAN→WAN transit never used it. Every transit hit detoured through `build_live_forward_request_from_frame` + `PendingForwardRequest` + `enqueue_pending_forwards`, which then discovered the shared UMEM and rewrote in place anyway.

- `stage_flow_cache_hit` now gates the inline path on the target binding sharing this worker's UMEM allocation (`WorkerUmem::allocation_ptr` equality, as `can_rewrite_in_place` in `tx/dispatch/mod.rs` tests) and hands the prepared TX to the target binding via the existing cross-binding prepared-TX plumbing (`InlineTxBindings` carrying the `poll_binding` split `left`/`right` slices from `worker/lifecycle.rs`, bounded with `bound_pending_tx_prepared`, target counters charged).
- The oversized/PMTUD/segmentation fallback (`flow_cache_hit_requires_pending_forward`), NAT64/native-tunnel and owned-frame exclusions, and the foreign-UMEM `PendingForwardRequest` detour are exactly as gated before; the completion recycle still targets the ingress slot via the shared-recycle path.
- Semantics-identical; no new allocation on the hit path.

## Validation

- New cells: `transit_cross_binding_shared_umem_takes_inline_path_14945` (cross-binding same-worker transit takes the inline path, lands on the target queue, no `scratch_forwards`, forwards byte-identically to the hairpin arm) and `transit_cross_binding_foreign_umem_keeps_pending_forward_14945` (foreign UMEM keeps the PendingForwardRequest detour, never a prepared offset into the ingress UMEM).
- `flow_cache_hit` suite: 60 passed; `tx::` suite: 209 passed (`--test-threads=1`).
- Pre-existing failure verified at base by stashing this change: `gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615` fails identically without it (already recorded in `docs/log/14945.md`).
- Log addendum appended to `docs/log/14945.md`.

## Risk

A prepared request now routinely lands on a sibling binding's queue from the cache-hit path; it carries an offset into the shared UMEM only when `allocation_ptr` equality holds, mirroring the dispatcher's `can_rewrite_in_place` and the #8916 neighbor-retry guard, and its `FillOnSlot(ingress)` recycle routes through the established shared-recycle completion path. Live throughput acceptance for #14945 (−P12 ≥22G v4 / ≥19G v6, retransmits near-zero) still requires the loss rig, so this references #14945 without closing it.

Refs #14945

## PR #15293 — nat: enforce generation-jump and peer caps on lease batch import (#14963) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14963-campaign`

Why:
ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch enforced neither cap that the forwarded-clear path already applied, so one forged or corrupted batch for a known peer at MaxUint64 advanced the durable watermark straight to MaxUint64: the importer cleared every local lease, persisted the poisoned high-water mark, and every genuine batch below it was dropped as stale indefinitely, surviving restart. Unbounded distinct origins also grew RemoteGenerations past the loader peer limit, so the state file failed to load on every restart and persistent-NAT lease export/import was bricked.

What:
In ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch, refuse a known-peer generation jump over maxPersistentNatGenerationJump14580 (counter + Warn, mirroring ClearPersistentNATLeasesWithGeneration) and refuse a new distinct origin at/over maxPersistentNatGenerationPeers11486. Unseen-origin first contact stays accepted at any generation, and the generation-0 no-barrier carve-out is preserved (cap applies to generation >= 1 advances). NOT changed: stale/local-clear fence handling, ImportIdleLeases helper boundary, or the clear path. New persistent_nat_generation_14963_test.go covers both refusals plus at-bound/unseen/known-at-cap controls; docs/log/14963.md records the change.

Validation:
Not run by the lane agent per campaign handoff discipline; main agent to run RED/GREEN: the new 14963 tests fail on origin/master (forged MaxUint64 batch accepted, 17th peer accepted) and pass with this fix, plus the 11486/14580 generation suites stay green.

Risk:
A known peer silent for >1024 clears then re-advertising is now refused until its generation is re-established, matching the existing forwarded-clear behaviour; accepted trade-off from #14580. Generation-0 first contact can still record 0-watermarks past the cap (no clear barrier, no lease wipe); bounded by the 30s sync cadence and the loader check on the durable file.

Closes #14963

## PR #15304 — userspace-dp: stop WG TunOrigin ICMPv6 session poisoning (#14958) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14958-campaign`

## Summary
`wg_tun_origin_packet_initiates` (tun_origin.rs) matched ICMP direction only for `PROTO_ICMP` (1). ICMPv6 is protocol 58 (`PROTO_ICMPV6`), so every ICMPv6 TUN packet fell to the directionless `_ => true` arm. An ICMPv6 Echo Reply (129) — the kernel's answer to an admitted peer→firewall Echo Request (128) — therefore counted as initiating and `publish_wg_tun_origin_entries` minted a `SessionOrigin::TunOrigin` pair. The synthesized reverse is the peer's Echo Request tuple as a LocalDelivery entry; a later unsolicited peer Echo Request HITs it and `tun_origin_reverse_exempt` skips host-inbound + junos-host NEW-session gates.

## Fix
One file, one function: split the ICMP arm.
- `PROTO_ICMP` → 8 | 13 (unchanged).
- `PROTO_ICMPV6` → 128 only. 128-only is deliberate: ICMPv6 has no timestamp query (133 is Router Solicitation), and the identifier-keyed parser yields no forward key for 133-137, so those types never reach the gate (test pins 137 → None).

Fail-closed: every other ICMPv6 type is non-initiating. UDP/other protocols keep documented directionless behaviour. Encap unchanged — the gate only gates publish.

## Regression
- `wg_tun_origin_icmpv6_reply_does_not_initiate_14958`: 128 → Some(true), 129 → Some(false), 137/1 → None.
- `wg_tun_origin_icmpv6_reply_publish_skips_14958`: production parse+build+publish of the 129 shape leaves shared/dedup/tombstones empty; 128 control creates all three.
- RED proven on mutant restoring master behaviour (ICMPv6 arm → `true`): both fail with `initiates(reply)==true`, 0 passed / 2 failed. Fix restored byte-identical, re-verified 19 wg_tun_origin cells green.
- Controls: full `wg_tun_origin_*` / `_10038` suite green. `tun_origin` filter: 28 passed, 2 pre-existing GRE env failures (`ha_inactive`) identical on two independent base binaries; diff touches tun_origin.rs only.

Closes #14958

## PR #15307 — dataplane: preserve tunnel-variant purge on session-store batch retry (#14965) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

`batchDeleteExactV4/V6` retry the tail per key with bare

dropping `RoutingDomain` and `PurgeTunnelVariants`; the userspace bare
delete re-derives scope from the surviving mirror row and can never
carry the purge flag, so a GRE0 policy-invalidation row deleted on the
recovery path exact-matches and leaks. `deletePeerBatchKnownExactV4/V6`

dataplanes without the capability. Peer forward/reverse scoped keys
carry `PurgeTunnelVariants` (set-matching uses the full key), and a
partial-batch error still retires applied entries' companions and
DNAT rows before returning the error. `Manager.DeleteSessionScoped[V6]`
sends a `mirror_delete` naming the caller scope + purge flag without
probing the mirror; `LegacyDataPlaneAdapter` forwards it. Compile-time
belts pin the capability on both published types
(`scoped_singular_delete_published_14965.go` /
`scoped_singular_delete_adapter_14965.go`). NOT changed: the bare
`DeleteSession` path (no scope to carry by construction) and the
RoutingDomain retry leg's #9146 self-scope behaviour for dataplanes
without the new capability.

included the missing key via bare retry; peer purge lost, companion
orphaned, 0 DNAT deletes) and pass after the fix

`scoped_singular_delete_14965_test.go`). `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/
./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean. Full affected suites: only two

`2a7bdd107b` (`TestOperatorPackagesDoNotImportBPFArtifactsDirectly`,
`TestTrunkWithNoUnitZeroPutsNoUnitRowOnTheParentIfindex_7509`).

Risk:
Dataplanes without the scoped singular capability keep the bare retry
(pre-existing behaviour). Peer partial-batch companion/DNAT retirement
is best-effort under the returned peer error.

## PR #15312 — config: refuse re-gated duplicate-policy folds on tolerant load (#14968) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14968-campaign-pub`

## Why

The tolerant #8752 duplicate-policy fold merges repeated `policy <name>`
statements into the first occurrence. #9571 refused a fold that turns a
restrictive statement into a merged PERMIT, but it compared only terminal
actions (D30-02, validated MATERIAL 3-way in research run `tpzkKgAuZL`).
Three re-gatings survived unpoisoned on `CompileConfigLenient` /
`CompileConfigForNodeLenient`:

- **Cross-product permit widening** — two PERMIT statements differing in
  ≥2 match dimensions fold into source-union × destination-union ×
  application-union, permitting combinations no statement permitted.
- **Excluded-set deny disarming** — an excluded-address flag/list from
  one statement is OR-ed/unioned onto a surviving deny, which then
  matches the complement and no longer covers traffic its own statement
  denied.
- **Scheduler narrowing** — a `scheduler-name` from one statement is
  inherited last-wins by an unconditional surviving deny, narrowing it
  to that window.

## What

- `mergeInstancesUnder` (`pkg/config/dup_instance_merge_8752.go`) captures
  every source statement's compiled policy (`compilePolicy`, the #9571
  reader) before folding; after the fold,
  `foldChangesPolicySemantics14968` compares the merged policy against
  the statements and poisons non-union folds via the existing
  `LenientContentDropped` mechanism (snapshot refused, previous-good
  retained, fresh-boot default-deny). The #9571 action leg is preserved;
  a `semantic` flag selects the `#14968` warning in both compiler entry
  points.
- NOT changed: the fold itself, strict-commit gates (#3473/#14449),
  scheduler definitions, and folds whose merged semantics are the union
  of the statements (single-dimension permit differences, identical
  excluded sets, one shared scheduler) — pinned unpoisoned by controls.
- Docs: `docs/log/14968.md`, `pkg/config/README.md`,
  `pkg/config/types_security.go`.

## Validation

- RED on base `b8f1ff7ac9`: new rows in
  `pkg/config/dup_policy_fold_crossproduct_14968_test.go` (cross-product
  zone-pair/global/source×application, excluded-set, scheduler) failed
  with nothing poisoning the merged policy on both lenient entry points.
- GREEN after the fix, including five semantics-preserving controls; the
  #9571/#9992/#11063/#12820/#14449 fold suites and downstream
  `pkg/policymatch` + `pkg/dataplane/userspace` fold-widening suites
  pass; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean.
- Two wider-suite failures (`TestDuplicateTriggerUntilTakesTheLastValue6771`,
  `TestFlatSetChainWalkRatchet8939`) reproduce identically on pristine

## PR #15313 — ipsec: capture VRF-enslaved st0 in divert, scope host-input fence to tunnel slaves (#14974) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14974-campaign`

Closes #14974

## Mechanism (D32-01)
A routing-instance member `st0.<N>` enslaved to a VRF (e.g. `vrf-blue`) presents `iifname=vrf-blue` and `meta sdifname=st0.0` at forward/input. Two defects followed:
- `inet xpf_ipsec_divert` emitted only `iifname "st0.0"` queue rules — never matching enslaved ingress, so IPsec capture was bypassed.
- `HostInputFenceOverlay` resolved the xfrmi `MasterIndex` to the VRF name and emitted a bare `iifname "vrf-blue"` DROP — fencing every co-member of the VRF, not just the tunnel.

## Fix
- `IpsecDivertRule.Master` / `ipsecQueueKey.Master`: `buildIpsecCaptureQueuePlan` resolves the master from the live link `MasterIndex` via `ipsecFenceLinkByIndex` (unresolvable → fail-closed quarantine, no keys); `emitIpsecDivertRules` renders `iifname <master> meta sdifname <tunnel>` + queue. Unenslaved rules are byte-identical.
- `HostInputFenceOverlay` gains `SlaveSet`/`MasterSlavePairs` (canonicalised, bound into the counter marker). `ipsecHostInputFenceOverlayForPermit` emits `(vrf-blue, st0.0)` pairs instead of bare VRF masters; unenslaved tunnels stay bare masters. Both renderers (netlink `buildHostInboundNetlink` and text oracle in `daemon_nft.go`) emit `iifname "vrf-blue" meta sdifname "st0.0" … drop` per pair; `VerifyHostInboundOverlay`/`decodeHostOverlayRule` verify the iifname+sdifname unions.
- `ipsecDivertSpecMasters9506` returns tunnel slave names so a divert-transition hold cannot fence the whole VRF.

## Tests
- RED on `origin/master` (detached worktree, tests only): both 14974 test files fail (missing `Master`/`SlaveSet`/`MasterSlavePairs`/`HostInputFencePair`, iifname-only shapes).
- GREEN: `TestIpsecDivertVRFEnslavedCapture14974`, `TestIpsecDivertUnenslavedUnchanged14974`, `TestHostInputFenceOverlayScopedToTunnel14974`, `TestHostInputFenceOverlayUnenslavedUnchanged14974`, `TestIpsecCaptureDivertSpecVRFEnslaved14974`, `TestIpsecCaptureQueuePlanResolvesVRFMaster14974` (incl. unresolvable-master quarantine control), `TestIpsecHostInputFenceOverlayVRFScoped14974` (mixed enslaved st0.0 + unenslaved st1).
- Adjacent: full `pkg/nftables` suite pass; daemon `TestIpsecCapture|TestHostInputFence|TestIpsecHost|TestIpsecPermit|TestRIMember` and netlink-parity suites pass.

Docs: `docs/log/14974.md`.

## PR #15315 — upgrade: preserve kernel-roll leases and rejoin on transient fence loss (#14992) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14992-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes D38-04 (#14992): `cmd_kernel_roll` stranded a drained node on a transient fence loss.

- `_fence_before_mutate` collapsed an UNCONFIRMABLE lease (peer SSH blip — no successor proved) into `lost_lease`, so the `finally` skipped the restore-forwarding rejoin; it then unconditionally deleted both `/var/lib/xpf/kernel-roll.lease` files. A deleted lease reads `leaseNone` in Go `KernelSelfRecovery.Tick` — a permanent no-op — permanently disabling self-recovery on the drained node.
- Fix: `_fence_before_mutate` gains an `on_unreachable` callback (invoked only on the unconfirmable branch; `on_lost` keeps its legacy both-outcomes behaviour when not supplied — the fence itself stays fail-closed on both outcomes, and no other caller changes). `cmd_kernel_roll` passes it, so only a PROVEN loss (fence `LOST` / keepalive) suppresses the finally rejoin (#5816 preserved).
- Fix: the `finally` now PRESERVES both leases whenever the roll drained the node and did not complete (mirroring `image-roll`'s never-both-down stance), leaving them to expire so the expired-lease `KernelSelfRecovery` fingerprint can fire. Clean success, pre-drain aborts, dry-run, and drained-but-rebooted rolls still release.

Scope: `scripts/deploy` only, per the issue's binding scope narrowing. The cited Go symbols needed no change — the defect was the Python finally destroying the lease state the Go machine correctly keys on.

## Tests
- New `KernelRollTransientFenceLossTests` + `FenceUnreachableCallbackTests` in `scripts/deploy/test_xpf_deploy_lease_renew_fence.py`, with a lease-state-tracking backend (assertions measure real lease presence, not mocks of the code under test).
- RED on `origin/master`: finally skipped the rejoin (`verbs == [('fw0','drain')]`) and deleted both leases; `on_unreachable` unsupported.
- GREEN here: drain + restore rejoin, `clears == []`, both leases present; proven-loss control keeps #5816 no-rejoin; arm-failure control rejoins and preserves.
- Adjacent suites green (81 tests): `test_xpf_deploy_lease_renew_fence`, `test_xpf_deploy_kernel_roll`, `test_xpf_deploy_correctness`, `test_xpf_deploy_recreate_keepalive_6762`, `test_xpf_deploy_daemon_hold_7559`.

Docs: `docs/in-place-upgrade.md` fence/lease-disposition paragraphs updated; `docs/log/14992.md` added.

Closes #14992

## Summary

Implements #14985 (D36-05, surviving leg only): `POST /api/v1/config/confirm` — and the gRPC `ConfirmCommit` twin, which share `Store.ConfirmCommitAs` — could be driven by a session that never held the config lock.

Mechanism: `ConfirmCommitAs` gated on `ensureHolderLocked`, whose `!configDir` and empty-holder bypasses are correct for candidate mutators but fail-open for confirm. A pending commit-confirmed window survives `ExitConfigure`, and leaving config mode is the routine post-`commit confirmed` state — so after the owner exited, any well-formed REST session token could cancel another operator's auto-rollback and make an unconfirmed config permanent.

Fix (one check in `ConfirmCommitAs`, same `s.mu` acquisition): when a window is pending and the caller is session-scoped, the caller must be the recorded effective holder, else `ErrConfigLockedByOther` (REST 409 / gRPC PermissionDenied). Internal (`""`) callers keep their bypass; the no-pending-window error is unchanged; holder confirms are byte-identical.

Excluded per the issue's binding scope narrowing (not reintroduced): the commit lock-turnover TOCTOU (already closed by the #6808 epoch-bound `CommitAuthority`) and the regex sub-leg (confirm carries no config path for `*-configuration` regexes to adjudicate).

## Validation

- RED on master `3d5bc4cd6c`: `StrangerAfterOwnerExit` — stranger REST confirm returned **200** and cleared the window.
- GREEN after fix: **409**, window still pending; controls `OwnerWhileHoldingLock` and `RESTHolderConfirmsOwnWindow` green before and after.
- Targeted `pkg/configstore` holder/confirm/commit-confirmed cells: ok (222s). `pkg/api` config/confirm surface: ok (43s). `go vet` + `gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/configstore` suite exceeded the 600s lane sandbox timeout (unrelated goroutine dump in `TestConcurrentMasterKeyCreateConverges_9898` at the tail). **Main agent: please run full `pkg/configstore`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/cli` suites before merge.**

Closes #14985

## PR #15321 — daemon: enforce faillock on root, ignore comment mentions, and strip managed PAM rules on rollback (#14973) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14973-campaign`

Closes #14973

## Why
`applySSHPAMFaillock` (D31-05) had three defects: the managed `pam_faillock.so` lines lacked `even_deny_root`, so root password guessing was never locked out; a comment in `/etc/pam.d/common-auth` merely mentioning `pam_faillock.so` was mistaken for an administrator-installed policy and silently suppressed the managed install; and `applySSHConfig` never stripped the managed PAM rules when a later step failed, leaving lockout policy behind after a failed apply.

## What
- Add `even_deny_root` to the managed preauth/authfail/authsucc lines.
- Decide "admin already has faillock" via `hasActivePAMFaillock`: only non-comment, non-blank PAM lines whose module field is `pam_faillock.so` (or a path ending in it) count. Real admin rules still suppress install; comment mentions no longer do.
- `applySSHConfig` records whether its faillock step changed `common-auth` and, via a deferred check on the final named result, strips the managed rules on any failure (drop-in write, `sshd -t` validate, reload, drop-in/legacy removal, sshd-config render) through `setSSHPAMFaillock(false)`. No-op when this apply changed nothing, so pre-existing admin faillock is never removed.
- Managed-block upgrade compatibility: pre-#14973 bodies (without `even_deny_root`) are recognised as known-good variants in `stripPAMFaillockBlock`, so hosts already carrying the old rules upgrade in place (strip + re-add) and remain strippable on rollback, instead of failing every apply as "modified". Tampered bodies are still refused.

## Validation
- New `pkg/daemon/ssh_faillock_14973_test.go`: `even_deny_root` enforcement; comment-mention install (comment preserved, idempotent) with real-admin-rule control; legacy-rule upgrade to byte-identical fresh install, legacy strip, tampered-body refusal; `applySSHConfig` rollback on reload, validate, drop-in-write, and content-build failures, plus success-keeps-rules control.
- Targeted: `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 14973|Faillock|11492 -count=1` — ok (includes existing #11492 tests: stock install, idempotence/reversibility, custom stack untouched, appliance skip).
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean.

## Risk
A failed SSH apply on non-appliance hosts rewrites `common-auth` once more to remove rules it just installed; a failing strip is logged and joined into the apply error, never masking the original failure. Appliance hosts, admin-installed faillock, and unsupported PAM stacks are untouched. No wire or config-schema change.

## PR #15322 — dhcp: gate DHCPv6 REBIND teardown on granting server (#14997) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14997-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes D40-03 (#14997): `v6RenewMatcher` accepted a DHCPv6 REBIND Reply from any server on transaction-ID + client-DUID alone (the #14600 RFC 8415 §18.2.5 any-server arm), and the run loop trusted its contents to tear down state — an IA_PD `NoPrefixAvail` cleared every held delegation (`pdRefused` arm), a valid-lifetime-0 IA_NA deconfigured the WAN address (`errV6AddrInvalidated`), and a valid-lifetime-0 IAPREFIX withdrew that prefix. Any on-link host that learned the transaction ID and client DUID (both observable on-link; the REBIND is multicast) could tear down the WAN lease and the whole IA_PD delegation with one spoofed packet at T2.

## Fix

Matcher-layer, fail-closed, in `pkg/dhcp`:

- `renew.go`: in REBIND, a Reply from a non-granting server is rejected when it carries teardown content (`v6ReplyTearsDownHeldBinding`: non-Success status at message or requested-IA level, valid-lifetime-0 IAADDR/IAPREFIX in a requested IA). Pure extensions from a failover partner still pass and become the next RENEW binding (#14600 preserved). RENEW is unchanged. RFC basis: §18.2.5 any-server Rebind covers bindings the server actually has; §18.2.10/§21 forbid a different server replacing the binding mid-renewal.
- `dhcp.go`: `RenewalBindingStats` gains `DHCPv6TeardownRejects` for observability.
- `README.md` + `docs/log/14997.md`: extension/teardown split documented, including why DHCPv4 needs no twin (partner NAK in REBINDING is the documented #14600 RFC 2131 §4.3.2 behaviour; v4 has no PD set).

Not changed: `parseV6ReplyChecked`, `extractDelegatedPrefixes`, `reconcileDelegatedPDs`, run-loop arms, acquisition/stateless matchers, DHCPv4, and the synthesis-refuted negative-status parser sub-leg. A granting server's teardown on RENEW/REBIND is byte-for-byte the pre-fix behaviour.

## Validation

- New `dhcpv6_rebind_teardown_14997_test.go`: five destructive REBIND cells from an attacker DUID RED on base (matcher accepted, counter 0) and RED-on-revert with the gate stashed; GREEN with the fix. Controls: partner/granting extension accepted end-to-end (held address kept, partner DUID stored, PD extended), granting teardown on REBIND/RENEW accepted, partner RENEW teardown identity-rejected.
- `go test ./pkg/dhcp/... -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/dhcp/` clean; gofmt / `git diff --check` clean.

## Risk

A failed-over partner that genuinely holds no binding now has its `NoBinding` Reply ignored at T2; the client keeps the binding until the partner grants an extension or the lease expires into a fresh Solicit (RFC 8415 §18.2.10 posture). No lab failover-pair capture; the gate is at the unit-tested matcher seam and the run loop is unchanged for accepted Replies.

Closes #14997

Branch: `fix/14998-campaign`

Why:
A co-held IA_NA+IA_PD RENEW/REBIND Reply whose IA_NA IAADDRs are all
valid-lifetime 0 (RFC 8415 §18.2.10.1 explicit invalidation) bypassed
`errV6AddrInvalidated` when a live IA_PD was present: parse returned an
address-less success lease (`LeaseTime` from the PD / 3600s floor),
`commitLease` stored it without removing the held kernel WAN address,
and timers re-derived from the bogus lease — orphaning the WAN address.
A delegated-prefix expiry interrupting the T1/T2 wait also restarted the
full tier wait on every prune (Path A only; Path B past-expiry stays
bounded by the lease deadline).

What:
- `parseV6ReplyChecked` fires `errV6AddrInvalidated` whenever the IA_NA
  is explicitly invalidated, regardless of co-held live PDs, so the run
  loop deconfigures via `abandonLeaseAfterExpiry`.
- `commitLease` removes the previous address whenever it differs from
  the committed address — including an address-less successor — before
  applying the new one.
- `runDHCPv6` anchors T1/T2 to `Obtained`-derived absolute instants and
  resumes after a PD prune via the new `remainingTimer` helper.
- Regression: `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6_coheld_invalidate_14998_test.go`; contract:
  `pkg/dhcp/README.md`; log: `docs/log/14998.md`.

Validation:

commit test `removed=[]` want `[prev]`; PD-prune test post-prune T1 wait
`#2 = 20s` want remaining ~1s. GREEN: targeted
`go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -run '14998|5927|13559|14598|CommitLease|RenewalTimers' -count=1`
passed; full `go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1` passed; race subset passed;
`go vet ./pkg/dhcp/` and gofmt clean.

## PR #15331 — cli: stop global InConfigMode escalating read-only users to PermConfig (#14986) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14986-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes D37-01 (#14986): `(*CLI).dispatch` routed every line to `dispatchConfig` whenever the store-global `InConfigMode()` was true, and every config mutation used `sessionID == ""`. Any holder (gRPC/REST/daemon) flipping that global flag let a local `read-only`/`unauthorized`/`operator` console user `set`/`delete`/`load`/`commit` with full `PermConfig` effect, bypassing `configure exclusive`.

## What
- `dispatch` now routes to config mode only when this CLI session itself passed the gated `configure` verb (`configOwned`); otherwise mutating verbs are priced at `PermConfig` via `checkPermission(["configure"])` (`checkConfigModePerm`, also enforced in `dispatchConfig` and `handleCommit`), view affordances (`show`/`?`/`help`/`exit`/`quit`) stay available, and a candidate held by another session refuses mutation/commit.
- `configure`/`configure exclusive` acquire via `EnterConfigureSession(local-cli)` / `EnterConfigureExclusive(local-cli)`; session-scoped mutators (`Set/Delete/Activate/Deactivate/Rollback/Annotate/Copy/Rename/Insert/Load*`, `ConfirmCommitAs`) pass that holder instead of `""`. Config-mode `exit` only releases a lock this session owns. Unset-class legacy no-RBAC mode unchanged.

## PR #15332 — daemon: take apply semaphore and fresh snapshot in management-only DHCP lease-change IPsec reapply (#14976) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14976-campaign`

Fixes the management-only DHCP lease-change IPsec reapply (D33-04, #14976).

## Defect
`onDHCPAddressChange`'s management-only branch called `applyMgmtVRFRoutes()` **without `applySem`** and passed both gated rebinds (`reapplyIPsecForLeaseChange`, `rebindWebMgmtForLeaseChange`) the `activeCfg` snapshot captured **before** any semaphore wait. A commit removing the DHCP-bound IPsec gateway (and its PSKs) during the wait was silently resurrected into swanctl; a just-added gateway was never re-bound. The #6716 inversion on the one callback #6716 missed.

## Fix
- New `managementOnlyLeaseRefresh()` owns the branch: acquires `applySem` once, runs the management-VRF route reconcile (new `mgmtRouteRefreshFn` seam), re-reads `store.ActiveConfig()` **after** acquiring, and evaluates both gated rebinds against that fresh snapshot under the single hold. Fail-closed: nil fresh config → rebinds skipped; route failures still latch #11450 debt.
- `reapplyIPsecLocked` / `rebindWebMgmtLocked` hold gate+apply under held sem. Legacy acquiring entry points preserved for the #4899 retry loop and direct callers.
- DNS keeps its own acquisition after the hold (nested takes deadlock; DNS merges live leases, not the gated snapshot).
- Wiring pins updated for the moved spellings (#14582, #11450).

## Regression
- `TestMgmtOnlyLeaseRefreshUsesFreshSnapshotAndSerializesRoutes14976` — drives the real `onDHCPAddressChange` through the management-only branch; route seam lands a real gateway-deleting commit mid-refresh (deterministic, no sleeps). **RED on `origin/master`: "management-VRF route reconcile ran WITHOUT applySem held"; GREEN after fix** (`ok pkg/daemon 1.139s`).
- `TestMgmtOnlyLeaseRefreshStillRebindsLiveGateway14976` — control: no intervening commit → exactly one rebind of the live gateway.
- Adjacent suites green post-rebase: `TestReapplyIPsecForLeaseChange|TestWebMgmtDHCP|TestMgmtRoute|IPsecRebind`.

See `docs/log/14976.md`.

Closes #14976

## PR #15333 — daemon: block symlink traversal through user-writable .ssh in login apply and deprovision (#14970) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14970-campaign`

Closes #14970

## Why
`/home/<user>/.ssh` is writable by the login user while the daemon acts on it as root (D31-02, Critical):
- `applySystemLogin` ran `os.Chown` on the `.ssh` path — follows a planted symlink, re-owning the **target directory**.
- `fsatomic.WriteFileDurable(authorized_keys)` created its temp file inside the (symlinked) directory and renamed it over the target's file — root **overwrite of an arbitrary path**.
- The emptied-key revocation (`applySystemLogin` else-branch) and `deprovisionLoginUser` ran `os.Remove(managedAuthorizedKeysPath)` — unlinks the **resolved victim file** when `.ssh` is a symlink.

## What
- `pkg/daemon/login_password.go`: `checkSSHPathNotSymlink` (Lstat; absent is not a refusal, other errors fail closed), `ensureSSHDirSafeForWrite`, and `removeManagedAuthorizedKeys` (refuses a symlinked `.ssh`/`authorized_keys` instead of deleting the resolved file; raw `os.Remove` error otherwise so `IsNotExist` handling is unchanged).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go`: key-install leg checks before `MkdirAllDurable`/`Chown` and again immediately before `WriteFileDurable` (key claim rolled back on refusal); emptied-key revoke uses the guarded removal (refusal → fail + marker retained).
- `deprovisionLoginUser` key removal uses the guarded removal (refusal → markers kept, retry next apply).
- Root's `/root/.ssh` is root-writable only and intentionally untouched. Docs: `docs/system-login.md` + `docs/log/14970.md`.

## Validation
- New `pkg/daemon/login_ssh_symlink_14970_test.go`: 4 regressions (symlinked `.ssh` on apply, symlinked `authorized_keys` on apply, symlinked `.ssh` on deprovision, symlinked `.ssh` on emptied-key revoke) **fail on unmodified origin/master**, pass after the fix; legitimate-path control passes before and after.
- Adjacent host-auth suites pass (`TestApplySystemLogin|TestReconcileAbsentLoginUsers|TestDeprovision|EmptiedKeys|TestApplyRootAuth|RootAuth`); `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean; full `pkg/daemon` suite shows only the pre-existing `TestRunStartupGoodbyeKeepsDistinctIdentityWithdraw10789` failure, identical on pristine `origin/master`.

## Risk
A pre-existing operator-planted symlinked `.ssh` now fails the login apply closed until replaced with a real directory; legitimate trees unaffected. A link swapped between the Lstat check and the operation is a TOCTOU residual of the same class accepted by the repo's other Lstat-then-act guards (#8482, #9897).

## Summary

`AuthorizeCommitAs` minted `authorityInternal` for a named session that passed `ensureHolderLocked` only via the `!configDir` / empty-holder bypasses, and `ForceExitConfigure` did not mark the evicted holder reclaimed. ## PR #15338 — frr: enable BFD before binding its profile on OSPFv2 and IS-IS (#15015) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15015-campaign`

## Summary

An OSPFv2 or IS-IS interface configured with `bfd-liveness-detection minimum-interval`/`multiplier` rendered only a profile binding (` ip ospf bfd profile xpf-<i>-<m>` / ` isis bfd profile xpf-<i>-<m>`) with no bare enable line. In FRR 10.6 neither profile line enables BFD monitoring by itself, so commit and frr-reload reported success while no BFD session ever ran; convergence silently fell back to the OSPF dead interval / IS-IS hold time.

Primary-source verification against FRR frr-10.6.0:

- OSPFv2 (`ospfd/ospf_bfd.c`): the `ip ospf bfd profile` DEFUN refuses with "ip ospf bfd has not been set" (CMD_WARNING) unless `ip ospf bfd` already allocated `bfd_config`; `ospf_bfd_write_config` prints ` ip ospf bfd` before the profile line. FRR docs: the profile command "Only takes effect if `ip ospf bfd` command is also present."
- IS-IS (`isisd/isis_cli.c`, `isis_nb_config.c`, `isis_bfd.c`): `isis bfd profile` sets only the `bfd-monitoring/profile` leaf; the `enabled` leaf is set solely by `isis bfd`, and `bfd_handle_adj_up` skips circuits with `enabled=false`. `cli_show_ip_isis_bfd_monitoring` prints ` isis bfd` first.

NOT changed (verified self-enabling): OSPFv3 (`ipv6 ospf6 bfd [profile ...]` is a single DEFUN setting `enabled=true`) and BGP (`neighbor X bfd profile` is documented as "Same as `neighbor X bfd`").

## Changes

- `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go`: emit ` ip ospf bfd\n` / ` isis bfd\n` immediately before the profile line in the OSPFv2 and IS-IS interface loops when custom timers select a profile; the IS-IS pair stays inside the interface block before `exit` (#2942). Bare-BFD branch byte-identical.
- `pkg/frr/bfd_profile_enable_15015_test.go` (new): `TestBFDProfileEnableLines15015`.
- `pkg/frr/README.md`, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/15015.md`.

## Validation

- `TestBFDProfileEnableLines15015`: **RED on base `299c7b6a29`** (profile line rendered alone, no enable line, for OSPFv2 300/3, IS-IS 250/4, and the interval-only cell), **GREEN after the fix**. Controls: bare BFD = exactly one enable line and no profile binding (both protocols); interval-only OSPFv2 gets the pair; no-BFD renders nothing.
- Adjacent suites green: `TestGenerateProtocols_OSPFBFD`, `_BGPBFD`, `_OSPFv3BFD`, `_OSPFv3BFDProfile`, `TestBuildManagedSection_SingleGlobalBFDBlock`, `TestGenerateProtocols_ISISBFDInsideInterfaceBlock`.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: 3 failures (`TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426`, `TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374`) reproduce identically with the fix stashed on the same tree — base-attributed at `299c7b6a29`, unrelated BGP neighbor-family tests.

Lab acceptance (BFD session visible in `show ip ospf interface` / IS-IS running-config on the loss cluster) remains an operator-side verify; the render contract is pinned by the regression test.

## PR #15340 — ddns: reject cross-family sibling claims without wire DHCID proof (#14995) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14995-campaign`

Why: crossTypeSiblingOwned matched only on canonical FQDN plus
opposite address family. A bare unauthenticated DHCP REQUEST that
merely named a victim's hostname from the other family therefore
entered the ownership store as a trusted sibling; upsertLocked
stamped SiblingFamilyOwned and the RFC 2136 backend downgraded
the claim to a per-type RRsetNotUsed guard, publishing a foreign
A/AAAA plus a second DHCID at the victim's name (RFC 4701 allows
one DHCID RR per owner name) and recording phantom ownership
whose later release aimed the DHCID prerequisite at the victim.

What: demote the store to a candidate source and make the wire
the proof. crossTypeSiblingOwned now returns the sibling record
narrowed to same scope modulo family and same backend endpoint;
upsertLocked threads its ClientID as SiblingClientID, and
reconcileOnceLocked stamps PairedClientID for a same-device
sibling desired in the same pass. pairedIdentityKey/sameDeviceClient
pair only provably same-device identities (verbatim-equal, or a
MAC-based DUID against the v4 MAC/Ethernet client-id).
dhcidDigestClientID canonicalizes the digest to the device, so
one device writes one identical DHCID RR across both families;
dhcidSharedWithOther/dhcidStillWanted compare device digests.
proveSiblingDHCID requires the sibling's exact DHCID on the wire
before any per-type downgrade in sendAddOwned/sendAdd; unproven
claims fall through to the unchanged name-level guards and are
refused with errDDNSConflictRefused. Deletes are untouched.
skip-existing publishes the device marker once per updater as
the sibling proof target. Strengthened the #14602/#14604/#2700
fixtures to a genuinely paired device (Ethernet client-id plus
DUID-LL embedding the same MAC); opaque fixtures fail closed.

Validation: new cross_family_hijack_14995_test.go cells fail on
origin/master 291ddb0066 (foreign A/AAAA published under
replace-owned and skip-existing) and pass after the fix (refused,
no foreign DHCID, no phantom ownership, victim untouched).
go test ./pkg/ddns -count=1 PASS; go test ./pkg/dhcpserver
-count=1 PASS; go vet clean.

Risk: records published before the device canonicalization carry
the legacy per-identity digest, so their guarded delete is a
counted skip (ownership dropped; stale RR remains for the
operator, documented in pkg/ddns/README.md). Opaque cross-family
pairings that cannot prove same-device fail closed (second
family refused) rather than hijackable.

Closes #14995

## PR #15341 — frr: fail closed on OSPF key with no authentication-type (#15014) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15014-campaign`

Closes #15014

## Mechanism (A12-02 surviving leg)

#14977 added a renderer guard omitting an OSPF interface whose `AuthType == ""` but `AuthKey != ""`. The guard was dead: the renderer reads the **unioned** interface (`config.OSPFInterfaceUnion12186.Merge`, #12186), and `Merge` only copied `AuthKey` under a matched `simple`/`md5` type. A key carried with no type — the foreign/tolerant construction the guard was written for (persisted pre-gate config, HA peer sync, rollback; strict commit refuses a bare OSPF `authentication-key`, #14402) — was dropped by the union, so the interface rendered `ip ospf area` with zero auth lines: an unauthenticated adjacency.

The other two A12-02 probes (OSPF `simple` with an unrenderable key; IS-IS area/interface passwords with an unrenderable key and IS-IS keyless type) were already withheld by #14977; they are pinned as regression controls in the new test file so they cannot regress.

## Fix

`OSPFInterfaceUnion12186.Merge` now preserves the first typeless key as auth-configured evidence (a differing second key is a field-name-only conflict; no type is invented, the key is never emitted or logged), so the existing #14977 guard withholds the interface. Typed fragments keep their own key handling. One predicate — "auth configured but no renderable auth line" — now reaches every A12-02 probe.

## Tests

- RED on `origin/master`: `TestOSPFKeyWithNoTypeDoesNotActivate15014`, `TestOSPFKeyWithNoTypeSplitFragments15014` (both rendered `ip ospf area 0.0.0.0` with no auth lines).
- GREEN after: all `15014` tests pass, with byte-identical keyed/plain controls (keyed simple/md5 OSPF, plain OSPF, keyed/plain IS-IS, healthy IS-IS sibling + global).
- `pkg/config` union tests pass; gofmt/go vet clean.

Main agent should run the full `pkg/frr` and `pkg/config` suites once.

## Risk

A tolerant-loaded OSPF config with a typeless key now loses that adjacency loudly (renderer slog) instead of forming it unauthenticated. Strict-valid configs cannot carry the shape and are unaffected byte-for-byte.

## PR #15343 — policy: fail closed on fragment-no-L4 sentinel against protocol-only deny/reject (#14956) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14956-campaign`

Closes #14956

## Summary
Fail closed on the fragment-no-L4 sentinel (`SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, 255) against protocol-only DENY/REJECT rules (D24-02 leg 1, 3-way MATERIAL in research run `tpzkKgAuZL`).

A protocol-only application term (no port, no ICMP type/code constraint — e.g. `protocol udp`, compiled as an empty-range `range_terms` entry) matches on the known protocol alone, so for a known protocol the flowless path decides it via `CompiledApplications::matches`. For sentinel 255 the protocol is unknown: `matches()` missed (no `by_protocol[255]` entry) and `has_l4_constrained_term` also missed (empty ranges are not L4-constrained; its 255 arm only scans port/ICMP constraints), so a protocol-only DENY/REJECT was never recorded as a skipped fragment deny in `try_match_rule`. The fragment fell through to a later permit, a default-permit, or the junos-host deliver-on-no-match fall-through — fail open.

## Changes
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs`: add `CompiledApplications::has_any_protocol_term` (true iff some protocol carries an empty-range protocol-only term; `match_any` excluded since `application any` direct-matches the sentinel first) and OR it, gated on `protocol == SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, into the `FragmentDenyOverlap` classification in `try_match_rule`. ## PR #15344 — eventengine: re-arm trigger on 1 on window decay (#15020) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15020-campaign`

Why:
withinMatches decided the #3756 edge-latch re-arm with the in-window
count including the current event, which evaluateEvent appends to the
window before calling it. For `within N { trigger on 1; }` that count
is >= 1 by construction on every event, so `counts[i] < wc.TriggerOn`
never held: once the first crossing armed rt.onLatched, no later event
could clear it. The policy fired exactly once per daemon lifetime (the
runtime is carried across same-revision Apply, and releaseEdgeLatch
runs only on non-admission), so the shipped lab pair
failover-on-probe-fail / restore-on-probe-success in
test/incus/xpf-test.conf went dead after its first outage cycle.

What:
pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go: test the count excluding the current
event (counts[i]-1 < wc.TriggerOn), so the latch re-arms exactly when
the ANDed condition was false before this event arrived — for N=1,
when no prior occurrence remains inside the window. The old re-arm
`return false` is split into an explicit inclusive count gate
(counts[i] < wc.TriggerOn -> no fire) so the latch mutation stays
distinct from the firing decision. Comments in evaluate.go,
engine.go (onLatched), and README.md updated to the pre-event
formulation; regression in engine_trigger_on1_rearm_15020_test.go.
NOT changed: queue.go releaseEdgeLatch, cooldown arming, Apply
carry-over, pruneWindow, and trigger-until semantics — for N>1 the
observable behaviour is unchanged (a sustained burst's pre-event
count stays >= N until decay; below-threshold events never fire).

Validation:
New TestTriggerOn1_*_15020 cells drive the real evaluateEvent path
on a deterministic clock. RED on pre-fix tree: isolated edges fired
1/2, lab-pair alternation fired failover 1/2 across two outages,
sustained-then-decayed fired 1/2; the multi-clause AND cell passed
pre-fix as an adjacent control. GREEN post-fix: all four pass.
Adjacent controls green: TestEdgeTriggerOn_*_3756,
TestWithinTriggerOnRearmIsIndependentOfClauseOrder,
TestWithinSingleTriggerOnKeepsEdgeSemantics,
TestWithinMultipleClausesAreANDed, TestInclusiveUntil_*_3756.
Full go test ./pkg/eventengine/ -count=1: only the 9 pre-existing
*6673* failures, reproduced identically on the base tree with the
fix stashed (base-attributed). go vet clean; gofmt clean.

Risk:
Behaviour changes only for trigger-on policies whose window has
fully decayed since the last occurrence — trigger on 1 now fires
per isolated edge instead of never. Sustained-level suppression,
cooldown interaction, multi-clause AND/order independence, and all
fail-closed belts are unchanged. Lab config needs no change.

## PR #15345 — frr: require all community members to match (#15008) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15008-campaign`

Why: `policy-options community X members [ a b ]` rendered one
`bgp community-list ... permit` line per member. FRR's
`community_list_match` returns on the first permit entry contained in
a route, so `from community X` matched a route carrying ANY one member
instead of ALL — Junos requires every member to match ("The evaluation
of all members must be successful for the named community evaluation to
be successful"). An accept term over-accepts on import, a reject term
over-rejects, and non-terminal actions hit the wrong routes for every
multi-member community.

What: in `pkg/frr/policy_render.go` the public name now renders as ONE
conjunctive permit entry — all literals space-joined on a `standard`
line (FRR `community_match` requires every value of the entry present),
or one `expanded` positive-lookahead conjunction over the joined sorted
community string with literal members anchored to whole tokens
(`(^| )m( |$)`) so `65000:100` cannot match inside `65000:1000` or
across a token boundary. Single-member/empty renders byte-identical,
duplicates collapse. `then community delete` targets a generated
per-member backing (`<frrName>-xpf-del-<digest>`) because the AND entry
strips nothing per-value under FRR `community_list_match_delete`;
`communityListCollision` (wired into `ApplyFull`) fails the apply closed
on FRR-name/backing collisions. Existing community tests updated to the
joined spelling. NOT changed: `invert-match` (never modelled), resolved
add/set literals (#12069), tolerant-path dangling delete.

Validation: new `policy_community_multi_15008_test.go` (4 tests):
RED on the reverted renderer (per-member OR lines, no conjunction,
delete against the public name), GREEN after the fix; updated
`TestGeneratePolicyOptionsCommunityListAndMetricType` /
`TestGeneratePolicyOptionsCommunityExpandedVsStandard` pass; full
`pkg/frr` suite shows only the three pre-existing BGP-family failures
(`TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`,
`TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374`,
`TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426`) also present on pristine
`origin/master`; `go vet ./pkg/frr/` clean. FRR semantics cited from
stable/10.6 `bgp_clist.c`/`bgp_community.c`; docs in `docs/log/15008.md`.

Risk: multi-member `from community` terms now match strictly fewer
routes (ALL instead of ANY) — the Junos-correct outcome; a new
`<name>-xpf-del-<digest>` list appears in frr.conf for multi-member
definitions and their delete clauses point at it. Anchored regex
members in a multi-member definition keep whole-string `^`/`$` meaning
under the conjunction, which can be stricter than Junos per-value
matching; single regex members are unchanged.

Closes #15008

## PR #15348 — configstore: stop rollback rebind blessing stale disk bytes (#15023) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15023-campaign`

Closes #15023

## Defect (A19-01)
`rebindRollbackMetadataLocked` (#14578) hashed whatever bytes were on disk for each rollback slot before writing `rollback-meta.json`:
- live entry: disk bytes replaced `entry.Config.Format()` before hashing, blessing a stale slot left by a prior slot-write failure (ENOSPC/EIO) or a crash during a commit-confirmed slot shift;
- tombstone entry: disk bytes replaced the marker, blessing a slot whose marker write never landed;
- success unconditionally cleared `rollbackPersistDegraded`.

After restart, `rollback N` returned a different generation's config with no warning and health green.

## Fix
`pkg/configstore/rollback_metadata.go` — `rebindRollbackMetadataLocked` only; callers unchanged:
- Live entry: hash the in-memory `Format()`; rewrite the slot durably whenever on-disk bytes diverge (missing/unreadable/oversized included); record only the identity after a verified match or successful rewrite.
- Tombstone: always record the marker; restore it durably when the file still parses as a real config. Bytes that already refuse at load (marker/empty/parse error — the trailing tombstones of a healthy #14578 boot-recovery ladder) keep their identity, so neighbouring behaviour is unchanged.
- A slot that cannot be made to match records an invalid (zero) identity → next load tombstones it (fail-closed); the rebind stays degraded instead of clearing the flag.

## Tests (`rollback_rebind_15023_test.go`)
- `TestRebindDoesNotBlessStaleLiveSlot_15023` — stale `hostStale` bytes at slot 3 rewritten to in-memory `hostC`; restart rb1=hostA rb2=hostB rb3=hostC. **Fails on master.**
- `TestRebindStaysDegradedWhenStaleSlotRewriteFails_15023` — injected ENOSPC: degraded stays true, restart tombstones slot 3 (REFUSED). **Fails on master.**
- `TestRebindDoesNotBlessTombstonedSlot_15023` — tombstone whose file still holds live bytes restored to the marker. **Fails on master.**
- `TestRebindHealthyLadderUnchanged_15023` — control: matching ladder rebound with slot identities unchanged (passes before and after).

Neighbouring suites green: #14578 rebind (runtime/boot/retry), #10723 mixed-generation, #7176 tombstone, broader `TestRollback|TestTombstone|TestSaveRollback|TestLoadRollback|TestPromote|TestBoot|TestAutoRollback|TestConfirmRecovery|TestSyncApply` set. Main agent should run the full `./pkg/configstore` suite before merge.

Docs: `pkg/configstore/README.md` rebind invariant; `docs/log/15023.md`.
