## PR #15351 — frr: render Junos loops N as allowas-in N-1 (#15009) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15009-campaign`

## Summary
- `loops 1` now emits no `allowas-in` line (Junos default = 0 own-AS occurrences allowed = FRR no-line), `loops N>=2` emits `allowas-in N-1` (`loops 10` -> `allowas-in 9`). Previously the value was copied verbatim, accepting one extra local-AS occurrence on every peer with `loops` (#15009, A11-03).
- Only `renderBGPAllowASIn` changes; compiler/storage/validation keep the authored Junos `loops` value, and the #11795 range gate (unset = silent, out-of-range tolerant values omitted with warning) is preserved.

## Semantics (evidence)
Junos `loops (Autonomous System)`: hidden when detected >=N times (`loops 1` hidden at >=1, default). Junos worked example: `loops 2` = "own AS can appear up to one time, hidden at two or more". FRR: filtered when count > `allowas-in K`; no line = 0 allowed; bare = 3 (never emitted). Hence Junos N == FRR N-1. The family-`loops` prose ("allowed N") was considered as the refutation; it does not govern the group/neighbor leaf xpf accepts and contradicts the AS-loops definition + example + FRR local-as default (1 occurrence permitted absent allowas-in, mirroring `Loops: 1`).

## Tests
- RED on origin/master `6eeff22941`: new `TestGenerateProtocols_BGPAllowASInLoopsOffByOne15009` failed all non-zero loops cells (verbatim lines), loops-0 control passed.
- GREEN: targeted `TestGenerateProtocols_BGPAllowASIn*` + #11460 AF-scope test pass; `pkg/config` loops controls pass; `go vet ./pkg/frr/` clean.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: only `TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426`, `TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374` fail — verified identical failures on pristine master (pre-existing, FRR-load environment).
- Live Junos/FRR run3.sh acceptance not run in this lane; render-level equivalence is pinned by the regression.

Docs: `docs/log/15009.md`, `pkg/frr/README.md`.

## PR #15357 — config: warn that DPD threshold is IKEv1-only on IKEv2 gateways (#15025) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15025-campaign`

## Why
DPD `threshold` renders to `dpd_timeout = interval x threshold`, but strongSwan honours `dpd_timeout` for IKEv1 only (its own swanctl.conf documents it as "Timeout for DPD checks (IKEV1 only)"). On IKEv2 — negotiated by default when no `version` is pinned, and the only version on `v2-only` gateways — a dead peer is declared only after charon's global retransmission budget (~165s) is exhausted, so the knob was silently inert on the default path (A16-02: 169s measured vs 6s configured).

## What
Implements the issue's accepted advisory alternative. Programming charon's `retransmit_timeout/base/tries` is daemon-global, not per-connection, and xpf owns only the swanctl snippet; deriving the global budget from the tightest gateway would silently change retransmission for every IKE SA on the box.

- New `appendDPDThresholdIKEv2AdvisoryLocked` (`pkg/config/dpd_threshold_ikev2_advisory_15025.go`): warns at commit when a DPD-enabled gateway with an explicit threshold (`DPDThreshold > 0`, set only by the `threshold` leaf) is not `v1-only` (dual default or `v2-only`), naming the gateways and pointing at `version v1-only`. Warning, never an error.
- Wired into both compile entries; suppressed on tolerant load / peer-sync via `suppressDPDThresholdIKEv2Advisory` (#8357 doctrine — no re-warning on every boot/sync).
- Renderer and DPD parsing unchanged (`dpd_timeout` is still emitted; IKEv1 needs it).

## Validation
- `TestDPDThresholdIKEv2Advisory15025`: RED on pristine `2c0e039020` with only the test file (`dual-default gateway with DPD threshold 3 must warn ...; warnings=[]`), GREEN on this head. Controls stay silent: `v1-only` + threshold, interval-only (no explicit threshold), no DPD stanza, and the lenient path.
- Adjacent suites pass: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'DPD|DeadPeer|ClusterWithoutNTP|8357'`, `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 'DPD'` (DPDModes, DPDBareAndTuningForms, TolerantDPDClamps). `go vet ./pkg/config` clean.

## Risk
One new advisory per commit for dual/v2 gateways with an explicit threshold; never blocks a commit, suppressed on boot/peer-sync. Residual (issue-accepted): IKEv2 dead-peer timing still follows charon's global retransmission budget.

Closes #15025

## PR #15360 — eventengine: skip no-change remediation commits (#15022) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15022-campaign`

## Summary

A no-`within` event-options policy on `ping_test_completed` whose `change-configuration` restores values already active (the ordinary restore-on-success shape) re-committed an unchanged candidate on every probe cycle. The 30s per-policy cooldown only throttled this to a perpetual full commit+apply every 30s, and every commit pushed an identical entry onto the bounded 50-entry rollback history — evicting the operator rollback ladder in ~24 minutes (report A14-03, consensus MATERIAL).

## Fix

- `pkg/eventengine/engine.go` (`applyOnce`): after `CommitCheck`, if the post-batch candidate equals the active config, skip the commit entirely — exit configure, count the new `SkippedNoChange` stat, return nil so `runAction` still counts the action committed and arms the cooldown exactly as for a real commit. No history entry, no cross-policy global-budget slot spent, no daemon `CommitFn` invoked. A 30-minute run of an unchanged batch now adds 0 history entries.
- `pkg/configstore/store_format.go`: new `Store.CandidateEqualsActive`, comparing candidate vs active under the existing canonical `guardedConfigHash` (#8564 post-persist-round-trip basis), so values the JSON encoding normalizes cannot cause a false skip or false commit.
- `pkg/api`: new `xpf_event_actions_skipped_no_change_total` metric (descriptor, collector, collect site), so a steadily climbing skip count makes the re-asserting policy visible.
- `pkg/eventengine/README.md`: transactional-batch step 4 + metrics list.

Scope: only the autonomous event-engine remediation path skips. Operator/CLI/gRPC/REST commits of an unchanged candidate still record history as before; a batch that genuinely changes the candidate commits exactly as before.

## Tests

New `pkg/eventengine/engine_noop_commit_15022_test.go` drives the exact A14-03 mechanism (no-within `ping_test_completed` policy re-setting the already-active host-name via `HandleEvent` → worker → `applyOnce`):

- `TestNoopCommit_UnchangedBatchSkipsCommit_15022` — history length unchanged, active untouched, `Committed=1`, `Rejected/DroppedStale=0`, global budget count 0.
- `TestNoopCommit_CooldownStillArms_15022` — in-window repeat suppressed; history stays at the seed commit.
- `TestNoopCommit_DaemonPathSkipsCommitFn_15022` — commitFn never invoked on the daemon path.
- `TestNoopCommit_ChangedBatchStillCommits_15022` (control) — a real change still commits and pushes one history entry.

RED evidence: with the gate stripped (Stats field retained so it compiles), the three skip tests fail — 30s timeout waiting for `SkippedNoChange` while the log shows `configuration committed` for the unchanged batch. GREEN with the fix.

Full `pkg/eventengine`, `pkg/configstore`, and `pkg/api` suites carry only base-attributed failures (6673, 9088/9880, REST-6960 families), each reproduced on pristine `origin/master` (0a898fae00). `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean on touched files (`pkg/api/metrics.go` is gofmt-dirty on base and was left as-is).

Closes #15022

userspace-dp: retain rebuilt derived sections on partial republish (#15043)

Why:
prepareSnapshotForApply revalidates Interfaces at apply time and, when
a row moved, rebuilds Routes, Fabrics, TunnelEndpoints,
MirrorConfigs/MirrorExclusions, the zone quarantine and its validated
flag into the published copy (#14209). The scheduler, deferred-worker-

ZoneSetValidated, zoneIDCollisions, wgFanUpBaseRows, xfrmDumpFailed)
from publishSnap into next; Neighbors is deliberately not captured

## PR #15367 — ha: derive config payload key from handshake secret (#15041) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15041-campaign`

Why: On an authenticated Noise-keyed link the #6629 config key came from an ephemeral X25519 exchange in ordinary droppable frames; `verifyFrame` admits sequence gaps, so an on-path relay could suppress both exchange frames, let `awaitConfigKey` time out into cleartext `syncMsgConfig`, and read the control-link PSK plus every config secret — after which heartbeat/sync/fabric HMACs are forgeable (A24-03).

What: `configKeyFromHandshake` (sync_config_crypto.go) HKDFs over the canonically ordered pair of directional Noise frame keys with a purpose-bound info string; `awaitConfigKey` returns it immediately on authenticated connections and never consults the exchange/timeout/legacy latch there. The `syncMsgConfigEncrypted` receive arm (sync_conn_read.go) derives the same key first, falling back to the ephemeral key only on unauthenticated connections. NOT changed: unauthenticated mixed-version cleartext fallback, #11773 alarm/counters, frame seal.

Validation: `TestConfigKeySuppressionNeverYieldsCleartextOnAuthedConn15041` fails pre-fix (`got type 8, want syncMsgConfigEncrypted (31)`) and passes post-fix with byte-identical receiver recovery and no cleartext stats; `TestConfigCryptoUnauthenticatedPeerStillFallsBack15041` control plus the #6629/#11773 suites stay green; `go vet` clean. Full `pkg/cluster` suite: one failure (`TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752`), base-attributed on pristine origin/master.

Risk: A pre-#15041 peer on an authenticated link seals under its ephemeral key, which this build no longer tries there; those payloads fail closed at decrypt and re-push on reconcile — authenticated pairs should upgrade both nodes together. Unkeyed links unaffected.

Closes #15041

## PR #15372 — ha: index scoped generation entries by tuple for bare deletes (#15039) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15039-campaign`

Closes #15039

## Why
Every bare session delete scanned the full scoped generation map
(`scopedKeysForTuple`): sender `takeDeleteGenV4/V6` under
`bulkSnapshotGenMu`+`genSentMu`, receiver `deleteGenGuardV4/V6` up to
twice under `recvGenMu` inside `applyMu`. Bare deletes are the
production close path and the receiver map is pinned near its cap by
tombstones, so each delete cost O(held scoped entries) — measured
6.9ms per sender delete at 50k held entries — serializing sender
stamping and capping the standby's delete apply rate.

## What
- `scopedTupleIndex` side maps (bare tuple -> set of scoped keys) for
  all four scoped generation maps; no generations held — the scoped
  map stays authoritative for every ordering decision.
- Maintained via `putScopedGenBounded` /
  `putScopedGenEvictingTombstones` / `deleteScopedGen` at every scoped
  stamp, record, tombstone, cap eviction (new
  `genTombstoneOrder.frontKey`), gen-0 delete and cross-space
  coupling; rebuilt/cleared in `resetRecvSessionGen`.
- Bare paths iterate `index.keys(tuple)`; `scopedKeysForTuple` deleted.
- NOT changed: wire format, capabilities, generation semantics,
  install guards.

## Validation
- RED on pristine `origin/master` `192c7455ba` (timing test
  transplanted alone): `sender bare delete = 6.90ms at 50000 held
  scoped entries, want < 2ms`; benchmark 61.8us/874us/7.55ms at
  1k/10k/50k held.
- GREEN: `TestBareDeleteCostFlatWithHeldScopedEntries15039` +
  `TestScopedTupleIndexTracksLifecycle15039` pass; benchmark now
  181ns/197ns/209ns at 1k/10k/50k. #14358/#10512 control suites pass;
  scoped `-race` subset passes; `go vet ./pkg/cluster/` clean.
- Full `./pkg/cluster/` (149s): sole failure
  `TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752`, documented in
  `docs/log/14358.md` as base-attributed on clean `origin/master`
  (install-table golden drift, disjoint from this diff).

## Risk
Index/map disagreement can only miss a reclaim/tombstone the scan
would have made (guards still read generations from the scoped map);
the lifecycle test asserts index/map agreement across cap eviction,
reclaim, namespace reset, gen-0 delete, bare close and scoped take
for v4+v6. Details: `docs/log/15039.md`.

Checks main agent should run: full `./pkg/cluster/` suite at final
head (expect sole base-attributed 9752 failure), loss-cluster smoke
per campaign.

`compileSystem` unconditionally reallocated `RootAuthentication`, `Archival`, and `InternetOptions` on every sighting, and the dispatcher calls it once per `system` root — so a second `system` root or a repeated child block silently discarded the earlier block's credentials. - `docs/log/15018.md`.

## PR #15376 — ipsec: render hexadecimal PSKs as raw bytes (#15027) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15027-campaign`

## Summary

`pre-shared-key hexadecimal <hex>` committed and rendered the hex digits as a quoted ASCII secret (`secret = "6162..."`), so strongSwan could never authenticate against a peer holding the same Junos hex key. Any qualifier word was accepted identically, and the block spelling dropped the key entirely (A16-04).

## Fix

- `IKEPolicy`/`IPsecVPN` gain `PSKHex` + `PSKQualifierInvalidSpec`; the compiler switches on the qualifier across packed/flat/block shapes (`classifyPSKQualifier`/`pskQualifierValue` in `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go`).
- New strict gate `validateIPsecPSKQualifierStrict`: unknown qualifier or malformed (odd/non-hex) hexadecimal refused at commit, warned on tolerant load/peer-sync. The malformed-hex error does not echo key material.
- Renderer (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go`): hex secrets render unquoted as `secret = 0x<hex>`; ASCII keeps the quoted #2126 render; a hex-flagged value that is not valid hex is skipped by name at render.
- Bare VPN-level `pre-shared-key <key>` unchanged (ASCII). `$9$` handling, AST redaction, schema arity unchanged.

## Regression (RED → GREEN)

- Base probe: `hexadecimal`/`bogus`/`ascii-text` all committed with `PSK="6162636431323334"` as ASCII; hex values `616`/`zz`/`0x6162` committed verbatim; block hexadecimal dropped (then #14139-refused as empty).
- `TestIPsecPSKHexadecimal15027` (pkg/config): probe `6162636431323334` compiles hex-flagged; ascii control; bogus refused at commit + warned lenient; malformed hex refused without echoing; block hex carried; block bogus refused; VPN-level hex + bare controls.
- `TestPSKHexadecimalRender15027` / `TestPSKHexadecimalPolicyFallback15027` / `TestPSKHexadecimalEndToEnd15027` (pkg/ipsec): structural (#6824) assertion `secret` == `0x6162636431323334` at `secrets/ike-v1`; bad/odd hex skipped with no orphan secret.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestIPsecPSKHexadecimal15027|TestIPsecPSKPresence14139' -count=1`: GREEN.
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1`: fully GREEN.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestIPsec' -count=1`: 7 failures, each reproduced identically with the fix stashed (base-attributed). Full pkg/config suite exceeds the local 600s timeout in the pre-existing `TestParseErrorCap_16MiBInvalidBounded_5827` cell (also on base).

## Risk

Unknown-qualifier configs (never Junos-legal) are now refused at commit / warned on load. Hex tunnels change rendered bytes deliberately (now match hex peers).

Closes #15027

## PR #15378 — vrrp: drop stripped-VLAN sibling adverts on untagged parent (#15049) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15049-campaign`

Why: An untagged-unit VRRP instance on a vlan-tagging parent binds its AF_PACKET ETH_P_ALL tap to the parent netdev. A peer advert for a tagged sibling arrives 802.1Q-tagged on the wire, but the NIC strips the tag into skb metadata before the ptype_all tap, so the frame reads untagged in data. The cBPF prefilter and Go parser both check only the in-data ethertype and no PACKET_AUXDATA was requested, so a same-VRID higher-priority sibling advert was enqueued on the parent instance — demoting the native MASTER / perpetually resetting its master-down timer and leaving the native VIP ownerless. This is the AF_PACKET sibling of #2886, which fixed only the raw fallback.

What: openAfPacketReceiver requests PACKET_AUXDATA (best-effort, debug-log on refusal, mirroring PACKET_IGNORE_OUTGOING). receiverAfPacket now reads via the afPacketRecvmsg (unix.Recvmsg) seam and, for instances bound to a non-VLAN netdev, drops frames whose auxdata reports TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID (afPacketAuxdataVLANTag, fail-open when the cmsg is absent/truncated, mirroring #2886). VLAN children are exempt and keep their own tagged adverts; untagged native adverts on the parent are kept. The cBPF is deliberately unchanged: the same array is attached to parent and child sockets so it cannot express "drop tagged only on the parent", and golang.org/x/net/bpf's VM cannot execute the SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG_PRESENT ancillary load, so a cBPF-only fix would be untestable in the #5088 bpf.VM harness; the PACKET_AUXDATA/TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID option is the per-instance equivalent. The #6560 loop test migrated from the retired afPacketRecvfrom seam to afPacketRecvmsg.

Validation: RED pre-fix (new tests fail to build on master: afPacketRecvmsg/afPacketAuxdataVLANTag undefined — the mechanism does not exist); behavioural RED with the drop neutered — parent received [10.0.61.3 10.0.61.2], i.e. the stripped VLAN-100 advert was enqueued. GREEN with fix: the 3 new #15049 tests (parent drops vlan_tci=100, untagged control kept, child ge-0-0-0.100 keeps its own VLAN), #6560 self-frame, #5088 cBPF, #2886 arrival-ifindex suites pass; full go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -count=1 passes; race on receiver tests passes; go vet clean.

Risk: On a kernel refusing PACKET_AUXDATA the drop is inactive (fail-open, debug-logged) — exactly the pre-fix behaviour, never worse. NOT changed: raw fallback path, cBPF filter set, any behaviour outside the cited AF_PACKET mechanism.

Closes #15049

## PR #15381 — config: default generic vrrp-group preempt to true, add no-preempt (#15047) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15047-campaign`

Closes #15047

## Defect (A05-05)
A generic `vrrp-group` without `preempt` compiled `Preempt=false` (Go zero value in the `parseVRRPGroups` constructor). Junos and RFC 5798 default Preempt_Mode to TRUE, so a backup never took over from a track-demoted master: `pkg/vrrp/track.go` only lowers the advertised priority, and `instance_rx.go` resets the master-down timer on every advert when `!getPreempt()`.

## Fix
- `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`: constructor defaults `Preempt: true`; new `no-preempt` arms in both the flat Keys loop and the child-node loop clear it; `no-preempt` added to `vrrpGroupPropertyKeywords` so it delimits packed virtual-address runs.
- `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go`: new `no-preempt` schema leaf (needed for flat-set structuring + the packed hierarchical one-liner splitter).
- `pkg/config/types_interfaces.go`: document the default on `VRRPGroup.Preempt`.
- RETH collection unchanged: `CollectRethInstances` still takes preempt only from explicit chassis `redundancy-group <id> preempt`.

## Regression (RED → GREEN)
`pkg/config/vrrp_preempt_default_15047_test.go`:
- RED on master: no-keyword flat-set and hierarchical configs compiled `Preempt=false`.
- GREEN: no-keyword (incl. a `track-interface` group) → true; `no-preempt` → false in flat-set, hierarchical, and packed one-liner shapes (packed control also proves the following `priority 150` still parses); explicit `preempt` → true.

Neighbours verified green locally: `TestVRRPPreemptHoldTime|TestVRRPTrackInterface|TestVRRPV6|TestGroupMerge10055`, golden `TestCompileGolden4406|TestGolden` (golden `Preempt:false` rows are chassis redundancy-groups, intentionally unchanged). `spelling_gate_members_7484.txt` gained the two `no-preempt` flag rows; the full spelling-gate suite timed out under shared load in the worktree — please run the full `pkg/config` + `pkg/vrrp` suites in CI.

Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` (#15047 note beside #2850), `docs/log/15047.md`.

## PR #15385 — cluster: carry PD expiry in RA desired set, decay at send time (#15057) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15057-campaign`

Why: buildRAConfigs baked the decayed remaining DHCPv6-PD lifetimes into RAPrefix.ValidLifetime/PreferredLife, so the 2s cluster reconcile hash (raDesiredHash) and ra.configEqual changed every second and ra.Apply hard-restarted the RA sender (3-RA startup burst, new NDP socket, two Info lines) on every pass, indefinitely, on any cluster advertising a PD prefix.

What: DelegatedPrefixesForRA returns the granted lifetimes with the original Obtained (expired prune/skip unchanged); DelegatedPrefix gains PreferredExpiresAt beside ExpiresAt; buildRAConfigs stamps absolute RAPrefix.ValidExpiresAt/PreferredExpiresAt (Unix-nano, Obtained+granted) plus the granted lifetimes; pkg/ra buildRA computes the remaining lifetime at send time (whole seconds, never more than remains, preferred 0 past its expiry, PIO omitted past valid expiry); configEqual and sortRAPrefixes compare the expiries, so decay is a no-op and a renewal moving the expiry restarts. Prefixes without an expiry keep the granted/default path verbatim. Golden compile fixture regenerated. NOT changed: RemainingLifetimes semantics outside the RA desired set; operator-prefix defaults; the sender restart machinery.

Validation: new pkg/daemon/ra_pd_expiry_15057_test.go (granted+expiry shape; five 2s-apart fake-clock passes produce ONE raDesiredHash — the RED mechanism; renewal moves the hash; decayed-to-zero shape; zero-obtained sentinel), new pkg/ra/sender_expiry_15057_test.go (7200->7140 at +60s, 3200/0 past preferred expiry, PIO omitted at/past valid expiry, no-expiry controls byte-identical, configEqual expiry identity). Updated the 14598/14606 producer cells that asserted the old decayed shape; decay is now asserted at the wire. pkg/ra and pkg/dhcp full suites pass; pkg/config golden passes; go vet clean on touched packages.

Risk: a sender whose prefix validly expires between the last prune and the next send now omits the PIO at send time instead of advertising the last decayed value; the next reconcile removes it from the desired set as before.

Closes #15057

## PR #15396 — daemon: re-test bootstrap gate under applySem (#15055) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15055-campaign`

Closes #15055

## What

The plain-commit bootstrap gate in `commitAndApply` was tested before `applySem.Acquire` and never re-tested (A32-02). A plain commit that passed the gate while a first commit-confirmed rollback held `applySem` parked, then bound the rollback's reset candidate generation in `commitWithGenBinding` and promoted the empty candidate — reporting success and persisting `committed=1`-empty, so the next boot classified NORMAL (the state #1922 Item 1b / #7291 exist to prevent).

## Fix

- `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go`: re-test `inBootstrap()` after `applySem.Acquire`, before any store promotion (mirrors the #9884 post-Acquire recheck in `beginBackgroundApply`).
- `pkg/configstore/store_commit.go`: bump `holderEpoch` in the first-commit branch of `PromoteRollback` only, so a holder-bound authority minted before the timeout fails verification at promotion; ordinary rollbacks are unaffected.

## Tests

`pkg/daemon/bootstrap_commit_race_15055_test.go` (5 cells):
- Race cell: parked plain commit is refused with the bootstrap error, no apply, in-memory + reloaded `everCommitted=false`.
- Holder-epoch cell: first-commit `PromoteRollback` bumps the epoch and the pre-rollback authority gets the holder-turnover refusal; non-first control does not bump.
- Controls: plain commit in bootstrap refused + commit-confirmed escape hatch; plain commit outside bootstrap succeeds.

RED before fix (gate cell: commit promoted first and confirmed the window; epoch cell: before=1 after=1), GREEN after. Docs: `docs/log/15055.md`, `pkg/daemon/README.md`.

Note: full-suite and -race verification should be re-run on a quieter host — this worktree's runs were under extreme sibling load (load avg ~90-112) and bounded shell timeouts expired before producing results; the targeted `15055` cells pass.

Lease.RemainingLifetimes. NOT changed: v4, stateless, acquisition.

expiry (lease-deadline bounded), matching the anti-outage rule;

## PR #15399 — ipsec: allow VRF-enslaved xfrmi to open permit so host fence retires (#15067) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15067-campaign`

Why:
`classifyIpsecTopologyLinks` marked every xfrmi with a resolved `vrf`/`bridge` master `ipsecReadyUnsafe`. The permit only OPENs on `ipsecReadySafe` and the host-input fence overlay retires only on the OPEN path, so a VRF-enslaved `st0.N` never opened and its slave-scoped DROP at the head of `inet xpf_hostinbound` never retired — tunnel-arriving host traffic stayed dropped for as long as the tunnel was enslaved (A35-02).

What:
A `vrf` master now leaves readiness unchanged (SAFE when subscribed); `bridge` and every other resolved master stay UNSAFE, unresolvable stays UNKNOWN. Since #14974 the divert matches `iifname=master` + `meta sdifname=st0.N` and the fence drops only that pair, so the VRF topology is supported end to end. NOT changed: fence renderers, divert, permit CAS. Stale `TestIpsecTopologyCensusRejectsVRFMaster9506` pin updated to assert SAFE.

Validation:
RED on `origin/master` `d9e033dae0`: `TestIpsecTopologyCensusVRFEnslavedSafe15067` failed `census ready = UNSAFE, want SAFE`; `TestIpsecHostFenceRetiresAfterVRFOpen15067` failed at the same census. GREEN after: all four 15067 tests pass; `pkg/daemon` fence/topology/permit suites and `pkg/nftables` `14974|HostInputFence` suites pass; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean.

Risk:
A VRF-enslaved tunnel now reaches OPEN; host traffic via `st0.N` is then judged by ordinary host-inbound zone rules and still fenced whenever the permit is CLOSING. Co-members such as `ge-0-0-3` were never matched by the slave-scoped fence and are unaffected.

Closes #15067

## PR #15402 — feeds: persist feed content epoch under its own digest (#15075) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15075-campaign`

feeds: persist feed content epoch under its own digest (#15075)

Closes #15075

## Why
The persisted feed content epoch (#14395) did not protect across a restart (A50-01): `ShrinkHighWaterSnapshot` stored the epoch prefix set with only `Hash` — the count high-water hash — as its key. Any ordinary non-rebasing install advances `highWaterHash` to the rotated set while the epoch moves only on bootstrap or ack, so the two diverge after one rotation and the restore had no epoch digest of its own to validate the set against; the first post-restart fetch could rebase the epoch unchecked, replacing an enforced deny/allow list wholesale with no refusal or acknowledgement.

## What
- `ShrinkHighWater` gains `EpochHash` (`epoch_hash,omitempty`): the `hashPrefixes` digest of the epoch prefix set, persisted separately from the count high-water `Hash`.
- `ShrinkHighWaterSnapshot` emits it; `RestoreShrinkHighWater` validates the restored canonical set against it. Pre-#15075 records without `epoch_hash` restore the epoch only in the epoch == high-water shape; a set matching neither key is dropped fail-closed while the count epoch still restores.
- On a bootstrap with a restored epoch, the existing #14994 guard evaluates `contentChurnTripped(restoredEpoch, candidate)` and refuses a churned candidate pending the exact-candidate ack instead of rebasing — now reachable across an ordinary rotation + restart.
- `pkg/feeds/README.md` updated; `docs/log/15075.md` records the analysis.

## Validation
- New `feed_shrink_15075_test.go`: non-rebasing 51% rotation keeps all 100 epoch prefixes + diverged `EpochHash`; post-restart 2%-of-epoch candidate refused; restart bootstrapping a disjoint set against the restored epoch refused, installs on exact ack; corrupt `EpochHash` drops the epoch while the count restores.
- Mutants (drop the `EpochHash` emit / ignore it on restore / re-key restore on the high-water hash — the A50-01 shape) each turn the tests red.
- Full `pkg/feeds` suite, daemon `FeedShrink|FeedHistory`, and grpcapi `12170` legs pass; gofmt/vet clean.

## Risk
Scoped to durable shrink-history restore. Additive JSON field; thresholds, ack tuple, hold policy, and true bootstrap unchanged. A mismatched epoch set restores the count baseline only and re-bootstraps under the #14994 guard.

## PR #15408 — flowexport: re-dial collectors after source renumbering (#15073) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15073-campaign`

## Summary
Collector sockets were dialed once at exporter build and never re-dialed. After the implicit source was renumbered (DHCP/SLAAC), IPv4 writes failed permanently on the stale socket and IPv6 kept sending from the removed address while health read healthy, until restart or an unrelated flow-export commit.

## Fix (`pkg/flowexport/transport.go`, shared by NetFlow v9 + IPFIX)
- Extract `dialCollector` as the single dial path shared by `dialCollectors` and recovery; a re-dial re-resolves the destination and re-picks the live implicit source exactly as a fresh build would.
- Write-failure leg: a failure on a proven-healthy socket whose `LocalAddr()` is no longer assigned re-dials once and retries that packet on the fresh socket (old socket closed only after the new write succeeds).
- Stale-source canary: healthy sockets whose source is no longer assigned are re-dialed before the write fan-out; `health()` reports them unhealthy with a not-assigned reason even while writes succeed (IPv6 leg). Enumeration failure conservatively counts as assigned (no churn).
- Still-assigned failures keep existing unhealthy+backoff behaviour with no re-dial churn; failed re-dials park unhealthy behind the existing probe backoff. `conn` moved under RWMutex so health/close never race a swap.

NOT changed: daemon hash-gating, backoff/write-timeout semantics (#4423), health surface shape, pinned source binds (re-dial re-resolves the same pinned source).

## Regression (`collector_redial_15073_test.go`)
- `TestCollectorRedial_WriteFailureRedials15073` — S1 renumbered to S2; failed write re-dials (1→2), closes old socket, delivers this packet from S2, churn-free after.
- `TestCollectorRedial_StaleSourceHealth15073` — IPv6 stale source reports unhealthy + next writeAll re-dials and sends from S2.
- `TestCollectorRedial_StillAssignedNoChurn15073` — control: no churn, no re-dial on ordinary refused write.
- `TestCollectorRedial_RedialFailureParksUnhealthy15073`, `TestCollectorRedial_SourceBoundCollector15073`.
RED on base (fix seams undefined / mechanism absent), GREEN after.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -run 15073 -count=1 -v`: 5/5 GREEN
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -count=1`: GREEN (also after rebase onto current master)
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -race -count=1`: ok (2.5s)
- `go vet ./pkg/flowexport/`: clean

## Risk
Live netns renumbering probe not run in this lane; unit fakes model the LocalAddr-vs-assigned-set kernel contract. Changelog: `docs/log/15073.md`.

Closes #15073

## PR #15411 — grpcapi: size forwarded failover proxy from cluster budget (#15081) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15081-campaign`

Why: proxyPeerSystemAction (and its pkg/cli twin) applied a flat 5s deadline to forwarded cluster-failover ... node <peer> and data failover. The peer's RequestPeerFailover sequence (20s failover-ACK, 3s commit-ready settle, 20s commit ACK; barrier ACK alone can be delayed 30+s by bulk session sync) routinely exceeded 5s, so the operator received a bare DeadlineExceeded while the peer completed the ownership move, inviting a needless retry during maintenance.

What: pkg/clusterfailover gains ProxyFailoverTimeout (2x20s ACK + 2x3s settle = 46s, mirroring the daemon's 2*settle+20s lease sizing) and IsFailoverActionString. grpcapi proxyPeerTimeout and cli peerSystemActionTimeout apply the long budget only to validated node-targeted failovers; all other forwards keep 5s. On a deadline outcome the proxy result is reconciled against heartbeat RG ownership (new cluster.PeerPrimaryRGs): committed transfers report success, anything else reports outcome unknown with verify-before-retry guidance, never a bare DeadlineExceeded. NOT changed: peer-side failover execution, fabric allowlist, cluster timeouts.

Validation: RED on pristine origin/master (forwarded deadline = 4.999s; CLI returned bare DeadlineExceeded after peer commit). GREEN: go test ./pkg/clusterfailover/ ./pkg/cluster/ ./pkg/grpcapi/ ./pkg/cli/ -run 15081 all pass; neighbouring Failover/SystemAction suites pass except two grpcapi cells reproduced identically on pristine master (base-attributed). go vet clean on all four packages.

Risk: a genuinely hung peer now holds the operator command up to 46s before the outcome-unknown report — deliberate, per the issue's cluster-budget sizing; the 5s answer was a false failure report.

Closes #15081

## Summary

Fixes A57-01 (#15089): the A/B ESP slots (`EFI/xpf-A`, `EFI/xpf-B`) held a bake-time copy of shim/grub/mm that nothing ever refreshed. Ubuntu `shim-signed` / `grub-efi-amd64-signed` updates install only to `EFI/ubuntu`, while BootOrder keeps booting the stale xpf slots — the Secure-Boot chain stayed on the bake-time bootloader for the life of the appliance (a SBAT/dbx revocation would never reach the booted loader) while dpkg reported the fixed version as installed. `validate.py` asserted only file presence, so the stale state shipped green.

- **`scripts/image/xpf-uefi-slots`**: new `sync_ab_slots()` — cmp-gated, per-file atomic (temp file in the same slot dir + rename, post-rename cmp verify) re-copy of `shimx64.efi`/`grubx64.efi`/`mmx64.efi` from `EFI/ubuntu` into both slots. - **`scripts/image/validate.py`**: new `_AB_SLOT_HASH_PROBE` + `_ab_slot_loader_hash_verdict`, applied in `assert_ab_kernel_channel` after the presence verdict — a stale/divergent slot loader fails the Tier-1 gate by name. mm absent from both source and slot (the bake fallback shape) still passes; a loader absent from `EFI/ubuntu` entirely stays the presence verdict's diagnosis.

NOT changed: the bake's one-time staging (still the initial seed), NVRAM registration / BootOrder logic, `xpf.selector` seeding/promotion, the kernel hold.

Alternatives rejected: holding shim/grub like the kernel (strands bootloader security updates with no verified delivery channel); an apt `Post-Invoke` hook (per-invocation, misses direct `dpkg -i`, can fire pre-configure).

## Validation

- **RED** on `origin/master` (6fd1efe432): new `scripts/image/test_slot_refresh_15089.py` (19 tests) — 6 failures + 10 errors (no hash verdict, no `--sync-only`, no triggers file, postinst rejected `triggered`).

Adjacent suites green (104 tests total): `test_validate_gate_reactions_10770`, `test_validate_ab_substrate_6498`, `test_validate_ab_slots_6494`, `test_uefi_slots_6499`, `test_validate_scenarios`. `sh -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean.

## PR #15419 — grpcapi: bound streamDiagCmd scan wait behind parked scanner (#15080) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15080-campaign`

## Summary
Bounds `streamDiagCmd`'s wait behind a parked scanner goroutine so a diagnostic slot cannot be pinned by the unbounded `c.Wait(); <-scanDone` join (A43-01, #15080).

**Mechanism:** `c.Wait()` joins exec's copy goroutine, which stays blocked in `pw.Write` while the scanner goroutine is parked inside `sendFn` (it holds the `io.Pipe` read end and is not reading). The wait therefore never returned and the handler never reached its `defer release()`, holding a process-wide `diagcmd.DefaultLimiter` slot (cap 4, shared with REST). #14980 bounded the handlers' per-line `Send` via `sendDiagFrame`, but `streamDiagCmd` itself kept the unbounded wait — a `sendFn` that only parks until its ctx is done, or any direct caller with a raw unbounded `Send`, wedged it until the full exec timeout.

**Fix:** run `c.Wait()` in a worker and select over `waitDone`/`scanDone`/`ctx.Done()`:
- `waitDone`-first: unchanged normal path (`pw.Close()`, drain `scanDone`, scan error wins, child exit error as final line).
- `scanDone`-first (send/scanner failure): join Wait (already reaped by the scanner's deferred `cancel()`+`pr.Close()`) and report `scanErr`, not the internal cancel's ctx error — this leg also avoids misreporting every early scan error as a cancellation.
- `ctx.Done()`-first: close both pipe ends (`pr.Close()` unblocks the copy goroutine), join only Wait under `requestExecWaitDelay` (5s), and return `ctx.Err()` without joining `scanDone` — a scanner parked in a ctx-independent `sendFn` is abandoned to the caller's per-write Send bound (#14980) rather than re-wedging the return.

NOT changed: handlers, `sendDiagFrame`, REST surface, monitor handlers, `buildPrimaryServer` keepalive.

Closes #15080

## Validation
- New `pkg/grpcapi/diag_scan_wait_15080_test.go` (3 tests):
  - RED on `origin/master` (`ac543c5b9e`, re-confirmed on pristine `f524416374`): `TestStreamDiagCmd15080CtxCancelUnblocksParkedSend` fails with "streamDiagCmd did not return within 5s of ctx cancel while sendFn parked: c.Wait() wedged on the scanner goroutine, diag slot pinned (#15080)"; draining control passes both sides.
  - GREEN post-fix: ctx-cancel returns `context.Canceled` promptly; real-path sever (real `streamDiagCmd` + `sendDiagFrame`-wired parked Send) returns the sever with the slot transferred (`InFlight=1` while parked) then freed on unblock; draining control (lines in order + exit error as final line) unchanged.
- Adjacent suites green: `TestDiagSendBound14980*` (6), `TestStreamDiagCmd*` (incl. #5060 `ErrTooLong` and #1819 send-error controls), `TestDiagConcurrencyLimitGRPC*`; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Docs: `docs/log/15080.md`, `pkg/grpcapi/README.md` updated.

## Risk
Fail-closed only on an already-cancelled RPC; healthy streams untouched. On the ctx path the scanner goroutine is abandoned to the caller's Send bound rather than joined — it exits when that Send unblocks on handler-return stream cancel, the #14980/#9891 worker lifetime.

## PR #15421 — authz: exempt session-plumbing probes from the command regex gate (#15077) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15077-campaign`

Why:
GetStatus and GetConfigModeStatus were charged to the canonical command "show version" in `methodCanonicalCommand`, and their REST twins (`GET /api/v1/status`, `GET /api/v1/config/status`) were charged likewise. `cmd/cli` calls `GetStatus` before every dispatched command (its reachability probe, `cmd/cli/main.go`) and `GetConfigModeStatus` at every config-mode prompt, so a class with `deny-commands "show version"` — or an `allow-commands` list naming anything else — was locked out of SSH management entirely and told "cannot reach xpfd", while `show version` itself (ShowText topic `version`) stayed denied. Commit gave no warning.

What:
Remove both charges. The probes return liveness facts (uptime, cluster role, dirty flag), not the version banner, so they are session plumbing: named in `methodsWithoutCanonicalCommand` / `restRoutesNoCommand` and exempted from the operational regex gates (`isSessionPlumbingMethod` on gRPC, `restNoCommandExempt14146` on REST), governed by the coarse `PermView` price alone. `show version` keeps its charge where it is actually served (ShowText topic `version`, `GET /api/v1/show-text?topic=version`). The cli startup probe now reports `PermissionDenied` as an authorization denial instead of a reachability failure. NOT changed: coarse permission prices, the on-box CLI gate, or any other RPC/route charge.

Validation:
New 15077 cells in `pkg/grpcapi` (`authz_probe_15077_test.go`) and `pkg/api` (`authz_probe_15077_test.go`) drive the real `authorizeRPCContext` / `authorizeRESTCommand`: RED on the pre-fix mechanism (probes denied under a `^show version$` deny; verified by reverting the three production files), GREEN post-fix with `show version` staying denied, `GetInterfaces`/`GetZones` admitted, and a view-less uid still refused at the coarse gate. Retargeted pre-existing cells that pinned the wrong charge (9633 unresolved set, 7172 empty/invalid-regex, 14146 exempt set, 14712 HEAD deny arm). Targeted subsets pass post-rebase; full `pkg/grpcapi`/`pkg/api` runs show only pre-existing failures base-attributed on `origin/master` (`session_iface_identity_6960`, screen-key census, NAT walks). `cmd/cli` adjacent subset passes.

Risk:
A class that used a `show version` deny to also block the liveness/config-mode facts loses that incidental coverage; the facts disclose no version banner and remain behind the coarse view permission. Documented in `docs/system-login.md`; per-issue log in `docs/log/15077.md`.

Closes #15077

## Summary

## PR #15424 — cli: execute top/up-prefixed config commands at target level (#15082) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15082-campaign`

## Why

`top delete … policy allow-all` printed `[edit]`, sent no Delete RPC (remote `cmd/cli`) / executed nothing (local `pkg/cli`), and returned success — both dispatchers treated `top`/`up` as pure navigation and never read trailing tokens. The permit policy stayed in the candidate and committed: a silent divergence between operator intent and committed enforcement (A53-01). `AuthorizeConfigMutation` also treated every `top`/`up` line as ungated navigation, so executing the inner command without unwrapping the prefix in the gate would have let denied deletes ride ungated.

## What

- `pkg/config`: `ResolveTopUpPrefix15082`/`ParseTopUpPrefix15082` split `top <cmd>` / `up [n] <cmd>` once (target cursor, inner tokens, quote provenance; bare navigation vs malformed prefix, prefixed out-of-range counts fail closed). `configMutationPaths` + embedded-payload scan unwrap the prefix so prefixed mutations are adjudicated as the inner command at the target cursor.
- `pkg/cli` + `cmd/cli`: `dispatchTopUp15082` — bare form navigates (`up n` count now honoured), prefixed form installs the target cursor, re-enters `dispatchConfig` (every gate re-runs), executes exactly the un-prefixed command (exactly one Delete RPC on the remote surface for the acceptance probe), restores cursor/prompt on success and error.

NOT changed: gRPC/REST handlers (already-resolved paths), `NavigateTop`/`NavigateUp` store primitives.

## Validation

- RED pre-fix (fix reverted, tests kept): local top/up delete left `allow-all` in candidate with nil return; remote sent zero Delete RPCs; invalid prefixes returned nil.
- GREEN: `pkg/cli`, `cmd/cli`, `pkg/config` 15082 cells pass; `pkg/config` authz subset pass; `go vet` clean on the three packages; `git diff --check` clean.
- Full `pkg/cli` run: 10 failures, all reproduced verbatim on pristine `origin/master` (base-attributed, none in the top/up path). `cmd/cli` dispatch-adjacent subset passes.

## Risk

Only config-mode lines starting `top`/`up` change: trailing tokens now execute instead of being silently ignored; malformed prefixes now error instead of silently succeeding. Bare `top`/`up` navigate as before. Denied mutations are refused by the unwrapped gate before execution.

Closes #15082

## PR #15425 — daemon: ignore SIGHUP instead of dying unscored (#15084) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15084-campaign`

Why:
Nothing in xpfd notified or ignored SIGHUP, so the default
action killed the daemon with no shutdown sequence (no HA
fence, no rg_active clear, no priority-0 advert, no RA
goodbye), and systemd scored the death as a clean exit, so the
unit's Restart=on-failure never revived the firewall. One stray
`systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` (or a closing controlling terminal)
was an indefinite forwarding outage standalone, or an
ungraceful peer-loss failover after which an HA node never
rejoined.

What:
- pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go: ignoreSIGHUP() installs an explicit
  no-op disposition at the TOP of Run (before the mutating
  startup phases, both modes, deferred release): a buffered
  signal.Notify channel logs each HUP ("xpfd has no
  reload-on-HUP; use commit") and discards it; the daemon keeps
  forwarding. daemonSignals() extracts the shutdown set as a
  named seam and SIGHUP is deliberately kept OUT of it — an
  orderly exit-0 stop would still score clean under systemd, so
  the "orderly stop" fix shape is rejected.
- test/incus/xpfd.service (the unit debian/rules stages and
  injects ExecStartPre into): RestartForceExitStatus=SIGHUP
  SIGPIPE, so even a HUP death in a window the capture cannot
  cover (pre-Run, older binary under the upgraded unit) is
  scored a failure and restarted within RestartSec. The
  version drop-in (pkg/upgrade/flip.go) rewrites only
  ExecStart/ExecStartPre, so the directive survives cuts.
- pkg/daemon/README.md (stale "(SIGHUP reload, ...)" claim
  corrected + disposition documented), debian/changelog,
  docs/log/15084.md.

NOT changed: surviving shutdown behaviour (daemon
SIGTERM+SIGINT, interactive SIGTERM only so the CLI keeps
Ctrl-C), commit/apply paths, the flip.go drop-in template, and
in-process SIGPIPE semantics (only the supervisor's scoring of
a SIGPIPE death changes).

Validation:
- RED on origin/master (6fd1efe432): the regression file alone
  does not build (undefined: daemonSignals, undefined:
  ignoreSIGHUP — no SIGHUP capture seam exists there) and the
  unit carries no RestartForceExitStatus.
- GREEN: TestDaemonSignalsExcludeSIGHUP15084 (shutdown set
  excludes SIGHUP, keeps SIGTERM/SIGINT),
  TestIgnoreSIGHUPSurvivesDelivery15084 (two real
  self-delivered SIGHUPs, process alive, single stop release),
  TestUnitRestartForceExitStatus15084 (parses the shipped
  unit), the #5807 startup-signal suite, pkg/grpcapi #8233 and
  pkg/dataplane/userspace #7675 unit consumers; go vet

*(truncated — 67 lines total)*

## PR #15428 — daemon: gate bare xpfd behind a singleton flock before any mutation (#15085) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15085-campaign`

Why: A bare `xpfd` or `xpfd -flag...` — the exact invocation the old
unknown-command error text recommended — booted a second full daemon on
a live firewall. Long before the #8233 management-port refusal fired,
Daemon.Run cleared the live owner's first-apply marker, and the later
phases re-ran compile, closed the transit gate, and re-attached XDP, so
an operator mistake the product itself suggested mutated host-global
state under the running daemon.

What: `daemon.New` now takes a non-blocking exclusive flock on
`/run/xpf/xpfd.lock` (0600, owner pid recorded under the lock, never
unlinked) before the config store is constructed, and the Daemon holds
it until `Run` returns; a second process fails with `xpfd already
running (pid N); use the 'cli' binary ..., or 'systemctl restart xpfd'
...`. `Daemon.Run` refuses any lease-less Daemon before any startup
mutation, and `clearHostInboundFirstApplyMarker` refuses to delete a
marker live-held by another process (`HostInboundFirstApplyLive`). The
cmdUnknown text no longer suggests running `xpfd` directly. NOT
changed: classifyCommand routing (bare xpfd must still start the daemon
under systemd; the singleton, not argv shape, is the gate), one-shot
subcommands stay lock-free, and no pidfile/blocking wait is introduced
(systemd `TimeoutStopSec` bounds predecessor exit; flock releases on fd
close).

Validation: RED pre-fix — `daemon_singleton_15085_test.go` fails to
build on origin/master (singleton API absent). GREEN post-fix —
TestAcquireDaemonLockRejectsSecondOwner15085 (busy refusal names pid +
alternatives, probe reads live, re-acquire after release works) and
TestDaemonRunRefusesSecondProcessBeforeMarkerClear15085 (real
Daemon.Run against a live flock + live first-apply marker: refused,
marker intact, no .configdb created) pass, plus adjacent controls
TestClearHostInboundFirstApplyMarker10751,
TestMarkerOwnershipLifecycle10751, TestFirstApplyMarkerRedirectedInTests10751
and the #12155 real-Run chain test (6/6). go vet/build/gofmt clean.
Full ./pkg/daemon suite shows 37–38 pre-existing failures reproduced on
unmodified origin/master (config-sync/RG0 + golden drift, unrelated);
./cmd/xpfd fully green.

Risk: A daemon started outside systemd now also refuses while another
instance holds the lock — intended. Restart overlap works unchanged:
predecessor exit closes its fd, successor acquires immediately after.

Closes #15085

## PR #15429 — config: fold brace-elided top-level interfaces into braced shape (#15062) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15062-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes #15062 (A01-01): a top-level `interfaces <name> { ... }` committed clean and compiled phantom interfaces (`unit`, `family`), losing the named interface's address/DHCP/MTU — including `fxp0` through the day-0 `CheckText` gate.

The parser builds `Keys=["interfaces","ge-0/0/0"]` with the interface body as children. `compileSections` dispatched on `node.Name()` and ignored `Keys[1:]`, so `compileInterfaces` received the `interfaces` node itself and named an `InterfaceConfig` after each body child. The scoped compact fold cannot name an operator-chosen interface name (#8879), and the #8879 cell asserted only `err == nil`, so the loss was invisible.

- `normalizeElidedInterface15062` (new) folds the elided node into the braced shape inside `normalizeCompactStanzas` — the #9620 routing-instance pattern. Every compile core and `SchemaValidate` normalize before reading the tree, so strict commit, lenient load, node-aware compile, and `configstore.CheckText` all see the braced shape, and `ValidateInterfaceName` now gates the elided name.
- Hooked in `normalizeCompactNodes` when the `interfaces` child is exactly `schemaInterfaces` (root + `groups` bodies; not class-of-service `interfaces`).
- Untouched: braced form, bare leaf `interfaces <name>;`, top-level apply statements, parser, compiler readers, display rendering (authored shape still renders verbatim).

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/interfaces_elided_normalize_15062_test.go`: elided↔braced tree equality (top level + inside groups) and compiled interface/unit/address/DHCP/MTU digest equality with phantom checks; neighbour shapes untouched.
- New `pkg/configstore/interfaces_elided_commit_gate_15062_test.go`: `CheckText` parity for fxp0/ge (address, MTU, DHCP); invalid name refused in both spellings.
- `#8879` cell now compares compiled values instead of only `err == nil`.
- RED on base (production stashed): phantom `unit`/`family`, named interface lost, bad name accepted elided-only. GREEN after fix on the rebased head; `go vet` clean.
- Full `pkg/config` suite at this base carries pre-existing failures verified identical on pristine master (LLDP block-form panic, IPsec/WireGuard degenerate-key rows, #2419 inventory drift) and times out under parallel lane load; no new failure attributed to this change in exercised suites.

Elided spellings now compile what their braced spellings always compiled. Configs that (incorrectly) relied on the phantom/loss behaviour now get the authored interface. `docs/log/15062.md` records the full history.

## PR #15432 — config: include kernel XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM in jumbo-MTU advisory budget (#15115) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15115-campaign`

Closes #15115

## Why
The #9727 advisory counted only the configured UMEM headroom (256), giving a 3822-byte budget. The kernel sums its fixed XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM (256) with the pool headroom (`xsk_pool_get_headroom`), so usable RX frame size is 4096-512=3584; MTUs 3567..3822 committed silently while full-size frames were dropped (`kernel_rx_dropped`) or the zero-copy bind was refused.

- Add `userspaceXDPacketHeadroom = 256`; `userspaceRxMTUBudget = 4096-(256+256)-14-4 = 3566`.
- Warning text names both headroom terms.
- New `userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_15115_test.go` derives 3566 from the Rust UMEM constants plus the kernel term independently (never from the budget constant) and pins 3566 silent / 3567, 3700, 3822 warning.

- GREEN after fix, including all existing 9727 neighbour controls (boundary/unit override, exclusions, mgmt/control, tolerant suppression, drift guard, compiled wiring); `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean.

## Risk
MTUs 3567..3822 on zoned interfaces now warn at commit (previously silent while dropping); no commit newly rejected, no behaviour change outside the advisory.

## Summary

Fixes A66-02 (#15096): the per-binding pending-neighbor cap `MAX_PENDING_NEIGH` (4096) ignored the binding's RX frame budget. At the default ring-entries 1024 the whole RX fill pool is 2048 frames (fill = 2*ring; total = reserved TX + 2*ring), so a permitted sweep of a large connected prefix parking one RX frame per distinct unresolved hop could pin twice the pool, drain the fill ring, and stall all RX on the affected queues.

## Fix

- `pending_neigh_cap_for_rx_fill(rx_fill) = min(MAX_PENDING_NEIGH, max(rx_fill/4, 1))` — at most one quarter of a binding's own RX fill pool may be parked; computed once at bind time in `BindingWorker` (production `create` + both test constructors).
- `rx_fill_frames_for_driver` derives fill as total − reserved TX from the existing bind arithmetic, so a reserved-TX policy change moves the cap with it.
- The poll loop's single admission call passes `binding.pending_neigh_cap`; refusals take the existing counted `CapacityDrop` arm (`pending_neigh_capacity_drops`, #2375) and recycle the frame — fail-closed, no silent park.
- NOT changed: probe schedules, pending timeouts, the negative-neighbor cache, per-source/per-prefix sub-caps (optional in the issue; the quarter-pool cap alone restores the fill-ring invariant), and the 4096 ceiling for large rings.

## Regression (RED → GREEN)

- `ring_1024_binding_parks_at_most_quarter_of_fill_pool_15096`: builds the ring=1024 pool from the production bind arithmetic (non-virtio/virtio/mlx5); asserts cap == rx_fill/4 < 4096, Buffer at cap−1, CapacityDrop at cap, DuplicateDrop for duplicates, plus the large-ring ceiling and degenerate-pool floors. Pre-fix the helper compared `len < MAX_PENDING_NEIGH` with no per-binding cap, so this fails on `origin/master`.
- `binding_worker_parks_at_most_quarter_of_its_pool_15096`: a real `BindingWorker` (256-frame mirror pool) carries cap 64 and a recorded refusal moves only `pending_neigh_capacity_drops`.
- `rx_fill_frames_is_total_minus_reserved_tx_15096`: fill derivation across drivers/rings.
- Controls re-pinned: `first_packet_buffers_siblings_duplicate_drop`, `new_key_capacity_boundary`, `record_drop_counts_capacity_separately`, and the live `invariant_n1` buffering half.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp --bin xpf-userspace-dp pending_admission` → 5 passed
- `… -- rx_fill_frames_is_total_minus_reserved_tx_15096 invariant_n1 pending_admission` → 7 passed
- `… -- neighbor_dispatch umem_sizing` → 56 passed, 1 ignored
- `… -- umem_sizing pending` → 67 passed, 1 ignored

Full log: `docs/log/15096.md`. Lab leg deferred to main: a /64 SYN sweep at ring=1024 should leave `rx_fill_ring_empty_descs` flat with an established flow unaffected.

Closes #15096

## PR #15436 — config: reject prefix-less VRRP virtual-address at strict compile (#15050) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15050-campaign`

Closes #15050

## Summary
The packed hierarchical one-liner `vrrp-group 1 virtual-address 10.0.1.100;` carried a bare (prefix-less) VIP past `SchemaValidate` and strict compile: the value rides the instance node's Keys as an unvalidated identity token, so the schema's `ValidateIPv4CIDR`/`ValidateIPv6CIDR` leaf never saw it. At runtime `pkg/vrrp` passes the string verbatim to `netlink.ParseAddr`, which requires a prefix; the failure is recorded as a failed VIP, `ok()` is false, and #5082 fail-closed reverts every promotion to BACKUP — the VRRP-protected gateway has no owner on every node carrying the config (reachable via hierarchical load / day-0 / config-sync, not via `set`).

## Fix
- New compiled-`*Config` gate `validateVRRPVIPPrefixStrict` (`compiler_validate_strict_vrrp_vipprefix.go`), wired beside the #8483 timers gate: strict commit/commit-check hard-rejects a parseable-but-prefix-less VIP, naming interface/unit/group/VIP and the corrected spelling.
- Tolerant load/peer-sync downgrades to a warning (`lenientVRRPVIPPrefix`, #1960 no-brick) and `normalizeBareVRRPVIPs` (tail gates) rewrites the bare VIP with the enclosing unit address prefix, or `/32`/`/128` when no same-family prefix exists — so the tolerant config **actuates** instead of reverting every promotion forever.
- Garbage literals remain the #7577 empty gate's concern (not re-reported).
- Incidental fix in the #15046 children gate: its Keys-packed scan now skips bracketed multi-value tokens of a `multi` leaf, so a bracketed `virtual-address [ a b ]` list's second address is no longer misjudged as an unknown group property (exposed by the new regression's bracketed spelling; bracketed lists are a supported #1813 spelling).
- Neighbour fixtures that authored bare VIPs as incidental setup now author the CIDR spelling (same addresses/assertions): `vrrp_track`, `dual_ast_differential`, #6779 count lines, #7577 control, #5837 DNAT, #15046/#15048 sibling tests; one #15047 fixture tracks its own configured `reth0` instead of an undeclared interface.

## Validation
- New regression (`compiler_validate_strict_vrrp_vipprefix_15050_test.go`): RED on `origin/master` (packed bare VIP commits clean — verified with a probe on a pristine base worktree), GREEN with the fix. Strict rejects packed / bracketed-bare-first / braced / IPv6; CIDR controls commit unchanged; lenient warns and normalizes `10.0.1.100` → `10.0.1.100/24`; host-prefix fallback passes the strict gate after normalization.
- Full VRRP-named suite green except `TestVRRPCrossGroupDifferentInterfacesCommits`, which fails identically on current `origin/master` for the unrelated #15034 unit-without-vlan-id reason. `pkg/vrrp` suite green; `go build ./...` green; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean on touched files.
- Other pre-existing failures confirmed identical on base: `TestZoneInterface*` (#14139), `TestSchemaValidate_Interfaces_AcceptedValuesCompileAsWritten` (#14574), compact censuses #2419/#8690, `TestDualASTDifferential/security-nat*`.

Log: `docs/log/15050.md`. Never merge — review only.

## PR #15437 — userspace-dp: bound L3 reverse bucket cost under SNAT fan-in (#15087) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15087-campaign`

Why:
  l3_reverse_index keyed every SNAT forward session by the
  protocol-erased (family, server, SNAT address) identity in a linear
  SmallVec bucket, so insert (contains), removal (retain), and every
  flowless-fragment probe cost O(bucket) — O(N) in the live
  same-destination session count toward one popular destination
  (resolver, CDN edge, bench target) on the worker session-table path.

What:
  Replace the bucket interior with L3ReverseBucket: a keyed hashed
  handle set plus per-protocol member counts (session/mod.rs), kept
  exact at the same insert/remove sites by passing the member's real
  reverse protocol. The fragment probe (session/lookup.rs) now decides
  from counts plus a bounded 8-member verification walk that
  re-derives live slab records; presence of an unvisited counted
  member answers fail-closed TRUE, matching every live outcome.
  NOT changed: the L3 key shape, 255-sentinel semantics, domain
  admission, the other NAT indexes, or GC ownership.

Validation:
  New session/l3_reverse_bucket_15087_tests.rs (6 cells): structural
  pin fails to compile on pristine master (5 errors naming the
  SmallVec bucket), 100k insert/remove flat (0.48s), probe-vs-control
  flat at 2k fan-in, survivor/mixed-protocol/plain/expiry controls.
  Post-rebase: l3_reverse_bucket_15087 filter 5 passed; session::
  filter 471 passed. The frag-filter cohort's 10 failures reproduce
  on sibling pristine-master binaries (shared global frag-assoc
  state) and are not this change — see docs/log/15087.md.

Risk:
  Fragment gate gains one bounded over-drop corner (all-expired
  bucket larger than the probe budget returns TRUE until GC).
  Per-identity memory grows by a 256-entry counts array plus hash-set
  overhead, bounded by distinct NAT destinations, not sessions.

Closes #15087

## PR #15438 — userspace-dp: reclaim oldest completed anchor across zones at shard cap (#15103) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15103-campaign`

## Why

`OverlapTracker::check_and_record_fragment_detailed` reclaimed completed anchors only at the candidate's own 32-entry `(routing_domain, ingress_zone)` reserve, and only over that zone's entries. At the fixed 64-entry shard cap it returned `ShardFull` with no reclaim at all. Two zones holding 32 completed anchors each therefore starved every third zone in the same routing domain and shard: all new fragmented datagrams for zone C dropped fail-closed for the anchors' TTL, even though completed anchors are the explicitly reclaimable class (#14321). Reachable by #14321's own attacker shape (4 untrusted senders) plus any moderately busy second zone.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs`, shard-cap branch only: when the shard is at 64 and the candidate's zone is below its own reserve (guaranteed by ordering — the own-zone check above either reclaimed, refused, or left it below 32), reclaim the globally oldest COMPLETED anchor (`overlap_entry_complete`: `pending == 0`, not failed, ranges cover the terminal end) of any zone in the candidate's routing domain before refusing. Incomplete anchors are never reclaimed; with none reclaimable the refusal is byte-identical to before (same `FRAG_OVERLAP_SHARD_FULL_DROPPED` bump + `ShardFull` reason).
- New observability counter `FRAG_OVERLAP_CROSS_ZONE_RECLAIMED` (global atomic alongside its siblings).
- Module docs (fairness + failure-direction bullets) updated at the mechanism. Callers (`poll_descriptor` pre-check / post-commit TX record) unchanged — they already drop on `ShardFull` and forward on admission.
- NOT changed: sender quota (8/shard), per-zone reserve (32), shard cap (64), TTLs, range geometry, shard hashing, `FragAssoc` (no completed-anchor class; A74-02 is OverlapTracker-only).

Deviations from the issue's fix direction, recorded per instructions:
1. The `and/or reserve per active zone` alternative was not taken: dividing 64 by active zones shrinks every zone's reserve as zones join, changes admitted behaviour for the two-zone case, and contradicts #14321's fixed 32-entry reserve. The primary direction (globally-oldest completed reclaim) fully satisfies the acceptance probe.
2. "Add a FragAssoc refusal counter": the OverlapTracker `ShardFull` refusal already had both a global counter (`FRAG_OVERLAP_SHARD_FULL_DROPPED`) and a binding-local batched counter flushed to binding state; adding a second refusal counter would double-count. The counter added instead measures the new event (cross-zone reclaims), which is the operator-visible signal for this fix.

Security trade, explicit: an evicted completed anchor loses overlap protection for the remainder of its reassembly window — the identical trade #14321 already accepts at the per-zone cap, extended across zones in one domain. The prior behaviour (third-zone blackhole) is the worse failure.

## Validation

- RED (base `fde73e9b28` + test only): `third_zone_admitted_by_cross_zone_completed_reclaim_15103` FAILED — `zone-C victim must be admitted by cross-zone completed reclaim, reason=Some(ShardFull)` (zones A/B = 32 completed anchors each in one shard).
- GREEN (with fix): same test passes; also asserts zone A stays capped via its own-zone reclaim, `len()` stays 64, no `SHARD_FULL` bump, exactly one `CROSS_ZONE_RECLAIMED` bump, and a shard full of incomplete anchors still refuses zone C fail-closed with no eviction.
- Controls: `cargo test --bins fragment_overlap` — 44 passed; `cargo test --bins 9950` — 28 passed (includes `shard_full_drops_without_evicting_live_9950`, `cross_zone_domain_fill_cannot_starve_other_zone_14321`, `completed_entries_hold_shard_capacity_until_expiry_10285`, `completed_anchors_preserve_routing_domain_reserve_14009`).
- `rustfmt --check` on the file was already dirty on base (58 hunks pre-existing); the change adds no new fmt hunks beyond that baseline drift.

## Risk

Under sustained churn of completed datagrams across many zones in one shard, anchors rotate faster than their 30s TTL; the `FRAG_OVERLAP_CROSS_ZONE_RECLAIMED` rate makes this visible. No behaviour change when a shard is below 64 entries or the candidate's zone is at its own reserve.

Closes #15103

## PR #15439 — userspace-dp: honour RouteEntry.reject in FIB route selection (#15098) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15098-campaign`

## Summary
`RouteEntry.reject` was stored by `forwarding_build` (since #13949) but never read by route selection: `select_v4_route`/`select_v6_route` treated only `discard` as terminal. Every reject route lost its dataplane ICMP unreachable and was counted as `no_route`; a reject+next-hop row was **forwarded** as an ordinary gateway, and a next-table leak whose target LPM is a reject route resolved `NoRoute` inside the target and fell through to forwarding. Residual of `3743c24ffd`, whose message claims a FIB change its diff does not contain.

## Fix
- `select_v4_route` / `select_v6_route` (`forwarding/fib.rs`): `discard || reject` is the terminal row, under the identical #13950 drivable-fallback preference gate — a reject row never reaches next-hop selection.
- `Static` arms of `lookup_forwarding_resolution_v4_inner`/`_v6_inner`: return the zero-egress terminal resolution with `RejectRoute` when `reject` is set, `DiscardRoute` otherwise (reject wins if both flags set; the Go producer never sets both).
- Leak walk unchanged: it already returns any non-`NoRoute` disposition immediately, so a target-LPM `RejectRoute` is now terminal rather than a miss. No other consumer changes — the `RejectRoute` disposition, poll arm, reply builder, and counters already existed (#13949/#14021/#14237/#14319).

## Tests
- FIB (`tests_lpm_parity_9522.rs`, snapshot-built via production `build_forwarding_state`): `reject_only_route_rejects_v4_v6_15098`, `reject_with_next_hop_still_rejects_v4_v6_15098`, `leak_into_reject_target_rejects_v4_v6_15098`, plus discard/preference controls.
- Poll level (`reject_reply_tests.rs`): `reject_snapshot_resolves_and_enqueues_icmp_unreachable_15098` — reject snapshot → production FIB → poll arm seam → exactly one ICMPv4 destination-unreachable enqueued.
- **RED** (fix reverted, tests present): 4 failed, 1 control passed. **GREEN**: all 5 pass; neighbouring `afxdp::forwarding::` + `reject_reply` suites 408 passed, 0 failed.

Docs: `docs/log/15098.md`, terminal-reject note in `forwarding/README.md`.

Closes #15098

## PR #15441 — userspace-dp: record refused replay upserts as repair debt (#15105) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15105-campaign`

Why:
Both reconcile replay sites pushed synced-session rows through
`push_bounded` and discarded its refusal at the 4096-command queue cap:
the bring-up replay fans a full shared snapshot into brand-new queues
via `replicate_session_upsert`, and `replay_late_synced_sessions`
appends a fresh snapshot behind a retained prefix. Any shared table
over 4096 rows therefore handed each new worker only the first 4096
rows; the rest were absent, took no SNAT holder reservation, and
carried no repair obligation (#6929 residual; #11360 covered the
import path only).

What:
A refused `UpsertSynced` now records #11360 session-import repair debt,
positioned after the queue prefix at refusal and recorded under the
queue lock, in `replicate_session_upsert` (worker id resolved from the
generation `WorkerCommandQueues` via a new Arc-identity
`worker_id_for_queue`) and in `replay_late_synced_sessions` (worker id
threaded from the spawn caller; existing test callers updated). The
worker re-reads each refused key from shared authority at that FIFO
boundary, so deleted rows take the delete path instead of
resurrecting. The per-worker repair bound rises to
`2 * MAX_PENDING_WORKER_COMMANDS` so a full queue ahead of a larger
snapshot can obligate the whole refused tail. NOT changed: the queue
cap, the drain budget, or any non-replay producer's ordering.

Validation:
New `coordinator/tests.rs` cells
`bringup_replay_over_cap_records_import_repair_debt_15105` and
`late_replay_over_cap_records_import_repair_debt_15105` seed cap+1000
shared rows through the real replay helpers: RED on origin/master
`0e8ce36bba` ("recorded no repair debt"), GREEN post-fix with the queue
still capped at 4096 and the full refused tail (1000 / 1001 rows)
covered by due debt; #9718 late-import control green. Adjacent
`afxdp::coordinator`/`ha`/`session_glue`/`worker_queue` suites: 932
passed, 14 failed — 13 reproduce identically on unmodified
origin/master `3d5c595678` (base-attributed), the 14th was the #11360
overflow fixture, updated to the doubled bound and now green.

Risk:
Steady-state sibling replication now also records debt on refusal
instead of dropping silently; repairs re-read current shared authority
so they cannot resurrect superseded rows. Past the 8192 per-worker
repair bound the behaviour degrades to the pre-fix drop-counter-only
signal rather than failing live traffic closed.

Closes #15105

## PR #15443 — userspace-dp: gate GRE fragment reassembly on endpoint (#15095) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15095-campaign`

Why: the #14645 outer-fragment reassembler buffered every fragmented
proto-47 datagram reaching stage 6, with no check that the outer
destination was a native-GRE endpoint. A transit GRE/PPTP datagram
fragmented upstream was consumed fragment-by-fragment; on completion
decap missed, the stage returned Buffered, and the descriptor was
recycled with no counter. Fragmented transit GRE was never forwarded
and the loss was invisible on every operator surface.

when `gre::outer_frame_targets_gre_endpoint` finds the frame's

fragment falls through as `NotGre` to the ordinary flowless /
fragment-association path. Key, transport-domain, egress and
host-inbound checks still run at decap. A completed datagram whose
decap then refuses is counted once via the new
`GreDecapCounters::reassembled_decap_refusals`, surfaced Rust -> Go ->
Prometheus as `gre_reassembled_decap_refusals_total` /
`xpf_userspace_gre_reassembled_decap_refusals_total`. NOT changed: XDP
shim steering (it has no per-endpoint table; the helper now declines
non-endpoint fragments) and no per-source pool quota (the gate removes
the non-peer flood vector).

Validation: new `tests_gre_transit_frag_15095` (5 cells: transit head+
tail NotGre with no endpoints and with a different-pair tunnel,
to-self control byte-identical decap, 65-head non-peer flood cannot
block peer reassembly, keyed-to-unkeyed completed refusal counted
once). RED measured with only the gate conjunct reverted: 3 failed
("must return NotGre, not Buffered"), 2 controls passed. GREEN:
`cargo test -- 15095 14645 14652` = 10 passed;

## PR #15444 — userspace-dp: bound wildcard zone-pair expansion to slot budget (#15092) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15092-campaign`

Why:
`configured_zone_pairs()` materialised every concrete zone pair per wildcard/global rule into a `BTreeSet`: both-any inserted Z² pairs and each unscoped `junos-global` cloned the universe for another cross product. At 8000 zones one Any×Any scope is 64M pairs inside the snapshot build (2–3 builds per commit) — a control-plane stall of seconds — while `ColdPathSlotMap` can only assign 255 slots.

What:
- `policy.rs`: new `configured_zone_pairs_bounded(limit) -> ConfiguredZonePairs { pairs, overflow }`. Exact `zone_pair_index` pairs first (unchanged slot priority), then the wildcard/global tier generated as sorted per-scope cross-product streams merged k-way with dedup, stopping at the slots left after the exact tier plus one overflow probe. No cross product is materialised; an Any×Any scope (both-any or unscoped global) subsumes every other wildcard/global scope and becomes the sole stream. Exact-tier members reached again by the merge consume no budget. `configured_zone_pairs()` delegates at the slot budget (every pre-#15092 test config fits, so it equals the old set there).
- `forwarding_build/mod.rs`: builds via the bounded form and ORs `overflow` into `ColdPathSlotMap::overflow_active` — without it a capped 255-pair input is indistinguishable from an exact fit and the operator starvation flag never fires for this tier.
- `cold_path_hist.rs` / `afxdp/mod.rs`: `COLD_PATH_ASSIGNABLE_SLOTS` and the module widen to `pub(crate)` so `policy.rs` clamps to the same constant.
- `docs/log/15092.md`, `docs/userspace-dataplane-architecture.md`: bounded-generation note.

NOT changed: slot assignment/retention/zeroing in `ColdPathSlotMap::build`; the exact-tier set and its priority; policy evaluation tiers. At/under-capacity configs return byte-identical pair vectors.

Validation:
- RED: test-only patch (3 new `*_15092` policy tests) on clean `origin/master` `d85a1c085a` fails E0599 (`no method named configured_zone_pairs_bounded`) at every call site; the unbounded path it replaces materialises 64M pairs per Any×Any scope at the acceptance shape, so the <50 ms bound cannot be met.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bins configured_zone_pairs` 7/7 (incl. `configured_zone_pairs_bounded_8000_zones_15092`: 8000 zones + both-any + 256 unscoped globals returns `(1,1)..(1,255)` ascending with `overflow` inside the 7-test suite's 0.09 s; `*_matches_unbounded_prefix_15092` bounded == unbounded prefix at limits 3/6/255; `*_exact_priority_15092` exact pair first at limit 4, no budget consumed by exact duplicates at limit 26); `--bins cold_path` 49/49 (incl. `bounded_pairs_overflow_reaches_slot_map_15092`); `--bins policy::` 268/268.
- Neighbouring: `--bins forwarding_build` 305 passed, 1 failed (`wg_live_endpoint_survives_one_peer_edit_rebuild_14640`, reproduced identically on clean `d85a1c085a` — base-attributed, unrelated WireGuard leg). Pre-existing clippy `mut_from_ref` deny at `afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241` untouched.

Risk:
Over-capacity configs keep the pre-fix ascending `(from, to)` slot winners and exact-pair priority. `overflow_active` fires for the same configs as before, reached without the stall. Residual: thousands of distinct scoped globals pay O(emitted × scopes) merge probes (≤255 × scopes), trivial next to the removed cross products.

Closes #15092

## PR #15448 — ipsec: promote the recovered set on a commit-path partial clear (#15128) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15128-campaign`

Closes #15128

## Problem (A90-01)
The commit path reaches `clearConfig` via `ApplyGeneration` with an empty config (`pkg/daemon/ipsec_sa_rg_9139.go:103`), not via `Clear()` (factory reset only). On a partial clear where charon still holds a prior connection, `clearConfig` rolls charon back to the prior file and returns `partialApplyError{names: priorSet, hashes: priorHashes, clear: true}`. `Clear()` promotes `pae.names`/`pae.hashes`, but `ApplyGeneration` discarded them and promoted the empty set — so xpf forgot VPNs charon still runs, their SAs were never terminated, and the persisted record said none. Deleting every VPN (e.g. decommissioning a compromised peer) under a partial clear left the deleted VPNs' configs and PSKs loaded in charon and on disk while xpf's record said empty.

## Fix
`ApplyGeneration` now promotes `pae.names`/`pae.hashes` for the clear case too, matching `Clear()`. The empty-set case is already encoded as `names={}` by `clearConfig` (and the `names == nil` encoding still promotes `{}`), so neighbouring behaviour is unchanged. The `partialApplyError` doc comment now states that for `clearConfig`, `names` is the recovered set charon runs.

## Regression (RED/GREEN)
Added to `pkg/ipsec/partial_load_14589_test.go`, driving the exact commit path through the same fake charon as the existing `Clear()` control:
- `TestA90PartialClearViaApplyEmpty` — partial clear via empty-config `ApplyGeneration`: prior file restored byte-identical, `prevConnNames` == charon's loaded set `{a,b}`.
- `TestA90FollowUpAfterApplyEmpty` — a later successful empty-config `ApplyGeneration` with live SAs for `a`/`b` must issue `--terminate --ike` for both.

Both fail on `origin/master` (`prev=map[] want prior {a,b}`) and pass after the fix. The `Clear()` control `TestPartialClearRestoresPriorFile14589` is unchanged and stays green.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 'TestA90|TestPartialClearRestoresPriorFile14589|TestPartialLoad|TestNonPartial' -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1`: 62 pre-existing render failures on pristine `origin/master`, identical count with the fix (checked by stashing the fix) — no new failures.
- `go vet ./pkg/ipsec/` clean; `gofmt` clean; `go build ./pkg/ipsec/ ./pkg/daemon/` OK

Docs: `docs/log/15128.md`, `pkg/ipsec/README.md` updated.

## PR #15450 — frr: omit multihop BFD peer without a valid local-address (#15135) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15135-campaign`

Why: #14587 keys every iBGP neighbor and every ebgp-multihop neighbor as a multihop bfdd peer, but appends `local-address` only when one is configured. A routine Junos shape — directly connected iBGP, or multihop eBGP, with `bfd-liveness-detection` and no `local-address` — therefore renders the bare line `peer X multihop`, which bfdd 10.7.1 rejects. `frr-reload.py` exits 1 and every commit of such a config fails with a degraded retry that can never converge.

What: `bfdSection.render()` in `pkg/frr/bfd.go` now skips a multihop peer whose `localAddress` is empty or fails the #9493 single-token belt (the same validity test as the BGP `update-source` line), logging a warning naming the peer. The neighbor still renders `neighbor X bfd profile <p>`, so the configured timers reach bgpd's own dynamic multihop session via the profile and the `bfd` block survives on the profile alone. No single-hop fallback stanza (the proven #14587 orphan) and no new commit gate. Neighbors with a valid local-address render `peer X [vrf V] multihop local-address L` byte-identically; single-hop peers are untouched. NOT changed: compiler/validation — the render-side primary fix direction was chosen over requiring `local-address` at commit.

Validation: new `TestBGPBFDMultihopNoLocalAddress15135` (iBGP, ebgp-multihop, whitespace-invalid local-address, and VRF accumulator cells, plus keyed/single-hop controls) fails pre-fix rendering `peer 10.255.0.9 multihop` / `peer 192.0.2.10 multihop` and passes after. The one assertion in `TestBGPBFDMultihopProfile14587` that pinned the bare line is flipped; its with-local-address and single-hop controls stay green. `go test ./pkg/frr/ -run 'TestBGPBFDMultihop' -count=1` PASS; full `pkg/frr` suite shows only 3 failures confirmed identical on pristine `origin/master` (base-attributed, unrelated). `go vet ./pkg/frr/` and gofmt clean.

Risk: only the no-valid-local-address multihop leg changes — those neighbors lose the invalid, reload-breaking static stanza and keep timer delivery via the bound BFD profile. Setting `local-address` restores the keyed stanza exactly as before. The four bfdd dry-run cells from the issue are covered at render level by the new test's four legs; a live bfdd dry-run remains a lab verify.

Closes #15135
