## PR #15451 — userspace-dp: carry persistent siblings as lease joins on reseed (#15110) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15110-campaign`

## Why

`reseed_retained_from` re-reserved each live flow through the non-persistent `reserve_flow`. Persistent siblings share one lease and one translated tuple but are distinct flow keys, so the first sibling claimed the occupancy bit as a plain PAT record and every later sibling was refused by the occupied-bit check. The refused sibling was not carried while its session kept forwarding, and the survivor's record named no lease — so its first release freed a tuple still in use: the #6765 reissue / reply-misdelivery hazard for persistent pools, via an ordinary add-an-address pool edit (A76-03).

## What

- Snapshot pass in `reseed_retained_from` now computes the non-deterministic persistent leases that have at least one live flow itself carried in range.
- The port-bearing carry arm carries records naming such a lease via `reserve_flow_maybe_persistent(..., Some((key, lease.timeout_ns)))` — first sibling mints the lease, later siblings join it, bit frees only at lease teardown (last release + carried idle timeout). Both untracked and per-worker holder arms.
- `dropped_persistent_*` counting skips carried leases; idle leases and removed-address leases are still counted/reported (#7560 semantics preserved).
- NOT changed: address-only carry, clear-replay fences (a cleared lease stays fenced; the join falls back to a plain reservation), deterministic BIB leases (kept on the plain path — their `deterministic_identity` cannot be rebuilt from a flow record).

## Validation

- New `nat/tests_reseed_persistent_siblings_15110.rs` (4 cells): binder asserts `refused == 0`, `reseeded == 2`, one lease with `active_flows == 2`, bit held until both siblings release + idle expiry. RED on `origin/master` 780fab7b3c (`refused: left 1, right 0`), GREEN after the fix.
- Controls: plain PAT carry mints no lease; idle persistent lease still counted dropped; out-of-range siblings still skipped.
- Two #7560 cells in `tests_pool.rs` updated from pinning the drop to pinning the carry.
- Full `nat::` suite: 686 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (debug `--bins`).

## Risk

Carried leases are minted `imported: true` by the existing synced-join constructor, so idle-lease export skips them until a local flow completes — conservative (no peer echo) and self-healing on completion.

Closes #15110

## PR #15455 — userspace-dp: credit exact queues their self-park lag at low rates (#15100) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15100-campaign`

## Summary

A backlogged exact queue parks for its own frame-refill time (1500 B at 8000 B/s = 187.5 ms), but the v8 lease rotation credited at most K×EPOCH = 1.6 ms per visit, banked the rest into an epoch-sized carry (12.8 B at 8000 B/s — never enough to reassemble a frame), and dropped it past the fixed 51.2 ms STALL cutoff. 64k/128k exact classes delivered 0% and 1 Mbps 29.5% of their configured rate.

Fix: rate-relative windows in the shared CoS lease.
- `lag_window_ns_for_rate(rate)` = max(K×EPOCH, one full frame's refill) and `stall_window_ns_for_rate(rate)` = max(fixed floor, 2× lag window) in `types/shared_cos_lease/epoch.rs`.
- Byte-sized carry reservoir/drain stored on `V8State` at lease creation (`lease.rs`), read by `rotate_epoch_v8.rs`. Per-rotation burst stays bounded (max(K×rate×EPOCH, one frame) + bounded drain); a genuine stall beyond the window still cold-resumes to one epoch and drops carry.
- Park-aware wakeup guard in `queue_service/settle.rs`: a queue already holding its need wakes next tick instead of parking for a frame refill.
- Rates whose fixed K window already covers a frame are byte-identical (all pre-existing #1630/#1863 carry cells unchanged in behaviour).

Validation: RED pre-fix — `new_v8(8000)` acquiring at t0 and t0+187.5 ms granted 1 B (want ≥1499); sustained 1 Mbps self-park delivered 24000/180000 B. GREEN — 7 #15100 cells pass; `shared_cos_lease` 109/109, `token_bucket` 27/27, combined neighbouring run 136/136.

Closes #15100

## PR #15456 — userspace-dp: bind neighbor probe token to probed MAC (#15097) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15097-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes A66-05: the kernel-monitor `NUD_PROBE` token no longer authorizes a MAC the dataplane refused.

- Solicited-probe evidence is now MAC-bound (`ProbedNeighbor`): locally-issued probes (warmer/resolver/dispatch) stay key-only; a kernel `NUD_PROBE` records a token only for the lladdr it carries **and** only when that is the dataplane's held MAC.
- On a refused probe (kernel probing attacker MAC `A`, dataplane holding `G`): mint no token, clear stale evidence, and rate-limited re-assert `G` into the kernel (`RTM_NEWNEIGH` REPLACE, `NUD_STALE`) so the kernel re-probes `G`. Genuinely moved hosts then fail to `NUD_FAILED` and resolve fresh.
- MAC-aware solicited peek in both monitor arms (v4+v6) and the direct XSK ARP arm.

Closes #15097

## Tests
- New: `refused_kernel_probe_mints_no_token_and_reasserts_held_mac_15097` (v4), `..._v6_15097`, `held_mac_probe_still_converges_and_failed_recovers_15097`, `refused_probe_reassert_is_rate_limited_15097`, `mac_bound_probe_token_authorizes_only_the_probed_mac_15097`.
- RED on pristine `origin/master` (3d5c595, test-only probe cell): step 3 returned `Upserted` — attacker MAC installed. GREEN post-fix with `G` kept at step 3 and exactly one `(key, G)` re-assert.

## PR #15457 — config: let nested apply-groups override outer groups (#15033) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15033-campaign`

## Summary
An outer `apply-groups` beat a nested one, opposite to Junos: the nested value met a peer already adopted from the outer group and was dropped as inline-wins. A global group's permissive interface filter (`PERMISSIVE`) therefore beat a per-interface hardening group's `STRICT` filter on a green commit.

## Fix
`pkg/config/ast_groups.go` now tracks, per adopted node, the origin level of the apply-groups application that adopted it (`groupExpandBudget.applyLevelByNode15033`, with `applyOriginLevel15033` set around each level's merge in the extracted `expandLevelRefs15033` so recursive container merges inherit the application's level, not the routing depth). Adoptions are tagged via pre-merge identity snapshots of the destination and descendant lists (first tag wins, so an ancestral merge never re-tags a leaf a nested application placed).

A later, strictly deeper application replaces a shallower adopted scalar/non-union peer (leaf override arm, leaf-list block arm, #4325 container guard). Inline peers never yield; same/deeper peers keep first-wins; leaf-list and range-free port unions are unchanged.

## Tests (RED → GREEN)
New `pkg/config/apply_groups_nested_level_15033_test.go` through strict `CompileConfig`:
- `TestNestedApplyGroupsBeatsOuter15033` — outer `PERMISSIVE` vs nested `STRICT` interface filter → `STRICT` (fails on base with `FilterInputV4="PERMISSIVE"`)
- `TestNestedApplyGroupsScalarBeatsOuter15033` — nested scalar `host-name` wins, inline `domain-name` kept (fails on base with `HostName="OUTER"`)
- `TestInlineStillBeatsNestedApplyGroups15033` — authored inline filter still beats both groups (control, green before/after)
- `TestOuterOnlyApplyGroupsControl15033` — outer-only inheritance unchanged (control, green before/after)

Validation: targeted apply-groups suites pass after rebase onto current master; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean. Full `pkg/config` suite run recorded in `docs/log/15033.md`.

Closes #15033

## PR #15458 — config: reject nameless lldp interface blocks instead of panicking (#15138) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15138-campaign`

Why:
`protocols { lldp { interface { disable; } } }` (and `interface { ge-0/0/1; }` / `interface { ge-0/0/1 { disable; } }`) panicked `compileProtocols` with `slice bounds out of range [2:1]`. Those block spellings carry `Keys=["interface"]` with the would-be name (or a bare `disable`) nested as a child; `nodeVal` falls back to that child's name, so the compiler treated `"disable"`/`"ge-0/0/1"` as an interface name and then sliced `child.Keys[2:]` on a 1-key node. The panic is reachable on the strict commit, authenticated load-override, tolerant `Store.Load`, and HA `SyncApply` paths with no `recover` above any of them, so a malformed but parseable config crashed xpfd.

What:
`compileProtocols` now treats only a name packed on the LLDP interface statement itself (`Keys[1]`, `len >= 2`) as a named interface. A nameless statement is rejected on strict compile with `protocols lldp interface: an interface name is required` (fail closed) and warned about with the same message plus `(ignored on tolerant load)` and dropped on the tolerant paths via the existing `lenientLLDPInterfaceTokens14616` opt, so a persisted config still boots. The guard makes the #14616 `Keys[2:]` read provably in range. Regression tests in `pkg/config` and a store probe (`CommitCheck` rejects, `SyncApply` tolerates) pin the behaviour; named block/packed/plain/flat controls are unchanged. NOT changed: `nodeVal`, the LLDP schema node, or LLDP runtime.

Validation:
RED pre-fix: all three nameless spellings panic `CompileConfig` and `CompileConfigLenient` with `[2:1]`. FAIL-ON-REVERT measured: tests kept + fix reverted fails `TestLLDPNamelessInterfaceBlockDoesNotPanicStrict15138` with the same panic at `compiler_protocols.go:84`. GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestLLDP|TestPrefixList|TestNoSchemaPathPanics' -count=1` PASS (census 1318 schema paths, 0 panics); `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 'TestLLDPNamelessBlock|TestLLDPNamedBlockStore' -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configstore/` clean.

Risk:
Strict commits carrying a previously-panicking nameless LLDP block now reject instead of crashing; tolerant loads warn and drop that entry. No dataplane or daemon behaviour change.

Closes #15138

## PR #15461 — userspace-dp: rebase stale scheduler lease on re-introduction (#15093) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15093-campaign`

Why:
A scheduler heartbeat lease stamped in an earlier scheduled era survived
a no-scheduled-policy era (Go sends no heartbeats then), so a snapshot
re-introducing a scheduled rule published already expired: scheduled
permits missed and inactive scheduled denies were enforced until the
post-apply heartbeat landed, revoking sessions revalidated in the window.

What:
Rust: SchedulerHeartbeatLease gains a prev_snapshot_scheduled era marker;
note_snapshot_published rebases the receipt stamp only on a
no-schedule -> schedule transition and only when already expired. The
coordinator drives it via publish_snapshot_policy after the
worker-visible RuntimeView store in the same-plan refresh and the full
reconcile, so rejected snapshots never rebase the live lease. Go:
requestApplySnapshotPreparedLocked sends a best-effort heartbeat before
apply_snapshot on re-introduction (gated on a prior heartbeat version);
the heartbeat send is factored into sendSchedulerHeartbeatLocked.
NOT changed: heartbeat cadence, lease length, expiry semantics in a
continuous era, version-zero never-expires behaviour.

Validation:
cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml -- 15093: 4 passed
(coordinator refresh-path, lease rebase, inactive-deny, controls);
scheduler filter: 33 passed. RED: without the production files the Rust
tests fail to compile (E0599) and the Go ordering test fails with
[apply_snapshot scheduler_heartbeat]. go test
./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestScheduled|TestSchedulerHeartbeat:
ok. Full package failure name-set matches the stashed base except three
timing-flaky tests that flip in both trees.

Risk:
Deferred-activation applies do not publish forwarding, so they do not
drive the Rust era marker until the deferred bring-up reconcile. A
Manager restart loses its version counter; the Rust publish rebase
covers that window.

Closes #15093

## PR #15462 — userspace-dp: suppress SYN-cookie replies on tunnel decap (#15131) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15131-campaign`

Why: GRE/WireGuard decap replaces the inner frame with a synthetic
zero-MAC Ethernet header marked TUNNEL_DECAP_INGRESS_FLAG. The screen
SynCookieChallenge leg and the session-miss AckRst leg in
poll_descriptor both funnel into enqueue_syn_cookie_reply, which
gated only the #12319 fabric stamp; the builders reflect the fake
header, so a challenged tunnel inner queued an unencapsulated
SYN-ACK / ACK-RST with dst/src MAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 on the physical
underlay binding, counted as sent.

What: enqueue_syn_cookie_reply now returns false at the top on
TUNNEL_DECAP_INGRESS_FLAG, before the fabric-stamp gate, the TX
budget, and any sent counter -- the #12864 reject / #14642 TE/PTB
posture. One choke covers both cookie legs; the builders have no
other production caller. NOT changed: a shared generated-reply
helper (each shipped gate checks the flag inline), the decap
producers, and native / fabric-stamp cookie behavior.

Validation: three new cookie_reply_tests (tunnel SynAck sent=false
with no pending TX and no sent counter, tunnel AckRst likewise,
native control still sends) fail on origin/master ccc2a6af55 with
the gate assertions and pass after the fix; cookie_reply +
reject_reply filter run 76 passed, 0 failed.

Risk: tunnelled SYNs under a syn-cookie screen now get no SYN-ACK
(the #12864 suppression posture) instead of a bogus underlay frame;
legitimate tunnel clients rely on the peer endpoint, matching the
reject/TE/PTB behavior already shipped.

Closes #15131

## PR #15463 — userspace-dp: scope NAT-external local delivery to matching rules (#15118) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15118-campaign`

## Summary
Every non-`off` DNAT/static-NAT destination was registered firewall-local keeping only its routing-instance, so the FIB LocalDelivered *untranslated* traffic to that address (any from-zone, interface, source, protocol or port) instead of routing it — a scoped `udp/53` DNS redirect blackholed `tcp/443`/ICMP to the same real host (A77-03).

Registration in `local_v*` is unchanged (proxy-ARP/ND, inject-source ownership, anti-poison and Stage-11 `local_nat_to_self_*` metadata keep the full set); the local-delivery *decision* is now rule-scoped at resolution time:

- `DnatTable::nat_local_match_possible` / `StaticNatTable::nat_local_match_possible` reuse the real match gates (DNAT exact/wildcard-port/protocol-any/prefix tiers with zone/interface/RI/source/L4 constraints; static port+source+from-scope). `off`/poisoned outcomes never claim.
- `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` claims an untranslated NAT address only for a matching flow; otherwise `lookup_forwarding_resolution_without_nat_local` suppresses just that address's NAT registration and the packet follows the FIB (interface addresses on the same IP stay local).
- Wired into session-miss resolution only when no DNAT/static/NPTv6/NAT64 translation fired (translated packets still resolve the translated target; DNAT-to-self/#9529 unchanged) and into the flowless base resolution for untranslated NAT-local destinations.

## Regression
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/tests_nat_scope_15118.rs` — 5 cells over the real snapshot → `build_forwarding_state` → scoped-resolution path: non-matching protocol/port, wrong zone, out-of-scope source, v6 twin, zone-scoped vs unscoped static NAT, and the DNAT-to-self control.

- RED on `origin/master` (same file, scoped helper stubbed to the pre-fix plain lookup): all 5 fail with `LocalDelivery` on the non-matching cells.
- GREEN after the fix: 5/5 pass.
- Neighbour controls: #3769 table-scoped FIB cells (static/DNAT/v6/default/unscoped) + all 9 #9529 host-bound post-DNAT cells pass.

Docs: `docs/log/15118.md`, forwarding README note.

Closes #15118

## PR #15465 — userspace-dp: resolve NAT wire survivors from owner index on removal (#15106) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15106-campaign`

**Userspace-dataplane change, not agent infrastructure.** Rust-only (`userspace-dp`); no agent harness operation.

## Why

#14383 reintroduced the #11299 shape: every NAT'd forward-session removal in `remove_shared_session_if` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/shared_ops/store.rs`) scanned the whole shared session map while holding its mutex, so lock-held close cost grew linearly with the shared table (~0.6 ms/close at 100k rows in a debug build per the issue measurement) — a potential loss-of-appliance-availability risk on the session-close path.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/mod.rs`: `SharedNatAmbiguityIndex` now also carries a per-wire-key owner multiset — `WireOwnerMultiset` (`FastMap<SessionKey, WireOwnerRoster>`), roster `SmallVec<[SessionKey; 2]>` — under the **same mutex** as the ambiguity aliases, plus a `wire_saturated` latch (fail-closed above the 16_384 wire-key cap, mirroring `saturated`). Methods: `observe_wire_owner` (idempotent per owner), `remove_wire_owner`, `wire_owners_trusted`, `wire_first_owner`, `reset_wire_owners`, `wire_owner_count`; `clear()` resets roster/latches.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/shared_ops/store.rs`: `publish_shared_session` records the live owner before the wire map write (same order as the existing #14383 observe). `remove_shared_session_if` resolves survivors in **O(1)**: exactly one remaining owner → restore its wire alias + `reset_to_owner`; none → ownership-checked alias delete (#9679) + `forget`; two or more → stays ambiguous. The roster is trusted only when it actually recorded the removed owner (exact count step) and neither saturation latch is set. Untrusted state (saturated, or a session seeded by a bare map insert that never observed an owner) falls back to the exact pre-fix `.take(2)` scan and reseeds the roster when the scan can name every survivor (count < 2); a roster owner absent from `shared_sessions` fails closed.

## Regression / acceptance

- `remove_shared_session_if_resolves_wire_survivor_from_owner_index_15106` (debug + release): seeds 2,000 unrelated NAT'd rows, publishes a colliding DNAT pair through the real path, then removes via `remove_shared_session_if` — survivor restores and `is_unique_for`; a 3-owner leg drains 3→2 (stays ambiguous) →1 (resolves) →0 (roster empty, alias forgotten), all asserted with `wire_owner_count`.
- `remove_shared_session_if_nat_removal_cost_15106` (release-only, `#[ignore]`d manual probe, same shape as the #11299 churn probe): median `remove_shared_session_if` close of a DNAT victim at 1k vs 100k rows, bound 100k ≤ 2×1k. **Exercised:** 1k=1473ns vs 100k=1424ns, ratio **0.97** — passes. RED claim: pre-fix the mechanism cell fails (no roster APIs / scan-backed removal) and the probe's 100k median scales ~linearly; the probe was not re-run against a pristine-master release binary in this lane, so probe-RED is by construction/mechanism, not a measured pristine-binary run.
- Controls staying green: `shared_forward_wire*` (3), `publish_and_remove_shared_session_tracks*` (3), `remove_shared_session_if_*` including #10612/#13672 (3) — all pass. Full `session_glue::tests`: 253 passed / 2 failed — `flush_session_deltas_update_syncs_without_an_rt_flow_create_9412` and `shared_nat_displacement_counter_counts_collisions_not_republishes`, the same failures recorded on this branch before the fix (outside the changed mechanism).
- `cargo clippy --bin xpf-userspace-dp --tests` completed with the crate's pre-existing warning profile. Tree-wide `cargo fmt --check` is dirty on unmodified master under this toolchain; touched files were not wholesale-reformatted to avoid mass churn.

## Risk

Bounded to wire-key owner bookkeeping; no Go, wire-format, or neighbouring-path change. A future publish path that inserts into `shared_sessions` without `observe_wire_owner` degrades to the legacy scan + reseed rather than mis-resolving. New index memory: one roster per distinct wire key (inline 2, same 16k cap discipline as the alias index, fail-closed at saturation).

## Not in this PR

- NAT reverse-alias (`nat_ambiguities`) owner multiset — the issue scopes to the forward-wire leg only.
- Live-hardware validation of close latency at 100k rows (the release probe is the in-repo proxy).

Refs: #11299 (same class, closed), #14383 (introduced the scan).

Closes #15106

## PR #15466 — config: reject unknown SNMP community children (#15124) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15124-campaign`

## Summary

An unknown child of `snmp community <c>` — `client 10.0.0.0/8`, `clinets …`, `client-list-nam L`, or any other undeclared keyword — was skipped by both community walks in `compileSNMP` with no error or warning, so a one-letter typo in the operator-authored source ACL left the community answering **every** source (an empty allowlist reads as allow-all) on a green commit. Prior fixes (#4289, #4834, #5472, #5833, #5898, #8778, #9416, #10687) each repaired a named spelling; none added a default arm. This adds the default arm.

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: judge every community block on the same views the compiler reads (expanded children via `expandFlatRun`, statements chain-nested under `authorization`/`routing-instance`, and the Keys-packed run on the community node scanned with schema arity) against the schema-declared permitted set plus the inert `view`/`logical-system` knobs.
  - **Strict** (commit / commit-check): hard-reject naming the offending token — never the community name, which is a secret.
  - **Lenient** (load / peer-sync): warn and quarantine the affected community to deny-all, sticky across same-name merge blocks, exactly like #5833's malformed-token quarantine.
  - Also warn on both paths about a defined-but-unreferenced `snmp client-list` (the usual residue of a `client-list-nam` typo).
- Deliberately **not** `closedWorld` on the community schema: that flag inherits and was measured (#9265) to refuse the legal flat-set chain `community <c> client-list-name L authorization read-only` and the deliberate accept-with-advisory `view` knob. The gate is scoped to the community level and reads its permitted set from the schema, so a child declared later is permitted automatically.
- Ratchets: `/snmp/community` moves `stillFailOpen` → `coveredDownstream` in `instance_name_armed_9265_test.go` (same verdict `/snmp/trap-group` carries for its #2990 gate); the schema-blind baseline entry stays with the reason recorded.
- Docs: `docs/log/15124.md`, `docs/feature-coverage.md`.

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/snmp_community_unknown_15124_test.go`:
  - Strict cells for `client`/`clinets`/`client-list-nam`/`zzbogus` in flat-set, braced, and Keys-packed spellings — **RED on `origin/master`** (verified in a base worktree: compiled clean, allow-all) and GREEN after.
  - Lenient cell: boots, warns naming the token, quarantines the affected community to deny-all while a well-formed sibling keeps its policy.
  - Controls: the `clients` enforcement is unchanged (listed source admitted, unlisted denied), the #9416 flat-set chain still commits, a braced community with every declared child still commits, `view` keeps its advisory, and a view *named* `clients` is treated as a value.
- Neighbouring SNMP suites (`TestSNMP*`, trap-group, inert-knob, packed-community) pass; the `/snmp/community` 9265 row passes. Pre-existing failures in the 9091/9265 ratchets (BGP teardown containers, DHCP pool subnets, VRRP track-interface rows) were base-attributed on `origin/master`.
- RED evidence was also captured pre-fix via probe: strict compile of all three typo spellings returned no error and no warning, lenient allowed `8.8.8.8`.

## Risk

A community carrying a genuinely unmodelled Junos child now rejects at strict commit instead of silently ignoring it; the tolerant path still boots with a deny-all quarantine for that community only. Inert `view`/`logical-system` knobs keep their accept-with-advisory posture — no neighbouring behaviour changes.

Closes #15124

## PR #15469 — ipsec: reject name-only full match on partial-load recovery (#15141) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15141-campaign`

## Why
#14589 partial-load recovery treated a full NAME-set match from `ListLoadedConns` as "candidate loaded" and returned the candidate hashes. When charon refuses a changed existing connection (e.g. its new certificate fails to load), the connection stays loaded under its OLD content, so the loaded name set equals the rendered set while charon runs the prior generation. `prevConnHashes` adopted a rotation charon never loaded, `promoteConnNames` saw no change, and the SA established under the superseded PSK/auth was never torn down — the #10878 guarantee lost, including on a later loadable generation.

## What
- `recoverPartialLoad14589` (pkg/ipsec/manager.go): the name-only full-set shortcut is removed; the reported set is always re-filed and re-loaded. On a full-set match, the confirm step compares before/after loaded CONTENT (`loadedContentStale15141`) and a content change diverts to the existing true rollback, promoting the prior hashes so a later loadable generation tears the stale SA down.
- `parseListConnsRaw` (pkg/ipsec/list_conns.go): each loaded connection now carries `LoadedConn.Content`, a SHA-256 fingerprint of everything charon reports inside its `list-conn` event (auth subsections, proposals, selectors, endpoints). `LoadedConns.Equal` is deliberately unchanged.
- Summary-lied / raced-to-full recoveries (content unchanged by the verification reload) still promote the candidate hashes and tear down the stale SA on the same apply — pinned by a control cell.
- NOT changed: `promoteConnNames`, teardown/re-initiation, the subset and prior-set/hybrid recovery arms, `clearConfig`.

## Validation
- New `pkg/ipsec/partial_refused_existing_15141_test.go` (fake charon refusing a changed existing connection once; records `--terminate` argv):
  - RED pre-fix: `TestPartialLoadRefusedExistingKeepsPriorHash15141` fails — refused candidate hash `c67db0db…` promoted over the gen1 hash `52dd7aa0…`.
  - GREEN post-fix: both cells pass (core gen1→gen2-refused→gen3-teardown; raced-to-full control).
- Targeted suites (`15141|14589|15129|ListLoadedConns|LoadedConns`) pass except `TestExpectedLoadedConnsRefusesApplyTimeLocalAddresses9641`, which fails identically on pristine master (base-attributed).
- Full `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1`: 62 failures, name-sorted set byte-identical to pristine master at this base (pre-existing gateway-grouping fallout, none introduced).
- `go vet ./pkg/ipsec/` PASS, `go build ./...` PASS, gofmt clean.

## Risk
Partial recovery now always pays the subset re-file + verification reload (one extra `--load-all`/`--list-conns` pair on that already rare path). The content comparison only ever diverts to the pre-existing true rollback; it never promotes a hash the old code would not have. Production `--list-conns --raw` does not echo the PSK itself, so a refused PSK-only rotation with byte-identical reported content remains indistinguishable from raced-to-full — inherent to charon's reporting, recorded in `docs/log/15141.md`.

Closes #15141

## PR #15470 — ha: require key confirmation before installing sync peer (#15140) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15140-campaign`

Why:
  Under Noise_NNpsk0 a session-sync msg1 is AEAD-tagged only over
  the prologue and the initiator ephemeral, so a passively captured
  60-byte syncMsgAuthHello re-verifies at a fresh responder with no
  PSK. The responder wrote msg2, split keys, recorded the peer as
  authenticated, and installed the connection — closing the real
  peer, sending it the sync stream, and (RG0 authority) the config
  including the control-link PSK.

What:
  Add a mandatory initiator key confirmation (syncMsgAuthConfirm
  type 44): HMAC-SHA256 under the initiator-to-responder frame key
  over the connect-confirm tag and the Noise channel binding. The
  responder returns a pending result after msg2 and only promotes
  via awaitInitiatorConfirm; recordAuthenticatedPeer and install
  now sit behind it. SessionSyncWireVersion bumps 2 -> 3 (flag
  day, #7163 discipline). NOT changed: the #6628 in-place upgrade
  (already confirmed) and unkeyed dual-accept behaviour.

Validation:
  New sync_auth_confirm_15140_test.go: replayed-msg1 install,
  silent post-msg2, and forged-confirm cells fail on origin/master
  with the replay displacing the legitimate conn; legitimate-pair
  control green before and after. Full pkg/cluster suite passes
  except TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752, identical
  on pristine origin/master. go vet clean.

Risk:
  Keyed pairs must run the same build on both nodes; the mixed-
  base gate refuses a 2/3 pair up front. A pending responder holds
  the connection only until the existing 3s handshake deadline.

Closes #15140

## PR #15473 — config: persist config-sync divergence across restarts (#15142) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15142-campaign`

## Why

SyncApply recorded a #9530 divergence only in process memory and durably deleted the unshared mark before `writeActive`, which degrades without failing. A restart after the heal — or after a failed heal write before the retry landed — discarded a partition-era commit with no alarm, reproducing #9530's own silent outcome.

## What

`unshared.json`'s record gains an optional `discarded` state. `recordSyncDivergenceLocked` persists it before the replacement is written and keeps the record; `reconcilePersistedUnsharedLocked`, called on SyncApply success and on the persist-retry heal, reduces it to a bare form (`digest == adopted`) that `Load` restores as the alarm but that can never re-classify. Pending records keep the discarded commit's digest, so a restart re-raises and a re-sync re-classifies. Local promotions and a different synced config clear the persisted record with the in-memory alarm. NOT changed: `classifySyncLocked`'s mark semantics for live marks, `NoteActiveSharedWithPeer`, or SyncApply's degrade-not-fail contract.

## Validation

New `divergence_persist_15142_test.go`: RED on base in 3 of 4 cells (restart-after-heal lost the alarm; mark deleted before a failed `writeActive`; retry-heal cell saw the same early delete), persisted-clear control passed. GREEN after the fix: all 4 #15142 cells and all existing #9530 cells pass; adjacent Commit/SyncApply/Load/Persist/Confirm/Rollback selection passes (126 tests). Full `pkg/configstore` suite exceeds the 240s test timeout in this environment on unmodified base as well (1037 tests listed).

## Risk

A persisted discarded record whose replacement never becomes durable stays pending and re-raises on restart by design; it is cleared by the next local promotion or a different synced config.

Closes #15142

A worker-decapped WireGuard record whose outer IP datagram was fragmented was lost: the first fragment was claimed and failed AEAD as a truncated record, and non-first fragments (protocol 255) went to the kernel, where transit inners drop as degraded. - Shim verifier: candidate and pristine master both REJECTED on this host/kernel (pre-existing baseline, tracked .o untouched) — must be re-run where master passes before merge.

Risk:
Fragmented UDP tails to a WG-armed box now reach the worker instead of the kernel; only tails whose head was admitted to a configured listener are buffered, others keep ordinary fragment adjudication.

## PR #15484 — userspace-dp: retry reinject accept errors instead of exiting (#15112) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15112-campaign`

## Why

The #9506 reinject submit and complete accept threads in `spawn_reinject_socket_servers` (`userspace-dp/src/server/reinject_9506.rs`) broke out of their loops on any non-`WouldBlock` accept error; the thread returned and the `UnixListener` moved into its closure was dropped. An idle EMFILE — descriptor/memory pressure with an empty backlog, where the kernel reserves the result descriptor before looking at the backlog — therefore deafened both sockets permanently. Every IPsec FORWARD flow using the #9506 adjudicated re-entry black-holed behind a healthy control socket until a helper restart that nothing triggers (A73-01). #9172 converted only the control and session loops to `accept_step`; these two were the residual.

## What

- Both reinject loops now decide through `lifecycle::accept_step` with `retry_unclassified = true`, exactly as the session loop does: `WouldBlock` keeps the previous 1 ms poll interval; EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOBUFS/ENOMEM retry on the shared 50 ms-doubling-to-1 s `AcceptBackoff` with one onset and one recovery journal line; unclassified errors log-and-continue; the `AcceptStep::Fail` arm (unreachable with `retry_unclassified = true`) sleeps at the backoff ceiling rather than spinning, mirroring the session loop.
- Each accepted connection is served under `catch_unwind` (the issue's optional serving wrap): a handler panic drops that one connection with a journal line and the accept loop continues, instead of unwinding the thread and dropping the listener.
- The peer-credential check and the inline, globally-serialized serving of each accepted connection are unchanged.
- NOT changed: `lifecycle.rs` (`accept_step`/`AcceptBackoff` reused as-is), the Go side (`pkg/nfqueue` already redials per reconnect), any neighbouring behaviour.

## Validation

- New regression cells in `reinject_9506_tests.rs` exercise the real spawned loops: lower the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to just above the open-fd count, drain the remaining slots with `/dev/null` duplicates so the idle listeners' `accept()` returns EMFILE, release the pressure, then prove service — the submit cell's ANNOUNCE applies permit epoch 4242 to the fallback core; the complete cell receives the queued completion and acks it. A third cell pins both `accept()` results through `accept_step` with `retry_unclassified = true` (same textual-wiring shape as the #9172 lifecycle cell).
- RED on `origin/master` (`699145ac4e`, tests only): all 3 FAILED — `complete listener dead after idle EMFILE (accept loop exited): Connection refused`, submit cell likewise, wiring cell found zero `accept_step` calls.
- GREEN after the fix: `cargo test 15112 -- --test-threads=1` → 3 passed; full `reinject_9506` module → 93 passed; #9172 lifecycle accept-step cells stay green.
- Full `--bins` suite on the fixed tree: 8585 passed / 54 failed / 8 ignored. Every failure was reproduced on clean `origin/master` worktrees or traced to concurrent campaign merges landing on `origin/master` after this lane branched (wire-fixture `protocol_wire_v1.json` and shim-tally drift from #15095/#15103/#15438-era merges); none touches the reinject accept path.

## Risk

A genuine descriptor leak now leaves the reinject sockets retrying with backoff and a journal line instead of the threads exiting silently — the same posture #9172 chose for the control/session sockets. Recovering a helper wedged by a real leak remains #9651. No behaviour change outside the two cited accept loops.

Closes #15112

## PR #15488 — cluster: chunk DHCP lease full-sets below the sync frame cap (#15160) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15160-campaign`

Why:
queueDHCPLeaseSnapshot wrote the entire Kea lease set as one session-sync frame with no size check. Past maxSyncPayload (16 MiB, ~165k v4 leases) the receiver's receiveLoop refuses the header and returns, tearing down the connection that also carries sessions, IPsec SAs and config; the re-push on reconnect repeats the cycle and DHCP takeover protection silently stops (B03-01, residual of #14607).

What:
Additive chunk types syncMsgDHCPLeaseV4Chunk=45 / syncMsgDHCPLeaseV6Chunk=46 (no wire-version bump; old peers ignore unknown types, #14607 precedent). Sets that fit one frame keep the exact legacy syncMsgDHCPLeaseV4/V6 shape. Over-cap sets split lease records across sub-cap chunk frames (`sync_dhcp_chunk_15160.go`: {generation, index, total, totalLeases} envelope + standard lease bodies, authority trailer on the last chunk); the receiver admits chunks in full-set-seq order through the existing per-family guard, reuses the legacy decode + semantic/identity filters, and commits the assembled set atomically (held-set store + high-water + callback under dhcpApplyMu) only when every chunk has arrived. Unclosed/inconsistent generations never commit (#7175 posture); a committed legacy set discards pending assemblies; single records too large for any frame drop counted via MalformedRecordsDropped, never over-cap.

Validation:
New pkg/cluster/dhcp_lease_chunk_15160_test.go: RED on base 885446e (chunk symbols undefined; base sender emits one frame regardless of size), GREEN after — 260k-lease v4 and v6 sets (each >16 MiB encoded) cross as multiple frames all <= maxSyncPayload and the receiver holds every lease with authority metadata and exactly one complete-set callback; withheld-final-chunk commits nothing then completes; replayed chunk generation ignored, newer legacy set still applies; small set stays a single legacy-typed frame; malformed/total-inconsistent generations never disturb the held set. Message census tests updated. Full pkg/cluster suite green except TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752, which fails identically on unmodified origin/master 61cfe3a (base-attributed).

Risk:
A mixed-version pair loses only over-cap lease pushes (old receiver ignores the chunk types) instead of the whole sync connection. A live two-node over-cap lease population remains an operator-scale check.

Closes #15160

## PR #15489 — wireguard: reject bit-255 twins of small-order keys (#15132) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15132-campaign`

## Summary

The #14373 WireGuard small-order denylist compared exact bytes, so the seven bit-255 twins — each listed key with byte 31's top bit set, which X25519 masks off per RFC 7748 — passed the Go commit gate, the Rust hydrate gate, and the engine reconcile gate while yielding the identical all-zero static-static DH secret.

## Fix

Mask byte 31 (`k[31] &= 0x7f`) before the denylist comparison in:

- Go `isDegenerateWireguardKeyHex` (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard.go`) — covers local private key, peer public key, and explicit PSK commit gates.
- Rust `is_small_order_wg_peer_key` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/mod.rs`) — covers `is_degenerate_wg_key_bytes` (hydrate: local private key, peer key, explicit PSK) and engine `reconcile_peers` admission.

No new table entries: the 7 canonical entries plus masking cover all 14 encodings. A legitimate key with bit 255 set is a different genuine point and stays admissible; the repeated-byte leg, snow DH handling, and absent-PSK semantics are unchanged.

## Tests

- Go `pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard_twin_15132_test.go`: all 7 twin peer keys refused at the predicate and at strict commit (plus upper-case spelling), twin private key and twin explicit PSK refused without echoing key material; controls (canonical refused, bit-255-set valid keys commit, repeated-byte/near-miss unchanged).
- Rust `bit255_twins_are_small_order_15132`: each twin yields an all-zero DH under a clamped scalar (executable same-point pin) and is refused by both predicates; valid bit-255-set and near-miss controls stay admissible.
- Rust `reconcile_refuses_bit255_twin_peers_15132`: 7 twin peers refused and counted; valid peer and its bit-255-set variant installed.
- Rust `wg_endpoint_with_bit255_twin_key_is_dropped_15132`: twin peer / twin local private key / twin explicit PSK each drop the row at hydrate; valid fixture and bit-255-set valid peer still hydrate.

## Validation

- RED verified pre-fix (tests present, fix absent): Go twin cells fail for all 7 twins; all 3 Rust twin tests fail (engine reconcile installed 9 peers instead of 2). Re-verified by reverting only the production files with tests in place.
- GREEN: Go `TestWireguardBit255*` + full #14373 degenerate suite pass; Rust `bit255` (3), `14373` (3), `wg_endpoint` (9) pass on the rebased head.
- Base-attributed (identical with/without fix, untouched): 6 `pkg/config` WireGuard failures and 4 `userspace-dp` `wg_` failures on this base, all stale repeated-byte fixtures vs the #14373 gate. Full `pkg/config` suite has pre-existing unrelated failures on this base (not exercised as a gate; WireGuard-scoped failure sets diffed instead).

## Risk

A config whose key is a bit-255 twin of a small-order encoding now fails commit / drops at hydrate where it previously loaded but could never authenticate — the intended fail-closed delta. No legitimate key changes behaviour.

Docs: `docs/log/15132.md`.

Closes #15132

## PR #15494 — userspace-dp: force interface PAT without a synthetic flow key (#15109) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15109-campaign`

## Why

The #14367 forced-PAT arm in `match_source_nat_result_for_tuple_inner` built a synthetic `SourceNatFlowKey{src_ip:10.255.255.253, src_port:flow.src_port, ..flow}`, minted it, minted the real flow, then rolled the dummy back. If a real internal host at 10.255.255.253 already held that exact interface identity, the dummy mint re-entered the victim's live record (`reenter_interface_record_locked`) and the dummy rollback unlinked it — the victim's flows were refused when a peer owned its preserved port and its interface-identity ownership was silently deleted.

## What

- `PortAllocator::allocate_interface_identity_excluding(flow, translated_ip, holder, must_pat, excluded)`: `must_pat` skips the preserve-first arm; the `excluded` predicate is consulted for every PAT candidate so a peer-owned candidate is skipped rather than minted and rolled back. `allocate_interface_identity` delegates with `must_pat=false` and a never-excluding predicate (behaviour unchanged for all existing callers).
- `match_rules` computes `must_pat = peer_owns(flow.src_port)` and passes the existing `peer_owns` closure (combined pool/NAT64 overlap index) into the walk. The post-mint `peer_owns` verification + rollback of the real flow stays as a fail-closed backstop for races.
- No fixed-address `SourceNatFlowKey` literal remains in production code; no synthetic flow key is fabricated.

## Validation

- New regression tests in `tests_iface_nat64_14367` (through `build_forwarding_state`):
  - `victim_at_synthetic_address_survives_peer_owned_preserved_pat_15109` — **RED on base** (production fix stashed): FAILED with `live_flow_count` 0 vs 1, the dummy rollback deleted the victim's record exactly as claimed. **GREEN after fix**, including idempotent re-admit.
  - `real_host_survives_forced_pat_of_colliding_flow_15109` — control: victim + colliding `10.0.0.2` flow keep distinct live records (green on both sides; the collider's dummy key differs from the victim key by `src_ip`).
  - `synthetic_address_without_peer_collision_preserves_15109` — control: no peer collision still preserves.
- Post-rebase on `origin/master@280301bf9c`: 15109 tests 3/3, 14367 suite 10/10, `tests_iface` 37/37 (`cargo test --release --bin xpf-userspace-dp <filter>`).

## Risk

The PAT walk now consults the peer predicate per candidate under the interface allocator lock; the predicate only reads peer occupancy bitmaps and address-only identity maps — the same queries the caller already issued outside the lock. A racing peer mint between walk and post-mint check still fails closed with `InterfaceIdentityExhausted`, never publishing a duplicate.

Closes #15109

## PR #15496 — upgrade: validate kernel-arm re-stamp before STOP and tolerate it on rollback re-flips (#15170) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15170-campaign`

Closes #15170

## Summary (B17-01)
Flip step 6d (the #6639 kernel-arm re-stamp) ran only inside `flip()`, after STOP and after 6a-6c repointed current/sbin/ExecStart. `loadKernelJournal` errors on any non-ENOENT read/parse failure, so a corrupt or unreadable `/var/lib/xpf/kernel-upgrade.state` failed the forward flip at 6d with the daemon down — and every rollback path re-ran the same 6d on its re-flip, failed again before `StartUnit`, and left the standalone daemon offline across the cut, auto-rollback, STOPPED resume and `--rollback`.

## Fix (both legs the issue names)
- **Pre-STOP probe**: `probeKernelArmRestamp`/`validateKernelArmRestampPreStop` (cutover.go, any journal not yet at STOPPED) read the kernel journal and, when a candidate is ARMED (shared `kernelArmRecordArmed`), `validateGateBin` the xpfd of both target and PreviousVersion. Failure refuses the cut with the daemon live. #6639's forward fail-closed cell is preserved — it just refuses before STOP. Nothing armed = byte-identical no-op.
- **Tolerant rollback re-flip**: `flip()` wraps a 6d-only failure in `restampError` after 6a-6c succeed; `rollback()`, `executeRollback` and `restoreStaleStoppedPrevious` use `flipToleratingKernelArmRestamp` to log and tolerate exactly that, leaving the stale arm record untouched (candidate boot gate refuses as pre-#6639: candidate lost, never an unvalidated promotion) so StartUnit runs. Genuine 6a-6c failures stay fatal.

## Validation
- New `kernel_arm_restamp_15170_test.go`: corrupt journal refused before STOP (no stop call, unitRunning, current untouched); corruption landing at STOP still ends `unitRunning=true` on 1.0.0 via auto-rollback; operator `RollbackTo` completes with a corrupt journal. All three **fail on base `61cfe3a483`** with the exact mechanism (verified by stashing only production files) and pass after the fix.
- `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -count=1` PASS (full suite incl. 6639 fail-closed + nothing-armed controls); `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Docs: `docs/log/15170.md`.

## Risk
Probe is read-only, no-op when nothing is armed. Tolerant rollback trades a lost kernel candidate for a running known-good daemon and cannot promote an unvalidated kernel (record byte-identical). Residual: corruption between probe and 6d on the forward leg is still found at 6d, but now ends with the daemon running on the previous version.

Never merge — campaign review gate applies.

  on PASS 1 only, both arms also ask iface_owns_for_pool beside the
  peer/static checks, rolling back into the existing Refused outcome;
  PASS 2 is unchanged. reserve_synced_interface_identity takes the rule
  slice and asks peer_owns_for_interface over the combined index
  before booking, refusing on

  GREEN: cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp tests_synced_iface_15146 —
  11 passed. Neighbours: -- 14367 9021 8115 14674 — 47 passed, 0
  failed.

Risk:
  A synced import colliding with a local cross-domain identity is now

cluster: restore owner promptly on peer-failover abort (#15164)

Why:
After RequestPeerFailover aborted locally, the requester reported an
error and demoted, but the owner kept advertising StateSecondaryHold
under its #5079 lease and electRG's Peer transfer out rule promoted
the requester again on the next heartbeat. Under preempt the owner
then reclaimed the RG at lease expiry: ownership moved contrary to
the reported outcome, with an unrequested second RG move.

Add a reqID-bound abort frame (syncMsgFailoverAbort /
syncMsgFailoverBatchAbort, additive so an old peer ignores it and
the lease remains the fallback). abortRequestedPeerFailover(Batch)
records the aborted reqID and sends the abort outside m.mu;
AbortRemoteTransferOut on the owner restores promptly only when the
reqID matches the armed lease. electRG refuses Peer transfer out
while abortedPeerTransferReqID is present; the marker is cleared by
commitRequestedPeerFailover, notePeerTransferCommitted, the raw
heartbeat expiry in applyTransferCommitOverridesOnPeerStateLocked,
ResetFailover, FinalizePeerTransferOut, peer loss, and RG removal.
NOT changed: the #5079 lease, commit, and dual-resign paths.

owner hold plus heartbeat re-promotion asserted) and GREEN after:

fails, reproduced identically on pristine master (base-attributed).

## PR #15504 — cli: execute flat config verbs from the gate lexer, fail closed on non-lexing lines (#15167) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15167-campaign`

Closes #15167

## Defect (V47-S1)
Local on-box CLI gated the raw config line with the config lexer (`AuthorizeConfigMutation`) but executed `set`/`delete`/`deactivate`/`activate` from `strings.Fields` tokens. The lexer stops at a non-ASCII byte (`TokenError`) and the gate judged only the lexed prefix, while unicode-aware `Fields` executed the full path — a restricted login class could mutate any path, including `system login class <self>`, by using a Unicode space (NBSP/EM/VT/FF/NEL/LS) after the verb or inside the path.

## Fix
- `pkg/config`: `lexConfigMutationLineStrict15167` reports whether the whole line lexed cleanly; `AuthorizeConfigMutation` (shared B23-01 decision) fails closed on a non-lexing gated line — including the verb-only prefix `set<NBSP>...` — for classes that configured `*-configuration` regexes. Unrestricted classes keep their ordinary errors.
- `pkg/config`: `ParseConfigMutationLine` exports the gate parse; the local CLI flat-verb arms derive their path from it and refuse non-lexing lines instead of re-splitting with `strings.Fields`. Quoted/tab/comment spellings execute exactly as adjudicated.

## Regression
`pkg/cli/unicode_space_authz_15167_test.go`: NBSP/EM/VT/FF/NEL/LS cells across all four verbs plus the own-class self-escalation spelling are denied with the candidate byte-identical; ASCII controls stay green (denied `system login` still denied, `set system services telnet` still allowed, quoted/tab allowed spellings reach the candidate). RED on `origin/master` dcba0c98be (cells ALLOWED, candidate mutated), GREEN after the fix. Adjacent `pkg/config` Authorize/Parse/TopUp/Split and `pkg/cli` dispatch/14716/14717/7172/14981/15082 selections pass. Pre-existing unrelated `TestUnitAliasVLANSplitDistinctUnitsClean_5878` fails identically on pristine base.

Docs: `docs/log/15167.md`.

## PR #15507 — cluster: seed bulk-send epoch from monotonic clock (#15182) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15182-campaign`

Why:
bulkSendNext was the one within-boot counter initGenState left at
zero, so a restarted daemon re-emitted bulk epoch 1 while a
surviving peer held bulkRecvEpoch at a dead-process high-water.
switched cannot fire on a daemon-only restart (the boot id changes
only on OS boot), so bulkStartStaleLocked refused the restarted
peer's authoritative re-prime between bulks: its pre-existing
sessions were never bulk-transferred and no BulkEnd reconcile ran.

What:
Store the MonotonicNanos seed into bulkSendNext in initGenState
beside syncEpoch, so the first epoch of a restarted process within
a boot is strictly newer than any epoch its predecessor emitted.
No receiver change; the #8966/#9174 guards and the #2198
cross-boot switched path are untouched. Three existing
sync_test.go cells asserted the literal first epoch 1; they now
assert the epoch the bulk actually drew. New
sync_bulk_epoch_restart_15182_test.go exercises the sender seed
and the end-to-end between-bulks acceptance plus controls.

## PR #15510 — userspace-dp: stop converting verdict-queue contention into denies (#15150) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15150-campaign`

## Why

`IpsecInnerVerdictQueue::try_post` returned `Err` on `try_lock` failure and counted E24 as if the queue were full. `post_worker_verdict` then posted an Uncertain deny, which terminalizes the still-Queued `ReinjectCore` entry and cancels the armed permitted write (armed before the post in the worker loop). Every worker takes the same verdict mutex every iteration, so permitted IPsec-inner traffic was lost at the lock-contention rate while the E24 "queue full" counter lied (the queue could be empty).

## What

- `IpsecInnerVerdictQueue::post` (new): blocking producer `lock()`; refuses only at true depth (`len >= IPSEC_INNER_VERDICT_QUEUE_DEPTH`), counting E24 only there.
- `try_post` keeps non-blocking semantics but counts contention on the new `IPSEC_INNER_VERDICT_QUEUE_CONTENDED_TOTAL`, never E24.
- `post_worker_verdict` / `requeue_worker_verdict`: at true-full, a `WouldPermit` is retained unchanged on the bounded fallback instead of becoming an Uncertain deny; `Deny` verdicts keep the fail-closed Uncertain terminal.
- `post_ipsec_inner_verdict` uses `post`.
- Contended counter plumbed Rust snapshot → `ProcessStatus` (additive, serde-defaulted, no wire bump) → Go `ProcessStatus` → Prometheus `xpf_userspace_ipsec_inner_verdict_queue_contended_total`; `protocol_wire_v1.json` regenerated.
- NOT changed: ingress `try_enqueue` E23 try-or-drop (socket producer never blocks; B12-03 is a separate issue), the consumer drain lock, the ReinjectCore permit join, all Deny handling.

## Validation

- 6 new `#15150` cells pass, 5× flake-clean: contended `try_post` counts contention not E24; blocking `post` delivers WouldPermit with the lock held (the issue's "yields WouldPermit with the lock held"); contended and true-full transport WouldPermits drain unchanged (E24 moves only at depth); Deny control stays Uncertain; armed retained WouldPermit still Proceeds to Written.
- RED at base: the contended state drained `Deny{VERDICT_UNCERTAIN}` with E24+1 (the old `contended_try_post_refuses_without_waiting` asserted exactly that).
- Adjacent: `ipsec_inner` suite 71 passed (incl. `verdict_queue_full_counts_e24_never_silent`); server counter projection/serialization cells pass; wire specimen regenerated with only the 3 contended-key additions.
- Go: `TestIPsecInnerStatusWireCensus10695`, `TestIPsecInnerStatusExportEndToEnd10695`, `TestCollectorDescriptorCoverage`, `TestEmitUserspaceDynamicBufferMetrics` pass (census 109→112: base already drifted +2 on origin/master, verified by stash, plus this series). Full `pkg/api` / `pkg/dataplane/userspace` failures are pre-existing NAT-pool/doc-guard/#15034 cells, base-attributed and untouched.

## Risk

A worker may now wait briefly on the verdict mutex (held only for bounded VecDeque push/drain) instead of dropping a permit; the consumer drains every worker tick. No other behavior change.

Closes #15150

## PR #15511 — frr: restore QNH metric overlay after failed reload (#15183) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15183-campaign`

## Why

`frr-reload.py --reload` deletes running lines absent from `frr.conf` — including the memory-only QNH `set metric N` overlay — *before* it reaches a line FRR rejects, then exits non-zero. Two return paths then skipped the restore:

- `reloadLocked`: when both `frr-reload.py` and the additive `vtysh -f` fallback failed, the hard-failure return ran before `reconcileQNHMetricOverlaysLocked`.
- `retryReloadOnce`: a failed degraded-retry attempt returned before its reconcile.

The backup static was exported into OSPF at the default external cost — tying with or beating the primary exporter network-wide — for as long as the rejected line persisted.

## What

- `pkg/frr/manager.go`: run `reconcileQNHMetricOverlaysLocked` on both failure returns. In `reloadLocked` a reconcile error is joined (`%w (additionally... %w)`) so the vtysh/primary causes and the #9947 pytools-missing classification stay `errors.Is`-visible and the hard failure still propagates. In `retryReloadOnce` a reconcile failure only logs; the attempt still returns failed and the episode stays degraded.
- Correct the stale lifecycle claims (QNH reconcile only after a successful load) in `commitManagedSection` / `noteReloadOutcomeLocked`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go`, and the README lifecycle bullet. No QNH pre-clear was added.

- `docs/log/15183.md`.

## Validation

- GREEN after fix; adjacent QNH/reload tests pass under `-race`.
- Full `go test ./pkg/frr/`: only 4 pre-existing BGP failures, reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` (0c468f7f4a) — base-attributed.

## Risk

A reconcile failure on the hard-failure path now surfaces joined to the reload error (never replacing it). The real-FRR live criterion rides the root-gated live QNH harness, which runs 3-of-4 failing identically on pristine master in this sandbox (pre-existing environment failure) and was not used as evidence here.

Closes #15183

## PR #15514 — upgrade: no-op same-version re-run of already-live committed version (#15186) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15186-campaign`

Closes #15186

## Why
A bare re-run of `xpfd upgrade` (or `--rolling`) when the staged version was already live and committed performed a full same-version cut: STOP/START of xpfd (plus `ForceSecondary` on HA), replacement of `.<ver>.dbsnap`, and a commit stamp `{version:<ver>, predecessor:<ver>}` that the reader rejects — breaking rollback to the real predecessor. A VERIFY failure deleted the live snapshot, and the neighbouring refusal advised `dpkg-reconfigure xpf`, which always mints a new generation and is refused again.

## What
- INIT (`cutover.go`): when `stagedVer ==` live `current`, require `.srcgen` equality with the pinned generation, a valid committed stamp, and byte-identical managed binaries (`mismatchedManagedBinary`); then return `already at <ver>; nothing to do` before any journal/snapshot/STOP. Otherwise refuse pre-PREFLIGHT with re-version guidance only. Sanctioned first-cut retry falls through to a real cut; the no-op mints no committed-cut evidence (#12143).
- `rolling.go`: same check via `alreadyAtStagedVersion()` before `ForceSecondary`; in-flight journals still resume through the inner `Run`.
- `commit_stamp.go`: never write `Predecessor == Version` (defence in depth).
- `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`: dbsnap removal guarded by `ver != cur && ver != j.PreviousVersion`.
- Dropped `dpkg-reconfigure` realign advice from both refusal sites and `docs/in-place-upgrade.md`; documented the already-live re-run.
- Updated `TestPreflipFailedRunInvalidatesEarlierEvidence12143` to stage a new 5.0.0 for its verify-rejected run (re-running live 4.0.0 is now a no-op by design; assertions unchanged).

## Validation
- New `same_version_rerun_15186_test.go`: RED on `origin/master` (stop/start on re-run, dpkg-reconfigure advice, live dbsnap deleted, ForceSecondary called, self-predecessor stamp rejected), GREEN after fix (no stop/start, dbsnap byte-identical, stamp/predecessor preserved, no journal).
- `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -count=1`: PASS. `go vet ./pkg/upgrade/`: PASS.

## Risk
Confined to the `stagedVer == prev` decision point, the stamp self-predecessor case, and the verify-cleanup snapshot guard. Legacy unstamped same-version live dirs under a pinned generation now refuse fail-closed with re-version guidance.

## PR #15515 — ha: gate kernel self-recovery on drain start and consume its lease (#15181) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15181-campaign`

Why: self-recovery treated ANY expired kernel-roll lease naming this node as a crashed-roll fingerprint, with no age bound, and never removed the lease after acting. A lease left by a crashed or transport-lost roll persisted on /var/lib/xpf, so about 2 minutes after every later ForceSecondary (ISSU) or rolling drain it ran ResetAllFailover against the operator intent — a drained node re-entered election and, with preempt, could reclaim primary during a maintenance window.

What: Tick now requires the expired lease to postdate the current drain (ExpiresAt after the earliest ManualFailoverAt, via the new Manager.LocalDrainedSince exposed on SelfRecoveryCluster and the daemon adapter); a stale or unknown-start drain fails closed. Before ResetFailover, Tick consumes exactly the authorizing lease under the orchestrator kernel-roll.lock flock, only when node and expiry still match, so it cannot re-fire or delete a successor lease. verifyAndPromote now ClearRollLease on PROMOTE, as REVERT/discard already did. NOT changed: the crashed-roll recovery cell, active/other-node/missing-lease no-ops, and the ARMED gate.

Validation: new 15181 cells RED on base (stale lease reset=1, zero drain start reset, lease left after recovery, promote 0 clears) and GREEN after the fix; go test ./pkg/upgrade/ PASS (full suite); pkg/cluster neighbours 15181/13222 PASS; go vet clean. Full pkg/cluster has one pre-existing failure (TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752) also failing on clean origin/master 53419c6cf2.

Risk: a crashed roll whose drain never stamped ManualFailoverAt now fails closed (stays drained for the operator) instead of recovering; all current drain setters stamp it. Consumption takes the flock non-blockingly, so a live orchestrator is never blocked or deleted.

Closes #15181

## PR #15521 — config: defer shifted rollback save when sync persist fails (#15190) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15190-campaign`

Why:
SyncApply pushes the old active onto history, promotes the synced tree in memory, and on a pre-rename writeActive failure continued to saveRollbackFiles unconditionally. The sidecar binds via rollbackActiveBindingForWrite (in-memory tree hash plus the old file identity), so a restart before the persist retry healed saw a generation mismatch and refused every rollback slot; the next save tombstoned the ladder. The standby silently lost its whole rollback history with RollbackHistoryDegraded false.

What:
SyncApply records whether it shifted history and whether the write persisted / was post-rename-visible. On a pre-rename failure with a shift it sets rollbackPersistDelayed and skips saveRollbackFiles, leaving the on-disk slots/sidecar describing the old active so a pre-heal restart yields the readable pre-sync ladder. The persist retry saves the shifted ladder once the synced config is durable (the #14578 rebind still covers the no-shift case). A successful saveRollbackFiles clears the flag. Post-rename failures and successful syncs save immediately, unchanged.

Validation:
New sync_rollback_binding_15190_test.go: degraded-restart cell RED on base (all slots refused, rollback slot 1 unreadable), GREEN after fix (pre-sync ladder readable); retry-heal keeps [C,B,A]; post-rename and successful-sync controls pass. Adjacent 14578/5473/DegradesNotFails suites pass. Full configstore suite exceeded the 300s harness timeout without failures before the kill — please run to completion.

Risk:
A deferred save whose retry-heal slot write fails sets RollbackHistoryDegraded via saveRollbackFiles, as with any rollback persist failure. No behaviour change outside the failed-sync rollback save.

Closes #15190

## PR #15525 — userspace-dp: decline TCP-MD5/TCP-AO in segmentation and MSS clamp (#15119) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15119-campaign`

Why: both segmentation builders copied the full TCP header, including a
kind-19 MD5 or kind-29 AO option, onto every output segment while
rewriting seq/lengths/checksums, so each segment failed the receiver's
authentication check, every segment was dropped, and no PTB was sent;
BGP-MD5/TCP-AO sessions stall on the first oversize segment. The
dispatch admission gate admitted on length alone, never reaching the
PTB arm. Sibling: clamp_tcp_mss rewrote the MSS of a TCP-AO SYN or an
IPv6 AH-protected SYN, invalidating its MAC/ICV.

What: shared tcp_header_has_auth_option walk in frame/tcp.rs (kinds
19/29); both segmentation builders (frame copy path + tx prepared-TX
twin) and forwarded_tcp_may_need_segmentation decline authenticated
datagrams so DF/IPv6 traffic reaches compute_forwarded_egress_ptb and
no-DF traffic forwards whole; clamp_tcp_mss declines AO/MD5/AH SYNs.
Regression cells for gate, both builders, PTB emission (Frag-Needed
MTU 1400), NOP control segmentation, and clamp no-ops. Log in
docs/log/15119.md.

Validation: cargo test --bins 15119: 5 passed GREEN; with production
guards reverted 4/5 fail (RED), NOP control passes. clamp suite 19
passed; admission suite 8 passed both sides; tcp_segmentation/ptb
subsets identical branch vs pristine base (2+1 pre-existing WG
failures). Full --bins pre-rebase: 8594 passed, 54 failed
(pre-existing families), 8 ignored. Post-rebase tip does not compile
its test harness due to a pre-existing origin/master error in
afxdp/mirror/mod_tests.rs (MirrorConfigSnapshot missing fields from
#15114/#15113), untouched by this change.

Risk: authenticated oversize TCP now depends on PMTUD instead of
local segmentation, matching the existing AH disposition; no other
behaviour change.

Closes #15119

## PR #15530 — ipsec: terminate demoted RG SAs on failover (#15194) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15194-campaign`

Why:
On RG demotion xpf removes the VIP but never terminates the IKE/CHILD SAs anchored on it. The stale SAs survive in charon (MOBIKE defers, and a non-MOBIKE peer generates no IKE traffic), so on failback `reinitiateIPsecSAs` -> `swanctl --initiate --child` is refused with "not establishing CHILD_SA ... due to existing duplicate", and the returning owner keeps encrypting with SPIs the peer already deleted. The black hole is bounded only by DPD, the next rekey, or peer initiation — on every planned failover/failback, preempt, and monitor-driven demotion without reboot.

What:
- `clearRethServicesForRG` (data RG loss) and the genuine-demotion arm of `applyRG0OwnershipTransition` (RG0 secondary) launch `terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs(rg)`: reads the LOCAL live SA set, keeps names attributed to the lost RG via the #9139/#9511 `ipsecConnRedundancyGroups` attribution (all candidates must equal the lost RG; unanchored names default to RG0), terminates each. RG0 gated on the existing `genuineDemotion` verdict (initial-secondary seating terminates nothing); data-RG sweep not gated on `IPsecSASync` (local hygiene). Failed live-SA read terminates nothing rather than guessing a connection another RG may own.
- `reinitiateIPsecSAs` belt: before initiating, terminate any peer-advertised name still live locally, so a raced/failed demotion terminate cannot leave a duplicate for charon to refuse.
- New `ipsec.Manager.TerminateConnection`: resolves the IKE connection owning the named SA from `--list-sas` (`ConnectionName`; gateway-named since #15024, children carry VPN names) and issues `swanctl --terminate --ike <conn> --force`. No matching live SA = no-op; failed list returned, never guessed. Test seam `Daemon.ipsecTerminateFn` mirrors `ipsecInitiateFn`.
- NOT changed: advertise gate, `ownsIPsecConn` initiate scoping, SA-sync wire format, `terminateRemovedConns` debt machinery. Docs: `docs/log/15194.md`, `pkg/ipsec/README.md`.

Validation:
- RED: daemon suite failed to build on unpatched master (unknown field `ipsecTerminateFn`); `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 15194` failed `m.TerminateConnection undefined`.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 15194` 6/6; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 15194` 2/2; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1` full suite green.
- Daemon 9139/9511/RG targeted suites green except `TestApplyIPsecTrackedRecordsOnlyALoadedGeneration9511`, `TestConfigSyncPeerConnectUsesRG0Reconciler`, `TestSyncConfigToPeerGatesOnRG0AuthorityAtPushTime` — pre-existing, base-attributed on clean `origin/master` worktrees. Full daemon suite exceeded the 300s lane timeout twice (targeted suites run instead). On-cluster run-v63 (MOBIKE/non-MOBIKE x trap/start, failback rc=0) is lab-bound, not exercised here.

Risk:
Demotion now forced-terminates exactly the lost RG's IKE SAs; a colliding multi-candidate name spanning a surviving RG is left to the takeover belt. `--force` skips the delete-ack wait by design (VIP already gone). Async sweep races are covered by the belt.

Closes #15194

Inbound persistent-NAT lookups passed `rule.from_zone` alone, so an interface-, routing-instance- or global-scoped rule-set (empty `from_zone`) collapsed to `PERSISTENT_NAT_EGRESS_UNSCOPED`, where any grant bucket admits. - `nat/source/mod.rs`: `SourceNatRule::persistent_rule_scope` — the single key both mints and lookups use.
- `nat/source/match_rules.rs`, `nat/source/synced.rs`: mint sites record under the rule scope.
- `afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs`, `policy_revalidation.rs`: admission and mirror lookups pass the rule + packet pair; revalidation resolves the internal zone from session metadata.
- New `nat::tests_persistent_nonzone_15133` (interface/global/RI siblings); #14322 cells exercise the production rule-keyed lookup. NOT changed: lease identity/tuple sharing (#9389), remote cap, wire `egress_scope` encoding, NAT64 unscoped behaviour.

Validation:
- RED on base `85433e0906` (probe with pre-fix lookup spelling): all 3 new cells fail, `Permitted` where `Denied` required.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15133` = 3/3; `-- 14322 14802 14315 15133` = 12/12.
- Main agent to run: full `nat::` suite + Go snapshot/lease suites before merge.

Risk:
Fail-closed only for the cited merge. Mixed-version HA peers fold v1 vs v2 differently until both run this build; standby may miss (fail closed) rather than merge grants during upgrade. Pre-fix v1 buckets expire with their leases.

Closes #15133

refused prefix until its own lifetime ended (A39-02). The
RFC 8415 infinite lifetime (0xFFFFFFFF s, decoded as
MaxUint32 seconds) sat below the 1<<62 ns sentinel, so

parseV6ReplyChecked now returns the typed errV6PDRefused

run loop clears the stored delegation via clearDelegatedPDs

both RENEW and REBIND. infiniteLifetime is the wire value
time.Duration(math.MaxUint32)*time.Second. The 15071
infinite fixture constructs the wire value; README and
docs/log/15224.md record the cohort. NOT changed: the mixed
ia-na+ia-pd pdRefused commit arm, silence keep-and-retry,
and the REBIND matcher binding.

fails to build (undefined errV6PDRefused). GREEN:
go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -run '15224' -count=1 passes (wire
infinite never decays/expires, finite control decays;
PD-only refusal typed, silence generic, live grant succeeds;
run loop empties DelegatedPrefixesForRA at RENEW and REBIND).

gofmt clean.

waiting for T2; the #14997 matcher still gates which REBIND

## PR #15546 — config: re-emit [edit] header after recursed siblings in compare (#15169) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15169-campaign`

Closes #15169

## Defect (B24-02)
`diffNodes` in `pkg/config/ast_format.go` printed its `[edit <path>]` header once, before its rendering loop. After a recursed sibling printed a deeper header, subsequent parent-level +/- lines inherited that unrelated context (e.g. an added/removed policy shown inside another policy's `then`). At the root no `[edit]` header was printed at all.

## Fix
Confined to `diffNodes`: each level now collects its ordered sections first (own lines rendered into buffers, modified block pairs as recursion arms — preserving the #15168 removals-first/new-order rendering), then emits them with the level's header printed lazily immediately before each run of own lines — bare `[edit]` at the root — re-armed only when a recursion actually produced output. A header with no lines under it is never printed; the all-recursable fast path is untouched. Rendering-only; no fail-open path is involved.

## Regression & controls
New `pkg/config/compare_header_15169_test.go` (5 cells): removed `deny-x` and added `new-x` policies governed by `[edit security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust]` rather than the recursed `keep` policy's `[edit ... policy keep then]` header; root addition opening with bare `[edit]`; single-header control; no-duplicate/no-empty-parent-header control.

- RED on current `origin/master`: addition cell fails (new-x governed by the deep header) and root cell fails (no `[edit]`); controls pass. On the pre-#15168 base the original removal probe also rendered under the deep header.
- GREEN after the fix. Controls green: all four #15168 order/duplicate compare cells, `TestInactive_CompareShowsDeactivate` (#2008 H1), configstore `Compare` suite incl. redacted/rollback compares, config format/redact/parser subsets (156 cells).
- Full `pkg/config` suite does not complete on this host under multi-lane load (times out in the spelling-differential gate on fixed and pristine trees alike); five `TestCompile*` cells fail identically on pristine `origin/master` — pre-existing, unrelated.

Log: `docs/log/15169.md`.

## PR #15550 — userspace-dp: meter inline input policer only from deferring term (#15189) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15189-campaign`

## Why

An input three-color policer on an inline-metered (host-bound / Stage-11) path was charged twice per packet whenever its filter contained any `routing-instance` term, including one the packet never matched. `evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter` gated its routing-bearing remainder on the filter-wide `affects_route_lookup` flag (plus a family-wide policer flag) and re-walked from term 0, so router-bound traffic (IKE/ESP reinjection, LocalDelivery hits on per-packet filters) was policed at about half the configured CIR/burst. D01-01, a regression of #14120 persisting past #14857.

## What

- The non-routing walks (`evaluate_filter_ref_non_routing_counted_v4/v6`) now record the term index they deferred at in the new `FilterResult::deferred_at_routing_term` field.
- The inline caller runs the routing-bearing remainder only when the walk actually deferred, via the new `routing_bearing_remainder_policer_drop_from(.., from_term)`, which threads `from_term` through the runtime TX-selection walks as a term slice (`from_term = 0` on every pre-existing full walk, zero extra allocation).
- A policer on the deferring routing term (or a later term that walk reaches before terminating) still meters exactly once; terms already metered by the non-routing walk are never re-walked; a packet that never defers pays no remainder.
- NOT changed: the tunnel outer gate keeps its full from-0 walk (its input evaluation passes `DeferToTxSelection`, so nothing there was charged twice), transit deferral, counter ownership, and the #14659 fall-through preservation.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/README.md` (#14120 section) and `docs/log/15189.md` document the fix.

## Validation

- New regression cells in `poll_descriptor/filter.rs`: `stage11_input_policer_not_double_charged_with_unmatched_routing_term_15189` (packet 1: Accept, green=1, drop=0; packet 2: Discard), `inline_next_term_policer_before_matched_routing_term_charges_once_15189`, `stage11_input_policer_after_matched_routing_term_not_charged_15189`, and `local_delivery_input_policer_with_routing_term_charges_once_14120` (the `*_14120` cell whose filter carries a routing-instance term).
- RED: forcing the remainder start index back to term 0 (pre-fix behaviour) fails `inline_next_term_policer_before_matched_routing_term_charges_once_15189` — `first packet must pass` with left `Discard`, right `Accept`.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bins -- 15189 14659 14120` passes 11/11, including all pre-existing #14120 cells and the #14659 cells (`pbr_input_term_enforces_three_color_policer_fc_and_dscp_on_runtime_tx_selection_14659`, `pbr_input_term_policer_replay_contains_pbr_term_14659`, `non_routing_walk_preserves_next_term_policer_drop_before_pbr_14659`). `cargo check --bins` clean.
- Base-attributed: the full test binary does not compile on pristine `origin/master` (460c8c469a) — `afxdp/mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032` omits the `ingress_vlan_id`/`unit_scoped` fields added by #15113/#15114 (E0063, verified via `git show origin/master:...`). Unrelated to this change; targeted runs used a temporarily completed literal, reverted before commit. **Main agent: run the full `--bins` suite and attribute/fix the mirror compile error before merging.**

## Risk

Bounded to inline-metered host-bound / Stage-11 input-filter evaluation. Transit packets still meter exactly once in the TX-selection leg; a policer on or after a matched routing-instance term still meters exactly once via the sliced remainder. No wire, counter, or `show` behaviour change outside the double-charge mechanism.

Closes #15189

## PR #15552 — networkd: order preferred address first within its subnet (#15222) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15222-campaign`

Why:
The Junos `preferred` leaf was inert for source selection: networkd ordered only `PrimaryAddress` first and gave the preferred address `PreferredLifetime=forever` in an `[Address]` section. That lifetime never chooses an IPv4 source and does not order same-subnet IPv6, so locally originated traffic used the first-added address in the subnet. The compiler also let `family inet` overwrite preferred last-wins while `inet6` was first-wins.

What:

## PR #15553 — userspace-dp: honour designated primary address in snapshot picks (#15155) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15155-campaign`

## Why

The Go snapshot builder sorts a unit's addresses by the address string and `InterfaceAddressSnapshot` carried no marker for the operator's `primary` designation, so Rust `pick_interface_v4/v6` and Go `pickInterfaceSnapshotV4/V6` returned the lexicographically-first address. On any multi-address egress unit, `primary_v4/v6` — and therefore every `source-nat interface` flow — used an address the operator did not choose (e.g. `10.0.0.10/24` over designated `10.0.0.9/24`).

## What

- Carry `primary` on `InterfaceAddressSnapshot` (Go `Primary` / `primary,omitempty`; Rust `primary` serde-default, pinned in `protocol_wire_v1.json`), marked by `buildConfiguredAddressSnapshots` from the unit's `PrimaryAddress` and overlaid by `mergeInterfaceAddressSnapshots` onto live rows.
- Both pick pairs scan the full family: marked primary wins, else first non-link-local, else first of family — bit-identical for unmarked snapshots.
- `ProtocolVersion` 53 → 54 in lockstep (Go + Rust `control.rs`); shape pin, contract golden, wire fixture regenerated.
- NOT changed: the address sort (compile determinism), `preferred` (no dataplane consumer; out of the cited mechanism).

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master 5c6b94dc21`: new Go/Rust test files fail to build (`Primary` field/arity); intermediate one-pass pick failed `pickInterfaceSnapshotV4() = 10.0.0.10, want 10.0.0.9`.
- Go: `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestPrimaryAddressSnapshot15155|TestBuildSnapshotMarksConfiguredPrimary15155|TestPickInterfaceSnapshotFamilyFilters|TestMergeInterfaceAddressSnapshots|TestSnapshotShapeIsPinned|TestSnapshotProtocolVersionLockstep|TestContractSnapshotGolden9821|TestBuildSnapshotIncludesUnitInterfaces'` — ok.
- Rust: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-15155 cargo +1.98.1 test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- primary_address_15155 wire_invariant` — 4 passed (incl. `egress_primary_carries_designated_address_15155`: `egress[42].primary_v4 == 10.0.0.9`, `primary_v6 == 2001:db8::9`).

## Risk

Mixed-version pairing is fenced by the exact-equality gate (v54): a v53 helper refuses the snapshot rather than SNATing from the lexicographic address. Residual: with no designation xpf keeps first-non-link-local in builder order where Junos would use the numerically lowest address — pre-existing, documented in `docs/feature-gaps.md`; designating `primary` is the supported way to choose. Details: `docs/log/15155.md`.

Closes #15155
