## PR #15562 — cli: fix policy simulator / shadow-check fidelity cohort (#15238) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15238-campaign`

Closes #15238

## Cohort (A55-01, A55-02, A55-03) — all in `pkg/policymatch`

**A55-01 — shadow pass names the wrong coverer within the single-wildcard tier.**
`analyzeCrossTierGlobalShadowing` enforced tier precedence (#12893) but iterated the lexically sorted `pairs` inside tier 1. `("any","untrust")` sorts before `("trust","any")`, so a `trust→any` deny authored first lost to an `any→untrust` permit and a scoped global was reported REDUNDANT instead of SHADOWED. The tier walk now iterates `cfg.Security.Policies` (authored order), so probe row 1 reports `policy "scoped-permit" is SHADOWED … (e.g. "to-any-deny")`; flipped authored order still reports REDUNDANT naming the permit (control).

**A55-02 — simulator permits flows the helper drops at transit martian gates.**
`routeDropClass` was destination-only and missed most of the Rust sets (`addr_class.rs` `transit_src_is_martian`/`transit_dst_is_martian`, gated pre-policy in `poll_descriptor`). It is replaced by one shared `transitMartianClass` mirroring both sets plus `routeDropClassForQuery` (source first, then destination). Probe rows now report `RouteDropBeforePolicy=true` for martian sources (0/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, 224/4, 240/4, directed broadcast; `::`, `::1`, ff00::/8, fe80::/10) and for the previously missed destination classes (`this-network`, `link-local`, `reserved`; unspecified dst keeps its established `unspecified` spelling). Advisory-only — Matched/Action/DefaultUsed unchanged; host-bound queries exempt; nil sides unclassified.

**A55-03 — global scoped only to a quarantined zone reported as matching.**
`globalScopeSetMatches` tested raw `cfg.Security.Zones` membership; the snapshot builder drops such a rule (`globalScopeFullyQuarantined`/`scrubPoliciesForQuarantinedZones`), so the published snapshot has zero rules. Quarantined members (`ZoneQuarantineExclusionsForConfig`, same set `zoneKnown` uses) are now skipped: probe row 1 (host global scoped only to z214) → `HostInboundUnmatched`; trust-scoped control unchanged; mixed scopes still match on survivors.

## Regression (`pkg/policymatch/cohort_15238_test.go`)

All three tests fail on `origin/master` (RED verified: A55-01 prints REDUNDANT naming `from-any-permit`; A55-02 14/15 corpus rows unstamped; A55-03 host global matched) and pass after the fix, each with named legitimate controls through the same path. Neighbouring suites (`TestRouteDrop*`, `TestCrossTier*`, `TestAnalyzePolicyShadowing*`, `TestSharedMatcherGlobalScope*`, `TestQuarantinedZone*`, grpcapi MatchPolicies/RouteDrop) stay green.

Pre-existing base failure, unrelated: `TestSchedulerInactiveSkipsLikeRuntime/inactive_scheduled_deny_->_falls_through_to_active_permit` fails identically on pristine master (verified in a clean base worktree) — scheduler inactivity, no overlap with this change.

Docs: `docs/log/15238.md`.

`build-userspace-xdp.sh` hashed only file contents and ran cargo with the ambient environment, so an unpinned install (`XPF_SHIM_ALLOW_UNPINNED_INSTALL=1`) or a pinned build under ambient `RUSTFLAGS` installed a PASS gate verdict recording no toolchain, pinned bit, bpf-linker version or codegen env. - Freshness gate adopts a verdict build digest only for pinned, on-pin (`rust-toolchain.toml`), pinned-linker, scrubbed-env provenance; anything else reads as stale.
- Retention gate requires schema 2 and validates the same provenance before release upload.

## PR #15567 — snmp: serve error/unicast/ifLastChange cols, trap-only enable, reth rows (#15232) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15232-campaign`

## Why

- **A48-03:** `snmpEnabled` required a community or v3 user, so a trap-group-only config committed clean but never started the agent/link monitor — configured linkUp/linkDown traps were silently never sent.
- **A48-04:** `buildSNMPIfData` built rows only from netlink links. Bondless reths have no kernel device, so they had no IF-MIB row and traffic appeared on a node-specific member ifIndex on failover.

## What

- `pkg/snmp/agent.go`: serve ifTable cols 9, 11–15, 17–20 (ifLastChange TimeTicks; ifIn/ifOut Ucast/NUcast, Errors, Discards, UnknownProtos Counter32) from new `IfData` fields; walk order remains sorted by construction.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_snmp_reconcile.go`: `deriveIfCounters` fills the new fields (IN unicast = RxPackets−Multicast clamped, IN non-unicast = Multicast, OUT unicast = TxPackets upper-bound, OUT non-unicast/UnknownProtos honest zeros); ifLastChange tracks per-ifIndex oper transitions as TimeTicks since daemon start; `snmpEnabled` also enables on `TrapGroups`; bondless reths get a synthesized row (stable ifIndex `1<<24+rethN`, owning-member counters, oper = RG-primary && member-up, standalone = primary) via `RethToPhysical` + `cluster.IsLocalPrimary`.
- NOT changed: kernel rows, ifXTable columns, member link-trap ifIndex keying.
- Docs: `docs/log/15232.md`, `pkg/snmp/README.md`.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master`: daemon 15232 tests fail to build (missing `IfData` fields/helpers); the snmp column mechanism has no served values pre-fix.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/snmp/ -count=1` passes (full suite, incl. updated last-column walk tests); `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 15232 -count=1` passes; daemon SNMP/IfData subset passes; `go vet ./pkg/snmp/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean. Main agent should run the full daemon suite before merge.

## Risk

Synthetic reth ifIndexes (`>= 1<<24`) appear in ifTable/ifXTable and ifNumber (intended parity). ifLastChange epoch is daemon start rather than agent-restart start, so after a day-2 restart it is a lower bound — still monotonic for flap detection.

Closes #15232

## PR #15571 — config: count keys in parse budget and require full-identity rename/copy sources (#15195) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15195-campaign`

## Summary

Closes #15195 (A01-05 + A01-06, hostile-review cohort, validator consensus MATERIAL).

**A01-05 — parse budget did not count keys.** `parseStatements` charged 1 unit per statement while `parseKeys` appended keys without bound; one node pins three parallel per-key slices, so a key-dense statement reached ~4× the documented ~37 MB live-AST bound at the 16 MiB input cap with zero parse errors.

**A01-06 — rename/copy via partial match mutated a different object.** `matchNodeKeys` returns 1 on a first-key-only hit; `findNodeWithParent`/`childrenAtPath` descended through it, so `rename firewall filter term T2` (naming no node — the node is `[filter F1]`) renamed `term T2` under F1, and `Store.Rename` recorded phantom lineage for the bogus path.

## What

- `pkg/config/parser.go`: `parseKeys` stops appending at `maxParseNodes` and latches the existing budget ParseError; `parseStatements` charges `1+len(Keys)` per statement.
- `pkg/config/ast.go` / `ast_edit.go`: new `matchNodeKeysFull` (exact key list, or prefix-of-wider-node for descent only). `findNodeWithParent` rejects a terminal prefix match as a source; `childrenAtPath` prefers exact matches. Missing source now returns "source not found" before any mutation. Lenient `matchNodeKeys` and the display walkers are untouched.
- `pkg/config/parse_node_budget_8597_test.go`: #8597 heap cells updated for the per-key charge (minimal `a;` costs 2 units → tree stops at `maxParseNodes/2` nodes; below-budget probe sizes halved).
- New regressions: `pkg/config/cohort_15195_test.go`, `pkg/configstore/cohort_15195_test.go`; log: `docs/log/15195.md`.

## Validation

- **RED on pristine `origin/master`** (`fa3fae56a4`, new tests only): key-dense cells `errs=[]`; rename/copy/truncated-source cells mutate the wrong node; store rename succeeds via partial match. Controls (normal keys, #9881 wide-prefix parent) pass on base.
- **GREEN after fix**: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 15195`, `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 15195|Copy|Rename|5822|Insert|TestStore` pass.
- **Neighbour comparison**: broad subset (`TestParse|TestRename|TestCopy|TestInsert|TestDelete|8597|5822|5827|9881|TestShow|TestFormat|TestSetPath|TestNavigate|TestCompile`) — branch fails exactly the 6 tests that also fail on pristine master (incl. `TestCopyRenameClearsBracketProvenance_9881`, verified pre-existing in a clean base worktree), no new failures. The full `pkg/configstore` suite exceeds the local 300 s harness window; its relevant subsets are green and the main agent should run the full suite once.

## Risk

Full-identity matching could refuse a loosely-spelled rename/copy path that previously resolved by first key; all in-repo callers spell full identities (#3982/#5822/#9881 suites green). The per-key charge halves the statement ceiling for 1-key statements to 100k — still ~400× the largest shipped config.

Never merge — review only.

## PR #15575 — userspace-dp: stamp deterministic identity on synced-first NAPT64 BIB (#15179) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15179-campaign`

Why:
When the standby imports a deterministic NAPT64 session and no BIB
exists yet, reserve_flow_maybe_persistent minted an endpoint-
independent lease tagged deterministic:true but with
deterministic_identity:None. allocate_deterministic_v6_at joins an
existing BIB only when the identity equals Some(V6(params)), so after
failover every same-socket flow to a new remote failed with
AllocatorExhausted while any synced flow was active and for 300s
after; on expiry the socket received a different port. This broke the

Thread the prefix DeterministicV6 through
reserve_nat64_pool_port{,_capture_and_replace} (Option<DeterministicV6>
replacing the bool) into a new allocator entry
reserve_flow_maybe_persistent_with_identity, which stamps
deterministic_identity:Some(V6(params)) on the minted lease. The
existing reserve_flow_maybe_persistent delegates with None, so source-
NAT synced reserves and reseeds are unchanged. Production caller
reserve_synced_nat64_port_unless_peer_owns passes prefix.
deterministic_v6 after its existing tuple-match validation. Also
correct the stale comment claiming persistent is constructed solely
in synced.rs. NOT changed: the strict join predicate (no adopt-on-
None, which would trust an unvalidated tuple) and round-robin pools.

## PR #15576 — ha: isolate flow-export build failures per group and sample per interface (#15230) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15230-campaign`

Closes #15230

## A46-02 — per-group build isolation
Reconcile (v9 + IPFIX) built the full replacement set and returned on the first `NewExporter` error, so one collector whose warn-only source-address was not yet local stopped export for every instance and froze the running config. Now each template group builds independently: groups that build are published with the new config, only the failing group is marked failed (`Daemon.FlowExportFailedGroups()`, family `BuildFailed` stays set, hash not recorded so the 30s retry/next commit retries it), and a failing group keeps its previously running exporter (per-group #3742). Live generations are tracked so a partial swap never closes a retained group; teardown joins each generation via `joinWithBudget`.

Acceptance from the issue: instance `a` is live with the new config and `b` alone is failed — pinned by `TestPartialBuildPublishesHealthyInstance15230` and `TestPartialBuildDoesNotFreezeHealthyInstance15230` (day-2: published `a` carries the new collector address, retained `b` keeps its old source, recovery publishes both and clears the failure).

## A46-05 — per-interface sampling
`BuildSamplingZones` OR-ed unit flags per zone. It now also records `IfacesV4`/`IfacesV6` keyed by authored unit ref, and the daemon callbacks gate on `ShouldExportIface(..., rec.IngressIface, rec.EgressIface)` (names resolved from the records' ifindexes; `EgressIface` resolved in pkg/logging). An unsampled interface in a sampled zone is denied before the 1-in-N counter and counts zone-filtered; nameless records and hand-built zone-only configs keep prior zone semantics.

Acceptance: the probe's ge-0/0/1.0 flow is not exported — pinned by `TestSamplingPerInterface15230` (flowexport) and `TestSessionCloseSamplingPerInterface15230` (daemon, real reconcile→ProcessRawEvent, v9+IPFIX, sampled ge-0/0/0.0 control exports).

## Tests / docs
- New: `pkg/flowexport/sampling_interface_15230_test.go`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport_partial_15230_test.go`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport_sampling_interface_15230_test.go` — RED on origin/master (mechanisms absent), GREEN after.
- Controls green: flowexport + logging full suites; daemon #3742/#9166/#14608/#9035 flow-export tests.
- Note: `TestReconcileDHCPRelayWiresIfNameResolver9406` and `TestReconcilePushSharesTheCommitOnlyWhenThePeerReadsSecondary_9530` fail identically without this change's flowexport parts (unrelated DHCP/HA tests; not touched by this PR).

## PR #15578 — cluster: keep kernel-upgrade hold across single-RG reset (#15239) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15239-campaign`

Why:
`Manager.ResetFailover(rgID)` cleared the node-global `kernelUpgradeHold` inline, so a per-RG operator reset (`request chassis cluster failover reset redundancy-group 1`, or gRPC `cluster-failover-reset:1`) on a candidate-trialling node (journal ARMED, promotion marker not yet written) made the whole node election-eligible and let the unverified candidate claim primary on every RG before `xpf-kernel-promote` verified the dataplane. The daemon's 5s reconcile never re-asserts the hold, so the release was permanent for the boot.

What:
- `ResetFailover` no longer touches `kernelUpgradeHold`; its per-RG work (manual-failover clear, transfer-commit state, lease, failoverGen, weight recalc) is unchanged and the election stays held.
- `ResetAllFailover` clears the hold synchronously via `ClearKernelUpgradeHold()` before the per-RG resets — the sole synchronous reset producer, preserving the never-both-down property at the all-RG scope.
- Orchestrator transport follows: `grpcCluster.ResetFailover` now issues the single node-local `cluster-rejoin` SystemAction (`ResetAllFailover`, `PermMaint`, fabric-denied, mapped in `SystemActionVerbCommand`) instead of per-RG `cluster-failover-reset` actions that depended on the removed clear. `LocalRejoinComplete` readback unchanged.
- Stale rejoin comments retargeted (`TestResetFailover_ClearsKernelUpgradeHold` now drives `ResetAllFailover`); `pkg/cluster/README.md` + `docs/log/15239.md` updated.

Validation:
- RED on master: `TestResetFailoverSingleRGPreservesKernelUpgradeHold15239` fails (`kernel-upgrade hold cleared by failover reset (rejoin) rg=1`, both RGs primary); GREEN after, with `TestResetAllFailoverStillClearsKernelUpgradeHold15239` + `TestResetFailoverNoHoldUnchanged15239` controls.
- Wire: `TestSystemActionClusterRejoinClearsHold15239`, `TestSystemActionSingleRGResetPreservesHold15239`, `TestSystemActionClusterRejoinNoCluster15239` GREEN.
- Suites: `pkg/cluster` full — only pre-existing `TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752` (fails on pristine base too); `pkg/upgrade` ok; `pkg/authz` ok; `pkg/grpcapi` — only pre-existing base-attributed failures (`6960` vlan-tagging, `8629` census, `10769` sun_path length, all reproduced on base worktree).

Risk:
An operator who used a single-RG reset to force-release a stuck kernel-upgrade hold must now use the node rejoin (`xpfd upgrade kernel rejoin`) or wait for the promotion-marker reconcile. Deliberate: a per-RG verb must not assert node-level verification it never performed.

Closes #15239

## PR #15588 — ha: anchor fabric rollout grace at persisted first keying (#15262) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15262-campaign`

Why:
The #11676 fabric rollout grace was anchored at the in-memory
no-key -> key transition in Manager.UpdateConfig. Every xpfd process
start satisfies that transition, so every restart of a long-keyed
node re-opened up to 5 minutes of tokenless read-only fabric RPCs
(GetSessions, interface monitor, safe ShowText) until the peer
authenticated — recurring read-only disclosure to on-segment hosts
with no operator action (B04-02).

What:
Persist the first-keyed instant per accepted-key-set digest in
/var/lib/xpf/fabric-auth-grace (cluster/fabric_auth_grace.go):
HMAC-SHA256 over a domain tag keyed by each accepted key, no key
bytes stored. UpdateConfig now anchors on the first keying of the
current set: a restart under an unchanged set restores the persisted
time (backwards-stepped clocks distrust a future stamp, which only
shortens the grace); a changed set re-anchors and still gets its
grace; clearing clears. Persist is best-effort via fsatomic with a
Warn naming the reopened-grace consequence. grpcapi docs updated;
the 5-minute length, read-only set, and arming sources are unchanged.

Validation:
RED on origin/master: pkg/grpcapi TestFabricAuth15262 fails to build
(cluster.SetFabricAuthGraceStatePathForTesting undefined) — the
restart behaviour does not exist. GREEN: grpcapi #15262 + #11676
suites and cluster anchor/UpdateConfig/rotation tests pass
(go vet clean).

Risk:
A wiped /var/lib/xpf or a persistently failing anchor write falls
back to anchoring at that apply — indistinguishable from a genuine
new keying; the failure is Warn-logged. Rotation steps that change
the accepted set each get a fresh read-only grace, closed early by
peer authentication as before.

Closes #15262

## PR #15608 — userspace-dp: refuse decapsulated PMech holds and replay owned frames (#15243) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15243-campaign`

Why:
A60-01: PendingPMechReversePacket stored the outer XDP descriptor with
the post-decap inner meta and discarded the owned inner frame, so
replay sliced the outer UMEM frame at inner offsets and re-ran GRE/WG
decap against inner bytes (NotGre/NotWg). The held reverse packet was
never delivered during the IPsec install window (fail-closed loss,
bounded at 4 per token / 512 per binding).

What:
Refuse the hold for native decapsulated packets: new
pmech_replay::pmech_hold_admissible gate at the hold site in
poll_binding_process_descriptor_with_injection recycles the descriptor
and counts pmech_decap_hold_refused, like the over-cap branch.
PendingPMechReversePacket gains owned_frame; the replay pop threads it
and sources raw_frame from the owned bytes when present, so an
admissible owned-frame hold replays the inner packet from its own
bytes. Counter plumbed BatchCounters -> BindingLiveState (size guard
re-measured 2624->2688, offsets +8) -> snapshot -> refresh/reset ->
protocol -> Go -> Prometheus xpf_userspace_pmech_decap_hold_refused_total.
NOT changed: drain, waiter registration, native non-decapped and
injected hold/replay paths.

## PR #15609 — ha: announce RETH VIPs after a live MAC change (#15276) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15276-campaign`

Why:
A commit that changes a RETH member virtual MAC on the RG primary (for example moving the RETH to another redundancy group the same node also owns) was applied live by programRethMAC. That path reported linkCycled=false, so step 2.6b sent no announce, and the 2s direct-VIP reconcile did not announce either because the VIPs were already present. Neighbours kept the old MAC until their own ARP/ND ageing, black-holing inbound traffic to that RETH's VIPs.

What:
programRethMAC now reports macChanged separately from linkCycled (true only where the target MAC was written), threaded through programRethMACWithWorkerJoin and programRethMemberMAC into step 2.6, which folds changed members into a per-RG set. Step 2.6b keeps the address reconcile gated on an actual link cycle but announces for exactly the changed RGs: scheduleDirectAnnounce in direct mode, or the new RG-scoped vrrp.Manager.ReconcileVIPsForRG forced GARP in VRRP mode. Existing call sites and the #5103 canary follow the new signatures; docs/log/15276.md records the evidence.

Validation:
TestC10LiveMACChangeNoAnnounce (live change announces once, no change announces nothing, cycled control announces once, VRRP mode fires no direct announce) and the pkg/vrrp TestReconcileVIPsForRG*15276 cells: RED on base (build failure, the mechanism absent), GREEN after the fix. Affected daemon reth/5103/6871/6915 cells pass. pkg/vrrp carries one pre-existing failure, TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate, identical on pristine origin/master.

Risk:
Announces are scoped to RGs whose member MAC actually changed and to the existing primary/MASTER gates, so no new announce storm is introduced; a cycled RG keeps its single link-cycle-recovery announce rather than gaining a second one.

Closes #15276

`build_live_forward_request_from_frame` preserved any `02:bf:73:<id>`
source MAC that parsed as a same-zone V2 stamp, even when the packet
arrived on a non-fabric LAN port. A LAN host could forge another
same-zone interface's scope and choose the interface scope the peer
applies to punted packets (A65-02, MATERIAL 3-way consensus).

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forward_request.rs`: preserve the frame's V2
  source only when `ingress_is_fabric(forwarding, ingress_ident.ifindex)`.
  Otherwise mint via `resolve_fabric_redirect_for_ingress_identity`
  from the real logical ingress identity, falling back to the V1
  zone-only stamp. `fabric_nat_scope_stamp_mac_for_zone` and the
  receive-side stamp parser are unchanged.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_bind_forward.rs`: three regression
  cells driving the anchored builder directly —
  `lan_ingress_forged_v2_stamp_not_preserved_15246` (RED pre-fix),
  `fabric_ingress_v2_stamp_preserved_15246` (fabric control),
  `lan_ingress_unstamped_gets_real_identity_stamp_15246` (LAN control).
- `docs/log/15246.md`: issue log.

## Validation

- RED on origin/master 30659af88f (fix stashed, tests kept): LAN forged
  and LAN unstamped cells FAILED, fabric control passed (1 passed,
  2 failed).
- GREEN after fix, rebased on latest origin/master:
  `cargo test --bins -- 15246` — 3 passed, 0 failed.

## Risk

LAN punts whose real ingress has no V2 scope now degrade to the V1
zone-only stamp, the existing fail-closed fallback. Fabric re-punts
are byte-identical.

Closes #15246

## PR #15623 — userspace-dp: choose batch arm from capped CoS peek (#15187) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15187-campaign`

Why:
`build_cos_batch_from_queue` chose its Local/Prepared arm from the uncapped `cos_queue_front` head but popped through the cap-aware `cos_queue_peek_min_bucket(queue, target_bps)`. On a shaped flow-fair queue whose uncapped lowest-finish bucket is over the #1229 v7 cap while a bucket of the other item kind is under it, the first capped peek returned the other kind, the arm-mismatch break left an empty scratch, and the build returned `None` with every item resident. `observed_bps` only decays on TX accounting, so the class (including newcomers) wedged until a CoS config change and stuck Prepared items kept their UMEM frames.

What:
Sample `compute_drain_target_bps` once at build entry and dispatch the arm on the same capped peek the pop uses. The capped peek falls back to the lowest-finish bucket when all buckets are over-cap, so unshaped / all-over-cap / single-kind queues keep byte-identical selection. NOT changed: exact drains and exact/waterfill selectors already preflight through the capped selection and fall back to the other arm.

Validation:
- New `nonexact_mixed_local_prepared_capped_head_does_not_wedge` + mirror: RED on pre-fix builder (both return `None`), GREEN after fix.
- Controls `nonexact_flow_fair_build_applies_v7_bucket_cap` + `shared_exact_surplus_build_is_v_min_throttled` (#13062) stay green; `queue_service` suite 112/112.
- `cargo +1.98.1 check --release --bins` clean.
- [INFERENCE] Full test-binary build on current master is blocked by a pre-existing `mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032` E0063 (`MirrorConfigSnapshot` missing `ingress_vlan_id`/`unit_scoped` from #15114, reproduced on pristine origin/master); validation used a temporary local completion of that literal, reverted before push — this PR does not touch that file.

Risk:
Only arm choice changes, only when capped/uncapped selection disagree on item kind (previously zero bytes every pass). Empty queues still return `None`; no fail-open direction.

Closes #15187

Branch: `fix/15247-campaign`

Why:
A66-03: XSK NA/ARP-learned neighbors were inserted authoritative with no RX lease and no on-link target gate, so unsolicited adverts created entries that never aged and pinned the per-shard learn cap. A66-04: the kernel-neighbor program limiter dropped a genuine change arriving while every way of its bucket was hot; the claimed later-advert retry was false because the next advert reports `map_changed == false` and hit the proven-present return.

What:
Gate both XSK handlers in `poll_stages.rs` on `src_ip_on_link_for_ingress` (link-local excepted) and insert via new leased `insert_*_at` APIs in `sharded_neighbor.rs` (`NeighborRecord::xsk_learned`, same-MAC refresh, kernel-backed promotion unchanged). Add a single newest-wins `owed` slot to `KernelNeighborProgramLimiter`: a hot-bucket refusal is recorded without touching any way timestamp and retries on the next exact same-binding advert. NOT changed: kernel-monitor inserts stay authoritative; the #5288 aggregate rate cap is preserved.

Validation:
`cargo test --bins 15247` (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-15247): 4 passed — new XSK lease aging, off-link ARP/NA rejection with on-link/link-local controls, hot-bucket owed retry, owed supersession. Neighbouring `cargo test --bins neighbor`: 320 passed, 1 failed (`tests_txn_flow_cache ..._6075`, fails identically on pristine base 6c88e78b59, base-attributed). RED is by construction: the new cells call the new `_at` APIs and assert leased aging the pre-fix authoritative insert cannot satisfy. The #15520 mirror-literal test-compile break is already fixed on current master (`..Default::default()` at `mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032`), so it did not block this run.

Risk:
Off-link ARP/NA adverts no longer create neighbors (on-link, link-local, Go-mirror and resolver paths unchanged); un-backed XSK learns now expire at the RX idle age unless refreshed; a hot-bucket-refused kernel program is delayed at most one interval plus one advert. The owed slot is newest-wins, so under a sustained multi-victim flood only the newest refused binding is owed-tracked.

Closes #15247

## PR #15627 — userspace-dp: use RFC 1191 plateau for zero-MTU Frag-Needed (#15252) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15252-campaign`

Why:
A pre-RFC 1191 router sends ICMPv4 Fragmentation-Needed with the
Next-Hop MTU field zero. translate_icmpv4_message_to_icmpv6 turned
that into 0 + 20 clamped to 1280, pinning every affected IPv6
client to the minimum MTU regardless of the quoted datagram.
RFC 7915 section 4.2 requires the greatest RFC 1191 plateau below
the quoted Total Length, floored at 1280.

What:
Add the RFC 1191 Table 7-1 plateau table and rfc1191_plateau_mtu
helper in userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs. When the Frag-Needed MTU is
zero, read the quoted IPv4 Total Length from src[8..] (version
checked; a truncated or malformed quote keeps the 1280 floor
rather than dropping the error) and emit that plateau. Non-zero
MTUs keep the plain +20 translation. NOT changed: the v6-to-v4
PTB direction, nexthop capping, and the refuted section 5.2
minus-28 sub-leg.

Validation:
RED on rebased base (production reverted, tests kept): the two
new 15252 tests fail with left 1280, right 1492 at
nat64_tests.rs:2531 and the strictly-below edge at :2562.
GREEN: nat64_v4_to_v6_frag_needed filter 4 passed (new plateau
probe 1500-byte quote yields 1492, plateau edges, plus the
1400-to-1420 control and the 1280 clamp control); full nat64::
suite 221 passed, 0 failed. Rebased onto a8765d38bf and the
frag-needed filter re-verified (4 passed).

Risk:
Only the MTU==0 leg changes; it can now advertise up to 65535
for jumbo quotes instead of 1280, which is the RFC 7915 plateau
behaviour. Malformed quotes retain the previous 1280 floor.

Closes #15252

## PR #15628 — userspace-dp: consume single-use policy rebinds once per generation (#15188) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15188-campaign`

## Summary

userspace-dp: consume single-use policy rebinds once per generation (#15188)

C08-02: after a full snapshot apply with `policy-rematch extensive`, the coordinator's retained `ForwardingState` kept that apply's single-use `policy_session_rebinds`/`policy_rename_ancestry`. Helper-internal republishes (neighbor push, HA fabric refresh) clone the retained state through `publish_runtime_view`, so every worker rotated onto a fresh Arc and re-applied every rebind record — two BPF conntrack restamps plus shared-table restamps per record, on every worker, on every rotation, with no generation check — until the next Go publish cleared them. The Go-side strip (#10509/#11530/#12073) does not cover this helper-internal path.

## Fix

- `Coordinator::clear_single_use_policy_metadata`: clears the retained rebinds/ancestry immediately after the `publish_runtime_view()` in both full-apply sites (`refresh_runtime_snapshot_inner`, reconcile `apply_snapshot`). The published Arc keeps its copy, so the full apply still ships the rename exactly once; every later helper clone ships `rebinds=0`. The choke point deliberately does not strip (documented inline — it cannot distinguish a full apply from a helper republish).
- Worker-side backstop: `last_rebind_generation` in `worker_loop` tracks the config generation whose rebinds were already consumed; a same-generation republish passes an empty record slice. A record is applied exactly once per generation even if a republish still carries it.
- Field docs on the two `ForwardingState` fields record the single-use contract.

## Validation

- New regression cells (all RED with the fix reverted, GREEN with it):
  - `neighbor_push_after_full_apply_ships_no_rebinds_15188` — real full apply, then neighbor push ships `rebinds=0`/`ancestry=0`, neighbor still published.
  - `fabric_refresh_after_full_apply_ships_no_rebinds_15188` — same via `refresh_fabric_links`, fabric link still published.
  - `later_full_apply_still_ships_fresh_rebinds_15188` — control: a later full apply ships its fresh metadata once; retained state stripped again (per-apply, not a latch).
  - `rebind_record_applied_exactly_once_per_generation_15188` — real `worker_loop`: gen-8 apply rebinds the pair to `dmz->wan/p-new`; same-generation republish with a zone-rewritten record must not move the pair; gen-9 fresh record consumed normally.
- Neighbouring rotation suites (10590/9526/5686): 39 passed.
- Note: unmodified `origin/master` does not compile its Rust test target (`afxdp/mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032`, missing `MirrorConfigSnapshot` fields from #15113/#15114 — pre-existing, unrelated). The above runs used a temporary, reverted `..Default::default()` at that one literal; nothing of it is in this PR.

## Risk

Two `Vec::clear()` calls on already-committed coordinator state after the worker-visible store, plus one `u64` compare on the cold worker rotation branch. No wire/config change; per-packet path untouched.

Closes #15188

## PR #15632 — userspace-dp: bucket AllowedIPs LPM by prefix length (#15250) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15250-campaign`

## Summary

Implements #15250 (A69-03): AllowedIPs lookups scanned one flat cross-family `Vec` linearly per packet — `peer_for_dest` on every encap/PTB/segmentation peer selection and `matches_for_peer` on every decap source gate — so cost grew with the configured peer/prefix count on multi-peer hubs. The module docs said the opposite of the code (decap-only, outbound LPM never consulted, "trie", linear scan fine), and `load_table()` paid a `load_full()` Arc allocation per packet.

## What

- `wg/allowed_ips.rs`: per-family prefix-length-bucketed hash maps (33 IPv4 / 129 IPv6 masked-key buckets, longest length probed first) — cost bounded by prefix-length count, independent of table size. Global-LPM semantics (WG §5.4.6), first-inserter tie-break for duplicate prefixes, duplicate-insert idempotence, and fail-closed misses preserved exactly.
- `wg/engine.rs`: `load_table()` via ArcSwap guard (`load()` + one refcount clone); new `peer_for_dest_in(&PeerTable, dst)` + `table_snapshot()` so a caller selecting the same peer more than once per packet pays one load and observes one atomic snapshot; `frame/wg.rs::wg_peer_outer_dst` gained the optional-table form (existing callers unchanged).
- Docs corrected in `allowed_ips.rs`, `engine.rs`, `wg/mod.rs`, `wg/peer.rs`, `wg/tests.rs`, `frame/wg.rs`. `counters.rs` was cited in the issue but contains no AllowedIPs representation claim (grep-verified) — unchanged. `try_encap`'s explicit-pubkey contract unchanged.
- New bench `benches/allowed_ips_lookup.rs` gates the acceptance "lookup cost flat across P=1..1024" (exits non-zero if the bucketed P=1024/P=1 mean-cost ratio exceeds 4×).
- `docs/log/15250.md` + `debian/changelog`.

## Validation

- `cargo test --release --bin xpf-userspace-dp allowed_ips_tests` — 11 passed pre-rebase (12 with the engine scale test post-rebase), including new `lpm_at_1024_peer_scale`, `v6_slash_zero_and_host_route`, `non_octet_boundary_prefixes`, and `peer_for_dest_at_1024_peer_scale_15250` through the production engine.
- Decap controls (`decap_rejects*`): 5 passed. `frame::wg`/`wg_encap`: 34 passed. `wg_control`: 80 passed.
- `wg::` module: 341 passed, 2 failed (`gre_tun_origin_*_10038`, `local_tunnel_resolution:ha_inactive`) — base-attributed: identical failures on pristine base `bda827750b` in a detached worktree; GRE local-origin builder, unrelated to AllowedIPs.
- Bench: flat scan 8.7 → 121.5 → 1125.4 → 8315.3 ns/query at P=1/16/128/1024; bucketed 38.8 → 42.8 → 40.5 → 39.7 ns; flatness ratio 1.02× (gate ≤ 4×) — PASS. The old shape's ~1000× growth is the RED the gate catches for this pure-cost defect.
- Base note: at the original branch base the test target had a pre-existing compile break (`mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032` missing #15113 fields, confirmed with `cargo test --no-run` on pristine base); branch runs temp-fixed then reverted that site. It is fixed on current master, and the rebased head builds clean (12 passed above).

## Risk

No wire, config, or counter change; LPM answers bit-identical (same winner, tie-break, fail-closed miss). Memory stays O(configured prefixes), rebuilt only at config commit.

Closes #15250

Synced deterministic-v4 (CGNAT mode 1) imports were booked without a
block-membership check. The NAT64 twin
(`reserve_synced_nat64_port_unless_peer_owns`) already requires
`deterministic_v6_tuple_matches`, but both synced v4 arms in
`reserve_synced_on_first_pool_owner` passed only
`rule.deterministic_v4.is_some()` as a tag to the allocator, so
`deterministic_v4_tuple_matches` had no production caller. A peer
whose deterministic map disagrees (config-sync window, or a peer
bug) could therefore publish a synced session naming an
out-of-block translated `(pool address, port)` on the standby — a
tuple this node would never mint, whose reverse mapping then
disagrees with the deterministic function. Once configs converge
the active's port is in-block under the shared map, so legitimate
imports are unaffected.

What:
- `nat/source/synced.rs` port-bearing arm: require
  `deterministic_v4_tuple_matches(det, src, pool_addresses_v4,
  addr_index, translated, port)` and return `Refused` otherwise.
- `nat/source/synced.rs` address-only arm: the wire preserves the
  source port, so require the address half only —
  `deterministic_indices_v4` must assign exactly the translated pool
  address. A non-V4 source cannot satisfy a V4 map and refuses.
  Both checks sit after `saw_candidate` is set, mirroring the
  pool-failure arm, so PASS 2 degrades to `Refused` rather than
  leaking the tuple into the interface domain, and PASS 1 still
  stops at the first owner.
- `nat/tests_synced_det_v4_15267.rs` (new, registered in
  `nat/mod.rs`): three fail-on-revert cells — out-of-block port,
  wrong pool address (port-bearing, PASS 2), wrong pool address
  (address-only, PASS 1) — plus two in-domain controls (in-block
  port reserved; address-only on the subscriber's address
  reserves its token).
- `nat/tests_idle_lease_sync_8121.rs`: update the lease-creation
  census pin from `reserve_flow_maybe_persistent` to
  `reserve_flow_maybe_persistent_inner` (the shared body behind
  `reserve_flow_maybe_persistent` and its `_with_identity` twin);
  same #7360 standby route, only the enclosing function name.
  This corrects the census expectation to match the code on
  master, where the `_inner` body holds the insert; NOT a new
  creation site.
- `docs/log/15267.md`: defect, fix, and RED/GREEN evidence.

Validation:
- RED (test file + census pin only, on `origin/master`
  51c40e851f): the three mechanism cells FAIL (imports accepted,
  ports/tokens booked); both controls PASS.
- GREEN (rebased onto `origin/master` 4ddf6c68ab): full `nat::`
  suite 695 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored — including the census

## PR #15635 — nat: honour source pool port range in NAT64 allocator (#15283) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15283-campaign`

Why: a source pool's `port range` was silently ignored when the pool
was used by a NAT64 rule-set. NAT64RuleSnapshot carried no port range,
the mode-2 deterministic block math and the Rust per-prefix
PortAllocator both used the fixed 1024-65535 window, so translated
ports spanned 1024-65535 regardless of the operator's range with no
commit error or warning (V52-S1).

What: carry the pool range end to end. NAT64RuleSnapshot gains
port_low/port_high (Go + Rust mirrors); buildNAT64Snapshots stamps
them from config.SourceNATPoolPortRange on usable pools and
deterministicNAT64V6Fields plus pkg/nat mode-2 poolParams compute
blocks against the pool range. The Rust allocator is built over the
effective range (snapshot range when valid, else the fixed default),
the #6982 aggregate charge follows it, and reload reuse is
range-aware so a changed range gets a fresh allocator. Protocol
v54 -> v55 fences the pairing; protocol_wire_v1.json and
docs/deterministic-nat-cgnat.md updated. NOT changed: pools without
an explicit range keep the default window byte-identically.

Validation: new Go cells in nat64_port_range_15283_test.go (snapshot
stamps 2000/3000, default control, mode-2 blocks-per-IP 10 vs 645
pre-fix) and Rust nat64_15283_* cells (first flow at 2000 vs 1024
pre-fix, deterministic block [2500,2599], range-change reset) pass;
413 nat64-filter Rust tests pass; TestDeterministicParamsMatchWire-
Builders, version lockstep and the #8892 shape pin pass at v55;
pkg/nat passes. Pre-existing failures reproduce on pristine
origin/master and are unrelated (pkg/dataplane/userspace compile-
error cells; wire fixture pmech/nat_scope drift from master).

Risk: a narrowed pool now exhausts at its real capacity instead of
silently spilling outside the range. Mixed-version pairs refuse the
snapshot at the v55 fence and keep the previous-good image rather
than dropping the range silently.

## PR #15636 — config: memoise address-set graph gate and expansion (#15003) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15003-campaign`

## Summary

Memoises the #12832 address-set graph gate and address-set expansion (#15003, A04-02). Both walks previously enumerated every DAG path with no memo, and the strict validator re-ran the gate once per root set, so a legal breadth-20 lattice at the five-edge cap cost ~B^6 per compile (~5.5s for a 741-line config) on commit, commit check (under the store read lock), boot load and SyncApply.

- Gate: per-node max-depth-below (height) memo; re-entry runs the live entry check first, then decides the depth cap arithmetically and reconstructs the exact naive first-node-wins depth error on overflow. Strict validator validates all roots against one shared memo.
- Expansion: deduped result + subtree height recorded per ID-graph/leaf mode. Fixes the leaf-mode `address-set` edge divergence (edges partitioned by an explicit `viaAddr` kind tag; previously leaf-mode set edges were mis-bucketed and dropped, returning empty expansions) and adds depth synthesis on memo hits (a shallow-path success is no longer served into a deeper, over-cap context).
- Cycle/depth messages, error precedence, the `ExpandAddressSet` ID-graph contract, and the tolerant-load warning downgrade are unchanged. `expandAddrSetMode` is removed; README and `docs/log/15003.md` updated.

## Validation

Fresh-binary runs (source mtimes verified against the test binary):

- `TestAddrSetGraphGateMemoised15003|TestAddrSetMemoPreservesSemantics15003|TestAddrSetExpansionIsLinear15003` — PASS. Breadth-20 lattice strict-validates in ~1ms (acceptance <1s); leaf expansion = 101 bodies for 121 sets (naive ~B^5; breadth 3: 16 vs 364); differential memo-vs-naive agreement on results and error text, exact cycle/depth messages pinned.
- `TestCrossKind*` — PASS (12502/12832 controls).
- Full `pkg/config` suite — identical 113 pre-existing base failures on branch and clean base worktree (`27920f2f8c`), zero regressions, zero address-set failures.
- `gofmt`/`go vet` clean on changed files.

## Risk

Accept/reject answers and diagnostics are differentially pinned to the pre-fix recursion; the only behavioural change is wall-clock on wide DAGs. No live-cluster mutation.

Closes #15003

## PR #15637 — userspace-dp: reclaim oldest incomplete anchor across zones at shard cap (#15288) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15288-campaign`

## Summary

Implements #15288 (gemini D4-01, adjudicated MATERIAL): two zones holding 32 incomplete fragment-overlap entries each in one shard left a third zone no reclaimable anchor, so its first fragment dropped `ShardFull` — defeating the #14321 per-zone reserve.

## Fix

At the 64-entry shard cap, when no **completed** anchor of any zone in the candidate's routing domain is reclaimable and the candidate's `(domain, zone)` is strictly below its 32-entry reserve, reclaim the globally oldest **settled-incomplete** anchor (`pending == 0`, not failed, ranges not covering a terminal end) of a **different** zone in the same routing domain. Completed anchors remain preferred (#15103 path unchanged); failed (poisoned) and still-pending anchors are never reclaimed. Per-zone fairness holds by ordering: a candidate already at 32 has exited through the own-zone branch, so admission can only displace another zone's anchor.

New counter: `FRAG_OVERLAP_CROSS_ZONE_INCOMPLETE_RECLAIMED` (sibling of the #15103 counter; delta-read in tests like its sibling).

## RED / GREEN

- RED on base `4ddf6c68ab` (test + counter only): `third_zone_admitted_past_incomplete_zones_via_incomplete_reclaim_15288` FAILED — `zone-C victim must be admitted by cross-zone incomplete reclaim, reason=Some(ShardFull)`.
- GREEN with fix: zone C admitted, `len` stays 64, zone A capped at 32 (fresh A key refuses rather than stealing C's slot), evicted A anchor no longer drops overlaps, C's anchor survives A churn, exactly one incomplete-reclaim bump, zero completed-reclaim / shard-full bumps, failed-anchor shard still refuses fail-closed.
- `cargo test --bins fragment_overlap`: 45 passed. `cargo test --bins 9950`: 28 passed. `cargo test --bins -- cross_zone`: 17 passed.
- The #15103 regression's Control 2 is updated to the surviving invariant (cross-domain candidate still fails closed over an incomplete fill); same-domain admission is now covered by the new test.

## Risk

An evicted settled-incomplete anchor loses overlap protection for the rest of its TTL — the trade #14321/#15103 already accept for completed anchors. No behaviour change below the shard cap, when a completed anchor is reclaimable, or at a zone's own reserve. `docs/log/15288.md` records the full analysis.

Closes #15288

GREEN on rebased ee1b26272b: `15145` 4 passed; `8115` 26, `9021` 4, `13691` 5, `14368` 6, `8121` 72, `nat::` 693. Base-attributed on pristine ee1b26272b: `strict_mirror_refusal_replays_imported_lease_and_holder_mask_11476_10789_f4` and `test_encode_session_open_carries_nat64_flag_and_snat_v4` fail identically unmodified; `9034`/`5798` wide-filter one-offs pass in isolation and paired on master.

## PR #15644 — nat: hold persistent lease for inbound sessions (#15111) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15111-campaign`

Why: persistent_inbound_lookup took no lease reference. An inbound-only
persistent binding expired at inactivity-timeout after the last outbound
flow; GC freed its tuple and a second internal host could be minted the
same tuple toward a live inbound peer, while new inbound peers lost
persistent-NAT reachability.

What: PersistentLease gains inbound_flows, counted separately from
active_flows; every lease-liveness predicate (lookup, reuse, GC, clear,
release/rollback completion, synced joins, BIB joins, address-only
contention, display export) treats an inbound hold as live and the
expiry index only holds leases with both counts at zero.
persistent_inbound_lookup returns the lease key; acquire/release/
rollback_persistent_inbound take and drop holds, re-arming expiry on
last release. Poll captures the key at DNAT lookup, acquires once the
final NAT decision is composed (skipped when SNAT joined via
active_flows, NAT64, NPTv6) and only on an anchoring install
(ForwardCandidate, LocalMiss, FabricPuntSeed, MissingNeighborSeed),
rolling back on every refusal exit. The release/rollback entry points
(worker, synced-untracked, untracked) also release the inbound hold
derived from the session key + decision, covering GC reap, delete-sync,
purge, promote, revalidation and dropped-delete repairs; HA synced
inbound sessions acquire/release through the synced reserve wrappers.
Revalidation stays read-only (it holds a live session already).

rebase onto origin/master. New regression

steal the tuple, release re-arms expiry, GC reclaims). Full nat::
suite 683 passed / 0 failed (pre-rebase head; the only rebased test

missing nat_scope_ifindex in rebind_once_per_generation_15188_tests.rs,
also present on origin/master itself). Full --bins suite 8584 passed /

## PR #15735 — userspace-dp: borrow shared UMEM for owner bind instead of panicking (#15730) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15730-shared-umem-owner`

Closes #15730

## Why
Under the default CrossNic shared-UMEM policy the helper worker threads panicked deterministically at `umem/mod.rs:106` and the helper never armed (loss cluster, master 7d95e004cb). `create_shared_binding_group` clones one `WorkerUmem` for every group member, so the `Rc` is shared before the first socket is created; since #15088 the owner (and the private fallback) reaches its `&mut Umem` through `Rc::get_mut(..).expect("single-owner umem")`, which is `None` the moment a second clone exists. The owner create therefore panicked after the zero-copy attempt had already reported EINVAL, so the copy-mode fallback never ran, worker bring-up failed closed, and RG1/RG2 had no forwarding primary.

## What
- `umem/mod.rs`: `WorkerUmemInner.umem` is now `RefCell<Umem>` (field order unchanged, still before `area` per #5192); `umem_mut(&self) -> RefMut`, `umem() -> Ref`, `as_raw_umem_ptr` borrows — any cloned handle can run its one-at-a-time bind-time create, and an overlapping borrow still panics loudly instead of aliasing libxdp ring state.
- `bind.rs`: `&mut worker_umem.umem_mut()` at the private and shared-owner creates.
- Stale `Rc::get_mut` contract text in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` / `worker/lifecycle.rs` now names the RefCell borrow (bind-time only, unchanged contract).
- Regression: hermetic cloned-UMEM cells in `umem/tests/shared_clone_15730.rs` (panics at the pre-fix expect; overlap control pins the loud panic) + source tripwire `tests/shared_umem_owner_umem_mut_15730.rs`, in the style of the #15088/#15244 pins.
- NOT changed: the `Rc` sharing itself, the bind ladder, roles, fallbacks, or the C bridge.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bins -- 15730`: both new cells pass (the no-panic cell panics on the pre-fix accessor); drop-order controls pass.
- `cargo test --test shared_umem_owner_umem_mut_15730 --test shared_owner_ebusy_retry_15088 --test post_create_bind_terminal_15244`: all pass.
- Controls (bind_identity_9904, bind_owner_retry_15088, umem_sizing_7497, tx_submit_ns_sidecar_single_writer_ownership_is_rc_not_arc, shared_owner_*_15088): 14 pass.
- Loss-cluster re-test with the `shared-umem mode off` stanza removed (mode auto) still needs the cluster and remains operator validation — do NOT remove that stanza from the cluster until this ships.

## Risk
RefCell moves exclusivity from compile time to runtime: a future caller holding `umem_mut` across a re-entrant create panics at bring-up (fail closed, loud) rather than aliasing; the overlap cell pins that. No hot-path change: `umem_mut` runs only at bind time. Private and shared-secondary binds are behaviour-identical.

## PR #15738 — cluster,daemon: follow RG ownership for statics and release spent failback holds (#15734) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15734-rg-transit-failback`

## Summary

Fixes both coupled defects from the recorded #12495 gate FAIL (#15734):

1. **Transit6 blackhole (RG2 on node1, RG1/WAN on node0).** `assembleFRRConfig` HA-filtered dynamic protocols by RG ownership (#11415) but passed static routes through unfiltered on every node. On the non-WAN owner the WAN statics (`::/0 via 2001:559:8585:50::1` on reth0.50, the `2602:…::/64` via reth0.80) stayed in the FRR managed section, zebra marked them inactive (egress connected prefixes leave with the VIPs), and the cluster-mode Null0 default became the selected route — verified read-only on the live cluster (node1: statics inactive, blackhole selected, no connected WAN /64; node0 healthy). New `frrHADemotionState.filterStaticRoutes` drops (or per-hop prunes) statics whose egress — explicit/inferred next-hop interface, or the RETH connected prefix containing the next-hop — belongs to an RG this node is not primary for. Non-RETH, next-table, discard/reject routes are kept; promotion re-renders via the existing HA FRR reconcile.

2. **Failback stranded >300s.** The gate's plain failback (`ManualFailover` on node1) demoted node1, node0's dual-resign guard cleared its hold, node1's committed-transfer pin re-elected it primary, and node0's re-armed `ManualFailover` could never clear again — `electRG` only released a hold for a resigned/transferred-out peer. `electRG` now also releases the hold (same 2s guard) when the peer is primary and the local RG is the committed secondary; clearing does not promote the local node.

## Regression tests

- `pkg/daemon/frr_static_ha_15734_test.go`: all-primary control; the recorded split drops both WAN statics, prunes the mixed route to its LAN hop, keeps the non-RETH route, no config mutation; promotion restores. Mutant-verified.
- `pkg/cluster/failback_hold_15734_test.go`: stranded shape clears and stays secondary (mutant-verified); hold preserved without the commit pin; 2s guard respected.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/cluster -run 15734 -count=1` — pass
- `go test ./pkg/daemon -run 15734 -count=1` — pass
- Adjacent daemon FRR tests (11415/11393/11449) — pass
- `pkg/frr` suite: 4 failures reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` (pre-existing; package untouched)
- Full `pkg/cluster` / `pkg/daemon` suites: see follow-up comment

Cluster was already restored healthy by SmokeMatrix before this lane (RG0/1/2 primary node0, transit 3/3); no lab mutation by this change. Live re-proof is the #12495 gate re-run on the converged build.

## PR #15739 — userspace-dp: single-write SessionKey hash and skip unused PTB inner-dst parse (#14300) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `perf/14300-sessionkey-hash-ptb-parse`

Refs #14300

## Why
Loss-cluster perf profile (user-supplied): `SessionKey Hash` 3.33%, `compute_forwarded_egress_ptb_with_dynamic` 1.21%, under `poll_binding_process_descriptor_with_injection` 16.18%.

- Derived `SessionKey: Hash` issues ~12 typed `write_*` calls; under the production `KeyedFxHasher` (`hot_hash_seed.rs`, #12989) **every** typed write is a full splitmix64 fold (~9 multiplies). Per established packet the key is hashed repeatedly (flow-cache `set_index`, `session_is_live_at`, `touch_if_stale`, `account_packet`, plus slow-path `key_to_handle` + alias indices).
- `compute_forwarded_egress_ptb` called `post_transform_inner_destination` (ethertype walk + `inner_dst_ip`) on **every** non-NAT64 forward, but only the WireGuard arm of `post_transform_inner_mtu` consumes it (GRE ignores it at `icmp_ptb.rs` `tunnel_inner_mtu`, plain path never calls it). It also resolved L3 ethertype-first, discarding the trusted stamp.

## What
- `session/key.rs`: manual `Hash` for `SessionKey` — one `Hasher::write` over a fixed 49-byte family-tagged stack image (af/proto, `(tag,16B)` src/dst, ports, routing_domain, `(disc tag,val)`). Eq unchanged; hasher/seed unchanged. New `session_key_hash_14300_tests` proves equal⇒equal-hash and every field (incl. `Keyed(0)` vs `Unkeyed` vs `None`, v4-vs-v6 aliasing) splits.
- `icmp_ptb.rs` / `tx/dispatch/mod.rs`: `post_transform_needs_inner_dst` (WireGuard endpoint only) gates the parse; NAT64 still returns `rewrite_dst`. PTB L3 resolution now prefers `nibble_trusted_stamp`, falling back to `frame_l3_offset`. New parse-skip test with parseable control.
- `benches/session_key_hash.rs` (+ Cargo registration): derived-vs-manual under KeyedFxHasher and SipHash.

## Validation (local, this host)
- `cargo test --bins -- icmp_ptb session_key`: 68 passed (incl. 62 PTB, seeded s3-clique dispersion #12603, new hash tests).
- Bench, KeyedFxHasher (production): derived **34.0 ns v4 / 41.9 ns v6** → manual **24.7 / 23.6 ns** (−27% / −44%). SipHash: 61.3/75.7 → 37.6/40.5 ns.
- NOT yet cluster-validated: no deploy/re-profile done (smoke lane owns the cluster; shared-UMEM still OFF there). Expected recovery is a share of the 3.33% hash slice, not the whole profile.

## Risk
- Hash **values** change: all `SessionKey` maps are node-local per-process (`hot_hash_seed.rs`: HA sync transmits keys, never hashes). No wire/persistence impact.
- PTB: WireGuard per-peer MTU path byte-identical (gate = exact consumer predicate, covered by `post_transform_wg_inner_mtu_is_per_peer_underlay`); GRE/plain previously discarded the parsed value. L3 stamp-first matches every other hot-path consumer (#9900 nibble check retained).

## Deliberately NOT in this PR (filed as issue, see #14300 comment)
`__memmove` 13.6% attribution: fast path is zero-copy (in-place / direct-TX / flow-cache inline); copies are (a) copy-fallback `vec![0; len+4]` + payload memcpy + second UMEM memcpy in `transmit` when shared-UMEM is OFF (cluster's current workaround state — fix #15735 is merged, so re-enabling shared-UMEM is the lever, needs smoke-lane validation), (b) decap/injected `to_vec`, (c) mirror clones, (d) TCP segmentation. No code change claimed without a cluster profile showing which dominates.

## PR #15744 — routing,userspace: import cluster unreachable default as reject (#15742) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15742-split-rg-transit`

## Summary
Fixes the split-RG transit half of #15742: with RG2 (LAN) on node1 and RG1 (WAN) on node0, v4+v6 transit blackholed while NA recovery succeeded.

**Root cause (live-verified on 8871e79a9d):** the cluster-mode Null0 default that exists to terminate a split node's lookup is installed by FRR in the kernel as `RTN_UNREACHABLE proto static metric 20` (zebra `S>* ::/0 [250/0] unreachable (blackhole)`, `ip route`: `blackhole default proto static metric 20`), but `ImportLearnedRoutes` adopted only RTN_UNICAST/RTN_BLACKHOLE, and `addLearnedRouteSnapshots` suppressed imported rows behind same-prefix config rows. The fw1 helper FIB therefore held only the config defaults (pref 5 via the peer-owned WAN egress) and no terminal default (`show route fib` captured live).

**Fix:** adopt RTN_UNREACHABLE as `LearnedRoute.Reject` (RTN_PROHIBIT stays excluded; HA sentinel 4242 excludes both negative forms), map to `RouteSnapshot.Reject` (Rust `RejectRoute` already exists), add Reject to the dedupe key, never suppress a negative learned row behind a forwarding row. Preference ordering (forwarding 5 < imported 200) keeps the real default selected while usable; HA demotion + fabric redirect fire when the egress RG is peer-owned.

**Failback half:** dispositioned in `docs/log/15742.md` — targeted failbacks return iter=1 in every reproduction (incl. this session); the gate's early plain-form shape remains under #13058's timing lane. No deadline widening.

## Test report
- `go test ./pkg/routing/ -run '15742|11398'` — pass (new: cluster unreachable adopted both families; HA sentinel unreachable excluded; prohibit-only negative cell).
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '15742|11398'` — pass (config default + imported reject coexist, forwarding preferred).
- Both Go cells mutant-verified RED (adoption revert; suppression revert), then GREEN.
- `cargo test split_rg_cluster_reject` — pass (RG1 active forwards v4+v6; inactive HA-demotes → FabricRedirect).
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite: 2 failures (`13149`, `13151`) reproduced identically on pristine origin/master — pre-existing, untouched area.
- Live: split-RG blackhole reproduced pre-fix under the cluster lock (v4+v6 0/3; helper FIB without reject default; cluster restored, RG2 back iter=1). Post-fix deploy + `test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` re-run is the remaining lab acceptance.

Closes #15742

v58 renders `discard cluster-terminal` pref 200 on split fw1, yet transit still 0/3 both families. LIVE trace (working-20705, split reproduced 5×, cluster restored healthy each time):

- fw1 per-probe: Forward candidates +3, TX +3, Session creates +0 — the demote chain (i) lookup `ClusterTerminalHAInactive`, (ii) `source_ifindex=14` (reth0.80/RG1), (iii) HA keeps demotion, (iv) fabric redirect with zone stamp all execute.
- fw0 per-probe: **Invalid fabric-stamp drops +3 per family** — step (v) fails: redirected frames arrive and die at fabric-ingress stamp validation.

Offline replay of the EXACT live snapshots (scratch harness, removed): fw0 `zone_to_rgs={wan:[1]}` only — **`lan` missing**, stamp parse → `Invalid`. Root cause: `populate_zone_to_rgs` lets any blank-zone row veto its shared ifindex; the physical member row (`ge-0/0/1`, zone="") sharing the RETH netdev zeroed ifindex 5, so `lan` never gained RG attribution and `zone_encoded_fabric_stamp_valid` (V1b) rejected every punt.

## What

`populate_zone_to_rgs`: a blank row vetoes only when it aliases a unit on the same ifindex (its name is that unit's base — the #13181 unzoned-alias shape); blank physical members do not vote. Conflicting nonzero zones still zero the claim; the `egress_zone` ledger gate is unchanged. No wire/protocol change. Full trace: `docs/log/15742f.md`.

## Validation

- New regression `zone_to_rgs_reth_member_blank_row_does_not_veto_15742f` (exact live RETH row shape). FAIL-ON-REVERT proven by live replay (`{13098:[1]}` → after fix `{13098:[1], 21230:[2]}`, stamp `Valid(21230)`).
- `cargo +1.98.1 test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- zone_to_rgs split_rg fib_dump` PASS (17, incl. the #13181 veto cell); `-- fabric` PASS (207); `-- forwarding_build` PASS (311).
- Live acceptance deferred to smoke lane (deploy, split, expect 3/3 both families, zero Invalid-stamp deltas).

## Risk

Only non-alias blank rows stop voting; contested zones still fail closed. Failback timing strand remains #13058.

## PR #15749 — userspace: resolve VLAN subinterface counters to parent binding (#15656) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15656-campaign`

Closes #15656

## Why
`Manager.ReadInterfaceCounters` matched only the exact `BindingStatus.Ifindex`. The AF_XDP helper binds only the parent physical netdev, so every VLAN subinterface (`ge-0/0/0.<vlan>`, own kernel ifindex) returned authoritative `(0,0,0,0),nil` while the parent carried traffic. REST `/interfaces` + `/stats/interfaces`, gRPC `GetInterfaces`, CLI and Prometheus all rendered that as real zero traffic (the #3464 `Unavailable` flag only fires on error, so success+zero was final).

## What
- `ReadInterfaceCounters` tracks `matched`: on no direct match it consults the retained snapshot — a row with `Ifindex == request && ParentIfindex > 0` resolves the VLAN child to its parent binding and returns the parent's aggregated RX/TX counters (minimum fix direction in the issue; per-`(ifindex,vlan_id)` helper counters remain future work, so sibling units share the parent aggregate).
- When neither a direct binding nor a bound snapshot parent covers the ifindex, it fails closed with `userspace interface counters unavailable: no binding covers ifindex %d` instead of a confident zero.
- A directly bound idle interface still matches and returns its real zero.
- Supersedes the #13273 "unknown ifindex = zero, no error" expectation (updated test).
- No consumer changes needed: existing #3464 contract maps the error to REST `Unavailable`, Prometheus omitted sample + `xpf_interface_counter_read_errors_total`, CLI warning.
- `docs/log/15656.md` + `debian/changelog` entry.

## Validation
- RED on `origin/master`: `TestReadInterfaceCountersVLANChildResolvesToParent15656` fails with child = `{0,0,0,0}` vs parent aggregate `{15,1500,23,2300}`.
- GREEN: `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-15656 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestReadInterfaceCounters|TestLegacyAdapterForwards' -count=1 -v` — all #13273 + #15656 cells pass (aggregates, VLAN child→parent, unbound parent fail-closed, uncovered ifindex fail-closed, idle bound zero, no-snapshot fail-closed, unavailable fail-closed, adapter forwarding).

## Risk
A configured interface the helper never binds now reports counter-unavailable instead of a clean zero — the intended fail-closed direction of the acceptance criteria. Directly bound interfaces are unaffected.

- Existing suites pass: #8993/#11329/#12851/#14330/#11007 fingerprint, quarantine, rename-ancestry.

## Risk
Fingerprint values change universally but are computed fresh on both sides of each commit diff (no persisted values to skew). Residual: reordering overlapping application terms with different inactivity timeouts no longer re-evaluates sessions; verdict/matched set unchanged.

## PR #15751 — config: scan global zone-leaf tails for collapsed match keywords (#15660) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15660-campaign`

Closes #15660

## Why
`policyUnsupportedMatchLeafFindings` short-circuited global `from-zone`/`to-zone` leaves (`if isGlobal && globalOnlyPolicyMatchLeaves[leaf] { continue }`) before scanning their collapsed tail. Global zone leaves are `multi:true`, so:
- `match from-zone any dynamic-application junos:FTP` (flat set) collapsed the unsupported criterion onto the zone leaf — strict commit misdiagnosed it as an undefined/mixed-zone error (#4626/#3402 wording) instead of the #3113 unsupported-leaf rejection, and tolerant load published an unscoped permit with `LenientContentDropped=false`.
- A hierarchical missing semicolon (`from-zone any` + `to-zone untrust;`) or `from-zone [ any to-zone untrust ]` fused the sibling zone keyword onto the first zone leaf and committed silently.

(Probe-verified: flat-set fused forms do not collapse — SetPath stops at the registered sibling and compiles correctly as separate leaves; the fused shape is hierarchical-only. The collapsed unsupported keyword reproduces in both forms.)

## What
- `pkg/config/compiler_policy_match.go`: scan `firewallMatchValues(m)` for global-only leaves exactly like supported leaves. Unsupported keywords are flagged as unsupported leaves (#3113); a fused `from-zone`/`to-zone` keyword as a swallowed structural token (#3673). Strict rejects with the correct diagnostic; tolerant load warns and sets `LenientContentDropped` so the snapshot builder poisons the rule (#5575). Corrected the stale "cannot arise in global scope" comment and message wording.
- The report's second hunk (rejecting `any`+unresolvable scopes in `unresolvableScopeElement`/`build_global_zone_scope`) is **deliberately not taken**: the contains-`any` wildcard is documented design (Rust tolerant backstop for corrupt/mixed-version snapshots, Go `IsWildcardZoneSet`, #9410 mirror contract), the strict gate already rejects mixing `any` with concrete zones at commit, and changing only the Go mirror would diverge `show security match-policies` from the helper. With the compiler fix, collapsed bogus tokens can no longer reach the snapshot as a clean scope. `TestPolicyZoneRejectionMixedAnyScopeIsWildcard15660` pins this with a `[ghost]` control.
- Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` #15660 paragraph, `docs/log/15660.md`.

## Validation
- RED on origin/master: 9 failing subtests (wrong-reason strict errors, silently committed fused forms, `LenientContentDropped=false`); legit-scope controls green pre- and post-fix.
- GREEN post-fix: `pkg/config/compiler_policy_match_15660_test.go` (strict unsupported ×4, strict fused ×3, lenient poison ×2, legit controls ×3) and `TestPolicyZoneRejectionMixedAnyScopeIsWildcard15660`.
- Targeted suites pass: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestPolicyMatch|TestGlobalPolicy|TestPolicyZone|Test.*3148|Test.*3142|Test.*3673|Test.*3113|Test.*11078|Test.*15200'`, `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestPolicyZoneRejection'`. Full `pkg/config` and `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suites should be run by the reviewer.

## Risk
Fail-closed only. Strict commit now rejects with the correct reason configs that previously committed silently (hierarchical fused) or with a misleading zone error; tolerant load still boots them with a warning but poisons the rule instead of publishing an unscoped permit. No wire, Rust, or wildcard-semantics change.

## PR #15755 — config: validate and merge generate route prefixes (#15658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15658-campaign`

Closes #15658

## Why
`routing-options generate route` carried an untyped destination and no same-prefix merge. `generate route 999.999.0.0/99 discard` committed clean; FRR silently omitted the blackhole (`validFRRRoutePrefix`) while the userspace snapshot passed the prefix to a helper that refuses the whole snapshot (`RouteDestinationUnparseable`) — FRR-vs-userspace split-brain. Duplicate same-prefix hierarchical blocks appended divergent `GenerateRoute` entries.

## What
- Schema: `generate route` identity arg typed with `keyValueType: ValueCIDR` + `keyValidator: ValidateRouteDestination` (reuses the #2448 static-route grammar; the per-instance routing-options node shares the same `generate` pointer, so instances are gated too).
- Compiler strict gates (`compiler_validate_strict_generate_route.go`, wired beside the static-route mask gate): invalid prefixes and helper-refused padded masks (`/008`, `/0032`, incl. folded aliases) rejected at strict compile for global + per-instance routes; tolerant load/peer-sync warns per offender and preserves the route (`lenientGenerateRoutePrefix`) so a published bad prefix still fails the helper snapshot closed.
- Merge: `compileRoutingOptions` folds every `generate` container and merges same-masked-prefix definitions deterministically (`mergeGenerateRoute`: first spelling wins, discard latches, first non-empty policy wins); `canonicalizeGenerateRoutesAcrossScopes` folds across routing-options roots and writes helper-supported padded masks canonically (`/08` → `/8`, #12507 doctrine). Folded spellings retained on compiler-only `GenerateRoute.prefixAliases` for diagnostics. One route per prefix reaches both consumers — FRR renders one `ip route <p> blackhole`, userspace installs one Discard snapshot.
- Two pre-existing `GenerateRoute` struct comparisons moved to `reflect.DeepEqual` (required by the new unexported slice field).

## Validation
- RED: with `keyValidator` stripped, compile-time merge reverted to append, and canonicalise removed — `SchemaValidate accepted generate prefix "999.999.0.0/99"` (×5 malformed prefixes) and `hierarchical same-prefix routes = 2, want 1 merged`.
- GREEN: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestGenerateRoute.*15658|TestGenerateRoutes|TestGenerateRoutePackedRun8939|TestGenerateRoutePolicy|TestGenerateRouteWithoutDiscard|TestUnnamedRoutingContainersMergeAt12120Sites|TestRoutingInstanceRoutingOptions|TestSchema2448|TestStaticNextHop' ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/frr/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` — all pass; `go vet` clean on the same packages. Details in `docs/log/15658.md`.

## Risk
Strict commits now reject previously-accepted malformed generate prefixes (intended acceptance criterion); tolerant paths keep persisted configs booting with warnings. Valid generate routes render identically in FRR and userspace.

## PR #15801 — config: compile functional-zone management into the management zone (#15668) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

The closed-world `security zones` schema modelled only `security-zone` and `compileZones` read only `security-zone` children, so Junos's `functional-zone management` stanza was rejected at strict commit (`unknown keyword "functional-zone"`) and silently dropped on tolerant load / HA sync (no zone, no warning). ## PR #15803 — api: validate full TLS chain and recover failed HTTPS legs (#15667) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15667-campaign`

Why:
The management TLS preflight parsed and validity-checked only cert.Certificate[0], so an expired or invalid intermediate in Certificate[1:] was served until the Go handshake failed, a CA or non-ServerAuth leaf was accepted, custom certificates got no SAN diagnostic, and tlsDesired latched true on an initial load failure so refresh never recreated the failed HTTPS listener. This is a preflight/diagnostics/recovery defect; Go TLS still verified trust at handshake, so no crypto bypass is claimed.

What:
Parse every DER entry in managementTLSCertificateChain (rejecting a Leaf/Certificate[0] mismatch and unparseable intermediates), store the chain on the certificate state, and run managementTLSCertificatePreflightError at custom load, generated load, custom/generated refresh, handshake selection, and the durable-pair loader: every entry in its validity window (leaf wording unchanged), leaf not a CA, leaf EKU allows ServerAuth when present, intermediates are CAs allowed to sign, and every adjacent signature link verifies. Log SAN diagnostics on custom load/rotate and on the invalid-cert error path. Split tlsDesired into tlsDesiredConfigured (operator desire) and tlsDesired (armed only on successful install) and record httpsDesiredAddrs; the monitor retries on the configured desire and recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked binds/serves missing HTTPS legs from the validated state after a successful refresh (Start path; legacy Run unchanged). Tests in tls_certificate_15667_test.go and docs/log/15667.md.
NOT changed: warnStaleLoadedCert SAN diagnostics (still leaf-only, deliberately diagnostic-only) and handshake trust verification.

Validation:
go test ./pkg/api/ -run '15667' -count=1: pass (valid chain, expired/not-yet intermediate, CA leaf, client-auth leaf, non-CA intermediate, bad signature link, expired-intermediate load rejection, SAN log, monitor recovery with a real handshake). Reverting the state preflight calls to leaf-only validity makes TestCustomChainRejectedAtLoad15667 fail (chain installs an HTTPS server). Targeted TLS/cert/reconcile suites pass.
Full go test ./pkg/api/ -count=1: fails only in TestEmitDropClassCounters_4768 (prometheus NewConstMetric panic), reproduced identically on a clean base worktree at d316277cb4 — base-attributed, unrelated to this change.

Risk:
A previously served chain whose intermediate is expired, non-CA, or mis-signed is now refused at load/refresh (fail-closed, the intended behaviour); operators must renew the full chain file. Self-signed single-leaf generated certs are unaffected (verified by the existing generated-cert suites). Recovery only creates legs on the Start lifecycle; the legacy Run/serveBound path still relies on the daemon ReconcileHTTPS retry.

Closes #15667

## PR #15817 — config: diff matched nodes in scoped compare (#15758) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15758-campaign`

## Summary

Scoped `show <path> | compare` (`FormatCompareAtPath`, #15272) silently returned `[no changes]` for leaf statements, container `Inactive` toggles, and empty containers, and flattened bare-keyword multi-match containers.

**Mechanism:** `FormatCompareAtPath` navigated both trees to the path and compared only the matched nodes' *children* (non-leaves only). A leaf match was skipped outright, a container's own `Inactive` flag was discarded with the node, an empty container produced an empty child list identical to a missing path, and bare-keyword multi-matches were flattened into one shared child list where duplicate `KeyPath`s could pair across siblings.

**Fix:** use `navigatePathWidth` on both sides — the contract `FormatPathSet` / `FormatPathJSON` already use — and diff the matched node slice `oldMatches` vs `newMatches` with `diffNodes` at the parent prefix `path[:len(path)-width]`, using the true consumed width so an ancestor value repeating the terminal node's keys cannot over-strip the prefix (#5717). All downstream surfaces (redacted twin, configstore `ShowCompare*AtPath`, local/gRPC/remote CLI) inherit the fix unchanged since they already route through `FormatCompareAtPath`.

## Validation

- **RED pre-fix:** `TestFormatCompareAtPathLeafAndContainerInactive` failed with `expected leaf compare at [system host-name] to show new-fw diff, got ""`; `TestFormatCompareAtPathEmptyContainerAndMultiMatch15758` failed with `expected empty-container add at [protocols ospf area] to render + area 0.0.0.0, got ""`.
- **GREEN post-fix:** both regression tests pass (leaf value change, container `Inactive` toggle, empty-container add/delete, bare-keyword multi-match value change with the unchanged sibling not rendered as changed; identical-tree / absent-path / child-edit controls).
- Neighboring suites pass: `TestFormatCompare*` (#15168), `TestCompare*15169`, `TestInactive_*`, configstore `TestShowCompare*` / `TestShowCompareAtPath15272` / redacted compare tests. `gofmt` clean. The full `pkg/config`+`pkg/configstore` run exceeded the 600s lane shell timeout before reporting; targeted suites were run individually.

## Risk

Scoped compares to a container path now render the matched node itself under its parent `[edit]` header (matching global compare and Junos) instead of only its children under `[edit <path>]`; unchanged subtrees, absent paths, and the global compare are byte-identical to before.

Closes #15758

Why:
Multi-member expanded community lists (#15008) rendered one pattern

regcomp(REG_EXTENDED) (POSIX ERE), which rejects lookaheads with
CMD_WARNING_CONFIG_FAILED, aborting the whole frr-reload whenever a
definition had >=2 members and a regex member.

communityExpandedConjunctionPatterns replaces the lookahead pattern
with the permutation disjunction: one expanded permit entry per
ordering of the distinct member factors joined with .*, so the
entry set matches exactly routes satisfying every member. Literal

render is unchanged. The factorial entry count is bounded at 4
members (24 entries) via expandedCommunityConjunctionRenderable,
wired into renderCommunityListDefinitions,
communityListMissingAtRender, communityDeleteTarget, and
communityListCollision; past the bound the definition renders
nothing and referencing terms fail closed (#10822). All-literal
standard lists are untouched. pkg/frr/README.md and
docs/log/15779.md record the new contract.

New TestExpandedCommunityConjunctionPOSIX15779 plus the rewritten
TestMultiMemberCommunityIsConjunctive15008 compile every rendered
pattern with regexp.CompilePOSIX and evaluate conjunctive match
semantics (both present matches; either alone, neither, and
65000:100 inside 65000:1000 do not). RED on origin/master
f7c921ce29: the lookahead pattern fails CompilePOSIX and the
past-bound definition renders. Post-fix the targeted tests and
TestGeneratePolicyOptionsCommunity* pass; full pkg/frr shows only
the 4 failures also present on unmodified f7c921ce29
(TestBGPNoExportNeighborGetsDefaultExport15157,

loading. Regex members that reuse one community token to satisfy

stricter than the (unloadable) lookahead form. No lab frr-reload
verification; POSIX validity is pinned via Go's CompilePOSIX

Branch: `fix/15783-campaign`

## Summary
`staticHopActive` (#15734) reused the protocol-oriented `inactiveInterface`, whose unmatched fallthrough follows instance groups then RG0 — dropping non-RETH interface-qualified and IPv6 statics when RG0 (or the VRF's RETH RG) is secondary. ## PR #15836 — userspace-dp: resume remainder policer at deferred routing term (#15792) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15792-campaign`

## PR #15839 — userspace-dp: resolve scoped-NAT session misses in the override table (#15768) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15768-campaign`

Closes #15768

## Why

The #15118 untranslated session-miss arm called `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` with no table argument, so PBR/native-VRF flows resolved in `inet.0`/`inet6.0` instead of their `route_table_override` (wrong-table egress / VRF leak or blackhole), the arm hard-coded `resolved_in_table=false` (clearing the installing-table stamp so every re-resolve ran in the default table), the registered-but-unclaimed NAT branch dropped the 5-tuple ECMP hash, and `lookup_forwarding_resolution_without_nat_local` deep-cloned the whole `ForwardingState`.

## What

- `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` (`forwarding/fib.rs`) takes `table: Option<&str>` + `icmp: Option<(u8,u8)>` and returns the full `ForwardingLookupResult`. Both arms resolve in the caller's table with `ecmp_hash_flow`; the claimed arm uses `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic_for_flow_in_table`; `selected_route` carries the resolving table's identity.
- The `ForwardingState` clone is gone: suppression is a `Some(dst)` marker threaded through `*_suppressing` inner variants into the per-table local-ownership predicates (configured-interface addresses stay local, exactly as the clone's guard did). Public wrappers pass `None` — all other callers (flowless, tunnel, WG, session re-resolve) are behaviour-identical.
- Poll caller passes `route_table_override.as_deref()` + `dnat_packet_icmp` and stamps `resolved_in_table=true` for the arm, matching the translated else-arm.
- Regression cells in `tests_nat_scope_15118.rs`; `docs/log/15768.md`, forwarding README, changelog.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` (f7c921ce): the new tests fail to compile against the pre-fix 6-arg helper — no table/ICMP/`selected_route` surface exists pre-fix.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp tests_nat_scope_15118` — **9 passed** (4 new #15768 cells: unclaimed-NAT-in-tenant-table + identity, non-NAT override flow, suppressed-branch ECMP spread over 64 tuples, claimed-control + stamp arithmetic; 5 pre-existing #15118 cells unchanged in assertion).
- Neighbours: `afxdp::forwarding::` 368 passed. `poll_descriptor` 437 passed / 6 failed and `session_glue` 356 passed / 2 failed — both failure sets verified byte-identical on pristine `origin/master` (pre-existing: #15189 policer, #6304 flow-cache, 4× prerouting-scope, #9412, contention).
- `cargo fmt --check` diffs in touched files are confined to pre-existing unformatted regions outside this change's hunks.

## Risk

Only untranslated session misses carrying a `route_table_override` change behaviour (resolve + stamp in that table, the #9752 semantics the translated arm already had). Default-table flows are identical except the unclaimed branch now also spreads by the flow hash (#2734). Claimed-NAT, flowless (`flowless_verdict.rs` `route_override` already threaded), and translated paths are untouched; no registration/proxy-ARP/ownership behaviour changes.
