The "pure guard" redesign and an `evaluate(candidate)` extraction are explicit non-goals — the guard functions are already pure/directly tested and `installSnapshot` owns the ack/epoch gates (#14395).

## What

- `parse.go` (new): `fetchResult`, `countingReader`, `parseFeed`, `isDefaultRoute9248`, `boundInvalidSample`, `canonicalize`, `coversWholeAddressSpace`, `prefixLastAddress`, `hashPrefixes`, plus `maxLineBytes`, `maxInvalidSample*`, `maxFeedPrefixes`.
- `fetch.go` (new): `fetchFeed`/`readFeed`, `maxFeedBodyBytes`, `httpClientTimeout`, `feedDialAttemptTimeout`, redirect policy (`maxFeedRedirects`, `sameOriginFeedURL`, `feedOriginPort`, `checkFeedRedirect`), SSRF destination validation (`blockedFeedDestinationPrefixes`, `feedDestinationAllowed/Blocked`, `resolveFeedIPs`, `resolveAndValidateFeedDestination`, `pinnedFeedClient`), feed-URL construction (`escapedPathJoin`, `joinFeedURL`, `resolveBaseURL`, `isPlaintextFeedURL`).
- `feeds.go`: retains `Manager`/`feedState`, shrink-guard epoch machinery, `installSnapshot`, publication/hold/failure handling, `SetPrivateFeedAllowlist`/`SetLabFeedTLSRoots`. Imports pruned per file.
- README entry points, `docs/log/16182.md`, `debian/changelog` updated.

**Regressions:** none intended and none possible by construction — no statement changed. There is no new test because the issue's decisive acceptance check is the move-only diff plus the existing suite reaching the moved functions unmodified; a split-specific test would be test-only-green (it could only re-test unchanged code through the same package).

**Perf impact:** none. Source-file layout only; identical declaration set and generated code. No hot-path (dataplane) code touched.

## Validation

- Move-only proof: base `feeds.go` and the three resulting files were chunked into doc-comment+declaration units and compared as multisets — all 88 chunks byte-identical, none added/dropped/edited; only the two new `package`/import headers differ.
- `go test ./pkg/feeds/ -count=1` green, with **no test file modified** (moved functions reached exactly as before).
- `go vet ./pkg/feeds/` clean; `gofmt -l pkg/feeds/` clean.

## Risk

Behaviour delta: none (same package, same symbols). The recorded Codex dissent — a standalone file-motion diff costs blame history with no coupling/test-reachability benefit — is honoured as the implementation constraint: the diff is purely positional and no modularity benefit beyond review locality is claimed.

## PR #16259 — userspace-dp: genericise prefix set over address family (#16189) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16189-prefix-set-generic`

Refs #16189

## Why

`userspace-dp/src/prefix_set.rs` carried twin `merged_ranges_v4`/`merged_ranges_v6`, twin `PrefixSetV4`/`PrefixSetV6` impls, and twin fail-open `MatchAny` defaults (~190 duplicated lines in a 421-line file). Exact duplicates drift silently. The `(1 << (BITS - len)) - 1` host-mask computation is safe only behind the len==0 / len>=BITS guards.

## What

- One generic `PrefixSet<F: PrefixFamily>`; `PrefixSetV4 = PrefixSet<PrefixV4Family>`, `PrefixSetV6 = PrefixSet<PrefixV6Family>` (aliases — every `policy.rs` caller compiles unchanged).
- `host_mask` is a **required** `PrefixFamily` method with the length guards inside each impl (no default body); call sites cannot inline the shift.
- `merged_ranges`, both factories, `contains`, `is_match_*`, `prefix_count`, `heap_bytes` written once behind a small `PrefixKey` (u32/u128) bound.
- NOT changed: `prefix.rs` — family prefix types keep their surface (`PrefixV4::directed_broadcast` stays v4-only), per the narrowed issue scope.
- Fail-open `Default::MatchAny` semantics unchanged per family (#7745 comment preserved).

## Validation

- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml prefix_set`: corpus green (16 pre-existing cells incl. #15091 typed budget, 850k-range memory bound, at-budget control, covered/adjacent merge) + 4 new #16189 cells:
  - `host_mask_guards_boundaries_16189` — pins the required trait method's guarded values directly (len 0/1/24/31/32/33/255 and 0/1/64/127/128/129/255 + `BITS`).
  - `builder_ranges_at_boundary_lens_16189` — range-correctness only: exact retained ranges at len==BITS (/32, /128) and BITS-1 (/31, /127) for both families.
  - `merged_ranges_byte_identical_per_family_16189` — exact retained ranges + distinct counts per family over covered/adjacent/disjoint/len==BITS corpus.
  - `generic_set_boundary_membership_16189` — edge /32 + /128 membership and MatchAny defaults.
- On the guard's observability, stated plainly: `host_mask`'s guard is an **impl-level** contract. `merged_ranges` has **no observable bypass shape** — constructors funnel len==0 to MatchAny and prefix lens cannot exceed BITS, so the builder only ever sees len in 1..=BITS, where the raw `(1 << (BITS - len)) - 1` shifts by 0 at len==BITS (0..BITS-1 overall) and yields exactly the guarded mask. No test through the builder can distinguish `F::host_mask(..)` from an unguarded inline shift; the builder cell is kept as range-correctness only and claims nothing more.
- `cargo check` clean for `prefix_set.rs` (only pre-existing dead-code notes shared with master).

## Risk / perf

Pure genericisation, monomorphised per family — no allocation, wire, or hot-path shape change (same Linear scan + `partition_point` search; `contains` is `#[inline]` as before). Perf impact: none by construction. No production caller changes.

## PR #16260 — image: install UMEM hugepage reservation on every provisioning path (#16243) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

## Why

Plan measured `Hugepage-backed bindings: 0/30`, ~5 GiB of 4 KiB-page UMEM on a ring-entries 16384 rig. The bind code was already correct (`MAP_HUGETLB` first in `umem/mmap.rs`, per-binding `hugepage_backed` status, loud fallback, 80-pages/binding sizing pinned by `umem_sizing_contract_tests`). The defect is provisioning: `etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` existed in the repo but **no path installed it** — not `scripts/image/bake.py`, not `debian/rules`, not any deploy tool — and the architecture doc said so explicitly. The rig therefore booted with `HugePages_Total=0` and every UMEM fell back. (The loss cluster's 18/18-backed fw1 vs 6/18 fw0 fixtures show the same split: hand-provisioned vs not.)

## What

- `scripts/image/bake.py`: `hugepages_conf()` reads the repo conf verbatim (single source of truth; bake dies if the pool vanishes) and `virt_customize` writes it to `/etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` in the appliance image.
- `debian/rules`: installs the same file into the `.deb` for foreign-host/manual installs (dpkg conffile — operator resizes are prompted, never silently clobbered).
- `scripts/image/test_bake_hugepages_16243.py` (new): pins the verbatim bake install, the ≥80×18-page reference pool, and the fail-closed loader.
- Docs: `docs/deploy-quickstart.md` gains the knob/resize/verify procedure + a `0/N` troubleshooting row; the architecture doc's stale "image ships NO reservation" claim is corrected; the conf header names its installers; changelog entry.

## Validation

- Mutation: `vm.nr_hugepages 1440→600` reds the pool test (exactly the one-NIC shortfall that caused this issue).
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp umem_sizing_contract` — 4/4 pass (pre-existing pins the new bake test relies on).
- `debian/rules override_dh_auto_install` dry-run shows the conffile install line.

## Pending-main checks (cluster reserved by failover lane — no deploy done)

1. Deploy to a ring-entries 16384 rig; confirm `show dataplane status` reports `Hugepage-backed bindings: N/N` and `HugePages_Total ≥ 1440` in `/proc/meminfo`.
2. Throughput spot-check (expect ~22.1 vs 20.4 Gbps class per the documented measurement).

## Risk

Baked appliances now reserve 1440×2 MiB (2.8 GiB) at boot, withheld from ordinary allocation — the documented trade in the conf header; unused at default ring-entries 1024. Topologies above 18 bindings still need an operator resize of the one file.

## PR #16263 — userspace-dp: measure TX descriptors-per-commit and per-kick (#16242) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16242-batch-histogram`

Refs #16242

## What
Measurement ONLY for the batch-depth question — no batch-size or const-assert changes (`TX_BATCH_SIZE=64` / `RX_BATCH_SIZE=64` untouched).

Existing histogram infra (`tx_kick_latency_*` / `tx_submit_latency_*`) measures latency, not batch depth, so this wires new cheap counters into the same owner-profile + stats export path:

- **Per-commit**: `record_tx_commit` at all six TX-ring `writer.commit()` sites (4 CoS exact-direct in `cos/queue_service/service.rs`, `transmit_batch`, prepared `write.rs`), `inserted > 0` only (zero-insert is already `dbg_tx_ring_full`). One bucket `fetch_add` + two scalar `fetch_add`s, Relaxed, no allocation/clock.
- **Per-kick**: worker-local `tx_pending_kick_descriptors` accumulator drained in `maybe_wake_tx` at each actual `sendto` into `tx_kick_batch_hist`.
- Buckets (11): 1..=7 exact, [8,16), [16,32), [32,64), >=64. Scalars give mean batch = descriptors/commits and full-batch share = hist[10]/commits.
- Export: `BindingLiveSnapshot` -> `BindingStatus`/`BindingCountersSnapshot` (Rust protocol) + Go mirrors in `protocol_binding.go`, zeroed on unbound slots; additive wire keys with defaults both sides.

## How to read it (also in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/README.md`)
Under `-P32` load per queue: if mean batch ~= 64 and bucket 10 dominates, batches already fill and raising the cap is dead — close #16242. If mass sits in buckets 0-6, batches are partial and the lever is drain starvation, not the cap.

**Mouse-latency note**: the 64 cap is the #920 L1d/latency purchase, so any future raise must pair before/after histograms under the same `-P32` load with the mouse-latency matrix (`test-mouse-latency-matrix.sh`); the histogram alone cannot show the latency cost.

## Validation
- `cargo test -- tx_batch tx_kick submit_local`: 19 passed — bucket-layout pin, snapshot propagation, Rust wire round-trip + pre-#16242 back-compat, and `submit_local_records_tx_batch_histogram` (end-to-end through a real submit; goes RED if `record_tx_commit` is removed).
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TxKick|TxBatch`: ok.
- Layout pins updated for the +192B owner profile (2688->2880, offsets +192).

## Pending-main checks (cluster reserved by failover lane — no cluster mutation)
1. Deploy on the tcp cluster, drive `iperf3 -P32` per queue, read `tx_batch_hist`/`tx_kick_batch_hist` from binding status; report mean batch + full-batch share.
2. Mouse-latency matrix run as the latency baseline for any follow-up cap proposal.

## PR #16264 — userspace-xdp: add per-arm branch hit counters (#16241) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16241-xdp-branch-counters`

userspace-xdp: add per-arm branch hit counters (#16241)

Refs #16241

## Why

The narrowed #16241 acceptance requires, in order: (1) fallback-reason/branch hit counts for plain TCP hit-forwards, (2) a per-arm fail-closed analysis, and only then (3) removal of arms proven disposition-identical. The recoverable share of the measured 8.6% BPF self time is unproven without per-arm attribution, and the three-way validation found the original RSS-only slimming UNSOUND (most branches are fail-closed dispositions preventing the #304 kernel-forward-with-no-policy bypass).

## What

Instrumentation + analysis only. **No arm is removed**, because the analysis proves none is disposition-identical to another today. The perf claim is therefore structural and negative: zero branches removed.

- **New per-CPU map `userspace_branch_stats`** (27 slots, index order = dispatch order in `try_xdp_userspace`). A separate map, not new indices in `userspace_fallback_stats`: the degraded indices are a pinned operator ABI (Go `degradedPathReasonNames`, the Rust debug reader, the #8258 index-agreement test), and a hit-forward is not a degraded disposition.
- **Counting is TRACE-gated** inside the single outlined `incr_branch_stat` callee (the `record_trace_packed` #4113-F7 precedent): with tracing off, the hot path pays one flag test in one subprogram, not a map touch per arm. A TRACE-off control test proves dispositions are unchanged while zero branch arms count (and degraded counters still fire).
- **Redirect partitioning**: `session_hit_redirect` / `session_miss_redirect` / `session_miss_ifnat_redirect` count at their classifying arms; `redirect` counts only successes no earlier arm claimed. The four slots partition every successful XSK redirect, so the plain-TCP hit-forward rate reads directly off `session_hit_redirect`.
- **Surfaces**: Go `xdpBranchArmNames` + `readXDPBranchStatsLocked` → `ProcessStatus.XDPBranchCounters` (`xdp_branch_counters`); loader pinning + disposable-pin reconcile + ABI-check exclusion for the new map; Rust `XDP_BRANCH_ARM_NAMES` + `read_xdp_branch_stats` → `XDP_BRANCH:` debug dump.
- **Per-arm fail-closed analysis**: `docs/log/16241.md` — all 27 arms with disposition, fail-closed role, and why no two collapse. Packet classes named by the issue (local / WG / GRE / NAT-miss / early-filter) each have a row and a test cell.
- **Tests proving identical disposition per packet class**: `TestXDPBranchDispositionMatrix16241` runs the retained program via `BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN` for plain-TCP hit (REDIRECT and PASS_TO_KERNEL sessions), plain-TCP miss, local miss, NAT-miss, early-filter multicast, GRE inner-PASS, ARP, and L2 parse-fail — asserting action AND arm counter AND absent arms. Plus the WG steer pair (with/without WG_RX) and index-agreement tests on both sides (`TestXDPBranchArmNamesAgreeWithTheShim16241`, `TestXDPBranchArmsAreAllCounted16241`, Rust `xdp_branch_arm_names_agree_with_the_shim_16241`), all self-enrolling when an arm is added in the shim.

## Verifier cost (measured, structural — not a throughput claim)

Pinned build (nightly-2026-05-23, bpf-linker 0.10.2, `MAX_INTERFACES=65536`) via `cmd/shimverify` on this host (kernel 7.2.8): master object 815623 processed insns (18.44% headroom, PASS) → **862896 (13.71%)**, below the 15% #4555 floor. The object LOADS (not a kernel reject); the +47k is the verifier re-walking the one outlined counter callee under the dispatch's calling states. Because the floor is not met, the tracked object is installed with `XPF_SHIM_ALLOW_LOW_HEADROOM=1`; the gate verdict records `verdict: OVERRIDDEN, override_consumed: true`, and `TestShimGateVerdictIsMeasuredPass14851`'s exception pin is updated to exactly 862896 with a #16241 note (that test's comment had gone stale: #15854 had already retired the exception at 815623 PASS). Retiring the override needs the entry-path restructure deferred since #14954, deliberately not bundled into an instrumentation-only change.

## Validation

Local (this host):

- cargo/bpf pinned build green; shimverify LOADS at 862896 (override disclosed above).
- Privileged BPF cells (root): disposition matrix, WG steer pair, TRACE-gate control — PASS.
- Go: `TestXDPBranchArmNamesAgreeWithTheShim16241`, `TestXDPBranchArmsAreAllCounted16241`, `TestValidateUserspaceShimSpecSkipsDisposableBranchStatsPin16241`, `TestShimGateVerdictIsMeasuredPass14851`, `TestShimHeadroomOutlinesStayOutlined14851` (extended with `incr_branch_stat`), `TestUserspaceXDPShimObjectMatchesSourceManifest`, stack-margin — PASS.

## Pending-main checks (cluster RESERVED by the failover lane — not run here)

- Branch attribution under plain-TCP load: expect `session_hit_redirect` ≈ hit rate, `redirect`=0 for that class, `early_filter`/`wg_steer`/`gre_*`=0 without those features configured.

## PR #16265 — config: refuse jumbo MTU on userspace-bound interfaces at commit (#16244) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16244-mtu-propagation`

## Summary

Traced config mtu -> netdev propagation for XDP-attached interfaces (#16244):

- **Config**: `interfaces <if> mtu` / unit family mtu compile to `InterfaceConfig.MTU` / `InterfaceUnit.MTU`.
- **Netdev**: `planPhysDesired` (pkg/dataplane) merges zoned refs into one MTU per netdev; `mapZoneInterface` writes it via `LinkSetMTU` **before** `LinkSetUp` and before the deferred XDP attach (attach ifindexes are only queued in the same call). networkd also renders `MTUBytes`. So the MTU write already survives XDP attach in-order — propagation to the netdev was never the broken half.
- **AF_XDP**: the Rust helper binds without multi-buffer (`XDP_USE_SG`) support into fixed 4096-byte UMEM frames (`UMEM_FRAME_SIZE`, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs`). Frames above the 3566-byte budget (4096 − 512 headroom − Ethernet/VLAN) cannot reach a worker: copy mode drops them (`kernel_rx_dropped`), zero-copy may refuse the bind. The issue and the Wonder pass are explicit that jumbo-as-workaround is UNSOUND without the UMEM frame-size redesign.

This PR takes the acceptance's second arm — **named refusal at commit** — until that redesign lands:

- `validateUserspaceRxMTUStrict` hard-rejects on strict commit/commit-check any AF_XDP bind parent whose effective MTU exceeds 3566, naming the authored interface, resolved bind netdev when different, effective MTU, budget arithmetic, and remedy (lower to ≤3566 or unzone). The Opus fold replaces the initial per-reference predicate with `userspaceRxMTUBoundParents`: surviving zone membership comes from `InterfaceZoneMap`, rows resolve through `ResolveKernelIfName`, tagged rows redirect to the physical parent, and the lowest referenced untagged unit overrides the interface MTU. #9727 consumes the same effective-parent projection.
- Tolerant load/peer-sync paths downgrade to a warning (`lenientUserspaceRxMTU16244`, #1960 no-brick); the #9727 advisory is suppressed there, so the downgrade is that path's MTU signal.
- Unzoned, tunnel, and lifeline (fxp/em/fab/lo0) MTUs are untouched — jumbo stays legal for kernel-forwarded traffic.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestUserspaceMTU|TestJumboMTU|TestRxMTU|TestVlanUnitMTU|TestCompileTree|TestLenientCompileOpts'` — boundary 3566 accept / 3567 refuse, untagged override both directions, tagged-parent refusal, untagged-sibling acceptance, tagged RETH refusal on resolved member, unzoned+fxp0 accept, lenient and node-lenient warnings
- [x] `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run TestCheckText.*16244` — day-0/commit-check gate refuses; at-budget and unzoned pass
- [x] `go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -run TestPlanPhysDesired.*16244` — plan carries 9000 to ordinary and tagged parents, 1500 when a referenced untagged sibling lowers the shared parent, and 9000 on the local member for a tagged RETH
- [ ] Full `pkg/config` / `pkg/dataplane` suites exceed the 300s job cap in the authoring environment; sampled broad subsets show only failures reproduced identically on clean `origin/master` (pre-existing #14139/#15034 drift, unrelated) — **pending main-agent full-suite run**
- [ ] Cluster is RESERVED by the failover lane — **no cluster deploy**; iperf at 9000-byte vs 1500-byte frames on the loss cluster is a **pending-main check** (acceptance's measurement arm; expected: 9000 now refuses at commit until the UMEM redesign, 1500 unchanged)

Refs #16244

## PR #16273 — api: share peer-proxy reconciliation table only (#16154) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16154-peerclient-reconcile`

## Summary
Refs #16154 — share **only** the transport-neutral peer-proxy reconciliation/timeout table in new `pkg/peerclient` (`TimeoutFor`/`IsDeadline`/`Reconcile`). Dialers stay per-surface: no unified Dialer, no unified forwarder, fabric-auth credential/token construction untouched.

## Why
CLI (`pkg/cli/peer.go:failoverProxyTimeoutMessage`) and gRPC (`pkg/grpcapi:failoverProxyTimeoutOutcome`) maintained verbatim copies of the #15081 proxy timeout sizing + post-deadline RG-ownership reconciliation, so wording/RG-completeness could drift. The narrowed survivor form (per issue validation) shares only the pure table, because the CLI's background TCP probe + nil-on-fail vs the gRPC ctx-bound GetStatus probe (#8597 `ResourceExhausted` = liveness) differ in wedged-server reachability, and a single Dialer/forwarder could change signed-request metadata.

## What

## PR #16274 — userspace-dp: extract partial-publisher pipeline and stamp dedup (#16153) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16153-partial-publisher`

## Why

W2.4 narrowed survivor (validated-by:research, Codex C binding on P8):

- **P4:** `stampCaptureAuthorityWithRoutesMode` (builder.go) and `refreshCaptureAuthorityLocked` assigned the same four capture fields field-by-field and could drift.
- **P2-narrowed:** `PolicyRuleSnapshot.Action` / `DefaultPolicy` were stringly typed; the send gate checked counts only, so an empty/malformed/future action token shipped to the helper relying solely on the Rust reader.
- **P8-narrowed (canary-aware):** no standalone `binding_plan.go` move — `snapshotBindingPlanKey` et al. stay in `maps_sync.go` where `binding_plan_key_crossplane_8901_test.go`'s source-text canaries read them.

## What

- New `manager_partial_publish.go`: `cloneRetainedSnapshotLocked` (single-use strip under the pending-full latch), `bumpRetainedGenerationLocked`, `preparePrehashedPublish` (single #15955 hash), `dedupHit` (hash match + #9520/#9684 unknown-outcome stand-downs), `adoptPublishedSnapshotLocked`, and `copyPreparedSectionsBack`/`adoptPreparedPublishLocked` (#15043) for the non-prehashed scheduler/worker-arm senders. Publishers keep their prep, protocol/disarm gates, error wrapping, and their own dedup predicate: capture ANDs `publishedSnapshot != 0`, link-refresh ANDs `resampled == 0` — characterized, not unified. `syncSnapshotLocked` deliberately not extracted (distinct retained-publish shape, no clone twin).
- P4: both capture stamps go through `captureAuthorityFields.applyTo` — the single detached writer of the four fields. Per-publisher detach only; no blanket deep clone.
- P2: typed `policyAction` vocabulary (`permit`/`deny`/`reject`, deliberately not unified with the filter `accept`/`discard` set) + `typedPolicyAction`; `validateSnapshotForSend` refuses unknown/empty rule actions and non-empty garbage defaults as known-unsent (`errSnapshotPolicyAction`, matched by `isKnownUnsentFailure` — no retry debt). `policyActionString` lowers through the typed tokens, deny fail-closed default. Rust enum remains the enforcement backstop, does not gate.
- #15955 hash leg reused, not re-fixed (coordination note in the issue).

## Validation

- New `partial_publish_16153_test.go`: capture dedup characterization (**RED** when the `publishedSnapshot` arm is dropped: unpublished capture republish returns `(false, nil)`), capture stamp detach+parity, send-gate differential table (known tokens + empty default admitted; empty/future/malformed/filter-vocab refused known-unsent), typed vocabulary + lowerer defaults, binding-plan helper reachability (P8 non-vacuity).
- Existing pins intact: `TestPublishHashDedup*15955` (overlay exactly-1-hash), route-overlay/capture/link-refresh/scheduler/worker-arm republish suites.
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` run: only pre-existing failures, base-attributed on `974028945c` (lab socket-path length, WG degenerate-key and unit/vlan config gates, owner-key parity) — identical on clean `origin/master`.

Behavior preserved by construction (same dedup predicates, one hash per publish, ACK-then-retained-cache). The only new refusal is fail-closed at the Go send gate for hand-built/corrupt snapshots with invalid action tokens, matching the Rust #3365 refusal; no wire change. Perf: extraction removes duplicate hash/copy work, adds no marshal or lock hold (all helpers run under the existing `m.mu`).



## Fold (review F1, head 6c42ddce3e)

Rebased onto master 9d098201cb. Link-refresh saved pub.snap before the send, so a #9520 content-conflict retry that republished at generation 9 was adopted as stale 8 (helper held 9; manager/retained/published/applied stayed 8). Fix: pub.snap = publishSnap after successful send in RefreshInterfaceRowsForLink, matching route-overlay/capture callers, so adoptPublishedSnapshotLocked commits the generation actually carried (also repairs postPublishHash preSendClear snapshot and binding-plan key inputs). Rebased onto master 26003e3408. TestScheduledSnapshotSeedsBestEffortHeartbeat11285 and TestScheduledReintroductionSendsHeartbeatBeforeApply15093 built PolicyRuleSnapshot with empty Action, so the new send gate refused before any heartbeat was reached; fixtures now carry Action "permit" plus Summary.PolicyCount=1 (the #15742 count arm — both tests also fail on clean current master for the count reason alone). ## PR #16276 — config: add in-package per-channel test kit (#16139) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

## Why
`pkg/config` had ~36 `must*` helpers; a scripted census (origin/master `9d098201cb`) found **73 pure hierarchical-parse clones** — single string arg, `*ConfigTree` return, only `NewParser(param).Parse()` + `len(errs)` guard + return — diverging in guard/message wording, plus per-file re-implementations of each compile channel. ## What
- New `pkg/config/helpers_test.go`: **one helper per compile channel, no bool lenient flag, no combined `MustCompile(opts...)`** (a lenient flag would let a test silently exercise the tolerant channel while claiming the strict one — `docs/engineering-style.md:50`):

  - `compileHierStrict` / `compileHierLenient`, `compileSetStrict` / `compileSetLenient`, `compileTreeStrictKit` / `compileTreeLenientKit`, `compileTreeForNodeKit`
  - `configstore.CheckText` deliberately **not** wrapped (import cycle; tests needing the operator commit gate belong in `pkg/configstore` or `package config_test`) — naming a `CompileConfig` helper "check" would flatten that distinction.
- **Decl census / one clone family:** migrate all 73 pure clones — 554 in-file + 670 cross-file call sites (1224 total) — onto `parseHierText` and delete every clone. Helpers that wrap text, inject fixtures (e.g. `parseHier6454`), expand groups, panic instead of `Fatal`, or assert extra premises are **not** clones and stay untouched.
- Fix stale doc comments that named deleted helpers.
- New `pkg/config/helpers_equivalence_test.go`: permanent clone-equivalence pinned against **independent expected fixtures** (leaf key paths, Format round-trip, set-vs-hier Format equality, channels agree on a valid fixture) — a comparison against the deleted functions cannot compile, so none is attempted. `TestKitChannelsNotFlattened16139` pins a strict-vs-lenient divergence fixture (keyless cluster, #6611: strict rejects, lenient warns) proving **no channel flattening**.

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; `gofmt` clean on all changed files.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestKit` — all 5 equivalence tests pass.
- Spot-check `TestInactive_`/`TestDuplicatePolicyName`/`TestApplyGroupsExcept` passes.
- Full `pkg/config` suite exceeded the 300s local tool timeout without completing; **CI must confirm the full suite green** (acceptance check).

## Risk
Test-only change; no production code. Residual risk is a misclassified clone changing a test's parse channel — mitigated by the scripted purity census and the permanent independent-fixture equivalence tests.

Stringly schema resolution let a typo'd or renamed path return nil and silently disable packed-body expansion, so a packed body was dropped with no signal (#16147).

- Static refs only: no-arg resolvers (`bgpLeafSchema8939`, `ospfSchema9408`, `filterThenSchema8971`, the #9235/#9792 families) and literal `schemaForPath(...)` sites now resolve through `refXxx.resolve()` (131 registered handles); chained refs model mid-path wildcard hops. - Init-panic LAST: `validateSchemaRefs()` runs as the last statement of `schema.go`'s `init()`, after the groups-wildcard wiring; no ref addresses a groups subtree and refs resolve lazily post-init, so the panic names every dead ref at once and fires only on a code-introduced bad ref — never on operator config. `#1960` no-brick is unchanged: config-driven resolution keeps its nil return.

## Summary

Refs #15952 (Refs-only; issue stays open for the drive-to-zero campaign to close).

`resolveNeighborsInner` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_neighbor.go`) re-issued `netlink.LinkByIndex` and a full `netlink.NeighList` dump **for every target**: `T` targets sharing one `(linkIndex, family)` — the normal case (many static-route next-hops / NAT addresses / `/32` address-book hosts behind one gateway) — re-dumped the identical neighbor table `T` times on every 15s pass, config apply, and HA takeover (issue H44-03, triple-validated, Low).

## What

- Extract `resolveNeighborTargets(targets, neighborResolveOps)` behind an injected netlink seam (`linkByIndex` / `listNeigh` / `probe`), mirroring the existing `failedNeighborCleanupOps` pattern in the same file.
- Interface names cached once per link per pass (failures cached too: `LinkByIndex` failure still skips exactly that link's targets, attempted once).
- Usable-neighbor sets (`REACHABLE|STALE|PERMANENT`) snapshotted once per `(linkIndex, family)` per pass, keyed by a struct key (not arithmetic encoding). `NeighList` errors still yield an empty snapshot → all targets probed, as before.

- Counted regression test `pkg/daemon/daemon_neighbor_resolve_15952_test.go` + changelog entry.

Snapshot semantics are the safe direction validated in the issue: an entry becoming usable mid-pass may draw one harmless extra probe; an entry usable when its `(link,family)` table was snapshotted is never probed. No goroutine/semaphore/capacity change (that arm was explicitly contested, not validated, and is out of scope).

## Validation

  - distinct links/families dumped separately; failed link attempted once, its targets skipped;
  - pass-authoritative snapshot (fake table gains a usable entry on a hypothetical second dump → dump count stays 1, target still probed once — the harmless-extra-probe case).
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon` clean; neighboring `TestCleanFailedNeighborsOnIfindexes11883` / `TestMonitoredNeighborIfindexesIncludesLoopbackAndSnapshot11883` pass; `gofmt` + `git diff --check` clean. Private `GOCACHE` under the worktree; no cluster used.

## PR #16293 — userspace-dp: fail closed on host-bound install failure and credit junos-host denies (#15951) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `impl-15951`

## Why

Refs #15951 (H41-01, H41-02).

- **H41-01**: a cacheable LocalDelivery session-miss whose local session could not be installed (capacity refused, or `install_helper_local_session_on_miss` returned false) fell through with `host_inbound_gate_proof` set, so the slow-path tail selected `SlowPathOutlet::Trusted` and reinjected the packet to the kernel with no installed session, no conntrack publication, and no revalidation anchor. `local_metadata` also hardcoded `fabric_ingress: false` + the raw ingress ifindex.
- **H41-02**: no `junos-host` deny path credited the global `policy_denied_packets` counter (`xpf_policy_denies_total` stayed 0 for every `to-zone junos-host` deny), and the deny RT_FLOW passed a default `NatDecision`, zeroing `nat_dst_ip`/`nat_dst_port` despite post-translation judging (#9529).

## What

- `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`: capture the LocalMiss install result; on refusal count `note_admission_refused()`, recycle, `continue` (never Trusted). Sessionless-by-design LocalDelivery (non-SYN TCP, WG listener tuples) untouched. Stamp `fabric_ingress: packet_fabric_ingress` + #7096 `stamped_ingress_identity` on `local_metadata`.
- `host_inbound_policy.rs`: credit `counters.policy_denied_packets` once per deny/reject inside `junos_host_local_policy` (covers Stage-11, session-hit, session-miss; per-rule counter already credited by evaluation, not double-counted). `emit_junos_host_deny` takes the packet `NatDecision`.
- `flowless_verdict.rs`: flowless `junos-host` deny credits once; lo0 `Filtered` does not.
- Callers pass `decision.nat` (miss/hit), default for Stage-11/flowless (no translation).
- Tests: new `tests_host_inbound_15951.rs` (6 cells), flowless counter assertion, updated #10981 `nat_dst_*` assertion. `docs/log/15951.md`.

Scope notes: the enrichment's `nat_scope_ifindex`/`StaleDestinationNat` arm does not exist at this head (no such `SessionMetadata` field; #9563 declines LocalDelivery revalidation) — documented in `docs/log/15951.md`. H41-02 arm 3 (fabric ifindex in events) was NEEDS_VALIDATION and is unchanged. No `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` conflicts taken against open PRs beyond the confined call-site edits above.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 15951` — 6 passed (capacity-0 DNAT-to-local drop + `admission_refused == 1`, capacity control delivers+installs, miss/hit/reject `policy_denied_packets == 1`, DNAT deny event carries `nat_dst 10.0.61.1:8080` with wire tuple retained)
- `10981` — 3 passed; `9529` — 12 passed; `flowless` — 132 passed
- Full `--bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite: **7881 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored**
- New cells assert only on counters/fields existing at base (`local`, `session_create`, `admission_refused()`, `batch.policy_denied_packets`, event `nat_dst_*`).

## Risk

Cacheable host-bound SYNs under session-table pressure are now dropped instead of delivered sessionless (intended fail-closed; `session_install_admission_refused` makes it observable). `xpf_policy_denies_total` now includes `junos-host` denies.

## Summary

- **H22-01 (High):** during the 30s cooldown, `evaluateEventMode` computed `withinMatches`, discarded it (`_ = matched`), and parked every event with `ThenCommands`; `drainDeferred` replayed it at cooldown expiry with no re-evaluation — so sub-threshold, over-ceiling, or already-latched events fired the remediation once without ever crossing.
- **H22-02 (Medium):** sd-syslog fallbacks emitted only two NILVALUE dashes (`RT_FLOW - - <body>`), placing the body in the RFC 5424 STRUCTURED-DATA slot where strict parsers misparse/drop it; `SCREEN_DROP`/`FILTER_LOG` had no structured handling.

## What

- `pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go`: `if !matched { continue }` before the defer branch — only a genuine crossing parks.
- `pkg/eventengine/engine.go`: `drainDeferred` re-evaluates `withinMatches` against the live policy/runtime, requires the parked semantic revision to still match, and only latches the authorizing generation. `staleReason` remains the commit-time backstop.
- `pkg/logging/format_rtflow.go`: third NILVALUE dash on both fallbacks (`RT_FLOW - - -`, `xpf - - -`); `FILTER_LOG` → `MSGID=FILTER_LOG` + NILVALUE SD + flat body as MSG (no Junos SD reference exists for filter logs — none invented); `SCREEN_DROP` → Junos screen SD arm cited from the Graylog Juniper SRX content pack (Junos OS 17.4+ sd-syslog: `RT_IDS - RT_SCREEN_TCP [junos@2636.1.1.1.2.40 attack-name=... ...]`), MSGID generalized to `RT_SCREEN_DROP` because Junos's per-category TCP/IP split cannot be derived from the wire record.
- Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` sd-syslog paragraph, `docs/log/15945.md`.

## Validation

- New `TestDeferred*15945` (fake-clock): latched sustained level and decayed parked edge park/replay nothing (`PendingDeferred=0`, exactly 1 commit); genuine crossing still replays; removed policy does not. RED pre-fix (`PendingDeferred=1, want 0`, verified by stash), GREEN post-fix incl. `-race`.
- New `TestSDSyslog*15945`: independent RFC 5424 field parser asserts STRUCTURED-DATA is `-` or `[...]` with the full body as MSG for SCREEN_DROP/FILTER_LOG/aggregate/generic/unknown records through both writers; session control byte-unchanged. RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix.
- `go test ./pkg/logging/ -count=1` fully passes. `pkg/eventengine` failure set identical to base `3bb1f7c4f6` (9 pre-existing #6673 multivalue failures, unrelated). `go vet`/`gofmt` clean. No cluster run (per assignment).

## Risk

- A parked edge whose window decayed during cooldown no longer replays — intended fail-closed direction.
- SIEMs keyed on the old two-dash fallback field positions will see corrected positions; that is the compliance fix.

Refs #15945

## PR #16298 — test: make session-sync idle baseline-relative (#16289) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16289-campaign`

Why: `ha_session_sync_idle_sample` required absolute `source sent == target received` for cumulative-since-daemon-start `Session create` counters. The daemons do not share a counter epoch (tcp-cluster evidence in #16289: sent=15, received=174, pending=0, static for the whole 30s window, later 74/233 — a constant offset of 159), so the pre-traffic session-sync precondition timed out forever on a fully caught-up pair, FAILed, and VOIDed every precondition-gated RG1 cell.

What:
- `test/incus/ha-assurance-lib.sh`: `ha_session_sync_idle_sample` now takes an explicit `(baseline_sent, baseline_received)` pair. Idle is `sent - baseline_sent == received - baseline_received` with `pending == 0`. The first sample of a wait only establishes the baseline (never idle by itself); a counter rewind since the baseline (daemon restart / epoch reset) is not idle and forces re-baselining instead of comparing across epochs; malformed or half-empty baselines are VOID (status 2). `drained` remains required/parseable, informational.
- `test/incus/test-failover.sh` (`ha_wait_for_session_sync_idle`) and `scripts/userspace-ha-failover-validation.sh` (`wait_for_session_sync_idle`): thread the baseline and re-baseline on every non-idle sample, so the existing 3-consecutive-idle rule proves "nothing sent since the baseline is unreceived" across consecutive samples.
- `test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh`: offset-baseline fixtures (below).
- NOT changed: parsers, the 3-consecutive/30s policy, pending/drained requirements. A genuinely stuck sync (sends arriving unreceived, or pending nonzero) still never goes idle.

Validation:
- `bash test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh` PASS, including new #16289 fixtures: static offset 15/174 pending=0 judged idle vs baseline; lockstep advance 74/233 idle; received stalled while sent grows not idle; pending=3 not idle; counter rewind not idle; malformed/half-empty baseline VOID; old 4-arg shape VOID.
- RED proof: reverting the helper to absolute equality fails the selftest on exactly the offset fixture (`expected 0, got 1 ... sent=15 ... received=174 ... pending=0`); restored and re-verified PASS.
- `bash -n` clean on all four scripts; shellcheck shows only pre-existing warnings.

Risk: live tcp-cluster `test-failover` precondition run not exercised in this lane (no destructive cluster); that remains the lab-verify item on #16289. Fail-closed intent preserved: unreceived sends or nonzero pending never reach idle.

Refs #16289

## PR #16301 — screen: drop non-multiple-8 non-last fragments at any offset (#16030) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16030-teardrop-offset0`

Refs #16030

Why: `check_teardrop` gated both IPv4 and IPv6 arms on `frag_offset>0`, so a non-last first fragment (offset 0, MF/M=1) with a payload that is not a multiple of 8 (e.g. 4 or 12 bytes) was never dropped. RFC 791/RFC 8200 require every non-last fragment payload to be a multiple of 8; the tunnel reassembly path already enforces this (`gre_reassembly: info.more && payload.len()%8`). Conformance/screen-completeness gap (Low, A1-C9 from #15985).

What:
- Remove the `offset>0` gate in `check_teardrop` (`userspace-dp/src/screen/stateless.rs`) for both families; replace `payload < 8` with MF-gated `payload % 8 != 0`, which subsumes `<8` and also catches 12/20-byte non-last fragments at any offset. Zero/under-length payload arm (#3027) likewise runs at offset 0.
- Legal short LAST fragments (MF/M=0, 1-7 bytes, #9426) remain admitted because `%8` stays MF-gated; multiple-of-8 first fragments pass.
- Re-anchor two stale controls that asserted the bug: `teardrop_first_fragment_passes` (v4, 4B first frag) and `teardrop_v6_first_fragment_passes` now assert `Drop("teardrop")` and are renamed `*_illegal_payload_drops_16030`.
- `icmpv6_fragment_drops` fixture gets a legal `frag_data` so teardrop does not mask its icmp-fragment claim (teardrop precedes icmp-fragment in `check_fragment_and_route`).
- #14325 wording test now asserts teardrop fires on the pre-fix reconstructed shape while ping-of-death still does not.
- New #16030 sweeps: first-fragment 4/12/20B drops (v4+v6), non-first 12/20B drops, legal 8/16/24B first-fragment passes, short-last passes, zero-payload first-fragment drop.

Validation:
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp teardrop` — 26 passed (incl. new 16030 cells; fail-on-revert by construction: restoring the offset gate or reverting to `<8` reds them).
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp screen::` — 362 passed.
- `afxdp::` suite: 41 failures, spot-checked identical on unmodified `origin/master` (pre-existing: `pkt_len_fixture_drift_6883`, `arp_two_vlans_same_ip`, `keyed_shards_disperse` etc.) — not introduced by this change.

Risk: Low. Only newly dropped packets are non-last fragments with non-multiple-of-8 or zero payload — illegal per RFC, not producible by a conforming sender. Legal fragmented traffic (all non-last fragments 8-byte multiples, any-size last fragment) is unchanged. A middlebox emitting illegal fragments will now drop as `teardrop` where previously forwarded — intended screen behaviour, gated on `profile.teardrop`.

## PR #16302 — config: compiler/show parity fixes - interfaces, screens, backup-router, cluster resolution (#15944) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `impl-15944`

Refs #15944

## Why

#15944 bundles seven validated compiler/show parity claims (H4-01, H4-04, H13-03, H21-01, H21-02, H21-03, H23-02). Every `61c7d45603` citation was re-verified at coding head `c364a824c9` (current origin/master) and each live defect was reproduced by probe before fixing. This PR drives six claims fully; H4-04's userspace-MTU on-wire arm is explicitly parked (below), per the triage note.

### What changed, per claim

- **H4-01** — `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`: inet owns only the legacy (IPv4) slots (first-wins), inet6 owns only the V6 slots and no longer mirrors into the legacy slots. `pkg/config/types_interfaces.go`: `Primary/PreferredAddressForFamily` family-check the legacy slot, so a v6 CIDR there never serves an IPv4 query. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go`: `planAddressReconcile` now also cycles a subnet's incumbent desired peer when the desired primary is not yet installed, so a fresh primary lands first instead of being appended as `IFA_F_SECONDARY`.
- **H4-04** — `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go`: logical-only RETH unit MTU precedence is unit MTU → interface MTU → parent kernel MTU (was parent-only). `buildBridgeDomainModels` carries the IRB unit's MTU/primary/preferred/DHCP/DAD-disable; `buildFabricBondModels` carries the units' minimum MTU and per-family primary/preferred.
- **H13-03** — `pkg/config/compiler_security_screen_family_9421.go`: unbracketed packed family tails expand with open levels so siblings stay siblings (`tcp syn-flood alarm-threshold 100 attack-threshold 500;` compiles both thresholds, strict + lenient); bracketed tails keep the original chain walk and still strict-reject as the flat path does. Valueless `limit-session` direction observed and pinned: stays 0 with no BadNumeric (no Junos limit-session default asserted — inventing one would silently arm a session cap the operator never chose).
- **H21-01** — `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: backup-router destinations accumulate across nodes (deduped, authored order; bare next-hop updates retain them; scalar stays in sync). `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_system.go`: renders every destination with a family-aware default (`::/0` for IPv6), matching the local CLI.
- **H21-02** — `cmd/cli/show_system.go`: remote license arm routes through the `license` ShowText RPC (shared `config.LicenseText`). Compiler arm probed at head (flat, packed-container, braced spellings) — already fixed, no compiler change, probe recorded in the commit.
- **H21-03** — `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: NETCONF reader iterates every `netconf` sibling (`FindChildren`); parsed-text fixtures confirm sibling containers survive to the compiler, and the typed-flag warning fires off the corrected flag.
- **H23-02** — `resolveClusterInterfaceAddr` takes `cfg` and resolves via `cfg.ResolveKernelIfName` (daemon call sites pass the active/epoch config); `transportVRFBinding` resolves through the active config; the duplicate-identity watcher translates authored refs to the kernel device before lookup (`pkg/cluster`'s only config symbol is `config.LinuxIfName`, as in sibling files).

### Non-overlap with #16296 (#15943, in flight)

No file in the #16296 diff is touched: it owns `pkg/config/{compiler_dispatch,schema_security,compiler_firewall,natpool,...}`, `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft*`. This PR touches different files in the same packages. H13-03 (screens) is in `compiler_security_screen_family_9421.go`, not `schema_security.go`. The one shared surface is `pkg/config/compiler_system.go` (not in #16296's list) and `pkg/config/types_system.go` is **not** touched here (the #15780 slice fields already exist).

### Deferred / parked

- **H4-04 userspace-MTU on-wire arm — NEEDS_VALIDATION, not claimed fixed.** Rust MTU precedence in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs` was not traced; the Go-side model/snapshot now carries the configured value, but no wire/oversized-forwarding consequence is asserted. Decisive follow-up: trace Rust snapshot-MTU precedence, then a probe asserting the effective MTU for a logical-only RETH unit.
- **H4-01 networkd-vs-live ordering** beyond the compile/plan cells: `generateNetwork` already orders per-family primaries/preferred (#15653) and now receives family-correct values; no separate change was needed beyond the compile fix. No live `perf`/wire measurement is claimed.

### Validation actually run (targeted, not full suites)

narrowed by the research: on the flow-cache hit path the deferring probe
charged the session and locally completed the handshake *before* the
cached output-filter/policer verdicts, so a packet then dropped had

merely withheld, never undone.

pre-probe `ProbeUndo` snapshots captured by `probe_hit_inner` for the
deferring arm, keyed by the producer's canonical stored key: accounting
target (including the reverse-only fallback), counters, observed
flags/ToS, both halves' handshake Booleans, and SYN-pressure index
membership; the withheld HA Update is discarded. Probe, emit and
rollback all resolve translated-alias packet identities to that
canonical key. A retransmitted completing ACK re-probes and, if
admitted, publishes exactly once.

restored — the probe's throttled keepalive refresh stands on a dropped
packet, preserving the documented pre-fusion keepalive-before-drop
behaviour. A dropped packet proves liveness; it must not charge,
complete, or publish.

## PR #16317 — cluster: bound DHCP lease-chunk totalLeases before allocation (#16036) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16036-dhcp-totalleases`

## Summary

Refs #16036. `decodeDHCPLeaseChunkHeader` bounded the chunk count `total` to `[1, 1<<20]` but checked the lease count `totalLeases` only for `!= 0`, and `dhcpChunkState.addChunk` executed `make([]SyncLease, 0, totalLeases)` at assembly completion **before** the `len(complete) != totalLeases` refusal. One chunk header with `total=1, totalLeases=0xFFFFFFFF` requested ~4.29e9-record capacity (~672 GiB (721 GB decimal) virtual) before any check refused the set, and the assembly survived disconnect.

## Fix (fail-closed, all three legs from the issue's acceptance)

- `decodeDHCPLeaseChunkHeader`: `totalLeases` bounded to `[1, 1<<20]`, exactly like `total`. Out-of-bound headers are refused as malformed (counted via `MalformedRecordsDropped`, prior held set retained).
- `addChunk`: refuse `received > totalLeases` as soon as the accumulated count crosses the announced total, before any completion work; the generation is dropped.
- `addChunk` completion: size the concatenation by `a.received` (leases the parts have already proven) instead of the announced `totalLeases`, so no wire-controlled value ever sizes an allocation.

Wire format unchanged. A conforming sender never announces >1<<20 leases (chunked sets are bounded by the 64 MiB Kea read / 16 MiB frames), so no legitimate set is affected.

## Validation

New cells in `pkg/cluster/dhcp_chunk_totalleases_16036_test.go`:

- `TestDHCPChunkTotalLeasesBound16036` — exact fixture `0xFFFFFFFF` plus `0` and `(1<<20)+1` refused; boundary values `1` and `1<<20` admitted (positive control).
- `TestDHCPChunkForgedTotalLeasesNeverCommits16036` — the one-chunk forged frame driven through `handleMessage`: held set undisturbed, no pending assembly, counted malformed.
- `TestDHCPChunkReceivedOverTotalRefused16036` — two chunks carrying 2 leases against `totalLeases=1` (each header in-bound, so only the early refusal stops it): never commits, assembly dropped.
- `TestDHCPChunkCompletionAllocationBounded16036` — `TotalAlloc` measurement in the #8792 idiom at the admitted boundary `totalLeases=1<<20`: mutation-verified — reverting the guard allocated **176,161,392 bytes** vs the 1 MiB budget; with the fix ~nothing.

Full `pkg/cluster` suite passes (144s); existing #15160 chunk cells unchanged-green. Docs: `pkg/cluster/README.md` chunked-set bullet documents the bound.

Note on severity: per the issue, NV-1 (fatal under shipped GOMEMLIMIT/overcommit) remains the unrun host check and is **not** asserted here — the cells assert the host-independent invariant (refused before allocation, nothing commits), so the Low grade stands regardless.

## Risk

Fail-closed only: over-bound or over-total generations drop with the prior set retained (the existing #7175 posture). No sender, format, or commit-semantics change for conforming peers.

## PR #16318 — ipsec: render ascii 0x PSKs quoted, not raw hex (#15991) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix-15991-ascii-psk`

## Why

An `ascii-text` PSK spelled `0x61626364` lost its ASCII provenance in the
`pkg/ipsec` gateway-group secret fold (#15991, IKE-DEEP-2; stale-audit
continuation at 5fc385cc98): members became bare strings (hex values prefixed
with `0x`), and the lone-value emission treated any `0x`-prefixed string as a
hex key — rendering `secret = 0x61626364` unquoted, so strongSwan hex-decoded
the credential instead of using the literal ASCII string the operator
authored. The fold also collapsed an ASCII `0x<digits>` and a hexadecimal
`<digits>` member on one gateway into a single raw-hex element.

## What

- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go`: carry `pskValue{value, hex}` provenance through the
  fold and dedupe (replacing the bare-string / `"0x"+d` encoding), and make
  emission decide solely on the flag:
  - lone hex → `secret = 0x<hex>` (#15027 unchanged)
  - lone ASCII → quoted, including `0x`/`0X` values (`secret = "0x61626364"`)
  - grouped → comma-join each element by its provenance inside the existing
    single quoted string (byte-identical prior render; an ASCII `0x…` and a
    hex member with the same digits now survive as two distinct elements)
- New `pkg/ipsec/policy_psk_ascii_hex_15991_test.go`: lone ascii-0x vs hex
  control, policy-fallback ascii-0x, grouped ascii-0x+hex distinctness,
  grouped dedupe + plain member, non-hex `0xzzzz` quoted, and an end-to-end
  `ascii-text 0x61626364` compile→render cell mirroring #15027's hex leg.
- README + changelog + `docs/log/15991.md` updated; compiler/schema/gates
  unchanged (`PSKHex` already carried provenance to the renderer).

## Validation

- Probe at base `30638bcad3` (temporary test, removed): `PSK="0x61626364",
  PSKHex=false` rendered `secret = 0x61626364`, indistinguishable from the
  hex control — the reported defect.
- New tests GREEN with the fix, RED with `policy.go` stashed (4/5 direct
  cells + end-to-end; the grouped ascii-0x+plain cell is a control that
  passed pre-fix).
- Existing `TestPSKHexadecimal*15027` / `TestGatewayGroup*15024` unchanged
  GREEN; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1` fully GREEN;
  `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestIPsecPSKHexadecimal15027'` GREEN;
  `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

## Risk

Only lone ASCII values starting with `0x` change render (deliberately):
they now authenticate as the literal string and stop matching a peer that
had compensated by configuring the hex-decoded bytes. Hex, plain-ASCII,
grouped-plain, and malformed-hex skip renders are byte-identical. No
real-charon verification (no charon binary in this environment); the
swanctl render contract is pinned as in #15027.

## PR #16319 — nfqueue: verify reinject helper peer via SO_PEERCRED before any byte (#16052) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16052-reinject-peercred`

Why: `SocketReinjectSubmitter` dialed both helper unix sockets (submit and complete) with a bare `net.DialTimeout` and never checked `SO_PEERCRED`. A squatter listening on the socket path in a non-default (operator-selected, writable/sticky) socket dir received ANNOUNCE plus decrypted IPsec-inner payloads, and could return spoofed completions the client reported as success while every packet was dropped — blackhole with lying success (all completion paths are `VerdictDrop`, so no fail-open forwarding). Severity Medium: the default root-owned `/run/xpf` disallows squatting; the precondition is a non-default socket dir plus a local squatter. The #9171 census verified the Rust helper side, never the Go client's peer; #15950's server-side change does not fix this.

What:
- `dial` (the single choke point for both streams, `pkg/nfqueue/reinject_socket.go`) now verifies the peer via `SO_PEERCRED` immediately after connect, before any ANNOUNCE/payload/completion byte, closing and refusing the connection on failure.
- Only uid 0 or this process's own euid is accepted, mirroring `verifyUnixPeerIsPrivileged`/`peerCredTrustError` in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/socket_trust_9003.go` (#9003). In production both ends are root; the euid arm lets a non-root test binary drive the real path against a socket it binds itself.
- The decision (`reinjectPeerTrustError16052`) is split from the syscall shell (`readReinjectPeerCred16052`), which NEVER substitutes a zero `unix.Ucred` for a failed read — a zeroed credential has `Uid 0`, so swallowing the error would fail open. Refusals wrap the sentinel `errUntrustedReinjectPeer16052`.
- `peerVerify` / `reinjectGetsockoptUcred16052` seams let tests present a foreign credential on a real socket and force a credential-read failure (a non-root binary cannot manufacture a foreign-uid peer).
- `reinject_peercred_16052_test.go`: decision table, fail-closed shell cells, the decisive squatter regression, and a trusted-helper control. `docs/log/16052.md` records the change.

## PR #16322 — dhcprelay: add per-sender fairness under aggregate rate limit (#16087) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16087-dhcp-relay-fairness`

## Why
#16087 (A10-17 fairness leg, split from #15988): the #5670 DHCP relay ingress limiter is one aggregate token bucket per interface, so a single sender sustaining >= `maximum-packet-rate` consumes every refill and legitimate DISCOVERs from other clients starve for the flood's duration. The eviction leg was refuted by all reviewers (pending capacity is rate-derived in `pending.go`) and is untouched. The Codex dissent is recorded honestly: chaddr/DUID are attacker-chosen, so per-sender fairness only stops a naive single-identity flooder — that limitation is documented in the README rather than hidden.

## What
- `fairLimiter` (relay.go) layered under the aggregate bucket on both relay paths (DHCPv4 chaddr key; DHCPv6 Client-ID DUID key, aggregate-only when no usable Client ID).
- Per sender: `ceil(rate/256)` pps sustained, burst floor 8 (a full DORA + retransmissions clears instantly); one identity can consume only ~1/256 of the aggregate.
- Aggregate bucket stays the pre-parse CPU/amplification bound; a fairness denial refunds its aggregate token so the flooder's drops cannot burn other senders' share.
- Table capped at 256 senders/interface, longest-idle (>=30s) recycling; identity rotation cannot evict established senders.
- Drops reuse `RequestsDroppedRateLimit` + warn-once log. No schema/counter/wire change.
- README documents the honest limit (multi-identity floods need switch DHCP-snooping/per-port controls); changelog + docs/log/16087.md.

## Validation
- Decisive check from the issue: `TestRunRelay_Fairness_SecondMACCompletesDORA` — 1-MAC flood (25 @ rate 5, frozen clock), second MAC's DISCOVER/REQUEST relayed and OFFER/ACK delivered. Plus `TestDHCPV6Fairness_SecondClientGetsShare` and `TestFairLimiter_*` (share, equal refill, bound, rotation, idle recycling).
- #5670 end-to-end tests updated to fairness-bound counts (single sender admits burst 8).
- Full `pkg/dhcprelay` suite passes except 3 pre-existing failures identical on clean origin/master (9406 x2, `TestInterfaceIPv4_Loopback` — env/fixture). Race run + `go vet` clean.
- RED-on-revert: removing either limiter layer raises single-sender admission in the 5670/fairness tests.

## Risk
A lone sender is capped at ~rate/256 sustained (1 pps at 100 pps default, burst 8) instead of the full aggregate — far above legitimate DHCP client behaviour; `maximum-packet-rate` raises every sender's share. Assignment verification was explicitly instructed, so tests were run in this worktree.

## PR #16324 — build: make cluster-deploy respects prebuilt deb (#16308) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16308-cluster-deploy-prebuilt-deb`

## Why

`make cluster-deploy` unconditionally rebuilt a stock deb via its `.PHONY deb` prerequisite, discarding a prebuilt high-version deb built with `make deb DEB_VERSION=99.0.x+…` (the #16219 downgrade-avoidance workflow). The rebuilt stock deb then won `cluster-setup.sh`'s `ls -t` selection and apt refused it as a downgrade (`Packages were downgraded and -y was used without --allow-downgrades`), so the documented entry point failed and the operator's `DEB_VERSION` bump was silently defeated. Agents worked around it by bypassing `make cluster-deploy` entirely.

Fixes #16308.

## What

- **Makefile**: replace the `deb` prerequisite of `cluster-deploy`, `loss-cluster-deploy`, and `cluster-deploy-and-gate` (`userspace-cluster-deploy` delegates to `cluster-deploy`) with an order-only `prepare-deb`:
  - explicit `DEB_VERSION` (command line/env, via `$(origin)`) → always build via `deb` (unchanged);
  - else a `dist-deb/xpf_*.deb` with filename version `>=` the stock version → **reused, no rebuild**, announced;
  - else (fresh tree / older-only) → build stock via `deb`.
  - Explicit `DEB_VERSION` is threaded to the scripts as `XPF_DEPLOY_DEB_VERSION` so the just-built deb deploys even beside a higher stale deb.
- **deploy-lib.sh**: new `deploy_deb_version` / `deploy_deb_newest` / `deploy_select_deb` — Debian version ordering via `dpkg --compare-versions`, never mtime; `XPF_DEPLOY_DEB_VERSION` / `XPF_DEPLOY_DEB_PATH` pins fail closed (die naming the pin).
- **cluster-setup.sh / test-rolling-upgrade.sh**: all `ls -t dist-deb` selections replaced with `deploy_select_deb`; deploy logs the selected deb + version.

## Validation (hermetic, no lab cluster)

- `bash test/incus/deploy-lib-selftest.sh` → **134 passed, 0 failed**, including 18 new #16308 cells: highest-version-beats-newest-mtime, empty-dir/stock-only, path+version pins (incl. missing-pin dies), and `make -n` decisions for reuse / fresh-build / older-only-rebuild / explicit-build + threading / `XPF_DEPLOY_FAST=1`.
- A real prebuilt `xpf_99.0.16308+601c5462a991.dirty_amd64.deb` (built via `make deb`, verified `dpkg-deb -f` → `99.0.16308+601c5462a991.dirty`) is reused by `make prepare-deb` with no rebuild; `deploy_select_deb` returns it.
- `shellcheck -S warning` clean on touched scripts; `git diff --check` clean.

## Risk

Selection is fail-closed on missing/unparseable pins; explicit-bump and FAST paths are unchanged; loss/tcp/udp env vars only threaded through. Live deploy acceptance remains lab-gated per the issue.

Refs #16219 (workflow preserved), #16290 (downstream manifest consequence).

## PR #16325 — configstore: preserve rollback history across active-rename crash window (#16064) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16064-rollback-meta-dual-binding`

Why: Config commit writes active.json first and publishes generation-bound rollback metadata only after rewriting every rollback slot. A power loss after the active rename but before that metadata publish left the sidecar binding the previous active identity, so boot tombstoned every generation-bound rollback slot even when all slot bytes still matched history. History was lost exactly when the just-committed config misbehaved.

What: Before WriteActive, plain and confirmed commits now durably publish a rollback preparation record (current committed entries plus next_active_hash and per-entry pending_hash with its own pending_timestamp/pending_comment). Boot certifies only that exact one-generation skew (including same-content commits) and admits matching slots at pre-shift positions (slot 1 = previous active hash, later slots = preceding committed entry, partially rewritten slots = prepared pending hash with pending attributes). A store recovered through the skew path re-arms preparation on every subsequent commit. Any other mismatch keeps the #10723 fail-closed tombstone behavior; completed commits clear the preparation fields. Adds fault-injection regression tests (real Commit path panicking at the slot writer after WriteActive, partial-rewrite gate test through the production loader, uncertified-rewrite guard, same-content certification, post-recovery re-arm). Updates docs/log/16064.md and debian/changelog.

Validation: go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run '16064' -count=1 green; neighboring -run '10723|10299|10825|10826|7176|3441|16064' green; full go test ./pkg/configstore/ -count=1 green (152.191s); go vet ./pkg/configstore/ clean; git diff --check clean.

Risk: Bounded to crash/skew recovery: relaxation is keyed to an exact recorded next-active hash and exact per-slot content hashes, so unrelated or corrupted history remains fail-closed. Successful commits pay one extra durable sidecar write before the active rename.

Refs #16064

## PR #16326 — dhcpserver: verify Kea lease-sync peer via SO_PEERCRED before any command (#16058) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16058-kea-peercred`

## Summary

Verify `SO_PEERCRED` on the Kea lease-sync control-socket dial (#16058), mirroring the reinject fix (#16052) and the helper-socket check (#9003).

## Why

The Kea lease-sync client dialed Kea's control socket by pathname (`defaultKeaDialer`: a bare unix dial) with no peer verification. A wrong/squatted server on that path was trusted as Kea: returned leases are sanitized, but sanitization cannot authenticate the wrong server, so fabricated lease data could be fed into HA lease sync — and lease-add/update commands would be delivered to the squatter on the seed path. The permissions arm of the claim is DUP A10-06 and out of scope; only the peer-verification arm is fixed here.

## What

- `pkg/dhcpserver/lease_sync.go`: `defaultKeaDialer` — the single production dial choke point for every Kea control-socket exchange (`lease{4,6}-get-all`, `lease{4,6}-add`/`-update`, `dhcp-disable`, display reads) — now verifies `SO_PEERCRED` immediately after connect, before any command byte is written, and closes/refuses on failure (`errUntrustedKeaPeer`). Trusted uids: the resolved Kea runtime user (`_kea`/`kea` via the #2450 lookup), root, or this daemon's own euid. The decision (`keaPeerTrustErrorAs`) is split from the syscall shell (`readKeaPeerUID`, `keaGetsockoptUcred` seam); a failed credential read never substitutes a zero Ucred (Uid 0 = root = trusted — the #9003 fail-open).
- `waitControlSocket` re-verifies when a custom dialer is in use, so a connectable squatter is never reported Kea-ready to the post-start seed.
- `pkg/dhcpserver/README.md` + `docs/log/16058.md` + `debian/changelog` updated.
- NOT changed: the `keaSocketDialer` test-seam contract (custom dialers are test doubles; `net.Pipe` cannot present credentials), the memfile fallback, sanitization, and all callers.

## Validation

- New `lease_sync_peercred_16058_test.go`: decision table (Kea/daemon/root admitted, foreign refused), no-Kea-user collapse, kernel-read positive control, fail-closed shell (non-AF_UNIX + forced `SO_PEERCRED` failure), readiness refusal.
- Decisive regression `TestSquatterRefusedAndSyncsZeroLeases16058`: squatter offering a fabricated lease, peer judged foreign via the `keaPeerVerify` seam for any test-binary uid, syncs 0 leases from it into an isolated memfile fixture (exactly its known 10.0.61.70 row returned) with 0 squatter commands recorded. Bare-dial mutant (removing the verify call) fails wanting exactly that fixture lease instead of the fabricated 10.0.61.99 row; restored GREEN.
- `go test ./pkg/dhcpserver/ -count=1`: only `TestKeaSubnetIDStableAcrossSpellingChange` fails — base-attributed (fails identically on unmodified `30638bcad3`). `pkg/cluster`, `pkg/daemon` lease-sync suites pass. `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

## Risk

Verification runs on every dial, and the seed path dials once per command (`keaControl` per `lease-add`, plus one for a conflict `lease-update`), so verification IS per command there — one `getsockopt` per seeded lease on the async takeover seed, never per packet. A refused peer degrades to the existing memfile fallback / fail-open seed exactly as a down socket does, so serving cannot wedge. A root- or `_kea`-compromised peer is still trusted (uid is the authentication granularity), matching #9003/#16052. No live cluster was mutated.

Refs #16058

## PR #16331 — userspace-dp: meter LocalDelivery policers before miss-path side effects (#15949) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `impl-15949-arm2`

Refs #15949.

Why: H34-04 arm 2 (deferred by the merged #15949 PR for the mod.rs collision). On the session-miss LocalDelivery path the ingress three-color policer metered only at the install site — after the PERMIT FilterLog, lo0, and junos-host evaluations, and (for an owner_syn_reuse SYN) after closing-pair eviction — leaving a false PERMIT audit record, lo0/junos-host counter increments, a prematurely evicted closing pair with no replacement, and a skipped persistent-hold rollback for policer-dropped host-bound packets. The session-hit path folds policer drops to Discard before logging; the miss path did not.

What: a new early gate (meter_miss_local_input_policers in poll_descriptor/mod.rs) captures the flow's cached policer handles and meters immediately after the input-filter verdict for locally-targeted destinations (effective target in the FIB local-address sets), before the PERMIT log emit, lo0, junos-host, eviction, and hold anchoring. A red packet re-emits its matched log (if any) with a truthful DENY (Discard) action, rolls back any persistent-inbound hold, and recycles without installing/delivering/evicting/anchoring. ## Why
Session display, clear-by-interface and flow-export keyed every unit on `{parent ifindex, VID = vlan-id else unit number}`:
- VLAN units were keyed by the parent netdev instead of their child device;
- two WireGuard units sharing one TUN (wg0.0/wg0.1, both VID 0) collided on one name, so `clear ... interface wg0.1` could delete wg0.0 sessions;

Stale parent-key comments in `pkg/dataplane/types.go` updated.
- Regression tests: `pkg/config` (shared-TUN refusal incl. determinism, child/per-unit keying, by-ifindex projection, nil/tolerant), `pkg/cli` (`TestClearWgSiblingCannotDeleteOtherUnit16065` — decisive clear check), `pkg/daemon` (flow-export refusal + VLAN child). `docs/log/16065.md` + changelog.

## PR #16335 — ddns: add require-tsig opt-in and live unsigned-posture gauge (#15992) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/15992-require-tsig`

## Why

RFC2136 DDNS without TSIG trusted a forgeable rcode: a forged NOERROR recorded durable ownership of an unwritten name in state that survives restart, and a forged REFUSED/YXDOMAIN suppressed legitimate publishes — with only a once-per-process runtime warning. The posture needed to be continuously visible and optionally fail-closed, without breaking legitimate source-IP-ACL unsigned BIND (the default).

## What

- `require-tsig` valueless leaf on both DDNS surfaces (DHCP `dynamic-dns` and Surface A `system services dynamic-dns provider`): strict commit refuses `require-tsig` + non-loopback `update-server` + no `tsig-key` (DHCP: including a disabled family, which still withdraws persisted records at runtime — the backend refuses those unsigned withdrawals too, so supply a key for signed cleanup or remove `require-tsig`); tolerant load/peer-sync downgrades to a warning (no-brick).
- Runtime backstop in the RFC2136 backend: a `require-tsig` config that arrives without a key refuses the non-loopback UPDATE before sending, so no durable ownership is recorded on a forgeable verdict (the backend's `exchange` only carries RFC 2136 UPDATEs; SOA zone discovery is a separate query path). Loopback servers are exempt, matching the commit gate.
- Live gauges `xpf_dhcp_ddns_unsigned_nonloopback_active` / `xpf_ddns_surface_a_unsigned_nonloopback_active` stay at 1 for as long as the forgeable-rcode posture persists — including owned records still pending cleanup at an unsigned non-loopback endpoint after disable/removal, an in-progress cleanup pass (in-flight hold), a keyed-endpoint transition whose old records withdraw via the previous unsigned updater, and the post-restart window before the first reconcile (seeded at construction from persisted ownership + the boot config's cleanup endpoint) — refreshed every reconcile (not once per process).
- Spelling-gate registry: the three `require-tsig` rows registered as `flag (read, but value-less)`; flag ceiling 197 -> 200 with the reason recorded.

## Validation

- `pkg/config`: require-tsig strict-reject (both surfaces, plus disabled DHCP families), tolerant-warn, loopback/keyed/default controls pass; the runtime DELETE refusal is pinned alongside the publish refusal.
- `pkg/ddns`: full suite passes, including reconcile-driven gauge tests (`ReconcileScoped`/`Reconcile` -> `Stats`), cleanup-after-disable tests, an in-flight hold test (scrape while a cleanup UPDATE is blocked mid-pass), a keyed-transition test (old records withdraw via the previous unsigned updater), and a fresh-manager restart regression (persisted ownership + disabled unsigned endpoint reports 1 before any reconcile, keyed/loopback/record-free controls 0); mutation checks prove the loopback exemption, gauge wiring, in-flight hold, and previous-updater capture are load-bearing.
- `pkg/api`: gauge test passes through real manager reconcile -> `Stats` -> collector.
- Base-vs-worktree spelling-gate comparison on base `eea94248f5`: the members registry, coverage ratchet, and differential gate already drift on the pristine base (140 arrived / 6 departed / 8 reclassified leaves, none of them `require-tsig`); this change adds only its 3 rows and does not alter that pre-existing drift. Same for `pkg/api` `TestRESTRecycledIfindexIsNotReportedAsFact6960`, red on base and unchanged here.

## Risk

Default posture unchanged: unsigned source-IP-ACL publishing keeps working without `require-tsig`. The new gate is opt-in; loopback servers remain exempt on both the commit gate and the runtime backstop. The gauge may stay 1 while cleanup is genuinely pending at an unsigned non-loopback endpoint (including kept orphan ownership) — that is the intended alarm.

Refs #15992

## PR #16338 — harness: name refused deploy in attestation VOID reason (#16290) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16290-manifest-attestation`

Refs #16290

## Why

`cluster-setup.sh deploy` invalidates the executable-attestation manifest *before* deploying, but only writes the new manifest *after* the deploy body succeeds. When the rolling cut refuses (e.g. `xpfd upgrade --rolling` rejects replacing the live version dir because the same version tag was re-staged with different bytes — `refuse-before-PREFLIGHT`), `set -e` aborts before `deploy_write_manifest` runs, leaving **no** `dist-deb/xpf-deploy-manifest.json` at all. Every subsequent cluster gate then records VOID (`exe_check=UNAVAILABLE`, build under test unattributable) with no hint that a refused deploy is the cause — one refused re-stage silently poisons attestation for all later gates until the next fully successful deploy.

## What

Implements suggested fix (2) from the issue (explicit marker naming the refused deploy), preserving fail-closed semantics:

- **`test/incus/deploy-lib.sh`** — a `.failed` sidecar marker next to the manifest (`deploy_manifest_record_failure` / `deploy_manifest_failure_reason` / `deploy_manifest_clear_failure`) naming the deploy target, failed step, and reason. It carries no binary identity and `deploy_manifest_sha` never reads it. `deploy_manifest_invalidate` clears a stale marker; a successful `deploy_write_manifest` clears it.
- **`test/incus/cluster-setup.sh` `cmd_deploy`** — an EXIT-trap guard armed immediately after invalidation (guard state in globals, not locals, so the trap survives function return under `set -u`; `$?` captured as the trap's first action). Any `set -e` abort or `die` between invalidation and the manifest write records the marker with the failed step; the explicit `die` paths record their specific reason and disarm so the trap cannot overwrite it. On success the flag is cleared and the trap removed, so successful deploy paths behave exactly as before.
- **`test/incus/harness-result.sh`** — when `exe_check` (or the helper leg) is `UNAVAILABLE`, the VOID reason gains `; attestation unavailable because deploy <target> failed: <reason>`. Verdict and `exe_check` are unchanged (still VOID/UNAVAILABLE).

Fail-closed is preserved throughout: a deploy that cut some nodes leaves the marker, not a manifest claiming the old build; completed nodes re-attest only when the whole deploy succeeds.

## Validation

- `test/incus/deploy-lib-selftest.sh`: **147 passed, 0 failed**, including the hermetic invalidate→refused-cut→manifest-state sequence (deploy-A control; all-node refusal leaves no manifest, a marker naming the refusal, and no attestation; single-node refusal preserves the peer slot and names deploy 1; recovery deploy clears the marker; invalidation supersedes a stale marker; a reason-less marker fails closed) and the rewired `cmd_deploy` ordering check (invalidate → trap armed → deploy → write → disarm → rebaseline).
- `test/incus/harness-result-selftest.sh`: **260 passed, 1 failed** — the single failure (`#12140` cluster gate census) pre-exists on the base commit and is unrelated. The new case asserts a refused deploy VOIDs with a `void_reason` naming the refused deploy, not a bare `exe_check=UNAVAILABLE`.
- Mutation check: making `deploy_manifest_record_failure` a no-op turns the #16290 sequence checks RED.
- `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` clean on all touched scripts.
- Not run: a live refused re-stage on the loss/tcp/udp clusters (no cluster available to this change). The acceptance sequence is covered hermetically with the real lib calls in `cmd_deploy`'s exact order.

## Risk

Low and harness-only. The marker is additive operator/ledger metadata: it never attests binaries, never revives stale provenance, and is cleared by the next invalidation or successful write. The EXIT trap exists only between invalidation and a successful manifest write.

## PR #16339 — vrrp: drop unknown-source priority-0/255 adverts once master learned (#16018) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16018-vrrp-unknown-source-z2b`

Refs #16018

## Why
xpf learned the legitimate master source per family (#10719) but only logged priority-0/255 adverts from other sources before applying them — a forged priority-0 armed the ~1ms backup takeover and a forged priority-255 demoted the master, even after the genuine master was learned and fresh. Separately (A7-03), native VRRP is consumed via AF_PACKET before netfilter input, so a zone host-inbound denial of `vrrp` never gated it and no commit-time signal said so.

## What
- `pkg/vrrp/instance_rx.go`: folds the #10719 counter/warning into `unknownSourceAdvert`, which also returns the drop decision. While the learned record is fresh (`observedMasterStaleLocked`), `handleBackupRx`/`handleMasterRx` return before any timer/state/record effect for a mismatched priority-0/255 source. Cold start, stale record, and the learned source itself keep RFC behaviour (genuine priority-0 still takes over in ~1ms); ordinary priorities 1–254 are ungated. Warning gains a `dropped` attribute.
- `pkg/config`: `validateHostInboundVRRPBypassWarnings`, WARN-only on every path (wired in `runTailGates`), names the AF_PACKET bypass per zoned interface carrying an explicit vrrp-group or active RETH-derived instance whose effective host-inbound protocols omit `vrrp`. Admitted/`all`/lifeline/no-VRRP stay silent; strict commit still succeeds.
- README trust-boundary section updated; the #10719 demotion cell now expects no demotion (known-source 255 demotion remains covered by its control test).

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run '16018|10719'` — 12 tests PASS (incl. new backup-255, IPv6, cold-start, stale-master, genuine-resign cells).
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'VRRPBypass|HostInboundManagedRouting|TestHostInbound'` — PASS.
- Fail-on-revert: disabling the gate call reddens the 16018/10719 cells; removing the tailgate append reddens `TestVRRPBypassCompileWarnOnly16018`.
- Full `pkg/vrrp` run: only pre-existing base failure `TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate` (verified identical on clean base); same for `TestVRRPCrossGroupDifferentInterfacesCommits` in `pkg/config`.

## Risk
A genuine master that changes source IP while still fresh has its 0/255 adverts dropped until the learned record goes stale (one master-down horizon), after which elections resume. Spoofing the learned source itself remains the VRRPv3 protocol floor. The commit warning is advisory only and never rejects.
