## PR #16341 — userspace-dp: verify snapshot interface/zone summary counts (#16056) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16056-snapshot-counts-z3b`

Refs #16056

## Why
The Rust snapshot apply handler checked `policy_count` against the built policies but never compared `summary.interface_count`/`zone_count` against the built `interfaces`/`zones` sections. A producer shape with `interface_count>0` but `interfaces=[]` passed all gates, built forwarding with zero bindings, unbound all workers, ACKed ok and persisted as baseline; `zones=[]` in a global-only config had the same joint-omission shape (zone-pair policies already fail preflight closed, so the surviving arm is availability-only, Low). Go also set the summary counts from the authored config maps before `quarantineCollidingZones`, so a naive Rust equality check would refuse legitimate quarantined snapshots.

## What
- Rust `apply` (after version + policy-count gates, before monotonicity/preflight/mutation): refuse `interface_count != len(interfaces) || zone_count != len(zones)`, and refuse an empty interfaces/zones install over a non-empty installed set even when both transmitted fields are zeroed (no full-clear signal exists for these sections, unlike policies' `clear_policies`). Refusals keep prior forwarding/snapshot, do not advance the reported generation, and count on `snapshot_policy_mismatch_total`.
- Go: full builder derives `InterfaceCount=len(built interfaces)`, `ZoneCount=len(built zones)` and reconciles all summary counts post-quarantine unconditionally; link-refresh and apply-time rebuild do the same; `prepareSnapshotForApply` re-syncs `InterfaceCount` after revalidation drops (incl. the config-less early-return path); `validateSnapshotForSend` refuses a section mismatch known-unsent (`errSnapshotPolicyMismatch`).
- Protocol v67 -> v68 both sides (Go `ProtocolVersion`, Rust `CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, shape/secure-tunnel pins; shape golden refreshed to the measured master digest `cf98a6a5` which already differed on clean `origin/master`).
- Existing Rust fixtures carrying zones/interfaces without summary counts now declare them; `TestSyncRetryRemarksUnlandedClear` keeps its interfaces through the clear retry (only policies legitimately empty).

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '16056|TestBuildSnapshotSummary|TestFullBuilderPopulatesEverySnapshotField|TestSnapshotShape|TestSnapshotProtocolVersion|TestSyncRetryRemarksUnlandedClear|TestValidateSnapshotForSend|TestCompileClearAll|TestBuilderInvariant'` — PASS, including new `TestBuildSnapshotSummaryCountsBuiltSections16056` (FAIL-ON-REVERT vs authored-map counts), `TestBuildSnapshotQuarantinedZoneCountReconciled16056` (z174/z214 collision), `TestValidateSnapshotForSendRefusesSectionMismatch16056`.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- apply_snapshot_` — 35 passed; 1 failure `apply_snapshot_wires_day2_preserved_mtu_reconcile` fails identically on clean `origin/master` (pre-existing, unrelated D11/D14 join).
- Full Go package run: only pre-existing master failures (secure-tunnel PSK fixtures, SNAT parity liveness, retry-debt hash, GOTMPDIR socket-path artifacts), verified against clean master where applicable.

Mixed-version pairs refuse on the exact-equality gate until both sides reach v68. ## PR #16342 — config: poison uncovered-family except arm on tolerant load (#16001) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16001-prefix-except-family`

Why: A sole-`except` prefix-list covering no address of its pool's family (v4-only `except` under `family any` / `inet6`, and the v6 mirror) warned on tolerant load but still installed verbatim, evaluating `except` over an empty per-family set and matching EVERY packet of the uncovered family — a fail-open over-accept on `then accept` (#16001, EX-4 from #15981). Decisive check: absent-family except+accept cannot admit v6/v4 when the list only contains the opposite family.

What:
- `pkg/config`: the #4426 AST gate (`validateFirewallFilterFamilyAnyMatchesAST`) now also returns the uncovered (pool, filter, term) sites for sole-`except` cases; `runPreWalkGates` threads them to `compileExpanded`, which stamps `FirewallFilterTerm.UncoveredFamilyExcept16001` on exactly the uncovered pool's term via `markUncoveredFamilyExcept16001`. `compileFirewall` clones a `family any` filter per pool (`cloneFirewallFilter16001`) — the pools previously shared one `*FirewallFilter`, so a per-pool mark would have leaked to the covered arm. The field joins `effectiveTermProjection15997` and is `json:"-"` (golden-neutral).
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace`: a marked term sets `FromUnrepresentable`, so the Rust compiler rejects the candidate snapshot whole and reconcile retains prior-good state. No wire/Rust change.
- lo0 mirrors (`pkg/daemon`): the text oracle emits the constant refusal bareword; the netlink DTO carries `FromUnrepresentable` — the whole lo0 candidate is refused the same way.

## PR #16350 — nat: key PAT port allocation per RFC 6056 (#16011) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16011-rfc6056-pat`

Why: fresh PAT ports were handed out in ascending order from a shared monotonic cursor (pool claim), a shared round-robin counter (interface PAT walk and try_next_port), so an observer of one translated port — e.g. a colluding server that sees the remote tuple — could predict the next port, multiplying tuple-guessing attacks.

What:
- Pool PAT claims start at a keyed splitmix hash of the full flow tuple under a per-boot secret drawn once from the audited OS CSPRNG (`hot_hash_seed::os_random_seed_u64`, never zero), then probe forward over at most `range` distinct offsets, then fall through to the existing FIFO recycle ring. Monotonic cursor + its debug seam removed.
- Interface PAT walk and stateless `try_next_port` use the same keyed start (flow-keyed variant at the synthetic call sites).
- Deterministic CGNAT block allocation deliberately keeps its documented lowest-free-in-block contract (subscriber-derived reproducibility); recycle ring remains FIFO-queued, with a test-only recycled-phase seam for the #9327/#9392/#7174 cost fixtures.
- Tests that pinned sequential values adapted to keyed order (in-range/set/distinctness); new `tests_16011` pins secret-dependence, non-sequential spread, bounded next-port prediction (~random over 2000 trials), fail-closed exhaustion, sole-free-port probe, and concurrent uniqueness. Changelog entry added.

Validation: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp nat::` — 736 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (includes 5 new tests_16011 tests). Fail-on-revert: restoring sequential allocation makes `pat_fresh_ports_are_not_sequential_16011` and `pat_next_port_prediction_advantage_is_bounded_16011` fail.

Risk: new-flow translated ports change distribution (by design); persistent/deterministic/synced reservations and release paths untouched, so live sessions and HA imports keep exact tuples. Per-boot secret is node-local, never synced — synced sessions carry explicit tuples, so failover need not reproduce a peer's fresh-port choice. Probe worst case is O(range) bitmap CAS like the prior cursor probe, with an exact `occupied == range` fail-closed gate.

Refs #16011

## PR #16352 — nat: charge persistent leases per source (#16013) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16013-nat-per-source-fairness`

## Why
The pool allocator capped persistent leases only pool-globally (`max_tracked_flows`), while the per-source session quota is per (zone, src) per worker and never charged idle leases. One host churning source ports accumulated idle persistent leases (300s–24h retention) after its flows closed, retaining the whole lease table — and, on a single-address pool, its ports — while other sources were refused (#16013, A2-C2).

## What
- Count leases per `(src_ip, routing_scope)` at the single insert/remove seam for `persistent_by_source`, so every mint, import, carry and removal stays in step with no second counting convention.
- Refuse a NEW lease key at 4096 (mirrors the session-layer per-source default `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_SOURCE`) after a bounded pressure-GC pass, on: local PAT, local address-only, HA-synced PAT, HA-synced address-only, idle-lease import, deterministic NAT64 BIB.
- Joining an existing lease is never refused by this gate; expiry/clear/GC/reseed release the charge through the same seam. Idle-lease per-source refusal reports through the existing `SkippedCapacity` outcome/counter.

## Validation
- New `nat::tests_persistent_per_source_16013` (6 tests): decisive churn cell (cap-many *closed* flows from one host → next new lease refused, second source still allocates), rejoin-not-charged, routing-scope separation, expiry releases charge, address-only charging, idle-import charging.
- Full `nat::` suite: 737 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo check --release --tests` clean.

## Risk
A single legitimate source needing >4096 distinct persistent leases (distinct source ports/protocols/scopes) in one pool is refused new leases until idle leases expire — the intended fairness bound, matching the existing per-source session ceiling. Spoofed-source churn on SAV-less LANs stays bounded by zone/session quotas (S2-01), not this allocator charge.

Closes #16013

## PR #16353 — userspace-dp: fail closed on tiny first-fragment unknown TCP flags (#16007) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16007-tiny-frag-flags`

Refs #16007

## Why
An 8-byte first fragment (declared L4 < 14 bytes) stamps `tcp_flags=0` in the shim (`first_fragment_l4`), so `syn-frag` cannot fire, SYN-flood/cookie logic keys on absent flags, and session admission reads the zero as a proven non-SYN — admitted under `no-syn-check` and exempt on LocalDelivery. The reassembled SYN arrives only in the offset-1 second fragment. Validated Medium (A1-C1 from #15985): default-config transit dies at the strict SYN check, but as `strict-syn-check`, not `syn-frag`, and the `no-syn-check` / LocalDelivery arms misclassify outright.

## What
Encode flags-UNKNOWN end to end and fail closed on it:
- **Shim** (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs`): `UserspaceDpMeta.tcp_flags_unknown` reuses the former `reserved` byte (96B ABI unchanged), folded out of `is_fragment && protocol==TCP && payload_offset==l4_offset` in the outlined meta store — the exact shape `first_fragment_l4` returns for declared L4 <14 — so no new `ParsedPacket` state for the verifier to carry.
- **Worker re-derivation** (`frame/inspect.rs`, `icmp.rs`): `frame_l4_flags_unknown` (verified L3 + IP-declared end + first-fragment walk) so slow-path/injected/replayed frames that never crossed the shim are covered; `meta_l4_flags_unknown` is the single consumer predicate (shim bit OR frame derivation).
- **Screen**: extractor fails closed with `TinyFirstFragmentFlagsUnknown` → reason `"syn-frag"` (per-reason index 13, existing `SCREEN_SYN_FRAG` counter) when a TCP first fragment's declared end (total_len/payload_len, never capture length) stops before L4+14; `check_tcp_flag_screens` drops unknown-flags first fragments as `syn-frag` defense-in-depth (never the false `tcp-no-flag` on tf==0).
- **Admission**: `strict_syn_check_drops_new_flow[_tunnel]` drop on unknown in every mode, including `no-syn-check` and the tunnel opt-out (a stamped SYN is not proven either).
- **LocalDelivery**: the poll-descriptor gate covers LocalDelivery only when flags are unknown — proven non-SYN LocalDelivery still reaches the local stack (peer RST/FIN for firewall-originated flows) — and LocalDelivery session caching declines on unknown (no helper-local session seeded off unseen flags).

Decisive regression (issue check): 8B first fragment + offset-1 second fragment drops in (a) default — `screen/tests_16007_tiny_frag.rs` (v4+v6) and live `stage_screen_check` drop with the legal second fragment passing as control; (b) `no-syn-check` — admission mode sweep; (c) LocalDelivery — unknown-only gate + cache-decline test.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16007`: 7 passed.
- `screen::` suite: 368 passed, 1 failed — `screen::tests::extract_info_from_ipv4_frame` is a pre-existing header-only fixture (34-byte frame, total_len=20, MF set, no L4 bytes) whose shape is itself this issue's unknown-flags case; it now correctly fails closed. Left untouched rather than silently rewritten; happy to update it in a follow-up if preferred.
- `afxdp::` suite: 5928 passed / 42 failed; failure set byte-identical to the pristine-baseline run (same 42), plus one flaky `icmp_ratelimit` test that passes in isolation twice.
- Shim: candidate builds with the pinned toolchain, but this guest kernel rejects even a pristine-source rebuild at the 1M verifier cap (tracked .o measures 856646 insns / 14.34% = LOW-HEADROOM), so the tracked `userspace_xdp_bpfel.o` is NOT regenerated here. The worker-side frame re-derivation makes the fix effective without the new shim bit; the bit takes effect with the next successful shim rebuild.

## Risk
Legitimate TCP connections fragmented so the flags byte lands in the second fragment now drop as `syn-frag` instead of forwarding — the fail-closed posture the issue requires (indistinguishable from the attack shape). Proven-flags traffic, non-first fragments, and non-TCP fragments are unchanged. No ABI size change; no allocation on the hot path.

## PR #16354 — sessions: shed unreplied flows protocol-symmetrically under pressure (#16019) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16019`

Closes #16019.

## Why
Per-source session limits key on the claimed (spoofable) source, and pressure shedding only relieved a TCP initial-SYN newcomer by evicting handshake-incomplete TCP. Rotating spoofed-source UDP/ICMP singles each minted fresh quota and filled the session table; a legitimate second zone/host's new flows were starved with no relief path (S2-01 from #15985).

## What
- `can_admit_new_syn` → `can_admit_new_flow`: trigger is protocol-symmetric (TCP keeps its initial-SYN-only gate; non-TCP first packets qualify), same 90% watermark and hard cap.
- Victim predicate/index generalized from TCP openings (`pressure_shed_openings`) to never-replied local sessions (`pressure_shed_unreplied`): TCP handshake-incomplete, or non-TCP with zero reverse packets accounted (`SessionCounters::replied()` — the exact signal, immune to the `established` seeding divergence between app-timeout and no-app-timeout installs). Closing, peer-synced, transient-seed, fabric-ingress and reverse-companion entries are never victims.
- `update_session` maintains the index for all protocols; the shared-map shed fence (`is_pressure_shed_shared_unreplied`) accepts non-TCP victims (handshake state 0 by construction; incarnation still fenced by session_id/decision/metadata).
- Docs: session README admission section + changelog.

## Validation

## PR #16355 — nat: revoke stored any-remote grants on permit tightening (#16017) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16017-persistent-nat-permit-revoke`

## Why (#16017, A2-C13)

`permits()` reads stored scopes; `SourceNatPoolAllocatorKey` = pool name + addresses + port range only, so `resolve_pool_allocators` reuses the previous allocator on a permit-only rebuild — leases + permissions carry across. Only revocation (`clear_persistent_leases`) fires from explicit coordinator clear, never on permit change; inbound hold disarms idle expiry while held. Mint an any-remote lease, rebuild same pool + tightened permit, probe `persistent_inbound_lookup_for_rule` from a non-target remote — **today: Permitted**.

## What

- Each bucket's `any_remote` grant records the **authorizing rule's permit epoch**: an allocator generation counter bumped on every allocator reuse in `resolve_pool_allocators` and shared by rules naming the pool. The epoch is threaded explicitly through `allocate_translation*`, `reserve_address_only_persistent*`, and `record_synced_persistent_permission_with_zones` to all mint/record sites; NAT64 BIBs pass 0 (no authorizing source-NAT rule).
- Permit-change sync **demotes every covered bucket** (`authorized_epoch := 0`) before any preserving `AnyRemoteHost` rule restamps it with the new epoch — stored grants, including imported grants, are revoked on tightening.
- **Stale-generation writers are fenced**: a writer whose epoch is older than a bucket's authorized epoch cannot restore `any_remote` (`record_with_zones` demotes the write); `permits()` honors only current-epoch authorization.
- **HA imports are demoted unless locally authorized**: generation validation proves record provenance, not local permit consent. Import APIs carry `permit_any_authorized` computed by the coordinator from live rules sharing the record's allocator/scope; `import_idle_lease_at_after_generation` defaults demoted, with `..._permit_any` as the authorized spelling (also used for NAT64 deterministic BIBs). Demoted imports still install and merge exact remotes; a later preserving sync restamps the wildcard.
- Exact target-host/target-host-port `remotes` stay permitted under every tighter mode.

Refs #9428: allocator key unchanged (permit is not pool-scoped; adding it would split one pool into two allocators and reintroduce duplicate `(addr,port)` mints).

## Test report

- **New** `nat::tests_persistent_permit_16017` (6 tests):
  - `persistent_permit_tightening_revokes_any_remote_grant_16017` — decisive check from the issue (tighten to `target-host-port`, non-target must be `Denied`).
  - `persistent_permit_tightening_to_target_host_revokes_any_remote_16017` — same for `target-host`.
  - `persistent_permit_unchanged_preserves_any_remote_grant_16017` — unchanged-permit preservation control.
  - `imported_any_remote_grant_is_revoked_on_tightening_16017` — imported grant revoked when the reusing generation tightens.
  - `stale_generation_writer_cannot_reauthorize_after_sync_16017` — old writer replays captured epoch after sync; inbound stays `Denied`.
  - `validated_import_after_tightening_stays_demoted_16017` — generation-validated wildcard import lands after tightening; lease installs, non-target stays `Denied`.
- **Existing**: full `nat::` suite **751 passed**; `idle_lease` filter **85 passed**; coordinator idle-lease tests **11 passed**.

## Risk

Fail-closed only: tightened/stale/unauthorized grants lose the wildcard until a current-epoch mint, preserving sync, or locally-authorized import re-grants. Exact remotes and lease installation unaffected; uncovered scopes untouched (#14322 preserved).

## PR #16356 — policy: adjudicate egress-unconstrained tiers on NoRoute (#16021) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16021-noroute-zone-tiers`

Closes #16021 (ZP-07).

## Why
A NoRoute flow (no userspace FIB egress, `to_id == 0`) skipped the whole policy tier walk in `evaluate_policy_result_counted`, so under `default-policy permit-all` the packet was delegated to the kernel FIB — which may still have a route during a flap / FIB-not-loaded / capped learned-route import — and an explicit deny was never evaluated.

## What
- The unresolved-egress (`egress_resolved == false`, `to_id == 0`) evaluation now walks the egress-unconstrained tiers in normal precedence and first-match order: `from-zone <from> to-zone any`, `from-zone any to-zone any`, then `junos-global` rules whose to-zone scope is `Any` (from-zone scope still applies) — with the usual hit-count and #4569 flowless fragment-association semantics.
- Egress-constrained rules (exact pair, `from-zone any to-zone <z>`, to-zone-scoped globals) stay ineligible: they name an egress zone the flow does not have.
- An eligible explicit PERMIT still delegates; only an unmatched NoRoute flow reaches the default policy. Resolved zone-0 egress and zone-0 ingress still deny unchanged.
- Forwarding NoRoute docs updated; `debian/changelog` and `docs/log/16021.md` entries added.

## Validation
- New `tests_noroute_unresolved_16021` cells: decisive default-permit + explicit-deny (to-any / both-any / unscoped + from-scoped global / reject), egress-constrained ineligibility in both directions, eligible-tier precedence, L3/L4 gating incl. flowless fail-closed — all pass.
- Neighbor suites 7480/9522/11067/6722/12226/16129/12906 pass.
- Full `xpf-userspace-dp` bin suite failure set is byte-identical to the clean-tree baseline (80 pre-existing failures, none in the touched area). Note: `slow_path_admit_single_site_6664::noroute_arm_adjudicates_before_reinjecting_7480` already fails on clean master (the #12906 refactor moved the call behind `noroute_policy_adjudication`, so the guard's literal string no longer appears in the arm) — pre-existing, untouched here.
- The dual-FIB live experiment (userspace route withdrawn, kernel route retained, default permit-all + explicit deny ⇒ DROP + deny-event) remains the cluster-level decisive check.

## PR #16358 — ha: anchor fabric rollout grace at persisted first keying (#16027) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16027-tokenless-grace`

Why:
The #11676 fabric rollout grace was anchored at the in-memory
no-key -> key transition in Manager.UpdateConfig. Every xpfd process
start satisfies that transition, so every restart of a long-keyed
node re-opened up to 5 minutes of tokenless read-only fabric RPCs
(GetSessions, interface monitor, safe ShowText) until the peer
authenticated — recurring read-only disclosure to on-segment hosts
with no operator action (A5-14, #16027). Key-touching commits that
changed the accepted set likewise re-anchored in-process.

What:
Persist the first-keyed instant per accepted-key-set digest in
/var/lib/xpf/fabric-auth-grace (cluster/fabric_auth_grace.go):
HMAC-SHA256 over a domain tag keyed by each accepted key, no key
bytes stored. UpdateConfig now anchors on the first keying of the
current set: a restart under an unchanged set restores the persisted
time (backwards-stepped clocks distrust a future stamp, which only
shortens the grace); a changed set re-anchors and still gets its
grace; clearing clears. Persist is best-effort via fsatomic with a
Warn naming the reopened-grace consequence. grpcapi docs updated;
the 5-minute length, read-only set, and arming sources are unchanged.

Validation:
RED on master: pkg/grpcapi TestFabricAuth16027 fails to build
(cluster.SetFabricAuthGraceStatePathForTesting undefined) — the
restart behaviour does not exist. GREEN: grpcapi #16027 + #11676
suites and cluster anchor/UpdateConfig/rotation tests pass
(go vet clean); full pkg/cluster and pkg/grpcapi suites pass.

Risk:
A wiped /var/lib/xpf or a persistently failing anchor write falls
back to anchoring at that apply — indistinguishable from a genuine
new keying; the failure is Warn-logged. Rotation steps that change
the accepted set each get a fresh read-only grace, closed early by
peer authentication as before.

Closes #16027

## PR #16359 — cluster: persist heartbeat epoch latch and floor across restart (#16022) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16022-heartbeat-persist-epoch`

Closes #16022.

The epoch-capable downgrade latch and boot-epoch floor were process-scoped: a receiver daemon restart cleared both, and >=65 captured sender incarnations replayed while the peer was down churned the 64-entry session ring indefinitely (1625/1625 epochless admitted pre-fix), sustaining forged peer liveness and delaying takeover.

## Fix
- Persist latch+floor+per-value session bindings in a key-set-scoped record (/var/lib/xpf/ha-peer-epoch, alongside ha-boot-epoch), digest = controlAuthKeySetDigest over the accepted key set (the #15262 construction).
- Written OFF the accept path: admitAuthed only marks the record owed; a sender-tick flush (10s cadence, 1s retry after failure) plus StopHeartbeat/Manager.Stop flushes write it under the boot-epoch sidecar flock. A failed/wedged write fails open to the pre-#16022 process-scoped behaviour — admission never waits on storage.
- Restored on the boot UpdateConfig apply and again before StartHeartbeat publishes a receiver (no window where an epochless replay meets an unrestored latch). A key-set change drops the restored state; clearing the key set removes the file; a corrupt/mismatched record degrades to the migration window.
- Engages the removed durable-latch pricing rather than ignoring it: no accept-path write, off-path lock, rotation-not-file-edit recovery. The epoch-bearing re-arm after any clearing (residual 5) is unchanged.

## Validation
- go vet ./pkg/cluster/ clean
- go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run 16022 + epoch/latch/rollback/receiver suites pass
- Full pkg/cluster sweep passes

Risk: a crash inside one 10s flush interval loses at most that interval advanc

e (bounded and documented). A deliberately rolled-back peer now needs the PSK rotation rather than a bare restart; the rejection warning already prescribed the rotation first.

## PR #16360 — userspace-dp: demote steering PASS on multi-zone nodes (#16026) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16026-zoneless-steering`

Closes #16026 (A1-C4).

## Mechanism
`UserspaceSessionKey` is a bare 5-tuple with no zone/ifindex/domain. A `PASS_TO_KERNEL` row published for one zone's peer-synced `LocalDelivery` session is honoured at the shim for any packet presenting the same tuple. The normal cross-zone case dies in the nft ingress-scoped host-inbound verdict, but on a shared/ambiguous netdev that re-derivation is impossible and the discarded zone is unrecoverable — a same-tuple UDP packet arriving on the second zone's interface passes to the kernel into the HA peer-synced row.

## Fix
- `ForwardingState::has_multiple_zones` built in `populate_zones` (admitted distinct zone ids; the `has_routing_domains` single-bool shape).
- `uses_kernel_local_session_map_entry` now also requires `!has_multiple_zones`: on a multi-zone node a peer-synced LocalDelivery session is published **REDIRECT** instead of PASS_TO_KERNEL and is judged by the worker's `session_hit_authority` (#9519) by live arrival zone (foreign drop, owner delivered via LocalDelivery). Threaded through every publish callsite. Single-zone deployments are byte-identical.

## Not taken (measured)
A shim-side PASS gate (new `userspace_session_pass_zones` map honoured only for resolvable arrivals, else demote) was implemented and **rejected at the 1M-insn verifier cap** even as one outlined map probe — the tracked shim object has no headroom for another PASS-path lookup. Reverted in full; no .o change, no `make generate` owed. Detail in `docs/log/16026.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16026`: `multiple_zones_demote_kernel_local_to_redirect_16026` (predicate pair; deleting `!has_multiple_zones &&` reds only the demotion assertion) and `the_worker_publish_reads_this_nodes_multiple_zones_flag_16026` (real worker publish path against the SESSION_MAP_WRITES recorder) — pass.
- Main-agent gates still owed: full userspace-dp suite, Go suites.

## Risk
Multi-zone nodes: host-bound peer-synced traffic takes one extra helper hop (safe direction, same as #9517). Single-zone: unchanged.

## PR #16362 — logging: unify raw-event parser behind logEvent/DecodeRawEventRecord (#16127) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16127-logging-parser`

Refs #16127

## Why
`logEvent` (live `Run`/`ProcessRawEvent` path) and `DecodeRawEventRecord` hand-parsed the same 144-byte RT_FLOW offsets with divergent validation and divergent unknown-address-family policy: the live path rendered any non-v6 family as IPv4, the decoder rejected unknown families. Two hand-maintained parsers for one wire shape drift on every wire change (the #16127 narrowed survivor: one zero-extra-allocation parser, explicit family decision, parser-only — fanout untouched).

## What
- `parseRawEvent(data, *rawEvent) bool` — the single offset parser, filling a caller-zeroed `rawEvent` in place (zero allocation, pinned by `TestParseRawEventZeroAlloc16127`); both callers keep their existing `len >= rawEventWireSize` gates.
- `formatRawEventAddrs` — the single address/NAT renderer for both paths.
- **Explicit unknown-family policy: REJECT.** Only `addrFamilyInet` (2) / `addrFamilyInet6` (10) — the only families either producer emits (eBPF `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6`, userspace-dp `libc::AF_INET`/`AF_INET6`) — are accepted. Decoder rejects, live path drops; the former live-only v4 fallback is gone. Documented at `parseRawEvent` and in `pkg/logging/README.md`.
- Live record now carries `Created` on non-close frames (decoder parity; previously close-only — additive, exporters read it on close).
- Golden frames + pins: `pkg/logging/raw_event_parser_16127_test.go` (short / legacy-144 / extended-160 / IPv6 cells, live-vs-decoded field parity, family policy, alloc).
- README + debian/changelog updated.

- `go vet ./pkg/logging/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Fail-on-revert: removing the family gate in `parseRawEvent` makes `TestRawEventFamilyPolicy16127` RED (family 0 accepted); restored green.

## Risk
- A hypothetical producer emitting a non-2/10 family byte (none exists in-tree) would now be dropped live instead of rendered as IPv4 garbage — that rendering was the divergence being removed.
- Non-close live records gain `Created` (wire slot the decoder already surfaced); no consumer reads it off close frames except the REST/SSE forensic surface, where it is now consistent with the decoder.

## PR #16364 — cluster: alarm on a forgotten key rotation past seven days (#16029) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16029-rotation-age-alarm`

**Acceptance (#16029):** rotation open beyond a threshold (days) produces a visible status alarm naming the open rotation. Record rotation-open-since and alarm on age.

**Mechanism:** `UpdateConfig` stamps `Manager.controlLinkRotationOpenedAt` when the additional key's identity changes (digest-keyed on the additional slot only — identical re-applies and signing-key swaps under the same additional key do not move it, so a routine commit cannot launder a forgotten rotation's age; a different additional key re-anchors; clearing it/finalize clears the stamp). `controlLinkRotationStatus` appends the window age (whole days/hours) to every existing peer-state clause, and past `controlLinkRotationStaleAfter` (7 days) appends an `ALARM` naming the window by its accepted key IDs (never key bytes) with the finalize remedy, rendered on the `Key rotation:` line in `show chassis cluster statistics` (CLI + gRPC share `FormatControlPlaneStatistics`). New `ControlLinkRotationOpenSince`/`ControlLinkRotationStale` accessors are the machine-readable half.

**Never auto-finalizes:** retiring a key the peer still signs with reopens the dual-master window (#6630), so the fix prompts the operator commit instead of taking it. The stamp is in-memory and re-anchors at the first apply after a daemon restart — a stale alarm can be up to one restart late, never early; a backwards clock step clamps age to zero rather than alarming early.

**Tests (hermetic, pinned clock, fail-on-revert noted in file):**
- `TestRotationAgeSurvivesRoutineReapply16029` — identical re-apply and signing-swap under the same additional key don't move the stamp.
- `TestRotationWindowIdentity16029` — changed additional key re-anchors; finalize clears; reopening starts fresh.
- `TestStaleRotationAlarmsByName16029` — fresh window: age only, no alarm; just under 7d: no alarm; past 7d: `ALARM ... still accepted ... open for 7d` naming both key IDs, reaching `FormatControlPlaneStatistics`, no key bytes rendered; finalize clears it.

**Validation:** `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run '...16029|TestPSKRotation' -count=1` ok; `go vet ./pkg/cluster/` clean; full `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1` ok (141s).

No lab/HA validation was run; proxied streams continue to die with the origin's primary re-auth, as documented.

## PR #16366 — userspace-dp: intern route tables inside ForwardingState only with dual-carry cell (#16131) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16131-intern-route-tables`

Refs #16131

## Why
The per-address local-delivery attributions in `ForwardingState` (`local_tables_v[46]`, `interface_nat_tables_v[46]`, nested `interface_nat_v[46]`) key owning route tables by canonical table NAME, so the packet path hashes the name string on every local-delivery probe. Interning onto the numeric `RouteIdentity{domain, table}` was proposed as a replacement — but the dissenting review preserved on #16131 (Codex, UNSOUND as a performance cutover) showed that form costs a second hash probe (`&str` → ID) before the membership test: strictly more probes than today's single string-set lookup. The accepted narrowed form is dual-carry only, and only if the agreement cell passes.

## What
- New interned twins inside `ForwardingState` only: `local_table_ids_v[46]`, `interface_nat_table_ids_v[46]` (`FastSet<RouteIdentity>`), `interface_nat_ids_v[46]` (`FastMap<RouteIdentity, i32>`), plus diagnostic `route_table_interning_complete`.
- `forwarding_build::intern::intern_route_tables` derives the twins once per build, immediately after `route_table_identities` is assigned and after every string-form writer (interfaces, late-stage NAT append). Identity is never synthesized: a name with no published identity row is omitted and flips `route_table_interning_complete` false; an incomplete identity map (legacy posture) leaves the twins empty.
- The string carry remains the ONLY form any lookup reads — no packet code reads the twins, so packet-path probe count is unchanged by construction (the dissent's condition). NAT zone interning is excluded (separate W3 allocator-API proposal; `synced_source_nat_zone_pair` is load-bearing for allocator matching + legacy-peer fallback, #6600).
- Dual-carry agreement cell `route_table_dual_carry_agrees`: per address, forward (every carried name's published identity is interned), reverse (every interned identity/ifindex is backed by a carried name of the SAME address — no phantoms), and cardinality. Asserted in the build before publish; a disagreement panics so the reconcile preflight keeps the previous live state (fail closed).

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp dual_carry` — 5/5 pass: hand-built agreement, built-state agreement over a real two-VRF `build_forwarding_state`, and phantom / missing-identity / wrong-ifindex corruption cells.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- forwarding` — 788 passed, 1 failed: `matched_family_pairs_are_still_admitted_7520` fails identically on a clean stash of this head (pre-existing on `ef4e62cad9`, unrelated ICMP family admission).
- iperf witness row: not run — no packet code changed and the issue makes no throughput claim, so no live witness can distinguish this change.

## Risk
Additive build-time derivation only. Memory grows by one small identity set/map per local address. A derivation bug panics the candidate build (fail-closed; previous state stays live) rather than publishing a divergent state.

## PR #16367 — userspace-dp: make GRE/WG frag pool head-only with per-source quota (#16028) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16028-gre-frag-pool`

## Why
#16028 (A1-C6 from #15985): GRE reassembly created a `FragEntry` for ANY fragment — tails included — behind only a tunnel-pair index probe, in one 64-entry pool shared with WireGuard. An attacker knowing/spoofing the configured tunnel peer source could tail-flood (or head-flood) the pool and starve legitimate WG/GRE reassembly for the 10s entry lifetime. The GRE buffer-time gate had no GRE-key, transport-domain, egress, or ingress-zone/host-inbound check.

Refs #16028

## What
- **Head-only creation**: `GreReassembler::offer`/`offer_for_protocol` take `OfferAdmission`. `Head` may create; `Tail` consults only and never creates; admission/offset mismatch is a counted refusal.
- **Per-source sub-quota**: `MAX_GRE_FRAG_DATAGRAMS_PER_SRC = 32` (half the shared 64) per outer source across protocols/ingresses (strictly stronger than per-(src,ingress/proto)), no eviction of other sources' entries.
- **Full GRE head admission**: new `gre::outer_head_admits_gre_endpoint` runs the complete `match_tunnel_endpoint` chain (key read from the head, transport domain, resolved transport egress, ingress host-inbound). Matcher/egress helpers gained `counted` twins redirecting charges to a `GreDecapCounters::scratch()` so probes charge nothing and successful datagrams aren't double-counted; the production decap path is unchanged (`counted=true`). Refused heads are consume-and-counted (`Buffered`), never forwarded as transit.
- WG stage passes Head/Tail by fragment offset; its head gates already include listener/zone/ownership.
- **Intentional trade-off**: a tail arriving before its head is dropped instead of buffered (pre-head tail buffering was the starvation vector). Correctly ordered fragmented tunnel traffic is unaffected. #14645/#15095 tail-first assertions updated to head-then-tail; the wrong-key refusal count is preserved (now charged at head admission).

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- --test-threads=1 16028 14645 15102 15095` → **18 passed** (5 new #16028 tests: tail-only flood creates zero state + legit decaps; GRE head flood capped at 32 with WG completing in the same pool; wrong-key and host-inbound-denied heads create no state, counted once; pool-level quota/consult invariants).
- Broader `gre_ wg_` run: 478 passed, 8 failed — the **identical 8 failures reproduce on unmodified origin/master** (pre-existing).
- `outer_frag`/`poll_descriptor_structure`: 17 passed.

## Risk
Fragmented tunnel datagrams whose tail beats the head (cross-path reordering) now lose that datagram — bounded to the reassembly use case, fail-closed and counted. Two peers behind one NAT source share one 32-entry sub-quota (deliberate: source is the only unspoofable-at-this-layer fair-share key available before decap).

## PR #16368 — api: bound global Basic lockout with successful-verify probe (#16068) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16068-global-basic-lockout`

Closes #16068.

## Why
The #11492 global per-username Basic bucket was reserved before verification (5 failures/10 min → 5 min lockout doubling to 1 h), so anyone who knew a username and could reach an off-loopback web-mgmt leg could re-spray after each expiry and keep the legitimate user locked out of REST Basic auth indefinitely — the decisive pre-fix check (5 bad passwords, then the correct password from another source) was refused with 429.

## What
- When ONLY the global Basic bucket is locked (caller's pair + source buckets clean), admit the attempt as a bounded probe: at most 1 concurrent verify per locked username (`authThrottleGlobalBasicProbes`), still paying full bcrypt cost.
- Successful probe clears-then-admits the global bucket (and its own pair), exactly like a normal clean success.
- Failed probe is charged to its pair/source buckets; `chargeLocked` drops it for the global bucket while locked, so wrong-password probes never extend the deadline.
- Pair/source lockouts remain hard pre-verification refusals — a correct credential from a locked pair/source can never rescue it, preserving the #11492 anti-spray and #10825 bcrypt-CPU caps.
- Tests: `TestRESTAuthGlobalBasicAccountBudgetAcrossSources11492` updated to the decisive 204 check; new `TestRESTAuthGlobalBasicProbeWrongPasswordKeepsLockout16068` and `TestRESTAuthGlobalBasicProbeCapAndPairLockout16068`; `docs/log/16068.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -count=1` passes (98s)
- Targeted throttle suite passes; gofmt/vet clean; `git diff --check` clean

## Risk
Only global-only-locked Basic requests change path (one bounded verify instead of immediate 429). All other lockouts, escalation, the 4096-entry bound, and API-key/Bearer namespaces unchanged.

## PR #16371 — cluster: cap bulk-sync receive window at table capacity (#16039) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16039-bulk-recv-cap`

## Why

Refs #16039. Bulk session-sync receive inserted keys into `bulkRecvV4/V6` before the install verdict, with no capacity cap and no window deadline inside an open bulk window; the sets reset only at BulkEnd/connection teardown. A keyed peer could grow receiver memory entry-by-entry at wire cost for as long as it held the window open. The sibling `bulkInstallFailedV4/V6` marker sets had the same unbounded shape.

## What

- Admission to the receive accumulators runs through `admitBulkRecvV4/V6`, still before the install verdict (a transiently failed key must count as received), but the combined distinct keys across both families may not exceed `bulkRecvCap()` = `maxCap()` — the forward-session table capacity (wired helper capacity when known, else the 200k default, ceiling `conntrack.MaxSessions/2`).
- The first distinct key past the cap invalidates the window: it never reconciles, acks, or releases the failover hold; further keys are counted and dropped without storing. At its BulkEnd the window is torn down and the sender's bounded re-drive re-primes a legitimate bulk.
- The transient-failure marker maps share the same combined cap with the same invalidation.
- A `BulkEnd` arriving more than `bulkRecvWindowTimeout` (1h, far beyond the sender's 35s ack-retry / ~150s daemon prime-retry cadence) after the accepted `BulkStart` aborts the window the same way.
- `reconcileStaleSessions` refuses an invalid window; new state is cleared on reconcile, abort, and full disconnect.
- Counters `BulkRecvCapped` / `BulkRecvAborted` ride `SyncStats` → snapshot → cluster status (rendered when nonzero). No wire change.

## Validation

- New cells in `pkg/cluster/sync_bulk_recv_cap_16039_test.go` (overflow abort + flood + legitimate at-cap completion, deadline abort + in-deadline control, marker-map bound, duplicates/incremental free): pass, including `-race`.
- #12166 bulk-ack regression set (`TestBulkAck*`, `TestBulkTransient*`, `TestBulkInstallFailure*`): pass.
- Full `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1`: pass (128.2s). One earlier full run flaked `TestAncestryReorderedGenerationsDropStalePair10511` (2s apply-callback timing); it passes in isolation on both base and this head, and the clean rerun confirms unrelated load flake.
- `go vet ./pkg/cluster/`, `gofmt -l` on touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.

## Risk

A peer whose legitimate table exceeds the wired capacity now has its bulk aborted instead of installed; the bounded re-drive re-primes once capacity is wired correctly, and the new counters make the condition operator-visible rather than silent memory growth.

## PR #16372 — cluster: refresh peer liveness only on semantic accept with per-type payload caps (#16041) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16041-cluster-liveness`

Refs #16041

Why: In the sync read loop, missedHeartbeats=0 and the last-peer-receive stamp ran for any well-framed frame before handleMessage semantic accept, so junk frames from a keyed peer refreshed liveness and masked a dead peer's failover trigger. There were also no per-type payload caps beyond the global 16MiB bound.

What:
- handleMessage and every receive handler return semantic acceptance (applied, queued, or matched a live waiter/incarnation; stale/malformed/superseded/undecryptable/unknown rejected). receiveLoop refreshes liveness only on acceptance. Retired persistent-NAT types 38/39 deliberately count as accepted (old-peer liveness; ignored by migration design).
- syncPayloadCap (sync_payload_caps_16041.go) gives all 44 dispatched labels encoder-derived caps, enforced in receiveLoop from the header BEFORE payload allocation/read; over-cap counts OversizeFramesRefused (+Errors, rendered in cluster statistics when nonzero) and drops the connection. Unknown types keep only the global cap (forward-compatible, ignored, never liveness). Config and full-set/chunk types keep maxSyncPayload as their per-type cap (encoders chunk below it).
- Updated #16168 census mutations and #6650 source pin for the bool signatures; README + changelog.

Validation: New sync_liveness_caps_16041_test.go drives the real receiveLoop over net.Pipe: rejected frames (unknown type, truncated session, impossible clock, stale DHCP full-set, short acks/caps) do not refresh lastPeerRxMono/PeerHealthy while Barrier/Heartbeat controls do; over-cap headers refuse and drop without a body; cap census covers every dispatched type and conforming encoders fit. Tests pass including -race; full pkg/cluster suite passes (156s); go vet clean.

Risk: A peer whose only traffic is semantically rejected (e.g. duplicate stale-generation installs) no longer refreshes liveness and ages out — intended failover behaviour; heartbeat ACKs remain accepted so healthy peers are unaffected. Failover-ack detail is capped at 4KiB of peer error text (real errors are far below). Mixed-version: new receiver drops over-cap frames from any peer; conforming old senders never emit them.

## PR #16374 — sessions: require exact seq for RST teardown (#16040) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16040-rst-exact-seq`

sessions: require exact seq for RST teardown (#16040)

Why: #16040 (S2-03 leg2, split from #15985, Low residual). `tcp_closing_seq_verdict` returned Valid for any closing segment with `behind < wnd || seq == rcv_nxt`, so an in-window but non-exact RST stamped session teardown for any of ~window blind guesses. Leg1 (foreign/filter-dropped seq-note poisoning) was already fixed by #15947; this PR is leg2 only.

What:
- `tcp_closing_seq_verdict(key, seq, tcp_flags)` now requires exact seq when the RST bit is set (RFC 9293 §3.5.3 / RFC 5961 §3.2: a non-matching RST draws a challenge ACK, never a close). RST|FIN is driven by the RST bit.
- Fold (Opus): the exact target is the ENDPOINT's receive-next, not the firewall-observed send-end. `tcp_rcv_nxt` is the send-end (transmitted high-water, including downstream-lost bytes), so exact-vs-send-end dropped legitimate ACK-derived RSTs in downstream-loss recovery. New `tcp_peer_rcv_nxt`/`tcp_peer_rcv_nxt_seen` state on the sender-direction entry, recorded high-water from the companion direction's ACK field in the `note_tcp_seq_scaled` seam (SYN-ACK ack = ISN+1; bare SYN excluded). RST is Valid iff `seq == tcp_peer_rcv_nxt`; until an endpoint ACK is observed, the RST verdict is Unknown (admitted), never a send-end guess.
- FIN keeps in-window validity; the #15947 receiver (companion) advertised-window logic governs FIN only. `no-sequence-check` still bypasses the verdict. The poll slow-path caller passes `meta.tcp_flags`; the flow-cache fast path still never stamps close.
- Decisive tests: `rst_requires_exact_seq_16040` (full delivery: non-exact RST Invalid, exact Valid, FIN retained); `rst_exact_uses_endpoint_rcv_nxt_not_send_end_16040` (downstream loss 100 sent/50 ACKed: RST@1051 Valid, RST@1101 Invalid; target advances on retransmit-ACK, duplicate ACK does not rewind); updated `in_window_rst_valid_blind_rst_invalid_15753`, `scaled_window_and_receiver_window_verdict_15947`, `rst_seq_validation_in_window_vs_blind_15753`. Docs/changelog updated.

Validation: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- rst_requires_exact_seq_16040 rst_exact_uses_endpoint in_window_rst_valid scaled_window_and_receiver rst_seq_validation seed_tcp_window_scale unilateral_wsopt` — 7/7 pass. Full `session::` module: 506 passed, 1 failed (`session_decision_typed_snat_layout_11064`, SessionDecision 116 vs pinned 112) — fails identically with the fold changes stashed, pre-existing on this head and unrelated. RED (first head): production change stashed with tests kept, the two updated tests fail on the pre-fix verdict. Unit level only; no live cluster run.

Risk: A legitimate RST desynced from the endpoint's ACK-tracked rcv_nxt is dropped instead of closing early; the session ages out on its normal timeout. Before any endpoint ACK is observed, RSTs are admitted (Unknown) as in the legacy no-state posture. FIN, no-sequence-check, and HA-imported (no local ACK state) paths are unchanged in posture.

## PR #16376 — screen: judge ambiguous fabric arrivals under raw and claimed profiles (#16051) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16051-screen-profile-ambiguous`

## Why

Stage 10 (screens + SYN-cookie) runs before any forwarding resolution exists, so it resolved its screen profile from the raw fabric ingress zone alone. On an ambiguous (#15916) arrival — claimed zone withheld pending owner-RG promotion — that skipped the claimed zone's screen profile entirely: the packet was later promoted and admitted under a zone whose stateless screens never ran, and a returning cookie ACK was validated only under the raw zone. RN-04 from the #15985 cohort (validated Low, unanimous MATERIAL).

## What

- `screen_zone_candidates` returns `[raw ingress zone, withheld claimed zone]`, each gated on its own #12875 screen state.
- `stage_screen_check_with_ambiguous` / `stage_screen_syn_cookie_ack_on_session_miss_with_ambiguous` charge the FULL profile (flood/cookie state, counters, challenge, validated-client bypass, ACK validation) to the raw zone only — the peer that minted a cookie screened under it.
- The claimed zone contributes ONLY a stateless veto via new pure `ScreenState::stateless_screen_drop_for_zones` (LAND / TCP-flag / fragment / source-route; #7168 conservative default for an unresolved claimed reference; claimed `alarm-without-drop` = log-only). A claimed Drop recycles at stage 10 (flow + flowless branches) and vetoes even a Validated cookie ACK. It charges no flood sketch, mints no challenge, seeds no bypass — it can only subtract, never admit — so no claimed-zone state exists before owner proof and no premature SYN-ACK is possible (#15947 deferred-challenge final admission still governs replies).
- The #11332 pre-screen input-filter walk runs when either candidate has screen state.
- Non-ambiguous callers pass `ambiguous_zone=None` via the existing wrappers — byte-identical behavior.
- Docs: `docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md` #16051 section, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/README.md`, `docs/log/16051.md`.

## Validation

- `ambiguous_claimed_zone_screen_drop_applies_16051` — decisive regression (issue's check): co-moved ambiguous `lan` stamp, SYN+FIN vs `lan`-only syn-fin profile → screen drop, no session, no forward, no SYN-ACK. Fail-on-revert: withholding `ambiguous_zone` at stage 10 makes the drop 0 and the session installs.

## PR #16378 — login: enforce argument-scoped command regexes on gRPC and REST (#16067) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16067-arg-scoped-commands`

Closes #16067

## Why
Canonical command strings carry no arguments, and both the gRPC and REST gates evaluated only the bare topic/path — so operator-authored argument-scoped regexes like `^ping 10\.99\.`, `^show route table secret-vrf` or `^show log .*` never matched remotely. The restriction the operator believes is enforced was silently inoperative (fail-open) on the remote surfaces.

## What
- **gRPC** (`pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_args_16067.go`): rebuild the full canonicalised command from the decoded request — every packed ShowText topic (route-table/protocol/prefix, log with count, screen statistics/ids-option, CoS name/type, firewall filter/effective, test-policy/routing/zone, applications, class-of-service, interfaces-queue, sessions-top), ShowText filters, Ping/Traceroute targets+options, GetSessions selectors (zone ID resolved via StableZoneIDOwnerForConfig), MatchPolicies selectors, ShowInterfacesDetail filter — and judge it with `EvaluateForms` alongside the argument-free charge. Reconstruction mirrors each handler's decoder; malformed packings/uncanonicalisable strings/unresolvable zones deny for restricted classes.
- **REST** (`pkg/api/authz_command_args_16067.go`): same reconstruction for show-text topics, diagnostics ping/traceroute bodies, session/match query selectors, interfaces/detail. REST show-text topics now resolve through the same longest-prefix rule as gRPC (previously plain map indexing denied every packed topic for restricted classes).
- **Advisories** (`pkg/config/login_command_surface_args_16067.go`): surfaces register argument-sample exemplars; the commit-time unenforceability advisory, per-alternative advisory and the once-per-class runtime warning now derive witnesses from the operator's pattern (literal spelling extending a registered command; unanchored literal segment occupying a proven argument slot) judged by the real compiled rules, so an argument-scoped pattern that fires remotely is no longer reported on-box-only. Witnesses are gated on registered samples, so fake/unproven surfaces keep the prior advisory (fake-surface #9340/#8189 tests unchanged and passing).
- Rewrote `TestArgumentLevelDenyIsOnBoxOnly7172` to assert the closed agreement; updated #11678 REST advisory test; docs (`docs/system-login.md`, `pkg/grpcapi/README.md`), gate/topic header prose, changelog.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run 'TestArgument|TestUnenforceable|TestMalformedPacked'` — decisive cells: deny `^show route table secret-vrf$` denies `route-table:secret-vrf` and allows `public-vrf`; `^ping 10\.99\.`, `^show log .*`, screen/test-policy/test-routing/route-prefix/session-zone/match-policies/interfaces-filter shapes deny; allow-exception `^show log messages 100$` lifts `^show log$` for that spelling only; malformed packed topics deny.
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -run 'TestArgumentScoped|TestRESTArgumentScoped'` — REST twins of the above.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestArgumentSamples|TestNoSamples|TestUnenforceable|TestCombinedDeny|TestWholeUnenforceable|TestPartialAdvisory'`.
- Main agent should run the full `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/api`, `pkg/config`, `pkg/cli` suites plus vet before merge (targeted runs above are green).

## Risk
Restricted classes may now be denied on requests whose arguments cannot be reconstructed (malformed packed topics, unresolvable zone IDs) where they previously passed on the bare path — fail-closed by design, matching the existing unmapped-command rule. Unrestricted classes are unaffected (the gate returns before reconstruction). Advisory witnesses only suppress warnings when a proven argument slot exists, never invent one.

## PR #16379 — nat: quarantine freed PAT ports on small pools (#16035) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16035-pat-quarantine`

Refs #16035

Why: free_recycle cleared the occupancy bit and FIFO-recycled the port immediately, so on a tiny/high-churn pool a delayed UDP reply reusing (translated_ip, port, remote) could land on a new owner of the same port. Large pools were already de-facto quarantined by FIFO-after-fresh-range reuse; TCP endpoints reject stray segments by sequence state.

What: stamp each recycle token with its monotonic free time and, for ranges <=256 ports, refuse to claim a token (via both the keyed probe and the recycled phase) until 60s after the free, retaining it with its original stamp. Production flow frees (release/rollback/unlink/allocation give-backs) thread now_ns into the stamp; lease-retention frees (expiry GC, persistent clear) stay unstamped because the lease already held the port for its full timeout. Retained tokens requeue without tripping the dedup bitset. Existing small-pool fixtures that pinned instant reuse now claim at post-quarantine times or use >256-port pools where they measured allocator mechanics, not reuse timing.

Validation: new tests_16035 cells (tiny-pool UDP quarantine + boundary reuse, TCP control, large-pool no-quarantine, recycled-phase token retention) pass; full nat:: suite 755 passed / 0 failed on rerun.

Risk: small pools under sustained churn can exhaust during the 60s window where they previously reused instantly - that refusal is the fix. Large pools, deterministic claim_in_block, and reserve paths are untouched.

Branch: `fix/16045-nat-fabric-zone`

## Summary
For an ambiguous fabric arrival (#15916 — claimed zone withheld pending the owner-RG gate), pre-routing NAT resolved its scope from the LOCAL fabric/logical identity (fabric interface zone / config name / routing-instance) and could select a translation under that identity. The session-miss policy later promoted the claimed zone, so the translated action was keyed to a zone the policy never adjudicated (RN-01).

Fix direction per the validated refutation in #16045: suppress the fabric fallback identity only; never grant the claimed zone before owner proof.

- `PreroutingIngressScope` gains `ambiguous_provenance`; `prerouting_ingress_scope_ambiguous` resolves the same local identity stamped ambiguous (claimed zone and V2 peer scope ifindex never substituted). Flow-backed miss and flowless pre-routing paths both stamp it.
- NAT-layer ambiguous-provenance siblings (ordinary matchers untouched): pool DNAT -> Poisoned fail-closed (needs the winner's scope tier, so `DnatOutcome::Translate` now carries it), static DNAT withholds, NPTv6 -> Untranslatable, NAT64 -> MatchUnavailable; the persistent-NAT reader is skipped (ingress-keyed lease scope).
- UNSCOPED rules still fire (identity-independent), native owner-scope ingress unchanged, session-hit revalidation untouched.

## Decisive regression (co-moved owner fixture)
`*_16045` in `poll_descriptor/prerouting_scope_tests.rs`: fabric-scoped DNAT cannot fire prematurely; native `fabric`-zone ingress still translates; claimed-zone DNAT stays withheld; unscoped DNAT still translates; interface-scoped static, NAT64 and NPTv6 legs.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16045`: 7/7. RED-on-revert verified for the NAT64/NPTv6 legs (fail on clean master code). Note: in the poll harness the DNAT/static legs are broker-gated (session installs via the fabric-link binding end in MissingNeighbor), so the DNAT invariant is additionally pinned at the NAT-table tri-state; see `docs/log/16045.md`.
- `nat::` suite: 751 pass. Fabric zone-stamp suite: 66 pass.
- Three `prerouting` VLAN failures reproduce identically on clean master (pre-existing, unrelated).

## Risk
Fail-closed only: ambiguous arrivals with scope-constrained pre-routing NAT now drop/withhold instead of translating under the fallback identity. Unscoped and validated flows are byte-identical.

## PR #16381 — userspace-dp: resolve PPTP data channel in claimed fabric domain (#16055) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/issue-16055`

## userspace-dp: resolve PPTP data channel in claimed fabric domain (#16055)

Fixes #16055 (RN-06).

### Why
The PPTP association table is domain-keyed, and associations are installed in the domain of the control flow that taught them — the domain stage 9b stamps from the claimed fabric identity (`ingress_zone_override.or(ambiguous_zone)`). The data-channel resolve instead derived its domain from the ingress interface plus the *validated* zone override only. On an ambiguous fabric arrival the two differ by construction: the claimed zone has no `zone_routing_domain` row, so stage 9b keys the flow in the per-zone quarantine band (`AMBIGUOUS_FABRIC_DOMAIN_BASE | zone`) while the resolve consulted the fabric link's own domain. The claimed tenant's association was missed, and a same-call-ID association in the wrong domain was claimed and idle-refreshed instead — the wrong-domain association refresh the issue names. (At the original evidence base the drift was narrower — override-only vs. the later ambiguous promotion in #15916 — but the invariant "resolve domain == install/re-key domain" is the same.)

### What
- New `pptp_resolve_routing_domain` helper in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`: fabric arrivals resolve via the claimed zone (validated or ambiguous); a fabric arrival with **no** claimed zone fails closed to domain 0 instead of falling through to the fabric link's ifindex domain; the absent-stamp suspect arm stays domain 0; non-fabric arrivals keep the physical-ingress derivation unchanged.
- The descriptor-loop PPTP resolve calls the helper (replacing the ingress-only derivation).
- Decisive regression cells in `pptp_domain_16055_tests.rs`, plus `debian/changelog` and `docs/log/16055.md`.

### Validation
- `pptp_domain_16055`: **5 passed** (pinned toolchain, release, `--test-threads=1`) on head `92b897008f`.
- Decisive check from the issue: same endpoint pair + same call IDs installed in the claimed (quarantine) domain and in domain 0; a fabric-arrival packet resolves to the claimed domain's handle, keys there, and idle-refreshes **only** that association (the wrong-domain row expires on schedule). A control cell resolving in the pre-fix domain claims the wrong tenant, proving the fixture distinguishes the defect.
- Mutation: reverting the helper's fabric arm to the pre-fix expression reds the claimed-domain and refresh cells (verified).
- Broader `pptp` filter: 99 passed, 1 failed — `pptp_open_frame_carries_the_call_id_pair_13965` fails **identically on unmodified master** (verified via stash); pre-existing, unrelated.

### Risk
Fabric-arrival PPTP packets whose peer encoded no zone stamp now resolve in domain 0 rather than the fabric link's ifindex domain; such arrivals carry no tenant identity, and domain 0 is the same fail-closed answer the suspect arm already gives. Non-fabric and single-instance (`has_routing_domains = false`) paths are bit-identical to before.

## PR #16384 — sessions: validate handshake ack numbers at all completion gates (#16042) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16042-handshake-ack`

## Why
Refs #16042 (S2-05 from #15985). Handshake promotion/completion keyed on flags + `handshake_pending`/`is_reverse` only — no ack-number check. A wrong-ack SYN-ACK could promote a pair, and a wrong-ack completing segment could clear `handshake_pending` and move both halves onto the long established window without the peer ever answering correctly.

## What
ACK-number validation at **all** completion gates: a segment promotes/completes only when its parsed ack equals the companion direction's ISN + 1 (wrapping; a SYN consumes one sequence number).

- `SessionEntry.tcp_peer_isn` tracks each direction's SYN ISN — learned by `note_tcp_seq` on SYN/SYN-ACK, seeded onto both halves at install by `seed_tcp_isn` (companion resolved through `reverse_session_key`, so SNAT/DNAT/NAT64 alias pairs validate identically). The poll path seeds it at all five install sites next to the existing WSOPT seed.
- Gates gated: lookup SYN-ACK promotion, lookup completing-ACK (SYN-first and SYN-ACK-first), fused `probe_hit` (incl. deferring variant), flow-cache keepalive, deferred-Owner replay, and the `update_session`/`promote_synced_with_origin` twin. The ack is threaded via `SessionQuery`, `SessionUpdate`, `DeferredSyncedPromotion`, the resolve/promote plumbing, and the poll/flow-cache call sites that parse the frame (`pending_tcp_seq_note`, `extract_tcp_seq_ack_window`).
- **Unknown evidence fails open, never closed**: companion ISN unobserved (mid-stream pickup), HA import (imports carry no ISN — fail-closed there would strand failover sessions), or unparsed ack → flags-only, exactly as before, bounded by the opening window.
- Companion resolution uses the non-counting `revalidation_record` resolver so ordinary hits don't perturb the #7919 lookup-miss counters (two counter/alias regressions in the first cut, caught and fixed).

Partial prior edits on this branch were audited: the broken `note_tcp_seq_scaled` truncation was restored, and the seed/expected-ack helpers were rewritten to resolve through the canonical record.

## Tests
New `handshake_ack_16042_tests.rs` — 12 tests, all passing, fail-on-revert (dropping any gate's `ack_valid` conjunct turns its bad-ack test red):
- bad-ack SYN-ACK never promotes / correct-ack promotes-but-stays-pending (lookup)
- bad-ack completing ACK never completes, then correct ack completes (lookup)
- wraparound: server ISN `u32::MAX` expects ack 0
- SYN-ACK-first: reverse completing ACK validated
- cached-hit (`probe_hit` + deferring variant) and keepalive gates
- `update_session` and `promote_synced_with_origin` gates
- NAT SNAT alias companion validated
- HA import unknown-evidence fails open (arbitrary ack and unparsed ack both complete)
- deferred-Owner replay gate

Fixture fix: `tests_session_hit_authority_9519` ACK-bearing frames hardcoded ack=0; they now carry ack=2 (acking the fixture SYN seq=1). Suite 29/29.

Full-suite note: 83 failures on this branch, reproduced identically on the base head via stash (e.g. `session_decision_typed_snat_layout_11064`, `in_window_rst_valid_blind_rst_invalid_15753`, event-stream golden trailers) — pre-existing, untouched by this change.

## Risk
Only positively-wrong acks are newly refused, and they stay on the opening window. Mid-stream pickups, HA imports, and frame-less callers are byte-identical to before. Hot path: one companion probe on handshake-pending hits / install seeding only; established hits pay one Option check.

## PR #16387 — api: bind REST config-session token to minting principal (#16069) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16069-rest-session-bind`

## Why
The REST config-session token was validated by format only (`restConfigSessionID` checked the `rest-` prefix + 32 hex chars). The store holder was the bare token string and the principal was recorded only for journal attribution, so any equally-privileged insider who obtained another operator's 128-bit token could set, commit, confirm, or release (exit) that operator's candidate. The gRPC twin never had the hole because its holder is the kernel connection identity (`conn-*`). Validated severity Low: attribution/workflow integrity, not privilege gain — the second principal still needs `PermConfig` and commit-time adjudication runs for the committing class.

## What
- `POST /config/enter` records a server-derived binding key (source, UID, username, class/superuser) for the authorized principal alongside the token in a mutex-guarded `Server` map (`restSessions`, lazily allocated so `&Server{store: ...}` fixtures need no setup).
- `restConfigSessionID` (now a `Server` method) verifies on **every** holder-scoped follow-up — enter re-entry, exit, set, delete, activate, deactivate, load, rollback, annotate, commit, commit-confirmed, confirm — that the presenting principal matches the minting principal, denying with **403** before the store is called. A missing principal also fails closed with 403.
- Exit unbinds on successful release; a successful re-enter rebinds so a stale-lease reclaim takeover cannot strand the new holder or keep the old owner working.
- Sessions entered directly in the store (CLI/gRPC/internal/test fixtures) carry no REST binding and remain gated solely by the store holder check, matching the `conn-*` contract.
- Regression test `TestRESTConfigSessionBoundToPrincipal16069`: mints as principal A (credential `alice`, class `ops`), stages, then presents A's token as principal B (`bob`, same class) and requires 403 on set / re-enter / commit / exit with candidate and lock untouched and the commit callback never invoked, while A's own set/re-enter/commit/exit and a freshly minted token behave correctly. Pre-fix every B operation succeeded.
- Fixed `enterRESTConfigSession` test helper to install the authorized principal on fresh enters (the middleware does this in production).
- Changelog entry added.

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/api/` — clean.
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -run 'TestRESTConfigSessionBoundToPrincipal16069|TestRESTConfigSessionsAreMutuallyExcluded'` — PASS.
- Full `pkg/api` suite: 23 failures, all verified to fail identically on the unmodified base (`git stash` A/B) — NAT metrics commit-check zone fixtures, a doc-guard path check, and a mutation-guard body-read count. None in the config-session surface.

## Risk
Low. The binding lives only in the REST layer; CLI, gRPC, HA-sync, and internal store callers are untouched. A principal whose identity changes mid-session (credential rotation to a different identity) must re-enter — intended fail-closed behavior. In-memory bindings do not survive a daemon restart, after which tokens are unbound and the store holder check alone gates — the pre-fix posture, not a regression.

Closes #16069

## PR #16388 — config: warn that interactive-commands has no emitter (#16075) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16075-interactive-commands`

## Why

The `interactive-commands` syslog facility is accepted and rendered (mapped to local7 in `pkg/logging`), but no code emits a per-command record to it — there is no slog or syslog producer in CLI dispatch. An operator configuring Junos-style command audit via `interactive-commands` on a syslog host/file/user destination gets an empty file/collector bucket and false assurance that CLI activity is audited. Non-destructive verbs (clear/test/show) are also unjournalled. Validated Low (MGMT-08, unanimous MATERIAL) at master `c1b86e871b`.

## What

`ValidateConfig` (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go`) now emits one warning per distinct syslog destination (host, file, or user) that names the `interactive-commands` facility, stating that xpf emits no per-command record to the facility (local7), that the destination will receive no CLI audit records, and that the commit journal records commits/destructive actions with principal but does not journal non-destructive verbs.

The warning is warn-only (never a reject), matching the #7146 syslog archive advisory: a hard reject would fail the tolerant load / peer-sync path on a config an operator already has (the #1960 brick-on-upgrade shape). Because `runTailGates` folds `ValidateConfig` into `cfg.Warnings`, the warning reaches both the strict-commit surface (printed by `printConfigWarnings`) and the show/validate surface.

New tests in `pkg/config/syslog_interactive_commands_16075_test.go` pin warnings for file/host/user destinations, once-per-destination dedup when the facility appears in multiple selectors, and silence for other facilities and absent syslog.

NOT changed: no per-command emitter was implemented. A real audit producer would need principal/verb/result plumbing through both the in-process and remote CLI surfaces plus flood control — a feature, not this bounded fix; the issue's fix shape allows either, and the warning is the honest minimum. The commit journal already covers commits and destructive verbs with principal.

## Validation

- `go build ./...` — rc 0
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` — rc 0
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestInteractiveCommands|TestSyslog' -count=1` — PASS (5 new cells green)
- Full `pkg/config` suite exceeds the 300s runner cap in this environment; the `TestValidate*` IPsec/NAT failures observed in a filtered run were reproduced identically on the stashed base at `a142c34` (pre-existing, base-attributed).

## Risk

Operators who already configured `interactive-commands` now see one extra commit warning per destination. No dataplane, apply, or rendering behavior changes.

Closes #16075

## PR #16390 — config: gate CommitCheck on the config-lock holder (#16070) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16070-holderless-commitcheck`

## Issue
Closes #16070 (A8-10 from #15987)

## Why
`CommitCheck` on both surfaces ran with no holder check: gRPC discarded its context (`_ context.Context`), REST ignored the request entirely (`_ *http.Request`), and `Store.CommitCheck` compiled the shared candidate under `RLock` with no holder parameter or admission limiter. Any PermConfig non-holder could obtain compile diagnostics about another session's staged candidate and trigger repeatable full compiles (CPU) at will.

## What
- **pkg/configstore**: `CommitCheckAs(sessionID)` verifies the config-lock holder via `ensureHolderLocked` under the read lock before any compile — a non-holder gets `ErrConfigLockedByOther` with no diagnostics leak and no compile cost. Every form takes the single-slot fail-fast `commitCheckSem` admission semaphore; a second concurrent check returns `ErrCommitCheckBusy` instead of queueing another full compile. `CommitCheck()` remains the internal/system form (`""` bypass, admission still bounded) for the in-process CLI and the event engine, which holds the lock itself.
- **pkg/grpcapi**: `CommitCheck` passes `connSessionID(ctx)` to `CommitCheckAs`; `configMutationStatus` maps `ErrCommitCheckBusy` → `codes.ResourceExhausted` (holder conflict stays `PermissionDenied`).
- **pkg/api**: `configCommitCheckHandler` requires the `X-Config-Session` header via `restConfigSessionID` (missing/malformed → 400 before the store, closing the `""` internal bypass), passes the holder identity to `CommitCheckAs`; `writeConfigMutationError` maps busy → 429, holder conflict → 409. Compile diagnostics (400) still reach the holder.
- The #9889 candidate-reading census guard now names `CommitCheckAs`.

## Validation
- New RED-on-revert pins: `pkg/configstore/commit_check_holder_16070_test.go` (non-holder/holder/internal + busy slot), `pkg/grpcapi/commit_check_holder_16070_test.go` (PermissionDenied / ResourceExhausted), `pkg/api/commit_check_holder_16070_test.go` (missing header 400, non-holder 409 with no leak, holder 200 + real ebpf diagnostic only for the holder).
- Full `pkg/grpcapi` (incl. #9889 census, #6515/#8484 advisory) and `pkg/api` suites pass; focused `pkg/configstore`/`pkg/cli`/`cmd/cli` suites pass; `-race` on the new admission paths passes; `go vet` clean.
- The pre-existing REST commit-check ebpf test now supplies a well-formed session header (its candidate is held by the internal no-holder enter, admitted via the documented no-holder bypass).

## Risk
Fail-closed only: non-holders lose diagnostics they should never have had, and a second concurrent commit-check gets a retryable busy error instead of a queued compile. Admitted callers' response shapes are unchanged.

## PR #16391 — daemon: re-resolve console login class on config change (#16071) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16071`

Closes #16071

## Why
`applyCLILoginClass` ran exactly once at daemon start, so the in-process console's user→class **assignment** went stale until restart — while class *definitions* were already re-read per command (`resolveClassPerms` reads `ActiveConfig()` every call) and remote surfaces resolve per-connection server-side. Revoking or changing a console user's class lagged until restart: the same revocation-lag class #9051 fixed for streams.

## What
- `pkg/daemon/cli_rbac.go`: new `consoleClassRefresher` — compares only the `system login` projection (`LoginConfig` pointer + `LoginDroppedByPacking`) against the seeded startup projection and re-runs the shared `applyCLILoginClass` resolution when it changes. Covers: re-class, user removal (→ `unauthorized`), first login stanza appearing, stanza removed (→ back to unset legacy mode), dropped-by-packing (fail-closed re-resolution). Unrelated applies are a no-op (no re-log spam).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go`: wires the refresher via `shell.SetRefreshUserClassFn(consoleClassRefresher(shell, d.store.ActiveConfig, osident.Current()))` right after the startup resolution.
- `pkg/cli`: `userClass` is now mutex-guarded; `UserClass()` is the sole read path (it can change while commands dispatch). `SetRefreshUserClassFn` + dispatch/completion-entry refresh hook (no-op when unwired, so standalone/test shells are unchanged).
- Canaries updated: `allowedSetUserClassCallers` gains `daemon::consoleClassRefresher` (required entry); the shared-resolver canary accepts the delegated shape (delegates to `applyCLILoginClass`, only direct write is the empty-class clear); the #6706 wiring test now pins exactly two `applyCLILoginClass` sites, both fed by `osident.Current()`.
- Docs: `docs/system-login.md` console section + `debian/changelog`.

## Validation
- New `TestConsoleClassRefresher16071` (7 rows: revoked / re-classed / first-stanza / stanza-removed / dropped-by-packing / unrelated-apply-no-op / no-login-never-set) + nil-active guard — passes, including under `-race`.
- Existing `TestApplyCLILoginClass*`, `TestConsoleLoginClassIsWiredToOsidentCurrent_6706`, `TestSetUserClassHasOneProductionCaller_6701`, `TestSetUserClassCallersResolveThroughTheSharedResolver_6701` pass; `go vet ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Full `go test -tags=unit ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/daemon/`: remaining failures are pre-existing on `origin/master` (verified against a pristine base worktree; identical failure sets apart from timing).

## Risk
A console user revoked mid-session loses access on their next command (the intended behavior). Deployments with no `system login` stanza are byte-identical — the class is never set. Refresh cost is one projection comparison per dispatch; no per-command config walk.
