## PR #16407 — config: share three config-lifecycle helpers only (#16156) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `u16156-config-helpers`

Closes #16156.

## Why
The confirm-only branch (`IsConfirmPending() && !IsDirty()`) was triplicated across gRPC (`pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go`), REST (`pkg/api/config.go`) and local CLI (`pkg/cli/cli_config.go`); the REST commit-error classifier mirrored the gRPC `commitApplyStatus` by hand (#5742/#15281); and `cfg.Warnings` extraction was open-coded in three places. A fix on one surface could silently diverge on the others.

## What
Exactly three shared helpers in `pkg/configstore` (`commit_helpers_16156.go`), per the narrowed W2.5 form validated in #16156:

- `Store.ConfirmOnly()` — the pure confirm-only predicate (confirm-pending && candidate unchanged). Pure strengthening: both flags are now read under **one** store lock hold instead of two separate RLock holds, so a concurrent edit can no longer land between the reads and route a dirty candidate into the confirm-only branch (the #4000 silent-drop hazard). No authority is minted; each surface keeps its own `ConfirmCommitAs` call.
- `ClassifyCommitError(compiled, err)` — the structural (compiled, err) commit-error class (`Canceled` / `DeadlineExceeded` first, then committed-tail vs rejected, fail-safe to rejected). gRPC `commitApplyStatus` and REST `writeCommitError` now only map the shared class onto their own wire codes/envelopes; human-readable text is byte-identical.
- `WarningsOf(cfg)` — nil-safe defensive-copy extraction of `cfg.Warnings`, replacing grpcapi `configWarnings` (deleted) and both open-coded copies in pkg/api.

Explicitly **not** done (per the B-codex dissent adopted in #16156): no `configops.Service`, no three-surface `CommitGate(store, session) -> authority`. REST/gRPC still mint holder-epoch authority via `AuthorizeCommitAs` before the gate; the local CLI still commits authority-free with its possibly-empty internal session — that path is untouched.

## Acceptance (issue decisive check)
- 12-cell table: `TestConfirmOnly16156` pins confirm-pending × dirty at the store; per-surface cells (`TestRESTBareCommitConfirmOnly16156`, `TestGRPCBareCommitConfirmOnly16156`, existing CLI `TestBareCommitDuringConfirmWindow*_4000`) pin confirm-only vs fall-through commit per surface. CLI authority-free path is unchanged (predicate only).
- Classifier differential REST-vs-gRPC over the #5742 corpus: both surfaces now consume the single `ClassifyCommitError`; the existing `TestCommitErrorClassification_5742` (gRPC) and `TestRESTCommitErrorClassification_15281` (REST) corpora stay green, plus `TestClassifyCommitError16156` pins the shared classifier directly including context-beats-config precedence.
- Byte-identical operator output: no wire code, message, or printed text changes (classifier/warnings helpers only move the shared logic).

## Validation
- New: `TestConfirmOnly16156`, `TestClassifyCommitError16156`, `TestWarningsOf16156`, `TestRESTBareCommitConfirmOnly16156`, `TestRESTCommitResponseWarnings16156`, `TestGRPCBareCommitConfirmOnly16156` — all pass.
- Mutant-checked: dropping the dirty conjunct from `ConfirmOnly` reds the new cells.
- Existing suites green: 5742/15281 classifier, 4000 confirm-window (configstore + CLI), 6515/8484/9841 warnings transport. `go vet` clean on the four touched packages.
- Note: `Test9880_StrictCommitAcceptsValuedModifiers` (pkg/configstore) fails identically on clean `origin/master` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
Low. Pure refactor onto shared helpers; the only semantic delta is the atomic single-lock confirm predicate, which strictly narrows the #4000 race. Fail-safe preserved: unclassifiable commit errors still classify as rejected (400 / InvalidArgument), never committed/retryable.

The wide dependency also made the collector's real inputs invisible at its type.

## What

- New `collectorDeps` seam (`pkg/api/metrics_collector_deps.go`): only what the collector reads — live objects (`store`, `dp`, `fwdSampler`, `eventBuf`, `gc`, `dhcp`, `startTime`), the two REST conn-gate accessors as closures (they keep reading the atomically loaded `connGate` installed after the Server literal in `NewServer`), and every optional daemon hook copied verbatim from the Server field of the same name (nil = family omitted, identical contract).
- `collectorDepsFromServer` snapshots the fields once at collector construction in `NewServer` — before serving; copying pointers (not pointees) preserves the old visibility (live config via `store.ActiveConfig`, live sampler/gate state), matching the lifetime the `c.srv` reads already assumed.
- `xpfCollector.srv` → `deps collectorDeps`; **zero `c.srv` accesses remain** under `pkg/api`. `activeConfig()` collapses the repeated `srv == nil || srv.store == nil` guards.
- Test literals that built `&xpfCollector{srv: &Server{...}}` now build `deps: collectorDeps{...}` directly; the #15086 panic-recovery fixture forces its panic through a panicking deps hook instead of a nil srv.

## Validation

- New decisive `pkg/api/metrics_collector_deps_16157_test.go`: reflection pin that no `srv`/`*Server` field returns to `xpfCollector`; nil-server → zero deps + nil `activeConfig`; `newCollector` bridging of store/startTime/hooks/conn-gate accessors (incl. bare-server 0 counts).
- Targeted seam, `TestMetricsLaneCollectRecoversPanic15086`, descriptor-coverage / FwdStatus / policy-counter tests pass; `go vet ./pkg/api/` and `gofmt -l pkg/api/` clean.
- Full `go test ./pkg/api/ -count=1`: failure set identical to pristine base (23 pre-existing NAT config-fixture failures, verified by stash comparison before/after).

## Risk

Low. No metric name, help, label, or value changes. Only timing change is the one-time deps snapshot before serving. One edge: `emitDataplaneSafety` on a plain-nil dp now returns no samples instead of panicking through `dataplane.Unwrap` (previously recovered only via the #15086 lane).

## PR #16463 — userspace-dp: route activation-pending HA sets to the locked path (#16382) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `wt-16382`

Refs #16382. The #16217 fabric-adoption stack this was diagnosed alongside remains open/unmerged; this is the standalone #16382 lease-publication leg on current master.

Why: live D31 instrumentation at the adoption gate showed the servicing workers' cached RG1 triple stuck at (active=false, lease=Inactive) with the fresh forwarding_active_rgs set EMPTY for seconds after RG1 reported active in the status view. Root cause is in try_refresh_ha_leases: for a mixed watchdog set (siblings matching, one RG activation-pending stored-inactive/incoming-active) the pending RG was kept inactive but the whole set still stored with refreshed>0, so the activation was neither published by the locked path (no epoch bump, RefreshOwnerRGS, prewarm) nor servable later.

What: try_refresh_ha_leases now returns NeedsLock for the whole set whenever any RG is activation-pending (stored inactive, incoming active), regardless of sibling matches - exactly the routing the pure-activation case (refreshed==0) already had. Activations are therefore published only by Coordinator::update_ha_state with its transition side effects, and no later tick can launder a pending activation into a match-arm lease mint. Demotion arms unchanged: stored-active mismatch still mints only while the stored lease is valid, expired stored-active is never resurrected.

Validation: new mixed_set_activation_pending_needs_lock_16382 (mixed RG0/RG1/RG2 set routes NeedsLock twice, RG1 never mints; FAIL-ON-REVERT) and mixed_set_no_activation_still_served_16382 control; cargo test 16382 2/2, 9629 29/29. Live aged P4 acceptance NOT re-run for this standalone commit; it remains the #16217 lane's gate (the same fix plus Wire30 still failed live there, residual narrowed to the per-worker snapshot visibility race - this fix removes the fast-path laundering, it does not by itself claim the aged-failover cure).

Risk: watchdog sets containing a pending activation now take the control socket until the locked path lands the transition; steady-state matching sets stay on the session fast path (control test). This deliberately trades one throttled control round-trip for fail-closed activation publication.

## Summary

Stage-A only (#16194): one test-only `load_subject(name, path)` helper in `scripts/lib/load_subject.py` replaces the repeated `spec_from_file_location` scaffolding in script tests. Zero `spec_from_file_location` call sites remain outside the helper.
- **Helper cells** (`scripts/lib/test_load_subject.py`, 9 cells): hyphenated load + identity, dataclass subject, self-import, exec-failure propagation + cleanup, prior-registration restore, missing-file `ImportError`, repeat-load replacement, fresh `-I` interpreter loading the real `close_keyword_lint` dataclass subject (per-file process isolation, as `run-selftests.sh` runs them), and original CLI invocation of a hyphenated subject by path in a subprocess.
- **Gate wiring**: `scripts/lib/test_*.py` added to `run-selftests.sh` §3, `selftest-census.sh` `PY_GLOBS` (+ its fixture in `selftest-census-selftest.sh`), and the #9669 main-guard scan — so the new test cannot accumulate unreached the way #7296/#15241 files did.
- Changelog entry. Net: 635 insertions / 581 deletions across 90 files (tracked test files alone: −168 lines net after the per-file 2-line bootstrap; the helper + its cells are new).

## Validation

- All 82 migrated test files executed: **80 pass**; the 2 failures are pre-existing and **identical on unmodified base `6235ac734e`** (verified in a detached base worktree): `scripts/dist/test_dist_resign_9920.py` (`test_all_cargo_recipes_use_pinned_toolchain`, 1 cell) and `test/incus/fairness_multi_sample_test.py` (3 harness-precheck cells). Neither touches a loader path.
- `scripts/lib/test_load_subject.py`: 9/9 pass. Confirmed the registration is load-bearing: loading `close_keyword_lint.py` without registration raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'`; with the helper it loads.
- `scripts/selftest-census.sh` passes (95 python files guarded, all tracked `scripts/*test*.py` covered); `test/incus/selftest-census-selftest.sh` 24/24; `test_selftest_main_guard_9669.py` and `test_selftest_lint_coverage_6499.py` pass; `git diff --check` clean; all touched files byte-compile.

The proposed `genGuard` struct name was **not** used: it collides with the #9915 cap counters `genGuardMapCap`/`genGuardMapDefaultCap`/`genGuardSessionCap`, which keep their names. The domains are `sessionGenState` (field `genState`) and `peerSnapshotState` (field `peerSnaps`), pinned by an AST test that no cluster type is named `genGuard*`.

## What moved
- `sessionGenState`: `genCounter`, `genSentMu`+sender stamps/scoped/overflow, `sentGenGuardCap`/`recvGenGuardCap`/`genGuardSessionCap`/`genGuardMapCeilingOverride`/`testGenCapAfterCeilingRead`, sent+recv identity memos, `recvGenMu`+receiver maps/scoped/tombstone orders.
- `peerSnapshotState`: `peerIPsecSAs(Mu)`, `peerDHCPLeases{4,6}` + snapshots + `RecvAt` + `peerDHCPLeasesMu`, and the #6650 `peerSnapshotProtocol`/`peerSnapshotProtocolWriteMu`/`peerSnapshotProtocolGeneration` triple.

Added the lock-order graph on `SessionSync` in `sync.go`: every mutex, its guard domain, every nesting edge (`bulkSnapshotGenMu -> genSentMu -> recvGenMu`, `applyMu -> recvGenMu`, `mu -> peerSnapshotProtocolWriteMu/fenceAckMu`, full-set `*ApplyMu -> recvSeqMu -> peerDHCPLeasesMu`, leaf locks, atomics), pinned by `TestSessionSyncLockOrderGraphPinned16159` so it cannot rot silently.

## PR #16883 — frr: restore per-QNH RIP metrics via offset-lists (#12531) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/12531-campaign`

Why:
RIP received only its default metric for QNH-redistributed routes while OSPF got the configured per-next-hop metric. FRR 10.7.1 offers no working ripd route-map transport: daemon-scoped `vtysh -d ripd -f` silently applies nothing, integrated loads broadcast the set-metric action to other daemons, and ripd ignores route-map `set metric` for redistributed statics even when present (live-verified: map readback metric 7, RIP database and RIPv2 wire metric 1).

What:
Deliver the RIP QNH metric with ripd-native offset-lists inside the integrated `router rip` stanza: one offset-list (offset = metric-1, clamped to wire metric 16; metric 0 renders none) per QNH destination, selected by a generated `xpf-qnh-rip-*` access-list that permits exactly that destination. ACL definitions render beside the QNH prefix-lists, gated on a bare-static RIP export in the scope; policy-exported RIP keeps authored policy semantics. OSPF overlay, shared metric-free QNH map, and cleanup are unchanged. Deliberate scope cut: no next-hop/interface discrimination in RIP (offset-lists cannot express it; lowest metric per destination wins).

Validation:
- New `rip_qnh_metric_12531_test.go` (7 tests): RED before (undefined ACL helper), GREEN after; #12071-era RIP warning test updated to pin restored behavior.
- Targeted QNH/RIP/redistribute suites pass; full `pkg/frr` passes except 4 failures base-attributed on origin/master (TestBGPNoExportNeighborGetsDefaultExport15157, TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564, TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374, TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426); `go vet` clean.
- Live FRR 10.7.1 netns: integrated config carries offset-list + ACL, ospfd has no set-metric copy, OSPF LSA metric stays 20, RIPv2 wire carries metric 10 for the QNH prefix.

Risk:
RIP database still displays metric 1 (offset applies on egress); operators read the wire/peer view. Metrics above 16 advertise as unreachable in RIP. Destination-only keying collapses multiple backups of one prefix to the lowest metric in RIP.

Refs #12531

## PR #16887 — userspace-xdp: remove disposition-dead GRE inner lookups (#16241) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16241-campaign`

userspace-xdp: remove disposition-dead GRE inner lookups (#16241)

Refs #16241
Refs #16695

## Why

PR #16264 delivered #16241's narrowed acceptance (per-arm branch hit
counters + fail-closed analysis) and proved no dispatch arm is
disposition-identical/removable. The three-way-validated residual
#16695 then found disposition-dead work *inside* the native-GRE arm:
on an inner session miss, `classify_native_gre_inner_ipv4`/`_ipv6` ran
up to five further hash lookups (DNAT exact+wildcard, interface-NAT,
local) returning `REDIRECT`-or-`0`. Both consumers act only on
`PASS_TO_KERNEL` (healthy arm plus local-outer gate; degraded twin via
`InnerSessionAction`), so `REDIRECT` and miss are indistinguishable —

  directly; `dnat_lookup_v4`/`v6` and the unused `ingress_domain`
  plumbing are deleted. Comments rewritten to state the true contract:
  inner classification decides only the `PASS_TO_KERNEL` case; a miss
  stays on the helper path where the worker adjudicates the inner
  packet (including DNAT/local) itself.
- The `dnat_table`/`dnat_table_v6` map *declarations* are deliberately
  retained — the Go loader replaces them with the pinned
  dataplane-owned tables and validates their shape; deleting them
  would break shim loading, not remove dead code.
- Regenerated shim object + gate verdict + manifest.

## PR #16891 — vrrp: keep VID-0 priority-tagged native adverts (#16426) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16426-vrrp-vid0-priority-tag`

Refs #16426

## Why

`receiverAfPacket` dropped any frame whose `PACKET_AUXDATA` carried
`TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID` on a non-VLAN netdev, without testing the VID
(#15049 regression). A priority-tagged peer advert (VID 0, PCP 6,
TCI `0xC000`) is stripped into skb metadata with `VLAN_VALID` set
exactly like a VLAN-100 advert, so the backup never heard the master,
its master-down timer expired, and both nodes held the VIP (dual
MASTER, ARP flapping). Linux treats VID 0 as native; only a non-zero
VID marks a frame as belonging to a VLAN sub-interface.

## What

- `pkg/vrrp/instance_receive.go`: gate the parent drop on a non-zero
  VID (`tagged && tci&0x0fff != 0`, masking PCP/DEI bits); update the
  `receiverAfPacket` contract comment.
- `pkg/vrrp/vlan_tag_present_15049_test.go`: add `hasAuxdata` to
  `vlanDelivery` and make `auxdataOOB` always encode `VLAN_VALID` so
  VID-0 deliveries are expressible (TCI 0 was previously conflated
  with "no auxdata"); new acceptance test
  `TestReceiverAfPacketParentKeepsVID0PriorityTaggedAdvert_16426`
  (PCP6/VID0 `0xC000` enqueues, TCI-0+VLAN_VALID enqueues, VLAN-100
  still drops) plus parser pins for VID-0 TCIs.
- `pkg/vrrp/README.md`, `docs/log/16426.md`: contract + action log.

NOT changed: the optional "only when the parent actually has tagged
VRRP siblings" refinement — the VID mask alone restores the #15049
contract and VID-N frames still drop unconditionally.

## Validation

- New test RED pre-fix (`parent received []` — both VID-0 adverts
  dropped), GREEN with fix.
- Targeted: `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run 'TestReceiverAfPacket|TestAfPacketAuxdata' -count=1` — 5 tests pass (incl. pre-existing #15049/#6560 cells); `go vet ./pkg/vrrp/` clean; gofmt clean.
- Full `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -count=1`: one failure,
  `TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate/RethVIPsForRG`,
  verified pre-existing on clean `origin/master@ce4445ddcb` via stash
  check, unrelated to this change.

## Risk

Fail-open direction unchanged for VID-N (still drops) and for
missing/invalid auxdata. Kernel cmsg contents are synthesized from
the af_packet ABI, not captured from a NIC (same limit as the #15049
harness). Lab verification on a priority-tagging L2 path remains
outstanding.

## Diagnosis (assertion proven correct, fixtures wrong)
`pkt_len` is the length of the buffer the meta describes from offset 0 (`types/mod.rs` #8581 contract; shim `packet_len = data_end - data`; `logical_ingress.rs` #8581 invariant tests; `tx/cos_classify.rs:151 packet_bytes = meta.pkt_len`, `flow_cache.rs observed_bytes = u64::from(meta.pkt_len)`). So `frame.len() - 14` fixtures were 14 bytes short — the guard assertion was not weakened.

At base the guard was red only on `resolver_enqueue_tests.rs:228`, and blind to 12 listed sites plus more found in-tree: `txn_meta_v6`, `gre_to_self_outer_meta{,_v6}` (`- l3`, VLAN-aware 14/18), GRE frag overwrites, `poll_stages_tests` VLAN meta (`- l3`), and 40 `txn_meta_v4(.., (len - 14) as u16)` call sites (the helper stores its 3rd arg verbatim into `pkt_len`) — all fixed to stamp the full buffer length. GRE "deliberate L3 length" hypothesis checked and rejected: those metas have `l3_offset: 14/18` over full Ethernet frames.

## Guard hardening
Replaces the 3 literal sinks with a comment-stripped scan flagging any `pkt_len` field/assignment value or `txn_meta_v4` 3rd argument containing `-14`/`-l3`/`saturating_sub(14)`; non-`pkt_len` wire-length invariants (IPv4 total / IPv6 payload length, e.g. `tests_mss_inject_inspect.rs`) stay legal. Stale "nothing gates on pkt_len" header corrected.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp fixture_pkt_len_is_the_full_frame_length_6883`: **ok, 1 passed** on fixed tree (at base it printed 1 site: resolver_enqueue_tests.rs:228).
- Real-Rust mutations reintroducing `(frame_len - 14)`, `frame.len() as u16 - 14`, `(inner.len() - 14)`, and `txn_meta_v4(.., (len - 14))`: each **FAILED (red)**, restored tree green.
- Targeted modules (gre frag/pool/transit, embedded poll filter, poll stages, native GRE ECN, resolver enqueue, txn flow cache): 249 passed, 1 failed — `stage11_local_ike_passthrough_honors_ingress_input_filter_13637`, which **also fails alone at base** (pre-existing; along with 20 nat64/gre-local-delivery failures identical before/after).

Residuals: absolute byte-threshold fixtures outside the targeted modules were not re-run as a full suite (no full selftest per campaign); byte assertions reading `meta.pkt_len` are self-consistent under the +14 shift.

## PR #16898 — feeds: restore legacy epoch sets without epoch_hash (#16427) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16427-restore-legacy-epoch`

Refs #16427

## Summary
`RestoreShrinkHighWater` required `digest == Hash` for durable records without `epoch_hash` (written before #15075). A legacy epoch whose count high-water had already rotated was therefore dropped on the first post-upgrade restart, and a wholesale same-count content swap of an enforced feed installed with no refusal — a regression versus the #14994 restore (R3-F05-07).

## Fix
For records without `EpochHash`, restore any canonical `Prefixes` set within the cap (the #14994 acceptance). The legacy `Prefixes` field was the epoch set and no epoch digest (and no MAC) was persisted to validate against, so the equality added no integrity and dropped exactly the rotated epochs. The restored set's own digest becomes the epoch hash, so the next snapshot persists it under `epoch_hash`. Records with a present `EpochHash` still must match it; non-canonical sets still drop fail-closed with the count epoch restored.

## Tests
- New `TestLegacyEpochWithoutEpochHashRestoresRotatedEpoch16427`: RED pre-fix (legacy record restored 0 epoch prefixes), GREEN post-fix (restores 100, identical set installs as control, disjoint equal-count swap refused and installs on exact ack).
- New `TestLegacyNonCanonicalEpochDropped16427`: pins the canonical bound for legacy records.
- Targeted `16427|15075|14994` run: 10/10 pass. Full `pkg/feeds` suite passes; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

## Risk
Scoped to the legacy restore leg. Corrupt-`EpochHash` fail-closed behaviour, thresholds, ack tuple, and true bootstrap are unchanged. The install-side epoch re-bootstrap for count-only records is #16651 (R3-A50-02), a separate fix site.

## PR #16899 — dhcp: reject non-granting REBIND replacement by omission (#16423) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16423-campaign`

Why:
The #14997 REBIND gate tested only teardown content (non-Success
status, valid-lifetime 0), so a non-granting on-link responder could
omit the held IA_NA address, offer a different live one, pass as a
pure extension, and have commitLease remove the held WAN address in
one packet (R3-F04-05). RFC 8415 18.2.10.1 leaves an omitted held
lease unchanged and adds only new leases; omission-plus-replacement
is neither, and the same shape abandoned every held IA_PD prefix.

What:
Extend v6ReplyTearsDownHeldBinding in pkg/dhcp/renew.go: for each
requested IA, read the held elements from the request echo and treat
a matched Reply IA that offers a live element but keeps none of the
held ones as teardown, reusing the DHCPv6TeardownRejects counter.
Silence on an IA and held-plus-new additions remain extensions.
Granting-server replacement, parse, reconcile, commitLease, the run
loop, and DHCPv4 are unchanged. Docs: pkg/dhcp/README.md bullet,
RenewalBindingStats comment, docs/log/16423.md.

Validation:
New TestV6RebindNonGrantingReplacementRejected16423 cells:
replace-IA_NA-only and replace-IA_PD-only rejected (counter 1),
granting replacement and held-plus-new/silent partner extensions
accepted. RED on revert of renew.go (both replacement cells
accepted, counter 0). Full go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1 PASS;
go vet clean; gofmt and git diff --check clean.

Risk:
A failover partner that holds the binding but echoes no held element
is now ignored until it extends or the lease expires into Solicit,
the RFC 8415 18.2.10 posture already taken for NoBinding. The
deliberate #14600 handoff (an accepted extension becomes the next
RENEW binding) is unchanged and remains the documented limit.

## PR #16900 — daemon: restore prior faillock rules on SSH apply rollback (#16421) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16421-campaign`

Why:
The #14973 rollback stripped every managed pam_faillock block when a failed `applySSHConfig` had changed common-auth. On the upgrade transition that change merely rewrites the pre-#14973 legacy rules the host already had (no `even_deny_root`), so a failed first post-upgrade SSH apply (sshd -t, reload, drop-in write, or config render failure) left a non-appliance host with no SSH password lockout at all — less protection than before the apply, with nothing in the apply error mentioning the PAM state.

What:
`applySSHPAMFaillockChanged`/`setSSHPAMFaillock` now also return the exact pre-apply common-auth bytes alongside the changed flag. `applySSHConfig` captures them and its deferred rollback (`restoreSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback`, replacing `stripSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback`) restores the prior bytes verbatim — the same posture as `revertDropIn` for the sshd drop-in — falling back to the old strip only when no bytes were captured. A fresh install from stock therefore still ends at stock, and a legacy upgrade ends back at the original 3 legacy lines. NOT changed: install/upgrade rendering, the tamper refusal, the appliance skip, or the #15229 advisory-failure posture.

Validation:
- New `TestApplySSHConfigRollbackRestoresPriorFaillock16421` (6 subtests) RED pre-fix (all 4 legacy failure rows ended at bare stock with 0 faillock lines; stock-rollback and legacy-success controls passed), GREEN post-fix with byte-exact prior restore.
- Existing #14973 stock rollback tests, #11492 install/idempotence and #15229 tuned-block suites stay green (22 faillock-related tests); `TestApplySSHConfig` suite green; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` and gofmt clean.

Risk:
A failed SSH apply now rewrites common-auth once more with the captured prior bytes instead of a strip render; if that restore write itself fails it is logged and joined into the apply error, never masking the original failure. Hosts with admin-installed faillock, appliance hosts, and unsupported PAM stacks are untouched. No wire/config-schema change.

Refs #16421

- Acquire the #15085 daemon singleton via `daemon.GuardDaemonLockForCleanup` before any transit/pin/fabric/FRR mutation and hold it for the whole teardown — acquiring (not probing) closes the check-to-mutation TOCTOU and also blocks a daemon starting mid-cleanup. Refusal wraps `ErrDaemonAlreadyRunning`, names `systemctl stop xpfd`, exit 1.
- Export `DaemonLockHeldByLiveProcess` probe form; update #6928 caller census for the `cleanupDataplane` seam; README + changelog.

No-holder path is unchanged (transit -> unpin -> fabric -> FRR, #10907/#1880 contracts). Postrm (transit-barrier remove) and deploy scripts (stop-first) unaffected.

Tests: `TestCleanupGuardRefusesLiveDaemon16430` (RED-on-neuter verified), `TestCleanupRefusesBesideLiveDaemon16430`, `TestCleanupProceedsWithoutLiveDaemon16430`, `TestCleanupStrayOperandRefusesBeforeGuard16430`; existing cleanup/dispatch/transit-barrier/#15085/#6928 suites pass; `go vet` clean.

- No proto change; REST has no cluster-failover verb, so no REST change.

## PR #16908 — userspace: ignore SIGHUP in helper (#16431) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16431-helper-sighup`

Refs #16431

## Why
#15084 made xpfd ignore SIGHUP, but the Rust helper kept the default disposition: xpfd's `signal.Notify` capture is a caught disposition that resets to SIG_DFL across exec, so `systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` (delivered to every unit process) killed `xpf-userspace-dp`, failed transit closed, and forced a supervisor backoff respawn with rebuilt per-worker state.

## What
- `userspace-dp/src/server/lifecycle.rs`: install SIG_IGN for SIGHUP via `libc::signal` at the very top of `run()`, before workers/socket threads spawn; log posture at startup. SIG_IGN discards HUP in-kernel without touching `running`; deliberately NOT ctrlc's `termination` feature (would route HUP to graceful exit = still outage). SIGINT/ctrlc and shutdown-verb semantics unchanged; bare SIGTERM disposition unchanged (out of scope, Go sends shutdown verb first).
- `userspace-dp/tests/sighup_16431.rs`: blackbox cells spawning the real binary (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_xpf-userspace-dp`), real SIGHUP x3 with ping before/after, plus shutdown-verb exit-0.
- Changelog + `userspace-dp/src/server/README.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --test sighup_16431`: 2 passed.
- Mutant (removed `ignore_sighup()?` call): SIGHUP cell RED (child dies by Hangup); restored GREEN.
- Lifecycle unit filters: accept_step 9 passed, peer_uid 2 passed.
- Full bin suite (>9k tests) exceeded 300s window without observed failure; not run to completion.

## Risk
Low: one disposition set once at startup, fail-fast on SIG_ERR; no hot-path change. Helper ignores HUP even hand-run, matching xpfd's no-reload-on-HUP posture.

## PR #16918 — image: decouple ssh host-key regeneration from day-0 loader (#16445) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `feat/16445-ssh-hostkey-regen`

Refs #16445

## Why
A zeroize writes its pending marker at the day-0 stamp path (`/etc/xpf/.day0-config-applied`) before the seal leg erases `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*` and rotates the machine-id. Any later leg failure or power loss left a boot where the stamp-gated `xpf-day0-config` unit — the only xpf `ssh-keygen -A` path — was condition-skipped, and Ubuntu's `ConditionFirstBoot` sshd-keygen was defeated by the fresh real machine-id. `sshd -t` then failed and the box was console-only.

## What
- New `xpf-ssh-hostkeys.service`: `ssh-keygen -A` `Before=ssh.service`, gated only on host-key absence (`ConditionPathExists=!/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key`) — never on the day-0 stamp, first-boot, or machine-id.
- Staged + enabled by both `debian/rules` (dh_installsystemd, clean list, .gitignore) and `bake.py`; pinned in the #16198 systemd-unit canary on both shipping paths.
- Day-0 loader keeps its stamp gate (twin: still skipped under the pending marker) and no longer regenerates keys; dead `regen_ssh_host_keys` stubs removed from its harnesses. Seal comments/docs/changelog updated.

## Validation
- `test_ssh_hostkeys_regen_16445.py` 2/2: failed-reset fixture (pending marker present, keys absent, rotated machine-id) — real day-0 condition fails, real regen condition succeeds via `systemd-analyze condition`, real `ssh-keygen -A` creates keys, `sshd -t` passes with key / fails without; existing-key arm is skipped. Re-gating the unit on the stamp reds it (mutation-checked).
- `test_day0_machine_id_independence_10769.py` 3/3, `test_systemd_unit_canary_16198.py` 7/7, day-0 suites 16/16 + 16/16, `day0-configdb-guard-test.sh` all pass, targeted `go test ./pkg/factoryreset/` ok, `systemd-analyze verify` clean. No full selftest (campaign scope).

## Risk
`ssh-keygen -A` only creates missing key types and the unit is condition-skipped when any host key exists, so existing keys are never rotated; a partial set is completed — the desired per-instance identity.

## PR #16921 — factoryreset: refuse zeroize for busy provisioned accounts before wiping (#16443) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16443-zeroize-busy-account`

Refs #16443

## Why
`userdel -r` refuses a busy account (exit 8), and the operator's own SSH/CLI session runs under an xpf-provisioned account. The wipe erased SSH host keys, login keys, sudoers, networkd and the config DB before discovering the login leg could never succeed from that session; every retry failed identically, leaving a half-wiped box recoverable only from the console.

## What
- `checkProvisionedAccountsIdle` (`pgrep -u <uid>`) gates both `performWipeWithLogInventory` (before `beginZeroize` writes the pending marker) and `performWipe` (before any destructive leg): a busy provisioned account refuses the whole zeroize naming the account, every surface intact. Ownership uncertainty and probe failures also refuse (unknown, never idle).
- Inside `wipeLoginAccounts`, `terminateBusyProvisionedAccounts` closes the check-to-use window: terminates live processes scoped to the marker UID (`pkill -KILL -u`, never root/UID 0, never the wipe's own UID), re-verifies idle, and only then lets `userdel` fire; still-busy accounts keep markers for retry.
- New seams redirected in `RedirectWipePathsForTesting` (idle default); `setZeroizeLoginPaths` hermetic for them.
- Follow-on: the #16138 move left the #6584 termsafe tripwire's `server_diag_zeroize.go` exemption stale; repointed at `factoryreset/wipe.go`, declared the moved exec helper, scan now covers `../factoryreset`.

## Validation

- Pre-existing unrelated grpcapi status-census failure (ShowConfig/GetSessionSummary) untouched

## PR #16922 — packaging: interest dpkg triggers on unpacked shim/grub payloads (#16452) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16452-dpkg-triggers`

Refs #16452

## Why
`debian/xpf.triggers` interested `/boot/efi/EFI/ubuntu/{shim,grub,mm}x64.efi`, but `shim-signed`/`grub-efi-amd64-signed` unpack only `/usr/lib/shim/*` and `/usr/lib/grub/x86_64-efi-signed/*`; `grub-install` writes the ESP from their postinsts outside dpkg. No package ever unpacked an interested path, so `xpf.postinst triggered` never ran on a bootloader update and the A/B slots stayed stale until the next boot — the documented no-reboot guarantee was false (R3-A57-02).

## What

## PR #16924 — firewall: re-assert recorded slot front after bootloader NVRAM rewrite (#16449) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16449-campaign`

Why: On the Ubuntu 26.04 base the grub-efi-amd64-signed / shim-signed postinst runs grub-install with NVRAM writes enabled, (re)creating the Ubuntu Boot#### entry at BootOrder[0]. The firmware then boots \EFI\ubuntu\shimx64.efi instead of an xpf slot, and xpf-uefi-slots preserved any non-xpf front as an operator choice forever, so the LANE-1 kernel arm refused with "BootOrder front is neither A/B slot" after the first routine bootloader security update.

What: `xpf-uefi-slots` records the BootOrder front it leaves in `/var/lib/xpf/uefi-bootorder-front`; when the current front is the distributor entry and the recorded front is an xpf slot, it re-asserts the recorded slot front non-destructively. A PXE front, or a distributor front with no recorded slot front, is preserved as an operator choice. Missing/garbled state never takes over. `bake.py` purges the state file at sysprep. The kernel arm gate is unchanged (no fail-open weakening).

Validation: RED on master script 6/9 new cells fail; GREEN `test_uefi_slots_6499` (29) + adjacent suites (94 total); `sh -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean. Baked-image VM probe remains lab-outstanding on the issue.

Risk: a hand-set Ubuntu front on a box whose recorded front is a slot is reverted once; documented in `docs/install-images.md`.

Refs #16449

## PR #16925 — cli: gate firewall live banner on applied marker after helper refusal (#16451) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16451-firewall-refused-live-banner`

Refs #16451

## Why
After an in-band helper refusal of a committed config's snapshot, both inputs of the #5067 liveness predicate (helper ack generation, last recorded apply generation) stay at the prior generation (7/7, armed), so `show firewall effective` certified the refused config as `dataplane-acknowledged (generation N)` and the RAW `show firewall` views paired the refused config's terms with the previous generation's counters.

## What
- `pkg/cli`: `firewallEffectiveLiveness` now additionally requires `store.ActiveApplied()` (via shared `firewallshow.Applied`) for `live`, with reason `active configuration not applied`. Both local RAW views print a previous-generation stale-counter WARNING when determined-but-not-live.
- `pkg/firewallshow`: shared `Applied` gate + `StaleCounterWarning` / `NotEnforcingWarning` texts so no surface copies the generation-only predicate.
- `pkg/grpcapi`: raw `firewall`/`firewall-filter:` topics print the stale-counter warning when helper status was obtained and the active config is unapplied; `firewall-effective*` topics print the NOT-enforcing/compiled-desired warning whenever unapplied (fail-closed even without helper status).
- Tests: refusal cell (7/7/armed unstamped → WARNING, never acknowledged; stamped twin → live banner) + RAW stale-counter cells (cli), four-surface gRPC cell; live fixtures stamped with `MarkActiveApplied()`.
- Docs: `docs/junos-cli-reference.md` generation-liveness section + `docs/log/16451.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/cli/ -run 'TestShowEffectiveFirewallFilters|TestShowFirewallRawStaleCounters16451|TestCLIShowFirewallRawFields15173|TestShowEffectiveFirewallFilter' -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run 'TestShowTextFirewall|TestShowFirewall' -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/firewallshow/ -count=1` PASS; `go vet` on the three packages clean
- Full `pkg/cli`/`pkg/grpcapi` suites carry pre-existing failures verified identical on clean `origin/master`.

## Risk
In-process surfaces rely on the daemon's in-memory `appliedDigest` (empty until first successful apply / boot apply stamp); before that stamp views warn — fail-closed, never a false live certification. No dataplane/enforcement change.

## PR #16930 — image: ship only the default-ring hugepage pool and drop the deb sysctl (#16455) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16455-hugepages`

Refs #16455

## Why
`etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` shipped `vm.nr_hugepages = 1440` (2.8 GiB) verbatim through the bake and the .deb's `/usr/lib/sysctl.d`, although the default `ring-entries 1024` needs 5 pages per binding (2560 frames x 4 KiB = 10 MiB, MAP_HUGETLB-rounded; 6 on virtio_net). The pool is applied at boot on every baked image — OOM kills on the 2 GiB Tier-1 validation VM, ~620 MiB free on the documented 4 GiB appliance before any service starts — and at package-install time on foreign hosts via systemd's `/usr/lib/sysctl.d` file trigger, contrary to debian/rules' 'next boot' claim and the #10733 unowned-host contract.

## What
- **Shipped default 1440 -> 90** in `etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` (5 x 18 reference bindings at ring 1024 = 180 MiB); header rewritten (default formula, large-ring formula, bake/rig + manual provisioning, .deb installs nothing).
- **bake.py**: `hugepages_conf()` now refuses any shipped default other than exactly 90 (exact-equality gate over the preserved review-16260 systemd/kernel consumer-model parse — all ineffective spellings still die). New `--hugepages N` rig parameter: refuses N < 90 at arg parse and N < 1440 (reference large-ring pool) when rendering; renders by rewriting only the effective (last-surviving) assignment's value bytes and re-verifies the rendered effective value. Threaded through `virt_customize`/`main`.
- **debian/rules**: installs **no** sysctl.d payload, so `apt install` on an unmarked host leaves `/proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages` unchanged.
- **validate.py**: scenario A asserts `HugePages_Total <= 90` and `MemAvailable >= 1 GiB` from one `/proc/meminfo` read in the 2 GiB gate VM (pure `_memory_floor_verdict`, unobserved readings fail).
- **Docs**: deploy-quickstart + userspace-dataplane-architecture rewritten (default pool shipped; large rings via `--hugepages` or /etc edit; .deb installs nothing). Changelog entry added.

## Tests
- `scripts/image/test_bake_hugepages_16243.py` re-based on 90 (18 cells): shipped-default equality, old 1440 default rejected at bake and at virt_customize, consumer-model spellings kept, override rendering (incl. shadowed-line and hex cases), `--hugepages` arg parsing, debian/rules sysctl-absence cells.
- New `scripts/image/test_validate_memory_floor_16455.py`: pre-fix meminfo fixtures (HugePages_Total 849 partial / 1440 full) fail, fixed 90-page fixture passes, unobserved readings fail, scenario-A wiring + bound cross-pinned against bake/conf.
- Full `scripts/image` unittest discover: **546 tests OK** (incl. updated reach-map count and main() namespace fixtures).
- `make -f debian/rules` dry-run: no sysctl install line; host `/proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages` observed unchanged (20 before/after).

## Risk
A ring-entries 16384 appliance that relied on the old universal 1440 default now boots with the 90-page pool and takes the advisory-THP fallback (loud helper WARNING, measured 22.1->20.4 Gbps class at ring 16384) until the operator bakes `--hugepages 1440+` or edits `/etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` per the rewritten docs. Correctness at any ring size never depended on the pool. No gate weakened: bake validation tightened from a >=1440 floor to exact-default equality; validate.py gains a new fail-closed assertion.

Residual: full `make deb` + real `apt install` in a VM not run (host is the shared control box); the .deb-side acceptance is pinned hermetically (rules payload absence + trigger mechanism documented from systemd's sysctl.d interest). Scenario A's live boot assertion runs with the next real bake/validate cycle.

## PR #16952 — userspace-dp: coerce tcp maximum window to wire range (#16482) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16482-userspace-tcp-window-coerce`

## userspace-dp: coerce tcp maximum window to wire range (#16482)

Refs #16482

### Why
`security flow tcp-session maximum-window` (#15753) reached the Rust u32 wire field `tcp_maximum_window` via `buildFlowSnapshot` with a raw assignment — the one FlowSnapshot integer with no #1977 coercion. A value above u32::MAX arriving through a tolerant path (`Store.Load` of a hand-edited/foreign DB, `SyncApply` from a peer with a wider range; strict commit's `ValidateInteger(1024,1048576)` is only logged there) made serde reject the whole `apply_snapshot` decode, leaving the helper unconfigured.

### What
- `flow.go`: new `coerceWireTCPMaximumWindow` + `maxTCPMaximumWindow` (1048576); `buildFlowSnapshot` caps over-ceiling values to the schema ceiling with a `slog.Warn`. In-range values (65536) pass unchanged; non-positive stays on the existing `> 0` guard (0 = Rust default 65535).
- Capping to the schema ceiling rather than `math.MaxUint32`: a peer value such as 2^31 is already outside this node's operator range, and the ceiling keeps every emitted value also strict-commit-legal here.
- Tests: extend `TestBuildFlowSnapshotCoercesOutOfRange_1977`, add the field to the Layer A/B agreement table (`flow_numwidth_agreement_test.go`), add `TestTCPMaximumWindowCoerced16482` (cap + warn + u32-decodable wire JSON + 65536 unchanged + unset omitted).
- NOT changed: schema/compiler range, protocol version, Rust side.

### Validation
- Targeted (6/6 pass): `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestBuildFlowSnapshotCoercesOutOfRange_1977|TestNumWidth_LayerAB_Agreement|TestTCPMaximumWindowCoerced16482|TestTCPFidelityKnobsReachWire15753|TestCoerceWireHelpers_1977|TestFullSnapshotMarshalsInRange_1977' -count=1`

- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean; `gofmt` clean on changed files.

## PR #16957 — userspace-dp: carry retained deterministic NAT64 tuples on pool length change (#16481) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16481`

Refs #16481

## Why
A deterministic NAPT64 pool append/shrink changed `host_count`, so the NAT64 rebuild built a fresh allocator and (since #15178) skipped the #6765 reseed. Revalidation keeps retained subscribers' sessions because their (pool index, block) did not move, so the fresh allocator re-minted each subscriber's lowest block port — the port its oldest surviving session still holds — and a second flow to the same remote shared the live reverse tuple.

## What
- `PortAllocator::reseed_retained_deterministic_v6_from`: carries live deterministic flows whose tuple still satisfies `deterministic_v6_tuple_matches` under the NEW params into the fresh allocator, rebuilding each BIB lease with the new `DeterministicPortedIdentity::V6` (sibling flows join one lease, holder masks preserved); invalid tuples are counted, not carried.
- `Nat64State` wires it for det->det transitions; RR->RR keeps the generic #6765 carry and mode flips still start fresh (#15178).
- `ReseedOutcome` gains `reseeded_deterministic`/`skipped_deterministic_invalid`, classified in `needs_report`. Dead `prev_prefix_is_deterministic` removed.

## Validation
- `r3n05_det_pool_append_reissues_live_tuple`, `vn05_det_pool_shrink_reissues_live_tuple_and_tears_down_removed` pass (F2 differs from F1, F1 held, removed subscriber torn down).
- 3 allocator cells in `tests_det_reseed_16481.rs` pass (append/shrink carry, block-change control).
- #15178 cells, `tests_pool`, `tests_reseed` green (287 passed combined targeted run). The `nat64_`/`reseed` parallel batch shows 16 failures identical on pristine origin/master (pre-existing), unrelated.

## Risk
Commit-time work only, no per-packet cost. Sessions outside the new geometry are still torn down by revalidation as #15178 intended; round-robin and no-op re-applies unchanged. Idle BIB leases are not carried (no live session; tuple re-derives deterministically).

Changelog: `docs/log/16481.md`

## PR #16965 — userspace-dp: stop refusing D11 admission on lock contention (#16495) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16495`

Refs #16495

## Why
D11 IPsec-inner admission refused admissible frames on lock contention at three sites left by #15151: router in-flight `try_lock` → `WORKER_QUEUE_FULL` (47, E23 counted with an empty queue), worker-set authority `try_lock` → `EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE` (52 → ADMIT_SHUTDOWN), tombstone `try_insert` → `LEASE_EPOCH` (50 → ADMIT_BAD_LEASE, attestation FAIL). Every refusal is a Go `VerdictDrop` of a permitted frame.

## What
Blocking `lock()` at all three sites (issue's accepted bounded-hold alternative): `authoritative_route` replaces `try_is_authoritative`/`try_route` (None only unpublished/empty); router in-flight lock (O(1) vs O(1) release); tombstone `try_insert`→`insert` (competing O(cap≤512) scans). E23 now moves only at genuine per-queue depth / per-flow in-flight bound; LEASE_EPOCH only duplicate/zero/at-cap. Per-queue BUSY (#15151 accepted risk), wire, Go, depths unchanged.

## Validation
`cargo test --bins ipsec_inner_queue::tests`: **32 passed**. 3 new deterministic ` *_16495` cells hold each competing lock from another thread across a spawned admit and require `Ok(0)` (inflight: E23 delta 0; tombstone: genuine duplicate still LEASE_EPOCH), each with positive control. Existing genuine-full/per-flow/BUSY controls green.

## Risk
Producer briefly blocks on bounded holds (no lock held across adjudication) instead of dropping. No lab production-rate measurement (matches finding evidence level).

- `GOTMPDIR` defaults to `/wtgt` (5 chars; worst-case canary path 97 octets) in `Makefile`, `scripts/run-selftests.sh`, and the `test-memlock-guards` recipe. `TMPDIR`/`GOCACHE`/`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` pins under `/var/worktrees/.cache` are unchanged; an explicit caller `GOTMPDIR` still wins.
- The modelled-length check is replaced by an executed canary: `scripts/sunpath-canary` reproduces the real TempDir shape (64-byte name + 10-digit random stand-in + `/001/control.sock`) and binds it. `scratch-pinning-selftest.sh` requires it to pass under `/wtgt` and fail under a deliberately long root, so the check reds in both directions. - `scripts/README.md`, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/16494.md` updated. NOT changed: per-test `shortSockDir` helpers (still needed for deeper-than-`001` socket layouts) and the stale on-disk `/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp` directory (now unreferenced).

- Canary: binds at 97 octets under `/wtgt`; fails at 120 under the old root and 116 under `/var/worktrees/.cache/gt` (proving no `/var/worktrees/.cache` path can fit).
- `sh scripts/scratch-pinning-selftest.sh`: green with new pins; RED on revert (restoring the 28-char pin fails naming all three GOTMPDIR/TMPDIR pins).
- Previously pinned-only failures pass under `/wtgt` and fail under the old root with the exact issue signatures: `pkg/nfqueue` TestReinjectSocketCompletionTimeoutResetsPartialFrame9506, `pkg/grpcapi` TestUngatedFallbackErasesDerivedHelperState10769, sampled `pkg/dataplane/userspace` event-stream/control/DumpFIB/HA-watchdog cells, and the two `pkg/daemon` event-stream race cells.
- `scripts/selftest-census.sh` still OK (62 self-tests invoked); `go vet`/`gofmt` clean on the canary.

## PR #16969 — userspace-dp: collect TX-selection handles only on deferred walk (#16496) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16496-campaign`

Why: `merge_matched_tx_modifiers` pushed an `Arc::clone` of every matched term's counter and three-color policer into `TxSelectionFilterResult` on every walk, including the metered and counted live transit walks that immediately discard them. Each matched counted term cost a strong-count RMW on the counter shared by all workers per packet, and ≥3 handles spilled the inline-2 SmallVec to the heap — re-adding the cross-worker line traffic #3073/#14656 removed on the non-flow-cache path.

What: thread a `collect_deferred: bool` through the TX-selection walk (runtime → inner → counted_family/v4/v6 → `merge_matched_tx_modifiers`); handles are pushed only when true. The sole collecting walk is the new `evaluate_filter_ref_tx_selection_deferred` entry (uncounted, unmetered, collect=true), preserving #15268 deferred semantics exactly. All live entries pass false and return empty handle sets. `resolve_cos_tx_selection_internal` switches its four `defer_side_effects` branches (flowless/flow-keyed × output/ingress) to the deferred entry; non-deferred branches, the cached walk (`CachedTxSelectionFilterResult`), inline counting/metering, and every fail-closed gate are unchanged.

Validation:

- Targeted: `cargo test --bins -- 16496 15268` → 5 passed (incl. existing `*_15268` deferred-replay cells); `cached_three_color_replay_latest_policer_dscp_wins_15793` green.

Component level only — no release perf/NUMA measurement, so throughput magnitude remains unquantified. The deferred walk still clones by design, once per generated reply off the transit path.

required `sent - baseline_sent == received - baseline_received`. Creates in
flight at the first sample then delivered (20/17 -> 20/20), or creates landing
between the two non-atomic CLI captures (20/22 -> 22/22), shrink the gap, so no
later sample ever reads idle. Both failover-gate precondition waits then time
out FAIL on a caught-up pair and VOID the downstream RG1 cells of

sequence 20/22 -> 22/22 verbatim, where the delta gaps are 2 vs 0 (counters
unequal in deltas, equal absolutely); a growing gap (20/20 -> 25/20) stays not
idle either way. Both wait loops (`test-failover.sh`,
`scripts/userspace-ha-failover-validation.sh`) consume the helper verdict and
need no change: the sibling sources the same lib, and its baseline-keeping /
rewind-only re-baseline discipline is unchanged. NOT changed: verdicts 1/2/3,
pending/drained parsing, the 3-consecutive-sample policy, any daemon code.

Validation:
`bash test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh` PASS, with new unit cells
(20/17->20/20 idle, 20/22->22/22 idle, 20/20->25/20 not idle, shrunk gap
pending=3 not idle) and new stateful loop cases for BOTH production wait loops
(shrinking gap PASS sample 4, received-ahead PASS sample 4, growing gap timeout
FAIL 8 calls). RED: equality-only revert fails on 20/17->20/20; inequality-only
(no counters-meet) fails on 20/22->22/22. `bash -n` + shellcheck clean.

Risk:
The counters-meet clause generalizes the issue's inequality on different-epoch
counters by treating absolute equality as caught up even if the baseline gap
was positive; pending==0 and the 3-consecutive-sample rule still guard it, and

## PR #16972 — userspace-dp: deliver D11 terminals for stale survivors and stop reaps (#16497) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16497-campaign`

## Why
#15149 residual (R3-B12-02): retiring a dead worker bumps the GLOBAL D11 worker-set generation, so descriptors queued on SURVIVING workers read stale in `drain_worker` and were dropped with no verdict; `stop_inner` likewise reaped every queue into `reaped_verdicts` but never delivered them. Both sets completed only by the 5 ms Go ack deadline (`pkg/nfqueue/pipeline.go`), with per-flow stall and ack-timeout mis-accounting; the undelivered list grew by the reaped count on every full stop. Fail-closed either way — the defect is the missing prompt Denied terminal.

## What
- `ipsec_inner_queue.rs`: the `drain_worker` stale branch records `Deny{stage:"d11_stale_generation", reason:STALE_GENERATION}` when `claim_stale` wins (exactly-once preserved), via a new `push_reaped_verdict` helper used by all three producers; a `reaped_count` atomic mirrors the Vec depth (`uncertain_count` precedent) so `has_pending_work` stays lock-free yet never hides an undelivered terminal.
- `worker/loop_body/mod.rs`: the worker loop takes reaped terminals after `drain_verdicts_into` and completes them on the same pass — a survivor is never swept, so this is the only delivery path for its stale descriptors.
- `coordinator/mod.rs`: `stop_inner` drains `take_reaped_terminal_verdicts` into `complete_ipsec_inner_verdict` right after its retire+join loops (slow path still installed; its ReinjectCore survives reconciles).
- NOT changed: the generation model, the `status.rs` dead-worker sweep, Go deadline behaviour.

## Validation
- Extended `dead_worker_sweep_retires_ipsec_inner_worker_15149` to run the survivor's drain: takes 0 (stale never adjudicated), records exactly one terminal, request 151492 completes `Denied`, both slabs reclaimed, zero leftovers. Pre-fix this drain completed nothing.
- New `stop_inner_delivers_reaped_ipsec_inner_verdicts_16497`: one queued request per worker, real `stop_inner(false)` → both complete `Denied`, `has_reaped_verdicts()` false, slabs reclaimed, second empty stop clean.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15149 16497 ipsec_inner`: **79 passed, 0 failed**.
- Coordinator suite (`afxdp::coordinator::`): 379 passed / 5 failed — all 5 (`apply_snapshot_wires_day2_preserved_mtu_reconcile`, `every_runtime_atomic_is_bound_or_knowingly_off_wire_6961`, `refresh_runtime_snapshot_publishes_a_coherent_view_pair`, `snapshot_duplicate_if_id_claimants_deny_through_adjudication_10540`, `snapshot_published_tunnel_rows_join_d11_10485`) reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` `037049d500` in a detached base worktree: base-attributed, not caused by this change.

## Risk
A reaped entry recorded by a worker that dies before its next pass is still flushed by the dead-worker sweep or `stop_inner`; no new stranding path. Enforcement unchanged (Denied either way). Component level only, matching the finding's evidence; no Go pipeline/lab run.

## PR #16973 — screen: cap per-source scan state at detection count (#16498) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16498-scan-cap`

Refs #16498

## Why
`ScanCore::check` fired port-scan/ip-sweep detection at the fixed `SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` (10) distinct destinations but kept inserting distinct destinations into a per-source heap `FxHashSet` up to `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` (1024). The window reset's `clear()` retained that bucket allocation and least-suspicious eviction preserved the fullest sets, so a spoofed-source new-flow flood could pin ~144 MiB (ip-sweep) + ~24 MiB (port-scan) of heap per worker per screened zone (~1 GiB at 6 workers with both screens on) — ~100x what detection requires — and paid hashing for destinations 11-1024 that carry no verdict information.

## What
- Recorded destinations now live in an inline `[Option<T>; SCAN_DETECT_COUNT]` buffer in `SrcEntry` (with `insert_unique`/`distinct_count`/`is_empty`/`reset_entries`): no per-source heap allocation, nothing retained across a window reset.
- `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` now equals `SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` (compile-time guard updated). A distinct destination past the count is not stored, counts once on the existing `skipped_pressure` signal (mirroring the old over-1024 path; a repeat of a recorded destination does not count), and the already-true verdict is still evaluated — no gate weakens, no fail-open.
- Eviction's least-suspicious ordering and cleanup's empty test read the capped count (<=10, semantics unchanged).
- scan.rs module doc + session README now publish the per-worker, per-zone bound: saturated records are 200 B (ip-sweep) / 64 B (port-scan), i.e. at most 4096 x (200 + 64) B = ~1.03 MiB per worker per zone for both screens' per-source records, plus the unchanged source-axis index overhead.

## Validation
- New `single_source_fanout_capped_at_detect_count_16498`: one source, 2000 distinct destinations in one window, both instantiations — fires exactly at the 10th, recorded count caps at 10 (RED on the pre-fix shape), inline bytes only, post-count pressure, repeat-not-pressure.
- New `per_source_state_capped_at_detect_count_16498`: cap equality, measured record sizes (200 B / 64 B), saturated 4096-source zone holds exactly sources x one fixed-size record.
- Existing bound cells (`per_source_unique_entries_bounded`, `memory_caps_bound_state_under_wide_window`) re-anchored to the new cap.
- `cargo test --bins screen::scan`: 34/34 green. Full `screen::` filter: 370/370 green.

## Risk
Verdict semantics unchanged. `skipped_pressure` now also counts distinct destinations past 10 (was: past 1024) — observability only, never a gate.

Residual: component level only, matching the finding's evidence; no appliance RSS/OOM measurement (the fix removes the attacker-driven heap axis rather than tuning it).

## PR #16974 — userspace-dp: cap WireGuard pad at inner budget (#16499) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16499-wg-pad-cap`

Why: TUN-origin WireGuard egress padded every record to a 16-byte multiple with no MTU cap. An operator `mtu` set by the standard underlay-minus-overhead formula (1420 on IPv6/1500, 1432 on IPv4 PPPoE 1492) made every full-size firewall-originated packet up to 15 bytes too big; each was silently dropped at `encap_mtu_drops` with no PTB.

Size models and `wg_inner_mtu` become the capped inverse; Go default wgN MTU drops the worst-pad subtraction and warns on an operator mtu above the default-underlay budget. Decap unchanged.

Validation: cargo `encap_and_send(1420-byte inner, v6 peer, outer 1500)` returns Sent with a 1452-byte record and decaps round-trip; probe rows (v6/1500→1420, v4/1492→1432, v4/1450→1390, v6/1450→1370) all fit exactly; Go `TestWgTunMTUForEndpoint` passes. ## PR #16980 — userspace-dp: key egress DSCP rewrite only on the final class (#16506) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16506-campaign`

## Why

`resolve_cos_priority_class_lp_rewrite` chained filter class -> BA class -> clamped queue. When an input filter reclassifies with `then forwarding-class <fc>` and the egress DSCP rewrite-rule has no entry for `<fc>` (a partial "bleach best-effort only" rule), the packet was queued as `<fc>` but re-marked with the overridden BA class's code-point (queued EF, emitted DSCP 0), and the cached seed replayed that BA-derived marking on every flow-cache hit. This violates the documented #14663 contract that the filter class is the packet's FINAL forwarding class for egress DSCP rewriting. The same resolver's clamped-queue arm (Y28-05 cohort) bleached an unmaterialized BA class absent from the rule with the default queue's entry.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify_ba.rs`: the rewrite now keys ONLY on the packet's final class (filter class when present, else the BA class) — its `(class, loss-priority)` entry, then the queue entry only when the egress queue IS that class's own materialized queue. `resolve_cos_class_lp_rewrite` delegates to the shared resolver. A packet no classifier assigned any class to keeps the pre-#13968 queue-keyed behaviour (the selected queue is the classification result; pinned by #11386/#11808).
- Stale "then the BA class, then the clamped queue" comments in `tx/cos_classify.rs` updated; final-class-only contract recorded in `docs/cos-traffic-shaping.md`.
- NOT changed: the drain fallback (`uniform_fc_rewrite` already keys by the queue's own class, so it cannot resurrect the overridden class) and `cos_lp_reclassify` arming.

## Validation

- New cells in `cos_filter_fc_14663_tests.rs`: filter class absent from rule (fresh + cached seed `None`, two-packet hit seed DSCP 10 / hit DSCP 46 -> `None`, DSCP-46 twin, controls A/B, flowless), unmaterialized-filter variant (clamped default queue must not bleach), Y28-05 BA-only variant (fresh/seed/hit `None`, materialized-BE control).
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16506 y28_05 14663 14636`: 10 passed. RED-verified by restoring the base resolver: all 3 new cells fail `left: Some(0) right: None`; restored green.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- cos_`: 437 passed, 0 failed.
- Full `cargo test --bins`: 9451 passed / 80 failed vs 9449/79 on unmodified origin/master `957f50f891` (scratch worktree). Failure-set diff: the only fix-only failure is `v8_release_unused_v8_concurrent_preserves_ledger_invariant`, an unrelated shared-lease concurrency test that passes twice in isolation (flake under full-suite load); all other failures are pre-existing and identical.

## Risk

Packets whose assigned class (filter or BA) is absent from the egress rewrite-rule now leave unrewritten instead of inheriting another class's code-point — the documented #14663 contract. Component-level verification only, matching the issue's executed evidence; lab wire-marking verification under a partial rewrite-rule remains outstanding.

## PR #16983 — userspace-dp: select NAT64 tunnel MSS with translated family (#16511) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16511-nat64-tunnel-mss-family`

Refs #16511

## Why
The NAT64 builder selected the tunnel-egress TCP MSS clamp with the ingress `ForwardPacketMeta`, so a v4->v6 SYN-ACK into GRE/WG was budgeted as IPv4 and advertised an MSS 20 bytes above the IPv6 tunnel budget (1436 instead of 1416 on a 1500-byte transport), making full-size segments depend on ICMPv6 PTB. The v6->v4 direction was 20 bytes low (safe but wrong).

## What
- `frame/mod.rs`: compute `nat64_translated_meta` once in `build_nat64_forwarded_frames_with_commit_and_dynamic`, select the MSS with the emitted family, and reuse that meta for GRE/WG encapsulation.
- `tx/dispatch/slow_path.rs`: flip the family the same way for NAT64 (static-only site, kept consistent).
- Tests: `nat64_gre_mss_uses_translated_family_16511` (both directions through the real GRE builder: 1436 forward / 1416 reverse) and `nat64_wg_mss_uses_translated_family_16511` (selection-layer WG twin: 1385 v4 / 1365 v6).
- `docs/log/16511.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16511`: 2 passed
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15948 14664 8896`: 23 passed
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16511 15948` (after mutation restore): 15 passed
- Mutation: reverting to ingress-meta selection fails the GRE cell (1416 vs expected 1436)

## Risk
Low — only SYN/SYN-ACK MSS selection for NAT64 tunnel egress changes; non-tunnel NAT64 keeps the all-tcp value (family-independent), unknown ingress families still fail closed in the inner builder. Residual: WG twin is pinned at the selection layer, not end-to-end through an established WG session.

## PR #16989 — userspace-dp: suppress per-page status in paged owner-RG export (#16518) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16518-campaign`

## Why
`ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` drops `m.mu` for each page RPC and applied that page's attached helper status on re-lock behind only a proc/procGen/generation/socket fence. A disarm queued behind the page on `controlReqMu` applies its fresh DISARMED status first, and the pager then overwrites it with the older ARMED page status — `userspace_ctrl.Enabled=1` and `lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true` while the helper is disarmed until the next page or the 1 Hz poll. Durable fail-closed disarms (protocol-failure / unsupported-publish) are the consequential case.

## What
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/owner_rg_export_paging_9344.go`: every page request now sets `SuppressStatus: true` and the per-page `applyHelperStatusLocked` is dropped; after the generation fence the pager re-reads the cached `m.lastStatus`. Both production callers (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_export.go:72,133`) discard the returned status, and helper truth keeps flowing in RPC order through the 1 Hz poll and explicit state verbs, keeping `applyHelperStatusLocked` the single writer in RPC order.
- NOT changed: unpaged `ExportOwnerRGSessions`, which holds `m.mu` across its single RPC, so no ordering gap exists there.
- New regression cell `TestExportPagedDoesNotApplyStalePageStatus16518`: fake helper deliberately ignores `SuppressStatus` and attaches a ready ARMED status on a #6994-seamed manager (where that status would enable ctrl), asserts every wire request carries `suppress_status=true`, ctrl never enabled, and neither cached nor returned status is armed — with a direct-apply control proving the fixture arms. The #9699 paged cell now asserts a status-bearing reply no longer fails the window.
- Changelog `docs/log/16518.md`.

Refs #16518

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean.
- Targeted: `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestExportPagedDoesNotApplyStalePageStatus16518|TestOwnerRGExport|TestPagedOwnerRGExportReturnsNoDeltasWithAStatusError9699|TestExportOwnerRGSessionsReturnsNoDeltasWithAStatusError9699|TestRuntimeOwnerRGExport' -count=1 -v` → 21 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `TestOwnerRGExportPageFitsTheResponseCap9344` (estimated 1863 below reflected worst-case 2001), reproduced identically on clean origin/master `07bede5e6a` — base-attributed, unrelated wire-size drift.
- #9344/#15161/#9856/#9699 paging cells stay green (included above).

## Risk
Returned `ProcessStatus` from a paged export is now the cached status at the generation fence rather than the last page's fresh status; both production callers discard it. Poll-path behaviour otherwise unchanged.

## PR #16995 — userspace-dp: send WG cookie replies unthrottled under load (#16526) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16526-campaign`

Refs #16526

## Why

Under load, `WgEngine::classify_initiation` gated every valid-MAC1,
MAC2-absent initiation on `CookieChecker::source_reply_allowed` — a
20/s, burst-5 token bucket keyed on the **unauthenticated** datagram
source (IPv4 /32, IPv6 /64, port ignored). MAC1 proves only knowledge
of the responder public key (public by design), so an off-path
spoofer forges valid-MAC1 initiations with a victim peer's address
(any port, or any address in the victim's /64) and spends the
victim's reply budget. The victim's own initiations are then dropped
silently without a cookie, blocking victim-initiated handshakes —
roaming / remote-access peers hardest — for the length of the flood.
The va69 research probe measured `victim_cookies` 0/434 under a 1 kpps
same-source spoof flood.

Both references reply unthrottled and rate-limit only MAC2-valid
packets: wireguard-go `SendHandshakeCookie` has no limiter and
`rate.limiter.Allow` runs only after `CheckMAC2` succeeds; Linux
`wg_cookie_validate_packet` runs `wg_ratelimiter_allow` only after
the MAC2 compare and sends the cookie whenever `packet_needs_cookie`.
A cookie reply (64 B) is also smaller than the triggering initiation
(148 B), so unthrottled replies are not amplification.

## What

- `engine.rs classify_initiation`: the `source_reply_allowed` gate is
  deleted; the MAC2-absent arm builds the cookie reply unthrottled.
  `Drop` remains only when the reply cannot be built (fail-closed on
  a broken CSPRNG, #4094 BUG-2). No other arm changes (not-under-load
  `Process`; bad-MAC1 `Process` with no reply — no reflection;
  valid-MAC2 → #9908 admission → `Process`).
- `cookie.rs`: `source_reply_allowed`, its bucket map, the reply
  token constants (`SOURCE_REPLIES_PER_SEC`, `SOURCE_REPLY_BURST`,
  `PACKET_COST_NS`, `MAX_TOKENS_NS`) and its test hooks are removed —
  clean cutover, no dead bucket. The surviving #9908
  `source_handshake_allowed` bucket (the only source-keyed limit, and
  only for MAC2-valid packets an attacker cannot forge) keeps

## PR #16996 — config: resolve annotate targets by full identity (#16523) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16523`

Refs #16523

## Why
AnnotatePath resolved through navigatePathWidth, the pair-consuming display walker. A node with 3+ keys and an odd count (the 3-key address-book leaf 'address a1 10.0.0.1/32') cannot be addressed: the walker consumes the (address, a1) pair then descends into the leaf's nil children for 10.0.0.1/32 and returns nil. FormatSet emits the full identity in its annotate line, so load set of display-set output and load merge of a commented file aborted atomically with path not found, breaking the #15718 round-trip contract.

## What
- AnnotatePath (pkg/config/ast.go) now tries an exact-identity walk first (new resolveExactPath): descend level by level choosing the sibling matchNodeKeysFull matches against the remaining path (exact whole-key-list preferred over proper prefix, then widest consumption), resolving only when the whole path is consumed exactly.
- Falls back to the existing navigatePath display walk, preserving prefix addressing (name-only, bare keyword landing on the first sibling per #3980, wider node by leading keys) and fail-closed ErrPathNotFound mutating nothing.
- Tests: pkg/config/annotate_odd_arity_16523_test.go (flat + hierarchical 3-key leaf, FormatSet replay round-trip, prefix-fallback controls, mutation-free not-found) and pkg/configstore/annotate_odd_arity_16523_test.go (ShowCandidateSet export to LoadSet, flat + hierarchical LoadMerge, re-export pins the single a1 line). Changelog docs/log/16523.md.

## Validation
- go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestAnnotateOddArity — pass (4 tests).
- TestAnnotationSurfaces15718 / TestAnnotationChangedValue15718 (#15718) — pass.
- go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run '16523|TestAnnotateMultiKeyContainers|TestAnnotate' (#4587 + store round-trips) — pass; bounded pkg/configstore verb-group run passes.
- RED-verified by removing only the resolveExactPath call: leaf/round-trip/LoadSet/flat-LoadMerge cells fail with the original path-not-found error; prefix/not-found controls green on both sides.
- Full ./pkg/config/ shows 65 failures plus a TestDualASTDifferential panic that reproduce identically on unmodified origin/master (same 65 named tests run there) — no new failure from this change.

## Risk
Low. Confined to AnnotatePath resolution; the fallback is the previous walker unchanged, so every previously-resolving path lands on the same node. The exact walk only adds resolution for full-identity paths that previously errored, and non-matching paths still fail closed mutating nothing.

## PR #16999 — userspace-dp: fragment tunnel outer below IPv6 for sub-1280 budgets (#16512) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16512-campaign`

Why:
An IPv6 inner in (budget, 1280] over a GRE/WireGuard tunnel whose derived inner budget is below 1280 (GRE-1300 gives 1276) got `EmitPacketTooBig{1280}` and was dropped. RFC 8201 §4 forbids the sender reducing below 1280, so the PTB can never resolve it: every non-TCP IPv6 datagram in that band, including 1280-byte DNS-EDNS and QUIC, was permanently blackholed.

What:
Deliver the band by link-specific fragmentation below IPv6 (RFC 8200 §5). New `outer_frag::fragment_outer_ipv4_frame` is the single outer-fragment writer. The TX dispatcher (and deferred neighbor-replay) diverts the band from PTB+drop to building the tunnel outer and fragmenting it at the outer MTU. GRE outers are built DF-clear for exactly this band; WG transit admits the band past the encap guard; the WG TUN-origin path sends via the kernel UDP socket whose IP stack fragments. IPv6 outers, inners >1280, fragmented inners, IPv4 inners, and plain sub-1280 links keep PTB+drop. 1400/1500 controls unchanged.

Validation:
- `cargo check` clean.
- New cells: outer_frag reassembly/DF/eligibility (3 passed); icmp_ptb sub-1280 predicate + GRE-1300/1280 regression + 1400 control; GRE-1300 encap guard/budget.
- Affected suites: 191 passed, 1 failed — `tunnel_wg_nodf_oversize_emits_ptb_with_inner_mtu_10705` (left 1340, right 1325), base-attributed on clean e533191ef7 (stale expectation after #16499), not caused by this change.

Risk:
Outer fragmentation adds reassembly load at the tunnel peer, bounded by the existing #14645/#15102 pool. Only sub-1280 underlays take the new branch.

Refs #16512

## PR #17000 — userspace-dp: honour configured gr- logical MTU on GRE transit (#16514) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16514-gre-logical-mtu`

Refs #16514

## Why
A configured `interfaces gr-… [unit N] mtu` was accepted and applied to the kernel anchor but never used on userspace transit. `native_gre_inner_mtu` — the SSOT for the PTB decision, the GRE MSS clamp and TCP re-segmentation — derived the inner budget only from the physical transport MTU, so DF flows larger than the configured MTU were encapsulated instead of answered with Frag-Needed/PTB and SYNs were clamped to the physical-derived MSS (1436 rather than 1360 for MTU 1400): a PMTUD black hole on a smaller downstream underlay path.

## What
- Carry `TunnelEndpointSnapshot.mtu` into `TunnelEndpoint.mtu`, validated by a new `TunnelMtu` newtype (negative fails the snapshot closed via `InterfaceMtuInvalid`; 0 stays the non-limiting unknown sentinel). The Go producer already emitted this value (`MTU: iface.MTU` — configured unit MTU else kernel anchor MTU); pinned by a Go test assertion.
- Cap the physical-derived budget in `native_gre_inner_mtu` with `min_nonzero_mtu(physical_inner, endpoint.mtu)`. GRE only — WireGuard keeps its physical-underlay derivation (#2680/#2684), and the #2331 encap drop guard stays physical-only (documented in `gre.rs`).
- Unconfigured GRE anchors default to 1500, so `min(1476, 1500)` keeps existing values bit-for-bit.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16514 post_transform_inner_mtu_gre tunnel_mtu_negative native_gre_inner_mtu` — 8 passed: logical 1400 → PTB inner MTU 1400 / MSS 1360 (incl. NAT64-over-GRE composition), logical 1500 and unknown 0 keep 1476 / 1436, smaller transport (1400) keeps 1376, negative tunnel MTU fails the build closed, existing `post_transform_inner_mtu_gre_*` cells green.
- Broader GRE/PTB filter (`post_transform_ native_gre tunnel_tcp_mss select_tcp_mss 10705`): 80 passed, 1 failed — `tunnel_wg_nodf_oversize_emits_ptb_with_inner_mtu_10705` (left 1340, right 1325), which fails identically on unmodified origin/master `e533191ef7` in a scratch worktree (pre-existing WG pad-expectation drift, unrelated).
- Go: `TestBuildTunnelEndpointSnapshotsBuildsUnitEndpoint` passes with the new MTU pin.

## Risk
Low. The cap only lowers the GRE inner budget when a logical MTU below the physical-derived value is present. No fail-open weakening: a negative MTU now fails the snapshot closed instead of collapsing to the permissive 0.

Residuals: component-level only, matching the issue's executed evidence (no end-to-end PMTUD black-hole reproduction on a smaller downstream hop); the local-origin TUN path keeps the kernel anchor MTU, unchanged.

A designation wins the shared-ifindex merge in either row order and off the consistently-zoned path, tracked via two build-time `ForwardingState` sets. RED on base `interfaces.rs`: `shared_ifindex_designated_primary_wins_over_base_row_16513` fails with the exact reported `InterfaceSharedIfindexAttributeConflict { ifindex: 42, attribute: "primary_v4", first_value: "10.0.0.10", second_value: "10.0.0.9" }`; `..._when_not_consistently_zoned_16513` fails with the silent `Some(10.0.0.10)` pick. Acceptance cells: `egress[42].primary_v4 == 10.0.0.9` / `primary_v6 == 2001:db8::9` in both row orders; unmarked control keeps `.10/::10`; tunnel units with different primaries still accepted.

## PR #17004 — upgrade: preserve post-rollback commits on ROLLINGBACK resume (#16529) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16529-rollback-rerestore`

Why:
A non-operator ROLLINGBACK journal preserved by the #14721 health gate leaves the rolled-back daemon running against the restored DB, but carried no record that the restore had already run. The next `xpfd upgrade` resumed it through `rollback()`, STOPped the healthy daemon, re-restored the cut-boundary snapshot over every commit made since the rollback, and deleted `ConfigDBDir.old` with no copy — durable config and configstore-history loss from a routine re-run (or the next apt postinst cut).

What:
- `pkg/upgrade/state.go`: new `Journal.AutoRollbackDBRestored`, the auto-path twin of the operator-only `RollbackDBRestored`.
- `pkg/upgrade/flip.go` (`rollback()`): persist the bit BEFORE the swap and again after `StartUnit`; on resume adopt it from legacy residue (surviving `.old`, live==snapshot byte-identity, or `current` already naming `PreviousVersion` on a ROLLINGBACK journal — which proves the mandatory restore-before-flip order already ran) and skip the restore. If `current` already names the destination and the daemon re-proves healthy, complete WITHOUT stopping it or touching its DB.
- `pkg/upgrade/rollback.go`: same fast path + pre-swap bit persistence + lost-save healing for the operator flavour.
- `restoreDBSnapshotWithRetention`'s byte-identity guard now applies to both flavours.
- Docs: `docs/in-place-upgrade.md` preserved-journal section + `docs/log/16529.md`.

NOT changed: first-restore snapshot/retention semantics, the forward cut, and the #14721 non-nil rolled-back outcome contract.

Validation:
- New `pkg/upgrade/rollback_rerestore_16529_test.go` (5 tests) drives the exact reported trace for legacy (no bit) and bitted journals, the healthy control, the identity guard keeping `.old`, and the operator flavour — all pass.
- RED proof: with `flip.go`/`rollback.go`/`cutover.go` reverted (field kept), the legacy cell fails with the commit destroyed plus a STOP (`calls: [stop dropin daemon-reload start health:1.0.0]`, matching the issue's probe), the identity cell fails with `.old destroyed`, and the operator cell fails with a STOP.
- Full `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -count=1` passes (97s); `go vet ./pkg/upgrade/` clean; gofmt clean.

Risk:
Resume trusts `current==PreviousVersion` + `AdvancedStateFloor` as proof the restore ran; that follows from `rollback()`'s mandatory restore-before-flip order, and a mid-restore crash (current still the failed target) cannot satisfy it. A running daemon that reports healthy at resume is left running (the acceptance requirement); one that does not re-prove healthy still gets the full stop/flip/start with only the restore skipped.

Refs #16529
