## PR #17326 — config: reject colliding WireGuard listen sockets at commit (#16531) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16531-wg-listen-port-collision`

Refs #16531

## Why

Two WireGuard tunnels on one listen-port in the same routing instance — or one in the default instance plus one in any VRF — committed with no diagnostic. Each endpoint's helper control thread binds its own `[::]:port` socket with no `SO_REUSEADDR`/`SO_REUSEPORT` (wildcard for the default instance, `SO_BINDTODEVICE vrf-<instance>` otherwise), so the second bind fails `EADDRINUSE`, the thread exits and respawns every 3s, and that tunnel never completes a handshake. Spawn order decides which tunnel dies, so a helper restart can move the outage.

## What

Option one from the issue: refuse the collision at strict commit.

- New gate `validateWireguardListenPortCollisionStrict` (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard_listen_port_collision.go`), wired into `runTailGates` after the #9909 scope gate, with a `lenientWireguardListenPortCollision` downgrade (warning on load/peer-sync, #1960 no-brick).
- It walks `EmitTunnelEndpointNames` (the SSOT emitter, so one interface-level tunnel's merged units never self-collide and pure inheritance is deduped by object), resolves each endpoint's effective transport instance the way `buildTunnelEndpointSnapshots` does (explicit `tunnel routing-instance`, then RI interface-list membership via the #9909 helpers), and rejects a same-port pair whose sockets collide — same instance, or wildcard against anything — naming both tunnels, the port, and the instance. Distinct ports and two different VRFs on one port (disjoint `vrf-<instance>` binds) still commit.
- No `SO_REUSEPORT`/demux socket: reuseport would hash datagrams to an arbitrary engine and MAC1 under the wrong key would drop them.
- Corrected comments/docs presenting same-port as unqualifiedly supported: steering-gate dedup notes, `tunnelemit.go` merge rationale, `wg/decap.rs` #14326/#15123 selection comment, `docs/wireguard-interop.md`.
- `TestWireGuardSameListenPortDoesNotWarn_1434` asserted the colliding shape commits clean; it now asserts strict refusal (#16531) plus steering silence on the lenient path.

## Validation

- New `TestWireguardListenPortCollision16531`: same-instance, default+VRF, same-VRF by stanza and by interface-list membership all rejected naming both tunnels; distinct-port and VRF/VRF commit clean; lenient warns naming both tunnels/port; direct-gate nil/single/GRE cells clean; 25-iteration determinism. On unmodified master the test fails to build (gate absent) — the defect itself was confirmed at the source base by the research probe cited in the issue (strict-compile probe + netns/VRF socket probe).
- WG-focused tests (`-run 'Wireguard|WireGuard|Steered|Multiport'`): green except 6 failures byte-identical on unmodified origin/master (pre-existing degenerate-key/peerless fixtures).
- Full `pkg/config`: 65 failing test names on both this branch and unmodified origin/master — identical set, pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk

A config that previously committed with a colliding same-port pair is now refused at commit with both tunnels named. Already-committed configs still load with a warning and the colliding tunnel stays inert exactly as before. VRF/VRF same-port and distinct-port shapes unaffected. No existing gate weakened.

Containers and `FormatSet` are unchanged (#6668 zero-churn kept; public `display set` byte-identical). ## PR #17347 — userspace-dp: bound SYN-cookie challenge fence by pool spans (#16537) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16537-campaign-pub`

Refs #16537

## Why
`candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerated every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 `pool_v4` address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode; the caller cloned the vector and scanned it even with no bindless fence configured. A /16 pool costs 65536 `NatDecision`s (~3 MB built/merged/cloned) per challenged SYN — a modest flood saturates every worker.

## What
- Precompute contiguous pool spans once at parse/build: `SourceNatRule::pool_ranges_v4/v6`, `Nat64Prefix::pool_ranges_v4` (a /16 is one span).
- `BindlessIpsecSelectorFence::matches_with_pool_ranges`: O(spans x selector rows) range intersection, no per-SYN allocation.
- `challenge_source_nat_shape` keeps the allocation-failure shape check O(1) at rule level; `syn_cookie_challenge_fence` returns `NoCandidate/Clear/Fenced`.
- Dead `candidate_source_nat_translations` enumerator removed. #15947 fence semantics preserved (any pool address suppresses; NAT64 deterministic prefixes keep any-address semantics, a conservative superset).

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16537`: 6 passed (one-span /16 collapse, challenge shape incl. failure + off cells, fence unit cells, /16 unfenced-reply and fence-on-last-address end-to-end).
- RED on base: new tests fail to compile (`ChallengeSourceNat` / `pool_ranges_v4` do not exist pre-fix).
- `15947` suite: 30 passed; `post_snat_fence`: 2 passed; `unfenced_challenge` (no retained allocation): passed.

## Risk
Lab flood with a /16 pool (worker pps vs interface-mode SNAT) not run in this lane; pool-size independence is pinned structurally by the one-span assertion. See `docs/log/16537.md`.

## PR #17350 — config: refuse one-child multi-token value blocks (#16535) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16535-multi-token-block`

Refs #16535

## Summary
The parser admits a sixth spelling of a two-element value list, `leaf { v1 v2; }` (one block child with Keys=[v1 v2]), that the #2419 spelling differential and #6697/#7126 slot-escape gates omitted. `validateMultiValueLeaf` checked only `c.Keys[:1]`, so:
- a rejected second value could commit and reach compilers that read every child key (e.g. RA `dns-server-address` via `firewallMatchValues`), and
- `Keys[0]` readers (`proxyARPAddressValues`) silently dropped a valid second proxy-ARP address.

## Fix
- `validateMultiValueLeaf` (typed multi leaves) and `walkSchemaNode` (untyped multi leaves such as proxy-arp `address`, whose values the compiler strict gate checks) now REFUSE a multi-token block child: one value per statement inside a value block. The error suggests the separate-statement or bracket spellings.
- Leaves with `allChildKeysAreValues` are exempt: their compiler reads every child key, and every token is validated there instead.
- Added form `G-hier-one-child-multi-token` to `TestSlotEscapeSweep`. The compiled-output differential deliberately still carries no such form (non-Junos spelling; 30 `Keys[0]` readers would be false defects) and now documents the validation-side closure.
- `docs/config-schema.md` updated; changelog in `docs/log/16535.md`.

## Acceptance
- Sixth-form sweep: 0 escapes (`TestSlotEscapeSweep` PASS, includes form G).
- One-child proxy-arp row is refused; bracket and one-per-statement spellings compile both addresses (`TestProxyARPOneChildRowCompilesBothOrRefused16535`).

## Tests
- New: `TestOneChildMultiTokenBlockRefused16535`, `TestProxyARPOneChildRowCompilesBothOrRefused16535`, `TestOneChildMultiTokenAllChildKeysValidated16535`, `TestOneChildMultiTokenRADNSRefused16535`, `TestSlotEscapeFormsIncludeSixth16535` — all PASS.
- Targeted: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestOneChild|TestProxyARPOneChild|TestSlotEscapeFormsInclude|TestSchemaValidate|TestWalker|TestRADNS|TestSSHKeyExchangeValidator|TestProxyARP|TestNameServerModifier|TestFirewallMatchValues'` — PASS.
- Pre-existing failures unchanged vs origin/master baseline (verified by stash comparison): TestSlotEscapeCoverage (29 no-verdict sites), TestSlotEscapeTable wireguard degenerate-key fixtures, TestCompilerStampsImplicitSourceNATScopes12525, TestMultipleWithinClausesUnaffected6771, TestMultiLeafAbsorptionPopulation9206, TestMultisiteAdmissionsAreRecorded8921.

## Risk
A persisted `leaf { v1 v2; }` on a non-exempt multi leaf now fails strict commit instead of committing with the second value dropped/unvalidated — intended fail-closed. The tolerant load/peer-sync path downgrades typed-leaf errors to warnings (#1960), so such a config still boots.

## PR #17360 — dhcp: honor server-supplied T1/T2 renewal timers (#16553) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16553-server-t1t2`

Why: The client never read server T1/T2 (IA_NA/IA_PD T1/T2 or DHCPv4 options 58/59); `renewalTimers` was always 50%/87.5% of the single IA_NA `LeaseTime`. A delegated prefix whose valid lifetime ended before that T1 was pruned, withdrawn from LAN RA, and only re-requested at the IA_NA T1, recurring every cycle — violating RFC 8415 §18.2.4 (Renew/Rebind not later than the earliest T1/T2 of any binding) and RFC 2131 §4.4.5 (0.5/0.875 are only defaults).

What: Carry `RenewAt`/`RebindAt` on `Lease` (IA_NA T1/T2 via new `ianaTimers`, or v4 options 58/59) and on `DelegatedPrefix` (IA_PD T1/T2), preserved across `carryForwardV6IANA`. New `renewalSchedule` in `commit.go`: earliest non-zero T1/T2 across the lease plus held PDs, per-tier fallback to 50%/87.5% of the shortest held valid lifetime, clamped to `0 < T1 < T2 < shortest-valid` for finite lifetimes. Both run loops use it; `renewalTimers` remains the no-server-timer wrapper. `LeaseTime` stays the expiry anchor.

Validation: New `pkg/dhcp/server_t1t2_16553_test.go` — 13-row `renewalSchedule` table (T1=60s acceptance, IA_PD T1=1s defect cell, one-sided fallbacks, degenerate clamps), parse-level IA_NA+IA_PD timer carriage with a no-timer control, DHCPv4 options 58/59, and two `runDHCPv6` seam cells asserting ~1s (server) / ~50s (fallback) T1 waits with the PD still in `DelegatedPrefixesForRA` at Renew. RED verified by neutralizing the server/PD terms in `renewalSchedule` (all five new entry points failed, restored green). `go vet ./pkg/dhcp/` clean; `go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1` passes including the updated #14998 anchoring assertion.

Risk: PD T1/T2 anchor at the lease `Obtained` like IA_NA timers (a Reply normally grants both together). Server T1/T2 at/after expiry are clamped pre-expiry rather than honored literally.

Refs #16553

## PR #17365 — config: group zero intervals and fold nullable repetitions (#16551) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16551-aspath-quantifier`

Why:
`parseTermWithOperator` emitted `wrapped + "{0}"` for `{0}` / `{0,0}`, but the wrapped base is often not a single ERE atom (a multi-digit AS number, the `.` token `[0-9]+`, a range fragment ending in a character class), so the interval bound only the last character and `65000{0}` matched the unrelated AS 6500 instead of zero copies of AS 65000. Separately, `{m}` / `{m,}` / `{m,n}` with m>=1 on a nullable single-token base demanded a `" <term>"` separator for every non-first copy even when that copy was empty, so `(65000?){2}` rejected the single-token path `65000` that Junos accepts. A `from as-path` term with these shapes therefore matched a different route set than the operator wrote, affecting BGP route acceptance.

What:
- `pkg/config/aspath_junos_translate.go`: attach `{0}` to a parenthesised `grouped` atom so the interval always zeroes the whole term. For single-token nullable bases, emit bounded repetitions as 0..hi present tokens joined by single spaces (stripping the whole-path `^$` null marker that can never match inside a repetition); `{m,}` on such a base is the `*` language. Multi-token nullable bases keep the copy form, since collapsing them to a token count would admit cross-copy token mixes Junos forbids. NOT changed: `*`, `+`, `?`, `{0,n}`, and non-nullable repetition output.
- `pkg/config/aspath_translate_16551_test.go`: regression cells covering the three reported mismatch rows, zero intervals on AS/range/set/dot bases, exact and ranged nullable repetitions in isolation and in concatenation, and controls pinning previously-correct shapes.
- `docs/log/16551.md`: per-issue action log.

Validation:
- Probe-first: the reported rows reproduced pre-fix (`65000{0} 65001` -> `^(65000{0} )?65001$` matching `6500 65001`; `(65000?){2}` rejecting `65000`).
- RED-on-revert: the new tests fail on the base translator with exactly those mismatches (13 assertion failures across the two test functions).
- Post-fix (at head 43b92e6ac5, after rebase onto origin/master 18a54f189f): `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestTranslateJunos|TestASPath|TestASNumericRange'` passes (16 tests, including the #15007 table/rejects/range-oracle suite); `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; gofmt clean.
- Full `./pkg/config/` and `./pkg/frr/` runs show failure sets identical to the branch base `04cf7a6bd2` (66 pre-existing pkg/config failures, 4 pre-existing pkg/frr failures, base-attributed in a clean worktree at that SHA).

Risk:
Residual: repetitions of multi-token nullable groups (for example `(65000 (65001?)){2}` with a partially empty copy) keep their pre-existing separator behaviour — outside the reported scope and deliberately unchanged. No other translator shapes change output.

Refs #16551

## PR #17367 — userspace-dp: fence neighbor MACs at snapshot build boundary (#16555) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16555-campaign`

Why: #13951 fenced the Go neighbor mirror verb, but a config apply rebuilt neighbors unconditionally from the Go snapshot (a mirror of the same kernel table), so a spoof-updated kernel MAC was laundered into the static table -- which wins lookup -- and the fence then defended the attacker MAC against the genuine one. The stored snapshot also kept the raw rows, so rebind/arm rebuilt the laundered binding. Every transit flow via the poisoned next hop (typically the default gateway) is exposed until the kernel row reverts.

What: `forwarding_build::fenced_neighbor_mac` is now the single #13951 accept rule (differing MAC accepted only when NUD_PERMANENT or the monitor dynamic entry confirms it, else prior static/dynamic MAC retained), used by `populate_neighbors` (now previous + dynamic), `Coordinator::apply_manager_neighbors_with_permanent`, and `Coordinator::fence_snapshot_neighbors`. The live dynamic map is threaded through the production preparsed builds (same-plan refresh, full reconcile); validation builds keep `None`. The stored snapshot now carries the fenced accepted set: `neighbors.rs` reads MACs back from the live forwarding table, `snapshot.rs` fences the stored candidate on every successful apply leg and clears the digest on change. NOT changed: Go publishing; lookup precedence.

Validation: `cargo check --bin xpf-userspace-dp` passed. New cells `snapshot_refresh_cannot_launder_refused_neighbor_mac_16555` (va71 subject), `reconcile_build_cannot_launder_refused_neighbor_mac_16555` (full-reconcile twin), `update_neighbors_stores_fenced_mac_not_refused_raw_16555`, `apply_snapshot_stores_fenced_neighbor_mac_16555`, plus `manager_neighbor_mirror_cannot_replace_live_mac_without_confirmation_13951` and the 12195/3771_9520 cells: 11 passed. RED evidence: neutralising `fenced_neighbor_mac` fails all 5 fence cells. `server::tests` 440 passed; `coordinator::tests` 212 passed / 3 failed and `forwarding::tests` 338 passed / 1 failed, all base-attributed on origin/master in a pristine worktree.

Risk: A legitimate unconfirmed MAC change now converges only via the monitor's probe-confirmed dynamic learn or a permanent row, on every apply path -- the #13951 invariant extended, not a new gate. First-ever installs and dynamic-confirmed changes are unaffected. No fail-open weakening.

## PR #17372 — dhcp: persist leases across graceful restart (#16566) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16566-lease-persist`

Refs #16566

## Why
On graceful restart only the kernel address survived: the new Manager had empty `Leases()`, the startup apply rendered FRR/DNS/PD-RA from nothing (withdrawing DHCP routes), and the client restarted at DISCOVER/SOLICIT. A restart during an upstream DHCP outage lost WAN egress for the whole outage despite a still-valid lease.

## What
- Persist every committed lease durably (`pkg/dhcp/lease_persist.go`, fsatomic DurableState): address, gateway, classless routes, DNS, server-id/DUID, Obtained/LeaseTime, PDs.
- Re-adopt at startup when unexpired and the kernel still holds the address (`AdoptPersistedLeases` from `reconcileDHCPClients`, one-shot, + `Start` backstop) so the first apply renders it.
- Resume in the renewal cycle: renewal loops extracted verbatim to `runV4RenewalCycle`/`runV6RenewalCycle`; first wire message after restart is RENEWING REQUEST / RENEW, falling back to INIT on expiry/NAK/NoBinding/refusal. Expiry/NAK/teardown delete persisted state.
- README restart contract corrected.

## Validation
- RED: `TestRestartLosesLeasePreFix16566` (pre-existing seams only) fails on clean origin/master (`Leases() = 0` after simulated restart); passes post-fix.
- 6 new `16566` cells: adoption rendering (address/gateway/classless/DNS), expired + kernel-missing rejection, first-wire RENEW v4+v6, PD re-adoption, NAK deletion.
- Full `pkg/dhcp` suite green. Daemon DHCP tests green except `TestFilterDHCPConfigForMasterRGs_TaggedRethUnitMatches` (fails identically on clean origin/master — base-attributed).

## Risk
Persist failure only logs and degrades to pre-fix restart behavior; never fails a commit. Kernel AddrList gates adoption so kernel-expired addresses are never resurrected. Lab restart-during-outage verification outstanding.

## PR #17378 — ddns: thread every ambiguous cleanup candidate and keep a bounded list (#16578) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16578`

Refs #16578

Fixes R3-A40-03 (residual of #15225 A40-02): Surface A threaded ambiguous cleanup candidates only when there were more than one and kept a single ambiguous slot, so two lost-reply shapes orphaned a live value.

Arm 1 (first-publish reply lost + renumber): pending row yields one candidate; the `>1` gate threaded nothing → Insert-only → orphan. Arm 2 (three renumbers in an outage): single slot overwritten each time → earliest desired lost.

Fix: drop the gate (thread every candidate != new value; backends already union PrevAddr+PrevAddrs), and keep a bounded append-only candidate list (`AmbiguousPriorAddrTexts`, max 16 FIFO) with the legacy slot folded in on load and synced to the first element. Withdraw deletes every candidate; loader validates them.

## PR #17382 — ddns: treat percent-escaped template values as literals (#16573) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16573-ddns-percent`

Refs #16573

Why:
Both mirrored generic-template detectors (pkg/config
`ddnsTemplateCarriesLiteralToken`, pkg/ddns `templateCarriesLiteralToken`)
treated any value containing `%` as specifier-only, so a percent-escaped
credential (`%2B`/`%2F`/`%3D`, e.g. a base64 token) over `http://` was
neither refused at commit nor by the runtime construction/issuance belts,
yet `renderGenericURL` transmits unknown `%x` verbatim — the credential
went out in cleartext on every update.

What:
- Both detectors now strip only recognised specifiers
  (`%h`/`%i`/`%u`/`%p`/`%%`) and terminated `{{...}}` placeholders and
  count any remaining byte as literal (`ddnsTemplateValueHasLiteral` /
  `templateValueHasLiteral`, kept in lockstep).
- A percent-escaped keyless query component (`?%2B%2F%3D`) and an
  empty-key escaped value count too. A plain keyless flag (`?flag`) stays
  a pinned value-less control (the #15225 tests pin `?flag&ip=%i` as
  accepted), as do specifier-only, placeholder-only, https and loopback
  http templates. An unterminated `{{` is verbatim, hence literal.
- NOT changed: `RedactURL` path handling — a credential-named path pair
  is already echoed via `RedactURL` in refusal errors pre-fix (documented
  there: scheme/host/path prefix preserved); out of scope.

Validation:
- New `TestDDNS16573*` in pkg/config and pkg/ddns: escaped, mixed,
  trailing-`%`, unknown-specifier, unterminated-placeholder,
  escaped-keyless/empty-key and escaped path-pair probes refused at
  strict compile, lenient drop, construction and issuance;
  specifier/placeholder/loopback controls accepted, including a loopback
  publish proving the escaped token is sent verbatim there.
- RED-on-revert verified: forcing the helpers back to the `%`-free
  predicate turns the new tests RED (config probes compile/classify
  false; the ddns issuance belt proceeds to a request).
- `go test -count=1 ./pkg/ddns/` — ok (18.5s, full package).
- `go test -count=1 -run TestDDNS16573 ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/ddns/` — ok.
- Adjacent config DDNS subset
  (`TestDDNS16573|15225|14386|Credentialed|Generic|Plaintext`):
  2 failures, both base-attributed on origin/master `db1b9a1fb7`
  (verified on a pristine worktree): `TestDDNSGenericAtInPathQueryNotMisclassified`
  (`?x=a@b` — pre-existing #15225 literal-value widening, not this change)
  and `TestDDNSPlaintextCheckIPURLRejected` Surface-A fixture
  (`#15034` vlan error, unrelated).

Risk:
An http:// generic template whose query value contains a non-specifier
`%` (including `%%` inside a mixed value) is now refused where it
previously compiled; operators must move such templates to https:// —
the intended credential gate. No behaviour change for https or loopback.

The SessionClose/SessionCreate queue budget (per-kind ceil((8192/2)/5)=820) was released only on ACK trim, not on channel drain. With the Go ACK on a 100ms tick, close/create bursts above 820 per ACK interval shed QueueFull — losing NetFlow/IPFIX closes (and whole flows whose CREATE shed, #16303) and session-close RT_FLOW records, defeating the #14609 never-shed contract. The #14609 test modelled a release-on-drain production never had.

## What
- Release telemetry budget exactly once at channel exit: steady-state drain_channel_into_write_buf (before replay push), dormant handle_drain_request channel drain, shutdown drain_remaining (unchanged).
- Replay retention holds no slot (bounded by REPLAY_BUFFER_CAPACITY, #2382 eviction counting unchanged): pop/evict/shutdown replay drains no longer release.
- No admission cap, GCRA, counter, or HA type-2 behaviour changed.
- Tests: new test_session_close_burst_5000_without_ack_16570 (real producer + real drain, no ACK); #14609 cell now uses real drain; budget cells rewritten via real connected loop. No budget seeding for retained frames.
- Docs: event_stream README, budget/replay/drain/producer comments, debian/changelog, docs/log/16570.md.

## Validation
- RED: burst cell fails without drain release; GREEN after.
- cargo test event_stream::: 120 passed, 1 pre-existing failure pptp_open_frame_carries_the_call_id_pair_13965 reproduced identically on pristine base 5b565d8c54 (unrelated).
- rustfmt clean on changed Rust files. Based on 5b565d8c54; origin/master advanced (incl. #16579 docs touching README/rt_flow.rs) — rebase may need trivial doc merges.

## Risk
In-channel bound unchanged; bursts above GCRA (8192/s/zone) or channel/backlog capacity still shed counted, as designed. Helper-internal accounting only; no wire change.

## PR #17386 — ha: release holder-less import reservation on accepted delete (#16575) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16575`

Refs #16575

## Why
An import whose `UpsertSynced` fan-out is refused (repair debt, worker queue at 4096) reserves `Untracked` (`holders==0`). If the peer delete's push is then accepted before the worker reaches the repair boundary, the worker drains a `DeleteSynced` for a session it never adopted — its local table has no entry, so `handle_delete_synced`'s alias-gated release never runs, and no sweep touches `Untracked` records. One `(pool_addr, port)` leaks per event on the standby until helper restart, surfacing as `AllocatorExhausted` after failover.

## What
- `delete_synced_session_gen_marked` now, after a successful shared removal of a forward entry, calls `release_unadopted_import_reservation_untracked` (SNAT untracked + NAT64 untracked-for-purge against the same runtime view). It frees only `holders==0` records, so an adopted twin survives for the last worker's own teardown and frees exactly once.
- An actual free increments `tunnel_purge_reservations_released` so the tunnel purge's own untracked sweep keeps its #8138/#14961 count when it no-ops after this delete; counter doc updated.
- Tests: SNAT + NAT64 defect cells (refused import, accepted delete, drain+repair), refused-delete Control A, accepted-delete Control B, two-worker adopted twin.
- Changelog: `docs/log/16575.md`.

## Validation
`cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16575 6979_f4 14961 6600`: 19 passed. Defect cells RED with the fix disabled (SNAT PORT_HELD=true, NAT64 active_flows stayed 1), GREEN with it; Controls A/B and adopted twin green both ways. Post-rebase smoke (16575+14961): 12 passed.

## Risk
Low — the untracked release is holders==0-only by construction (`drop_holder_locked` keeps adopted records), keyed on the removed forward entry's exact NAT decision, no-op for reverse/non-NAT entries; no gate weakened. Counter `tunnel_purge_reservations_released` now also counts holder-less frees from ordinary synced deletes (documented).

## PR #17389 — routing: stop config apply re-upping keepalive-down GRE tunnels (#16582) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16582`

Refs #16582

## Summary
During a peer outage, any config apply re-upped a keepalive-down GRE tunnel: the dataplane zone loop (`mapZoneInterface`) `LinkSetUp`'d every zoned netdev after `ApplyTunnels` honoured `skipUp`, and the runner's down edge (`state.Up && Failures>=MaxRetries`) never fired again. Both fix options from the issue are implemented:

1. **Held-down predicate (prevention):** `tunnelManager.TunnelHeldDown` / `Manager.TunnelHeldDown` (runner present, `Up==false`, `Failures>=MaxRetries`). The daemon registers it as `dataplane.SetTunnelHeldDownResolver` (same injection shape as `SetProtectedInterfaceResolver` — pkg/dataplane must not import pkg/routing; lazy `d.routing` read since routing is built in phase 3). `mapZoneInterface` consults it by Linux netdev name before `LinkSetUp` and leaves a held-down tunnel down as an intentionally-down surface (same XDP-skip disposition as `disable`, so arm-coverage does not report it uncovered). Zone admin writes move behind `zoneLinkSetUpSeam`/`zoneLinkSetDownSeam` so the guard is bindable in tests.
2. **Runner robustness (correction):** `keepaliveTick` arms `wantDown` at `Failures>=MaxRetries` regardless of `state.Up`, suppresses it only when the link is observed admin DOWN (IFF_UP clear), and re-downs an externally re-upped link on the next dead tick. A re-down does not re-fire the liveness-change callback. Generation guard, commit-after-success, and exactly-one-down steady state unchanged.

## Tests
- `TestKeepaliveExternalReupIsRedowned16582`: threshold down once → held-down silence → external re-up re-downed on next dead tick (second `LinkSetDown`, no spurious callback) → recovery still one `LinkSetUp`.
- `TestTunnelHeldDown16582`: predicate truth table + facade nil-guards.
- `TestZoneLoopLeavesKeepaliveHeldDownTunnelDown16582` through real `programZoneMaps`: held-down zoned tunnel gets zero `LinkSetUp`; `TestZoneLoopHeldDownControls16582`: no-resolver / not-held / other-name controls each get exactly one.

Counts: `go test ./pkg/routing/ -count=1` PASS (full package). Targeted `pkg/dataplane` 16582 + armproof + 14680 wiring PASS; `-count=5` on the new cells PASS. Full `pkg/dataplane -count=1` has one pre-existing unrelated failure (`TestOperatorPackagesDoNotImportBPFArtifactsDirectly` flags `pkg/conntrack/gc.go` cilium/ebpf import — untouched here, fails identically on origin/master). `go vet` + `gofmt` clean on changed Go files.

## Residuals
No live-cluster/FRR/Rust-FIB end-to-end run (research probes were likewise component-level); route/FIB re-selection consequence remains inferred from the documented `link_up` contract. Writers other than the zone loop (operator `ip link set up`, networkd) are corrected by the runner within one probe interval, not prevented.

## PR #17390 — routing: skip peer fabric bonds in chassis clusters (#16587) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16587`

Refs #16587

## Summary
With the shipped HA config each node realized the peer's fabric stanza as a local, slave-less, admin-UP bond (`fab1` on node0, `fab0` on node1): the daemon passed every `len(FabricMembers)>0` interface to `ApplyBonds`, and the bond manager skipped only `LocalFabricMember != ""`, which is also empty for the peer's fab. Neither IPVLAN stale sweep reaps a bond-typed link, so the phantom was zoned into `control` and queued for XDP attach.

## Fix
- `bondManager.shouldBond`: in a chassis cluster a fab bonds only when >=2 fabric members are local (slot via `config.InterfaceSlot`/`SlotToNodeID`; unparseable slots count as local). Zero local = peer's fab; exactly one = vSRX IPVLAN mode. Outside a cluster the #9872 standalone multi-member shape still bonds; plain `Apply` unchanged.
- `ApplyCluster` / `Manager.ApplyClusterBonds` carry `cfg.Chassis.Cluster` identity from `applyInterfaceReconcile`. A tracked ghost leaving the desired set is deleted by the existing differential delete pass; an untracked slave-less ghost from a pre-fix binary is reaped only on the daemon's first reconcile (`Daemon.bondGhostReapDone`). The reap never touches member-carrying bonds or same-name foreign non-bond links.

## Tests
- routing: per-node no-bond, standalone + dual-local positive controls, tracked reap, untracked upgrade reap with member/foreign negative controls — 5 tests pass.
- daemon: same through `applyInterfaceReconcile` + first-apply-only arming — 2 tests pass; pre-existing `TestApplyInterfaceReconcile*` still pass.
- Full `pkg/routing` suite passes. Two `pkg/daemon` `TestApply*` failures (`TestApplyIPsecTrackedRecordsOnlyALoadedGeneration9511`, `TestApplyTailReconcilesSurfacesVRRPIdentityCollision`) reproduce on unmodified origin/master — base-attributed, unrelated.

## Residual
Dataplane #9872 planner and networkd bond models are unchanged: a remote-only fab ref still resolves to the fab name, but no netdev is now created so the zone loop takes its not-found path.

## PR #17392 — userspace-dp: backfill NAT aliases published while saturated (#16564) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16564-campaign`

Why: `SharedNatAmbiguityIndex::remember` returned early while the index was saturated, dropping the alias record for any session published inside a saturation excursion. `owners` and the shared NAT map still recorded the session, but no alias record was ever installed (`reset_to_owner` is only reached from a wire co-owner removal), so after removals dropped the live population below 16,384 those long-lived sessions stayed unresolvable for their whole lifetime through the ambiguity-gated shared lookups (shared reverse-NAT match, quoted-tuple embedded-ICMP reversal, reverse-flow prevalidation, shared wire match). The #15104 regression only exercised a pre-saturation session.

What: Bounded, arrival-ordered FIFO (16,384) of unrecorded `(alias, owner)` claims in `SharedNatAmbiguityIndex` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/mod.rs`). `remember` queues owner claims refused while saturated; `track_owner`/`reset_to_owner` queue instead of discarding; `forget_owner` dequeues the departed claim, re-queues a still-live sole owner, and drains the queue into freed alias capacity — revalidating each claim against the live `owners` multiset, draining multi-owner aliases as ambiguous (`None`), never unique, and never exceeding `MAX_KEYS`. New publishes queue behind waiting claims instead of stealing freed slots. One #15104 cell updated (a single removal no longer clears saturation now that tail aliases refill freed slots; it removes until below the bound and probes a survivor). NOT changed: the 16,384 bound, fail-closed lookup semantics, #14383/#15106 logic. The sibling wire-roster latch was fixed separately by #16561; this branch is based on current master including it and carries no wire-latch code.

Validation: 5 new cells drive the real `publish_shared_session`/`remove_shared_session` over the real 16,384 bound (subject backfills and passes `shared_forward_nat_candidate_is_unique`; saturation-era collisions stay ambiguous with survivor restoration; removed subjects never resurrect; partial recovery stays bounded/FIFO; exact-population accounting). RED on shimmed master and on enqueue-neutered fix (`subject claim must be queued`). 10/10 targeted cells pass (5 new + 3x #15104 + 2x #16561) at head f3255fc789. Full `cargo test --bins`: 9513 passed / 78 failed, same environment-attributed failure shape as the pre-change full run (9507/81) — main agent to confirm base attribution.

Risk: Queue memory bounded by 16,384 `(alias, owner)` pairs, only non-empty after a saturation excursion; claims shed past the queue cap keep the pre-fix fail-closed behavior (no fail-open weakening). Lab verify (loss cluster under >16k concurrent shared NAT flows) still outstanding, recorded in `docs/log/16564.md`.

Refs #16564

## PR #17393 — userspace: page persistent-NAT lease exports under the control cap (#16589) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16589-paged-idle-leases`

Refs #16589

## Why
export_idle_leases and export_persistent_lease_display built one unpaged JSON response. Past the 64 MiB control cap (measured ~186k leases at 4 remotes, ~125k at 10 — below one pool's 262,144 tracked cap, and per-pool caps never bound the sum across pools) Go's bounded reader refused the answer, so every 30s idle-lease push delivered NOTHING to the standby and a failover lost every idle persistent mapping. The SHOW display export failed the same way.

## What
- Wire (v70->v71, both planes together): request lease_export {paged, cursor, max}, response lease_export_more / lease_export_continuation; MinProtocolPersistentNatLeasePaging=71 gates both Go exports before any lease request crosses (a pre-paging helper ignores the field and answers unpaged).
- Helper: both handlers sort the population by full wire identity (allocator map order is nondeterministic) and cut pages under an 8192-row ceiling AND a half-cap serialized byte budget; unpaged callers keep single-shot; bad cursors refuse.
- Go: pagedLeaseExport16589 follows continuations, failing closed on repeated / empty-with-more / complete-with continuations, page errors, or 2048 pages — a partial population is never returned as complete. Small populations stay single-page.
- Deadlines (#11840 shape): work floors for both verbs (~19s, under the #7675 67s bound).
- Fixture regenerated; v71 pin and one generation-test seed updated.

## Validation
- Rust: paged_export_300k_leases_each_page_under_cap_16589 (unpaged control > cap; every page <= cap; exact reassembly; single-page small control), paged_export_150k_by_4_remotes_and_cursor_refusal_16589 — 2/2 pass.
- Go: both Manager verbs page to completion over a real socket; single-page control; fail-closed arms; pre-paging refusal; page ceiling; deadline floors; wire-fixture completeness; version lockstep; persistent-NAT generation suites — pass.
- Known-red at base (verified in pristine base worktree, unrelated): TestOwnerRGExportPageFitsTheResponseCap9344, Rust every_runtime_atomic_is_bound_or_knowingly_off_wire_6961.

## Risk
Mixed v71-daemon/v70-helper pairs refuse lease exports (and snapshots, by pre-existing exact equality) instead of silently crossing the cap — fail-closed by design. Imports ungated (caller-bounded). Offset paging re-reads/re-sorts per page on the existing 30s cadence.

SchemaValidate rejection of malformed ids and install-id-only provider materialisation), zone-hash subtests in TestCloudflareLegacyWithdrawValueScopedFallbackLogged16086 and TestCloudflareStalePrevOwnership16086.

Two installs deliberately sharing one install-id remain one owner by construction, as before.

## Why

A Junos reth LAG (two or more child links per node on one reth) committed strict-clean while xpf implements no reth LAG. `RethToPhysical` binds only the lexically-first local child, so the VIP, virtual MAC and zone landed on `ge-0/0/1` and `ge-0/0/2` came up zoneless with a duplicate `169.254.<rg>.<node>` link-local and its physical MAC — the configured intra-node redundancy/bandwidth was silently lost, contrary to the accepted-only doctrine (#2078/#4231/#5804, ae in #6544).

## PR #17397 — userspace-dp: arm delta loss on drain response write failure (#16584) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16584-drain-write-loss`

Why:
`drain_session_deltas` and the owner-RG collect destructively pop a batch into the control response; if encode/write/flush then failed (peer hit its 3 s deadline and closed, or the serial backlog stalled the round trip) the handler returned `Err`, the accept loop logged it, and the batch vanished — no re-queue, no `set_delta_loss`. The closes in the batch left stale standby rows until peer GC.

What:
Track exactly which bindings (fair drain) and workers (owner-RG collect, via export-buffer drained-counter diffs threaded through the open window) contributed to `response.session_deltas`. The dispatcher tail now encodes+flushes first; on any delivery failure with a non-empty batch it arms `set_delta_loss` on every contributor before returning the error, so owning workers re-export table truth (deliver-or-resync, #2442/#2874/#5290). Empty drains/collects arm nothing and no longer flag a persist; `write_state` runs after a successful flush (persist-after-flush, #5294 ordering in effect). No wire change.

Validation:
- New `drain_session_deltas_write_failure_arms_delta_loss_16584`: connected control drains 8 and arms nothing; closed-client arm Errs, arms slot 0 only, follow-up drain empty. Pre-fix the latch stays false (RED).
- New `owner_rg_collect_write_failure_arms_delta_loss_16584`: closed-client export arms contributor slot 7, non-contributor slot 9 clear.
- Existing `drain_session_deltas_survive_write_state_failure_5294` and #5290 overflow/no-overflow cells green; targeted drain/export run 13 passed, 0 failed.

Risk:
A failed write triggers one debounced owner-RG resync per contributing binding — the intended recovery, bounded to episodes where a batch was actually lost. Empty drains no longer write the state file (best-effort observability, self-corrects periodically).

Refs #16584

## PR #17400 — ddns: withdraw skip-existing/strict-fail device marker with last family (#16597) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16597-dhcid-marker`

Refs #16597

## Why
Under skip-existing/strict-fail, the same-device first-family add publishes an RFC 4701 DHCID proof marker so the sibling family can prove co-ownership (#14995), but the marker was tracked only in the per-cycle updater with no owner and no delete path. After a dual-stack lease expired, the A/AAAA were withdrawn while the lone DHCID remained, permanently burning the name: the same device returning single-family, or any later client, was refused against xpf's own leftover and counted as a third-party conflict (R3-A40-06).

## What
- `LeaseDNSRecord.KeepSiblingMarker` set by the manager from `markerSharedWithSibling` (same canonical FQDN, same scope-modulo-family, same device digest), mirroring `dhcidSharedWithOther` for replace-owned.
- The skip-existing/strict-fail delete path in `sendRemoveForward` withdraws the marker value-specifically (exact device DHCID) when the last family is removed and preserves it while a same-device sibling survives; a never-published marker delete is an exact-match no-op so a foreign DHCID is never removed, and a marker-delete failure still attempts the forward delete.
- The marker is retained only after a successful publish exchange, cleared after a successful last-family marker delete, and reset on a name switch in `UpsertLease` so multi-name lifetimes cannot leak one name's proof into another.
- README + changelog updated.

## Validation
- New `marker_lifecycle_16597_test.go` (stateful fake, manager-driven): dual-stack under both skip-existing and strict-fail leaves no RR after full teardown and a same-device single-family re-claim is not refused/counted; partial teardown keeps the marker; single-family ghost delete leaves a foreign DHCID untouched.
- `go test ./pkg/ddns/ -count=1` — PASS (full suite).
- Adjacent cells re-run green: `TestCrossFamily*`, `TestDualStack*`, `TestPartialDualStackTeardownKeepsSharedDHCID`, skip-existing/strict-fail + garbage-policy delete cells.

## Risk
Low — confined to the skip-existing/strict-fail delete path; replace-owned guarded deletes, PTR handling, and foreign-hijack guards (#14995/#15072) unchanged. Legacy orphan markers published before this fix are removed by the value-specific delete when the owning device is next withdrawn; operators can clear older orphans manually.

## PR #17401 — userspace-dp: reclaim own oldest incomplete at sender quota (#16599) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16599-overlap-sender-quota`

## Why

`OverlapTracker`'s per-sender quota (8 incomplete entries per shard, key `(routing_domain, family, src)`) counted abandoned tail-lost datagrams for the full 30 s TTL. At ≈4.3 abandoned/s a conformant sender saturates all 16 shards and every surviving fragmented datagram to every destination is `ShardFull`-dropped — driven by ordinary upstream loss or the firewall's own tail drops, not an attacker. A receiver timing out those datagrams does not refuse the sender's new ones; #13937 exempted completed entries on that principle and abandoned entries were the unhandled twin.

## What

In `check_and_record_fragment_detailed` (`userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs`), at the sender bound, reclaim the sender's **own** oldest settled-incomplete entry (`overlap_entry_incomplete`: `pending == 0`, not failed, ranges not covering a terminal end) instead of refusing, counted by new `FRAG_OVERLAP_SAME_SENDER_INCOMPLETE_RECLAIMED`.

- Eligibility = quota-counting predicate AND own-ness (same `overlap_sender` on arrival keys, same `fairness_origin` on post-translation keys), so under the #14127 poisoned broadening another origin's entry is never the one evicted.
- Still-pending and failed (poisoned) anchors are never reclaimed; the sender never holds more than 8 incomplete entries per shard (#10658 bound unchanged); the reclaimed slot decrements the zone count so the insert is not charged twice against the 32-entry reserve.
- `post_nat_sender_quota_is_per_tenant_14127` updated: its ninth-datagram refusal expectation is superseded by #16599 — it now asserts admission via tenant A's own oldest entry, A's survivors and tenant B's anchor untouched, B's tail still admitted.

NOT changed: TTL/lifetime, zone/shard reclaims, overlap membership, any fail-open direction.

## Validation

- New `sender_at_quota_reclaims_own_oldest_settled_incomplete_16599`: 8 settled-incomplete across destinations fill the quota; 9th admitted reclaiming exactly the oldest (counter +1, zero ShardFull delta); survivors + 9th still detect overlap; evicted key replants; held-token still-pending fill and failed fill both fail closed evicting nothing.
- New `sender_quota_under_tail_loss_16599` (acceptance shape): 1000/s for 60 s at 1% tail loss, simulated `now_ns`, zero ShardFull refusals, 600 abandoned heads recycled.
- RED-on-revert: with reclaim eligibility neutered both fail (9th drops `ShardFull`; acceptance train desyncs after 256 completions).
- Full `fragment_overlap` module: **48 passed, 0 failed**, including `one_domain_cannot_starve_other_domains_10658` and `completed_datagram_rate_does_not_exhaust_sender_quota_13937`.
- Two `afxdp::tests_nat64_overlap_8115` failures under a broader `overlap` filter are pre-existing on the base commit (verified on pristine master), untouched here.

## Risk

The evicted abandoned anchor loses overlap protection for the rest of its TTL — the same trade the completed (#15103) and cross-zone incomplete (#15288) reclaims accept; its late tail replants a fresh entry. A sender at quota whose entries are all still-pending or failed still fails closed as before.

Refs #16599

## PR #17403 — userspace-dp: recycle own-oldest frag association at session quota (#16593) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16593-frag-assoc-quota`

## Summary
Fixes the #16593 regression: `FragAssoc::install_with_session` refused every new first fragment once a session held 32 associations in a shard, entries were only reclaimed on expiry (2s idle TTL refreshed on every tail hit, no completion release), capping one NAT'd fragmented flow at ~16 datagrams/s and starving same-zone sources sharing its shard.

- MF=0 tail consults release a completed datagram's association (`final_fragment_key` + `FragAssoc::release`) on both NAT64 and same-family/plain consult paths — only after the consult's fences pass, never on a miss.

including unrelated static denies — a host-inbound fail-open from a DNS
blip (R3-N09-01).

What: stale-while-error. `Address.DNSLookupFailed` (runtime-only) marks
a failed (re)resolution; on error the previous `DNSAddresses` are kept,
on success (even empty) the answer replaces them and the flag clears.
The strict gate exempts a closure empty only due to a failed lookup
(the existing match-nothing warning remains); the userspace builder
emits no address sentinel and no `PolicyContentRejected` for it — a
positive permit takes the empty book row (match-none), a deny/reject
or excluded side is poisoned per-rule via its application terms — and
the junos-host projection keeps sibling static terms rendering. A
successful empty answer keeps every pre-existing fail-closed gate.
Refs #16595

Validation: new `pkg/config/dns_stale_16595_test.go` and
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/dns_stale_16595_test.go` (9 tests incl. the
probe's SERVFAIL arm: `sentinelRules=0` with the stale prefix retained,
junos-host static rule still rendered, strict commit of an unrelated
change succeeds while the resolver is down); RED-on-revert verified
for stale retention, the builder lowering, and the junos-host/strict
exemptions. `pkg/daemon -run TestDNS` green (one cell updated to the
new actually-applied semantics). Pre-existing failures in the touched
areas fail identically on pristine base (recorded in the commit body).

Risk: a name that stops resolving keeps its last answer indefinitely
(max-stale age optional per issue; the 5-minute tick retries). A
never-resolved deny still makes the helper retain previous-good via
its application sentinel — the strongest per-rule fail-closed the
current wire expresses — with no Go-side content rejection.

## PR #17409 — cli: refuse trailing tokens after load source (#16602) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16602-load-trailing-args`

## Why
Both CLIs' `load merge|set|override <source>` never read `args[2:]`, so the Junos `load merge terminal relative` form — and any trailing garbage — silently dropped the modifier. The snippet applied at the root, printed `load <mode> complete`, and committed clean whenever valid at the root (a VRF default route became a master-table route; a group body applied device-wide). Neither the local apply path nor `pb.LoadRequest` carries an edit path, so `relative` cannot be honoured on this surface; a modifier that is not implemented must be refused, not dropped (the `load rescue` arm already refuses extra args).

## What
- `pkg/cli/cli_config.go` (`handleLoad`, local console) and `cmd/cli/main.go` (`handleLoad`, remote): after the known-mode check and before any terminal/file read, content gate, store mutation, or Load RPC, refuse `len(args) > 2` with `load: unexpected argument "<first-extra>"`.
- Tests: `pkg/cli/load_trailing_args_16602_test.go` (scripted terminal reader; candidate byte-identical, zero lines consumed) and `cmd/cli/load_trailing_args_16602_test.go` (counting Load stub; zero RPCs on refusal, exactly one on plain load).
- `docs/log/16602.md` changelog.
- NOT changed: `load rescue` handling, exact two-argument forms, content gates (#9892/#10305/#14718/#6753).

## Validation
- New suites green: `TestConsoleLoadTrailingArgRefused16602` (10 subtests) and `TestCtlLoadTrailingArgRefused16602` (14 subtests); targeted `Load` tests and `go vet` green on both packages.
- RED-on-revert: deleting the guard makes the console cells load/consume input and the remote terminal cells panic on the nil readline (guard no longer precedes the paste).
- Full suites: `pkg/cli` 15 failures, `cmd/cli` 2 failures — each reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` cbe42bd4f3 (pre-existing, untouched).

## Risk
Operators scripting `relative` loads now get a hard error instead of a silent root load — the intended behaviour change. Implementing cursor-relative loads (wire path field + prefixing + gate pricing) remains possible later; refusal satisfies the issue acceptance ("either error with nothing loaded, or RI1Static=1").

Refs #16602

The dns-name refresher applied a private CloneForDNSRefresh clone to the dataplane but never published it to the config store. - configsContentEqual also compares DNS answers, so routeOnlyPublishHybrid refuses a stale partial republish.
- Existing #15962 cells premised on a legitimately stale store copy updated to re-read the published generation; compiled-swap tripwire reviewed 8->9.

Validation:

## PR #17412 — userspace-dp: mirror received frame for prebuilt transit (#16603) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16603-prebuilt-mirror-original`

Refs #16603

## Why
The #15251 mirror arm in `enqueue_pending_forwards` cloned the already-translated egress frame for embedded-ICMP NAT/NAT64 reversals, so the analyzer received a packet that never crossed the ingress wire (post-reversal addresses, egress MACs/VLAN, decremented TTL, other family for NAT64), violating the plan-1376 contract ("full original Ethernet frame") that Live/Owned arms honour.

## What
- Add `PendingForwardFrame::PrebuiltTransit { frame, ingress_frame, ingress_meta }` carrying the translated wire frame plus the received bytes/meta.
- Queue it from the same-family embedded-ICMP reversal and both NAT64 arms (v4→v6, v6→v4).
- Dispatch forwards the wire frame with the wire meta exactly as before, but stages the mirror from the ingress bytes/meta, moving (never cloning) the ingress copy only when a mirror row matches and the sample selects.
- Plain `Prebuilt` (device-generated Time-Exceeded) mirroring unchanged (#15947 deliberate choice).
- 15251 fixtures rewritten to assert clone == ingress bytes for IPv4 NAT and NAT64 (both directions); new `CountingAlloc` no-extra-allocation gate; embedded poll-filter extractions updated for the new variant.

## Validation
- `prebuilt_` + `retry_pending_neighbor_mirrors_original` + `embedded_icmp` + `nat64_icmp`: 61 passed, 0 failed.
- mirror filter: 103 passed, 1 failed (`strict_mirror_refusal_replays_imported_lease_and_holder_mask_11476_10789_f4` — pre-existing, verified failing identically on pristine base 72329d9b35).
- dispatch filter: 163 passed, 2 failed (`seed_lifecycle_expires_on_app_window_not_default_10267`, `tunnel_wg_nodf_oversize_emits_ptb_with_inner_mtu_10705` — both pre-existing on the same base).

## Risk
Analyzer-only fidelity change; forwarding/filtering/enforcement byte-identical (wire frame + wire meta untouched, queued policy still judges the wire frame). One bounded Vec per queued reversal at poll time; dispatch never clones when unmirrored/sampled-out.

## Why
The owner's secondary-hold heartbeat could promote the requester before the

the bound abort, and timeout returns discarded the request ID.

  commit override path.

  priority election for a higher-priority non-preempt requester.

  request ID on timeouts and failed batch ACKs.

  replying with a failed fence ACK.

  batch, and check that the actual abort frame carries the transmitted reqID.

Evidence: `/var/worktrees/.cache/16592-cluster-final.jsonl` and
`/var/worktrees/.cache/16592-mutation.jsonl`; details in `docs/log/16592.md`.

No cluster deployment, full selftest or live dataplane-overlap measurement.
Lost aborts still rely on the owner lease and existing election. A lower-
priority former owner seeing a higher-priority healthy secondary can remain
secondary when re-electing; this fix prevents requester promotion after abort

## PR #17416 — config: preserve quoted whitespace edit cursor as one token (#16608) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16608`

Refs #16608

## Why
`NormalizeEditPathTokens` re-lexed `strings.Join(cursor, " ")`, so a quoted element with interior whitespace (`edit firewall family inet filter "lan in"`, stored as the single lexed token `lan in`) split into two tokens. A discard term added from that cursor landed in a new empty unapplied filter `lan`, the applied filter `"lan in"` was unchanged, and commit check returned nil on both CLIs.

## What
- Keep the cursor as lexed tokens: `NormalizeEditPathTokens` re-lexes from the quoted join (`JoinConfigPathTokens`) when any stored token bears whitespace; otherwise keeps the raw joined lex #14716 requires (raw decorated tokens only collapse re-lexed as typed — the two spellings cannot coexist in one real cursor).
- Gate split-comment re-lex quotes only the line tokens behind its prefix guard.
- `[edit …]` banners (both CLIs) and compare headers (`diffNodes` child paths from node `Keys`, never `Fields(KeyPath())`) quote via `JoinConfigPathTokens`.
- Local/remote `edit` normalize the existing cursor before appending; `top`/`up` resolve/restore against the normalized cursor; groups gate replay quotes the cursor with the raw remainder.

## Validation
- `pkg/config`: Normalize units (whitespace/doubled-space, plain + #14716 controls, idempotence), anchored gate deny/allow on the real vs split path, quoted compare header + scoped compare.
- `pkg/cli`: defect arm compiles `"lan in"` terms=[allow block], no stray `lan`, CommitCheck nil; `lanin` control unchanged; scoped compare.
- `cmd/cli`: stored cursor, quoted banner, exact wire `firewall family inet filter "lan in" term block then discard`, `up` pops the whole filter identity.
- RED on revert (source restored, tests kept); #14716 suites + CLI 15237/15082 cells green; `go vet` clean.

## Risk
Gate resolved-path string remains space-joined (pre-existing #9154): anchored regexes cannot textually distinguish quoted vs split spelling, but gate and executor now judge/act on the same token sequence.

## PR #17422 — routing: gate rib-group peer returns on import-rib (#16616) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16616-peer-return-auth`

Refs #16616

## Why

The #11062 peer-return rules installed, for every tenant leaking its interface routes into `inet.0`, destination-scoped returns to **every other** tenant leaking into main (kernel ip rules at 1001-1999), and the AF_XDP FIB mirrored each as an `A.inet.0 -> B.inet.0` NextTable row. Two tenants following the textbook shared-services pattern (each `import-rib [ <self>.inet.0 inet.0 ]`) were thus reachable from each other in VRF context — VRF-bound sockets/daemons, non-AF_XDP slaves, slow-path reinjects — with no import-rib authorizing it, contradicting the documented contract in `docs/rib-group-route-leaking.md` that B's routes go into `b.inet.0` and `inet.0` only, never into `a.inet.0`.

## What

Install a return (and mirror it into the FIB) **only** when the source instance's own interface-routes rib-group for that family names the peer's rib (`<peer>.inet.0` / `<peer>.inet6.0`) in its import-rib list — the VRF→VRF import case — and the peer leaks into main for that family:

- `pkg/routing/rules.go`: new `ribGroupImportsInstanceRib` gates `ribGroupPeerReturnPrefixes`.
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go`: new `ribGroupReturnAuthorized` gates the live-rule mirror, so a stale kernel rule from an older binary cannot republish an unauthorized row (the `clear()` sweep still removes the stale rule itself). Both sides fail closed.
- The VRF→VRF *forward* leak remains Phase-2 deferred (warned, not installed); naming a peer rib authorizes only this destination-scoped return to the peer's leaked connected prefixes.
- NOT changed: the 30000-band main leak (main→tenant still resolves), the #9819 miss terminator, next-table/PBR returns.
- Docs: `docs/rib-group-route-leaking.md` §89-203 rewritten (lookup contract table gains the authorized/unauthorized rows), `pkg/routing/README.md` return band, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/16616.md`.

## Validation

- `TestRibGroupReturnRules9819` now expects **zero** return rules for main-only tenants (was 8); new `TestRibGroupReturnRulesAuthorizedPeer16616` pins the authorized src↔b pair and excludes third tenant c.
- `TestRibGroupRulesApply_Fake` counts drop 6→2 per family (leaks only); #14975 LPM/EEXIST and #11319 band-order fixtures re-authorized.
- Real-kernel `TestVRFMissTerminatorOnRealKernel9819` (`XPF_REQUIRE_NETNS=1`): **PASS** — peer-prefix positives (v4+v6 socket/slave) flipped to `unreachable`; main→A and main→B controls still resolve.
- FIB: new `TestBuildRouteSnapshotsSkipsUnauthorizedRibGroupReturn16616` asserts no `src.inet.0 -> b.inet.0` row for a stale unauthorized kernel rule; authorized mirror + LPM cells re-fixtured.
- `go test ./pkg/routing/ -count=1` PASS; `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestBuildRouteSnapshots` PASS. The 8 failures in the full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite (WireGuard degenerate key, vlan-tagging, quarantine, retry-debt) reproduce identically on a pristine `origin/master` worktree — base-attributed, unrelated.

## Risk

An operator relying on the undocumented tenant→tenant reach via mutual main leaks must now name the peer rib in import-rib explicitly — the intended authorization. The FIB gate duplicates the kernel authorization against compiled config; rib-group storage changes must update both (same pattern as the existing `ribGroupLeaksIntoMain` mirrors). No Rust/wire change.

## PR #17431 — config-authz: bind commit gate verdict to priced candidate (#16611) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16611`

Refs #16611

## Why
The #14981 commit-time expanded deny-configuration gate priced the candidate at the gRPC interceptor / REST middleware, but the daemon promoted whatever candidate existed after the `applySem` wait and re-adopted a changed one on generation conflict (`commitWithGenBinding`). A same-holder `copy`/`rename`/`apply-groups` landing in between was committed unadjudicated.

## What
- Interceptor/middleware stash the priced snapshot (admitted config, class, candidate generation, active tree) in the request context at gate time — capturing the generation at pricing time, not handler time.
- gRPC and REST `Commit`/`CommitConfirmed` handlers stamp it into `CommitAuthority` via `WithCommitGate`.
- `verifyCommitAuthorityLocked` re-prices a changed candidate for the committing class under the store lock and refuses promotion: the gate's permission-denied for a denied change, or `ErrCommitCandidateChanged` for an allowed-but-changed candidate (deliberately not `ErrCandidateGenerationConflict`, so the adopt-on-conflict retry cannot automate the substitution; the daemon loop also refuses that sentinel explicitly).
- Unchanged candidates commit as before; unrestricted classes and internal/system committers are never bound.

## Validation
- New 16611 cells in `pkg/configstore`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/api`: copy-between refused for Commit and CommitConfirmed; allowed-change refused as changed then commits when re-priced; unchanged twin commits with a gate-bound authority; before-commit copy still refused at the gate; internal/unbound authorities unaffected.
- RED verified by neutering `verifyGateBindingLocked` (denied candidate promoted); GREEN post-fix.
- Adjacent 14981/6808/15208/14990 targeted suites pass; gofmt/vet clean on changed files.

## Risk
A restricted class whose candidate changes between gate and promotion must re-issue the commit (fail-closed, intended). CLI commits are single-process and unbound; the residual is the documented concurrent-stream window.

## PR #17433 — userspace-dp: bound PPTP permanent-collision self-retry (#16609) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16609-pptp-self-retry`

Refs #16609

## Why
A PPTP first-learn install refused by a permanent alias collision was retained as a self-retry with no TTL/cap. On a single-worker helper a PPTP server reusing one call-id alias could grow `pending_call_installs` by up to 64/s for the control channel's lifetime, and each entry was cloned, re-installed and re-counted (`allocator_collisions` +N/s) every second on the only forwarding worker.

## What
- Classify the refusal (`install_collision_is_transient` in `afxdp/pptp_broadcast.rs`, via the new non-counting `PptpAssociations::install_error_for` probe): retain a self-retry only while a queued/pending CDN or channel forget (inbox or not-yet-applied worker command) will retire the colliding association, or the owner was learned strictly before the retry (the #15251/#12133 replacement shape); otherwise drop it after its single counted attempt.
- The retry walk probes without counting and calls the counting `install` only once the alias has freed, so a retained refusal is never re-counted per tick.
- Hard cap `MAX_PENDING_CALL_INSTALLS = 256` (drop-newest, enforced before commitment) and age bound `CALL_INSTALL_RETRY_TTL_NS` = association idle timeout, pruned under the inbox lock in `take_call_install_retries_at`.
- NOT changed: peer-queue `InstallPptpCall` apply semantics (counted once, never re-attempted); no fail-open weakening.

## Validation
- New `permanent_collision_self_retry_is_bounded_and_counted_once_16609`: 64 same-alias replies, single worker — 1 learned, collisions stay 63 across 6 ticks, retention within cap (pre-fix +63/tick).
- New `pending_call_installs_are_capped_and_age_pruned_16609`: 320 records cap at 256; past-TTL retries pruned to 0.
- Guards green: `own_retry_retains_allocator_collision_until_cdn_frees_alias_12133`, `12133` filter 16 passed, `first_learn_collision_backlog_learns_replacement_on_both_workers_15251`.
- Broader `pptp` filter: 101 passed, 1 failed — `pptp_open_frame_carries_the_call_id_pair_13965` fails identically on a pristine origin/master build (pre-existing, untouched).

## Risk
Same-drain-pass permanent collisions whose owner was learned on an earlier pass are retained (locally indistinguishable from a queued-teardown replacement); bounded by cap/TTL, never re-counted, expire with the colliding association.

## PR #17434 — config: model RIP per-group export end-to-end (#16625) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

## Why
RIP per-group `export` was flattened into one global ripd redistribute chain: the compiler appended every group's neighbors/exports into global `Interfaces`/`Redistribute`, `RIPConfig` had no group field, and the renderer emitted one composed chain on every interface. Two groups with different exports (CUSTOMERS `DEFAULT-ONLY` vs CORE `ALL-STATIC`) committed strict-clean, and stanza order decided leak vs loss.

## What
- `RIPConfig.Groups []*RIPGroup` carries name/interfaces/export out of the compiler (unions retained for legacy consumers).
- pkg/frr: grouped RIP redistributes the union once, then confines per interface via `distribute-list prefix xpf-rip-<inst>-grp-<n>[-v6] out <if>`; accepted prefix sets computed in chain evaluation order (first terminal wins; reject terms render as earlier deny entries). Inexpressible chains (bare token `static`, non-prefix accept) fail closed: deny-all list + warning.
- Strict gate rejects an interface in 2+ groups with differing exports (global + routing-instance); lenient warns (#1960) and the renderer withholds contested interfaces.
- `resolveRIPIfNames` deep-copies Groups; group-less RIP is byte-identical legacy.

## Validation
- New config + frr tests incl. probe in both orders: CUSTOMERS permits only `0.0.0.0/0` (never `192.168.50.0/24`), CORE permits `192.168.50.0/24`; contested/bare-token/legacy/reject-term cells.
- Full pkg/frr: identical 5 failures to unmodified master `f5c9f32701` (base-attributed). pkg/config `TestDualASTDifferential`/`TestDR15H3ControlsAgree14418` also fail on unmodified master.

## Risk
Live-FRR `distribute-list ... out` ripd semantics not verified in this lane (defer to loss cluster). QNH offset-lists stay router-global (harmless).

## PR #17436 — userspace-dp: make coordinator drain arm bulk-aware (#16630) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16630-campaign`

Refs #16630

## Why

#8593 made the push-side cap arm bulk-aware (`push_session_delta_bulk_export`
counts a cap drop without arming), but the drain-side arm was not covered.
`Coordinator::drain_session_deltas` armed `set_delta_loss` on every binding
with ANY undrained residue when the fair drain's budget ran out, and
`drain_session_deltas_fair_tracked` computed `overflow` from
`has_pending_session_deltas()` (any entry, bulk or incremental).

A LossResync exporting >256 owned sessions into the RPC-fallback buffer
therefore re-armed itself on the next Go tick (256 drained per tick, 5 s
connected / 100 ms fallback): the worker re-ran LossResync, refilled the
buffer, and looped for as long as owned sessions exceeded the per-tick
budget — regardless of traffic. Each pass is a whole-table candidate walk
per packet worker plus N peer installs on the control socket / sync link.

## What

- Tag each RPC-fallback queue entry with its origin:
  `pending_session_deltas: VecDeque<(SessionDeltaInfo, bool)>`
  (`bool` = bulk-export), set by the producer-routed push — mirroring
  #8593's principle that the marker rides with the delta/producer, not a
  call-site flag a future drain site could pass wrongly.
- New `BindingLiveState::has_pending_incremental_session_deltas()`.
- Key both drain-side sites on it:
  `drain_session_deltas_fair_tracked`'s overflow bit and the coordinator's
  per-binding arm in `drain_session_deltas_attributed`.
- Bulk residue still drains and is delivered to the RPC consumer exactly
  as before; it just cannot trigger the resync that produced it.
  Incremental residue arms exactly as #5290 intended.
- NOT changed: the #16584 drained-batch write-failure arms (attribution
  is batch-driven, not residue-driven) and the push-side cap arm.
- Docs: `binding_state/README.md` (#16630 bullet next to #8593),
  `event_stream/README.md` (#5290 note), `docs/log/16630.md`.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16630 8593 drain_session_deltas`:
  **17 passed, 0 failed** (7 new cells):
  - `drain_bulk_residue_does_not_arm_loss_16630` — the issue's acceptance
    cell: bulk-300 / drain-256 asserts `armed=false` (44 bulk remain).
  - `drain_incremental_residue_still_arms_loss_16630` — incremental-300
    control asserts `armed=true` (#5290 preserved).
  - `drain_bulk_no_residue_does_not_arm_16630` — bulk-200 / drain-256.
  - `drain_mixed_residue_arms_only_incremental_binding_16630` — per-binding
    precision across two bindings.
  - 3 binding-level classification cells in
    `delta_high_water_8108_tests.rs` (`has_pending_incremental_session_deltas`).

## PR #17439 — config: bound OSPF MD5 and simple key lengths (#16628) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16628`

Refs #16628

## Why
OSPF MD5 keys longer than 16 characters and simple-passwords longer than 8 committed strict-clean, rendered verbatim into frr.conf, and ospfd silently truncated them (RFC 2328 D.4.3: the MD5 key is 16 bytes; D.2: simple password is a 64-bit field). Every frr-reload then saw a delete-and-add pair for the key — a perpetual diff that permanently defeats the #15203 reload certification — and the effective key diverged from `show configuration`. OSPF sibling of #15013 (RIP).

## What
- `pkg/config`: `ValidateOSPFMD5KeyLength` (1..16) / `ValidateOSPFSimplePasswordLength` (1..8) typed-leaf validators on the shared `ospf` schema subtree (global + routing-instance via `schemaProtocols`); compiled gate `validateOSPFKeyLengthStrict` beside #14397 in `runUniformGates` (runs after the #15051 `$9$` decode, so the bound applies to decoded plaintext); `lenientOSPFKeyLength16628` downgrades to a warning on tolerant load/HA sync (#1960). Errors/warnings name only the length, never the key.
- `pkg/frr`: render belt withholds an over-long MD5 entry (valid rollover keys still render; no survivor ⇒ #14388 whole-interface omission) and omits the whole interface for an over-long simple-password — fail-closed, never a truncating or unauthenticated line.
- Tests: new `ospf_key_length_16628_test.go` (config + frr); a $9$-simple cell in the #15051 suite pins that the bound applies to decoded plaintext. Pre-existing over-long sentinel fixtures shortened to at-bound values (leak-identifiability preserved).
- Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` (#16628 section + #15013 correction), `docs/log/16628.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 16628` PASS — strict global+RI MD5-17 rejected / 16+1 accepted, simple-9 rejected / 8+1 accepted, rollover mix rejected, `SchemaValidate` (CheckText surface) rejects 17/9 accepts 16/8, rune-boundary validators, lenient warns without leaking the key.
- `go test ./pkg/frr/ -run 16628` PASS — over-long MD5 withheld + interface omitted, over-long simple omitted, rollover mix keeps valid key, VRF belt, at-bound controls byte-identical.
- Neighbouring OSPF/RIP auth suites pass. Full `pkg/config`/`pkg/frr`/`pkg/grpcapi`/`pkg/configstore` suites show only failures also present on the branched base `725372c2b9` (base-attributed, verified in a pristine base worktree).

## Risk
A persisted/peer-synced config already carrying an over-long OSPF key now boots with a warning and loses that key (loudly, via slog; MD5 rollover survivors still render) instead of churning every frr-reload — intended fail-closed posture, consistent with #15013/#14397/#14977. Strict-valid configs (MD5 ≤16, simple ≤8, no-auth) render byte-identically. Lab replay (`--test` empty after reload on a live FRR box) not run in this lane; render-belt unit tests pin the exact line behaviour.

## PR #17442 — dataplane: target planned parent MTU for statement-less VLAN reset (#16633) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16633`

Refs #16633

## Why
Raising a `vlan-tagging` parent's interface `mtu` (or deleting a lowered one, which plans the 1500 default) left every VLAN unit with **no MTU statement** at the old kernel MTU until the next commit, with no `MTUUnconverged` record. The #9757 reset in `applyVLANSubInterfaceMTU9757` read the parent's *cached pre-write* MTU, and the child step runs before the parent's per-phys write in the same `mapZoneInterface` call — so the stale target equalled the child's live MTU and the reset no-opped silently. Residual of #9845/#9757; the #9845 retry only fired on a *refused* write, and no write was ever attempted.

## What
- `applyVLANSubInterfaceMTU9757`: for a statement-less unit, target `mtuCtx.parentWant` (`st.physDesired[physName].mtu`, already threaded at the single call site for #9841 grading) when a plan exists. A raised target is refused by the kernel while the parent is still low and converges on the existing #9845 retry after the parent write; a lowered/defaulted target applies inline. With no plan (fabric/tunnel-owned parents, direct calls) it falls back to the live parent MTU, where an unreadable parent still records `MTUGradeResetTargetUnresolved`; with a plan, an unreadable parent no longer blocks the reset.
- Defensive nil-parent guard mirroring the existing nil-child guard (a nil-seeded cache entry now records instead of panicking on `Attrs()`).
- README #8119/#8120/#9845/#9757 bullet and the `MTUGradeResetTargetUnresolved` comment updated; `docs/log/16633.md` added.
- Tests: three new #16633 cells — parent raise (DEFECT arm: `child=3000` after apply #1, refused-attempt + retry, no records), converged no-write control, deleted lowered parent MTU. Updated #9757/#9841 cells whose fixtures plan 1400 against a 1500 live parent to the planned target; reshaped `TestChildMTUResetTargetUnresolvedRecords9841` onto a fabric-owned parent (deliberately never planned, so the no-plan fall-back arm still exists); pinned `TestPhysLowerBlockedByLiveChild9841`'s blocker with an explicit 1500 statement (its statement-less fixture child now legitimately converges to the 1400 plan, which had made the cell zone-order flaky).

## Validation
- `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -run 'MTU|9757|9761|9841|9845|8119|8120' -count=1` — pass.
- RED check: the three new DEFECT cells copied onto unmodified `f5c9f32701` fail (child stuck at 1500/1400); the converged control passes there too.
- `TestConvergedApplyWritesNoMTU_9845` and `TestUnitMTUResetIsIdempotent9757` still write nothing on a converged host.
- Full `go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -count=1`: only pre-existing baseline failures, each verified failing identically on unmodified `f5c9f32701`. `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/` clean.

## Risk
Low. Single production call site already threaded `parentWant`; explicit-unit and no-plan paths unchanged. A statement-less child now draws a refused first attempt + one retry on a parent raise — the same shape an explicit unit raise has had since #9845 — recorded by #9841 and cleared on convergence. No hot-path change.

## PR #17446 — userspace-dp: gate refresh-reconcile XDP attach on Compile admission (#16637) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16637-campaign`

Refs #16637

## Why
`reconcileInterfaceAttachmentsForRefreshLocked` attached the XDP shim to every untracked ingress ifindex, so a link event or revalidating publish attached it to the raw-L3 `wgN` TUN compileZones' #8279 gate refuses, to administratively disabled interfaces, and to non-tunnel VLAN children. `syncInterfaceAttachments`' raw-ingress allowed set then never reaped it, breaking the "shim is never attached to a raw-L3 netdev" invariant; the shim misparses inner source octets as an ethertype (8.0/16, 134.221/16, VLAN TPIDs drop local WG traffic).

## What
- `dataplane.ShimAttachRefused` (new export in `netdev_framing_8279.go`): the #8279 known-non-Ethernet gate; an unresolvable link is not refused (keeps prior behaviour, per `netdevFramingKnown` polarity).
- `refreshAttachAdmission` (`manager_link_refresh.go`): VLAN-child refusal with the tunnel carve-out mirroring `attachUserspaceShimXDP`, an `AdminDisabled` veto only from the row that owns the ifindex (a disabled unit-0 sibling cannot strip an enabled base), framing via `linkByNameFn`. The reconcile consults it before attaching.
- `syncInterfaceAttachments` drops non-VLAN-child refused ifindexes from its allowed set so a stale refused attach is detached at the next Compile.
- NOT changed: `buildUserspaceIngressIfindexes` (adjudication), Compile's attach loops, detach-before-publish ordering (#5485).

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean.
- New `TestRefreshAttachAdmission16637`: PASS with fix; RED with the admission call disabled (attaches 40 wg / 13 disabled / 31 VLAN child). Positive controls (Ethernet owner, disabled unit-0 sibling on enabled base, unresolvable link) still attach.
- `TestInterfaceLinkRefreshAttachesRecreatedIfindex14133` and the 14133/14333/15042 refresh cells stay green; `pkg/dataplane` 8279 cells green.
- Pre-existing failure `TestInterfaceLinkRefreshTracksBindOnlyTunnelNetdev11530` fails identically on origin/master (#14139 PSK fixture), untouched.

## Risk
A netdev whose link lookup transiently fails keeps the prior attach behaviour (fail-closed fence if unshimmed). VLAN children stay in the sync allowed set, matching delegated-child tracking Compile leaves behind. Lab/kernel attach not exercised (hook-stubbed, as the #14133 cells).

## PR #17451 — eventengine: window parked-direction events so trigger-until ceilings hold (#16641) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16641-within-parked-window`

Refs #16641

## Why
#15021 cooldown parking early-continued before the sliding-window append (`evaluate.go`), so events on a parked (policy,event) direction were never windowed. A `within W { trigger until N }` window (N ≳ 4) therefore never reached its ceiling during a sustained storm, and the remediation replayed every 30 s cooldown. Coordinated with R3-F16-01 (#16848): the #15945 drain-time `withinMatches` re-check discarded genuine `trigger on` crossings whose short `within` window decayed during the cooldown.

## What
- Append + prune every matching event even while its direction is parked; skip only the park/fire decision.
- Record the evaluate-time `withinMatches` verdict on the parked `deferredEdge`; the drain replays that verdict under a revision/liveness (semRev + policy present) re-check only, with `staleReason` as the commit-time backstop.
- Legacy deferred edges with no recorded verdict keep the #15945 live-window re-check, so synthetically parked sub-threshold/latched/decayed edges still cannot replay (`TestDeferredSubThresholdNoReplay15945`, `TestDeferredRecordedVerdictFalseNoReplay16848`).
- Regression tests: #16641 storm (zero over-ceiling re-fires after the single recorded replay; window holds all 15 storm events) and sparse control; #16848 recorded-false verdict and short-window flap probe (t=15 defect arm ends `link-down-remediated`, t=25 control unchanged). README + changelog updated.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/eventengine/ -run 'TestParked|TestDeferred|TestEdgeTriggerOn|TestInclusiveUntil|TestTriggerOn1|TestWithin|TestWindow' -count=1`: 35 passed.
- RED checks: reverting only the windowing hunk fails both #16641 tests (starved window=2); reverting only the drain verdict fails the recorded-false cell (commits=2) and the t=15 flap arm while the t=25 control stays green.
- Full `pkg/eventengine` run: only the 9 pre-existing `multivalue_leaf_runtime_6673` failures, identically present on unmodified origin/master.
- gofmt / go vet / git diff --check clean.

## Risk
A parked edge now replays its recorded crossing even if later windowed events push the window past a trigger-until ceiling; that single replay is the crossing that fired at/inside the ceiling, and post-drain live events over the ceiling stay silent (storm test asserts no further commits and PendingDeferred=0).
