## PR #17452 — userspace-dp: fold helper-down scheduler and overlay transitions into retained snapshot (#16643) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16643-helperless-partial-publishers`

Refs #16643

## Why
`UpdatePolicyScheduleStateWithLatch` and `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshotWithLatch` returned "converged" while the helper was down (crash / restart backoff) without writing their content into `m.lastSnapshot`. The supervisor restart replays `m.lastSnapshot` verbatim (`syncSnapshotLocked`), so a closing-window permit stayed enforced (or an opening-window deny never engaged) and an ip-monitoring failover route was missing from the restarted helper's FIB until the next scheduler/ipmon transition or commit.

## What
- Scheduler helperless arm: clone the retained snapshot, run `rebuildScheduledPolicySectionsWithLatchLocked` (enforces the #6480/#5680 hybrid guard; refusal returns a retryable error so the scheduler keeps `republishPending`), refresh capture authority, bump the retained generation.
- Overlay helperless arm: rebuild routes with the desired overlay (stashed across `prepareSnapshotForApply` so its derived-section rebuild cannot resurrect pre-overlay routes), plus scheduler sections when a scheduler state is carried; route-only folds enforce the #5680 hybrid guard explicitly.
- Both folds deliberately do NOT advance `publishedSnapshot`, `lastSnapshotHash`, or the applied identity — the helper accepted nothing, so the restart tick still sees unpublished work and replays the folded content; the applied/show scheduler state commits only when that publish lands.
- The #3780 "no snapshot ever published" nil arms are unchanged.
- The pre-existing no-helper test that pinned the stale-retained behaviour (`TestUpdatePolicyScheduleStateWithoutHelperDoesNotMutateSnapshot`) is updated to the new contract.

## Validation
- New `helper_down_fold_16643_test.go`: scheduler + overlay defect cells (retained snapshot carries `inactive=true` / the overlay route immediately; published/applied bookkeeping stays 0; modelled restart through the real `syncSnapshotLocked` sends exactly that content), helper-up controls, #3780 nil-arm cell — all pass.
- Fail-on-revert confirmed: restoring either early return reds its defect cell.
- Related suites pass: 9520, 5328, 13717 (#13717 latch staging), Overlay/Scheduler/Schedule filters.
- Known pre-existing failure (not introduced here): the `policy_sessions_convergence_12072` deferred-policy family fails identically on unmodified base `c40fe40` (`#15742` summary-count refusal in its own fixture setup).

## Risk
Retained-only folds run builders under `m.mu` while the helper is down (off the hot path, same builders as the helper-up path). Generation advances without a publish, which the status tick already treats as unpublished work. No daemon or wire changes.

## PR #17454 — feeds: re-bootstrap content epoch on first guarded install (#16651) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16651-rebootstrap-epoch`

Refs #16651

## Summary
A feed restored with a count baseline but no usable content epoch (legacy count-only record, epoch digest dropped as corrupt, or pre-#15075 rotated record) never re-established its epoch: `installSnapshot` keyed the epoch rebase on `!hasRememberedBaseline`, so the #14395 churn guard stayed predecessor-only forever, successive 51%-retained rotations could cumulatively replace an enforced set with zero refusals, and the epoch-less record was re-persisted on each restart.

`installSnapshot` now establishes the content epoch from the installed set whenever no epoch exists and the candidate has passed every guard (including the restored count high-water), and persists it via `rememberShrinkEpochLocked`. A live epoch is never moved by the new arm, so cumulative-rotation non-rebase semantics are unchanged. Restore-side comments and `pkg/feeds/README.md` updated to name the re-bootstrap on the first guarded install. The #16427 restore acceptance and the fail-closed digest-mismatch drop are unchanged.

RED pre-fix (`Prefixes:[] EpochHash:` persisted), GREEN post-fix.
- `TestCorruptEpochRestoreRebootstrapsEpoch16651` — digest-mismatch shape: epoch dropped on restore, re-bootstrapped on first install, refuses at step 2. RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix.

## PR #17456 — userspace-dp: preserve build overlay in apply-time route rebuild (#16640) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16640-overlay-rebuild`

Refs #16640

## Why

`rebuildDerivedSectionsAfterRevalidate` rebuilt `snap.Routes` with `routeOverlayForSnapshot(snap)`, which returned nil for every fresh Compile snapshot (its `Config` is not yet `m.lastSnapshot.Config`). The overlay the full build applied was discarded whenever apply-time revalidation moved or dropped a row — on HA nodes on every Compile, because the peer-fabric row is dropped — so the helper FIB routed the overlaid prefix (typically the WAN default) via the failed primary next hop from the Compile publish until the commit-tail `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` republish, spanning `applyFRRFull`/`applyRoutingRules`.

## What

Record the overlay a snapshot was built with on the snapshot itself:

- `ConfigSnapshot.builtRouteOverlay` (unexported; never on the wire or in the content hash) stamped by the full builder from its `routeOverlay` argument (cloned).
- Re-recorded by every site that rebuilds `Routes` from an explicit overlay: `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshotWithLatch` (helper-up and the #16643 helper-down fold, from `desiredOverlay`), `RefreshInterfaceRowsForLink` (from `m.routeOverlay`), and the apply-time rebuild itself (from the overlay it used).
- `routeOverlayForSnapshot` returns the recorded build overlay when present; a snapshot with no recorded build (hand-built) falls back to the previous retained-config identity check, so a foreign hand-built snapshot still never re-applies a moved `m.routeOverlay`.

NOT changed: the rebuild trigger, the route builder, and the commit-tail republish.

## Validation

- New `TestRebuildAfterRevalidatePreservesCompileOverlay16640` (3 cells) drives the real `prepareSnapshotForApply` with a dropped interface row:
  - fresh-Compile cell (built with overlay `10.0.0.253`, manager overlay since moved to `10.0.0.99`) keeps `10.0.0.253` — **RED pre-fix** (rebuilt default falls back to `10.0.0.1`), green post-fix;
  - retained-config control keeps the current overlay (passes both ways);
  - foreign hand-built snapshot keeps its authored route, no re-apply (passes both ways).
- Targeted `#14209/#14333/#15043/#15939/#16643` and route-overlay suites pass (`go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '...|TestHelperDown|16643'`, ok).
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` run shows only pre-existing base failures (config-fixture cells and `TestRetryDebtRetryConvergesAndSteadies9642`), verified identical on pristine `origin/master`.

## PR #17457 — eventengine: stop releasing e.mu for cooldown parks (#16645) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16645-cooldown-unlock`

Refs #16645

## Why
`maybeDeferCooldownLocked` unlocked `e.mu` mid-loop to take `pendingMu`, so a concurrent same-name redefinition landing in the unlock window paired the OLD policy's commands/plant class with the NEW semantic revision — in both the returned `triggeredPolicy` and the parked cooldown edge. `staleReason` compares revisions only, so the retracted batch passed the #3750 'policy redefined' gate and committed once under the new definition.

## What
- `captureDeferCooldownLocked` builds the parked `plannedAction` under `e.mu` from the live policy + current revision; never releases `e.mu`.
- `evaluateEventLocked` collects parks; `evaluateEventMode` inserts them under `pendingMu` only after `e.mu` is released (`insertDeferredCooldownParks`, first park per (policy,event) wins as before).
- Parked actions therefore always carry the producing generation's revision; after a redefinition the commit-time `staleReason` backstop rejects them as 'policy redefined'.
- New deterministic regression test holds `pendingMu` to land the redefinition exactly in the old unlock window (RED pre-fix: 'old p2 paired with new revision'; GREEN post-fix), plus a #15021 replay control.
- README + `docs/log/16645.md` updated.

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/eventengine/` clean
- New tests PASS, count=5 stable, `-race` clean together with #15945 deferred cells
- Targeted `TestEvaluateCooldown|TestDeferred|TestStale_` suites PASS
- Full `pkg/eventengine` suite: only the 9 pre-existing `multivalue_leaf_runtime_6673` failures (documented at #15945, on pristine base)

## Risk
Low. Deferral insertion shifts from mid-loop to just-after-evaluate (same `HandleEvent` call, before enqueue); first-park-wins semantics preserved; no lock-order change (`pendingMu` is simply never taken under `e.mu` on this path now).

## PR #17461 — userspace: discard stale status poll replies after a concurrent apply (#16653) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16653-stale-poll-fence`

Refs #16653

## Why
The 1 Hz status poll releases `m.mu` for its RPC and fenced the reply only on helper process identity and the link-cycle lease. A status applied by a concurrent mutator (durable fail-closed disarm, RG update, snapshot apply) while the poll was off-lock was overwritten by the older poll reply, resurrecting `userspace_ctrl.Enabled=1`, ready binding rows and `lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true` for up to one tick, with that tick's desired-forwarding reconcile seeing no delta.

## What
- `statusLoop` snapshots `m.lastStatusSeq` before dropping `m.mu` and discards the reply if any other status was applied in between (same whole-tick discard shape as the link-cycle fence). Every apply bumps `lastStatusSeq` via `setLastStatusLocked`, so the fence is exact and O(1).
- The owner-RG export pager sibling (R3-B16-02) is already closed by #16518 (`SuppressStatus`, pager never applies a page status) — verified on this head, no change needed.
- New `TestStalePollDoesNotOverwriteNewerDisarm16653` (overlap/twin/control arms through the real `statusLoop`) and `docs/log/16653.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestStalePollDoesNotOverwriteNewerDisarm16653|TestStatusLoopDoesNotHoldManagerLockAcrossStatusRPC13093|TestStatusReadAPIsDoNotWaitForManagerLock13093|TestStatusPollDoesNotRearmWorkersAfterLinkCycleStarts13093|TestExportPagedDoesNotApplyStalePageStatus16518' -count=1` — all pass.
- RED on revert: disabling the fence fails only the overlap arm (`Enabled=true ForwardingArmed=true`); twin and control pass.
- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean.
- Pre-existing `TestOwnerRGExportPageFitsTheResponseCap9344` failure is identical on the base head (unrelated reflected-size drift).

## Risk
A discarded poll skips one tick of level-triggered servicing; the next tick re-evaluates against the newer cached status, so no debt is lost. No new locking, allocation, or RPC behaviour.

## PR #17466 — eventengine: recompute deferred wake from parked state (#16658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16658-pending-wakeat`

Refs #16658

## Why
The #15021 deferred worker seeded each iteration's wake from the stored `pending.wakeAt`; the cooldown/budget candidate loops could only lower it and `drainDeferred` never cleared it. After the first deferred edge or budget deferral fully replayed, the stored wake lay in the past, the timer delay clamped to zero, and xpfd spun on zero-length timers (taking `pendingMu` and `e.mu` via `drainDeferred` on every pass, ~a core) for the rest of the daemon's life.

## What
- `deferredWorker` recomputes `wake` from zero on every iteration: minimum over cooldown anchors of parked cooldown holds plus, only when a budget hold is present, the budget expiry (`budgetWakeAtFn` override preferred, else oldest slot expiry). `pending.wakeAt` is stored unconditionally — zero when both maps are empty, so no timer is armed and the worker blocks on `pendingWake`/`stopCh`.
- `deferBudget`'s stored `wakeAt` is now only a hint for `wakeAtLocked` observers; it can never seed a timer.
- Regression tests `TestDeferredWorkerNoTimerSpinAfterCooldownReplay16658` (real-clock park→replay at ~30s, then timer count over a 1s idle second) and `TestDeferredWorkerNoTimerSpinAfterBudgetReplay16658` (deterministic budget drain) count deferred-worker timers and assert `wakeAt` is zero after drain. README documents the idle invariant; `docs/log/16658.md` added.

## Validation
- Both new tests FAIL on pre-fix code (stale `wakeAt` assertion) and PASS after; budget test also PASS under `-race`.
- `go vet ./pkg/eventengine/` clean; gofmt clean.
- Deferred-family suite (`-run 'Deferred|15945|16641|16848|Cooldown|Budget|16645'`): 28 PASS, including #15021/#15945/#16641/#16848 replay tests.
- Full `pkg/eventengine` suite: only the 9 pre-existing `multivalue_leaf_runtime_6673` failures, byte-identical on pristine master (base-attributed).

## Risk
Production path unchanged except the wake computation: with `budgetWakeAtFn` nil the worker takes the oldest-slot expiry exactly as before; fake-clock tests keep the 20ms timer cap. No queue, budget-cap, cooldown, or commit-path semantics change.

## PR #17470 — daemon: stop treating the WAN as the lifeline on committed boots (#16671) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16671-campaign`

Why:
On a committed xpf box fxp0 lives in vrf-mgmt (rendered without a main-table gateway), so the main-table default route is the WAN. `setupBootstrapLifeline` nevertheless wrote that route NIC over the verified persisted lifeline record, and `installFailClosedBootHostFences` added the route NIC to the protected set — so the bootstrap input guard admitted the WAN whole and the live-address fences withheld the WAN addresses. On a #1960/#10297 fail-closed cold boot, sshd/IKE stayed reachable on the untrust side until a compilable commit, and the record stayed poisoned.

What:
- `setupBootstrapLifeline` returns early when `EverCommitted()` is true: never-committed boxes still record a lifeline from route detection (appliance factory fallback already gated the same way); committed boxes keep the persisted record and the retained last-known-good state, and the WAN is never renamed to fxp0.
- `installFailClosedBootHostFences` derives management only from the persisted record plus the explicit leaf (via `resolveProtectedInterfaces`) and management-class names (`fxp*/fab*/em*` via `config.IsManagementIfName`), never from a main-table default route; the route-presence check is dropped and skip-on-unknown is kept in verified form (route error, or a detected management-class NIC that is not a verified identity, still skips).
- The input guard needs no change: with the record unpoisoned its existing rule excludes the detected WAN.
- NOT changed: never-committed foreign-host route fallback (accepted A7-05 recovery posture).

Validation:
- New `pkg/daemon/bootstrap_committed_wan_lifeline_16671_test.go`: committed witness RED pre-fix (record overwritten pci 0000:67:00.1 -> .2; fence installs 0 host fences — WAN withheld) and GREEN post-fix; guard excludes eno3 / admits eno2; fence covers 192.0.2.10 + 2001:db8::10, spares 10.0.0.1; never-committed control still writes the bootstrap .network.
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run '16671|TestResolveEarlyInputGuardLifelines|TestFailClosedBoot|TestSetupBootstrapLifelineAppliance|TestChooseBootstrapLifeline|TestIsApplianceFactoryBoot' -count=1` — PASS.
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` — clean. Full package run left to main-agent verification.

Risk:
Committed bootstrap boots no longer rename any NIC from route detection; they stay reachable at the existing management address on retained networkd state (documented #1960 freeze) and recover via a compilable `commit confirmed`. Residual: a committed box whose management NIC is kernel-named (eno*), unrecorded, and not the leaf now has that NIC fenced rather than exposed — console recovery applies (docs/log/16671.md).

## PR #17473 — lldp: wake RX goroutine via ppoll and eventfd on Stop (#16669) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16669`

Refs #16669

## Summary
LLDP Stop()/re-Apply could not wake the RX goroutine parked in a bare Recvfrom on the AF_PACKET socket: shutdown() is ENOTCONN on the connectionless socket and close() does not wake an in-flight Recvfrom on Linux, so teardown blocked until a frame arrived (forever on a silent link), wedging the daemon config-apply pipeline behind applySem and forcing the TimeoutStopSec SIGKILL path. This makes recv cancellable: a per-session wake eventfd + ppoll on {rxFD, wakeFD}, stopLocked reordered to cancel -> signalStop -> wg.Wait() -> close(), and a ctx re-check after every successful recv. The socketpair-only seam (which masked the defect, since shutdown does wake a SEQPACKET reader) is replaced with a real-wake ppoll seam plus a namespace-gated AF_PACKET/veth silent-vs-chatty acceptance test.

## Validation
- go vet ./pkg/lldp/ clean

- go test ./pkg/lldp/ -count=1 -race -run TestStop/TestSession/TestRxLoop/TestApply/TestStopSilent ok

## PR #17483 — daemon: return lifeline .network write error so bootstrap refuses the rename (#16682) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16682-lifeline-network-error`

Refs #16682

## Why
`writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork` laundered a failed `fsatomic.WriteFileAtomic` into `(false, nil)` — the #5842 shape, since `(false, nil)` already means "already correct". `setupBootstrapLifeline` refuses only on a non-nil error, so on a storage fault (ENOSPC/EROFS/EIO) it still wrote the `.link`, renamed/cycled the management NIC to fxp0 and reloaded, with no fxp0 `.network` to re-address it: the name-keyed host config no longer matched and the link cycle flushed the default route on a bootstrap box with nothing committed to roll back to.

## What
- Writer returns the wrapped write error (`write fxp0 .network %s: %w`, mirroring `writeLinkFile`/`writeBootstrapFxp0Network`), so the existing caller refusal fires before the `.link` write, the rename and the reload; the caller log now names both error sources (observation or write).
- The refusal is unconditional — not provenance-scoped like #6789's observation refusal — because a failed write means no correct `.network` exists for either provenance (the appliance factory DHCP content is exactly what failed to land).
- New witness test `TestLifelineNetworkWriteFailureRefusesRename16682` driving the real `setupBootstrapLifeline` over the in-tree #6789 seams with an index-0 `enp5s0` lifeline (static 192.0.2.10/24): witness (occupied target → write fails) + write-succeeds control + observation-fails control.
- README, debian/changelog, docs/log/16682.md updated.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestLifelineNetworkWriteFailureRefusesRename16682' -count=1 -v` — 3/3 subtests PASS (witness: renamed=false, reloaded=false, no .link, target untouched, writer returns (false, non-nil); controls unchanged).
- Fail-on-revert verified: restoring `return false, nil` reds the witness (`writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork on a failed write = (changed=false, err=<nil>)`).
- Regression sweep `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run '16682|6789|7114|12152|12156|SetupBootstrapLifeline' -count=1` ok; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean; gofmt clean.

## Risk
A box whose `.network` write fails now stays on its kernel name in bootstrap (console-only, retried next boot since the file is re-derived) instead of renaming onto a missing `.network` — the documented posture. No behavior change when the write succeeds or the observation fails.

## PR #17489 — logging: match event protocol by number, reject unknown tokens (#16688) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16688-event-protocol`

Refs #16688

## Why
`ParseEventFilterArgs` stored the protocol token raw and `EventFilter.matches` compared it with `EqualFold` against the rendered name (TCP/ICMPv6/ESP), never `ProtocolNum`. So `protocol 6` (the value the view prints as `protocol-id="6"`), `58`, `50`, `icmp6`, and a typo like `tcpx` all yielded an empty answer with no error — a forensic false negative on the local CLI, remote ShowText, gRPC `GetEvents` and REST surfaces sharing this matcher, while matching events sat in the buffer.

## What
- `EventFilter` gains `ProtocolNum`/`HasProtocol` (mirroring `HasZone`, so protocol 0/HOPOPT stays selectable); `matches` compares the resolved number against `rec.ProtocolNum`, falling back to resolving the rendered name only when `ProtocolNum==0` (mirrors `monitorFlowFilter`, #13553), and resolves a directly-set `Protocol` string through the same table so literal filters behave identically.
- New `logging.ResolveEventProtocol` wraps the `appid.ProtocolNumber` SSOT.
- All builders resolve once and fail closed: `ParseEventFilterArgs` → unknown-protocol usage error, gRPC `GetEvents` → `InvalidArgument`, REST → HTTP 400.
- NOT changed: action matching stays exact case-insensitive (#2939); an absent protocol stays no-filter on every surface.

## Validation
- New tests pass post-fix: logging 18 protocol-token subtests (6/58/50/icmp6/47/89/ospf/0 defect cells + name controls + legacy `ProtocolNum==0` fallback) plus unknown-token rejection and direct literal filters; gRPC numeric/alias/absent/bogus; REST same matrix (HTTP 400).
- RED evidence: reverting only the `matches` protocol arm to `EqualFold(rec.Protocol, f.Protocol)` makes `protocol=6` return 0 events (want 2) and 58/50/icmp6/47/ospf/17 likewise fail.
- Existing pins green: `TestParseEventFilterArgs`, `TestEventFilterExactNotSubstring` (#2939), zone-0 (#3338), limit (#4926); full `pkg/logging` suite ok. `go vet` + gofmt clean.
- Full `pkg/api` suite: only pre-existing NAT 10437/10438 failures, byte-identical on pristine master (base-attributed).

## Risk
Builders that previously accepted any protocol token now error — the intended fail-closed change (#3347 class); no enforcement-path effect. A hand-built bogus `EventFilter` still matches nothing. A non-zero `ProtocolNum` remains authoritative over the rendered name, as in #13553.

Branch: `fix/16675-lifeline-rename-rollback`

Refs #16675

## Why
Bootstrap exit renames a non-index-0 foreign-host lifeline positionally
(`enp6s0` → `ge-0-0-0`, writing `10-xpf-ge-0-0-0.link` with
`OriginalName=enp6s0`), but `runBootstrapTeardownSteps` removed only
takeover `.network` files and kept every `.link`. A timed-out first
`commit confirmed` therefore left the management NIC renamed and
unaddressed across reboots — the host's own kernel-name-keyed config
(netplan `[Match] Name=enp6s0`, ifupdown, networkd `Name=`) never
matched again — while the rollback logged success. Console-only
recovery, on exactly the event commit confirmed exists to survive.

## What
- `captureBootstrapLifelineRenamePreExit` (new, called from
  `maybeExitBootstrapOnFirstConfig` BEFORE `runBootstrapExitStartup`):
  records the lifeline's pre-takeover kernel name and the positional
  logical name from the same `assignName` derivation the takeover will
  use. Positional mode only — device-map never claims an unmapped
  lifeline, and index-0 renames to fxp0, already covered by the
  `.network` restore.
- The pair persists in the generation-bound
  `bootstrapLifelineSnapshotRecord`
  (`LifelineKernelName`/`LifelineLogicalName`), so it survives a daemon
  restart inside the first-commit window; cleared on confirm and on
  durable-teardown completion.
- `restoreBootstrapLifelineRename` (first-commit teardown only, the
  `restoreLifeline`/`confirmPrevFirst` scope): verifies the takeover
  `.link`'s `OriginalName=` against the captured kernel name, renames
  back via `renameInterfaceFn`, and only then removes the `.link`.
  Fail-closed on provenance — mismatched `.link`, an unprovenanced
  logical-named lifeline, an unexpected live name, or a failed rename
  all retain file + live name and report DEGRADED instead of a clean
  rollback. Rename-first ordering means a failed rename-back never
  destroys the retry evidence.

  NIC; the index-0 fxp0 `.network` restore path.

## PR #17491 — daemon: drop peer-slot DHCP and RA members on the peer node (#16685) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16685-peer-slot-dhcp`

Refs #16685

## Why
A shared-section DHCP group member on the peer node's FPC slot (`ge-0/0/3` shared, compiled on node1) was kept on both nodes: it is not RG-scoped, so the #6520 node-local arm retained it, and the #15206 belt kept it because the name is declared (on the peer). Node1 has no `ge-0-0-3` device (its ports are `ge-7-0-*`), so Kea refused the whole family file and the peer served nothing — including RETH segments after RG failover, with the #6535 converger re-driving the refused state indefinitely.

- `filterDHCPConfigForMasterRGsWithMasters` (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go) drops a non-RG member whose `config.InterfaceSlot` maps via `config.SlotToNodeID` to a node other than `cfg.Chassis.Cluster.NodeID` (`isPeerSlotInterface16685`), setting `MembersFiltered` when a group shrinks; a peer-slot-only group disappears. - `clusterRAConfigSets` (pkg/daemon/daemon_ra_reconcile.go) applies the same rule to node-local RA interfaces, whose sender would otherwise fail to bind a nonexistent device on every reconcile.

- `go test -count=1 -run TestPeerSlot ./pkg/daemon/` — ok (5 tests: per-node CompileConfigForNode shared shape v4+v6, mixed group MembersFiltered, grouped shape unchanged, Kea-render precondition, RA sibling both nodes/masterships).

Not introduced by this change.

## Risk
A cluster config whose Chassis.Cluster.NodeID disagreed with the actual node would drop that node's own slot members; NodeID is the compiled per-node identity used by every other slot predicate (monitor.go, RethToPhysical).

## PR #17494 — daemon: reconcile rollback-target feeds at fire time (#16661) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16661`

Refs #16661

## Why
A commit-confirmed window whose abandoned config removes or renames a dynamic-address feed could never roll back. C2's apply cancels the rollback target's (C1's) feed producer, so the #9615 fire-time check deferred 24x5s waiting for a producer only the rollback's own apply would restart, then entered bootstrap — resigning every RG / dropping transit.

## What
- pkg/daemon/confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go: before classifying a feed-only refusal at fire time, detect whether any feed named by the target's bindings has no running producer (rollbackTargetFeedProducersAbsent via feeds.Manager.AllFeeds). If absent, reconcile the feed producers FOR THE TARGET (reconcileFeeds(target), the same step a normal target apply runs), restart the bounded deferral, and let the async fetch converge through onUpdate / the next deferred fire. Bootstrap is never reached for a feed-only refusal whose producer was absent.
- Present-but-unfetched (late feed, #9615) and present-but-never-installing (server down) producers keep the existing bounded deferral then safe-state semantics; no-manager / half-built daemon (#6739) unchanged. DNS-only (#16612), statically refused, and healthy targets unchanged; arm-time #6707 gate untouched.
- Regression tests with a real feeds.Manager against an httptest TLS feed server (apply body runs only real reconcileFeeds): remove and rename arms apply c1-feed-target with bootstrap=false; classifier pins absent vs present; feed-still-down control still takes the bounded safe state.
- README (#9615 section) and docs/log/16661.md updated.

## Validation
- go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 16661/9615 cells: 4 new + 8 existing controls pass.
- -race run of new cells + healthy/refused/feed-bound 9615 controls: pass.
- Pre-existing TestRecoveredDNS*16612 failures reproduce identically on clean origin/master (environment DNS), unrelated.

## Risk
While the target's producers run during deferral, onUpdate applies the still-active C2 with the target's feed overlay (idempotent; C2 binds no removed feed). Bounded deferral still guarantees resolution within 24x5s of producer restart. No lab run; bootstrap teardown remains in-process only, as in the source probe.

## PR #17497 — userspace-dp: subtract 28 for fragment quotes in PTB translation (#16666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16666-campaign`

Why:
The PTB arm of `translate_icmpv6_message_to_icmpv4` advertised `PTB_MTU - 20` unconditionally. When the packet in error is a translated IPv6 fragment it carries an 8-byte Fragment Header and is `v4_len + 28`, so the relayed Next-Hop MTU was 8 bytes too large: every DF-clear retry at that MTU still exceeded the IPv6 bottleneck and elicited another PTB — a non-converging PMTUD black hole violating RFC 7915 §5.2's MUST to take the Fragment Header into account.

What:
- `EmbeddedV6ToV4Layout` carries `has_fragment_header` from the `ipv6_fragment_header` walk it already performed (`userspace-dp/src/nat64/icmp.rs`).
- The PTB arm inspects the embedded quote via that shared layout and subtracts `NAT64_HEADER_DELTA + NAT64_FRAGMENT_HEADER_LEN` (28) when a Fragment Header is present, 20 otherwise. A quote that fails the layout aborts the whole error translation anyway, so the -20 fallback cannot emit a wrong MTU.
- New `NAT64_FRAGMENT_HEADER_LEN` (8) in `userspace-dp/src/nat64/translate.rs`.
- Reverse Frag-Needed arm (§4.2) audited and documented in place: fragmented outer ICMP is dropped before it (#2562), so its +20 is correct for every reachable input; the quote's own fragment state is handled by `translate_embedded_v4_to_v6` emitting the quote's Fragment Header.
- NOT changed: clamps, plateau logic, embedded-quote translation. No gate weakened, no fail-open path added.

Validation:
- `nat64_v6_to_v4_ptb_fragment_quote_uses_delta28_16666` (1400 → 1372, embedded MF + checksums verified), `nat64_v6_to_v4_ptb_atomic_fragment_quote_uses_delta28_16666` (1372), `nat64_v6_to_v4_ptb_unfragmented_quote_keeps_delta20_16666` (1380 control) — 4 passed including the pre-existing 1500→1480 cell.
- RED evidence: forcing the delta back to 20 fails both fragment tests (1380 != 1372); control passes.
- Full `nat64::` module: 243 passed, 10 failed — identical 10 failures on origin/master base (240 passed), pre-existing and unrelated.

Risk:
Only the advertised MTU for fragment-quoting PTBs changes (8 bytes smaller, the RFC-correct value). Residual: none known.

Refs #16666

The six `expired-leases-processing` leaves were validated min-only, so a value above the deployed Kea parser's hard maximum (e.g. `max-time 30000`) committed clean, rendered verbatim, and made Kea refuse the whole family file at the fail-closed restart — a family-wide DHCP outage on the node, and on both cluster nodes because the block is synced and rendered there (#9348). ## PR #17502 — config: reject over-limit route-based VPNs at commit (#16699) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16699-campaign`

## Why
The IPsec capture generation is bounded to 32 distinct route-based VPN tunnels (`ipsecCaptureMaxTunnels`, 4 NFQUEUE provenance classes each), but no commit-time limit existed. A 33rd distinct `bind-interface` committed cleanly, `stageIpsecCapture` discarded the bound error (`staged, _ = quarantineWith(QUEUE_OPEN, errIpsecQueueExhausted)`) and returned a QuarantineAll(QUEUE_OPEN) runtime with a nil error, and `commitIpsecCaptureStage` installed it — every apply dropped all non-loopback, non-lifeline kernel INPUT/FORWARD while the commit reported success (residual of #15068).

## What
- `pkg/config`: export `MaxRouteBasedVPNCaptureTunnels = 32`; the `validateSecureTunnelBindInterfaceAST` gate counts DISTINCT non-zero XFRM if_ids and hard-rejects above the limit on strict commit/commit-check naming the limit, warns on the lenient load/peer-sync path (#1960, mirrors #10638). VPNs sharing one bind-interface count once (distinct tunnels, not VPN stanzas).
- `pkg/daemon`: alias `ipsecCaptureMaxTunnels` to the config constant (no drift); every QUEUE_OPEN `quarantineWith` site in `stageIpsecCapture` (per-generation bound, queue alloc, queue open, reinject submitter) now returns its wrapped error. The staged quarantine runtime is still installed fail-closed by `commitIpsecCaptureStage`, but `captureStageErr` joins the apply error so an over-cap fails the commit visibly. Unknown-reason quarantines keep nil return (out of QUEUE_OPEN scope).

NOT changed: the 32-tunnel capacity itself; plan-level IFIDUnderivable/LinkLookup/OwnerContested quarantines. Note `applyConfigLocked` marks capture committed on stage error and still installs the staged quarantine via `commitIpsecCaptureStage` (fail-closed preserved); only error visibility changes.

## Validation

- Daemon: `TestIpsecCaptureBeyond32TunnelsStillQuarantines15068` now requires a non-nil stage error naming 32/#16699 wrapping `errIpsecQueueExhausted` (RED on master: nil error); `TestIpsecCaptureAdd31To32` / `Rezone32` controls pass; full `TestIpsecCapture*`/`TestIpsecQueue*` suites pass; `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean.

## PR #17506 — ha: replay session deltas on reconnect (#16627) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16627-connected-drain-replay`

ha: replay session deltas on reconnect (#16627)

Refs #16627.

## Why
While the event stream was connected, Go's 5s reconciliation drain popped the RPC-fallback copy of every already-streamed delta and re-stamped it with a fresh generation. A partial replay resurrected sessions the stream had already closed (surviving the open-only LossResync until idle timeout) and transiently deleted live same-tuple successors.

## What
- Per-binding sequence: `SessionDeltaInfo` gains `stream_seq` (Rust + Go `StreamSeq`), returned by the lossless enqueue (`push_delta_lossless_within_seq`) and stamped from the binary frame header in `installEventStreamCallbacks`. 0 = never stream-carried.
- Rust `flush_session_deltas`: mirror to the fallback buffer ONLY when the lossless enqueue did not succeed — not on mere `is_connected` (connected-but-full still mirrors, seq 0; CommandExport always mirrors per #9630).
- Go connected discard (`discardUserspaceSessionDeltasLocked`): discard ONLY items with `StreamSeq != 0 && StreamSeq <= LastAppliedSequence()` (applied watermark from `eventstream.go`); queue everything else. Schema fingerprint recorded ONLY on valid status (err == nil) in `full_resync_transaction_9767.go`.

## Validation
- Go: `TestConnectedDrainDiscardsStreamedReplay16627` (same-KEY successor — same SrcPort — plus standalone {close S1, open S2} suffix), `TestConnectedDrainQueuesUnsequencedReplay16627`, `TestDiscardOnlyCoveredByAppliedWatermark16627`, `TestDiscardRecordsSchemaOnlyOnValidStatus16627`. RED-on-revert executed: connected arm reverted to the queueing drain fails replay_open_S1_only / replay_close_S1_only / replay_open+close_S1.
- Rust: `stream_delivered_delta_is_not_left_in_fallback_buffer_16627` (streamed incremental+bulk leave fallback empty with seq 1; connected-but-full mirrors seq 0; disconnected/no-handle/CommandExport mirror).
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace` targeted parity/schema tests pass; `cargo check` clean.

## Risk
`stream_seq` participates in the #7194 derived schema fingerprint on both sides (agreement preserved); a mixed old/new helper-daemon pair mismatches and withholds like any prior schema addition. A delta whose enqueue races a disconnect is mirrored with seq 0 and queued once, healed by the loss-of-sync resync it also triggers. No lab cluster run; daemon-level + helper unit-level coverage per the issue acceptance.

## PR #17514 — daemon: propagate sync-hold mirror transitions on VRRP, cluster, and reconcile paths (#16692) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16692-synchold-vrrp`

Refs #16692

## Why
In legacy `no-private-rg-election` mode, `watchVRRPEvents` never refreshed the #15258 sync-hold mirror. The preempt MASTER event that `ReleaseSyncHold` itself triggers was judged against `syncHold=true`: no rg_active write and no RETH services. `syncRGSyncHold` in `handleClusterEvent`/`reconcileRGState` then discarded the transition its own `SetSyncHold` produced, so neither path saw `tr.Changed` — the preempt-failback owner served no RG-scoped Kea DHCP and re-initiated no RG-anchored IPsec SAs until an unrelated edge or commit.

## What
- `syncRGSyncHold()` now returns per-RG transitions.
- `watchVRRPEvents` and `watchClusterEvents` refresh the mirror scoped to the event's RG at the top of per-event handling and pass the transition to the extracted `handleVRRPEvent` / `handleClusterEventMerged`, which re-refresh scoped and merge via `mergeSyncHoldTransition` (widens only `Changed`, keeping the caller's final Active/Epoch/InvalidateSeq).
- `reconcileRGState` ORs the pass-wide refresh into each RG's `tr`.
- Scoping prevents one RG's event from consuming another RG's pending release edge (pinned by test).
- Docs: README contract section, debian/changelog, docs/log/16692.md.

Note: upstream master already added the nil-`applySem` guards to the connected-RG republish entry points during rebase, so that ancillary hunk dropped out; production code change is `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go` only.

## Validation
- New `reth_sync_hold_vrrp_16692_test.go` (4 tests), services observed via the proxy-ARP nudge `applyRethServicesForRG` always sends:
  - post-release VRRP MASTER: rg_active=true written, services exactly once;
  - release-only reconcile: held control writes/serves nothing, post-release pass writes+serves exactly once, steady-state pass does not re-run;
  - post-release cluster promotion activates;
  - scoped refresh leaves RG2's mirror held until reconcile actuates it.
- RED-on-revert verified: disabling the VRRP merge and the reconcile OR makes the first two rows FAIL (restored after).
- Sibling guards pass: `TestRethSyncHold*14406/15258`, `TestEventVsReconcileEquivalence16124`, `TestRethDemotionFence*`, fence/actuation and proxy-ARP nudge tests. `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean. Post-rebase re-run green.

## Risk
Bounded to legacy RETH-VRRP mode; private-RG default unaffected (`InSyncHold` false → no-op merge). Services run exactly once per release (Changed only widened when the mirror itself flipped). Residual: R3-A34-04 (cluster-leg service producer) is distinct and untouched.

- Full `go test ./cmd/cli/ ./pkg/cli/ -count=1` carries pre-existing origin/master failures, sampled base-attributed in a pristine worktree (FRR parity, zones detail, predefined application sets, multi-pipe dispatch; remote gofmt/value-slot census). Base at branch point: `e3dba79c90`.
- Prompt string is not directly observable in a unit test (chzyer/readline keeps it in its RuneBuffer, no getter), so cells assert the state that determines it (`configMode`/`InConfigMode`, cleared cursor, exit banner).

## PR #17521 — config: skip event plant-class compiles when no commands payload exists (#16722) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16722`

Refs #16722

## Why
Every interactive candidate mutation ran `StampChangedEventPlantClasses`, which ran two full `CompileConfigLenient` compiles (before+after trees) under the config-store write lock even when the config had no event-options at all — ~0.1-0.6s per `set` at 1k-8k lines, O(lines × config) for pasted input, blocking other sessions and confirm-timeout rollback.

## What
Gate the stamper on `treeMayHaveEventCommands9984`, a cheap raw scan that descends only into event-options subtrees (direct and nested-container policies), group definition bodies, and policy-local `apply-groups`/`-except`. It requires a real `change-configuration commands` payload (tail values or children, reusing `eventPolicyHasCommands9984`), so bare keywords and unrelated `then`/description lookalikes never trip it. When neither tree may carry commands, stamping is a provable no-op and returns before either compile; otherwise behaviour is byte-identical.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run '<stamp+gate suites>'` — all #9984/#14142 tests plus new `TestTreeMayHaveEventCommands16722` (18 rows) and `TestStampGateSkipsOnlyCommandless16722` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/eventengine/ -run 'PlantClass|9984'` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 'TestSetHostNameLargeConfigNoEventCompile16722|TestFlatSetCannotForgeSuperuserPlantClass9984'` PASS (16k-line commandless `set system host-name` under a generous 5s ceiling; decisive fail-on-revert is the gate unit tests)
- `TestEventPlantClassPersistsReloadsAndRollback9984` fails identically on clean origin/master (pre-existing #14660 `link_down` fixture rejection), unrelated
- gofmt/vet clean

## Risk
A gate false-negative would silently skip re-stamping a changed commands payload (fail-open attribution). Mitigated by forcing the full path for grouped, nested, packed, flat child-shape, inactive, and policy-local apply-groups shapes, all pinned by tests; the gate errs toward compiling.

## PR #17525 — ipsec: drop box-shared local PSK owner and scope secrets to peer only (#16708) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

## Why
#15193 added a local owner (`%any`, the pinned local address, or the configured local-id — all shared by every VPN on a box) to every non-responder PSK secret. strongSwan enumerates a secret when ANY owner matches EITHER side of the `(me, other)` pair and the IKEv2 PSK verifier tries every enumerated secret, so each secret verified every peer: a holder of one VPN's PSK authenticated into another fixed VPN from its peer's address, and into a responder-only `dynamic hostname` VPN from any address (reopening #14591), installing the child SA on the victim's st0 if_id.

A hostname-addressed PSK VPN with no `remote-identity` has no peer selector, so a new render belt skips it like the #14591/#15989 shapes.
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_responder_identity_14591.go`: the same hostname/inline-hostname shapes are rejected at strict commit (tolerant paths warn, render belt skips).
- NOT changed: connection rendering (remote.id pin, local.id, proposals), pubkey and responder-only connection shapes, hex PSK rendering.
- New `policy_shared_owner_16708_test.go` / compiler hostname test; #15193/#16680/#15766/#5630/#6469 expectations and #9641 fixtures move to peer-only secrets; README/config-schema/log updated.

## Validation

- GREEN after: full `pkg/ipsec` and `pkg/config` suites pass.
- Charon 6.1.0 netns lab (`docs/log/16708.md`): HEAD wrong-key attempts establish in both cases (if_id 0x1/0x2); fixed render answers `AUTH_FAILED`, and correct-key peer- and xpf-initiated IKEv2 establish in the default, pinned-local, local-id, multi-address and dynamic shapes.

## Risk
Operator-visible: a PSK VPN on a hostname-addressed gateway with no `remote-identity` no longer loads (commit rejects, render skips; siblings unaffected) — configure `remote-identity` or use an IP literal. IKEv1 initiator selection is argued from `phase1.c` (configured-identity + address fallbacks) and loss-cluster IKE lab verification remains outstanding, as for #15193/#16680.

## PR #17529 — configstore: bound pre-commit LCS diff to linear memory (#16718) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16718-lcs`

Refs #16718

## Why
Every console `commit` and gRPC Commit called `CommitDiffSummary`, which built a full `(lines+1)^2` int LCS table: 1.1 GiB at 12k set lines, 2 GiB at 16k, inside xpfd — seconds of stall and OOM risk on the 4 GiB appliance for configs that pass every size gate, for a cosmetic counter.

## What
- `sequenceLineDiffCounts` now trims the common prefix/suffix, computes the exact LCS length of the remaining middle with two DP rows (`lcsLengthLinear`, shorter side as row axis), and falls back to multiset counts only when the middle exceeds `maxExactLCSCells` (1<<22) so a pathological full rewrite cannot stall the commit.
- Order/duplicate semantics from #15168 and #13231 stay exact for ordinary inputs; the oversized-middle fallback keeps multiplicities, not order (documented in code, changelog, `docs/log/16718.md`).
- NOT changed: callers (CLI/gRPC), summary format, any commit behaviour. REST never called it.

## Validation

- RED on old implementation: 1,180,047,352 bytes at 12k lines, failing the 10 MiB bound (temporary probe, removed after verification).
- `TestCommitDiffSummaryReorder15168`, `TestCommitDiffSummaryDuplicateLines_13231`, `TestCommitDiffSummary` green. Commit-focused suite `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 'TestCommit|TestSequence|TestStoreCommit|Diff' -count=1` = 92 PASS, 0 FAIL; `go vet` clean.

## PR #17530 — userspace-dp: learn WG outer PMTU from validated underlay PTB (#16711) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16711-wg-pmtu`

Why: The AF_XDP WireGuard transit encap sized its IPv6 outer to the
local egress link MTU (or a static route `mtu`) and emitted it as one
unfragmentable datagram. Nothing learned the underlay path MTU from
an ICMPv6 Packet-Too-Big, so a smaller MTU beyond the first hop
dropped every oversize outer silently and permanently (TCP stall,
large non-TCP loss, no PTB to the inner source, `encap_mtu_drops`
stayed 0).

What: Per-peer outer PMTU soft state (`wg/pmtu.rs`: floor 1280 v6 /
68 v4, shrink-only, 10-min aging, RFC 8201) on `Peer` +
`WgEngine` accessors + `pmtu_learned` counter.
`frame::wg::consume_wg_outer_ptb` (ICMPv6 type 2, ICMPv4 3/4)
accepts only a quote that is a live WG outer: UDP, quoted src port
= `wg_listen_port`, quoted dst = a peer's configured-or-roamed
endpoint (address+port), quoted src = the local PTB destination.
Wired into the flowless poll arm after the #5690 reversal; the PTB
itself still falls through to normal LocalDelivery (no gate
weakened). The learned value caps `wg_encap_frame` and the
`outer_physical_egress_mtu` SSOT behind `post_transform_inner_mtu`
/ segmentation, so the next oversize inner yields an inner-source
PTB advertising `wg_inner_mtu(learned)`. Unchanged: IPv4 DF-clear
twin, TUN-origin guard, `wg_tcp_mss` (residuals in
`docs/log/16711.md`).

Validation: `cargo check` clean. `cargo test --bins -- wg_pmtu`:
3 passed — valid PTB(1400) -> inner MTU == `wg_inner_mtu(AF_INET6,
1400)` == 1320, 1320 inner encaps / 1321 drops; forged quotes
(wrong ports / non-peer dst) ignored, larger PTB never raises the
learned value; floor/aging rules. Broader `wg_`/`post_transform_wg`:
234 passed, 4 failed, all 4 base-attributed on `e3dba79c90`
(stash-verified).

Risk: A forged PTB quoting a live peer endpoint+port can lower
that peer's budget to the floor until aging expires it (standard
PMTU exposure, bounded by quote validation, visible via
`pmtu_learned`). Lab two-hop reduced-MTU verify outstanding.

## PR #17532 — flowexport: saturate tracker deltas and keep Touch monotonic (#16750) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16750-campaign`

Refs #16750

## Why

`deltaRecord` (`pkg/flowexport/tracker_15655.go`) subtracted the last-export baselines with plain unsigned arithmetic, and `Touch`/`TouchBidirectional` overwrote every stored cumulative counter field with whatever the latest snapshot carried. This is latent while the live feed misses every lookup (R3-A46-08 / #16760), but the moment that feed hits, a snapshot that races backwards (helper restart, mirror-row alternation between workers) can drive a stored field below its baseline and the next interim/final emits a ~2^64-wrapped delta — one such record poisons collector top-talker / billing aggregates. The close path already saturates via `satSub` (`exportSessionCloseRemainder`: "Saturating at zero guards a close whose counters raced backwards"); the tracker path did not.

## What

- `Touch` / `TouchBidirectional`: keep the per-field maximum instead of overwriting; a backward field never lowers the stored cumulative.
- Activity is now any single field advancing (per-field progress), not the forward+reverse sum — the sum can stay flat while one field genuinely progresses and a backward mirror field offsets it.
- `deltaRecord`: use `satSub` for Packets/Bytes/RevPackets/RevBytes, matching the close-remainder contract.
- Deliberately NOT changed: #16760 (live-feed byte order) — cohort issue, separate lane; this PR is the saturation/monotonicity half so it is safe to land before or after #16760.

## Validation

- New tests `pkg/flowexport/backward_counters_16750_test.go` (4 tests):
  - Acceptance probe: after a first interim at 100 fwd packets, a backward forward snapshot (50) with genuine reverse progress (900) reports **0 forward / 900 reverse** on the second interim — never a wrap, never past the lifetime total.
  - Per-field max for both `Touch` and `TouchBidirectional` with an advancing sibling field as control.
  - Direct `deltaRecord` saturation below baseline with an above-baseline control field (2000−1000=1000).
  - Per-field activity: sum-flat-but-one-field-advancing counts as activity; a fully backward snapshot does not revive an idle flow, whose final still carries the monotonic maxima.
- RED evidence: all 4 fail pre-fix (second interim wrapped to `18446744073709551566` forward packets), pass post-fix.
- Full package: `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -count=1` PASS (existing #15655/#16303 delta-sum tests unchanged and green); `go vet` clean; gofmt clean.

## Risk

A flow fed only backward readings no longer counts those readings as inactive-timer activity and can expire on the inactive timer; its close still exports the unexported span via `CloseFlow` baselines, as before. Residual: #16760 must still land for the live feed to hit at all — this PR only guarantees that when it does, backward readings cannot corrupt exported deltas.

## PR #17536 — config: refuse commits discarded by commit-confirmed rollback (#16719) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16719-campaign`

Why:
A non-first `commit confirmed` (A -> C) with staged edits C' let a bare commit parked on applySem promote the rollback target A after the confirm timeout discarded C', reporting success ("commit complete: N statement(s) changed") with the pre-rollback C->C' summary while A ran and no timer remained. The #15055 holder-epoch bump was scoped to the first-commit branch, so an ordinary rollback left the parked commit's authority valid — the exact success-for-a-candidate-not-promoted property #6808/#15055 protect.

What:
- `PromoteRollback` captures `dirty` before the reset and, on a dirty discard, advances a dedicated monotonic `rollbackDiscardGen` counter (not `holderEpoch`: the holder never turns over in this shape, so pre-/post-discard mints share an epoch and no ordering on it separates them).
- `AuthorizeCommitAs` records the counter in every store-minted authority; `verifyCommitAuthorityLocked` refuses a stale mint with the new `ErrCommitConfirmedRolledBack` sentinel (never a generation conflict — the daemon retry would adopt the reset candidate — and never a holder turnover).
- `InternalCommitter` commits are fenced in the daemon: `commitAndApply`/`commitConfirmedAndApply` sample `RollbackDiscardGen()` before `applySem.Acquire`; `commitWithGenBinding` re-checks via `PromotionStale` before every promotion attempt.
- Clean rollbacks invalidate nothing (the #15055 control is preserved); fresh mints after a discard commit normally.
- NOT changed: first-commit #15055 bump/bootstrap recheck, boot recovery, standalone CLI non-Gen path.

Validation:
- `go vet ./pkg/configstore/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run '16719|15055'` PASS; `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run '16719|15055|TestCommitWithGenBinding|TestCommitSeam|TestRenameAncestry'` PASS (17 tests, incl. no-timeout twin control and parked commit-confirmed arm).
- RED probe: neutralizing the `rollbackDiscardGen` advance fails `TestNonFirstRollbackDiscardingDirtyCandidateInvalidatesPreRollbackAuthority16719` and `TestPromotionStaleTracksDirtyDiscard16719`.

Risk:
A commit racing a dirty-discarding rollback now returns an explicit "commit-confirmed window rolled back; staged edits were discarded" error instead of success; operators must re-stage the discarded edits. No other commit path changes behaviour.

## PR #17540 — daemon: report unmanaged sshd in show and commit advisory (#16737) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16737-ssh-show-truthful`

## Summary

Refs #16737 (R3-A45-03). Removing `system services ssh` only removed the xpf-managed sshd drop-in; sshd kept serving under base-image defaults while both `show system services` renderers dropped the SSH row entirely, so a Junos-trained operator decommissioning SSH on a zone admitting `ssh`/`all` kept tcp/22 reachable with no visible signal.

Implements the acceptance's show-plus-advisory leg (enablement ownership deliberately not taken — lifeline recovery depends on sshd existing outside xpf's config lifecycle):

- Both renderers (`pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_system.go`) always print an SSH row: `running (not managed — no system services ssh; sshd serves under base-image defaults)` when the stanza (or `System.Services` itself on the gRPC path) is absent. The stanza-present row is byte-identical to before and composes with the just-landed #16735 effective root-login display (rebased onto it).
- A commit whose zone `host-inbound-traffic` admits SSH (`ssh`, `all` via the #3226 expansion, or `any-service`; zone-level and per-interface overrides) with no stanza carries a per-zone advisory naming the zone, the mechanism, and the remedy (`pkg/config/ssh_unmanaged_advisory_16737.go`). Suppressed on tolerant load/peer-sync paths via the new `suppressSSHUnmanagedAdvisory16737` opt, registered in the #16166 lenient-completeness allowlist.
- The divergence is documented in `docs/feature-gaps.md` (SSH Key Exchange row) and `pkg/daemon/README.md` (factory drop-in section); changelog in `docs/log/16737.md`.

NOT changed: the drop-in lifecycle, `HostInboundServiceMatch` (the `all` expansion still admits tcp/22 — the fix makes that visible rather than silently narrowing admission), sshd start/stop, and the #16735 stanza-present display cell.

## Tests

RED on origin/master with only the new test files copied in: advisory cells fail (`warnings=[]`), both not-managed show cells fail (no SSH row); managed-row controls pass pre- and post-fix.

Post-fix (and re-verified after the rebase onto #16735):
- `pkg/config`: `TestSSHUnmanagedAdvisory16737*` (5 tests incl. tolerant-path silence) + `TestLenientCompileOptsCompleteness16166` — pass
- `pkg/cli` / `pkg/grpcapi`: `TestShowSystemServicesSSH*` (2 + 3) and the full adjacent `TestShowSystemServices` suites — pass
- `go vet` clean on all touched packages; `gofmt` clean

## Residuals

- Live-VM proof that sshd listens after stanza removal was not re-run; the mechanism is structural (no stop/disable/mask exists in the tree).
- Per-interface overrides are checked independently, so a replace-style override that removes SSH while the zone set admits it still warns once — advisory-only over-warning, never a false negative.

## PR #17548 — cluster: confirm never-seen peer absent without a receiver (#16751) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16751-campaign`

Why:
`peerConfirmedAbsent` was written only by `handlePeerNeverSeen`, whose sole production caller was the heartbeat receiver's `checkTimeout`. When the heartbeat could not start at all — the control interface has no address because a back-to-back control cable to a powered-off peer has no carrier and networkd (`ConfigureWithoutCarrier=false`) never configures it, so the daemon's 60s start retry exhausts — no receiver existed, absence was never confirmed, and every non-preempt RG stayed secondary indefinitely. The hold precedes the readiness gate, so not even the 2-minute degraded fallback armed: the surviving node of a dead pair forwarded nothing for as long as the peer stayed down.

What:
Own the never-seen clock in the Manager. `UpdateConfig` arms it while a control interface is configured and no peer has been seen; after the same `heartbeatStartupGrace` floor the receiver uses, it drives the existing `handlePeerNeverSeen` itself, re-probing the #11566 fresh session-sync proof every 1s with no fixed cap. A peer heartbeat, removal of the control interface, or `Stop` disarms it (generation-guarded against a callback parked on `m.mu`); routine config re-applies keep the first arming stamp so a commit cannot push the floor out. The receiver's own never-seen arm is unchanged and both paths funnel into the at-most-once confirmation, preserving the #4386 floor, #11566 suppression and #10697 readiness-gated/degraded shape by construction.
NOT changed: the daemon heartbeat retry and networkd unit generation — the Manager clock bounds the outage regardless of why the address is missing, making `ConfigureWithoutCarrier` hardening unnecessary here. Complementary to #16746's config-layer gate (different files, no overlap; coordinated with that lane).

Validation:
- New `heartbeat_neverseen_noreceiver_16751_test.go` (6 tests, 8 cells, **no receiver ever created**): ready RG promotes, unready RG promotes degraded via the fallback, floor holds inside the grace, fresh sync proof suppresses then silent proof confirms, heartbeat/removal/Stop disarm, re-apply keeps the floor.
- RED evidence: deleting the `armNeverSeenClockLocked()` call makes the promotion cells fail by timeout (peer never confirmed absent); restoring passes.
- Existing never-seen family (#4386/#11566/#10697/#11682) green unchanged.
- Full `pkg/cluster` suite passes; `-race` over the never-seen family passes; `go vet` clean.

Risk:
A lone node in a two-node config whose peer is merely slow beyond the 30s floor now confirms absence exactly as it already did when a receiver existed — no new election semantics. The residual trigger (networkd not configuring a carrier-less control link) is bounded by this fix rather than removed; the lab cell (power off node0 of a direct-cabled pair, reboot node1, verify RGs leave secondary) remains an operator follow-up recorded in `docs/log/16751.md`.

Refs #16751

## PR #17552 — daemon: bind web-management on VRF-enslaved interfaces (#16709) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16709-webmgmt-vrf-bind`

Refs #16709

## Why
`web-management http|https interface fxp0.0` resolved fxp0's addresses and bound them with an unscoped `net.Listen`. fxp0 is always enslaved to `vrf-mgmt`, so its IPv4/global-IPv6 addresses live only in table 999's local table and the bind is refused `EADDRNOTAVAIL` on every apply; for HTTP the IPv4 leg binds first, so Start failed with nothing serving.

## What
- `pkg/api`: `Config.BindDevices` (listen address -> VRF master) + `Server.listenAddr`, the single bind entry for Start, reconcile, `Run`/`bindListeners`, and HTTPS cert recovery. Scoped legs bind via `net.ListenConfig` with `SO_BINDTODEVICE` (grpcapi fabric pattern); an injected `ListenFunc` always wins. Scope is part of leg identity (`SetBindDevices` snapshot; adoption requires live scope match).
- `pkg/daemon`: `webMgmtBindDevice` resolves scope from committed config (management-class -> `vrf-mgmt`; tenant virtual-router member -> `vrf-<name>`); `resolveAPIBinds` stamps it and drops it for clamp-rewritten loopback legs; the endpoint fingerprint carries it so a scope-only change rebinds. Default-VRF interfaces keep the unbound bind.

## Validation
- `go vet` + `gofmt` clean on touched files; targeted `-race` suites green (pkg/api + pkg/daemon 16709 cells, listener/management regressions).
- Real-kernel netns acceptance `TestWebMgmtVRFBind16709Netns`: fxp0 enslaved to vrf-mgmt (table 999), production `desired()`->`startTo` binds `192.0.2.5:443` and `[2001:db8::5]:443` and serves `/health` to a client inside the VRF on both families; ge-0/0/0 control serves unscoped.
- RED evidence: neutering `listenAddr`'s scoped branch reproduces the exact production `EADDRNOTAVAIL` on both families; restored to green.
- Full `pkg/api` failures (NAT-pool/metrics) and `TestMgmtRouteRetryWiring11450` reproduce identically on base `e3dba79c90` (base-attributed).

## Risk
A scope named before its VRF device exists fails visibly and retries via the existing 30s mgmt re-assert owner. No cluster/lab smoke run by this lane.

## PR #17554 — cluster: keep preempt incumbent while rejoiner is sync-held (#16741) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16741-preempt-hold`

Refs #16741

## Why

Under `preempt`, a rejoining higher-priority node that had armed (weight back to 255) but was still in the #7162/#14406 startup sync hold made the incumbent demote (`Preempt: lower priority`), leaving the RG owned by neither node until the hold released (up to 30 s). The hold gated only the rejoiner; nothing on the wire said it could not take over.

## What

- Daemon installs a startup-hold election debt (`cluster.SetStartupSyncHold`, reserved monitor `__session-sync-startup-hold__` at the same floor-1 cost as the dataplane-arm debt) for the life of the hold, so the rejoiner advertises weight 1. RETH mode arms it with `vrrp.SetSyncHold` at bringup and clears it via a new `vrrp.SetOnSyncHoldRelease` hook (bulk-sync and 30 s timer edges); no-RETH mode arms/clears it in `arm/releaseNoRethSyncHold`.
- The receiver records that shape as `PeerGroupState.takeoverReady=false`; a preempt incumbent that already owns the RG skips its lower-priority/tie-loss yield arms until the real weight returns and ordinary preempt hands the RG over.
- Cost never reaches weight 0 (a lone held node keeps VIP ownership); no wire-format change. The `peerYieldedOwnership` promotion side (#9452) and non-preempt election are unchanged.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run '16741|16739|12164|9452'` PASS — 6 new cells (held-armed owners==1 across 10 rounds then takeover after release; wire weight 1 held / 255 released; takeover-hold row; non-preempt row; weight-0 fail-open control; committed-owner guard) plus all #12164/#9452/#16739 cells.
- Full `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1` PASS (228 s, pre-rebase base; targeted suites re-run green after the #16739 rebase).
- `go vet` clean on touched packages. `pkg/vrrp` `TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate/RethVIPsForRG` fails at base too (reproduced with this change stashed) — base-attributed, unrelated.

## Risk

Lab step not run (stays on #16741): loss cluster with `preempt` on RG1, reboot fw0 under iperf3, assert no both-secondary interval. A held node now advertises weight 1 instead of 255 for up to 30 s — the same shape it already advertised before XDP arm completed.

## PR #17555 — flowexport: export orphan closes via close-time sampling (#16742) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16742-flowexport-close`

Refs #16742

## Why
After #16303 a SESSION_CLOSE exported only if the same exporter object recorded the SESSION_OPEN. Flows spanning an RG failover (promoted node gets no CREATE, #15126) or an exporter-replacing commit silently lost their close record while the sampler advertised 1-in-N (R3-A46-01).

## What
1. **Close-time fallback**: when no group of an instance holds open state (`HasFlowState`), daemon close callbacks make one shared close-time 1-in-N decision per instance (`SampledForClose` via `sync.OnceValue`, `CloseFlowOrSample` per group). Recorded opens consume no second slot.
2. **State carry**: replacing reconcile transfers tracker entries (with interim baselines) and sampled marks to the same-group-key replacement (`TransferFlowStateTo`/`AbsorbSampledInto`, `FlowTracker.Clone/Adopt`, `carryFlowStateV9/IPFIXLocked`) before publishing.
3. **Promote-as-open**: HA session-sync walker registers peer-synced opens via `trackFlowOpenFromSync` — an open for flow export without a syslog CREATE (Rust producer unchanged; #15126 pin intact, no duplicate audit record).

Updates the #15230 nameless-close cell to the new fallback semantics (named-unsampled denial unchanged, still fail-closed before the counter).

## Validation
- `pkg/flowexport` full package: 201 PASS (new fallback/transfer tests + #16303 remainder/live-feed pins).
- `pkg/daemon` flow suite (`TestFlow|TestSessionClose|TestDualFormat|TestOutputOnly|TestClose|TestReconcileFlow|TestReconcileIPFIX|TestPromote|TestNonSessionClose|TestEventFrame`): 30 PASS, incl. acceptance (a) open→replacing reconcile→close exactly once, (b) no-open close at rate 1, rate-2 cadence control, promote registration, and (c) `TestDualFormatOpenConsumesOneSlotPerInstance16303`.
- `go vet ./pkg/flowexport/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean; gofmt clean.
- Two unrelated daemon failures (RxVlan #11446, VRRP #5083) confirmed FAIL on origin/master base — pre-existing, untouched.

## Risk
Close-time fallback consumes a sampling slot for orphan closes (by design; restores the pre-#16303 close decision). State carry keeps source state until retirement; the retired Run flush never re-emits tracker state, so no double export.

## PR #17558 — cluster: fall back for pre-ACK peers in config-stale gate (#16756) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16756-peer-config-ack-cap`

Refs #16756

Why: the #9569 config-stale gate requires a type-40 config-apply ACK
from every peer. Against a connected peer whose build predates
28556c2b19, the bare ISSU verb and untargeted/batch failover refuse
forever with "standby has not acknowledged applying config
generation G" — blaming a config-apply failure that never happened.
Recovery was an unplanned xpfd stop.

What: advertise ACK support as `capFlag2ConfigApplyAck` in a second
capability byte appended after the identity tail of
`syncMsgPeerCapabilities` (first flags byte is full, bits 0..7; the
byte cannot sit at a fixed offset because a #9818 peer's [5:21] is
its boot id, so the receiver reads `len-1` only when the frame is
longer than every pre-#16756 layout). `recordLastSentConfigGen`
records the receiving incarnation's capability alongside the sent
generation, and `handleConfigApplyNack` records the newest NACKed
generation. `PeerConfigStale` then judges a legacy send by the
pre-28556c2b19 semantics — stale iff the newest sent generation was
NACKed — and names that reason ("peer predates config-apply ACK"),
while a peer that promised an ACK keeps the strict gate (silence or
NACK refused until the matching ACK). A downgrade-on-reconnect is
re-judged under the current incarnation, whose promised ACK can
never arrive. The bit is incarnation-scoped exactly like the first
byte: per-connection store, priming-connection restore on the
boot-ID switch, cleared on incarnation advance and full disconnect.

Validation: new `peer_config_stale_capability_16756_test.go` —
legacy peer without NACK passes `PeerConfigStale` and the
`ManualFailover`/`ForceSecondary` verbs; legacy peer NACKing the
newest send is refused (batch form, `ErrPeerConfigStale`) with the
pre-ACK reason; straggler NACK ignored; ACK-capable peer silent or
NACKing still refused until the matching ACK; downgrade-on-reconnect
unblocks; local advertisement bit set; wire round-trip (a
pre-#16756 frame with a nonzero last identity byte does not read as
capable). Full `pkg/cluster` suite ok (217s, after updating the
four #9818 payload-length expectations for the extra byte and the
#11070 fixture to model an ACK-capable incarnation); `pkg/daemon`
PeerConfigStale tests ok; `go vet` clean; gofmt clean.

Risk: a legacy peer that silently failed to apply without NACKing
now passes the gate. That is exactly the pre-28556c2b19 semantics
the acceptance prescribes, bounded to peers that cannot ACK; an
ACK-capable peer is judged as strictly as before.

## PR #17560 — upgrade: preserve predecessor DB snapshot across failed re-stage (#16765) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16765-predecessor-dbsnap`

Refs #16765

## Why
#14720's predecessor backup ran after PREFLIGHT, but PREFLIGHT (and the #6556 resume re-snapshot) rewrite `.<target>.dbsnap` from the live DB first. Re-staging the committed predecessor then backed up the wrong-era DB, and `restoreCommittedPredecessorBackup` restored only when the snapshot was absent — so a failed re-stage permanently replaced the predecessor's rollback DB snapshot with the live newer-era DB. A later two-step rollback would restore the wrong config into the older binary (or be refused by the envelope gate).

## What
- Take the predecessor backup **before** PREFLIGHT in `Run`, marked stash-immune until COPY lands.
- `snapshotConfigDB` (now variadic over the backup, like `copyStaged`) stashes the backup copy in place of the just-written snapshot while stash-immune, so the journal keeps naming `.<target>.dbsnap` while its content stays the pre-cut bytes. COPY clears stash-immunity so a START/flip auto-rollback still consumes this cut's cut-boundary snapshot.
- `restoreCommittedPredecessorBackup` restores the DB snapshot **unconditionally** on every failure arm (verify-fail, pre-STOP refusal, kernel-arm refusal, envelope refusal); a COPY-demoted stamp stays demoted (#12177) but the snapshot is still restored. Backup temp trees are discarded on all non-restore exits (no `.predbak-*` leaks).
- The #14720 tests now assert snapshot/stamp **byte content** instead of existence; new tests cover pre-STOP refusal, #6556 resume re-snapshot, START/auto-rollback, and the successful-cut arm.

## Validation
- Targeted: `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -run 'TestVerifyFailure_PreservesCommittedPredecessor14720|TestVerifyFailure_SameGenerationReusePreservesPredecessor14720|TestStartFailure_Predecessor|TestPreStopEnvelopeRefusal_PreservesPredecessorSnapshot16765|TestResumeResnapshot_PreservesPredecessorSnapshot16765|TestSuccessfulCutToPredecessor' -count=1` — PASS (8 tests incl. subtests).
- RED on base production code: the same content assertions fail with `.1.0.0.dbsnap` holding the `LIVE-2.0.0-ERA-DB` marker.
- Full `pkg/upgrade` suite: PASS. `go vet` clean.

## Risk
Confined to the committed-predecessor re-stage path in `pkg/upgrade`; ordinary cuts pass a nil backup and are unchanged. The stash adds one snapshot copy on predecessor re-stages only.

## PR #17563 — daemon: skip applySem for settled IPsec fence ticks (#16777) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16777-fence-settled-early-return`

Refs #16777

## Why
With a SAFE census, a CLOSING permit and an ACKed overlay authority — the steady state of every box without a route-based VPN — `reconcileIpsecHostInputFence` acquired `applySem` on every 5 ms supervisor tick only to reach `tryOpenIpsecPermitAfterFenceAck`, which no-ops with no committed divert. During a commit the tick parked in `Acquire` for the whole commit, stalling the supervisor's allocator tick and authority re-announce.

## What
- New `ipsecHostInputFenceSettledNoDivert` helper: CLOSING + SAFE + exact ACKed overlay authority + no `ipsecCaptureRemovalPending` + no committed divert under `ipsecCaptureMu` + no conntrack revocation owed — mirroring `tryOpenIpsecPermitAfterFenceAck`'s own guards.
- `reconcileIpsecHostInputFence` returns on it **before** `applySem.Acquire`. This covers both settled shapes: empty ACKed overlay (no xfrmi census) and non-empty ACKed overlay with the divert since removed.
- Non-SAFE, un-ACKed, removal-pending, revocation-owed and divert-active states still take the semaphore; install/readback and OPEN/retire paths unchanged. `docs/log/16777.md` + `debian/changelog` added.

## Validation
- New `TestReconcileIpsecHostInputFenceSettledSafeSkipsApplySem16777` (5 subtests): SAFE settled (non-empty + empty overlay) returns while `applySem` is externally held; divert-active control still blocks then opens; UNSAFE un-ACKed and SAFE un-ACKed controls still block.
- RED check: neutering the helper to `return false` fails exactly the 2 settled subtests (`blocked on held applySem for 150ms`); restored green.
- Existing suites: `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestReconcileIpsecHostInputFenceSettledSafeSkipsApplySem16777|TestHostInputFence|TestIpsecCapture|TestIpsecFence' -count=1` — 49 tests PASS, 0 FAIL. `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean, `gofmt` clean.

## Risk
The pre-semaphore check samples ACKed overlay / removal-pending / committed divert without `applySem`; a racing capture commit can flip them right after the sample. Benign both ways: a missed opening retries on the next 5 ms tick once the divert commits, and a stale settled verdict only skips work the post-semaphore pass would have no-oped on for the sampled permit record. No lab/cluster smoke in this lane (unit coverage only).

## PR #17564 — frr: render a term's route-filters Junos longest-match (#16762) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16762-routefilter-longest`

frr: render a term's route-filters Junos longest-match (#16762)

Refs #16762

## Why
A term's route-filters rendered as one first-match FRR prefix-list in authoring order (walkup/OR semantics), so `192.168.0.0/16 orlonger` + `192.168.100.0/24 exact` admitted 192.168.100.128/25 even though Junos' default longest-match selects the /24 exact filter, fails it for /25, and stops. xpf does not model `walkup`.

## What
- Factor the single per-entry permit derivation into `routeFilterDerivation16762.emit` (`renderRouteFilterEntry` delegates, byte-identical permits/skips).
- Add `renderRouteFilterListGroup`: per term and family, sort renderable permits by descending base-prefix length (stable) and interpose `deny P le <family-max>` after each distinct prefix P that another renderable filter's base CONTAINS, so a route under P whose match type failed first-matches the deny and stops. Entries re-sequence from seq 5 per group.
- Stops only on true containment: single, disjoint, and same-base lists render byte-identically (acceptance); the family root never gets a stop.
- Update seq-pinning tests to the re-sequenced layout; document the contract in `pkg/frr/README.md`; per-issue log in `docs/log/16762.md`.
- RIP per-group path (#16625) unchanged — it composes its own ordered permit/deny list across terms.

## Validation
- New `policy_routefilter_longest_16762_test.go`: acceptance fixture rendered via `generatePolicyOptions` and evaluated with an FRR first-match simulator — 192.168.100.128/25 denies, 192.168.100.0/24 and 192.168.5.0/24 permit; authoring-order independence; nested /8→/16→/24 stops; IPv6 (`le 128`); /0 root with no stop; same-base `prefix-length-range` windows (no stop, gap route NOMATCH); single/disjoint byte-identity.
- Self-contained mutation probe red on base production (falls through to the /16 permit), green with the fix.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: only the five failures already present on origin/master (verified on a detached base worktree). `go vet ./pkg/frr/` clean. Post-rebase targeted suite green.

## Risk
Nested (containing) route-filter terms intentionally change rendered bytes and prefix-list sequence numbers; disjoint and single-filter terms — the common cases — are byte-identical. Deny lines use the established `deny P le <max>` idiom. No config schema or compiler behaviour changes.

## PR #17567 — flowexport: enrich tracker records with direction and route masks (#16754) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16754-flowexport-tracker-fields`

Refs #16754

## Why
Tracker-emitted interim (active-timeout) and final (inactive-timeout) records were verbatim copies of the SESSION_OPEN template built in `Daemon.trackFlowOpen`, which never resolved SrcMask/DstMask or Direction. Only close records ran `buildFlowRecord` enrichment (#2866/#3744 masks, #3270 IE 61), so a long flow's interim/final records exported /0 masks and Direction 0, and `export-extension flow-dir` mislabelled egress-sampled flows on interims.

## What
- `exporterCore.collectDueExports` (the single shared drain for both v9 and IPFIX exporters) now enriches each drained record: Direction, when the template left it unset (0), is derived from the exporter's own sampling config via `FlowDirectionIface` over the open-time zone/interface snapshot; route masks are resolved via `resolveMasks` with the ingress VRF (InIf, OutIf fallback), counting unresolved halves into `routeMaskUnresolved` exactly as the close path.
- `FlowRecord`/`SessionCloseData` gain the never-encoded `InZone/OutZone/InIface/OutIface` attribution; the daemon snapshots it once at SESSION_OPEN (Direction stays per-exporter — template groups have distinct sampling configs).
- `exporterCore` gains `cfg *ExportConfig` wired by both constructors (same pointer the outer exporters already held); `TrackFlowOpenWithMeta` preserves a caller-set Direction; scalar `TrackFlowOpen` unchanged.
- Close path / `buildFlowRecord` untouched — close records byte-identical.

## Validation
- RED: pre-fix raw tracker drain for an egress-sampled flow returned Direction 0 / masks 0/0 (probe against `FlowTracker.CollectDueExports`, the exact pre-fix drain).
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -run 'TestTracker.*16754' -count=1` — 4 tests: both exporter families (egress interim Direction=1, masks 24/30, equal to close record), ingress control, preset-Direction control, ingress-VRF scope pin, inactive final.
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestTrackerInterimEgressDirectionAndMasks16754' -count=1` — production SESSION_OPEN → tracker → interim chain (egress Direction=1, masks 24/30, close remainder still exported, flow forgotten).
- Full `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -count=1`, adjacent daemon cells (live-feed #16303, dual-format open, per-group baselines, flow-dir close), `go build ./...` pass. pkg/refactoraudit has 4 failures byte-identical on unmodified origin/master (pre-existing, unrelated Rust-side census).

## Risk
Templates that already carry a Direction keep it (0 is the ingress value, so only an explicitly egress-derived 1 is distinguishable from unset — documented at the drain); zero-value exporters without cfg keep the templated Direction; nil MaskResolver keeps masks 0/0 as before.

## PR #17568 — configstore: hold rescueMu across rescue delete unlink (#16783) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16783-rescue-delete-unlink`

Refs #16783

## Why
`DeleteRescueConfig` claimed its generation and bumped `rescueAppliedGen` under `rescueMu`, then released `rescueMu` before its durable unlink. A save started after the delete claims a later generation, so it could take `rescueMu` in that window, write rescue.conf durably, report success, and only then be unlinked by the delete — leaving no rescue.conf for a later `rollback rescue`. The reverse ordering of the race #14722 fixed.

## What
- `DeleteRescueConfig` now holds `rescueMu` across the generation bump, the `rbRemove` unlink and the `rbSyncDir` dir fsync. A later save either completes before the delete's critical section (legitimately removed) or writes only after the delete finishes (legitimately recreates rescue.conf).
- #14722 no-deadlock property preserved: a save held at `rescueWriteBarrier` has not taken `rescueMu`, so the delete still supersedes it promptly.
- Docs updated (`SaveRescueConfig`/`DeleteRescueConfig`, `store.go` rescueMu contract); changelog `docs/log/16783.md`.
- NOT changed: generation claiming, supersede checks, #5197 durable unlink+dir-fsync discipline, any caller.

## Validation
- New `TestDeleteRescueConfigDoesNotUnlinkLaterSave_16783` pauses the delete inside the `rbRemove` seam (generation claimed/applied, unlink not landed) while a later save runs. RED with fix reverted: `rescue.conf missing after later save reported success: no such file or directory`. GREEN post-fix.
- Targeted set (5 passed): the new test + `TestDeleteRescueConfigDoesNotResurrectInFlightSave_14722`, `TestSaveRescueConfigNewestWins_14722`, `TestDeleteRescueConfigDirSynced`, `TestDeleteRescueConfigAbsentNoDirSync`. Three race tests pass under `-race`; full `-run Rescue` subset passes. `go vet ./pkg/configstore/` clean, gofmt clean.

## Risk
A delete now waits for a save already inside its `rescueMu` critical section to finish one durable write — operator-visible only as a marginally slower `rescue delete` racing a `rescue save`. No other behavior delta.
