## PR #17569 — cluster: chunk IPsec SA sets over the 4096-name bound (#16758) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16758-ipsec-sa-chunk`

Refs #16758

## Why
A primary with more than 4096 active child SAs emitted its whole set as one legacy `syncMsgIPsecSA` frame. `decodeIPsecSAPayload` refuses any frame over `maxIPsecSANames` (#9061), so the standby froze `peerIPsecSAs` at its last ≤4096 set (or empty) and `reinitiateIPsecSAs` would re-initiate that stale set on RG takeover — missing current tunnels and resurrecting dropped ones. The sender had no count check and no alarm; the only signal was a repeating Warn on the standby.

## What
- `QueueIPsecSA` keeps the legacy single frame for sets ≤4096 and splits larger sets across additive `syncMsgIPsecSAChunk = 49` frames (new `sync_ipsec_chunk_16758.go`, the #15160 DHCP precedent): header `{generation, index, total, totalNames}` plus ≤4096 newline-joined names per chunk, each chunk with its own increasing full-set seq.
- `handleIPsecSAChunk` assembles by `(incarnation, generation)` under `ipsecApplyMu` and commits atomically only when every chunk lands; unclosed/inconsistent generations never commit, and a committed legacy set discards pending assemblies.
- Sender latches `IPsecSAOversizeAlarmLatched`, counts `IPsecSAOverCapSets`, warns on the primary, and refuses (counted) a name over `maxIPsecSANameLen` or a total over 1<<20 before any frame is written.
- Receiver counts malformed legacy (#9061) and chunk refusals in the new `IPsecSAMalformedIgnored` stat. Both are rendered in cluster status (`FormatStatus` Warning + `IPsec SA malformed/over-cap` rows).
- Census/cap/liveness lists learn type 49. NOT changed: the #9061 decoder bound itself — truncation stays refused.

## Validation
- New `ipsec_sa_chunk_16758_test.go` (9 tests): 5000-name round-trip to the standby, at-bound legacy shape vs 4097 chunked, incomplete generation never commits, malformed counted + seq unconsumed, forged `totalNames`/over-per-chunk refusals, inconsistent assembly, sender over-long/over-cap refusals, header bounds, rendered alarm.
- RED evidence: forcing the sender legacy-only fails the 5000-name and 4097-name cells (1 frame emitted, want multiple/2 chunk frames).
- `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1` PASS (230s); `go build ./...` PASS; gofmt clean.

## Risk
Additive wire type: a pre-#16758 peer ignores type 49, so a mixed pair loses only over-bound pushes (never the connection) until both sides upgrade — same posture as #15160. Chunk seqs advance the shared IPsec high-water per frame, so a generation that never completes still advances it; the next complete push supersedes. No dataplane/hot-path code touched.

## PR #17574 — daemon: retire replaced flow exporters per exporter (#16752) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16752-campaign`

Refs #16752

## Why
#15230 builds each flow-export template group independently, but all
exporters of one build shared a single generation context. When a
later commit moved the healthy instance while a sibling still failed
to build, the old generation was mixed (retained + replaced) and kept
whole, so the replaced healthy exporter kept running, kept its
SourceID, and kept sending template refreshes and finals to the
collector the operator had removed.

- `v9Group`/`ipfixGroup` carry their own `cancel`/`wg`; each new
  exporter runs under its own child of the daemon context.

  `retireIPFIXGroups` retire, cancel, bounded-join (`joinWithBudget`),
  and close exactly the old exporters no longer published; retained
  exporters of the failed instance keep their handles.
- Generation types and the mixed-generation keep-whole arm removed;
  teardowns capture the live bundle before unpublishing and retire
  each live group once. The #9035 AST guard now binds the per-group
  teardowns.
- New cells: `daemon_flowexport_mixed_16752_test.go` (v9 datagram arm
  + IPFIX live-set mirror).

instead of at daemon shutdown; retained exporters of a failed

## PR #17575 — daemon: derive shell ownership only from shell marker (#16755) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16755-shell-ownership`

Refs #16755

## Why
`deprovisionLoginUser` inferred shell ownership from the account marker (`ownsShell || ownsAccount`), but `reconcileUserPassword` writes that marker for any pre-existing account whose password xpf sets. A pre-existing account whose shell already equals the class shell (e.g. `/bin/bash` for super-user) therefore got `usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin` on removal although xpf never set its shell — revoking the operator's out-of-band key login and regressing the #5841/#6797 never-touch-non-xpf-credentials invariant.

## What
- `pkg/daemon/login_password.go`: remove the `ownsAccount` inference; shell ownership derives only from the shell marker.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go`: write the shell marker in the useradd branch (where xpf chooses `-s`), alongside the account marker, fail-visible — so xpf-created accounts still reset on removal (#14695 acceptance preserved). Pre-existing accounts whose shell was actually changed already claim the shell marker; unchanged.
- Account-marker semantics / factory-reset enumeration deliberately unchanged (they legitimately include password-only accounts).

## Validation
- RED pre-fix (production reverted, tests kept): `TestDeprovisionPreexistingClassShellEqualKeepsShell` fails with `usermod [[usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin -- alice]]`; `TestApplySystemLoginCreatesRestrictedShell10833` fails with no shell marker.
- Post-fix (rebased head): `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestDeprovision|TestApplySystemLogin|TestLoginShell|TestReconcileAbsentLoginUsers' -count=1` → ok (5.1s); broader login/provenance set ok; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Full `./pkg/daemon/` suite times out at 600–720s on both base `44002b8b0a` and this branch — pre-existing, base-attributed, not a regression from this change.

## Risk
Accounts created by xpf before this fix carry only the account marker, so their xpf-granted shell is no longer reset on removal — the conservative direction (never take an operator shell); the account marker cannot distinguish them from the protected pre-existing shape. Recoverable manually as root.

## PR #17579 — daemon: re-apply standalone RA on same-lifetime PD renewal (#16773) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16773`

Refs #16773

## Why
Since #15057 the RA desired set carries the absolute expiry (Obtained+granted). A fixed-lifetime DHCPv6-PD renewal stores a fresh Obtained with identical lifetimes, so delegatedPrefixesChanged stays false, commitLease fires only the unchanged-lease hook, and standalone mode — whose only RA applier is the commit-path applyServicesReconcile — never re-applies RA. The live sender keeps the first lease's ValidExpiresAt, deprecates the LAN PIO at its preferred expiry and omits it after its valid expiry while the delegation is still held; downstream hosts lose SLAAC global IPv6 until an unrelated commit or restart.

## What
- onDHCPUnchangedLease now also nudges a depth-1 coalescing wake channel (raRenewWakeCh, non-blocking — the hook runs on the DHCP client goroutine; an inline apply parks on applySem and deadlocks, #16559).
- New standaloneRARenewLoop owner started unconditionally in Run runs reconcileStandaloneRAOnce under applySem, which runs the digest-gated reconcileStandaloneRAServices against lastStandaloneRAHash.
- lastStandaloneRAHash is a separate digest from the cluster lastRAReconcileHash, kept in sync by applyServicesReconcile on every successful standalone apply and cleared on bootstrap withdraw; cluster mode is a no-op in the new reconcile and remains owned solely by reconcileClusterRAServices.
- Test seams CommitLeaseWithPDsForTesting / ReplaceDelegatedPrefixesForTesting drive the real commitLease predicates; new daemon cells pin the renewed ValidExpiresAt/PreferredExpiresAt, the no-churn digest gate, the loop lifecycle, and the cluster no-op. READMEs and docs/log/16773.md updated.

## Validation
- go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestStandalonePD|TestStandaloneRenew|TestDesiredHash15057|TestBuildRAConfigs15057|TestClusterReconcileBypasses|TestDeadSender' -count=1 PASS (includes the #15057 cluster no-churn cells); post-rebase focused re-run of the new cells + TestDesiredHash15057 PASS.
- go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -run 'TestCommitLease|TestDelegatedPrefixesChanged|TestUnchanged' -count=1 PASS.
- Two pkg/daemon failures in a broader pattern run (TestStandaloneApplyReceivesTheResolvedConfig9349, TestHostInboundTeardownClearsEnforcedThenFailedReinstallFences_5790) reproduce identically on pristine origin/master — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
One extra digest-gated buildRAConfigs per content-identical renewal in standalone mode; no sender restart when nothing moved. A failed renew-reconcile apply logs Warn and retries on the next renewal. The renew pass holds applySem like the dead-sender reassert (#4001), so it serializes with commits and no-ops if a commit already synced the digest.

## PR #17581 — snmp: emit ifAdminStatus in link traps in OBJECTS order (#16778) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16778-link-trap-ifadmin`

Refs #16778

## Why
linkUp/linkDown traps (v2c and v1) omitted ifAdminStatus; ifDescr occupied its varbind slot, contrary to the RFC 2863 `OBJECTS { ifIndex, ifAdminStatus, ifOperStatus }` clause. Receivers could not tell an operator `disable` from a fault-down (alarm rules keyed on ifAdminStatus never fired), and position-based parsers misread varbind 4.

- Thread event-time `adminUp` end-to-end: `linkAdminUp` (`attrs.Flags&net.FlagUp`, mirroring `buildSNMPIfData`) in `applyLinkState` → `emitLinkStateTrap`/`linkStateEmit` seam → `NotifyLinkUp/Down(ifindex, ifname, adminUp)` → `sendLinkTraps` → all builders + deferred v1 `trapJob.adminUp` → worker `buildLinkTrapV1WithUptime`, so backlog-delivered v1 traps keep event-time admin state.

## Why

`liveFlowCounters` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go`) built `dataplane.SessionKey{,V6}` with host-order ports from `flowexport.FlowKey` (`parseSrcPort`), but the session maps carry `__be16` ports — the Rust helper writes `src_port.to_be()` (`bpf_session_key_v4/v6`). A BPF hash lookup compares raw key bytes, so every live lookup missed: `feedFlowLiveCounters` never called `Touch`, flows kept their open-time `lastActivity`, and with the default 60s/15s timeouts every flow longer than 15s was exported as one 0-packet/0-byte inactive record with its real close suppressed — defeating the #15946 contract this feed exists to satisfy. The v6 arm additionally parsed the bare `FlowKey` addresses via `parseHost`, whose last-colon strip truncates a bare IPv6 address at its final hextet (returns nil), so v6 could never hit even with correct ports.

## What

- Convert both ports with `userspaceHostToNetwork16` (v4 and v6) in `liveFlowCounters`; parse `FlowKey` IPs with `net.ParseIP` directly.
- Add a live-feed miss counter: `Daemon.flowLiveFeedMisses`, incremented per tracked key per group on a miss, surfaced via `Daemon.FlowLiveFeedMisses()` and the Prometheus counter `xpf_flow_export_live_feed_misses_total` (pkg/api Config/Server/collector-deps plumbing, descriptor registered in the #16202 table, emitted before the dataplane gate, family omitted when unwired).
- R3-A46-04 was directed to land in the same change; it already landed separately as #16750 (saturating deltas + monotonic Touch), so the now-hitting feed cannot emit wrapped deltas.
- Docs: `pkg/flowexport/README.md` note + `docs/log/16760.md`.

## Validation

- `TestLiveFlowCountersRustLayout16760`: real production `liveFlowCounters` (seam nil) against a byte-keyed fake store written through the production (network-order) encoder, v4+v6, plus absent-tuple controls. RED with the conversion reverted (`v4 Rust-layout lookup = 0/0/0/0 ok=false`), GREEN with it.
- `TestLiveFeedMissCounter16760`: one miss per group, hits uncounted, nil-daemon safe.
- `TestFlowLiveFeedDrivesActiveInactive16303` and the daemon flow test subset pass; `pkg/api` live-feed metric tests (value, `NewServer` hook retention, omitted-when-unwired) pass.
- Pre-existing `TestCollectorDescriptorTableAgreement16202` failure on base f134e728a0 (658 vs 660, unrelated `userspaceSessionGCExpired`/`bindingFlowCacheEvictionsArm`) is unchanged in kind: 659 vs 661 with the new descriptor registered. Not fixed here (out of scope).
- Lab acceptance (flow >60s shows non-zero active interims + close remainder) not run — no lab in this lane; the unit probe covers the Rust-layout lookup returning `ok=true`.

## Risk

Low. Lookup-key encoding only; forwarding/enforcement untouched. The miss counter is one atomic add per missed tracked key per 1s poll.

## PR #17587 — logging: bind filter-term syslog gate to snapshot generation (#16775) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16775`

Refs #16775

## Why
The filter-term syslog gate held the previous config's positional (filter,term) map from the dataplane snapshot publish until apply-tail step 14b, and FILTER_LOG events carried no generation. During that window a `then log` hit whose new index collided with an old `then syslog` term was forwarded off-box, and a `then syslog` hit at a new index was suppressed.

## What
- Rust: `emit_filter_log_event` stamps `meta.config_generation`; encoder writes GEN1 marker at [140:144] + generation at [144:152] for FILTER_LOG (additive, legacy 144-byte frames unstamped); decoder reads it back.
- Go logging: `filterLogConfigGeneration`, `SetFilterTermSyslogForGeneration`/`FilterTermSyslogGeneration`, `allowsAtGeneration` — stamped mismatch suppressed on both stream and system-syslog sinks; local buffer unchanged; unstamped frames keep current-map behaviour.
- Daemon: `applySyslogConfig` installs the projection generation-bound at the publish (retained across `SnapshotPublishDeferred`); deferred-publish completion installs the new generation.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/logging/ -count=1` PASS — new `filter_log_generation_16775_test.go`: window case (0,0) suppresses, same-generation control forwards unchanged, stale mismatch suppresses, unstamped legacy unchanged.
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestApplySyslogConfig|TestFilterTermSyslog` PASS.
- `cargo check --tests` PASS. Full cargo test binary build exceeded the 300s job cap on this host (compile check passed; Rust assertions added in codec round-trip + event_emit payload tests).

## Risk
Stamped mismatched-generation events are suppressed (transient missing `then syslog` records) rather than mis-routed off-box. Unstamped legacy/eBPF frames unaffected. Cached filter-log replays stamp the hit packet's live generation, so a stale cached term may be suppressed after a commit instead of resolved under the new map.

close-shared REDs handler cell; per-host fingerprint-ignored REDs

## PR #17597 — frr: stop emitting vty pipe sequences in community-lists (#16776) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16776-community-pipe`

Refs #16776

## Why
FRR's vty pipe hook treats `| ` in any frr.conf line as an output pipe; a non-`include` token after it prints `% Unknown action`, the line never executes, and frr-reload.py exits 0. xpf spelled literal conjunction boundaries `(^| )`/`( |$)` (every multi-member conjunction with a literal member) and emitted operator regex members such as `^((56) | (78)):(.*)$` verbatim, so those community-lists silently never installed and `from community X; then reject` terms over them failed open.

## What
- Literal factors anchored `(^|[ ])` / `([ ]|$)` (identical POSIX meaning).
- Shared belt `rewriteFRRPipeSequences`/`sanitizeFRRPipeValue` (`pkg/frr/render_validate.go`): drops grouping whitespace around alternation outside bracket expressions; preserves bracket/escaped bytes. Applied to public conjunction patterns and the per-member delete backing.
- Atom-space members (`a| b`) refused by `config.ValidCommunityMemberPipe16776` at strict commit; render belt omits the list and `communityListMissingAtRender`/`communityDeleteTarget` share the predicate so reject terms fail closed per #10822.
- Neighbor description carrying `| ` refused at strict commit (`validateBGPNeighborDescriptionPipeStrict16776`, lenient flag `lenientBGPNeighborDescriptionPipe16776`) and omitted at render with a warning — installs or is refused, never silently dropped.
- README + debian/changelog + `docs/log/16776.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/frr/ -run 'Community|TestMultiMember|TestExpanded|TestReject|...'` — 56 cells pass, 0 fail.
- New `TestCommunityPipeRender16776`: BOTH (`666:.*` + `65000:1`) matches `65000:1 666:5` conjunctively with no `| ` in any rendered line; operator grouped regex preserves 56/78 semantics; atom-space member renders deny-all; bracket pipes untouched.
- `pkg/config` Pipe16776 cells: grouping accepted, atom refused, strict reject + lenient warn for both gates.
- Daemon oracle `TestCommunityListPipeLiveBgpd16776` passes under sudo (root-only, skips unprivileged): private netns/pathspace, production render loaded via `vtysh -f`, installed state asserted via `show bgp community-list` on running bgpd 10.7.1 (BOTH + OP present, pipe-safe spellings). Manual control probe: old spelling `(^| )65000:1( |$)` yields `% Unknown action` and `OLD community-list not found`.
- `go vet ./pkg/frr/ ./pkg/config/` clean; touched files gofmt-clean.
- Pre-existing on exact base `107e8a4949` (reproduced in a pristine worktree at that SHA; fixed on newer master): `TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestGeneratePolicyOptions_SetClauseSanitizedAndPrefixListOmitted_10823`.

## Risk
Grouping acceptance is deliberately conservative — a `| ` the validator cannot prove grouping-only is refused with a documented `[ ]` remedy instead of risking a divergent pattern. Single-member literal renders unchanged.

That file governs the config-archive scp transfer (StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, #10298), so the rotated-out key could still impersonate the archive host — a regression of the #5112 contract that applied trust must not outlive desired trust.

NOT changed: the #14694 authorized_keys sibling (scoped out by the issue), the partial-validity render path, the empty-config removal.

Three wider pkg/config failures fail identically on origin/master (verified in a pristine base worktree) — pre-existing, unrelated. `go vet` and `gofmt` clean on touched files.

Risk: strict commit now rejects truncated Junos-style key shorthand that previously committed but never rendered; tolerant-path configs carrying an invalid entry lose the managed file on next apply — the deliberate #5112 revocation direction.

## PR #17600 — snmp: answer in-band polls alongside vrf-mgmt listener (#16781) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16781-snmp-inband`

Refs #16781

## Why
With any management interface configured, the SNMP agent's only UDP/161 listener was SO_BINDTODEVICE-pinned to vrf-mgmt, so in-band polls admitted by host-inbound-traffic system-services snmp on data zones were never received. Silent outage on a clean-committing config; regression shape of #11427 (which required only the management leg).

## What
- Agent.Bind opens two listeners when a VRF device is set: the SO_BINDTODEVICE vrf-mgmt socket first (missing device still fails the bind synchronously) plus an unbound main-table socket, sharing :161 via SO_REUSEPORT with kernel L3-domain demultiplexing under udp_l3mdev_accept=1.
- Both sockets arm IP_PKTINFO/IPV6_RECVPKTINFO (exactly one family per socket); Serve fans in over both and each reply is written on the receiving socket with pktinfo pinning egress ifindex + source to the request ingress (in-band reply from the polled trust address, management reply from fxp0 via vrf-mgmt).
- handleMu serializes packet handling across sockets (per-Agent v3 lastPacket auth state); traps keep the #11427 VRF-pinned dialer; no daemon reconcile change.
- Regression test: netns with fxp0 in vrf-mgmt + trust0 in main table, two manager namespaces, 3 polls each way asserting reply source = polled address; plus pktinfo parse/echo unit test.
- pkg/snmp/README.md contract + docs/log/16781.md.

## Validation
- RED pre-fix: management subtest PASS, in-band poll to 198.51.100.1 timed out.
- GREEN: unshare -Urn go test ./pkg/snmp/ -run TestSNMPInbandPollWithManagementVRF16781|TestSNMPManagementVRFReplyAndTrap11427 — both pass (#11427 reply + trap legs unchanged).
- go test ./pkg/snmp/ -count=1: only pre-existing TestV2cNamedClientListRestrictDenies9416 fails (verified identical on clean origin/master). Daemon SNMP/11427/11740/16626 tests pass; race tests pass; vet/gofmt clean.

## Risk
Zones not admitting snmp still drop packets in the dataplane before the socket; the in-band leg answers only where host-inbound config admits it, per docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md.

## PR #17610 — config: enforce pipe-only login denies through the pipe save (#16780) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16780`

Refs #16780

## Why
The #14686 pipe-boundary "saved" arm in `CompiledLoginRegexes.EvaluateForms` overturned a full-form tier denial whenever a pipe-less form affirmed the core allow, without checking that the vetoing deny ever matched the command core. `denyingCoreTier` is false exactly for pipe-text denies, so a deny matching only pipe/format text (`display set`, `| match`, an anchored `… \| display set` spelling) had no effect for any class allowed the bare command — contradicting docs/system-login.md ("the pipe is matched as typed, so a deny on `display set` still sees it … a deny that wins on any spelling vetoes the command").

## What
- `pkg/config/login_regex.go`: new `pipeOnlyDeny` predicate (deny hits the full piped form, never its pipe-less core, and the core itself is allowed). All three pipe-boundary saves refuse pipe-only denials; the post-veto pipe arm returns a pipe-only tier denial immediately; the inner public-vrf exception additionally requires a deny hit on the truncated core. A companion core-denied exception affirm keeps `^show log 100$ | match x` allowed (its full form is allowlist-denied on the $-anchored core, a path the veto loop never reached).
- New regression cells: `pkg/config/login_regex_16780_test.go` (10, pure `/ EvaluateFormsWithPipe`) and `pkg/cli/permissions_regex_16780_test.go` (10, through `evaluateCommandRegex` incl. split-suffix and subtree spellings).
- `docs/system-login.md` converse rule beside the #14686 paragraph; `docs/log/16780.md`; `debian/changelog`.

## Validation
- RED on aa051bfd25: 5 pipe-only cells ALLOWED in the config probe (CLI cells exercised through the same gate).
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run '16780|14686|7172'` PASS; `go test ./pkg/cli/ -run '16780|14686|9628|9022|9505|7172|14987|14715'` PASS; `go test ./pkg/cmdtree/ -run 'CanonicalForms|16472'` PASS; grpcapi/api login-regex suites PASS; gofmt/vet clean.
- Existing #14686/#9022/#9628 cells (`^show log 100$` through a pipe, public-vrf, anchored core denies) stay green.
- Pre-existing failures verified identical on clean master and untouched: full `pkg/config` suite failures (spot-checked TestCompileGolden4406, TestGatewaylessPSK15989) and `TestMultiPipeDispatch*14714`.

## Risk
Narrow to `EvaluateFormsWithPipe` (pipeBoundary only); non-pipe `EvaluateForms` callers (gRPC/REST/config-read) unaffected. Fail-closed only: previously-allowed pipe-only-denied commands now deny; no new allows except restoring the documented `^show log 100$` piped exception.

## PR #17623 — config: widen zone ids to u32 (#16557) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16557`

Refs #16557

## Why
Security-zone ids were a 16-bit FNV name-hash fold, so valid pairs such as vlan163+vlan364 (both 51948) and zone109+zone237 (both 9074) hard-failed strict commit, with ~12% birthday collision probability at only 128 zones.

## What
- `config.StableZoneID` widened to a 32-bit fold `[1, 4294967293]` (sentinels at `u32::MAX-1/MAX`), mirrored across the Rust dataplane (ZoneSnapshot.id, u64 zone-pair keys, reserved constants), Go compile/apply maps, snapshot/status/counter wires, and every display/HA consumer. Ids remain a pure function of the zone name.
- Strict collision gate and lenient quarantine retained for the now-rare residual u32 collision.
- Frozen u16 session/event/HA/BPF records carry the low 16 bits of the id; all consumers now key explicitly by that truncation (never a silent skip). Dense counter slot maps treat ids >65535 as overflow/uncounted. PolicyRenameAncestry zone ids widened to u32.
- Zone-quarantine test premises migrate to the residual u32 pair zzq17760/zzq8100; new TestZoneID16557* acceptance tests. Docs + changelog updated.

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` clean; `cargo check` and `cargo test --no-run` clean for userspace-dp.
- New TestZoneID16557* pass (former pairs commit, stability across unrelated add/remove, residual gate). Targeted Go zone/quarantine/rename suites pass; Rust zone/zone-pair/flood/zone-counter/cold-path subset 124 passed.
- Wider-suite failures reproduce identically on a fresh origin/master worktree (pre-existing, zone-unrelated).

## Risk
Ids above 65535 are policy-exact in the dataplane but lose exact attribution on u16 session/event/fabric records (low-16-bit aliasing, fail-closed, never merged in policy evaluation) and are uncounted by dense counter slots; widening those records is a separate flag-day.

## PR #17631 — config: reject private-RG clusters without a complete control link (#16746) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16746-complete-control-link`

Why: private-RG election is the default and suppresses RETH VRRP, but the heartbeat — the only peer detector in that mode — starts only when both `control-interface` and `peer-address` are set. A cluster with redundancy groups but an incomplete pair committed cleanly: with no control-interface both nodes elect primary for every RG (dual-primary, duplicate VIPs), and with control-interface but no peer-address peer absence is never confirmed, so non-preempt RGs stay secondary forever (no primary).

What: `validateChassisClusterStrict` now strict-rejects redundancy groups under `PrivateRGElection` lacking a complete control-interface + peer-address pair, each arm naming the missing leaf, the consequence, and the remedy (set the leaf, or set `no-private-rg-election` so RETH VRRP arbitrates — the fabric-transport migration). It runs after the RG0 config-sync gate so that gate keeps first-error precedence. Tolerant load/peer-sync paths keep the `lenientChassisRG` downgrade to a warning (#1960 no-brick). NOT changed: election semantics — #16751's Manager-owned never-seen clock bounds lenient-loaded arm (b) at runtime. Pre-existing cluster fixtures exercising unrelated gates now opt out with `no-private-rg-election`. Docs: `docs/feature-coverage.md`, `docs/log/16746.md`.

Validation: new `compiler_validate_strict_chassis_controllink_16746_test.go` — three incomplete arms strict-rejected, all three warn on the lenient path, complete pair / no-private-rg-election / RG-less / standalone controls commit. Full `go test ./pkg/config/ -count=1`: 80 failures, a set identical to base ca0a6bf631 (all base-attributed, zero new). Targeted cluster/parser suites pass; pkg/configstore CheckText DHCP cell migrated likewise, its two remaining failures also reproduce on base.

Risk: operators committing fabric-transport clusters without a control link must add both control leaves or set `no-private-rg-election` — that rejection is the fix; persisted configs from older binaries still boot via the tolerant warning. Residual: lenient-loaded incomplete configs keep the pre-fix election behaviour until #16751 lands.

## PR #17899 — userspace-dp: Scope input-filter purge (#16889) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16889-filter-rotation`

## Why
Input-filter rotation can tear down every session in the same address family, including sessions matched by unchanged sibling DSCP/L4 entries. Direct ingress on a configured VLAN child carries the child ifindex even though the logical-ingress resolver is parent-keyed. A session whose saved tagged identity was unknown must still use the conservative fallback; a child introduced only in the new snapshot cannot retroactively validate it.

## What
- Scope teardown to sessions whose resolved ingress filter identity appears in the DSCP/L4 change set.
- Resolve configured VLAN children in each forwarding snapshot separately. Require the old snapshot to prove the saved identity, and retain that old identity if the new snapshot no longer resolves it.
- Preserve the conservative family fallback for old unknown tagged ingress; cover both old-known child preservation and new-only child configuration with an old unknown synced session.
- Add rotation, VLAN remap, reverse-pair, and unknown-ingress regressions; update the filter-rotation documentation.

## Validation
- Base issue RED at `4cc55c5bee`: the original same-family regression expected one purge and observed two.
- The new-only child regression failed before its correction (zero purges, expected one). All 10 tests matching `16889` pass now.
- Full `afxdp::session_glue::tests` module: 285 passed, 3 baseline failures, 1 ignored.
- Latest full `xpf-userspace-dp` suite: 9592 passed, 86 failed, 10 ignored. Base run: 9582 passed, 87 failed, 10 ignored. Comparing the saved failure lists, the latest set is the prior 87-failure set minus `afxdp::icmp_ratelimit::tests::rotating_v6_iids_in_one_64_do_not_starve_victim_15248`: it failed in the prior run and passed in the latest. No new failure identifiers appeared; the issue regressions are not among current failures.

## Risk
Old unknown tagged VIDs and missing ingress identities retain conservative family-wide fallback. Known old child identities remain scoped if the child disappears from the new snapshot. No wire protocol changes.

## PR #17900 — cluster: tie standby HOLD to primary liveness (#16880) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-26)

Branch: `fix/16880-hold-liveness`

Fixes #16880

## Why
A busy primary flow could outlive the receiver import window because HOLD refresh cadence used compiled defaults and sweep publication could consume a new cadence registration before its row was visible. Deferred worker snapshots must not advance the sender profile before the receiver actually applies them. FIB-only publication could also feed a retained candidate timeout config back into that profile.

## What
- Tie capability-gated primary-liveness refresh cadence to the reconciled receiver profile: configured UDP/ICMP and TCP established/opening/closing/TIME_WAIT windows, including TIME_WAIT override and flags.
- Update profile only from full snapshots committed as the applied config authority; FIB-only capture commits no longer promote retained candidates. Seed from capture authority, and use the stable applied marker only for the synchronous legacy backend.
- Cache the latest applied profile and reconcile it during session-sync publication, covering an apply callback between constructor seeding and publication.
- Gate V4/V6 delta, sweep, and bulk primary-liveness markers on peer capability. Revalidate queued frames at write time and strip the optional tail if a reconnect replaces a capable peer with one lacking the marker, preserving legacy frame shape.
- Assign primary liveness its own second-byte capability bit (1<<2), separate from persistent NAT lease provenance (1<<1), and test neither/provenance-only/liveness-only/both advertisements plus queued-marker stripping to a provenance-only reconnect peer.
- Restore TCP handshake/close state from sender memos before enumeration and fenced recheck without drawing a generation.
- Preserve cadence registrations that race post-enumeration publication through one lagged scan; consume wake payload only with its channel token and initialize both single- and dual-fabric sweep wake channels.
- Add deadline, TCP, timer, profile-source, publication-handoff, FIB-only producer, marker-capability, reconnect-downgrade, publication-race, and constructor regressions; update liveness docs and the stale census comment.

## PR #17905 — daemon: cancel background DHCP waits at shutdown (#17018) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/17018-quiesce-join`

Closes #17018

## Why
A DHCP lease callback can park on an unbounded `applySem.Acquire(context.Background())` while a Background-bound holder owns the semaphore. `dhcp.Manager.Quiesce` joins that callback before the bounded apply drain and the #9035 fail-closed actions, so shutdown can hang through `TimeoutStopSec` before clearing `rg_active` and stopping Kea.

## What
Create a daemon-lifetime background admission context in `New` and cancel it with `fenceBackgroundApplies`. Full background applies and DHCP route, DNS, IPsec, and web-management semaphore waiters use that context and re-test the fence after acquiring; if shutdown wins the race they release the permit without running. Work already admitted remains Background-bound. `Quiesce` still joins callback work and preserves clients/leases; no `StopAll` behavior was introduced. Added short-debounce cross-package coverage and updated shutdown documentation.

## Validation
- RED before the fix: `TestParkedApplyConfigAbortsOnFence17018` failed after 3.07s because the waiter remained parked on the held semaphore.
- PASS: focused `go test -race ./pkg/dhcp ./pkg/daemon` cancellation and #6788 regressions.
- PASS: `go vet ./pkg/dhcp ./pkg/daemon`, `gofmt` on touched Go files, and `git diff --check`.
- Full `go test ./pkg/dhcp ./pkg/daemon -count=1`: `pkg/dhcp` passed; the sole daemon failure, `TestCommitAndApplyRespectsSemaphore` (nil-store `RollbackDiscardGen` panic), also reproduces at base `c2002c26b815eaafdbc171cdacea20df0371f901`; no new failure set.

## Risk
A callback that has already acquired `applySem` and entered non-cancellable work is still joined until it finishes; this change cancels parked admission waits, not already-running work. DHCP leases and clients remain intact across graceful restart.

## PR #17906 — daemon: bound shutdown tunable restore (#17014) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-26)

Branch: `fix/17014-shutdown-tunables`

Closes #17014

## Why

`restoreStep0TunablesOnShutdown` was a third shutdown-path `applySem` acquire and could block forever after the drain and scheduler stop gave up. Giving the four shutdown attempts fresh five-second waits (including Run's deferred scheduler cleanup) could also consume the full `TimeoutStopSec` multiple times.

## What

`Run` now lazily creates one `applyCloseoutDrainTimeout` context and shares it across startup-abort/normal `runShutdownSequence` and Run's deferred scheduler stop. The drain, scheduler stop, and tunable restore acquire through the same context-aware helper, spending only the remaining deadline and trying `TryAcquire` once it expires. Restore skips unsafe snapshot/map access and preserves the snapshot if the lock is still held. An atomic stopped latch makes the deferred scheduler stop return before acquiring after the ordered sequence has already stopped it.

Regression coverage exercises serialized concurrent shutdown critical sections, remaining-deadline behavior, the full shutdown sequence plus deferred scheduler stop with a wedged holder, no over-release, and an AST scan of relevant shutdown source files for direct `applySem.Acquire` calls outside the bounded helper. The existing live scheduler tick acquisitions are explicitly distinguished. README and scheduler test documentation now describe the shared deadline, and the rebased shutdown fence-cancellation behavior (#17018) is retained.

## Validation

- The original restore regression failed before the fix after 6.16s with the semaphore held.
- Focused shutdown tests passed after rebase under `-race -count=1`:
  `go test -race ./pkg/daemon -run 'Test(ShutdownApplySem.*|RestoreStep0Tunables.*|StopPolicySchedulerLoopDoesNotWaitAgainAfterShutdown_17014|RunShutdownChainAndDeferredSchedulerStopShareDeadline_17014|StopPolicySchedulerLoop.*8597|FenceIsSetBeforeTheApplyDrain6788)' -count=1`.
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon` passed; touched Go files were gofmt'd.
- The affected-package suite, skipping the known pre-existing `TestCommitAndApplyRespectsSemaphore` panic, has the same 99 unique failing test names on this branch and current master (`21cf04c4989eb6f7e316179b6859298c8b6dfd82`); failure-set comparison found no new failures.

## Risk

If the shared deadline expires while `applySem` is still held, tunable restoration is skipped and its snapshot retained, avoiding a race with apply-owned maps. Host tunables may therefore remain at their xpfd-applied values after process exit.

## PR #17969 — userspace-dp: preserve recorded persistent NAT lease ownership (#17683) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-26)

Branch: `fix/17683-campaign`

Closes #17683

## Why
Pressure shedding, queue-full deletes, shared materialization, and HA refresh could lose, duplicate, or misattribute inbound persistent-NAT lease references.

## What
- Carry allocator/incarnation lease handles through pressure-shed, shared-hit, HA-refresh, and expiry ownership.
- Reuse unchanged coordinator holds and migrate references only when a refresh selects a different allocator.
- Release a fenced WorkerLocalImport replica exact hold on expiry while preserving the serving entry reference and cache/NAT state.
- Keep queue-full ordinary NAT/NAT64 repair separate from persistent-hold release; the refusing worker drop sweep consumes its exact hold.
- Add cross-scope pressure, owner migration, shared replica, expiry, and queue-full/sweep regressions with controls.

## Validation
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-17683 cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 17683 -- --test-threads=1` — 10 passed after all temporary production reverts were restored.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp replica_expiry_does_not_evict_serving_cache_16223 -- --test-threads=1` — 1 passed.
- Cp-backed RED reverts: pressure propagation failed with `(Some(2), Some(0))` instead of `(Some(1), Some(1))`; removing shared-materialization acquisition left 1 reference instead of 3; omitting the coordinator previous-hold argument produced `Some(2)` instead of `Some(1)`; restoring the legacy queue-full release changed pre-sweep counts from `(Some(2), Some(1))` to `(Some(2), Some(0))`.
- Broad filters: `nat::` 779 passed, 1 failed, 1 ignored; `session::` 571 passed, 4 failed; `ha::` 217 passed, 2 failed. Every failure name also appears in the clean-base suite.
- Full bin comparison at previously committed HEAD `4fd6401978`: 9628 passed, 86 failed, 10 ignored; clean base `3ca0da24b3`: 9624 passed, the same 86 failure names, 10 ignored. The full suite was not rerun on the final worktree.

## Risk
Queue-full repair defers only the refusing worker persistent hold to its delete-drop sweep. Fenced expiry releases only the expired replica exact hold, leaving the serving reference and cache intact.

## Summary
- Keep next-table, unreachable-shadow, and rib-group rules in the shared prefix/kind priority algebra. Install each target lookup with its fail-closed shadow before adding slot-0 main-table exceptions.

## PR #18019 — userspace-dp: match WG ingress zone map value width (#17996) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-26)

Branch: `fix/17996-campaign`

Closes #17996

This fixes the live gate failure that prevented the userspace dataplane helper from starting. Go uses full-width StableZoneID values; the Rust shim now matches that contract: WG ingress values, WG admission zone IDs, and LAND-screen keys are u32. The admission key has explicit trailing bytes for the matching 28-byte repr(C) layout; its u8 map value already matched. The embedded XDP object was regenerated.

Recovery path for existing nodes: the three changed WG maps contain configuration-derived rows. Their old pin shapes are excluded from the read-only live ABI comparison and reconciled after the old daemon stops, before collection load; the rows are then rebuilt from the current snapshot. Reconciliation checks type, key/value sizes, capacity, and flags. State-bearing maps remain subject to the strict pre-flight ABI check and are never reset. This provides the recovery path for the next daemon rollout; merging alone does not change running processes.

The privilege-free layout regression serializes actual untagged and VLAN plan values and checks their sizes against the compiled Rust object. A real eBPF Map.Update regression also covers a full-width zone ID and both rows where BPF map creation is available.

Validation: make generate-userspace-xdp; go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run WG -count=1; targeted ABI inventory, old-pin pre-flight, and rebuilt-pin tests; go test ./pkg/memlockcensus -run TestMemlockCensusMatchesTheTree -count=1; go build ./.... See docs/log/17996.md.

## PR #18106 — factoryreset: bind zeroize erase set to image seal tuples (#17085) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17085-campaign`

## Why

`pkg/factoryreset/wipe_seal_10769.go` claimed its seams mirror `scripts/image/bake.py`'s `SYSPREP_ENABLE_OPS` / `SYSPREP_PURGE_PATHS` — which bake.py declares the SINGLE SOURCE for the image seal — but no test bound the Go wipe to the Python tuples. #10769 was the demonstrated cost (SSH host keys, machine-id, SNMPv3 EngineID survived a factory reset). STEP-0 on current `origin/master` (f681f07dd7) proved the mirror is **already divergent today**: `/var/lib/xpf/uefi-bootorder-front` (added by #16449 to `SYSPREP_PURGE_PATHS` so a golden image never ships a recorded BootOrder front) has **no zeroize counterpart anywhere in `pkg/`** — a factory reset hands the next tenant the prior tenant's recorded EFI BootOrder front for `xpf-uefi-slots` to trust.

## What

- `wipeSealMapping` (wipe_seal_10769.go): binds every member of both tuples (keys verbatim — virt-sysprep op names / absolute purge paths) to a production wipe leg or a survivor-with-reason. The single survivor is `/etc/xpf/.day0-config-applied`, held through the wipe as the zeroize-pending record and removed only by `completeZeroize` after every leg succeeds; narrowing prose (stem-gated `/etc` backups, xpf/DHCP-gated `/dev/shm`) lives as leg scope in the mapping.
- Aligned the divergence to the authoritative seal producer (bake.py): new `wipeUEFIStatePath` seam erased in the xpf-owned leg of `wipeImageSealResidue` (every host posture, beside the SNMP engine identity), redirected by `RedirectWipePathsForTesting`.
- `pkg/factoryreset/seal_parity_test.go`: parses both tuples from bake.py (fails closed on absent/empty parse), requires exactly one disposition per member and no stale rows, and drives a full redirected `PerformZeroizeWipe` asserting every leg member's planted prior-tenant path is gone (machine-id rotated, not merely present). Fixture-copy calibration: an unmapped member spliced into a doctored tuple copy is parsed and detected.

## Validation

Named hermetic cells only (class U):
- `go test ./pkg/factoryreset/ -run '^TestSealParityMappingCoversBakeTuples17085$'` — PASS
- `go test ./pkg/factoryreset/ -run '^TestSealParityLegsErasePlantedPaths17085$'` — PASS
- `go test ./pkg/factoryreset/ -run '^TestPerformZeroizeErasesSafeImageSealResidue10769$'` — PASS (neighbor)
- `go vet ./pkg/factoryreset/` — clean
- RED proofs: deleting the `uefi-bootorder-front` mapping row reds the mapping cell; removing `wipeUEFIStatePath` from `wipeImageSealResidue` reds the legs cell (planted path survives).

## Risk

Test-only binding plus one additive erase of the xpf-owned `uefi-bootorder-front` state file (regenerated by `xpf-uefi-slots` on every run; absence is the sealed-image state). No wipe leg narrowed, removed, or reordered. Future seal members without a mapping row now fail CI instead of silently reopening the #10769 cross-tenant residue class.

Closes #17085

## PR #18108 — cluster: move heartbeat-timeout suppression into pkg/cluster (#17056) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17056-campaign`

## Why

Peer-heartbeat-timeout suppression was split across the pkg/cluster boundary: the daemon held the policy and its 5s-cap stamp, the reset event (heartbeat admission) sat under `cluster.Manager.mu`, and three hooks joined them. The split caused #12165 (stamp never re-armed on recovery; a second gap inherited an expired cap and promoted the secondary) and forced an unlock/guard/relock recheck in `handlePeerTimeout`.

Closes #17056.

## What

- New `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_suppress.go`: `(*Manager).syncSuppressesPeerTimeoutLocked(now)`, `hbSuppressCapExceeded`, 2s recency / 5s cap constants, `hbSuppressStart` as a plain field under `m.mu`. Admission clears it in the same critical section; publishing a sync source resets it.
- `handlePeerTimeout` decides under `m.mu` — no unlock/relock around the suppression decision (transfer-commit → #2080 freshness → sync suppression → transfer-commit re-check, identical ordering/timing).
- Daemon replaces `SetPeerTimeoutGuard` / `SetPeerHeartbeatRecoveredFunc` / `SetPeerNeverSeenSyncFreshFunc` with one `d.cluster.SetPeerSyncSource(ss|nil)` at publish/stop (`wireClusterPeerFailoverHooks`, `stopClusterComms`, `unpublishSessionSyncIfCurrent`). Never-seen freshness reads the same source. Hook setters/fields, `InstalledHooks` keys, and the daemon atomic are removed; `SyncSourceInstalled()` binds the publish for #7280.
- Tests migrated to drive the Manager directly; #12165 repeat-gap + interleaving regressions preserved. CLAUDE.md / cluster README citations updated. `docs/log/17056.md` included.

## Validation

- STEP-0: defect live on origin/master `f681f07dd7`.
- RED-on-revert: deleting the admission clear fails `TestHandlePeerTimeout_SuppressedGuardClearsLateHeartbeatStamp12165`; restored passes.
- Named hermetic cells PASS: cluster suppression/cap/never-seen/freshness cells; daemon `TestHeartbeatRecoveryRearmsSuppressionCap12165`, idle-sync and hooks-bound cells.
- `go vet ./pkg/cluster/ ./pkg/daemon/` pass; gofmt clean.
- Acceptance: 0 pkg/daemon sites for `hbSuppressStart|shouldSuppressPeerHeartbeatTimeout|notePeerHeartbeatRecovered|SetPeerTimeoutGuard|SetPeerHeartbeatRecoveredFunc` (non-test); no unlock/relock in `handlePeerTimeout`.

## Risk / gate

Timing unchanged (2s, 5s, CLOCK_MONOTONIC). Cluster HA gate: NOT-EXAMINED (Incus-only; hermetic named cells per campaign isolation) — parent to run `make test-failover` gate before merge.

## PR #18115 — upgrade: unify mixed-base protocol gate into GateProtocolCompat (#17091) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17091-campaign`

## STEP-0 verdict

The doc overclaimed: `upgrade.GateMixedBaseSwap` existed but was wired into **no binary** (its only callers were `imageversions_test.go`; `grep 'GateMixedBaseSwap('` over non-test Go found only the definition and comments). The live gates were two other hand-kept copies: `targetWireVerdict` (LANE-1) and `_gate_mixed_base` (LANE-2 Python), pinned only by retyped vector tables. This PR fixes the **code** to match the documented intent (one named gate), rather than editing docs to bless the dead copy.

## What

- One Go rule: `GateProtocolCompat(target, peerHA, peerWire, UnknownWirePolicy) ProtocolCompatVerdict`, with `RefuseUnknownWire`/`PermitUnknownWire` encoding the single deliberate lane difference (LANE-1 permits a pre-#7990 unknown wire, #14991; LANE-2 refuses). `Err` carries the cannot-run case (nil/missing target), preserving "unprovable target = error, never a peer refusal".
- `targetWireVerdict` is now a thin adapter (`PermitUnknownWire`); `GateMixedBaseSwap`/`MixedBaseVerdict` deleted, no shim/alias. `grep -c 'peerHA < target.HAProtocolMinCompat' pkg/upgrade/rolling.go` == 0.
- Shared fixture `scripts/deploy/mixed_base_gate_fixture.json` (target / missing / peer HA+wire / policy / survive|refuse|error), consumed by `TestMixedBaseGateFixture17091` (Go, also asserts the LANE-1 adapter agrees on permit rows) and `MixedBaseFixture17091Tests` (Python), following `version_fixture_16190`. The negative-peer-wire row is `python_only` (Go uint16 cannot represent it; Go parse-side rejection stays pinned by `TestParseImageVersions_NegativeSessionSync_FailsClosed`).
- All citing comments/docs rewritten to name the real executor (Python `_gate_mixed_base` for LANE-2, `GateProtocolCompat` for LANE-1). Historical logs/reviews unchanged.

Residual (stated, not hidden): the Python executor keeps its own fail-closed body — it runs where no Go binary is present. The drift hazard is now bounded by the shared fixture: a one-sided rule edit reds that language's fixture test instead of drifting behind retyped tables.

## Validation (named hermetic cells only)

- `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -run 'TestMixedBaseGateFixture17091|TestGateProtocolCompat|TestParseImageVersions|TestRollingTargetCompat|TestRunRolling|TestMalformedPeer|TestParsePeerHA|TestDrain|TestAllowMixedHA|TestProtocolVersionsProbe' -count=1` — PASS
- `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run 'TestSessionSyncWireCompatible7990|7925' -count=1` — PASS
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.deploy.test_xpf_deploy_gate` — 34 tests PASS
- Mutations RED then restored GREEN: Go unknown-wire flip & exact-match drop red `TestMixedBaseGateFixture17091` on the named fixture rows; Python unknown-wire permit & exact-match drop red `MixedBaseFixture17091Tests`. (A Python mutant that merely deletes the `peer_sync == 0` early-return stays refusal-correct via the later exact-match leg, so the fixture's unknown-wire row cannot distinguish it; the realistic permit-mutant does red, both languages.)

Fixes #17091. Finding R4-Q46-03. Log: `docs/log/17091.md`.

## PR #18122 — daemon: answer interface-ref RG ownership from the config SSOT (#17086) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-27)

Branch: `fix/17086-campaign`

**Head SHAs:** parent `8cc2a15b51` + fold `fae42953d3` (Rev18122Opus NOT-READY blocker folded)

## Why
`pkg/daemon` had nine hand-rolled resolvers for "which RG owns interface ref X" using four unit-split rules and two member-parent rules, bypassing the #6781 `RethRGOwners` SSOT. One config got three answers for the same member ref, and `rpmProbeTestGating` still filtered on a `reth*` name prefix, so a structurally valid `bond0` RETH in RG2 gated its ip-monitoring test on RG1 — the node holding the live RG lost its failover sensor.

Rev18122Opus then found the parent migration regressed declared dotted owners: `TestBuildZoneRGMapDeclaredDotted9821` failed because `RethRGOwners` owned a name only via `RedundantParent` membership or `reth*` spelling, so declared dotted `p.0`/`q.0` (RedundancyGroup set, no members) resolved to RG 0.

## What
- `Config.InterfaceRefRG` / `RefRG` / `RefRGFromOwners` / `RefRGIndex` in `pkg/config/reth_rg_owner.go` (`SplitInterfaceUnitRef` split, cycle-guarded `RedundantParent` chain, `RethRGOwners` membership as the only ownership test; first positive owner wins, group-0 owners stay owned at 0, strays own nothing).
- Migrated RPM gating, proxy-ARP, IPsec VPN RG, DDNS `rgForInterfaces`, DHCP relay gate (daemon-cached `RefRGIndex`), DHCP lease scope, `buildZoneRGMap` + fold map (`configuredInterfaceRG` deleted), Surface A `RGOwner`, `userspaceRGConfigured`, RA stable link-local, SNMP RETH infos, and both RETH virtual-MAC loops.
- Rewrote the #6781 guard from a five-function enumeration to a package-wide grep forbidding raw `.RedundancyGroup` reads in `pkg/daemon` outside two documented non-ownership exemptions.
- **Fold (`fae42953d3`):** widened `RethRGOwners` via `declaresDeclaredDottedRG` — a declared dotted interface name (#9821, numeric `.<unit>` suffix) carrying a non-zero `RedundancyGroup` owns that group without members. Membership stays the only test: undotted strays (`p0`, `ge-0/0/5`) and dotted non-numeric names (`a.b`) still own nothing. The 9821 cell is **UNMODIFIED** — its expectation stands (declared-first: a declared dotted name outranks a parse). `TestInterfaceRefRG17086` rows extended to pin `p.0`/`q.0` owned and `a.b`/`p0` not.

## Validation (named hermetic cells only)
- `TestInterfaceRefRG17086` (pkg/config) PASS — incl. `p.0.1`/`p.0`/`q.0.1` owned, `a.b`/`a.b.1`/`p0`/`p0.0` unowned, plus reth/bond/member/chain/cycle/RG-0/index parity.
- `TestBuildZoneRGMapDeclaredDotted9821` PASS **unmodified** (blocker cell).
- `TestRGResolverParity17086`, `TestSurfaceARGScopeOwnerParity17086`, `TestRAStableLinkLocalParity17086`, `TestDaemonRGReadersUseTheSharedPredicate`, `TestAllRGReadersAgreeOnStructuralPair`, `TestBuildZoneRGMap` PASS.
- Adjacent cells unchanged: `TestMixedRGProbeGatesPerTest15074`, `TestProxyARPRedundancyGroupResolution8297`, `TestRelayInterfaceRG`, `TestUserspaceRGConfigured`, `TestBuildSurfaceAScopesAttributesRG` PASS.
- `grep -c 'HasPrefix(name, "reth")' pkg/daemon/daemon_rpm.go` = 0; `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean; gofmt clean.

## Risk
Behavior changes only where a hand-rolled resolver disagreed with the SSOT — structural non-`reth*` RETHs now resolve on RPM, DDNS, relay, zone, RA, SNMP and MAC paths, and stray groups on non-RETH interfaces no longer leak into zone RG sets, scope ownership, or MAC programming. Relay per-packet cost stays one map lookup. Fold risk: only dotted-declared names with a set group newly own; VRRP/VIP collectors now see them (they iterate units; with no member they fall back to the interface's own name), while GARP/MAC loops keyed on `RethToPhysical` skip them. Undotted stray half-application is unchanged.

## PR #18131 — policy: distinguish omitted port from literal port 0 (#17081) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-27)

Branch: `fix/17081-campaign`

## Summary

`policymatch.Query` encoded "port omitted" as `0`, colliding with literal L4 port 0. Against a `0-N` application term the simulator returned the inverse of the enforced verdict in both directions — the exact traffic class of #13920, whose simulator fix was reverted within 30 minutes because the encoding could not distinguish the two.

Closes #17081

## Fix

- `Query.SrcPort/DstPort` and `SelectorArgs.SrcPort/DstPort` are now `*uint16` (nil = omitted, `PortPtr(0)` = literal 0), mirroring `ICMPType/ICMPCode`. `ParsePort` returns `(*uint16, error)`; empty = `(nil, nil)`, explicit `"0"` = present 0.
- Matcher gate is now `!l4Present || port == nil || !portMatches(spec, *port)` for both destination (#3330) and source (#3415) gates — `grep -n 'Port <= 0' pkg/policymatch/*.go` finds nothing.
- Proto `MatchPoliciesRequest` ports become `optional int32` (regenerated, pinned protoc 3.21.12 / protoc-gen-go v1.36.11); gRPC (`grpcPortValue`), REST (absent key = omitted, present `dst_port=0` = literal), remote CLI, and the `test-policy:` text topic (now forwards `port=0`) all carry presence.
- Restores the deleted #13920 Go test as `port_zero_literal_17081_test.go` (both rule directions, omitted-still-fails-closed, source-port sibling, selector presence) and adds shared corpus case `port-zero-range-17081` asserted by both corpus halves.

## Test plan

- [x] STEP-0 probe on origin/master `f681f07dd7`: deny rule `udp 0-1023`, default permit — `dport=0: matched=false default-permit` (inverse) vs control `dport=53: matched deny d`
- [x] `go vet ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` clean; gofmt clean
- [x] Named hermetic cells (exact): `TestPortZeroLiteralMatchesRange17081`, `TestPortZeroOmittedStillFailsClosed17081`, `TestPortZeroSourceLiteral17081`, `TestSelectorArgsPortZeroIsPresent17081`, `TestParsePort`, `TestValidatePort`, `TestPortConstrainedAppOmittedQueryPortNoMatch`, `TestPolicyVerdictCorpusGoHalf9167` (incl. `port-zero-range-17081`), `TestMatchPoliciesRejectsInvalidPort`, `TestTestPolicySourcePort`, `TestNetworkPortByteOrder10592` — all PASS
- [ ] Rust corpus half `policy_verdict_corpus_differential_9167` — NOT-EXAMINED: repeated workstation `cargo test` invocations timed out in the initial full-workspace compile (>280s each, compile of `xpf-userspace-dp` bin target not completing within the cell budget); no Rust code changed and the Rust reader already passes literal `u16` ports. Please run the named cell on a warm target.

Details: `docs/log/17081.md`. STOP per campaign: parent dispatches/merges.

## PR #18136 — cluster: merge failover request/ack skeletons into one registry (#17102) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17102-campaign`

## Summary

Merges the four hand-copied failover request/ack skeletons (`SendFailover`, `SendFailoverBatch`, `SendFailoverCommit`, `SendFailoverCommitBatch`), four waiter maps, four completers, two result senders and four `handleDisconnect` drain loops into one registry, one round trip and one ack-frame sender, per `docs/log/17102.md`.

- `failoverWaiterRegistry` keyed by `{phase partition, batch-key RG set, single}` is the single non-test waiter-map declaration; `SessionSync.failoverWaiters` is the one field.
- `failoverRoundTrip` is the only `time.NewTimer(failoverAckTimeout)` — register → write → double-select drain → reqID/ch-matched delete, returning a `failoverTripResult` (`Ack`/`ReqID`/`Outcome`/`Err`/`UsedConn`) so wrappers keep exact legacy errors/logs/stats and public signatures. On send failure every wrapper disconnects `res.UsedConn` — the conn the round trip actually wrote to — not a re-resolved active conn.
- `sendFailoverAckFrame` picks single/batch encoding by msgType (`isBatchFailoverAck`, not RG count) and owns the #14160 two-conn disconnect protocol; it preserves master's #17093 `clampFailoverAckPayload` single-ack clamp (batch detail clamped inside `encodeFailoverBatchAckPayload`).
- `drainAllFailoverWaits` replaces the four drain loops, preserving per-shape cleared counts.
- New `sync_failover_registry_17102_test.go` pins exactly-one-timer / one-map structure, the unified single+batch reqID-on-error contract, the 1-RG batch-ack decode, and the used-conn disconnect under a mid-write active-conn swap across all four wrappers.

## Validation

Named hermetic tests only (`go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run '^Name$' -count=1`), re-run firsthand on the merged head, all pass: `TestFailoverRegistrySingleTimer17102`, `TestFailoverRoundTripReqIDOnErrorContract17102`, `TestFailoverRoundTripSendFailureDisconnectsUsedConn17102`, `TestSendFailoverAckFrameOneRGBatchAckDecodes17102`, `TestFailoverDetailClampedToCap17093`, `TestSendFailoverBatchResultDualFailureDisconnectsBoth14160`, `TestSendFailoverBatchResultDisconnectsBrokenAckConn14160`, `TestSendFailoverBatchResultHealthyAckKeepsConns14160`, `TestSendFailoverResultDisconnectsBrokenAckConn14160`, `TestSendFailoverWaitsForAck`, `TestSendFailoverBatchWaitsForAck`, `TestSendFailoverPropagatesPeerRejection`, `TestSendFailoverDisconnectReleasesWaiter`, `TestSendFailoverRejectsOutOfRangeRGID`, `TestSendFailoverIgnoresStaleAckForEarlierRequest`, `TestSendFailoverCommitWaitsForAck`, `TestSendFailoverCommitBatchWaitsForAck`, `TestSessionSyncLockOrderGraphPinned16159`, `TestDownstreamRejectedFramesDoNotRefreshLiveness16041`, `TestSendFailoverAbortWire15164`, `TestFailoverWireAckOutcome16592`. `go vet ./pkg/cluster/` clean; `gofmt` clean.

RED proof (fold): strengthened M1 cell on pre-fold head 549f631b69 with only the new test file fails to build (`assignment mismatch: ss.failoverRoundTrip returns 4 values` — no `UsedConn`); it passes on the merged head. ReqID contract corrected: pre-fix both single and batch arms already returned reqID 0 on send failure (verified on origin/master arms); the merge preserves that, it does not change it, and Manager callers discard it.

## Risk

Internal registry only; no wire-format change. Send failure returns reqID 0 for both single and batch (unchanged from pre-fix, both discarded by Manager callers). Fail-closed directions preserved: broken used conns are torn down, overlapping failovers refused, ack payloads clamped to their per-type caps (#17093).

Closes #17102

- Single `IdleLeaseImportCounts::record` outcome mapping; `DETERMINISTIC_NAT64_BIB_TIMEOUT_NS` now `pub(crate)` and used at coordinator + `nat64_ports.rs` NAT64 BIB sites (remaining 300s literal is a test fixture).

- `cargo check` passed; `wire_invariant_default_specimens` fixture regenerated (lease keys only).
- `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run '^(TestPersistentNatLeaseTypedPoolRoundTrip17099|TestPersistentNatLeaseGenerationBatchRoundTrip11486|TestPersistentNatLeaseOldPeerGetsLegacyRefresh16877)$'` passed; `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '^TestProtocol'` passed.

Protocol v77 exact-equality refuses mixed helper pairings by design (consistent with prior lease-wire bumps). Cluster peers without the capability receive legacy frames with typed fields stripped.

## PR #18151 — policy: unify the per-rule tier step across both policy walkers (#17100) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-27)

Branch: `fix/17100-campaign`

Closes #17100

## Why

The per-rule tier step (`try_match_rule`, the 1-based counter handle, the frag-deny override and count, or note the skip) was copy-pasted at 8 sites across `evaluate_policy_result_counted` and `evaluate_junos_host_policy_l3_aware_at_with_hit_count`. Every per-rule semantic change was an 8-site lockstep edit (#11285, #11009, #12226, #16021), and the #4569 fragment-deny fix landed in the transit walker only, leaving the host walker fail-open until #6465.

Fold (Rev18151Opus F1): `counter_handle` claimed to be the ONLY handle encoder, but `rule_binding_by_stable_id` (stable-ID/HA-import path) encoded independently with a fallible `index + 1` conversion.

## What

- `counter_handle(idx)` is now the single encoder of the 1-based hit-counter handle, paired with the decoder `PolicyState::hit_counter_by_idx`.
- A `TierWalk` struct carries the walk state (query fields, `scheduler_expired`, `packet_len`, `hit_count`, `skipped_frag_deny`); its `#[inline(always)] fn step(idx)` performs the one per-rule semantics: try the match, stamp the handle, apply the #4569 override and count (#12226 count-after-override), or note a skipped frag-deny.
- Both walkers express every tier as `for idx in <iter> { if let Some(r) = walk.step(idx) { return r } }` (host walker wraps in `Some(..)`). Tier index sources (exact pair, NoRoute deny-only, from-any/to-any two-pointer merge, both-any, global with scope pre-filter; host exact/from-any/host-scoped global), the global scope pre-filters, and each walker's post-walk default posture (transit default-policy fall-through vs host deliver-on-no-match lifeline) stay per-walker.
- `note_skipped_frag_deny` records its handle via `counter_handle`; the stale host-walker cross-reference (named the wrapper `evaluate_policy_result_l3_aware`) now names `evaluate_policy_result_counted`.
- Fold: `rule_binding_by_stable_id` routes through `counter_handle(index)` (its index comes from rule-table enumeration, so the old fallible conversion's failure arm was unreachable for a live rule — saturation would need ~4.29e9 live rules); the `counter_handle` doc names this path.

Acceptance on current master: `rg -c 'match try_match_rule\(' userspace-dp/src/policy.rs` 8 → 1; `rg -c '\(idx as u32\)\.saturating_add\(1\)'` 9 → 1.

## Validation

Named hermetic tests only (no broad suites):

- `cargo check -p xpf-userspace-dp` clean.
- 9 named tests pass: `every_tier_counts_once_and_skips_overridden_permit_12226` (#12226 six-tier, unchanged), `explicit_deny_after_skipped_deny_counts_once_12226`, `flowless_fragment_fails_closed_against_skipped_port_bearing_deny_4569`, `flowless_fragment_override_does_not_count_permit_rule_12226`, `junos_host_flowless_fragment_fails_closed_against_skipped_port_bearing_deny_6465`, `junos_host_flowless_fragment_fails_closed_on_deliver_fall_through_6465`, `junos_host_fragment_override_does_not_count_permit_rule_12226`, `flowless_fragment_evaluates_app_and_l3_once_per_deny_rule_11009`, `policy_verdict_corpus_differential_9167` (#9167 corpus).
- Mutant check: dropping the override inside `step` (count the matched permit directly) is killed by both the transit test (`flowless_fragment_fails_closed_against_skipped_port_bearing_deny_4569` + six-tier) and the junos-host test (`..._6465`) — all 3 failed under the mutant; file restored and acceptance counts re-verified (1/1).
- Fold cells (`-- --exact` full paths, each 1 passed): `policy::tests::synced_hit_counter_rebinds_by_stable_rule_identity11070`, `afxdp::ha::session_import::rejected_mirror_reservation_10790_tests::synced_import_rebinds_policy_counter_by_stable_rule_identity11070`, plus re-run `every_tier_counts_once_and_skips_overridden_permit_12226` and `policy_verdict_corpus_differential_9167`. RED proof: a mutant returning handle 0 from `rule_binding_by_stable_id` reds both stable-ID cells (left 0, right 2); restored and re-verified green.

## Risk

Behavior-preserving refactor of the core security-policy evaluation path; the #12226 six-tier hit-count tests and the #9167 verdict corpus pass unchanged, pinning verdict and counting parity across every tier of both walkers. `step` is `#[inline(always)]` over stack-resident state — no allocation or extra per-packet work versus the inlined copies. The walkers' different post-walk default postures remain per-walker by design, per the issue's acceptance. The fold changes no reachable handle value; its only theoretical delta (saturating vs failing at ~4.29e9 rules) is unreachable for a live rule.

## PR #18160 — session: add SessionDelta::from_shared for HA shared entries (#17122) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17122-campaign`

Closes #17122.

## Why
The `SyncedSessionEntry` -> `SessionDelta` mapping was hand-written as two 21-field literals in `ha/export.rs` (bulk Open) and `ha/tunnel_purge.rs` (purge Close). Both shipped HA bugs when a field changed: #14303 (`pptp_call_ids: 0` withheld PPTP sessions on failover-after-resync) and #14960 (`fabric_redirect_sync: true` + `session_id: 0` on every bulk-exported plain session). Every new `SessionDelta` field was a lockstep edit the compiler could not check for correctness.

## What
- `SessionDelta::from_shared(entry, kind)` in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/synced_entry.rs`: carries every field the shared entry owns (key, decision, metadata, source_nat_static, origin, session_id, tcp_close_class, tcp_handshake_state, pptp_call_ids, snapshotted packet counters), derives `fabric_redirect_sync` from the disposition in one place, defaults the no-local-snapshot fields once.
- Bulk export: `from_shared(entry, Open)` + the site-local #16217 handshake restamp.
- Purge: `SessionDelta { source_nat_static: None, fabric_redirect_sync: false, ..from_shared(entry, Close) }` — deliberate overrides stay visible. ## PR #18165 — screen: route extractor through shared IPv6 ext-chain walk (#17106) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-27)

Branch: `campaign/17106`

Closes #17106

## Why
`extract_screen_info` kept a private IPv6 extension-header walk (`for _ in 0..8` in `screen/extract.rs`) plus a second walk via `ipv6_ah_sighted`, beside the shared `walk_ipv6_ext_chain`. That residual copy produced screen-only defects #14129 and #14325 after the shared walker already carried the correct first-non-ATOMIC rule, and every fragment-semantics fix had to be made twice on the screen security path.

## What
- `afxdp/frame/inspect.rs`: `ExtChainWalk` gains `rh_source_route_seen` (any readable Routing header with type 0/1; the type byte at offset+2 must be readable, else the walk reports `Truncated` — matching the old screen `offset + 4` gate) and `second_non_atomic_seen` (latched in `record_fragment_sighting` on a second readable non-ATOMIC Fragment header; ATOMIC repeats never set it). The exempting comment at inspect.rs:65-69 is rewritten.
- `screen/extract.rs`: private walk, local `NEXTHDR_*` consts, and the release-compiled-out `debug_assert` are deleted; the entry `ipv6_ah_sighted` second walk is gone. The IPv6 arm calls `walk_ipv6_ext_chain(frame, l3_offset)` once and folds `first_non_atomic_fragment` -> `is_fragment`/`is_first_fragment`/`ip_frag_off`/`frag_data_off`, `L4(off, 6)` -> `tcp_offset`, `ah_present` -> AH, `rh_source_route_seen` -> source-route, plus the #9114 sentinel protocol recovery from the governing Fragment header.
- Error mapping preserved: `Truncated` -> `TruncatedIpv6ExtChain`, duplicate -> `MultipleIpv6FragmentHeaders` (after the outcome mapping, so a truncated second header still reports Truncated).
- **Explicit OverLimit decision:** the old private walk returned `Ok` with `tcp_offset = None` on an 8+ chain. `OverLimit` now maps to `Err(TruncatedIpv6ExtChain)` ("ip-malformed"), matching the forwarding fail-closed posture (`frame_l4_offset` -> None, `ipv6_ext_chain_over_limit` -> drop). The #6885 depth cell is changed only to pin this Err at n>=8; the #9901 parity R1 now covers `Truncated|OverLimit`, and the sharing pin is repinned to the shared-walk call. README keep-out wording updated (NAT64 translation-ineligibility remains the sole keep-out).

Acceptance greps: `for _ in 0..8` in `screen/extract.rs` == 0; `ipv6_ah_sighted` in `screen/extract.rs` == 0; single shared-walk call at the IPv6 arm.

## Validation
Hermetic, exact-name cargo cells (`-- --exact`), all PASS:
- `screen::tests::screen_ext_header_depth_agrees_with_the_forwarding_walker_6885` (depth cell, with the explicit OverLimit Err pin)
- `screen::tests_14129_chained_frag::*` (7 cells), `screen::tests_16007_tiny_frag::*` (4 cells)
- `screen::tests_9901_walker_parity::*` (4 cells — all-256-next-header x truncation sweeps)
- `afxdp::frame::tests_10661_atomic_chain::*` (11 cells) + 11 `extract_screen_info_ipv6_*`/routing cells
- Mutant proof: neutering the sticky-first-non-ATOMIC rule in `record_fragment_sighting` reds a screen test (`chained_real_first_then_atomic_syn_frag_drops_14129`) and the tracker cell; reverted green.

## Risk
Fail-closed only: over-limit (8+) chains on screened zones now drop as `ip-malformed` instead of passing unscreened with `tcp_seq = 0`; forwarding already dropped the same chains, and <=7-header legitimate traffic is byte-identical per the parity sweeps. No shim (userspace-xdp) change. Lands before #17109 per campaign ordering.

## PR #18167 — lldp: single-source effective timing with clamped hold time (#17130) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-27)

Branch: `fix/17130-campaign`

## Why

Finding R4-Q47-10 (#17130): LLDP effective timing was computed three times. The runtime gained the uint16 TTL clamp (#4596, `encodeTTL`), but the two verbatim `show lldp` renderers (pkg/cli, pkg/grpcapi) re-derived `interval*holdMult` unclamped, so a commit-legal `transmit-interval 32768` + `hold-multiplier 10` printed "Hold time: 327680s" while every advertised TTL is 65535. Defect confirmed live on origin/master (ed11628ee0).

## What

- `pkg/lldp`: export `EffectiveTiming(cfg *LLDPConfig) (interval time.Duration, holdMult, ttlSeconds int)` — runtime defaults (30s/4 via `config.SecondsToDuration`, preserving the #8642 overflow fallback), product clamped to [0, 65535] exactly as `encodeTTL` — and `RenderSummary(w io.Writer, cfg *LLDPConfig, neighbours int)` as the sole `show lldp` summary renderer. `Apply` derives `interval, _, ttl` from `EffectiveTiming` and passes the clamped ttl into `txLoop` (signature drops the redundant holdMult and its local unclamped product).
- `pkg/cli` / `pkg/grpcapi`: delete the duplicated rendering; map config onto `lldp.LLDPConfig` and delegate to `RenderSummary` (negative neighbour sentinel preserves the no-neighbour-source omission).
- Signature note: the issue names `cfg *config.LLDPConfig`; at this head the runtime config type is `lldp.LLDPConfig` (exported), distinct from the config-compiler type. The exported pair takes `*LLDPConfig`; both surfaces map their `config.LLDPConfig` fields onto it. Rationale recorded in docs/log/17130.md.
- Tests: `TestEffectiveTimingClampsHoldTime17130` (32768×10 → 65535, plus 16384×4, exact-max, in-range, defaults) and `TestRenderSummaryPrintsClampedHoldTime17130` (prints 65535s, never 327680).

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/lldp -run '^(TestEffectiveTimingClampsHoldTime17130|TestRenderSummaryPrintsClampedHoldTime17130|TestEncodeTTL|TestEncodeTTL_ClampsOverflow_4596)$' -count=1` — PASS (named hermetic tests only; broad suites not run per campaign).
- RED-on-revert mutant: removing the clamp makes both new tests fail printing "Hold time: 327680s".
- Acceptance: `grep -rn 'Hold time:' pkg --include='*.go' | grep -v _test.go` → exactly one hit, in pkg/lldp.
- `go vet ./pkg/lldp ./pkg/cli ./pkg/grpcapi` clean; `gofmt -l` clean.

## Risk

Display-only; wire TTL unchanged (already clamped by encodeTTL). txLoop signature change is internal, single caller. In-range output bytes unchanged on both surfaces. No shim/alias left behind.

Closes #17130

## PR #18169 — dataplane: widen SessionDeltaInfo zone IDs to u32 (#18148) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-27)

Branch: `fix/18148-zone-width`

Closes #18148

## Why
Rust emits `ingress_zone_id` as u32 (`userspace-dp/src/protocol/control.rs:1257`, `protocol/binding.rs:1504`, `SessionPolicyMatch` at `control.rs:1618`; widened by #16557), but the Go JSON fields were `uint16` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol_ha.go:83,113,350`). A real hash-derived zone — `config.StableZoneID("lan") = 262430026` — failed every JSON status poll, the #9651 supervisor killed the helper every ~32s on both loss nodes, and the fabric starved.

## What
- Widen all three JSON zone fields to `uint32`: `SessionPolicyMatch`, `SessionSyncRequest`, `SessionDeltaInfo` (ingress + egress).
- Propagate to consumers that must carry the full value: `runtime.SessionIdentity`, `PolicySessionRebind` (Rust already `u32` at `protocol/security.rs:615`). `remappedQueryZones`/`reauthorizePolicyCandidates` now resolve helper-JSON IDs exactly (`oldNameByID`) while the BPF twins keep their genuinely-u16 truncated resolution — no low-16-bit aliasing on the rename/rollback path.
- Binary event-stream audit: the Rust binary frame is **genuinely u16** (`event_stream/codec/session_sync.rs:272,276` writes `metadata.ingress_zone as u16`; close takes `u16` params), so it is left u16 and zero-extended, with the JSON/binary divergence documented at both decode sites and on `SessionDeltaInfo`. Widening the binary frame would be a flag-day layout change, out of scope.
- Frozen u16 ABIs (BPF `SessionValue{,V6}`, `EventRecord`, RT_FLOW) keep explicit, commented truncations; no silent narrowing remains. Census of `ingressZone()`/`zoneNameByID` and all zone-ID consumers is in `docs/log/18148.md`.
- Regression cells in `session_delta_zone_width_18148_test.go` unmarshal `ingress_zone_id: 262430026` through all three structs plus the supervisor's `ControlResponse` poll shape.

## Validation
- Named hermetic cells pass: `TestSessionDeltaInfoJSONZoneID18148`, `TestSessionSyncRequestJSONZoneID18148`, `TestSessionPolicyMatchJSONZoneID18148`, `TestControlResponseJSONZoneID18148`, `TestDecodeSessionEventZoneIDAbove255`, `TestDecodeSessionCloseEventZoneIDAbove255`, `TestRematchRenamedMatch*`, `TestReauthorize*`, `TestRemappedQueryZones*`. The new cells build-fail if any field reverts to uint16.
- `go vet` clean on `pkg/dataplane/userspace`, `pkg/dataplane/runtime`, `pkg/daemon`.
- Pre-existing `TestRenameAncestryOwnershipTransfersAtBindTime10511/fatal` failure reproduced on the clean base — unrelated to this change.

## Risk
JSON numbers are width-free: old helpers serde-default missing IDs to 0 and old daemons ignore the wider value, so rolling upgrade is safe. The binary frame is byte-untouched. Zones above 65535 still lose exact attribution on the frozen u16 BPF/RT_FLOW/binary records (documented #16557 fail-closed behaviour; separate flag-day), but they can no longer fail to decode — the loss blocker. Gate re-run follows separately.

# #17145 — pkg/vrrp open-codes the track-demoted effective priority and Master_Down_Interval (R4-Q36-02)

- **Timestamp**: 2026-10-27
- **Issue**: #17145 (R4-Q36-02)
- **Base**: `origin/master be463f60e7`

## Defect (STEP-0, verified at base)

Live on `be463f60e7`. In non-test `pkg/vrrp`, `grep -cF '> 254 {'` counted 12
sites (the issue's 11 at its older base plus `skewTimeLocked`, added since by
#16771) and `grep -F '(256-'` counted 8 code sites. The RFC 5798
effective-priority rule (0/255 pass through; minus `TrackPriorityCost` while
tracked-down; clamp [1,254]) was re-typed in `effectivePriorityLocked`,
`armMasterDownTimer`, `armMasterDownSafetyTimer`, `shouldPreemptObservedMaster`,
`preemptingLiveLowerMaster`, `heldMasterIsStale`, `armPreemptHold`,
`observedMasterStaleLocked`, `skewTimeLocked`, the `getPriority` pending-resign
branch and `prioritySnapshot`; `3*advert + (256-p)*advert/256` was re-typed at
the matching Master_Down_Interval sites. Two preempt copies spelled the owner
sentinel as the literal `255`. Only the `prioritySnapshot` copy was pinned
(`TestGetPriority_TrackMatrix`), so a drift in any other copy survived the
suite — the exact "one formula, many gates" shape banned by
docs/engineering-style.md first principle 3.

## Fix

- `pkg/vrrp/instance_timing.go`: pure `effectivePriority(prio, cost, trackDown,
  trackIface)`, `skewFor(advert, effPrio)`, `masterDownFor(advert, effPrio)`,
  and lock-held `(vi) masterDownLocked()`. `masterDownInterval` and
  `skewTimeLocked` now delegate to them; the lock discipline is unchanged
  (#6230 — no RLock is ever taken under the write lock; the #15927
  single-hold snapshot → Reset → note invariant in the arm functions is
  preserved, with `Reset` now fed by `masterDownLocked()` inside the same hold).
- `pkg/vrrp/instance.go`: `effectivePriorityLocked`, `armMasterDownTimer` and
  `armMasterDownSafetyTimer` (still `max(3×masterDown, 500ms)`) delegate.
- `pkg/vrrp/instance_preempt.go`: `shouldPreemptObservedMaster`,
  `preemptingLiveLowerMaster` and `heldMasterIsStale` compute from their
  RLock-snapshot locals via the pure functions (owner sentinel now
  `addressOwnerPriority`); `armPreemptHold`'s watchdog arm uses
  `masterDownLocked()`.
- `pkg/vrrp/instance_rx.go`: `observedMasterStaleLocked` compares against
  `masterDownLocked()`.
- `pkg/vrrp/track.go`: the `getPriority` pending-resign branch and
  `prioritySnapshot` delegate to `effectivePriority`; `prioritySnapshot`'s
  `trackDown` return keeps its exact prior meaning (active demotion branch:
  non-0/255 priority, link down, track interface set), so status/event
  consumers are unchanged. `clampConfigPriority` is untouched — it is a
  distinct config-domain clamp, the one other legitimate `> 254` site.
- New `pkg/vrrp/priority_formula_17145_test.go`: `TestEffectivePriority_17145_Matrix`,
  `TestMasterDownFor_17145_ExactValues`, `TestFormulaAgreement_17145` (every
  former copy site — advert path, pending-resign branch, snapshot, locked
