## PR #18191 — conntrack: retire dead GC sweep and its constant metrics (#17155) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17155-campaign`

Closes #17155 (R4-Q36-04).

## Why
`pkg/conntrack`'s GC sweep cannot run on the only remaining dataplane: every non-userspace runtime returns a retirement sentinel, and the userspace runtime implements `DrainSessionDeltas`, so the daemon always set `gc.SkipSweep=true` and `sweep()` returned at its first statement. The daemon still constructed/ticked the GC every 10s, fed it commit config into a no-op sink, and `pkg/api` exported eight `xpf_conntrack_gc_*`/`xpf_gc_*` families that are constant 0 by construction.

## What
1. `MaxSessions` (unchanged `10_000_000`) moved to `pkg/dataplane`; users updated (`pkg/cluster` `genGuardMapCap`, `pkg/daemon` `genGuardCapacityForRuntime` fallback, #9915 tests).
2. Daemon no longer constructs/runs the GC (`d.gc`, `daemon_gc.go`, SkipSweep/IsLocalPrimary/OnDelete wiring, `gc.Run` goroutine gone) and the `SetAgingConfig`/`SetSessionLimitEnabled` commit sink is removed. The #3440 "aging is inert on userspace" commit advisory in `pkg/config` is kept. HA deletes already flow via session deltas/events.
3. The eight GC metric families are **deleted** (not re-sourced — no helper counters with equivalent semantics), along with the `gc` plumbing through `api.Config`/`grpcapi.Config`/`collectorDeps`.
4. `pkg/conntrack` deleted outright; its canary folded into the retirement canary (allowlist entry + constructor test removed, docs row marked RETIRED).

It diverged on short UDP/ICMP (admitted with payload == L4 instead of failing closed, #2376 semantics) and on the ICMP payload offset (L4 instead of L4+8), and carried a rustc-flagged unreachable `6 => None` arm left by the #13713 copy-only fix. Delete `packet_rel_l4_offset_and_protocol_for_ipsec` and rewire GRE/WG/wg-uncovered/frame-wg callers to `crate::afxdp::frame::*`. ## PR #18215 — cos: count TX ring-full submit stalls on non-exact submit path (#17159) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17159-campaign`

Closes #17159

## Why
`count_tx_ring_full_submit_stall` was called only at the four exact direct-service sites. The non-exact CoS submit handlers (`submit_local` / `submit_prepared`) hold the queue identity and receive a typed ring-full `TxRetryReason` on their Retry arms but never counted, so a ring-starved non-exact queue reported `tx_ring_full_submit_stalls == 0`. The comment in `cos/tx_completion.rs` justified the gap with two false statements: the handlers do not carry queue identity, and Retry failures are counted in `tx_submit_error_drops` (a Retry never touches that counter; only the Drop arm does).

## What
- `submit_local` / `submit_prepared`: on `Err(TxError::Retry(reason))` with reason `TxRingInsertFailed | PreparedTxRingInsertFailed`, call the single existing `count_tx_ring_full_submit_stall(binding, root_ifindex, queue_idx, items.len())` before restoring items. No new copy of the duplicated ring-commit epilogue; the queue-less `tx/transmit` primitives stay untouched and both CoS callers share the one helper (single source of truth — the cited divergence cannot recur without both pinned tests going RED).
- `tx_completion.rs`: rewrote the helper header comment to document all six callers and that a Retry never bumps `tx_submit_error_drops`.
- `types/cos.rs`: updated the `tx_ring_full_submit_stalls` field doc from exact-drain-only scope to both paths.
- `tests/submit.rs`: three hermetic guard tests forcing a real `inserted == 0` through `submit_local` / `submit_prepared` on a non-exact queue (64-slot test TX ring filled with never-reaped committed descriptors), asserting per-queue stalls increase by the staged count, `tx_submit_error_drops` stays unmoved, stalled items are restored to the queue head, plus a negative gate that `NoFreeTxFrame` does not count.
- `docs/log/17159.md`: change log.

## Validation
STEP-0 on `origin/master` 3abae28d24: grep found only the four exact call sites plus the helper — defect live. Named hermetic exact runs only (`cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- --exact <full test path>`):
- `submit_local_counts_tx_ring_full_submit_stall_on_ring_full` PASS
- `submit_prepared_counts_tx_ring_full_submit_stall_on_ring_full` PASS
- `submit_local_no_free_frame_retry_does_not_count_stall` PASS

Mutant: deleting the count call from both Retry arms makes both positive tests RED on the stall assert (0 vs 3 / 0 vs 2), negative gate stays green; restoring the fix makes all three PASS again (FAIL-ON-REVERT by assertion, documented in test header). No broad suites run.

## Risk
Low. Counter-only telemetry change on the expected-backpressure Retry arm; no packet-path, scheduling, or drop behavior changes. Added work per ring-full retry: one `matches!` on a Copy enum plus the existing inline helper. `tx_ring_full_submit_stalls` will now rise on ring-starved non-exact queues — the intended observability fix.

- Cross-language golden following the #17131/#9412 pattern: `pkg/nfqueue/testdata/reinject_submit_frame_18207.hex` (140-byte frame, zone id `0x00010017` = 65559, above the u16 range so truncation changes bytes). Go `TestReinjectSubmitGoRustPinnedLayout9506` byte-matches the golden from the real encoder; Rust `submit_wire_matches_pinned_go_vector_and_both_decoders` byte-matches it, checks the file (regenerated only under `XPF_WRITE_GOLDEN_18207=1`), and decodes it through both `decode_submit_batch` and `decode_submit_batch_into_pool`.
- Updated exact-bytes tests to the u32 layout (`TestEncodeSubmitBatchPMechTailTwoFrames9506`, `codec_submit_roundtrip_and_exact_bytes`); docs + changelog.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/nfqueue/ -run '^TestEncodeSubmitBatchPMechTailTwoFrames9506$' -count=1` — PASS
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- slowpath_reinject_9506::tests::submit_wire_matches_pinned_go_vector_and_both_decoders --exact` — PASS
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- slowpath_reinject_9506::tests::codec_submit_roundtrip_and_exact_bytes --exact` — PASS
- Mutant RED: Go u16 writer fails the Go golden cell (138 vs 140 bytes); Rust u16 readers fail decode with `TrailingBytes`. Both reverted.

## PR #18239 — config: share one family extractor across firewall, interfaces and forwarding-options (#17196) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17196-campaign`

# Issue #17196 — shared compound/split `family` extractor

- **Issue:** The compound/split `family` walk had one shared extractor in firewall (`firewallFamilyMembers9883`) and three hand copies elsewhere (interfaces, forwarding-options `family inet6 mode`, sampling instance families). The sampling copy indexed `afNode.Keys[0]` with no guard, so it panicked on an empty-Keys child (malformed persisted/synced AST); all three copies kept the `Keys[1]` preference #9883 removed from firewall, so a leading junk token (`family { bogus inet { … } }`) was silently ignored and the trailing family installed.
- **STEP-0 (defect live on origin/master `843c77ca26`):** `grep -rn 'afNodes = append' pkg/config` returned 6 lines at 3 sites (interfaces, services ×2). A hand-built empty-Keys sampling tree panicked with `index out of range [0] with length 0` on both strict and lenient compile; hierarchical text probes installed the trailing family with no error: `forwarding-options { family { bogus inet6 { mode packet-based; } } }` set `FamilyInet6Mode="packet-based"`, sampling `bogus inet` set `FamilyInet`, interfaces `bogus inet` set `FamilyInet` with its address, and `family { inet mtu 1500 { address … } }` installed nothing (name-keyed gate vs Keys[1] install disagreement).

## What

1. Moved `firewallFamilyMember`/`firewallFamilyMembers9883` from `compiler_firewall_family_9017.go` to the new `pkg/config/family_members.go` as `familyMember`/`familyMembers`, verbatim semantics (packed `Keys[1]`, split child `Name()`, structured-only `Residue`, nil-safe on empty Keys). Renamed all firewall callers (compileFirewall, #3884/#4296/#9017 gates, #16450 level gate, fused-then, valueless-from, nameless-term) — no alias shim.
2. Replaced the three hand copies with the shared extractor: `compiler_interfaces.go` (was `Name()` then `Keys[1]`), `compiler_services.go` forwarding-options family loop (was `Name()` then `Keys[1]`), and `compileSampling` (was unguarded `Keys[0]` then `Keys[1]`; signature now takes `opts compileOpts, warnings *[]string`, threaded from `compileForwardingOptionsWithOpts`).
3. Each caller decides how an unknown member is reported, per the fix direction: `unknownFamilyMember17196` (effective token or structured residue token outside the caller's declared set) + `unknownFamilyMsg17196` (#9017-style `… family "bogus" is not a known address family (known: …) — the configuration under it compiles to NOTHING …`). Strict rejects; lenient (`lenientFamilyMembers17196` in `compiler_opts.go`, registered in `lenientCompileOpts()`) warns and installs nothing for that member. Declared sets: interfaces = Junos AF tokens the interface gates recognise (`isInterfaceFamilyAF12090` set plus iso; known-but-unconsumed families still fall through to the #12090/#12656/#15654 gates), forwarding-options family = `{inet6}`, sampling = `{inet, inet6}`.
4. Interface install token is now the child name for a two-key child (D58-04 direction): `family { inet mtu 1500 { … } }` is residue-unknown and installs nothing, pinned by a fixture in the new test file; well-formed `inet { address …; mtu …; }` spellings are controls.
5. Updated neighbour tests whose fixtures encoded the old silent behaviour: `TestChildShapedFamilyStillCompiles7522` now rides the lenient path (strict rejects the malformed sibling, lenient warns and still compiles the well-formed sibling — addresses assertion unchanged); `TestOnlyTheInet6FamilySetsTheInet6Mode8797` now asserts strict rejects an undeclared forwarding-options family while the lenient seam pins the original invariant that a non-inet6 `mode` is never taken.

## Validation

- **Acceptance census:** `grep -rn 'afNodes = append' pkg/config --include='*.go'` (non-test) returns 0; pinned hermetically by `TestFamilyMembersSingleExtractorCensus17196`.
- **Named hermetic tests (new):** `go test ./pkg/config -run '^TestFamilyMembers(EmptyKeysNoPanic17196|BogusSmuggleRejected17196|InterfaceResidueFixture17196|SingleExtractorCensus17196)$' -count=1` — PASS (empty-Keys child under all three tops: strict error / lenient warning, never panic, nothing installed; bogus smuggle at all three tops: strict #9017-style rejection naming `bogus`, lenient warning + nothing installed; residue fixture + well-formed controls).
- **Named hermetic tests (neighbours, adjusted only as above):** `TestMalformedAddressFamilyNodeDoesNotPanic7522`, `TestWellFormedAddressFamiliesStillCompile7522`, `TestChildShapedFamilyStillCompiles7522`, `TestCompoundFamilyLookupIsNotTwoLevel8797`, `TestOnlyTheInet6FamilySetsTheInet6Mode8797`, `TestLenientCompileOptsCompleteness16166`, `TestLenientCompileOptsHaveReaders17143`, `TestStrictCompileOptsSingleSource17148` — PASS.
- `go vet ./pkg/config` — clean. No broad suites run per campaign isolation.

## Risk

Strict commits carrying an undeclared family token under `interfaces … unit family`, `forwarding-options family`, or a sampling instance `family` — or a structured residue member such as `family { inet mtu 1500 { … } }` — now reject where they previously committed silently (the intended fail-closed change; the same text on the tolerant load/peer-sync path warns and boots, #1960). Persisted trees with an empty-Keys family child now error/warn instead of panicking (sampling) or silently skipping (interfaces/forwarding). Known-but-unconsumed interface families (mpls, ethernet-switching, …) keep their prior fall-through behaviour and existing gates.

## PR #18247 — userspace: consolidate host-inbound admission into one decision (#17192) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17192-campaign`

**Why:** Four hand-copied host-inbound admit bodies in `forwarding/host_inbound.rs` had diverged: the zone arm admitted ND (ICMPv6 133-136) to a catalog multicast group on the bare ND default while the interface-override arm denied it — under a comment claiming they agreed. The documented "production" entry point `host_inbound_admits_iface` had zero production callers, so ~98 test cells pinned a function no packet reaches. Rev18247Opus review of the first head (8a5f31e49d) found the kernel-parity claim over-stated for unscoped ingress, the parity cell Rust-vs-Rust circular, and `ViewKind` semantically inert; this fold corrects all three.

**What:**
- Single decision body `host_inbound_decide(view, pkt)` (`HostInboundPkt` only; `ViewKind` deleted — its only use was a `debug_assert` in a `None` arm an override can never reach, and its doc claimed a divergence the body does not have): global-accept → ND → catalog multicast → set, written once; `is_ndp_type(` occurs once in non-test `host_inbound.rs`. Callers pass `Option<&ZoneHostInbound>` only; the `None` arm is explicitly fail-closed for a catalog destination and unchanged for the #3405/#5659/#6873 destination default on every other destination.
- `host_inbound_admits` / `host_inbound_admits_for_destination` delegate with the zone view; `host_inbound_admits_iface_for_destination` selects the override view when present, else the zone view. ND to a catalog group requires an explicit `ndp` positive (or `any-service`) on a present view; unicast/non-catalog ND keeps the #15671/#15931 default.
- Kernel posture, stated exactly (no blanket parity claim): on SCOPED ingress the kernel denies ND to the five v6 catalog groups (`ff02::5`, `ff02::6`, `ff02::9`, `ff02::d`, `ff02::12`) unless the view's token set opens that exact group, because the ingress-scoped catalog drop precedes the ND accepts in both renderers — that scoped verdict matches the Rust deny. On UNSCOPED ingress (destination-fallback or wholly scopeless views) the kernel emits its ND accept with NO catalog drop ahead of it, so the kernel ADMITS an `ssh`-only view's ND to `ff02::5` unscoped. Userspace has no ingress-scope bit and deliberately stays STRICTER there: fail-closed for a catalog destination on an unknown view, rather than reproducing a kernel fail-open that exists only because no drop was emitted.
- New Go kernel-posture cells pin kernel truth by first-match order: `TestKernelNDCatalogPosture17192` (pkg/daemon, nft TEXT) and `TestKernelNDCatalogPostureNetlink17192` (pkg/nftables, NETLINK chains) render {ssh-only, ndp-positive, ndp-except, any-service} x {ff02::5, ff02::1} scoped plus ssh-only destination-fallback and scopeless. The Rust parity cell `ndp_zone_override_catalog_parity_17192` cites them (zone==override Rust verdicts only) and adds unknown-view fail-closed, `any-service` and `protocols all` positive cells.
- `host_inbound_admits_iface` is now `#[cfg(test)]`-only, delegating with an explicit unicast destination — no non-`cfg(test)` definition remains.
- Docs naming the dead function as the production path now name `host_inbound_admits_iface_for_destination` (`forwarding/README.md`, `junos-cli-reference.md`, `afxdp/README.md`, `poll_stages.rs`, `forwarding_build/interfaces.rs`); `docs/log/17192.md` and the `host_inbound_decide` comment carry the corrected scoped/unscoped prose.

**Validation (named hermetic cells only):**
- Rust `-- --exact`: `ndp_zone_override_catalog_parity_17192` (updated), `ndp_interface_override_default_15931`, `ndp_token_and_except_15671`, `empty_configured_zone_default_denies`, `ospf_multicast_is_scoped_to_exact_group_family_and_token_11571`, `vrrp_multicast_is_dual_family_default_deny_and_override_scoped_11571`, `per_interface_override_keys_by_ifindex` — all PASS (7 passed via the built test binary; full-path exact names).
- Go: `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run '^TestKernelNDCatalogPosture17192$' -count=1` — PASS; `go test ./pkg/nftables/ -run '^TestKernelNDCatalogPostureNetlink17192$' -count=1` — PASS.
- Mutant RED (pre-fold): gating the catalog-ND arm on the old zone/override split made the parity cell FAIL; reverted. `ViewKind` is now deleted, so that mutant shape no longer exists.
- `cargo check --bin xpf-userspace-dp` — PASS. No broad suites run.

**Risk:** One deliberate fail-closed change: ND to a catalog group via a zone view now requires an explicit `ndp` token (already denied on scoped kernel ingress and on the override arm). For unscoped/unknown views userspace is deliberately stricter than the kernel's unscoped admit. Unicast/non-catalog ND unchanged.

Closes #17192

## PR #18254 — config: judge packed relay groups and accept digit-less members (#17205) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17205-campaign`

Closes #17205.

## Why
`validateDHCPRelayDHCPv6AST` re-walked the dhcpv6 relay tree by hand instead of using the compilers' shape readers, so it rejected configuration both compilers read correctly — the canonical Junos `server-group { SG6 { addr; } }` block (reporting the server address as an unsupported keyword) and flat-set/display-set `interface a b` lists (told apart from scalar-plus-option by `KeyBracketed` provenance, which `FormatSet` does not carry, breaking the display-set → load-set round-trip).

Fold (Rev18254Opus NOT READY on f0ce2ca510): B1 the digit requirement in `dhcpRelayInterfaceMemberValid` refused legal digit-less bare names (`uplink`, `vrf-mgmt` — #6834 census) the old gate accepted, breaking strict configs on upgrade. B2 (fail-open) the gate iterated only `inst.node.Children` while compilers also consume the instance `Keys[2:]` packed run, so container spelling `group { G6 unsupported-knob interface badname; }` strict-compiled clean with `Interfaces=[badname]`. B3 parity asserted only element `[0]`.

STEP-0 on `c4e12aafc3`: v6 canonical block strict-rejected naming `2001:db8:9::9`; v6 hierarchical bracket compiled but its display-set replay rejected naming `ge-0/0/2.0`; v6 flat-set bracket/extra-token interface lines rejected; all v4 shapes clean.

## What
- Extract `dhcpRelayGroupInterfaces` (Keys[1:] plus every child key, empty-filtered) as the single relay-group interface member reader; call it from `compileDHCPRelay` (v4) and `compileDHCPRelayV6Group9553` (v6). No new copy of the pattern.
- Rewrite the gate's `server-group`/`group` iteration over `namedInstances(...)` so it judges exactly the instances the compilers compile; nested-leaf refusals preserved per instance.
- Drop the digit requirement: a bare member is valid iff `ValidateInterfaceName` passes (unit form keeps base + `ValidateLogicalUnit`). Packed-remainder refusal preserved BY POSITION (old gate mechanism): behind a unit-carrying first value, an unbracketed unit-less tail (`interface ge-0/0/0.0 disable`) refuses by name even though `disable` alone is legal; braced-child remainders keep the children guards; flat/display-set unit-carrying lists stay accepted member-by-member.
- Add `checkGroupPacked`: walks each group instance's `instanceValueTail` (the same tail `compileDHCPRelayV6Group9553` consumes) with the compiler grammar — unsupported knob refused, interface members validated, scalars via existing closures — before the children loop.
- Parity table {v4, v6} × {canonical block, compact, flat-set repeated, flat-set bracket, hierarchical bracket} × {direct, display-set replay} now compares FULL `Servers`/`Interfaces` slices; new cells pin digit-less ACCEPT, single-bare ACCEPT vs packed/braced-child REFUSE, and container-packed REFUSE.

## Validation

## Why
`cargo clippy` exited 101 on the crate (deny-by-default `mut_from_ref` at `umem/mmap.rs` since the first commit, `never_loop` in a #15950 test, plus a #17134 E0308 in `shared_umem_tests` that kept the test target from compiling), yet 246 `allow(clippy::…)` lines were maintained for a tool nothing ran — unfalsifiable ceremony. ## What
- `#[expect(clippy::mut_from_ref, reason = "SAFETY: see # Safety above; AF_XDP single-writer")]` on `slice_mut_unchecked` (expect, not allow, so a future non-triggering refactor reds as stale via the leg-1 deny below).
- #15950 test rewritten as a real bounded loop: adopt the drained window once (`mem::take`), then drive the in-flight `worker_export` with no fresh commands until it clears (≤16 passes); trailing assertions unchanged.
- Fix `shared_umem_tests` E0308: originally via `serde_json::from_value` as sibling cells did; at the fold's plain master merge, master's #18234 `typed_userspace` helper superseded that hunk, so the merge kept master's typed construction and dropped the `from_value` form.
- Convert all 246 `allow(clippy::…)` → `#[expect(…)]` with reasons; delete the 26 the clippy oracle proves stale. Final at reviewed head: 0 allows, 221 expects. At merge, plain master merges (through c2816a9ab4) brought new `allow` sites; they were re-converted to `expect` (2 stale allows on <=7-arg fns deleted): merged tree 0 allows, 228 expects.
- Fix deny-pass blockers: 37 `empty_line_after_doc_comment/outer_attribute` detachments, duplicated `#[inline]` in occupancy.rs, 8 `drop_non_drop` no-ops, 1 redundant rebinding.
- `make clippy-rust`: leg 1 is the full `--workspace --all-targets` clippy with `-D unfulfilled_lint_expectations` (targeted deny — that lint is warn-level, so without it a stale expect stays green among ~2.7k warn-level warnings; `-D warnings` rejected because leg 1 is not warning-clean enough), plus leg 2 with `-D clippy::correctness -D clippy::suspicious -A clippy::duplicate_mod` (duplicate_mod allowed only for the intentional shim-parity multi-load, rationale in Makefile). CI rust job runs it beside the compile check; `docs/ci-gate-contract.md` updated.

## Validation
On pinned 1.98.1: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` exits 0 with 0 `unfulfilled_lint_expectations`; deny pass exits 0; `make clippy-rust` exits 0 (both legs). Fold proof: planted a stale `#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on `slice_mut_unchecked` → `make clippy-rust` exited 101 (`error: this lint expectation is unfulfilled`, `Makefile:595: clippy-rust Error 101`); scratch removed → exit 0. Named hermetic tests PASS (`--exact`, re-run on the merged head): `batched_export_window_ships_only_last_rgs_under_last_token`, `batched_export_commands_last_window_wins_at_accept`, `shared_umem_mode_unknown_falls_back_off_17149` (3 passed, 0 failed). Merge-train parent re-verified on merged head 2d6d97f63b: Makefile leg-1 `-D unfulfilled_lint_expectations` present (Makefile:595) and `shared_umem_mode_unknown_falls_back_off_17149 --exact` 1 passed. Full clippy gate not re-run at merge (reviewer ran it at 094550a2c2). No broad suites run. Cluster gates ENV-BLOCKED — not run. Full detail: `docs/log/17200.md`.

## Risk
Behavior-preserving: attribute conversions/deletions, doc blank-line removals, one duplicate `#[inline]` removal, no-op `drop()` removals on non-Drop values (scope-exit order preserved); unsafe fn signature/safety contract untouched. Residual warn-level clippy noise stays non-gating by design except the targeted `unfulfilled_lint_expectations` deny; a future stale expect reds leg 1 — intended falsifiability. CI note: the rust job's `timeout-minutes: 20` may be tight for the two-leg clippy run (~28 min locally under heavy parallel load); the Makefile has no timeout knob, so a CI timeout fix would raise `timeout-minutes` in `test.yml`.

## PR #18271 — nat: extract shared pre-routing DNAT verdict for Stage 11 (#17197) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17197-campaign`

Closes #17197.

## Why
Stage 11's `ipsec_destination_matches_transit_dnat` modelled the production DNAT decision (dynamic tier only, collapsing `lookup_with_counter_scoped`, raw-ifindex scope) and drifted after #16045/#14947, so IKE/ESP/AH could be claimed for local XFRM where production would translate or drop.

Fold (Rev18271Opus NEEDS-FOLD on e1f04742bf): the "pure verdict" claim was false for the persistent tier — the verdict called `persistent_inbound_lookup_for_rule`, which unconditionally takes `lock_live()` and charges `live_write_lock_acquisitions` (+contended) exported in NAT status, so Stage 11 took a write lock and charged allocator lock telemetry on a path the deleted mirror never touched the allocator from.

## What
- New `poll_descriptor/prerouting_dnat.rs`: `#[inline]`, allocation-free `prerouting_dnat_verdict` returning `Static | Persistent | Dynamic | Poisoned | Denied | None` with borrowed counters / lease keys (never applied: no NAT rule counter charged, no lease hold taken).
- Session-miss poll loop calls the counting verdict and applies side effects at the existing committed-install / poisoned-drop sites; its persistent tier keeps the counted `lock_live()` telemetry, unchanged from pre-extraction.
- Stage 11 builds scope via the same `prerouting_ingress_scope{,_ambiguous}`, claims only `None` or translate-to-self, never `Poisoned`/`Denied`; mirror deleted (acceptance grep = 0). Stage 11 calls the new non-counting twin `prerouting_dnat_verdict_peek`: the scoped persistent lookup is split into a guard-taking core in `nat/allocator/mod.rs`, and `persistent_inbound_peek_for_rule` runs the identical read-only body under the deliberately uncounted `read_live()`, so the claim path takes no write guard and bumps no allocator lock telemetry.

## Validation
Named hermetic tests only (`cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp --bin xpf-userspace-dp <name> -- --exact`):
- `prerouting_dnat_stage11_parity_17197` (new, 2×7 matrix) — pass
- `prerouting_dnat_stage11_peek_no_lock_telemetry_17197` (fold, new: Stage-11 persistent-row snapshot invariance, counting verdict as positive control) — pass
- `stage_ipsec_ambiguous_scope_parity_16047`, `flow_backed_poisoned_dnat_counts_drop_16483`, `acquire_persistent_inbound_hold_with_snat_takes_hold_16619`, `prerouting_dnat_scope_uses_logical_vlan_unit_zone_5802` — pass

## Risk
Hot-path session-miss refactor; no NAT rule counters are charged and no lease holds are taken by either verdict entry point, and allocator lock telemetry is charged only by the counting entry point, so behaviour changes only where Stage 11 previously diverged (static/persistent/poisoned/ambiguous rows). The peek classification can race a concurrent lease mint/revoke like any read-guard snapshot; the poll loop re-evaluates with the counting verdict before installing, so a stale peek never installs state. Residual (Finding 2, acknowledged): the parity matrix reconstructs the production verdict's scope/meta arguments in the test harness, so future call-site wiring drift at either production call site is not caught by the matrix alone — the telemetry regression exercises the real Stage-11 claim path, and call-site argument drift remains review-covered (see `docs/log/17197.md`).

## PR #18278 — coalesce: cancel in-flight actuation on Loop.Stop (#17226) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17226-campaign`

## Summary
`coalesce.Loop.Stop` closed `stop` and waited on `done` without cancelling the in-flight actuation. The route listener's `applySem.Acquire` (on a `context.Background()`-derived ctx, 30s default actuate timeout) could therefore hold shutdown's `wg.Wait()` past `TimeoutStopSec=20`, skipping the #9035 fail-closed block. The #3758 cancel existed only privately in ipmon, which never uses `Loop.Start/Stop`.

Closes #17226

## What
- **pkg/coalesce**: `Loop` owns a cancellable context created in `StartWithContext(parent)` (`Start()` = Background parent); `run()` hands `Loop.Context()` to `Tick`; `Stop()` calls `cancel()` **before** `<-l.done`. Added `Loop.Context()`; externally-driven `Tick` keeps its caller ctx (documented: pass `Context()`). Tick pacing / dirtyGen semantics unchanged.
- **pkg/ipmon**: private actuation context deleted (`grep -n actuateCancel pkg/ipmon` is empty). Engine starts the loop, ticks with `loop.Context()`, and `Stop` closes `e.stop` then `loop.Stop()` (cancel-first) before waiting on `e.done`.
- **pkg/daemon**: route listener calls `loop.StartWithContext(ctx)` so daemon run-ctx cancel alone aborts a queued `applySem.Acquire`.
- ipmon's #3758 `TestStopAbortsBlockedActuation` assertion moved into pkg/coalesce; daemon cell pins the applySem-held + run-ctx-cancel join.

## Validation (named hermetic tests only)
- `TestCoalesceStopAbortsBlockedActuation17226` PASS — held semaphore, default 30s timeout, Stop <100ms (acceptance)
- `TestCoalesceParentCancelAbortsBlockedActuation17226` PASS
- `TestIpmonHasNoPrivateActuateCancel17226` PASS
- `TestDaemonRouteListenerSemantics17226` PASS — applySem held, run-ctx cancel, listener goroutine joined <1s
- ipmon `TestStopAbortsBlockedActuation`, `TestActuationTimeoutRetriesWithoutStop` PASS; coalesce 7437/11414 cells PASS; daemon 8915/11423 cells PASS
- `-race` PASS on coalesce/ipmon Stop cells; daemon `-race` build exceeded the 240s tool window on the 866-file test package (compile-bound; non-race cell PASS)
- `go vet` + `gofmt` clean on touched packages. No broad suites run.

## Risk
Control-plane lifecycle only, no packet path. No adopter relies on an actuation outliving Stop (only the route listener uses Start/Stop; ipmon drives Tick). ipmon now also runs the loop's sweep goroutine alongside its own Tick — actuations stay single-flighted by the loop's throttle/dirtyGen state, pinned by the ipmon cells. Live-cluster shutdown timing is inferred from the hermetic joins, not measured.

STEP-0: defect confirmed live on current origin/master (9f39e9331e) — bare `unix.Recvfrom`, watcher-close wake, cancel+delete teardown, no ctx re-check before send. #16669 is closed but fixed LLDP only (inline ppoll), so this copy survived.

## What
- **New shared primitive `linuxsock.PpollRecv`** (pkg/linuxsock/ppoll.go): ppoll on {socket, wake eventfd}; `SignalStop` wakes a parked `Recv`; owners `Close` only after joining the receiving goroutine (signal → join → close). This is the one cancellable raw-receive primitive the issue's fix direction requires; it replaces the suggested SOCK_NONBLOCK+netpoller sketch with the mechanism #16669 already proved for AF_PACKET.
- **LLDP migrated onto it**: `ifSession` now holds `*linuxsock.PpollRecv`; inline ppoll/wakeOnce/close machinery deleted. Behaviour unchanged (same wake, same `stopLocked` signal→wait→close, same ctx re-check after successful recv). `errRecvStopped` is now an alias of `linuxsock.ErrWakeStopped` (identity preserved for existing comparisons).
- **Proxy-ARP migrated**: `cluster.OpenARPSocket` → `cluster.OpenARPReceiver` returning the primitive. The loop publishes the receiver for teardown signalling, owns its `Close` (deferred, runs before `done` closes), self-wakes if cancelled before publish (closing the open-window race), and re-checks ctx after every successful recv before sending. Teardown (`syncProxyARPResponders` !keep and empty-address branches, `stopProxyARPResponders`) now calls `r.stop()` = cancel → SignalStop → join on `done`, never cancel-and-forget.
- **Canary**: `TestNoDirectBlockingRecvfrom` (AST, pkg/linuxsock) rejects any direct `unix.Recvfrom` outside the primitive, allowlisting nfqueue's two poll-guarded reads. It was RED pre-migration, flagging exactly the proxy-ARP site.
- Existing fake-responder fixtures whose `cancel` never closed `done` now simulate real goroutine exit on cancel so the new join returns; docs (linuxsock/lldp READMEs, docs/log/17231.md, debian/changelog) updated.

## Acceptance (issue criteria)
- `TestQ53ProxyARPCloseDoesNotUnblockRecv` (netns, real AF_PACKET on veth): silent arm — responder's done closed **<100ms** after cancel; chatty arm — live request answered (positive control), **zero replies after cancel**. ✅
- #16669's silent arm (`TestStopSilentVsChatty16669`) still returns <1s on the shared primitive. ✅
- Canary fails on a newly added blocking Recvfrom under pkg/. ✅ (verified RED before the daemon migration)

## Validation (named hermetic tests only)
- `go vet` clean: pkg/linuxsock, pkg/lldp, pkg/cluster, pkg/daemon.
- linuxsock: `TestNoDirectBlockingRecvfrom`, `TestPpollRecvWakesOnSignalStop17231`, `TestSocketForcesCloexec`, `TestSocketRealFDIsCloexec` pass.
- daemon: `TestQ53ProxyARPCloseDoesNotUnblockRecv`, `TestProxyARPResponderStopJoinsParkedRecv17231`, 8621/9237/10316/15764 proxy-ARP cells pass; join/reconcile cells also pass under `-race`.
- lldp: `TestStopSilentVsChatty16669`, `TestStopUnblocksParkedRX`, `TestSessionRecvWakeAndForeignFD16669`, `TestRxLoopStopsAfterSuccessfulRecv16669` pass.

## Risk
Teardown now blocks until the responder goroutine exits, bounded by the eventfd wake (<100ms measured silent). `syncProxyARPResponders` holds `arpResponders.mu` during the join; responder goroutines never take that mutex (documented lock order in daemon.go), so no cycle. Known unrelated pre-existing failure: `TestNoDirectUnixSocket` on master flags `pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive.go`'s direct `unix.Socket` — not introduced or touched by this change.

Packaging metadata only; no code, wire or config change. ## PR #18296 — daemon: keep wedge detector from counting decode failures (#18293) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/18293-campaign`

## Why

The #9651 wedge detector counted any non-rejection status-poll error as silence (`statusLoop` fed every error to `noteStatusPollResultLocked`, which reset only on `nil`/`errHelperRejected`). A Go/Rust wire drift that made every status answer undecodable (#18207-class) therefore SIGKILLed a healthy, answering helper once a minute — fw0 logged 1324 identical decode errors/hour, each <1s before a `killed` helper exit, while the helper provably answered other requests seconds before each kill.

## What

Answered-but-undecodable is now a distinct typed class end-to-end:

- `errStatusDecode`/`statusDecodeError` (verbatim decoder message, `Is`/`Unwrap` beside it — the `helperRejectedError` convention), minted in `requestDetailedAtSocket` only for `req.Type == "status"` and only past the arms that remain silence: bare EOF/`ErrUnexpectedEOF` (#1961 pre-reply close, untagged) and response-cap truncation (re-tagged for `status` in `statusLoop` via a new `errResponseCap` sentinel; cap message unchanged). Absent/partial status (`validateRequiredStatusReply`) is re-minted in the same class. All other verbs keep the bare decoder error.
- Read-deadline/timeout errors (`isStatusReadTimeout`: `os.ErrDeadlineExceeded` chain or `net.Error.Timeout()`) stay untagged silence, checked before any byte-count reasoning, so a helper that accepts and stalls/never writes — or writes a partial prefix then stalls — remains wedge-countable; the decode mint additionally requires `bounded.received > 0`.
- `noteStatusPollResultLocked`: a decode poll increments `liveness.decodeErrors` + the process-lifetime counter, never kills, and neither advances nor resets an in-progress silence streak. Genuine silence unchanged (30 polls + 30s span + RG grace → kill, supervisor restarts).
- `statusLoop` logs it distinctly: `status poll decode failed; helper answered but its status could not be decoded (#18293)`.
- Metric: `userspace.StatusPollDecodeErrors()` exported as `xpf_status_poll_decode_errors_total` through the existing silent-skips collector, always emitted including at zero (`BindingWedgeGiveups` shape).

## Validation

- READY verdict by Rev18296bOpus (meta/muse-wonder-1.0) on head `7b04b75c70`: real-socket probes (never-write and 1-byte-then-stall = silence/wedge-countable; garbage-complete = decode; pre-reply EOF unchanged); named 18293/9651 suites PASS.
- Firsthand on merged head `d2f645248c` (plain merge of `origin/master`, never rebase): `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '18293|9651' -count=1` PASS (pkg ok, 18.2s).
- Named cells include: `TestUndecodableAnswersNeverKill18293`, `TestStatusLoopUndecodableAnswersNoKill18293`, `TestSilentHelperStillKilledOnSchedule18293`, `TestWedgedHelperIsKilledAndRestarted9651`, `TestStatusPollDecodeClassifiedOnRealSocket18293`, `TestStatusCloseWithoutReplyIsSilence18293`, `TestDecodeFailureNeitherAdvancesNorResetsSilence18293`, `TestStatusDecodeClassification18293`, `TestStatusStalledHelperIsSilence18293`, `TestStatusLoopSilentDecodeSilentSequence18293`.
- Regression cells cited on PR: `9322` response-cap, `TestContentConflictIsClassifiedOnTheRealSocketPath9520`, `TestRequiredStatusReplyDistinguishesAbsentStatusFromZeroPID10868`, `TestStatusLoopWiresTheLivenessCount9651`; `go test ./pkg/api/ -run 'TestDataplaneSilentSkips' -count=1` PASS; `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean.
- Cluster gates ENV-BLOCKED — not claimed.

## Risk

A helper answering garbage forever is no longer wedge-killed — intended: it is provably alive, and the decode counter/Warn is now the operator signal instead of a crash loop. Silent helpers are unaffected (timeout/EOF polls return to the original #9651 kill schedule; fail-closed direction only). `controlRequestHook` test paths do not mint the class (they bypass the decoder, as before). No wire, config, or Rust change; no allocation on the poll path beyond the failure error value.

Docs: `docs/log/18293.md`.

Closes #18293

Fixes #18297: the #7689 additive-wire exhaustive-literal ratchet is RED on master (`SessionDeltaInfo: 2 exhaustive literals, ceiling 1 (+1)`), and that master-inherited failure blocks PR #18231 (#17147) — its merge-train run hit the identical failure on the merged head and proved by master control (pure `origin/master` worktree, same exact cell) that it is pre-existing.

**STEP-0 (verified firsthand on `origin/master`, now `df7184e85b`):** the exact cell `protocol::cos::cos_literal_guard_7689::additive_wire_exhaustive_literals_only_ever_decrease_7689` fails with `SessionDeltaInfo: 2 vs ceiling 1`. ## Disposition: raise the ceiling 1 -> 2 (reviewed table row)

The specimen is intentionally exhaustive, so the preferred disposition applies. The ratchet only ever goes DOWN by design; this is the table's first increase and the row carries its justification in a `#18297` comment:

- **Production converter** — tailing it would silently default any FUTURE field instead of forcing a wire-mapping decision at compile time: the exact #6949 failure (JSON leg carrying none of the binary leg's fields). It must stay exhaustive.
- **#17142 specimen** — tailing it (`..Default::default()`) would serialize byte-identically *today* (it enumerates all 60 fields), but a future field would then enter the struct with no sentinel and no compile error anywhere; the Go value cell restates the sentinels it knows, so the new field would pass undetected. The exhaustive literal is the only forcing function keeping the transposition census complete. That alternative was considered and rejected; see `docs/log/18297.md`.
- The ceiling now holds **exactly** these two; a third exhaustive `SessionDeltaInfo` literal still reds.

## Changes

## PR #18305 — config: single-source VRRP and WireGuard list readers (#17241) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17241-campaign`

## Summary
Single-sources the VRRP `virtual-address`/`virtual-inet6-address` and WireGuard `allowed-ips` list readers through `firewallMatchValues` (#6714 SSOT), removing the hand-rolled pre-#6714 copies that read only `Keys[0]`/`Name()` of each child and silently dropped the second value of the packed braced spelling `{ a b; }`.

## Why
The VRRP and WireGuard list readers in `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go` were hand-rolled pre-#6714 copies: the VRRP reader read `prop.Keys[1:]` + `child.Name()` (Keys[0] only) per child, and the WireGuard reader read `prop.Keys[1:]` + `vn.Keys[0]` only for `vn.IsLeaf` children. As a result the second-and-later values of the packed braced spelling were silently dropped with no warning, strict or lenient.

STEP-0 evidence (live on origin/master @ a60e77bda3):
- `virtual-address { 10.0.1.100/24 10.0.1.101/24; }` → `vips=[10.0.1.100/24]`
- `allowed-ips { 10.0.0.0/8 192.168.0.0/16; }` → `allowed=[10.0.0.0/8]`
- Controls (one-per-child, bracket) compiled both values; no warning strict or lenient.

## What
- `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`: both sites now `append(..., firewallMatchValues(prop)...)`; VRRP still dedupes via `DedupeVRRPVIPs`, WireGuard downstream validation unchanged. Both leaves are schema `args:1, multi:true, children:nil` (no per-value options), so the SSOT no-descend contract applies exactly.
- New `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_list_readers_17241_test.go`: parity table (one-per-child == braced-packed == bracket == repeated-leaf == flat-set, strict == lenient) for `virtual-address`, `virtual-inet6-address`, `allowed-ips` — pinned RED on the packed rows before the refactor, PASS after — plus a single-source census guard.
- Fold (canonical gate): `allChildKeysAreValues: true` on all three leaves (`virtual-address` + `virtual-inet6-address` in `vrrpGroupSchemaNode`, `allowed-ips` in `wireguardSchemaNode`), so `validateMultiValueLeaf` validates every packed token instead of refusing the packed child. Previously untyped `allowed-ips` now carries `valueType: ValueCIDR` + `ValidateWGAllowedIPPrefix`, mirroring the strict `netip.ParsePrefix` gate, so its packed tokens are value-validated at `SchemaValidate`, not merely shape-checked.
- Fold (nested refusal): new scoped schema flag `refuseNonLeafBlockChildren` (`pkg/config/schema.go`) set on all three leaves in `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go`; `validateMultiValueLeaf` refuses any block child with `len(c.Children) > 0 || !c.IsLeaf`, fail-closed, naming the leaf and offending child token (bogus grandchild, real-prefix grandchild, empty-block `a { }`). Scoped to these three leaves only; other typed multi leaves keep legacy tolerance.
- Fold round 2 (store ingress): the nested-list finding has a dedicated error class preserved through secret scrubbing and the #16012 collect-all path, with a bounded collector fallback for the typed-error-cap / early-stop cases; `compileTreeLenient` hard-refuses only that class, so tolerant `Store.Load` / `Store.SyncApply` also refuse nested content instead of installing a truncated config, while all other typed/schema errors retain the existing tolerant warning policy.
- `docs/log/17241.md`.

## Validation
Named hermetic cells:
- `TestVRRPWGListReaderParity17241`, `TestListReadersSingleSourced17241`: PASS
- Fold cells: `TestVRRPWGListReaderCanonicalGate17241` (SchemaValidate-then-strict-compile packed rows, both values honoured, fail-on-revert for the opt-in), `TestVRRPWGListReaderPackedBogusRefused17241` (`{ valid bogus; }` refused by SchemaValidate naming `bogus`, all three leaves), `TestVRRPWGListReaderNestedRefused17241`, `TestListReadersNestedRefusalCensus17241`: PASS
- `pkg/configstore` cells: `TestLoadRefusesNestedAllowedIPs17241`, `TestSyncApplyRefusesNestedAllowedIPs17241`, `TestSyncApplyDoesNotLetPriorSchemaErrorHideNestedRefusal17241`, `TestSyncApplyRefusesNestedAllowedIPsBeyondTypedErrorCap17241`, `TestLenientIngressStillToleratesOtherTypedLeafErrors17241`: PASS (final focused serial `go test -p 1` run in `pkg/config` + `pkg/configstore`, `-count=1`)
- Existing: `TestVRRPFlatRun13537`, `TestJuniperBareVRRPCommitsSameAsCIDR16558`, `TestWireguardAllowedIPsBracketList{FlatSet,Hierarchical}`, `TestWireguard{SinglePeerCompiles,DualPeerCompilesFlatSet,DualPeerCompilesHierarchical}`, `TestWireguard{SamePeerRepeatedPrefixPasses,DistinctAllowedIPsPrefixesPass,DuplicateAllowedIPsPrefixRejected}`: PASS
- `go vet ./pkg/config/`: clean
- Note: a full-suite attempt (`go test -p 1 ./pkg/config ./pkg/configstore -count=1`) did not pass (unrelated failures / timeout recorded in `docs/log/17241.md`); the claim rests on the final focused named-cell PASS above.

## Risk
No dataplane, wire-format, or persisted-format change; this changes config validation and store ingress. Previously dropped second-and-later packed-braced values are now honoured. The proven fail-closed deltas are: bogus packed tokens error at the strict commit gate on all three leaves; non-leaf/quoted tokens reach strict validators instead of being silently dropped; nested block content (`leaf { a { b; } }`, including empty-block `a { }`) is refused at both `SchemaValidate` and tolerant Store.Load / Store.SyncApply rather than committing or installing the truncated config. `allowed-ips` gaining a typed validator also moves malformed-prefix rejection to `SchemaValidate` with the same accept set as the strict compiler's `netip` gate.

Round 2 risk boundary: the three configured leaves (`virtual-address`, `virtual-inet6-address`, `allowed-ips`) now refuse nested block children both at the strict canonical commit gate and on tolerant Store.Load / Store.SyncApply ingress. Only this dedicated nested-list error class is promoted to hard failure; unrelated schema and typed-leaf violations continue through the existing lenient warning/compile policy. A persisted config containing the refused nested form now follows the existing `ErrConfigCompile` recovery path rather than booting a truncated compiled config, and SyncApply leaves the prior active config unchanged.

Scoped claim boundary: what is proven is the canonical sequence (`SchemaValidate` then strict `CompileConfig`) — packed `{ valid valid; }` commits and honours both values, and packed `{ valid bogus; }` is refused by `SchemaValidate` naming `bogus`, on all three leaves. Direct `CompileConfig` without the gate is NOT claimed to reject garbage VRRP tokens (its VIP path tolerates unparseable tokens by design); the pin is on the canonical operator commit path.

Closes #17241

- Acceptance greps: `RouteMapSequenceCount(po, f)` returns nothing in `pkg/frr/redistribute.go`; `defaultVerb` exists in exactly one non-test file (`pkg/frr/route_map_chain.go`).

  - `TestChainComposerParity17026` / `TestChainComposerTerminatingRender17026`: BGP vs redistribute byte-parity modulo the tail verb.
  - `TestChainComposerOversizeParity17026`: genuinely oversized chains still quarantine to one bounded deny on both adapters.
- `go test ./pkg/frr/ -run '15156|16868|5732|5277|16125|16869|15157' -count=1` — pre-existing suites pass, including the #16125 byte-identical goldens (`TestProtocolsRenderGolden16125`), satisfying acceptance (4).

## PR #18310 — ha: consolidate failover announcement engines (#17052) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17052-campaign`

## Why

Failover announcement ran on two mode-selected engines — `pkg/vrrp` `sendGARPReservedMode` (VIP-only) vs daemon `directSendGARPs` (VIP + router-LL NA + pool GARP/NA) — with the #5695 clamp duplicated in both. Fixes landed in one engine only in both directions (#2377→#3922, #2867→#2898), and the router-LL NA (#15684) and IPv6 pool NA (#12172) existed only in direct mode: legacy VRRP mode never sent them, so hosts kept the old node's MAC for their default router until NUD ageing.

## What

- New `pkg/cluster/announce.go`: `AnnounceTarget{Iface, IP, Kind(VIP|RouterLL|PoolV4|PoolV6), Burst, ProbeIP}`, `AnnounceTargets` (VIPs via #17140 `Config.RethVIPsForRG`, router LL via #17049 `RouterLinkLocalPlacements`, pool via #17086 `Config.RefRG`), and `SendAnnounceTargets` holding the frame sequence and the **single** announce-path `ClampGratuitousARPCount` call, plus the #8405 64-address bound.
- `directSendGARPs` becomes a wrapper (keeps #2898 fence + per-RG warn-once); daemon sends the non-VIP half on the legacy VRRP MASTER arm (`sendVRRPModeNonVIPAnnounce`); `pkg/vrrp` keeps epoch dedup/dampener/`vipMu` bookkeeping but takes count + per-VIP frame send from the shared engine.
- Non-VIP claims are monotonic and generation-bound under `nonVIPAnnounceMu`: claims at or behind the stored activation generation are rejected (absent entries distinguished from stored zero), and sends are bound to the exact still-active, still-claimed generation, so a delayed claimant cannot re-emit after deactivate/reactivate or a stale producer regress the marker.
- New mode-parity test: (iface, IP, kind) set on activation identical in both modes.
- NOT changed: `GatewayProbeTarget` stays in `pkg/vrrp` (passed in — no cycle); `reconcileProxyARP` added-GARP stays (commit-path trigger, different timing).

## Validation

Named hermetic cells only (class U; seam senders, no host sockets/netlink), at final head 585b3f0e061ab41bbebba39143aa9dc69f3ea059:
- `TestAnnounceModeParity17052` PASS; RED mutant (legacy leg stubbed) FAILs with exactly the missing router-ll/pool kinds, restored GREEN.
- Triple review complete at final head: B1/B2 repros (stale claim regression 3->2 / duplicate burst 3->6; delayed claimant re-emit after deactivate/reactivate) FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix, mutation-verified; `-race` 7 cells PASS.
- Direct gate cells (#2898), #15684 per-unit router-LL, #8405/#12172 pool cells, `pkg/vrrp` probe/clamp/force/abdicate cells, `pkg/cluster` GARP/burst cells — all PASS.
- `go vet ./pkg/cluster/ ./pkg/vrrp/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean; acceptance grep: one `ClampGratuitousARPCount(` outside `pkg/config`.
- Cluster smoke: NOT-EXAMINED — daemon-only change; no dataplane/cluster gate required.

## Risk

Legacy-mode failovers now emit the previously-absent router-LL + pool announcements (intended fix; same clamp/cap/fence). Direct-mode frame order is now deterministic. Per-target failure log wording now comes from the shared sender.

## PR #18312 — cluster: clear fabric slot state on comms stop (#17060) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17060-campaign`

## Why

R4-Q32-06 (#17060): fabric slot state outlived its comms epoch. `stopClusterComms` nilled only the fabric refresh channels — both slots' iface/overlay/peer/MAC/`populated` state (and the helper identity constraints) survived teardown — while `RefreshFabricFwd`, launched as `go d.RefreshFabricFwd()` from three event-watcher sites, probed and refreshed those stale slots with `context.Background()`, outside any epoch and unserialised with the per-epoch populate loops. A fabric removed before a comms restart was still refreshed on the next cluster/VRRP event, and `reconcileRGState`'s fabric gate read the stale `fabric1Populated` (masked only by the #15918 helper conjunct).

STEP-0 on current master (`a60e77bda3`): 4× `context.Background()` in `daemon_ha_fabric.go`, 3× `go d.RefreshFabricFwd` in `daemon_ha.go`, no slot-clearing site anywhere; sole writers are the two populate loops. R4-Q32-01's `fabricSlot` struct does not exist on master, so the existing field/slot layout is preserved and epoch ownership is landed directly — no new abstraction.

## What

- **`clearFabricSlots`** (`daemon_ha_fabric.go`): zeroes both slots (iface, overlay, peer IP/MAC, populated), probe rate-limit + queued-probe flags, and drops each old peer's helper identity constraint (`RegisterFabricPeerMACConstraint(peer, nil)`, deduplicated when both slots share a peer, mirroring the populate loops' peer-changed clear).
- **`stopClusterComms`** calls it under `clusterCommsMu`, alongside the channel nilling and **after cancel + `clusterCommsWG.Wait()`** — deliberately that late, so a populate loop that re-stores its config between cancel and clear cannot resurrect the slot (the same ordering #15918's note implies for readiness consumers).
- **`RefreshFabricFwd`** is now `queueFabricProbe()` + the existing non-blocking `triggerFabricRefresh()` poke. The per-slot 2s rate-limited probe is queued (`fabricProbePending{,1}`) and executed by the epoch-owned populate loop on wake, with the epoch ctx, before its refresh — probe-then-refresh order, probe target (`overlayOrParent`), rate limit, and coalescing all preserved, but nothing runs on `context.Background()` or outside an epoch. With comms stopped the channels are nil and the poke is a no-op.
- The three `go d.RefreshFabricFwd()` sites call it directly; it never blocks.

Acceptance greps: `context.Background()` in `daemon_ha_fabric.go` = **0**; `go d.RefreshFabricFwd` in production = **0**.

Failover behaviour preserved: populate loops, the 30s safety-net ticker, `monitorFabricState`/`triggerFabricRefresh`, readiness gating, retain-on-neighbour-miss, identity recording, fab1 handling, and the #7072 `activeClusterTransport` non-clear are untouched.

## Validation

Named hermetic cells only (synthetic seam links; `linkByNameFn` errors pre-transmit wherever a probe path is reachable — no netlink/kernel reach). Full log: `docs/log/17060.md`.

```
go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestRefreshFabricFwdRaceWithPopulateLatch17060|TestStopClusterCommsClearsFabricSlots17060' ./pkg/daemon/   # PASS
go test -count=1 -run 'TestStopClusterCommsClearsFabricSlots17060|TestFabricConstraintClearedOnStop17060|TestRefreshFabricFwdAfterStopIsNoOp17060|TestRefreshFabricFwdWakesEpochLoops17060|TestTriggerFabricRefresh|TestRefreshFabricFwd1|TestFabricPeerNDP|TestReconcileRGStateFabricReadyWithFab1Only|TestRetainFabricFwd' ./pkg/daemon/   # PASS
go vet ./pkg/daemon/   # clean
```

New cells in `pkg/daemon/fabric_slot_epoch_17060_test.go`:
- `TestStopClusterCommsClearsFabricSlots17060` — the vq32 lifecycle probe as a hermetic cell: both slots seeded + channels + constraints, real `stopClusterComms`, everything zeroed. (Its slot assertions describe exactly what survives on master; the whole file does not compile on master since it also pins the new queued-probe flags, so RED was established per-assertion in STEP-0 rather than by a master run.)
- `TestFabricConstraintClearedOnStop17060` — an ambiguous link-local segment fails closed after stop, proving the identity constraint was dropped.
- `TestRefreshFabricFwdRaceWithPopulateLatch17060` (`-race`) — `RefreshFabricFwd` concurrent with populate-loop latch writes (chained under `fabricMu`, mirroring `refreshFabricPeer`'s only `fabricMu` write); `populated` ends at each writer's last write.
- `TestRefreshFabricFwdAfterStopIsNoOp17060` — post-stop poke neither blocks nor latches.
- `TestRefreshFabricFwdWakesEpochLoops17060` — positive/control: a live-epoch poke still wakes both loops and queues both probes (behaviour the three former `go` sites relied on).

## Risk

Fail-closed: a fabric event arriving while comms are mid-restart now no-ops instead of refreshing stale state; the new epoch's populate loop does its immediate fast-retry pass, so no refresh is lost beyond the restart window that already cancels those loops. A probe queued just before a stop is dropped with the slot; the next epoch re-probes on its own schedule. No allocation added on the refresh poke path beyond the existing channel sends.

## PR #18347 — upgrade: preserve cut-boundary snapshot on resume (#17817) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17817-campaign`

Why

A COPIED/VERIFIED resume skipped the only predecessor-stash immunity reset. The later cut-boundary snapshot could therefore be replaced by the older committed-predecessor snapshot, causing automatic rollback to lose the DB captured after STOP. If backing up that original snapshot failed, restoration also mistook the failed backup for an absent snapshot and deleted the original.

What

- End stash immunity after the COPY block even when the journal resumes at COPIED or VERIFIED, so the current cut's boundary snapshot remains the rollback source.
- Fail before PREFLIGHT when the committed predecessor's stamp or snapshot cannot be secured; do not treat a failed backup as evidence that no snapshot existed.
- Add crash-at-cut COPIED/VERIFIED resume regressions and deterministic backup-copy failure coverage.

- PASS: focused regressions plus adjacent predecessor/resume/snapshot cells passed.
- PASS: `go test ./pkg/upgrade -count=1`.

Risk

Behavior changes only when re-staging a committed predecessor: a failed backup now aborts before snapshot mutation. Ordinary cuts are unchanged.

Closes #17817

## PR #18353 — ipsec: enforce chunk name limit during decoding (#17826) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `eng/17826-ipsec-chunk-name-limit`

Closes #17826

## Why

The IPsec chunk receiver enforced the 4096-name per-chunk cap only after `decodeIPsecSAChunkBody` had decoded and copied every name. A peer could send a permitted-size body with millions of short names and cause avoidable allocation and GC work before the chunk was refused.

Separately (commit `ae12bb0b9f`), a chunk generation that started before a newer set committed could still complete afterwards: its remaining chunks carry fresh, later frame sequences, so sequence admission alone did not fence it. Without a generation watermark at completion, that stale generation would replace the newer committed set and fire `OnIPsecSAReceived` with older names — an older generation overwriting a newer committed set. The interleaving is proven by `TestIPsecSAChunkOlderGenerationCannotOverwriteNewerCommit17826`: generation G's final chunk is refused, the newer generation H commits, then G's valid later-sequenced retry completes and must be dropped.

## What

- Enforce `ipsecChunkNamesPerChunk` in `decodeIPsecSAChunkBody` before appending the first over-limit name; return the named `errIPsecSAChunkTooManyNames` sentinel with no names, never truncate.
- Return named errors for overlong individual names and log decoder errors while preserving malformed-frame accounting.
- Remove the now-redundant post-decode count check from `handleIPsecSAChunk`.
- Add named `t.Run` decoder boundary cells asserting named errors with `errors.Is` for over-limit bodies, at-limit success, over-limit valid-tail refusal, and overlong names; add a large-body receiver cell for refusal accounting and held-set retention.
- Add a `committedGen` per-incarnation watermark in `pkg/cluster/sync_ipsec_chunk_16758.go`: `ipsecSAChunkState.committedGen` (`map[uint64]uint64` keyed by incarnation, since generation numbers are only comparable within one sender incarnation) with `recordCommit` (monotonic advance only) and `supersededByCommit` (strictly-older check) helpers; incarnation 0 bypasses the fence. Legacy full-set commits in `handleIPsecSA` also `recordCommit`, so a legacy commit fences older in-flight chunk generations.
- At chunk completion in `pkg/cluster/sync_lease_recv.go:138-144`, after an assembly closes and before the held-set store and callback, drop `supersededByCommit` completions: increment `IPsecSAStaleIgnored`, log the stale-generation warning, and return `false` — the newer committed set is retained and no callback fires. Non-stale completions `recordCommit` in the same completion path.
- Add the `TestIPsecSAChunkOlderGenerationCannotOverwriteNewerCommit17826` G/H interleaving regression in `pkg/cluster/ipsec_sa_chunk_16758_test.go`.

## Validation

- RED before the decoder change: `go test ./pkg/cluster -run '^TestIPsecSAChunkBodyNameBoundAtDecode17826$' -count=1` failed because the decoder accepted and returned 4097 names.
- `gofmt -w pkg/cluster/sync_ipsec_chunk_16758.go pkg/cluster/sync_lease_recv.go pkg/cluster/ipsec_sa_chunk_16758_test.go`.
- `TestIPsecSAChunkOlderGenerationCannotOverwriteNewerCommit17826` passes: the stale G completion is dropped, H's committed set is retained, no extra callback fires, and `IPsecSAStaleIgnored == 1`.
- `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/cluster -run '^TestIPsecSA' -count=1` PASS (all tests in `ipsec_sa_chunk_16758_test.go` and related named IPsec tests, including the fence regression above).

## Risk

No wire-format or accepted in-bound behavior changes. Over-bound chunk bodies receive the same malformed refusal, now as a named decoder error before the decoder materializes the rest of the names.

The generation fence rejects only completed generations strictly older than `committedGen` for the same incarnation; equal or newer generations, in-progress assemblies, and incarnation-0 traffic retain existing behavior. No wire-format change.

Closes #17828

Why: A successful system-syslog client could remain cached after it had been retired and closed. A failed same-endpoint configuration change left the old fingerprint cached, so reverting reused the closed pointer. A foreign handler replacement or shutdown drain could also close a cached pointer while the fingerprint gate failed open into per-host reuse.

What: Evict a host's cache entry whenever its construction fails, regardless of the old fingerprint. Before per-host reuse, discard cache entries whose client identity is no longer installed in the handler. Add regressions for A → failed B → revert A and for external `SetClients(nil)`, checking fresh dialing, pointer replacement, successful sends, and unchanged-apply zero-dial controls.

Validation:
- RED before the failed-change fix on `62a4b44a8fe1`: revert dials stayed at 2 instead of 3, proving the closed pointer was reused.
- RED before the handler-identity fix on PR head `e6457706046a`: apply after external retirement dials stayed at 1 instead of 2.
- GREEN on current master `85ee385d1eb6`: all six named daemon syslog cells passed (`TestSystemSyslogUnchangedApplyZeroDials16767`, `TestSystemSyslogPartialFailurePreservesHealthy16767`, `TestSystemSyslogDNSLossKeepsWorkingClient16767`, `TestSystemSyslogPerHostFingerprintRebuildsOnlyChanged16767`, `TestApplySystemSyslogFailedChangeThenRevertDoesNotReuseClosedClient`, and `TestApplySystemSyslogDoesNotReuseExternallyRetiredClient`).
- `go test ./pkg/logging -run '^TestSetClientsPreservingKeepsSharedClient16767$' -count=1` passed.
- `gofmt -l` on touched Go files was empty; `git diff --check` passed.

Risk: Failed builds no longer retain a cached client that the preserving install closes, and stale cache entries removed from the handler's installed set are evicted before reuse. Healthy clients still installed for successful host builds retain per-host reuse; unchanged complete configurations retain the zero-dial fast path.

## PR #18355 — cli: resolve history mutations against edit path (#17829) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/17829`

Why:
Malformed config-mutation history lines with a leading unterminated quote can leave the lexer with zero tokens, so the raw mutation verb and a context-gated credential in its tail are missed by both live history filtering and seed replay.

What:
Extend the unlexable-line Fields fallback to every config mutation verb and add a regression proving a quote-artifacted `delete community` secret is omitted from both the live recorder and history seed. See `docs/log/17829.md`.

Validation:
- RED before the fallback extension: `go test ./pkg/cliterm -run '^TestHistoryUnlexableMutationLineSuppressed17829$' -count=1` failed at the live predicate, persisted file, and seed.
- GREEN named history/CLI cells: `go test ./pkg/cliterm -run '^(TestReadHistorySeedInterleavedSharedHistory17829|TestReadHistorySeedCursorAware17798|TestReadHistorySeedReentryDualCursor17972|TestHistoryMutationEditContext(SecretsNotPersisted|BenignRetained)17829|TestHistoryUnlexableMutationLineSuppressed17829|TestHistoryEditContextSecretsNotPersisted16794|TestBothSurfacesShareHistoryWiring_15284)$' -count=1`.
- `go test ./pkg/cliterm -count=1`, `go vet ./pkg/cliterm`, and `gofmt -l` on both changed Go files passed.
- Triple hostile review at head 7e497af966: Rev18355Task initially requested a seed-replay revision; the shared-history seed suppression was folded. Rev18355bTask PASS (seed suppression). Rev18355Glm2 READY (unlexable fold verified with independent RED; benign lines retained).
- Final-head CI status is not green: `lint` passed and the broad affected-Go job passed `pkg/cliterm`, but other affected packages and the repository-wide gofmt census failed. Harness self-test failed its `test.yml` census-wiring check; proto regen failed fetching a pinned artifact (HTTP 404); the Rust job could not find `python3`; advisory tooling hit missing `/var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir` and permission failures. These failed checks do not identify a failure in the changed history-filter package.

Risk:
Live history recording still judges mutations using the submitting session's edit cursor. Shared-file seed replay has no session markers, so it suppresses mutations/edit commands carrying a value after a context-sensitive secret keyword even when a benign cursor seems plausible; benign generic identifiers such as GRE `key` or policy-options `community` can therefore be omitted from recalled seed history. Seed history is only recall convenience and is never executed as configuration; existing history files are not rewritten.

Closes #17829

## PR #18358 — configstore: skip rescue deletion superseded by newer save (#17825) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17825-rescue-delete-superseded`

Closes #17825

## Why
`DeleteRescueConfig` can claim generation N and be delayed before taking `rescueMu`. A newer save can then claim and durably apply N+1. The old delete would acquire the mutex afterward and unconditionally unlink the newer save's `rescue.conf`.

## What
- Compare the delete generation with `rescueAppliedGen` under `rescueMu`; if a newer operation has already applied, keep its file and return `ErrRescueDeleteSuperseded`.
- Preserve the `rescueMu`-protected unlink and directory fsync, and the #14722 in-flight-save behavior.
- Map this expected gRPC race to `FailedPrecondition` rather than `Internal`.
- Add deterministic claim-to-lock coverage, a named gRPC classification cell, and update the #16783 test comment plus `docs/log/17825.md`.

## Validation
- RED before the fix and on RED-on-revert: `TestDeleteRescueConfigSkipsNewerSave_17825` fails with `rescue.conf missing after stale delete resumed`.
- GREEN on current master `9e48fe602b`; `-race` passed the six configstore cells: `TestDeleteRescueConfigDoesNotResurrectInFlightSave_14722`, `TestSaveRescueConfigNewestWins_14722`, `TestDeleteRescueConfigDoesNotUnlinkLaterSave_16783`, `TestDeleteRescueConfigSkipsNewerSave_17825`, `TestDeleteRescueConfigDirSynced`, and `TestDeleteRescueConfigAbsentNoDirSync`.
- `-race` passed the complete `rescue_action_fence_10769_test.go` cells, including `TestRescueDeleteSupersededIsFailedPrecondition_17825`.
- `go vet ./pkg/configstore ./pkg/grpcapi` passed; `gofmt` applied to modified Go files.

## Risk
Only an overlapping delete superseded by a newer applied rescue operation now returns an error. The gRPC surface reports it as `FailedPrecondition`; normal durable deletion is unchanged.

## PR #18363 — frr: preserve RIP group permits at empty host boundaries (#18361) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-28)

Branch: `fix/18361-campaign`

## Why

A `/32 longer` route-filter is a valid empty match set. The RIP per-group renderer treated it as unrenderable, causing the entire group list to become deny-all and losing otherwise valid sibling permits. The generic renderer preserves a nested max-length boundary with a bare exact-host deny rather than an FRR-invalid `le` equal to the base length.

## What

- Keep max-length `longer` route-filters as empty boundaries in RIP per-group lowering.
- Treat a lone boundary term as no-match so later terms can run; when an accepting term has a broader sibling permit, emit a bare exact-host deny before it.
- Keep the gate fail-closed if a later accepting action could change the boundary host's outcome, which a flat prefix-list cannot express.
- Add regressions for the nested `/32` boundary, empty-term fallthrough, and the later-accept fail-closed control; update `docs/log/18361.md`.

## Validation

- RED before the fix: `TestRIPPerGroupMaxLengthLongerBoundaryPreservesSibling16625` failed with only `deny 0.0.0.0/0 le 32` in the group list.
- PASS on this PR branch: named RIP group cells, `TestRouteFilterLongerFRR`, `TestRouteFilterOrlongerMaxLengthValid`, and named #16762 longest-match cells:
  `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/frr -run '^(TestRIPPerGroupExportRendered16625|TestRIPPerGroupBareTokenFailsClosed16625|TestRIPPerGroupContestedWithheld16625|TestRIPNoGroupsLegacyByteShape16625|TestRIPPerGroupRejectTermConfines16625|TestRIPPerGroupMaxLengthLongerBoundaryPreservesSibling16625|TestRIPPerGroupEmptyMaxLengthLongerTermFallsThrough16625|TestRIPPerGroupBoundaryWithLaterAcceptFailsClosed16625|TestRouteFilterLongerFRR|TestRouteFilterOrlongerMaxLengthValid|TestRouteFilterLongestMatchAcceptance_16762|TestRouteFilterLongestMatchAuthoringOrderIndependent_16762|TestRouteFilterDisjointByteIdentical_16762|TestRouteFilterSingleAndSameBaseByteIdentical_16762|TestRouteFilterNestedChainStops_16762|TestRouteFilterLongestV6_16762|TestRouteFilterRootHasNoStop_16762)$' -count=1 -v` — PASS.
- Compatibility on a disposable worktree combining this branch with PR #18350 head `566bcab7831b7d66c74d5872a6593d9ce8909d0e`: the named RIP cells and #17823 boundary cells passed. A broader combined run failed `TestRouteFilterLongerFRR/mixed_skipped_then_valid_keeps_seq_and_match` (expected `/24 longer` permit at seq 5; observed only `/32` deny). This generic-renderer failure is outside this PR's diff and was not changed here.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

## Risk

Only RIP per-group max-length `longer` boundaries change. Other invalid/inexpressible shapes retain fail-closed behavior. ## PR #18367 — userspace-dp: avoid crash accounting for planned stops (#18213) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/18213-planned-stop-crash`

Closes #18213

## Summary

- Use `KillMode=mixed` so systemd's initial stop signal reaches xpfd alone and the daemon can stop the helper through its owned shutdown path.
- Avoid double-charging a supervised helper exit observed during a failed retry: the crash handler owns that exit's count and restart timer, while the defer charges only if no new exit was handled. Clear `procSup` whenever the handler clears `proc`, preserving the manager invariant.
- The stop boundary is waiter publication, not physical death. A SIGKILL immediately before the non-blocking check whose `Wait` has not yet published remains treated as part of the planned stop; this boundary is documented rather than adding a second race-prone observation mechanism. Genuine later-generation SIGKILLs still count.

## Validation

RED on 44b2a4de: `TestRestartUsesTheCurrentConfigNotTheDeadGeneration5838` observed 3 timers / 8 attempts instead of 2 / 7; `TestBringUpDetectsAChildThatDiesBeforeReady5838` found `procSup` still set.

PASS: twelve named cells normally (userspace 9.716s; daemon 2.312s), including both #5838 cells and all ten PR cells.

PASS: nine userspace cells with `-race` (17.200s); three daemon cells with `-race` (13.288s).

`git diff --check` passed; no test files changed. No live cluster deployment/rolling-restart smoke was run.

The full package command `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace ./pkg/daemon -count=1` timed out after 300s and reported failures in other userspace tests (stale generated snapshots, source-NAT parity, helper socket ownership, and Unix-socket bind cases); no full-package pass is claimed.

## Fold

Folded at `40c58d7f25`. The unpublished-SIGKILL-at-retirement case remains intentionally outside the claim: only an exit published by closing `exited` before the check is counted by that stop observation.

## PR #18371 — cluster: fence stale DHCP chunk generations at completion (#18369) [OPEN]

Branch: `campaign/18369-dhcp-generation-fence`

Closes #18369

## Why

A DHCP chunk generation can remain pending after a chunk is refused downstream of per-frame sequence admission. Its remaining later-sequenced chunks can complete after a newer DHCP set commits and then overwrite the newer held lease set and callback state.

## What

- Add a monotonic committed-generation watermark per DHCP family and sender incarnation.
- Advance it for legacy full-set commits using the full-set sequence and completed chunked sets using the generation.
- Drop a completed generation strictly older than the watermark before storing the snapshot or invoking OnDHCPLeasesReceived; count and warn through the existing DHCP stale-ignore path.
- Add the G/H interleaving regression: refuse G downstream of sequence admission, commit H, retry G with a fresh frame sequence, and assert H remains held, no stale callback fires, and DHCPLeasesStaleIgnored increments once.

## Validation

- RED before the fence: go test ./pkg/cluster -run ^TestDHCPLeaseChunkOlderGenerationCannotOverwriteNewerCommit18369$ -count=1 failed because G completed after H.
- GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/cluster -run ^TestDHCP -count=1 PASS.
- GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/cluster -run ^TestIPsecSA -count=1 PASS.

## Risk

No wire-format change. Only generations strictly older than the latest commit for the same sender incarnation and DHCP family are fenced. Equal or newer generations and incarnation-zero traffic retain existing behavior.

## PR #18377 — cluster: Rearm never-seen confirmation retry (#17805) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17805-campaign`

Why:
When the Manager timer's freshness probe returned false, sync proof could
become fresh before handlePeerNeverSeen's second probe. The helper then
suppressed absence after the only timer was consumed, leaving a no-receiver
manager without an absence retry and non-preempt RGs held secondary.

What:
Report fresh-proof suppression from handlePeerNeverSeen and have the
Manager-clock owner rearm its existing 1s recheck only if its generation and
current state still permit it. Add the scripted false/true/false no-receiver
regression and docs/log/17805.md. NOT changed: the cold-boot grace, heartbeat
receiver, or election behavior.

Validation:
- RED before fix: GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/cluster -run '^TestNoReceiverNeverSeenFreshProofBetweenChecksRearms17805$' -count=1 — failed after 5s because absence was never confirmed.
- GREEN, named never-seen family + direct helper cells (20 named test functions): GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test -race ./pkg/cluster -run '^(TestNeverSeenConfirmedFloor|TestColdBootNeverSeenFloorSuppressesPromotion|TestColdBootNeverSeenSyncFreshSuppressesPromotion11566|TestColdBootNeverSeenSilentSyncAllowsPromotion11566|TestColdBootNeverSeenReadinessGate10697|TestPeerHeartbeatClearsConfirmedAbsence10697|TestSeenThenLostPathUnchangedByNeverSeenFloor|TestColdBootIdleSyncAliveNeverConfirmedAbsent11682|TestColdBootIdleSyncAckCadenceHoldsNeverSeenPeer11682|TestColdBootTrulySilentSyncStillPromotes11682|TestPeerRecentlyActiveWithinSilenceWindow11682|TestNoReceiverNeverSeenReadyPromotes16751|TestNoReceiverNeverSeenDegradedPromotes16751|TestNoReceiverNeverSeenFloorHolds16751|TestNoReceiverNeverSeenSyncFreshSuppresses16751|TestNeverSeenClockDisarms16751|TestNeverSeenClockReapplyKeepsFloor16751|TestNoReceiverNeverSeenFreshProofBetweenChecksRearms17805|TestNeverSeenTakeoverMarkedDegraded15211|TestNeverSeenSyncFreshDoesNotMarkDegraded15211)$' -count=1 — PASS.
- GREEN flake check: GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test -race ./pkg/cluster -run '^TestNoReceiverNeverSeenFreshProofBetweenChecksRearms17805$' -count=5 — PASS (5/5).
- gofmt -l on both touched Go files returned no output. Only named cells were run.

Risk:
The added retry occurs only after fresh proof suppresses the Manager callback's
second check. The generation/state guard prevents a retry after heartbeat,
stop, control-link removal, or ownership by a newer timer; absence and election
semantics are unchanged.

Closes #17805

## PR #18378 — daemon: preserve VRF retry debt across listener planes (#17812) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17812-campaign`

Why:
A failed same-address rebind must retain the old scope fingerprint so a later commit retries. In dual-plane operation, the API's shared legDevices map was also pruned using only the just-reconciled plane, erasing the sibling plane's live scope. The next reconcile then treated a correct socket as mismatched and attempted a colliding same-address bind, preventing retry convergence.

What:
Preserve live scope records for both installed HTTP and HTTPS planes whenever either plane reconciles. Keep the management scope fingerprint unchanged until every plane driven by the scope change succeeds. Add regressions for failed A-to-B rebind retry and for a follow-up HTTPS reconcile adopting its unchanged socket after HTTP reconciliation. Update API/daemon documentation and the issue log.

Validation:
RED before the daemon fix: TestMgmtFailedVRFRebindKeepsFingerprintAndRetries17812 advanced the fingerprint to vrf-b after the failed bind.
RED before the API fix: TestReconcileHTTPPreservesHTTPSBindScope16709 lost the HTTPS scope after HTTP reconciliation.
GREEN: all nine named daemon VRF cells and all five named API VRF cells passed, including the new retry/adoption controls and the real-kernel netns acceptance.

Risk:
The scope record set now follows every installed leg on both planes; retired addresses still drop when no plane retains them. Failed scope changes keep retry debt until a later reconcile succeeds.

Closes #17812

## PR #18379 — config: mask comment-only embedded commands (#17813) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17813-campaign`

Why: Nonempty comment-only embedded commands lex to zero tokens, bypassing redaction and retaining credentials in rendered configuration and rejection logs.

What: Fail closed for every nonempty zero-token payload; preserve whole-payload placeholders through joined and block AST rewrites and compare fingerprints; add regression coverage for redacted config persistence and event-engine warning logs.

Validation: RED on the named comment-only config cells before the fix. GREEN on the named config redaction cells and TestClassifyPlanLogsRedactedCmd16726 after the fix.

Risk: Only nonempty zero-token payloads change rendered output. Empty and whitespace-only payloads and ordinary tokenized redaction are unchanged; the live stored command remains cleartext.

Closes #17813

## PR #18380 — logging: reconcile deferred filter syslog generation (#17810) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17810-campaign`

Why:
A syslog retry could reinstall the filter-term map under LastApplyResult.Generation after a retained-snapshot partial publish advanced the applied snapshot identity. H-stamped FILTER_LOG events then mismatched stale G indefinitely. Also, SnapshotPublishDeferred remains set in LastApplyResult after its deferred publish lands, so a later partial H plus retry could leave G installed.

What:
Expose the userspace manager's applied snapshot generation through its adapter and use that identity when wiring filter-term syslog maps. Preserve LastApplyResult as fallback for runtimes without this capability, resolve both from one published dataplane, and treat a deferred flag as pending only while the applied generation is older than that full-apply generation. Prevent deferred completion from overwriting a newer applied generation. Add named retry regressions for an already-H map and deferred G→partial H, proving H-stamped `then syslog` events reach a UDP collector.

Validation:
- RED on unmodified origin/master: `TestSyslogRetryKeepsFilterMapAtAppliedSnapshotGeneration17810` failed because retry installed generation 41,true instead of applied partial generation 42.
- GREEN: all named filter/syslog wiring cells in pkg/daemon (including the deferred-G→partial-H control) and filter-generation routing cells in pkg/logging passed. Exact test names are recorded in docs/log/17810.md.
- gofmt applied to changed Go files.

Risk:
Only filter-term syslog generation selection changes. Deferred maps remain unchanged until the applied identity reaches the deferred full generation; genuinely stale events remain fail-closed. Runtimes without the applied-snapshot capability keep the existing full-apply fallback.

Closes #17810

## PR #18383 — config: scope NAT pool range validation to range leaf (#17811) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17811-campaign`

Why:
The source-pool tail validator was attached to the whole `port` container. A valid range followed by `no-translation` was parsed as one malformed range, while a modifier-first tail returned early and bypassed the `port` descendants' schema validators.

What:
Move the shared source-pool range-tail validator onto the `range` child. This keeps the compiler's range parser and authored-order behavior, while sibling modifiers are checked by their own schema nodes. Add regressions for flat and hierarchical range plus `no-translation`, both flat statement orders, and malformed deterministic child values in either order. Update allocation-modifier controls to retain their fail-closed assertion when sibling errors are reported by the closed-world walker rather than the range parser.

Validation:
- RED on origin/master 9aa0072: `TestSourceNATPoolPortRangeWithNoTranslation17811` rejected valid range-first flat and hierarchical `no-translation` cases; `TestSourceNATPoolPortSiblingStillSchemaValidated17811` accepted `deterministic block-size 0` when that sibling preceded the range.
- GREEN on the branch rebased onto origin/master ef523497ee32bd978a9b127a02d1dacea267adbe: 23 named `pkg/config` NAT-port regression cells and four named #17836 `pkg/api` middleware cells passed with campaign GOCACHE/GOTMPDIR; exact cells and commands are in `docs/log/17811.md`.
- `gofmt -l` on the four changed Go files produced no output. No broad package tests were run.

Risk:
Low. Only schema ownership changes; range validation still uses the compiler's strict parser, and sibling modifiers now reach their existing schema validators. Named controls cover malformed, repeated, misplaced, and out-of-range input.

Closes #17811

## PR #18384 — config: restrict credential-shape redaction to keyword positions (#17806) [OPEN]

Branch: `fix/17806-campaign`

Why: The substring classifier ran against every flattened token, so identifiers such as `password-admin` hid their ordinary descendant configuration. Exact `password` identifiers in credential contexts could also trigger the generic context gate.

What: Walk the live schema to classify keyword positions and skip schema arguments and dynamic identifiers. Keep open-world credential leaves structurally gated, preserve the `user-password` exemption, and add rendering and direct-index regressions.

Validation: Named redaction/credential cells passed on current origin/master, including all nine #16731 credential rows and `user-password` exemption coverage. The new identifier regressions failed before the fix for `password-admin` and API-auth username `password`.

Risk: New unmodelled credential leaves require explicit structural recognition; arbitrary open-world tokens do not trigger substring redaction.

Closes #17806
